This kind of tension provides, for Iser, the psychological excitement of reading. In short, Iser thinks the healthy reader should work hard and forego relaxation. There’s not enough work to do in either of two scenarios: if, on the one hand, the text just seems real, if there’s no spin on the everyday and there’s no sense of this being a fictive world. Here the gap isn’t big enough. As an implied evaluation of what is being read, this is a disputable claim. The history of fiction recurrently favors fictional worlds that aspire to be identical to the way things are. Arguably, Jonathan Franzen’s novels are well received for this reason. The violation of expectations is not the driving force behind this kind of fiction. Another kind of psychological pleasure is involved that Iser is perhaps not taking into account, the pleasure in imitation that causes us to exclaim, as Aristotle says, “Ah, that is he.”

另一方面，伊瑟尔认为，阅读那种不断维持幻觉的文本也毫无价值。换句话说，文本创造了一个我们明知是幻觉的“永无乡”，但一旦我们身处其中，便能如此舒适地生活，几乎无需改变预期，以至于它变得像子宫一样温暖舒适。伊瑟尔在这里指的是他所谓的“美食小说”，包括护士小说、言情小说和某些侦探小说等文学子类型——尽管很多侦探小说远比这种描述所暗示的要好得多。现实生活中，穷人很少能嫁给王子，但在美食小说中，这却是一种理所当然的预期。因此，伊瑟尔不赞成这两种阅读体验，因为它们都缺乏阅读的必要性。

On the other hand, Iser says, neither is there any value in reading a text in which an illusion is perpetually sustained. In other words, a never-never land is created that we know to be an illusion, but we get to live in it so comfortably and with so little alteration of expectation once we’re there that it becomes womblike and cozy. Here Iser is referring to what he calls “culinary fiction,” subgenres of literature like nurse novels, bodice rippers, and certain kinds of detective fiction—although a lot of detective fiction is much better than that description would imply. The pauper rarely gets to marry the prince in life, but in culinary fiction it’s an unviolated expectation that this will happen. Iser disapproves, then, of both these reading experiences because there’s no reading work to be done.

伊瑟认为，文本与读者之间的关系必须是一种合作。文本的多义性——即优秀文本会蕴含多种意义的可能性——与读者对舒适幻象的渴望，是两种相互对立的因素。换言之，任何读者都无可否认地渴望安然沉浸在未经改造的现实虚构世界，或是护士小说、言情小说的世界中；但优秀的文本会不断地打破读者的认知，阻止他们建立这种舒适区。因此，我们维持幻象的倾向与文本不断瓦解幻象的方式之间的张力，正是伊瑟想要强调的阅读心理兴奋点，即阅读的“张力”。

The relationship between text and reader must be a collaboration, Iser argues. The polysemantic nature of the text—the fact that the text hazards many possibilities of meaning if it’s a good text—and the allure of comfortable illusion for the reader are constructively opposed factors. In other words, there is something in any reader that does undeniably wish to settle comfortably into the fiction of untransformed reality or into the world of the nurse novel or the bodice ripper; but a good text is perpetually bringing the reader up short and preventing that comfort zone from establishing itself, so that the tension between the tendency on our part to sustain an illusion and the way in which the text keeps undermining the illusion is again that aspect of the psychological excitement, the “tension,” of reading that Iser wants to promote.

现在来说说《拖车托尼》。我想提一下几个地方，在这些地方，预期及其可能落空的问题就出现了。公平地说，如果我们要认真地以这种方式解读托尼，就必须把自己代入幼儿的视角；作为读者或旁听者，我们必须像幼儿一样看待阅读文本时的心理兴奋。这并不难做到。例如：

Now a word about Tony the Tow Truck. I wanted to call attention to a few places where the issue of expectation and its possible violation arises. It’s only fair to say that if we’re going to read Tony seriously in this way we have to put ourselves in the shoes, or booties, of a toddler; as readers or auditors we have to regard the psychological excitement of experiencing the text as that of a toddler. It’s not so very difficult to do. For example:

我是拖车托尼。
I am Tony the Tow Truck.
我住在一个黄色的小车库里。
I live in a little yellow garage.
我帮助抛锚的汽车。
I help cars that are stuck.
我把它们拖到我的车库。
I tow them to my garage.
我喜欢我的工作。
I like my job.
有一天我遇到了难题。
One day I am stuck.
谁能帮助托尼这辆拖车？
Who will help Tony the tow truck?

这是一个绝妙的例子，展现了期待与悬念之间的张力：期待有人会帮助托尼，却又不知道这个人是谁。从成人的角度来看，这是一个充满趣味的时刻，因为我们知道故事发生在民间传说的世界里，而民间传说中，任何事情都会重复三次。即使不看下文，我们也知道会有两辆车出现却拒绝帮助托尼，而第三辆车会伸出援手。甚至连标题《拖车托尼》都巧妙地运用了头韵。当我们阅读俄国形式主义者的作品时，会发现他们早期的研究成果之一：“诗歌中的重复类似于民间传说中的同义反复。”《拖车托尼》中正是如此， “t-t-t”，然后是三个事件：尼托车、斯皮迪车和邦比车依次出现，最终由邦比解决了问题。

This is a wonderful example of the tension between having an expectation, the expectation that someone will help Tony, and being in a state of suspense, not knowing who that someone will be. From the adult point of view, this is a culinary moment because we know that we’re in the world of folklore and that in folklore everything happens three times. We know without reading farther that two vehicles are going to come along and refuse to help Tony and that the third vehicle will. Notice even the title: Tony the Tow Truck, with its alliterative triad. When we read the Russian formalists, we will encounter one of their early research findings: “repetition in verse is analogous to tautology in folklore.” We have exactly that going on in Tony the Tow Truck, “t- t- t,” and then the three events: Neato the Car, Speedy the Car, and Bumpy the Car coming along in sequence, with Bumpy resolving the problem.

总之，我们都抱有期待。我们面临着悬念的辩证法：一方面，这场危机能否得到解决？——另一方面，对于成年人来说，民间传说中它肯定会得到解决。毫无疑问，幼儿也已经抱有期待，但这种期待又被对期待落空的恐惧所抵消。

In any case, then, we have an expectation. We have the dialectic of suspense: on the one hand, will this crisis be resolved?—and on the other hand, for the adult, the folkloric certainly that it will be resolved. For the toddler there is already a sense of expectation, no doubt, but it is offset by the fear that the expectation will be violated.

“我帮不了你，”汽车尼托说，“我不想弄脏自己。”
“I cannot help you,” says Neato the Car. “I don’t want to get dirty.”
“我帮不了你，”斯皮迪汽车说，“我太忙了。”
“I cannot help you,” says Speedy the Car. “I am too busy.”
我很难过。
I am very sad.
这时，一辆小汽车开了过来。
Then a little car pulls up.

我认为“pulls up”和伽达默尔被“pulled up short”（突然被拉住）的比喻非常贴切；而且，在我看来，这句话里似乎还隐藏着另一种预期危机。作为一个蹒跚学步的孩子，我需要理解这个表达的习语含义。我才三岁，也许我根本不知道“pulls up”是什么意思。正因如此，这句话对一个蹒跚学步的孩子来说并不那么深思熟虑，但同时，它也恰好契合了我们的目的，因为它提出了一个阅读难题，一个读者在继续阅读故事之前必须完成的虚拟任务。蹒跚学步的孩子必须弄明白“pulls up”是什么意思，就像成年读者在阅读《想象的乐趣》时必须弄明白“plastic”（塑料的）是什么意思一样。正如我所说，这种特殊的阅读困难恰恰是伽达默尔所说的“突然被拉住”，这真是一个绝妙的讽刺。

I think it’s wonderful that “pulls up” is just like Gadamer being “pulled up short”; and there is, it seems to me, another crisis of expectation in this line. As a toddler, I need to negotiate that expression idiomatically. I’m three years old and maybe I don’t know what “pulls up” means. It’s not very thoughtful writing for a toddler precisely for that reason, but at the same time it lends itself to our purposes because it poses a reading problem, a piece of virtual work that needs to be done before the reader can get on with the story. The toddler has to find out what “pulls up” means in the same way that the adult reader of The Pleasures of the Imagination has to find out what “plastic” means. As I say, it’s a wonderful irony that this particular difficulty in reading is precisely what Gadamer calls being pulled up short.

于是你解决了这个问题，然后，瞧！

So you solve the problem and then, lo and behold:

这是我的朋友 Bumpy。
It is my friend Bumpy.
颠簸推了我一把。
Bumpy gives me a push.
他不停地推搡——我这就出发。
He pushes and pushes and—I’m on my way.
“谢谢你，Bumpy，”我回应道。
“Thank you, Bumpy,” I call back.
“不客气，”邦比说道。
“You’re welcome,” says Bumpy.

这里又产生了一种期待。这是一个蕴含寓意的故事。拖车和帮助它脱困的帮手之间建立起一种温暖的互惠关系，因此人们期待故事中会蕴含某种寓意。它会是什么呢？就像《古舟子咏》一样，有很多方法可以赋予故事寓意。我们并不确定《古舟子咏》最终会选择“热爱一切事物，无论大小”这个寓意。托尼的故事也是如此。它以“这才是真正的朋友”结尾，但由于还有其他可能的寓意，我们必须保持悬念才能找到答案。再一次，读者能够带着一种愉悦的兴奋感度过这段悬念，直到寓意揭晓。通过这种方式，我们可以以一种启发沃尔夫冈·伊瑟“阅读行为”的方式来解读《拖车托尼》。

Here there arises another expectation. This is the kind of story that has a moral. A sense of warm reciprocity is established between the tow truck and the helper that saves the tow truck from being stuck, so the expectation is that there will be a moral. What will it be? There are many ways in which—as in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner—a moral could be attached here. It’s by no means clear that The Rime of the Ancient Mariner will settle on the moral “Love all things, great and small things.” And so it is with Tony. It happens to end “Now that’s what I call a friend,” but because other morals were possible we must remain in suspense to find this out. Once again, there is that moment of suspense that the reader is able to survive as it were with a kind of pleasurable excitement until the moral is revealed. By some such means, then, Tony the Tow Truck can be approached in a way that sheds light on Wolfgang Iser’s “act of reading.”

最后，我想提出一个问题：如果伽达默尔和伊瑟尔之间存在如此显著的区别——伽达默尔似乎强加给我们一套传统的经典，而伊瑟尔似乎强加给我们一套创新的经典——那么历史主义难道不是一种解脱吗？任何追求客观历史主义的努力都必须允许经典自然演进。或许有些奇怪，诠释学原则几乎默认地蕴含着评价性的前提。相比之下，历史主义难道不是开放了经典，并将阅读过程和阅读体验本身，从经典化转变为档案式的、包罗万象的吗？

I’ll conclude by posing a question: if there exists this remarkable distinction between Gadamer and Iser, where Gadamer seems to impose on us a traditional canon and Iser seems to impose on us an innovative canon, isn’t there some relief in historicism after all? Any effort to achieve objective historicism must let the canon evolve as it will. It’s odd, perhaps, that hermeneutic principles do almost tacitly entail evaluative premises. Doesn’t historicism by contrast open the canon and indeed make the process of reading, the experience of reading, archival and omnivorous rather than canonical?

问题就在这里：只有当我们能够像赫希所说的那样区分意义和重要性时，避免诠释学束缚才能带来解放性的结果。如果我们真的确信历史主义的阅读方法是有效且可行的，那么之后，如果我们愿意，我们可以通过宣称某些文本具有某种重要性，而这些文本正是我们关心并想要阅读的文本，来建立一套经典；但这始终是一种自愿的行为，而非必然之举。然而，如果意义和重要性相互交融，那么我所做的，实际上是在无意识或半意识层面建立一套经典。我会告诉自己，文本的意义就在于此，但与此同时，我会在不知不觉中找到方法，肯定某些意义，否定另一些意义。

Well, here’s the hitch: this would be the liberatory consequence of avoiding hermeneutic strictures only if we could distinguish, in Hirsch’s terms, between meaning and significance. If we really are sure that the historicist approach to reading is effective and works, then later on, if we wish, we can establish a canon by saying certain texts have certain kinds of significance and those are the texts that we care about and want to read; but that would always be a voluntary gesture and not a necessary one. If, however, meaning and significance bleed into each other, what I’m going to be doing is establishing a canon as it were unconsciously or semiconsciously. I’ll tell myself that such and such is just what the text means, but at the same time, I’ll be finding ways, without realizing it, of affirming certain kinds of meaning and discrediting certain other kinds of meaning.

因此，我们或许已经从各个角度证明，价值观确实源于我们对阅读方式的假设。评价似乎与简单的阅读方式考量相去甚远，但它却以一种我们永远无法完全摆脱的历史视角来表达自身。

So what we’ve shown perhaps from every standpoint is that values do follow from our assumptions about how to read. Evaluation would seem rather distant from simple considerations of how to read, but it has a way of speaking from within the historical horizons we can never escape altogether.

 

 

文本与结构

Text and Structure

 

 

第五章

CHAPTER 5

自主艺术作品的理念
The Idea of the Autonomous Artwork

阅读材料：

Readings:

Wimsatt, William K. 和 Monroe Beardsley。“意图谬误。”载于《批判传统》，第 811-818 页。

Wimsatt, William K., and Monroe Beardsley. “The Intentional Fallacy.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 811–818.

摘自菲利普·西德尼爵士、伊曼努尔·康德、沃尔特·佩特、奥斯卡·王尔德、约翰·克罗·兰塞姆的作品。

Passages from Sir Philip Sidney, Immanuel Kant, Walter Pater, Oscar Wilde, John Crowe Ransom.

本次讲座我们将开启一系列探讨二十世纪“形式主义”的方法。这是一个含义丰富的词，而且常常带有贬义。我希望在系列讨论结束后，大家不会再觉得它那么令人生畏，也能更清楚地了解它的各种语境和内涵。我们现在探讨的主题既属于批评史，也属于文学理论。我曾说过，批评史和文学理论之间存在差异，其中一个区别在于，批评史涉及文学评价：即我们为何关注文学，以及我们如何判断一部作品的好坏。这种文学思考方式往往脱离了文学理论，但却存在于我们目前正在阅读的材料之中。当温萨特和比尔兹利谈论一首诗的“成功”时，他们认为整个批评事业，包括其理论基础——定义一首诗，决定我们应该如何最好地解读它——仍然以文学评价为导向。虽然我们目前的主题属于文学批评的范畴，但我们将以理论的角度来解读它，重点关注诗歌的定义以及我们应该优先考虑哪些标准才能以最佳方式解读诗歌。

In this lecture we begin a series of approaches to twentieth-century “formalism.” That’s a big word, and has often been a pejorative one. At the end of our series of discussions, I hope it won’t seem quite as daunting and that its varied settings and implications will have been made clear to you. The topic we take up now belongs as much to the history of criticism as to literary theory. I’ve said there’s a difference between the history of criticism and theory of literature, one difference being that the history of criticism involves literary evaluation: the question of why we care about literature, and how we can find a means of saying that it’s good or not good. This is an aspect of thought concerning literature that tends to fall out of literary theory but not out of the materials that we are reading at present. When Wimsatt and Beardsley talk about the “success” of a poem, they understand the whole critical enterprise, including its theoretical underpinnings—defining a poem, deciding how we should best read it—still to be geared toward literary evaluation. Although our present subject matter belongs within the practice of literary criticism, then, we’re going to be reading it with a theoretical spin, focusing on how poems are defined and the criteria we should favor to read poems in the best way.

我可能只会称他为“温萨特”，但您应该知道，他在这篇文章中的朋友和合作者门罗·比尔兹利是一位专攻美学的哲学家，曾在坦普尔大学任教。温萨特与比尔兹利合作撰写了三篇文章，收录了《意图谬误》一文，该文也收录在《语言偶像》一书中，本文便是其中之一。温萨特曾在耶鲁大学任教，耶鲁大学通常被认为是新批评派的摇篮，而温萨特则是该派的理论领袖。这个群体（成员还包括克林斯·布鲁克斯）巩固了一种教学方法和文学态度，这成为了耶鲁大学英语系和比较文学系最为密切相关的文学理论研究的第一波浪潮——也是两波浪潮中的第一波。事实上，一些新批评派学者在来到耶鲁之前就已经完成了许多重要的研究工作。另一些学者则从未到过耶鲁，但这一运动至今仍与这所大学紧密相连。如果这是一门其他类型的课程，例如由我们将要讨论的作者之一约翰·吉洛里教授的课程，那么授课者就可以合理地将这种关联解释为文学教育社会学的一个方面。

I’ll probably just refer to “Wimsatt,” but you should know that his friend and collaborator on this essay, Monroe Beardsley, was a philosopher specializing in aesthetics who taught at Temple University. For the book in which “The Intentional Fallacy” appeared, The Verbal Icon, Wimsatt collaborated with Beardsley on three essays, and this is one of them. Wimsatt taught at Yale, which is usually considered the home of the New Critics, with Wimsatt its theoretical leader. This group, which also includes Cleanth Brooks, consolidated a teaching method and attitude toward literature that turned out to be the first wave—the first of two waves—of involvement in literary theory with which the Yale English and Comparative Literature departments have been most closely identified. In truth, some of the New Critics did much of their important work before they arrived at Yale. Others never were at Yale, yet the movement is still closely associated with this institution; and if this were a course of another kind, one taught for example by John Guillory, one of the authors we shall discuss, the instructor could plausibly explain this association as an aspect of the sociology of literary education.

我到耶鲁的时候，温萨特还在教书，克林斯·布鲁克斯刚退休不久，还在主持一年一度的垒球赛，所以我跟他们之间有一种特殊的联系。我能切身体会到，正如我希望我们最终都能体会到的那样，新批评中发展起来的“细读”风格对后来的许多批评和理论产生了多么深远的影响，而这些批评和理论通常对新批评持敌对态度，也并非总是承认这种影响。但是，关于新批评如何被其后继者们几乎持续不断地愤慨否定，直到今天，尽管它仍然影响着每一位仍然相信诠释的批评家（并非所有人都如此），这个话题最好留待以后再谈。

When I arrived at Yale, Wimsatt was still teaching, and Cleanth Brooks, recently retired, was still hosting the annual softball game, so I feel a personal connection with them. I can understand at first hand, as I hope all of us will eventually, the degree to which the style of “close reading” that evolved within the New Criticism left an important mark on much subsequent criticism and theory, typically hostile to it, that hasn’t always acknowledged this debt. But the whole topic of the way the New Criticism has been indignantly repudiated by its successors almost continuously until this day, even as it continues to influence every critic who still believes in interpreting (not all do), is best left for later occasions.

如果没有新批评派，你们恐怕谁都无法耐心地坐完中学英语课。1939年，克林斯·布鲁克斯和诗人兼小说家罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦（当时他们都还没到耶鲁大学）出版了《理解诗歌》一书，这本书随后风靡全国，不断再版，突然间，教师们找到了让学生在课堂上待满五十分钟的方法。“精读”——即你可以对文本进行深入思考——这种理念认为，教授文本不仅仅是背诵、表达情感，然后徒劳地寻找新的解读——首先在教育学上具有革命性意义。它引入了复杂而不断展开的意义领域，学生们很快意识到自己也能贡献自己的见解。他们看到了老师引导他们去理解的思维模式和阐释模式的方法，不知不觉中，五十分钟就过去了，每个人都度过了一段愉快的时光。从我们的角度来看，很难相信这种情况以前从未在英语课堂上发生过。

If it weren’t for the New Critics, probably none of you would have been able to sit patiently through any of your middle and high school English classes. When in 1939 Cleanth Brooks and the poet-novelist Robert Penn Warren (neither of them yet at Yale) published a book called Understanding Poetry, subsequently reissued again and again as it swept the country, suddenly schoolteachers had a way of keeping kids in the classroom for fifty minutes. “Close reading,” the idea that you could take a text and do things with it—the belief that teaching a text isn’t just a matter of reciting it, emoting over it, and then looking around in vain for something else to say about it—was first and foremost pedagogically revolutionary. It introduced complex fields of unfolding meaning to which students soon felt they could contribute their own insights. They saw patterns of thought and ways of elaborating patterns that the teacher was guiding them toward, and the next thing they knew the fifty minutes were over and everybody had had a pretty good time. Hard to believe from our point of view that that had never happened in an English class before.

说真的，现在对这类课程感兴趣的许多人，其实早就因为新批评而对文学产生了兴趣——尤其是那些上过私立学校的人；但只要老师们大学时上过英语课，精读也是公立学校教学的一大特色。暂且不论精读本身的价值，它总是能填满课堂时间。即使你只有五十分钟以上的时间，也能充分利用它。新批评的先驱之一T·S·艾略特却对精读持保留态度，称之为“榨汁机式教学”。他的意思是说，精读是一个费时费力的过程，会耗尽学生的精力。但这个过程在智力上却极具启发性，因为它能让学生意识到，他们原本以为简单的事物实际上有多么复杂。新批评营造了一种氛围，在这种氛围下，人们可以坦然地认为，微妙而复杂的思考令人振奋，而不是像口臭一样令人尴尬；甚至连诗人（那些创作出《玫瑰是红色的》的诗人）也应该因其深思熟虑而受到赞扬。许多学生在这些课堂上恍然大悟：更好的解读就是更好的思考。

Seriously, many people who now take an interest in courses like this one have long taken an interest in literature because of the New Criticism—especially if they went to private school; but close reading is a feature of public school teaching, too, whenever the teachers have actually taken English classes in college. Its merits aside, close reading always filled the time. If you had more than fifty minutes, you could still make ample use of it. T. S. Eliot, who was one of the intellectual forebears of the New Criticism, nevertheless took a somewhat dim view of it and called it “the lemon squeezer school.” All he meant was that it was a painstaking process that drained the subject. But the process was wonderfully galvanizing intellectually because it made students notice how intricate what they had thought to be simple really was. The New Criticism created an atmosphere in which it was acceptable to notice that subtle, complex thinking was exhilarating, not a social embarrassment like bad breath, and that even poets (the good folks who brought us “Roses are red”) might be credited with thinking carefully and well. It dawned on many students in these classrooms that better interpretation is just better thinking.

细读需要关注形式，而形式自始至终都未曾逃过优秀批评家的关注。柏拉图在其《理想国》第十卷中，专门论证应将诗人逐出理想国，其中一项论据便是诗人拙劣的模仿。他们的模仿与我们在现实中遇到的事物的理想形式相去甚远。他们事事出错。他们认为水中折射的木棍一定是弯曲的。他们受制于各种各样的错觉，不可信赖，苏格拉底甚至称他们为骗子。因此，在柏拉图看来，诗歌本身就是一种形式：一种扭曲了正确模仿的糟糕形式。

Close reading entails attention to form, which indeed from the beginning has never escaped the attention of good critics. When Plato devoted book ten of his Republic to an argument supporting the banishment of the poets from his ideal republic, part of his complaint was that poets are terrible imitators. Their imitations are three times removed from the ideal forms of the objects we encounter in reality. They get everything wrong. They think that a stick refracted in the water must be a crooked stick. They are subject to every conceivable kind of illusion, not to be trusted, and Socrates calls them liars. So for Plato, poetry is already defined as form: bad form distorting proper imitation.

亚里士多德在撰写《诗学》时，显然是有意识地反驳柏拉图在《理想国》中的论点，而他反驳的核心或许就在于此：柏拉图认为诗人拙劣地模仿现实，而亚里士多德则认为这是范畴错误，因为诗人并非模仿现实，而是重构现实。诗人模仿的并非事物本来的样子，而是事物应该有的样子。换言之，诗人的职责在于组织、赋予形式以意义，以应对现实的纷繁复杂。顺便一提，这里的现实并非柏拉图所理解的现实，即理念的领域。亚里士多德笔下的诗人所做的，是重新调整、更好地规范现实世界中存在的各种要素。这才是形式主义的真正起源。

When Aristotle writes the Poetics, he does so very consciously in refutation of Plato’s arguments in the Republic, and perhaps the cornerstone of his refutation is simply this: whereas Plato says poets imitate reality badly, Aristotle says this is a category mistake because poets don’t imitate reality, they reconstruct reality. Poets imitate things not as they are but as they should be. In other words, the business of poets is to organize, to bring form to bear on, the messiness of reality. This reality, by the way, is not Plato’s reality, which is the realm of the ideal forms. What Aristotle’s poet does is to realign, the better to regularize, the elements existing in the real world. This is really the origin of formalism.

文艺复兴时期，诗人兼朝臣菲利普·西德尼爵士创作了一部文笔优美、文采斐然的诗歌辩护之作，其中一个版本名为《诗歌辩护》。尽管他是柏拉图的忠实拥趸，但在这部“辩护”中——而诗歌辩护必然是对柏拉图的反驳——西德尼以惊人的修辞技巧发展了亚里士多德的形式论，令人印象深刻地阐述了亚里士多德最初提出的论点。在你引用的段落中（见附录），西德尼谈到了各种有价值的论述：神学、赞美诗、科学、哲学、历史、世俗诗歌——换句话说，所有能够为人类福祉和进步做出贡献的方式。他认为，除了赞美诗之外，每一种论述都是一种“服务性的科学”。也就是说，除了赞美诗之外，所有论述都服务于自然界或神圣领域；它们的重要性在于它们忠实地模仿，或者至少是颂扬那些毋庸置疑的世界。因此，你文章的第一句话是：“世间没有一种艺术不是以自然之作为主要目标的。” 这就是为什么即使是虔诚的西德尼认为远胜于世俗诗歌的艺术——赞美诗，以及神圣的知识或神学——即使是那些神圣的论述，也同样是“服务于科学的”。西德尼对诗人的描述非常特别，诗人介于神性与诗歌传统上与之竞争的其他论述之间：科学、哲学和历史。这就是诗歌的独特之处：

In the Renaissance, the poet and courtier Sir Philip Sidney produced an elegant, splendidly written defense of poetry, called in one version The Apology for Poesie. Although he was a fervent admirer of Plato, in this “defense”—and defenses of poetry must always be defenses against Plato—Sidney develops Aristotle’s concept of form with striking rhetorical ingenuity, impressively laying out the case that Aristotle first made. In your passage (see the appendix), Sidney is talking about the various kinds of worthwhile discourse: divinity, hymnody, science, philosophy, history, secular poetry—in other words, all the ways in which one can contribute to human welfare and betterment. He says that each discourse except one of them is a “serving science.” That is to say, all but one, even hymnody, are subservient either to the natural world or to the realm of the divine; their importance lies in their faithful imitation or at least celebration of those unquestioned worlds. Thus the first sentence of your passage: “There is no art [but one] delivered to mankind that hath not the works of Nature for his principal object.” Here is why even the arts that the devout Sidney thinks far superior to secular poetry–hymnody, and also divine knowledge or theology—even those sacred discourses are also “serving sciences.” Sidney is saying something very special about the poet, who stands somewhere between divinity and the other sorts of discourse with which poetry is traditionally in rivalry: science, philosophy, and history. Here is what’s unique about poetry:

只有那些不屑于受制于任何此类束缚（换句话说，不屑于受制于事物现状）的诗人，才能凭借自身创造力的力量，实际上发展出另一种本质……他不肯定任何事物，因此也从不说谎。
Only the poet disdaining to be tied to any such subjection [subjection, in other words, to things as they are], lifted up with the vigor of his own invention, doth grow in effect another nature.… He nothing affirms, and therefore never lieth.

因此，柏拉图错了。诗人并非说谎者，因为他谈论的并非任何可验证或可证伪的事物。他将自己局限于他自己创造的世界的框架之内。西德尼认为这是一种魔法。例如，他援引了伪科学占星术。他说，诗人“在他自己的智慧的黄道带中自由驰骋”。他还援引了伪科学炼金术，指出诗人与我们其他人一样，生活在一个虚无缥缈的世界里，而他用这个虚无缥缈的世界——“虚无缥缈”指的是黄铜——创造了一个金色的世界。简而言之，诗歌具有变革性。它描绘的不是事物本来的样子，而是事物应该是什么样子，从而改变了现实。这一论点再次证明了文学的合理性，即文学能够以形式弥补现实的不足。

Plato, then, is wrong. The poet is not a liar because he’s not talking about anything that’s verifiable or falsifiable. He confines himself to the parameters of the world he himself has brought into being. Sidney thinks of it as a kind of magic. He invokes, for example, the pseudoscience of astrology. The poet, he says, “ranges freely within the zodiac of his own wit.” He also invokes the pseudoscience of alchemy when he says that the poet, like the rest of us, inhabits a brazen world, and of this brazen world—“brazen” means brass—he makes a golden world. In short, poetry is transformational. In representing not things as they are but things as they should be, it transforms reality. This argument then once again justifies the idea of literature as that which brings form to bear on the inadequacies of the real.

现在，我并非想暗示，在西德尼之后，直到康德之前，关于形式的观念就停滞不前。当然，期间发生了很多变化，但康德在哲学史上著名的“哥白尼式革命”的一个方面，是他对一种特殊能力的思考，这种能力调节着我们对事物的审美理解，他称之为“判断力”。在1790年出版的《判断力批判》中，他概述了美的哲学以及“判断力”感知事物之美的途径（“美”一词在拉丁语中是formosus的对应词）。正如你将看到的，在很大程度上，康德虽然对西德尼一无所知，但在这方面却继承了西德尼的思想。

Now I don’t mean to imply, as I continue this thumbnail account, that ideas of form just stood still after Sidney until you get to Kant. A great deal changed, of course, but one aspect of Kant’s famous “Copernican revolution” in the history of philosophy is his thinking about the special faculty that mediates our aesthetic understanding of things, a faculty that he calls “the judgment.” In The Critique of Judgment of 1790, he outlines among many other things a philosophy of the beautiful and of the means whereby “the judgment” perceives objects as beautiful (schn, or “beautiful,” is the equivalent of the Latin formosus). To a large extent, Kant, without knowing anything about Sidney, nevertheless follows Sidney in this regard, as you’ll see.

我会坚持不懈地阅读这些段落，希望一切都能豁然开朗，尤其是这一点：正如我们所见，西德尼实际上将诗歌的地位置于神学和其他科学之间。诗歌并非人所能追求的最高职业。西德尼对此深信不疑，以至于当他身负重伤，即将离世时，他下令焚毁自己所有的诗作。他毫不怀疑诗歌逊于更高层次的思想。某种程度上，康德也表达了类似的观点，尽管他指的并非神圣的科学，而是理性能力所提出的道德准则。在你将要读到的段落中，你会发现他的观点并非艺术和对美的判断是人类所能达到的最高表达。他的观点，正如西德尼的观点一样，仅仅是它们具有其他任何事物都不具备的特殊属性。这正是整个传统试图阐明的要点。以下是我从康德著作中摘录的第二段文字中他的原话：

I’m going to read these passages with some perseverance, so all will become clear, I hope, but especially this: Sidney, as we’ve seen, actually ranks poetry somewhere between divinity and the other sciences. Poetry is not the supreme vocation that a person can pursue. Sidney believed this so passionately that when he knew himself to be dying, having been mortally wounded in a battle, he ordered that all of his own poems be burned. He had no doubt that poetry was inferior to a higher form of thought. In a way, that’s what Kant’s saying, too, though he is thinking not of divine science but of the moral imperatives posited by the faculty of reason. In the passages you’ll read, you’ll see that his point is not that art and the judgment of the beautiful are the supreme expressions of which humanity is capable. His point is only, like Sidney’s, that they have a special characteristic that nothing else has. That’s the point that this whole tradition is trying to make. Here is how Kant puts it in the second passage I’ve taken from his work:

愉悦和善都与欲望能力有关[愉悦是我们欲望、我们的感官能力——顺便一提，康德称之为“知性”——体验对象的方式。对知性而言，事物要么是愉悦的，要么是不愉悦的。相反，善是我们的认知和道德能力——康德称之为“理性”——与这些对象达成和解的方式。事物要么值得赞同，要么不值得赞同；但正如康德所论证的，无论是对知性还是理性而言，事物的存在都与欲望能力有关——我想要，我不想要；我赞同，我反对]，而且它们都给前者（即愉悦）带来了一种病态的、条件反射式的满足；后者是一种纯粹的实践满足，它不仅取决于对象的表象，还取决于主体与对象存在的表象联系[换句话说，取决于我想要它还是不想要它，赞成它还是不赞成它]。
The pleasant and the good both have a reference to the faculty of desire [The pleasant is the way in which our appetency, our sensuous faculty—which Kant calls “the understanding,” by the way—experiences objects. Things for the understanding are either pleasant or unpleasant. The good, on the contrary, is the way in which our cognitive and moral faculty—which Kant calls “the reason”—comes to terms with those same objects. Things are either to be approved of or not to be approved of; but in the case of either the understanding or the reason, as Kant argues, things exist in reference to the faculty of desire—I want, I don’t want; I approve, I disapprove], and they bring with them the former [that is to say, the pleasant] a satisfaction pathologically conditioned; the latter a pure practical, satisfaction which is determined not merely by the representation of the object but also by the represented connection of the subject with the existence of the object [in other words, by the way in which I want it or don’t want it, approve of it or don’t approve of it].

换句话说，我的愿望决定了我对感知对象的态度，包括我的理解力和理性。但是，对于一个既不令人愉悦也不被认为是好的对象，我的态度是冷静客观的，我看待对象并非出于自身，而是将其视为自身的一部分。这就是判断的态度，它将对象视为美，而非愉悦或美好。

My wishes, in other words, determine the attitude toward objects of perception both of my understanding and of my reason. But my attitude toward an object perceived as neither pleasant nor good is dispassionate and views the object not for me but in and for itself. This is the attitude of the judgment, viewing the object not as pleasant or good but as beautiful.

那么，请看下一段：“品味是一种判断事物的能力，或者说是一种完全客观地表达满意或不满意感受的方法。”换句话说，在其他两种能力的影响下，我仍然会根据事物的愉悦或不愉悦、好或坏来判断它的好坏，但此时我的喜好与欲望或赞同都无关。我喜欢或不喜欢它，是基于判断能力而非理解能力（理解能力是欲望性的）或理性能力（理性能力是道德性的）所产生的原则。

Take the next passage, then: “Taste is the faculty of the judging of an object or a method of representing it by an entirely disinterested satisfaction or dissatisfaction.” In other words, under the sway of the other two faculties, I still like it or don’t like it as the pleasant or the unpleasant or the good or the bad, but now my liking has nothing to do either with desire or with approval. I like it or I don’t like it according to principles that arise from the faculty of judgment and not from the faculty of the understanding, which is appetitive, or the faculty of reason, which is moral.

因此，康德的第四段论述是：“美是客体目的性的形式，只要这种目的性在被感知时不带有任何目的的表象。”在此，康德区分了有目的的（purposive ）和有目的的（purposeful）。有目的的是指客体的实际目的。它能做什么？它能为我做什么？它在世界上如何运作？它在其他客体中扮演什么角色？它对我的生活——尤其是我的生活——有何影响？这适用于知性，也适用于理性。但是，通过判断感知到的客体目的性，是指客体自身自足的方式。它有其内在的目的，这种目的并非必然与任何其他事物相关。可以说，它具有内在的连贯性。它的各个部分之间存在着一种动态性，这种动态性完全与其自身的存在相关。它是一种形式。这种形式，因为我们可以看到它具有结构，因为我们可以看到它具有组织性和复杂性，所以它是有目的的，尽管它并非有目的的。

Hence the fourth passage: “Beauty is the form of the purposiveness of an object so far as it is perceived in it without any representation of a purpose.” Here Kant makes a distinction between the purposive and the purposeful. The purposeful is the practical purpose of the object. What can it do? What can it do for me? How does it go to work in the world? What is its function among other objects? What bearing does it have on—in particular—my life? This is true both for the understanding and the reason. But the purposiveness of the object as perceived by the judgment is the way in which the object is sufficient unto itself. It has its own inner purpose, which is not a purpose that has any bearing necessarily on anything else. It has, as one might say, an internal coherence. It has a dynamism of parts that is strictly with reference to its own existence. It is a form. That form, because we can see it has structure and because we can see it has organization and complexity, is purposive though not purposeful.

这就是康德著名的区分：目的性（purposive），即审美对象的内在组织结构；以及目的性（purposeful），即任何对象——包括从欲望或道德角度看待的审美对象——在世界中或为我们发挥作用的性质。正如我刚才提到的，审美对象可以被视为具有目的性。我看到一个裸体，艺术史学家称之为“裸像”。假设我不认为它仅仅是一个裸像。我想要它，或者我不赞同它，那么，它就不再具有审美意义了。我稍后会再谈到这一点，但我希望你们能明白这个例子是如何展现目的性和目的性之间的区别的。

So that’s Kant’s famous distinction between the purposive, the inner organization of an aesthetic object, and the purposeful, which is the quality of any object—including the aesthetic object viewed appetitively or morally—insofar as it goes to work in the world or for us. As I’ve just indicated, an aesthetic object can be viewed as purposeful. I see a naked body, which the art historians call a nude. Let’s say I don’t accept that it’s merely a nude. I want it or I disapprove of it and, presto, it’s no longer aesthetic. I’ll come back to that in a moment, but I hope you can see how this example shows the difference between the purposive and the purposeful.

为了重述这些重要的区别，我想引用塞缪尔·泰勒·柯勒律治的一段话。至少在这一点上，他是康德的追随者，而且我认为，他对我们刚才讨论的康德的论点进行了有益的转述。柯勒律治在这里比康德更强调道德能力优于审美能力，尽管道德能力与审美能力都源于欲望的动机。这是第五段，大部分内容可以在附录中找到：

In order to rephrase these important distinctions, I want to turn to a passage from Samuel Taylor Coleridge, who is, at least on this occasion, a disciple of Kant and is, I think, usefully paraphrasing the arguments of Kant that we have just been engaged with. Coleridge here emphasizes more strongly than Kant does the superiority of the moral faculty to the aesthetic one, even though the moral has in common with the appetitive one the motivation of desire. This is the fifth passage, most of which you’ll find in the appendix:

柯勒律治说，美既与低于它的令人愉悦的事物区分开来，又与高于它的善事物区分开来：因为两者都必然与某种利益相关：两者都作用于意志，并激发人们对所思考的图像或想法的实际存在的渴望，而美的感觉则仅仅存在于沉思或直觉之中，无论它是虚构的阿波罗还是真实的安提诺乌斯。
The beautiful [says Coleridge] is at once distinguished both from the agreeable, which is beneath it, and from the good, which is above it: for both these necessarily have an interest attached to them: both act on the will, and excite a desire for the actual existence of the image or idea contemplated, while the sense of beauty rests gratified in the mere contemplation or intuition regardless whether it be a fictitious Apollo or a real Antinous.

美的判断并不取决于对象的实际存在（它可以在我们智慧的范畴内自由游走），因此，这表明这种满足感并非源于“兴趣”或欲望。我们欣赏它，并非将其视为一种占有物，而是将其视为一种形式。

The judgment of beauty does not depend on the actual existence of the object for its satisfaction (it could be ranging freely within the zodiac of our wit), hence purports to show that the nature of this satisfaction does not arise from “interest,” or desire. We admire it not as a possession but as a form.

奥斯卡·王尔德——这位一向妙语连珠、以看似非传统的方式创造了大量优秀文学理论的作家，或许比历史上任何一位文学思想家都多——在构成《道林·格雷的画像》 “序言”的一系列格言中写道：“一切艺术都是毫无用处的。”我希望，在阅读了前面的段落并理解了这些解释之后，您能立刻明白王尔德所说的“一切艺术都是毫无用处的”是什么意思。他借用了功利主义传统中一个带有贬义的词语——天哪，竟然有什么东西是无用的！——并指出艺术的无用之处是独一无二的；它不诉诸于任何纯粹的欲望或崇高的理性，因此我们对它没有任何工具性用途。我们不必对它拥有“利益”——就像拥有公司股份那样。我们不需要对它拥有利益才能欣赏它。我们可以与自身的主观欲望、需求、喜好和厌恶保持距离，从而以一种愉快且富有建设性的方式与艺术共存，这对我们自身和艺术作品都有益处。因为如果我们认识到世间存在着一些事物，它们本身具有内在价值和重要性，我们称之为美，但它们并非我们渴望或想要摒弃之物，那么我们就能在自身中发现一种超脱于私利的能力，同时也能让艺术作品摆脱我们对其的预设。由此，我们便能在自身中发现一种特质——自由，而自由正是许多价值体系的基石。

Oscar Wilde—ever the wag and a person who generated more good literary theory in ways that didn’t seem like literary theory at all, perhaps, than anyone else in the entire history of thinking about the subject—says in the series of aphorisms that make up his “Preface” to The Picture of Dorian Gray, “All art is quite useless.” I hope that after reading these prior passages and enduring the explication of them, you can immediately see what Wilde means in saying all art is quite useless. He’s appropriating a term of disgust in the utilitarian tradition—heaven forbid that anything might be useless!—and pointing out that art is uniquely useless; it appeals to no merely appetitive or exaltedly rational form of subjective interest, hence we have no instrumental use for it. We don’t have to have an “interest” in it—in the sense of owning part of a company. We don’t need to have an interest in it in order to appreciate it. We can distance ourselves from our subjective wants and needs and likes and dislikes, and we can coexist with art in a happy and constructive way that is good both for us and for the work of art, because if we recognize that there are things in the world that have intrinsic value and importance and what we call beauty, and yet are not the things that we covet or wish to banish, we recognize in ourselves the capacity for disinterestedness and at the same time we allow the work of art to be free from our designs on it. We thereby recognize in ourselves an attribute, freedom, that is the cornerstone of many systems of value.

意识到我们无需对事物抱有工具性的利益才能认识到它们的自足性和价值，这向我们揭示了关于自身的一些至关重要的东西。王尔德的观点，以及我认为在他之前的康德的观点，对于我们认识到自身作为独立道德主体的价值至关重要。无利害性意味着认识到，自由不仅对我而言是可能的，对那些我对其没有工具性利益的事物而言也是可能的。因此，这种关于艺术和人类判断的观点所隐含的是——这并非我们第一次在这些讲座中提及这一点，也不会是最后一次——它是一种认识到，除了我们所有其他属性（其中一些非常出色）之外，我们也是自由的、自主的。这种对自身自由的发现，以及由此引申出的其他事物摆脱我们欲望的自由，赋予了形式主义传统以道德完整性；你将会看到，它需要这种辩护来抵御我们将在必要时逐一提出的无数反对意见。许多针对形式本身具有内在价值的辩护的指责——例如十九世纪末沃尔特·佩特宣称“为艺术而艺术”的价值——源于未能或愤怒地拒绝区分无私和冷漠。

To realize that we don’t have to take an instrumental interest in things in order to recognize that they are self-sufficient and valuable shows us something crucially important about ourselves. Wilde’s suggestion, but I think also Kant’s suggestion before him, is important for our recognition of our own value as independent moral agents. Disinterestedness entails the realization that freedom is possible not just for me but for those things in which I have no instrumental interest. What’s implicit then in this view of art and of human judgment is that once again—and this is not the first time we’ve brought this up in these lectures, nor will it be the last—it’s a way of recognizing that in addition to all our other attributes, some of them wonderful, we are also free, autonomous. This discovery of our freedom, and by implication the freedom of other things from our desires, is what lends moral integrity to the formalist tradition; and you’ll see that it needs this defense to ward off the countless objections that we’ll be taking up in turn as need arises. Many of the charges against defenses of form as intrinsically valuable—as when Walter Pater at the end of the nineteenth century proclaimed the value of “art for art’s sake”—arise from the failure or the angry refusal to distinguish between disinterestedness and indifference.

约翰·克罗·兰索姆从未就读于耶鲁大学，但他却是自称为“新批评家”这一学派的创始人或早期成员之一。他出版了一本名为《新批评》的书，该术语便源于此书。您或许已经注意到，在温萨特的《意图谬误》一文中，有一个脚注提到了乔尔·斯平加恩，他于1924年撰写了一篇名为《新批评》的文章。斯平加恩的文章主题与“新批评”并无关联。他所指的只是“新近出现的批评”，虽然从某种意义上说，兰索姆在撰写其著作时也表达了类似的观点，但这个标签很快就与某种特定的观点联系起来。此外，自“新批评家”时代以来，罗兰·巴特及其一些同时代人的作品——例如我提到的普莱、让·斯塔罗宾斯基等人——在法国媒体上被称为《新批评》，但这个标签也与我们当前的讨论主题无关。

John Crowe Ransom, who was never at Yale but is nevertheless one of the founders or first members of a self-identified school of figures who called themselves the New Critics, published a book called The New Criticism, where the term comes from. You may have noticed that in Wimsatt’s “Intentional Fallacy” there is a footnote to a Joel Spingarn, who wrote an essay called “The New Criticism” in 1924. Spingarn’s topic has nothing to do with the New Criticism. He just means criticism that is recent, and while in a sense that’s what Ransom meant too on the occasion of writing his book, the label soon attached itself to a particular viewpoint. Also, since the time of the New Critics, the work of Roland Barthes and some of his contemporaries—Poulet, whom I mentioned, Jean Starobinski, and others—was called in the French press La Nouvelle Critique, but that label too is not to be confused with our present topic.

新批评家，有时也被称为“美国新批评家”，是一个学派——我特意使用这个词，因为他们乐于将自己定义为一个群体——他们完善了我们一直在追溯的艺术作品的独立地位这一理念——兰索姆称之为“离散的本体论对象”——以及欣赏其所有复杂性的独立性的方法。

The New Critics, the “American New Critics” as they are sometimes identified, were a school—and I use that term advisedly because they willingly identified themselves as a group—who refined upon the idea we’ve been tracing of the independent status of the work of art—Ransom calls it a “discrete ontological object”—and the means whereby it can be appreciated as independent in all of its complexity.

我们将首先阅读温萨特和比尔兹利的《意图谬误》，以此来初步了解这一学派的思想。我稍后会详细讲解；但在此，我们先回顾一下附录中兰塞姆的两段文字。这两段文字将你在阅读《意图谬误》时遇到的思维方式与我一直试图描述的传统联系起来。第一段文字现在对你来说应该非常清晰，因为它只是对我之前引用的康德和柯勒律治的段落的转述：“兰塞姆说，被称为美的体验超越了强大的伦理意志，正如它超越了动物的激情一样……事实上，这两者既相互竞争又相互协调。”换句话说，伦理意志和动物的激情之间的共同之处在于，它们都根植于利益。这正是肯尼斯·克拉克爵士提出的“nude”（最好发音为“nyewd”）一词的意义所在。对于裸体的人而言，无论从欲望还是道德理性的角度来看，“裸体”一词作为常用术语，从康德所谓的“知性”和“理性”的角度来看都完全恰当；但如果我们相信存在另一个范畴——审美，由一种被称为“判断力”的独立能力来看待，那么我们就需要另一个词来描述我们所观察的对象。像菲利普·珀尔斯坦和卢西安·弗洛伊德这样的现代人体画家会强烈反对这种观点，他们坚持认为任何视觉感知中都存在欲望和厌恶，但他们的观点恰恰有助于我们论证自己的观点。当我们欣赏一幅传统的裸体画作时，我们不会说“哦，那是一个裸体”，而是会说“那是一个裸体”，这种本能的用词选择印证了我们所有人潜意识里都承认审美判断必然与欲望判断和道德判断有所不同。

Our first foray into the thinking of this school will be our reading of Wimsatt and Beardsley’s “The Intentional Fallacy,” which I’ll get to in a minute; but, simply as a reprise, take a look at the two passages from Ransom that complete what’s in the appendix. They provide a link between the sort of thinking you’ve encountered in reading “The Intentional Fallacy” and the tradition that I’ve been trying to describe. The first of these ought to be completely transparent to you now because it is simply a paraphrase of the passages I have given you from Kant and Coleridge: “The experience [says Ransom] called beauty is beyond the powerful ethical will precisely as it is beyond the animal passion … and indeed these last two are competitive and coordinate.” In other words, what they have in common with each other, ethical will and animal passion, is that they’re both grounded in interest. That’s the point of Sir Kenneth Clark’s word, “nude,” which is best pronounced “nyewd.” For the naked human being, as viewed both by the appetite and by moral reason, the expression “naked body” is just fine as a common term from the standpoint both of what Kant calls “the understanding” and from what he calls “the reason”; but if we do believe there is another category, the aesthetic, viewed by an independent faculty called “the judgment,” we need another word for what we’re looking at. Modern painters of the body, like Philip Pearlstein and Lucian Freud, would strongly disagree, insisting on the presence of appetite and disgust in any visual perception as they do, but in a way that helps us to our point. When we’re looking at a traditional painting of a naked body, we don’t say, “Oh, that’s a naked body.” We say, “That’s a nyewd,” and that instinctive choice of terms bears out the semiconscious way in which all of us acknowledge that aesthetic judgment must somehow differ from appetitive and moral judgments.

然而，许多有思想的人认为这种区分毫无意义。事实上，二十世纪的主流观点是，根本不存在所谓的“无私”，无论我们注视什么，我们都对其感兴趣，而康德所说的这种冷静或无私的沉思，正是二十世纪早期批评家I.A. Richards所说的“幻影般的审美状态”。在接下来的讲座中，我们将更多地赞同Richards的观点。不过，为了恰当地阐述康德的崇高思想，我们不妨略作提及：的确，在某种程度上，我们突然发现自己，并非出于本意，也并非仅仅是某种文化暴政的受害者（比如，“这是《蒙娜丽莎》，我最好在她面前表现得欣喜若狂”），而是站在某物面前，双手紧握，微微歪着头，感受到某种与我们平常观看事物时截然不同的情绪。这其实也是一种直觉式的承认：尽管定义或捍卫无私可能十分困难，但在某些特定的体验时刻，我们确实会感受到类似的心境。比如说，我们欣赏某件艺术作品或某处风景时，感受与欣赏其他事物时截然不同。或许我们并不清楚个中缘由。或许我们怀疑这种差异是否如康德所坚持的那样绝对。然而，我们确实倾向于拥有这种感受，也没有理由否认它的存在。至少，这有助于我们理解我所描述的传统存在的意义。

And yet a lot of thoughtful people think this distinction is nonsense. The predominant view in the twentieth century has, in fact, been that there’s no such thing as disinterestedness, that whatever we are looking at we have an interest in, and that this Kantian moment of dispassionate or disinterested contemplation is what the early twentieth-century critic I. A. Richards called a “phantom aesthetic state.” In the lectures that follow, we’ll spend more time agreeing with Richards than not. Just to do justice in passing to Kant’s noble idea, however: there is a certain sense, is there not, in which we suddenly find ourselves, without meaning to and without being merely the victims of any sort of cultural tyranny (this is the “Mona Lisa,” I’d better look rapturous in front of it), standing in front of something, clasping our hands, tilting our head, and feeling somehow or another different from the way we feel when we typically look at things. And that, too, is an intuitive way of admitting that however difficult it may be to define or defend disinterestedness, something like that state of mind does seem to occur at certain moments of experience. We just feel different looking at a certain work of art or a certain landscape, let’s say, than we feel looking at other sorts of things. Maybe we don’t know why. Maybe we doubt that the difference is absolute in the way that Kant wants to insist it is. Nevertheless, in tendency we have feelings of this kind and there is no reason not to acknowledge them. At least it helps us understand why the tradition I have sketched in exists.

现在让我们来看看温萨特。他立刻抨击了他所谓的“浪漫主义文学观”。他所说的“浪漫主义”是什么意思呢？它指的是这样一种态度：认为“诗”（新批评派用这个词来指代“文学作品”）是某种激情或深刻才华的表达，最终融入某种形式，但重要的是表达本身。顺便一提，温萨特和伽达默尔在这一点上是相同的，因为伽达默尔也反对浪漫主义以作者为中心的观点。伽达默尔感兴趣的是他所谓的“主题”，即“事物本身”（die Sache）。他感兴趣的不是你如何表达这一本质内容，也不是我如何表达。他感兴趣的是读者如何理解文本所传达的意义，正如我所说，尽管温萨特和伽达默尔的研究方向截然不同，但他们在这一点上确实有共同之处。

Let us turn now to Wimsatt. Immediately he attacks what he calls “the romantic understanding of literature.” What does he mean by “romantic”? It’s the attitude that supposes a “poem” (the New Critics used this term to mean “work of literature”) to be an expression of some passion or profound genius working its way into a form, but that the important thing is the expression. This much, by the way, Wimsatt has in common with Gadamer, because Gadamer too disapproves of the author focus of romanticism. Gadamer is interested in what he calls the subject matter, die Sache. He’s not interested in your expression of that essential content or my expression of it. He’s interested in the way a reader can come to terms with a meaning conveyed by a text, and that much, as I say, despite the profoundly different nature of their projects, Wimsatt and Gadamer do have in common.

因此，诗歌并非一种表达方式，而是一个拥有自足意义的独立个体。如果这种意义对于细心的读者而言并非显而易见，那么我们便不会评判这首诗是否成功。这正是评价的意义所在。一首诗的成败取决于意义的实现，而非取决于我们查阅档案，探寻作者在信件、朋友或报社的言论。如果诗歌本身的意义不够清晰，我们就将其评判为失败之作。我们不会去探究作者的意图。如果我们尊重诗歌的自主性，就没有理由去诉诸作者的意图。

So a poem is not an expression but an independent object with a self-contained meaning, and if this meaning is not self-evident to the attentive reader, then we don’t judge the poem a success. This is where evaluation comes in. The success or failure of a poem depends on the realization of meaning. It doesn’t depend on our going to the archive, finding out what the author said in his letters about it, or what he told his friends, or what he told the newspapers. If the meaning is not clear in the poem itself, we judge it a failure. We don’t refer to an authorial intention. We have no reason to appeal to one if we respect the autonomy of the poem.

因此（811）：“作者的意图或设计既不可行也不可取，不能作为评判文学作品成功与否的标准。”由此可见，即使是短诗，即使是充满激情的抒情诗，也不应诉诸作者。即使是个人抒情诗，也应以戏剧化的方式去理解，如同理解勃朗宁或T·S·艾略特的戏剧独白一般。在温萨特看来，任何诗歌的叙述者都具有某种性格、某种观点和某种论点，而我们对这一性格如何被塑造的理解，必须从诗歌本身出发，而非通过对作者的传记式描述来强化，仿佛作者就站在诗歌的背后。

Hence (811): “[T]he design or intention of the author is neither available nor desirable as a standard for judging the success of a work of literary art.” It follows from this that even a short poem, even a short lyric poem passionately expressed, doesn’t warrant an appeal to the author. Even a personal lyric should be understood dramatically, as though the poem were one of Browning’s or T. S. Eliot’s dramatic monologues. The speaker of any poem on Wimsatt’s view is a speaker endowed with a certain character, a certain viewpoint, a certain argument to be put forward, and our sense of the way this character is elaborated has to be derived from the poem itself and not reinforced by biographical reference to the author, standing somewhere behind the poem.

那么，我们为什么要关注“诗”呢？请注意，我们从未听说过“文学”，甚至从未听说过“诗”。这类分析的对象是诗。正如约翰·邓恩所说，诗是一个精心构建的小世界。它是一个微观世界，一种提炼或精髓。换句话说，它是一个范例，展现了文学如何被理解为一种世界建构——它并非是对事物现状的再现，而是对事物应有状态的再现。亚里士多德所说的“事物应有状态”在此并非一定指理想状态，而仅仅是指形式上的、有组织的，以及最重要的，具有连贯性且自洽自足的。正因如此，诗歌，尤其是抒情诗，在新批评的文学论述形式中占据了特殊的地位。在新批评派看来，所有文学作品都隐含着“诗”的概念，但抒情诗才是分析的重点，唯有抒情诗才能使这一更广泛的论断显得合情合理，从而涵盖所有可能同时被考虑的内容。浪漫主义中“诗歌”一词的缺失也意义重大。“诗歌”（而非“诗”）指的是自然流露之物，是强烈情感的自发涌现。新批评派对这种自发涌现的强烈情感并不感兴趣。温萨特曾开玩笑说，可以像A.E.豪斯曼建议的那样，喝上一品脱啤酒，然后散散步。新批评对由此可能产生的自发涌现毫无兴趣。

So why should we focus on the “poem”? Notice that we never hear about “literature.” We never even hear about “poetry.” The object of attention for an analysis of this kind is the poem. The poem is, as John Donne puts it, a little world made cunningly. It’s a microcosm, a distillation or quintessence. It is a model, in other words, for the way in which literature can be understood as world-making—a representation, again, not of things as they are but of things as they should be. Aristotle’s “as they should be” is not in this case necessarily an ideal, but rather simply that which is formal, that which is organized, and above all that which has a coherence and makes sense self-sufficiently and within itself. That’s why the poem, the lyric poem, is privileged among the forms of literary discourse in the New Criticism. All literature for the New Critics is by implication a “poem,” but the actual lyric poem is the privileged site of analysis whereby this broader statement can be made to seem reasonably to account for everything that can be held in mind at once. The absence of the Romantic word “poetry” is also significant. “Poetry,” as opposed to “the poem,” is that which just spills out. It’s the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings. The New Criticism isn’t interested in spontaneous overflows of powerful feelings. Wimsatt has his little joke about drinking a pint of beer and taking a walk, as A. E. Housman recommended. The New Criticism just isn’t interested in the spontaneous overflow that might result from that.

总之，温萨特接着论证说，如果我们从诗歌本身寻找意义的证据，就应该记住，证据分为三种，重要性依次递减至零。对诗歌意义影响最大的是“语言”——也就是说，我们所有人都能共享的、属于公共领域的词汇，我们可以完全理解这些词汇（必要时可以借助一本好的词典），从而准确理解诗歌的含义。一个词——当然，这正是你在高中课堂上长时间保持专注的原因——通常有五六个含义。新批评乐于展示这五六个含义是如何与诗歌的意义产生某种联系的。所有这些都被认为是完全合法的证据，可以用来构建对诗歌的解读。而完全无关紧要的，恰恰是我之前提到的那种“证据”：作者在写给朋友的信、写给报纸的文章等等中对诗歌的描述。如果这些声明没有反映在诗歌中，或者——更有可能的是——显然与诗歌作为连贯的表达的成功或失败没有任何关系，那么它们就无法帮助解释诗歌。

In any case, Wimsatt goes on to argue that if we take our evidence of meaning from the poem itself, we should remember that there are three kinds of evidence, in order of importance descending to nil. What has the most bearing on what a poem means is “language”—that is to say, words in the public domain that all of us share and that we can understand fully (with recourse to a good dictionary if necessary) in order to come to terms with the exact meaning of the poem. A certain word—this is, of course, what kept you alert in your high school classes for so long—typically has five or six meanings. The New Criticism delights in showing how all five or six of those meanings do have some bearing on the meaning of the poem. That’s all considered entirely legitimate evidence, which one uses to build up the interpretation of the poem. What is not relevant at all, at the other end of the scale, is the “evidence” I’ve mentioned already: what the author said about the poem in letters to friends, to newspapers, and so on. If such pronouncements aren’t reflected in the poem or—what is more likely—clearly have no bearing on its success or failure as a coherent utterance, they cannot help with interpretation.

不过，温萨特也承认，在这两者之间还存在着相当复杂的第三类证据，它与语言有关，因此在某种程度上是合理的，但也与作者的个人特质有关——例如，这位作者使用语言的方式，比如使用某些小圈子词汇，甚至对某些词语存在个人理解上的误解。读惠特曼的作品时，你必须明白他所说的“同志”是什么意思。这和我们通常所说的“同志”或“同志情谊”并不完全相同。这个词本身就带有丰富的内涵——温萨特或许也会承认——如果我们想要理解惠特曼的意图，就必须考虑到这些内涵。这一点非常棘手，因为它确实涉及到作者自身的因素。 Wimsatt 在本文的剩余部分讨论了证据类型之间模糊的界限：第二种证据类型不适用，第三种证据类型可能适用，但必须谨慎处理。

At this point, though, Wimsatt acknowledges that there’s a rather messy third category of evidence in between that has to do with language, and is therefore legitimate to a point, but that also has to do with the author’s idiosyncrasies—the way that particular author used language, for example, by sharing certain coterie words or even indulging a private misunderstanding of certain words. You’ve got to know when you’re reading Whitman what he means by “camerado.” It’s not exactly what the rest of us typically mean when we speak of comrades or comradeship. The word is loaded in ways that—Wimsatt would probably acknowledge—need to be taken into account if we’re going to understand what Whitman is up to. Now this is very tricky because it certainly does bring the author into play. Wimsatt spends the rest of this essay talking about the murky boundaries between types of evidence: type of evidence number two, which is out of play, and type of evidence number three, which may be in play but has to be dealt with in a gingerly way.

但我最感兴趣的是这条关于语言独特性（取决于特定作者的用法）的论证中引出的一个脚注。这条脚注（814-815n）可以说是我们整个课程中最具颠覆性和反直觉性的论断，也无疑是新批评领域中最具震撼力的论断：“诗歌创作之后，词语的历史可能会赋予其新的意义，如果这些意义与最初的模式相关，就不应因对创作意图的顾虑而被排除在外。” 这真是大胆的论断。创作者“举起了他的塑料手臂”——大家都知道阿肯赛德指的并非聚合物，但如今我们都对赛博格趋之若鹜，对塑料的性能也格外重视。某种程度上，暗示他拥有假肢既是对创作者的致敬，也是对“世界至高精神”存在于永恒瞬间这一事实的认可。他不受历史的束缚。这位“神灵”早在十八世纪就已预知，塑料终有一天会指代聚合物。因此，如果世界的创造者选择举起他的假肢，那只不过是让我们理解在永恒瞬间拥有全能全知的感受。简而言之，如果你认真对待温萨特的脚注，它便提供了一种合情合理的方式，既不以讽刺的方式削弱阿肯赛德的诗句，又能强化其含义，并赋予其原本不具备的形式上的丰富性。

But I’m most interested in a footnote that arises from this argument about the idiosyncratic nature of language as a particular author may use it. This footnote (814–815n), is just about as devastating and counterintuitive a pronouncement as you’ll find anywhere in our entire course, and certainly the most earth-shattering pronouncement that anybody could ever possibly have made within the New Criticism: “And the history of words after a poem is written may contribute meanings which if relevant to the original pattern should not be ruled out by a scruple about intention.” Now that is bold. The creator “raised his plastic arm”—everybody knows Akenside didn’t mean polymers, but now we’re all into cyborgs and we take the capabilities of plastics very seriously. In a way, the implication that he has a prosthetic limb is a tribute to the creator and also an acknowledgment of the fact that the “Sovereign spirit of the world” lives in the Eternal Moment. He’s not subject to history. This “spirit” knew in the eighteenth century that someday plastic would mean polymer. Therefore, if the creator of the world chooses to raise his prosthetic limb, that is simply a way of making us understand what it is like to be omnipotent and omniscient in the Eternal Moment. In short, if you take Wimsatt’s footnote seriously, it gives you a legitimate way not to undermine Akenside’s line ironically but to reinforce its meaning and to give it a formal richness that it would not otherwise have.

下一讲我将以叶芝1935年创作的诗作《青金石》开篇。诗中他写道，那些重建被摧毁之物的人总是“快乐的”。如果我们探究其意图，叶芝指的并非我们日常意义上的“快乐”。他使用的是尼采《快乐的科学》中德语单词“fr hlich ”的英文译名。叶芝是一位敏锐而细致的尼采读者，事实上，他在《青金石》中正是对尼采在该书中论述的进一步阐释。下一讲伊始，我们将以刚才分析“塑料”一词的方式来分析“快乐的”一词，然后探讨克林斯·布鲁克斯的一篇文章，并结合新批评及其先驱的其他方面进行分析。

I’ll begin the next lecture by talking about a poem of Yeats called “Lapis Lazuli,” written in 1935, in which he says that people who build up things that have been destroyed are always “gay.” If we invoke intention, Yeats doesn’t mean that they’re always gay in our colloquial sense. He is using the English translation of the German word frhlich from Nietzsche’s The Gay Science. Yeats is an astute and careful reader of Nietzsche, and in fact he is elaborating in “Lapis Lazuli” on what Nietzsche says in that book. At the beginning of the next lecture we will do the same thing with the word “gay” that we’ve just done with the word “plastic,” then consider an essay by Cleanth Brooks alongside other aspects of the New Criticism and its antecedents.

 

 

第六章

CHAPTER 6

新批评及其他西方形式主义
The New Criticism and Other Western Formalisms

阅读材料：

Readings:

Richards, IA “文学批评原则”。载于《批评传统》，第 764-773 页。

Richards, I. A. “Principles of Literary Criticism.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 764–773.

埃姆普森，威廉。《七种歧义》。纽约：新方向出版社，1966 年，第 16-19 页。

Empson, William. Seven Types of Ambiguity. New York: New Directions Publishing, 1966, pp. 16–19.

Brooks, Cleanth. “反讽作为结构原则。”载于《批判传统》，第 799-806 页。

Brooks, Cleanth. “Irony as a Principle of Structure.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 799–806.

在上一讲中，我开始举例说明，如果认真对待温萨特（Wimsatt）《意图谬误》（The Intentional Fallacy）中那条非同寻常的脚注，将会发生什么。温萨特在脚注中写道：“一首诗创作之后词语的历史很可能与诗歌的整体结构相关，不应仅仅因为对意图的顾虑而忽略它。” 这番话听起来确实令人震惊，不仅对那些对意图有所顾虑的人，也对那些仅仅想知道什么才算证据的人而言。试想一下，一位语言学家面对这样的观点：在理解一首诗的意义时，某个特定历史时期词语的含义可以被补充甚至推翻。为了让这条脚注显得更有说服力，我又回到了那位伟大的创造者举起他塑料手臂的场景，并提出，或许我们可以建设性地丰富阿肯赛德（Akenside）的诗意，承认“塑料”（plastic）一词的现代、时代错置的含义与诗歌的意义相关。

In the last lecture, I started giving examples of what might happen if one takes seriously that extraordinary footnote in Wimsatt’s “The Intentional Fallacy,” where he says “the history of words after a poem was composed may well be relevant to the overall structure of the poem and should not be avoided owing simply to a scruple about intention.” That should be truly shocking to hear, not just for anyone with a scruple about intention, but for anyone simply wondering what counts as evidence. Just imagine a philologist being confronted with the idea that the meaning of words at a certain historical moment can be augmented or even overridden in understanding the meaning of a poem. So to make the footnote seem just a little more plausible, I went back to the great creator raising his plastic arm and suggested that after all one might constructively complicate Akenside’s meaning by conceding that the modern, anachronistic meaning of “plastic” would be relevant to the sense of the poem.

这里还有一个更贴近现实的例子，出自叶芝1935年的诗作《青金石》。这首诗以“我听说歇斯底里的女人说/她们厌倦了调色板和琴弓，/厌倦了那些总是同性恋的诗人”开头。<sup> 1</sup>即将到来的战争的阴云开始聚集。许多人说：“够了，别再搞这种软弱无力的文化了。我们需要思考一些重要的事情，特别是政治和社会秩序。”叶芝不同意，他用一种厌女的廉价攻击来坚持认为，艺术仍然扮演着重要的角色——事实上，即使在这样的时代，艺术也确实可能继续发挥作用。所以他“厌倦”了所有人说他们不想谈论绘画、音乐，或者那些“总是同性恋”的诗人。

Here’s another example a little closer to home from Yeats’s “Lapis Lazuli” of 1935. It’s a poem that begins, “I have heard that hysterical women say / they are sick of the palette and fiddle-bow, / of poets that are always gay.”1 The storm clouds of the coming war are beginning to gather. A lot of people are saying, “Enough of this effete culture. We need to think about important things, particularly about politics and the social order.” Yeats disagreed, insisting with the help of a misogynistic cheap shot that there is a continuing role for art—as indeed after all there may well be, even in such times. So he’s “sick of” everybody saying they don’t want to talk about painting, about music, or about poets who are “always gay.”

这首诗中出现了一块石头，一块雕刻过的中国青金石，上面有一个瑕疵，这个瑕疵就像一条“水道”，让人联想到一位僧侣朝圣者沿着它向上攀登，最终获得启迪。随着诗歌的展开，叶芝谈到了文明的崩塌：万物皆会衰落，但随后又可以重建。“万物皆会衰落，又会被重建/而那些重建它们的人是快乐的。” 正如我上次所说，毋庸置疑，叶芝并没有意识到我们可能会倾向于赋予“快乐”一词的时代错置含义。叶芝想到的是尼采的“ fröhlich ”一词，在上下文中，你可以将其翻译为“充满活力的喜悦”。叶芝借用了尼采著作《快乐的科学》的译名。

The poem involves a stone, a piece of carved Chinese lapis lazuli that has a flaw in it, a flaw that’s like a “water-course,” where one can imagine a monastic pilgrim climbing upward toward enlightenment. As the poem goes on, Yeats talks about the way civilizations crumble: all things fall, but then it’s possible to build them back up. “All things fall and are built again / and those that build them again are gay.” As I said last time, needless to say Yeats was not aware of the anachronistic meaning of “gay” that we may be tempted to bring to bear. Yeats is thinking of Nietzsche’s word fröhlich, which in context you might translate as “energetically joyous.” Yeats borrows that word from the translated title of a book by Nietzsche, The Gay Science.

这当然很好，但如果你是一位酷儿理论家，或者你对强调酷儿性在我们文学传统中的重要性感兴趣，你很可能会认为这种时代错置的意义丰富了这首诗：那些重建文明的人不仅作为创造者充满活力和喜悦，他们也是公开的或显而易见的同性恋者。（也许这使得关于歇斯底里女性的讨论也变得意义非凡。）这种基于文本的论断或许会引起语文学家的反感，也或许不会，但它确实为这首诗增添了一种额外的连贯性。至少，它或许可以被称作埃德·赫希（Ed Hirsch）所说的“意义”，你或许还记得吧。

Well and good, but if you were a queer theorist or if you were interested in making a strong claim for the importance of queerness in our literary tradition, you would be very tempted to say that the anachronistic meaning enriches the poem: those who build civilizations again are not just energetically joyous as creators, they are also openly or discoverably gay. (Maybe that makes even the chatter about hysterical women significant.) This text-based claim may or may not raise the hackles of the philologists, but it does lend a supplementary coherence to the poem. At least it might pass as what E. D. Hirsch, you’ll remember, calls “significance.”

在《拖车托尼》的第二行，我们得知“我住在一个黄色的小车库里”。当然，正如克林斯·布鲁克斯所说， “黄色”一词的本义仅仅是车库被漆成了黄色。而其引申义——作者无疑没有意识到这一点，毕竟这是一本写给幼儿的书——是带有贬义的懦弱暗示，或许也带有贬义的亚洲人暗示。也许温柔的托尼其实是个胆小的亚洲人。好吧，我们说，这和文本本身无关；但假设它真的有关呢？我们完全可以把作者拉到沙发上，问他为什么车库是黄色的而不是其他颜色。再一次，一个几乎在所有方面都无关紧要的暗示，却能让读者浮想联翩，无论好坏。

In the second line of Tony the Tow Truck, we learn that “I live in a little yellow garage.” Now of course, as Cleanth Brooks would put it, the denotation of the word “yellow” is just that the garage is painted a certain color. The connotation, which undoubtedly the author had no notion of—this is a book for toddlers—is the derogatory imputation of cowardice, possibly also the derogatory imputation of being Asian. Maybe the gentle Tony is really a cowardly Asian. Well, fine, but this has nothing to do with the text, we say; yet suppose it did. We could always put the author on the couch and ask why the garage is yellow and not some other color. Once again an implication that’s irrelevant on nearly all counts can set the reader’s mind racing, for better or worse.

所以，您现在应该明白温萨特脚注的非凡意义了。我们的例子也表明，或许在今天的讨论之前，统一性这一概念对新批评家来说有多么重要（我曾用连贯性和复杂性来指代这一概念）。本次讲座的所有内容都将围绕统一性的评价规范展开，康德称之为目的性多面体的完整性，即判断认为美的要素。因此，即使一个词的内涵在语文学上是不正确的，只要它有助于文学文本的统一性，有助于这种统一性的复杂构建，那么这个内涵就是有价值的，应该被运用。然而，如果这种语文学上的错误仅仅是伽达默尔所说的“不良偏见”——某个读者个人投入的、在文本解读中根本无法发挥作用的方面——那么就应该将其排除在外。因此，评判标准是：内涵必须与我们作为批评家试图在文本中实现的统一形式相关。统一性标准支配着阐释决策，不仅适用于我们基于温萨特脚注所做的半戏谑式解读，也适用于那些可能具有一定边缘合理性的解读。

So you see the extraordinary implications of Wimsatt’s footnote. Our examples also show, perhaps in advance of today’s discussion, how important the notion of unity is to the New Critics (a notion entailed in such terms I’ve used as coherence and complexity). Everything we have to say in this lecture will concern the evaluative norm of unity, which Kant would call the integrity of a purposive manifold that the judgment deems beautiful. Thus the connotation of a word is valuable and ought to be invoked even though it’s philologically incorrect if it contributes to the unity, the complex building up of the unity, of the literary text. If, however, the philological transgression is merely what Gadamer would call a “bad prejudice”—some aspect of a particular reader’s private investment that nothing could possibly be done with in interpreting the text—then it should be thrown out of play. So the criterion is this: the connotation must be relevant to the unified form that we as critics are trying to realize in the text. The criterion of unity is what governs interpretive decisions, not just for the sorts of semifacetious readings we can do on the strength of Wimsatt’s footnote but also for readings that may have some marginal plausibility.

现在，我们来谈谈新批评的直接渊源。首先，20世纪30年代和40年代的学术界见证了一套品味标准的兴起，这套标准主要由伟大的现代主义作家，特别是T·S·艾略特所引入。例如，布鲁克斯似乎对约翰·邓恩有着一种近乎痴迷的喜爱。这种喜爱源于艾略特的论文《玄学派诗人》，而这篇论文本身又是一篇评论文章，评论的是邓恩的一部诗集，这部诗集一夜之间让邓恩在许多读者心中成为了英国传统诗歌的核心人物。在《玄学派诗人》中，艾略特的一些观点对新批评产生了深远的影响。他指出：“在我们这个时代——我们所处的世界如此复杂——诗歌必然是晦涩难懂的。”他还认为，诗歌必须调和各种截然不同的体验：阅读斯宾诺莎、烹饪的气味、打字机的声音等等。所有这些都需要像约翰·邓恩或约翰·赫伯特的诗歌那样，以意象的形式巧妙地融合在一起。这种复杂性模式对于现代文学和文学批评都至关重要。其他现代主义者，如詹姆斯·乔伊斯，也对艺术作品独立统一性的理念做出了贡献。在《青年艺术家画像》中，斯蒂芬在论述形式、阿奎那以及其他相关内容时指出，艺术作品与其创作者是分离的，因为创作者会从中抽身而出，如同那句著名的谚语所说，独自修指甲。你或许还记得，温萨特曾论证——他可能正是受到了乔伊斯这段话的启发——艺术作品在诞生之初就与作者“分离”。它的脐带被剪断，它独自游荡于世，成为一个独立的个体。

Now a word or two about the immediate antecedents of the New Criticism. In the first place, the 1930s and 1940s in the academic world bear witness to the rise of a canon of taste largely introduced by the great modernist writers, particularly by T. S. Eliot. You may notice that Brooks, for example, has a kind of Donne obsession. He gets that from Eliot’s essay “The Metaphysical Poets,” which in turn is a review essay of a volume of Donne’s poems that made Donne overnight, for a great many readers, the central poet in the English tradition. In “The Metaphysical Poets,” Eliot makes several remarks that had far-reaching consequences for the New Criticism. He says, “Poetry in our own time—such is the complexity of the world we live in—must be difficult.” He says also that poetry has to reconcile all sorts of disparate experience: reading Spinoza, the smell of cooking, the sound of the typewriter. All of this needs to be yoked together in the imagery of a good poem, as is done in a poem by Donne or Herbert, and this model of complexity is what matters both for modern literature and for literary criticism. Other modernists like James Joyce also contribute to this idea of the independent unity of the work of art. In The Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man, Stephen in his disquisition on form and Aquinas and all the rest of it argues that the work of art is cut off from its creator because its creator withdraws from it and sits paring his fingernails, in the famous expression. You remember that Wimsatt argues—probably thinking of that passage in Joyce—that the work of art is “cut off” from its author at birth. Its umbilical cord is removed and it roams the world on its own, a unity unto itself.

因此，现代主义是一个来源，但我们也需要考虑学术批评的现状。20世纪30年代，兰索姆在其论战宣言《新批评》和《世界之躯》中，点出了两个主要的对手：首先是老派的语文学，他们始终坚持“可塑性”的含义与18世纪相同。语文学家占据了教授中的绝大多数。这是文学研究走向成熟的黄金时代。标准版本不断涌现。伟大的学术期刊正处于起步阶段，权威地汇集着知识的贡献。文学传统的基本事实仍在确立之中，尽管几乎所有重要的内容都已积累完毕，这也是一些新一代学者感到不安的原因之一。十九世纪末二十世纪初语言学的繁荣为我们创造了如今我们使用和习以为常的档案，但新批评家们看到了某种程度的僵化，并认为在知识积累的过程中，解释的挑战已被遗忘。

Modernism is a source, then, but we need also to consider the state of academic criticism. In the 1930s, Ransom, in his polemical manifestos The New Criticism and The World’s Body, singled out two main adversaries: first there was old-fashioned philology, which would always insist that “plastic” means what it meant in the eighteenth century. The philologists made up a large majority of the professors. This was the golden age during which literary scholarship reached its maturity. Standard editions were being created. The great learned journals were in their early phase, magisterially stockpiling contributions to knowledge. The basic facts of the literary tradition were still being established, although nearly all that mattered much had by then been accumulated, and that was one reason why some in the new generation were restless. The flourishing of philology in the very late nineteenth and early twentieth century had created for us the archive that we now use and take for granted today, but the New Critics saw a certain hardening of the arteries and felt that amid the accumulation of knowledge the challenges of interpretation had been forgotten.

另一种主流教学方法可以称之为“欣赏式教学”。剑桥大学里，与理查兹同时代的著名学者、人称“Q”的亚瑟·奎勒-库奇爵士，其引人入胜的讲座几乎没有任何内容，仅仅是对文学巨著的欣赏式解读。在耶鲁大学，与“Q”同时代的人也颇为相似，威廉·里昂——人称“比利”——菲尔普斯，他会走进教室，热情洋溢地引用丁尼生的诗句，双手合十，赞叹这真是美妙绝伦的诗歌。学生们对此感激不尽，终其一生都向大学捐赠了数十万美元。换句话说，这是一种极具价值的教学方法——但新批评派对此却避之不及。

The other dominant practice was what might be called “appreciative teaching.” A contemporary and colleague of I. A. Richards at Cambridge had been the famous “Q,” Sir Arthur Quiller-Couch, whose mesmerizing lectures had virtually no content at all. They were simply evocations, appreciative evocations, of great works of literature. At Yale, exactly contemporary with “Q” we had a similar figure, William Lyon—”Billy”—Phelps, who would enter the classroom, rapturously quote Tennyson, clasp his hands, and say that it was truly wonderful poetry. The students in turn were so appreciative that they gave hundreds of thousands of dollars to the university as long as they lived. In other words, this was valuable teaching—but the New Critics wanted no part of that either.

他们所追求的——而他们所处的学术环境与俄国形式主义者所处的学术氛围颇为相似——是一种系统且经过深思熟虑的阐释方法，从而使批评实践不再那么迂腐和散漫，或者说不再那么热情洋溢和散漫。正是在这种学术背景下——这种背景本身也受到英国学院主流思想的影响——新批评在20世纪30年代和40年代兴起。

What they wanted—and in this their surroundings were similar to the academic atmosphere that you’ll see the Russian formalists found themselves in—was a systematic and carefully considered approach to interpretation, so that the practice of criticism could become less pedantic and scattershot, or less effusive and scattershot. It was against this academic backdrop—itself influenced by the prevalent ideas of the British academy—that the New Criticism arose in the 1930s and 1940s.

本次讲座介绍的第一位人物是I.A. Richards。在加入剑桥大学英语系之前，Richards接受过巴甫洛夫心理学的训练，因此在他的文章中你会读到“刺激”和“需求”这两个概念。他对心理如何对经验做出反应的理解——他将反应分为简单反应、抵抗反应和适应反应——同样可以追溯到巴甫洛夫的理论。这些源于心理学的思想甚至影响了Richards在撰写《文学批评原理》（1924）期间对自身文学事业的理解。对Richards而言，阅读是一种体验，是心灵如何受到阅读内容的影响。因此，尽管他的研究对象是文学，但他始终在探讨人类心理学：文学满足了哪些需求，心理如何对文学做出反应，心理反应的优缺点是什么，等等。

The first figure whom you read for this lecture is I. A. Richards. Before he joined the English department at Cambridge, Richards was trained as a Pavlovian psychologist, which is why you read in his essay about “stimuli” and “needs.” His sense of the way the mind reacts to experience, dividing reactions as he does into the uncomplicated, the resisting, and the adjusting, can likewise be traced to Pavlovian principles. These ideas derived from psychology govern Richards’s understanding even of his literary vocation during the period when he wrote Principles of Literary Criticism (1924). For Richards, reading is experience, the way the mind is affected by what it reads. Thus even though his subject matter is literature, he’s nevertheless constantly talking about human psychology: what needs are answered by literature, how the psyche responds to literature, what’s good and bad about psychic responses, and so on.

理查兹作为科学家的另一个方面在于，他确实相信指涉——语言与世界真正相连的方式。对理查兹而言，可验证和可证伪的陈述是科学实践的精髓，他对此极为重视。换句话说，他不像许多文学评论家那样——或许甚至不像布鲁克斯那样（布鲁克斯也追随理查兹，做出了我即将描述的根本区别）——他对科学并不像大多数文学评论家和艺术家那样抱有某种程度的反感。他的学生威廉·恩普森也是如此，恩普森在转学英语专业之前是数学专业的。理查兹确实相信文学研究可以建立在科学的基础之上。

Another aspect of his having been a scientist is that Richards really did believe, seriously believed, in reference—the ways in which language really can hook on to the world. Verifiable and falsifiable statement is for Richards the essence of scientific practice, and he cares very much about that. He does not, in other words, share with so many literary critics—perhaps even with Brooks, who follows Richards in making the fundamental distinction I’m about to describe—he does not share with the majority of literary critics and artists a measure of distaste for science. This is also true of his student, William Empson, who was a math major before he became an English major. Richards really did believe that literary studies could be put on a scientific footing.

由于理查兹对科学极其认真，他实际上颠覆了我们上次在讨论西德尼、康德、柯勒律治、王尔德和温萨特时所提出的观点。他颠覆了只有艺术才是自主的观点。他认为科学是自主的（参见766页），这意味着科学事实可以用陈述句来描述，而无需参考任何心理背景或依赖于人类的各种需求。科学的自主性体现在它是对事实或谬误的纯粹、不加修饰且不受任何影响的陈述。

Because Richards takes science so seriously, he actually reverses the idea that we talked about last time in Sidney, Kant, Coleridge, Wilde, and Wimsatt. He reverses the idea that it’s exclusively art that’s autonomous. He says science is autonomous (cf. 766), meaning that scientific facts can be described in statements without reference to any kind of psychological context or any dependency on the varieties of human need. Science is autonomous in the sense that it is a pure, uncluttered, and uninfluenced declaration of fact or falsehood.

然后他说：

Then he says:

宣称科学自主与将所有活动都置于其之下截然不同。[诗歌在此发挥作用。] 这仅仅是断言，任何未被扭曲的参考体系都属于科学。这绝非断言，为了获取利益，任何参考体系都不得被扭曲。正如无数人类活动（例如科学活动）需要未被扭曲的参考才能得以实现一样，无数其他同样重要的人类活动也同样需要扭曲的参考，或者更直白地说，需要虚构。
To declare Science autonomous is very different from subordinating all our activities to it. [Here’s where poetry comes in.] It is merely to assert that so far as any body of references is undistorted it belongs to Science. It is not in the least to assert that no references may be distorted if advantage can thereby be gained. And just as there are innumerable human activities which require undistorted references if they are to be satisfied [scientific activities], so there are innumerable other human activities not less important which equally require distorted references or, more plainly, fictions.

在这里，你可以看到理查兹对所谓“科学陈述”和“情感陈述”的基本区分：一方面是真正具有指涉性、无可辩驳地可验证或可证伪的内容，另一方面是情感表达的内容。后来，理查兹改变了他的用词，不再谈论科学语言和情感语言。更危险的是，对于任何喜欢诗歌的人来说，他用“陈述”（指科学）和“伪陈述”（指诗歌）来代替。如果你要为诗歌辩护——而理查兹一直这样做——称其为“伪陈述”，那你真是太冒险了，但“伪陈述”当然只是他在这里所说的“虚构”的另一种说法。

Here you see Richards’s basic distinction between what he calls “scientific statement” and what he calls “emotive statement”: the distinction between what is truly referential, what is incontrovertibly verifiable or falsifiable, on the one hand, and what is emotive, on the other. Later on Richards changes his vocabulary, no longer talking about scientific and emotive language. Even more dangerously from the standpoint of anybody who likes poetry, he talks instead of “statement,” meaning science, and “pseudo-statement,” meaning poetry. You are really out on a limb if you’re going to defend poetry—which Richards kept doing—as “pseudo-statement,” but of course “pseudo-statement” is just another expression for what he here calls “fiction.”

一旦我们适应了这套词汇，一旦我们习惯了这种不容置疑的科学视角，我们或许会疑惑，我们究竟为何需要伪陈述或虚构作品。顺便一提，我们很清楚，许多杰出的科学家根本无法忍受阅读诗歌，因为诗歌是“虚假的”。正如理查兹所说，诗歌思维总是带有某种古老或返祖的色彩。这并非意味着它不试图表达真理，正如西德尼所说（它“不肯定任何事物，因此也从不说谎”）。事实上，理查兹甚至援引柏拉图的观点，认为诗歌本身就是在说谎。诗歌似乎总是陷入困境：“显而易见，诗歌的大部分内容都是由一些只有傻瓜才会试图验证的陈述构成的。它们并非那种可以被验证的东西”（768）。

Once we settle into this vocabulary, and once we get used to this unquestioningly scientific perspective, we may wonder why on earth we need pseudo-statement, or fiction, at all. We know very well, by the way, that there are many excellent scientists who simply cannot stand to read poetry because it’s “false.” As Richards says, there’s always something archaic or atavistic about poetic thinking. It’s not that it’s not trying to tell the truth, as Sidney said (it “nothing affirms, and therefore never lieth”). It is in fact, Richards goes so far as to say, following Plato, lying. Poetry seems to get itself in trouble constantly: “It is evident that the bulk of poetry consists of statements which only the very foolish would think of attempting to verify. They are not the kinds of things which can be verified” (768).

通常，这种思路会导致这样的人提醒我们，例如，尽管民主社会是最佳的社会，但诗歌却偏爱封建社会，因为封建社会能孕育出更好的诗歌。同样，尽管我们都知道宇宙的本质——我们甚至不能再称之为哥白尼式的宇宙观了——但诗歌却对托勒密式的天文学有着一种奇特的偏爱。换句话说，诗歌中的一切都是对某种早期思维方式的回溯。但理查兹欣然接受了这种观点，并未加以批判。这就是他所说的“虚构”或“伪陈述”。

It usually follows from this line of thought that somebody like that will remind us for example that although a democratic society is the best society to live in, poetry prefers feudal society because it makes better poetry. And likewise whereas we all know that the universe is of a certain kind—we can’t even call it Copernican anymore—poetry has an odd preference for Ptolemaic astronomy. In other words, everything in poetry is a throwback to some earlier way of thinking. But Richards cheerfully embraces this idea without criticism. It’s what he means by “fiction” or “pseudo-statement.”

如果这就是诗歌，我们为何需要它？理查兹认为，诗歌满足了我们心理构成中科学无法满足的需求。我们内心充满各种欲望，其中既包括对真理的渴望——我们可以从科学中学习到的知识——也包括许多需要通过奇幻或想象来满足的需求。他指出，这种满足之所以重要且值得珍视，是因为除非我们的需求得到组织或协调，从而以一种他有时称之为“综合”的方式协同运作，否则它们实际上会将我们撕裂。文学能够调和冲突或对立的需求，而理查兹对这一基本理念极为重视，以至于在另一篇文章中（并非你刚刚读到的这篇文章），他令人震惊地说道：“诗歌能够拯救我们。”换句话说，诗歌如今能够做到宗教曾经做到的事情。诗歌——请记住，这是一位科学家在说话——并不比宗教更真实，但它可以发挥宗教的功能，因此能够拯救我们。因此，尽管理查兹在《文学批评原理》等书中似乎贬低了他声称要颂扬的事物，但他仍然认为诗歌的使命是调和相互冲突的需求。

If that’s poetry, why do we want it? Because, according to Richards, it fulfills needs in our psychological makeup that science can’t fulfill. We are a chaos of desires. They include the desire for truth—what we can learn from science—but a great many of our needs require fanciful or imaginative fulfillment. The reason this fulfillment is important and should be valued is, he says, that unless our needs are organized or harmonized so that they work together in what he sometimes calls a “synthesis,” they can actually tear us apart. Literature is what can reconcile conflicting or opposing needs, and Richards cares so much about this basic idea that in another text, not in the text you’ve just read, he says, shockingly, “Poetry is capable of saving us.” In other words, poetry is capable of doing now what religion used to do. Poetry—remember this is a scientist speaking—is no more true than religion, but it can perform the function of religion and is therefore capable of saving us. Thus even despite the seeming derogation of the very thing that he purports to be celebrating in books like The Principles of Literary Criticism, Richards does hold it to be the mission of poetry to harmonize conflicting needs.

这有点像亚里士多德的“净化”（catharsis）概念，它可以有多种解读。弥尔顿在《力士参孙》的结尾将其理解为通过情感的消耗来净化情绪的顺势疗法：通过这场悲剧，我们可以获得“内心的平静，所有激情都已消散”。这或许可以作为理查兹作品的座右铭。通过诗歌体验来调和相互冲突的需求，会带来一种净化，一种“内心的平静，所有激情都已消散”。悲剧可以作为理查兹阐述其理念的绝佳范例。虽然他没有明说，但我们可以想象他会说，悲剧调和了对暴力的需求与对正义的需求。

It’s somewhat like Aristotle’s idea of catharsis, which can be understood in various ways. Milton at the end of Samson Agonistes understands it as the homeopathic purgation of emotion through the expenditure of emotion: as a result of this tragedy, we can have “calm of mind, all passion spent.” That could be the motto for Richards’s work. The reconciliation of conflicting needs through the experience of poetry results in a kind of catharsis, a “calm of mind, all passion spent.” Tragedy would serve Richards as a good paradigm for his idea. Although he doesn’t say so, we can imagine him saying that tragedy reconciles the need for violence with the need for justice.

理查兹的本科生威廉·埃姆普森找到理查兹，说他有一个关于歧义的想法。他觉得关于歧义有很多东西可以写，所以问理查兹是否介意他着手研究一下。理查兹觉得这个想法不错，便让他去工作。几个月后，埃姆普森带来了他的手稿，这本手稿后来成为二十世纪最伟大的批评著作之一，也是最令人意想不到的著作之一：《七种歧义》。你阅读清单中埃姆普森的这段节选就出自《七种歧义》。

Richards’s undergraduate student, William Empson, went to Richards and said he had an idea about ambiguity. He said he felt there was quite a bit that could be written about it, and so he wondered whether Richards would mind if maybe he worked on it. Richards said it sounded good and sent him off to work. A few months later Empson brought him the manuscript of one of the greatest books of criticism in the twentieth century, and one of the most incredibly surprising: Seven Types of Ambiguity. The brief excerpt from Empson in your list of readings is taken from Seven Types of Ambiguity.

我认为埃姆森是文学评论界最幽默的人，他拥有优秀单口喜剧演员那种冷幽默的技巧和精准的节奏感。我非常喜欢读他的作品，所以当有人邀请我写一本关于他的书时，我欣然应允。希望你也喜欢他。他的作品引人入胜，他作为评论家的才华与阅读他的乐趣密不可分。我对你提供的这段摘录特别感兴趣，因为他在其中谈到了“氛围”。这是他对“热情洋溢”或赞赏式批评的回应。“Q”、比利·菲尔普斯以及所有其他赞赏派作家和讲师的惯用伎俩之一，就是声称他们阅读是为了感受“氛围”，认为当人们遇到伟大的文学作品时，会有一种直击心灵的感觉，而他们作为讲师和评论家的目的就是唤起作品的氛围。埃姆森回应说，氛围当然存在，我们当然应该讨论它；但归根结底，如果氛围不能起到阐释作用，那它又有何用呢？如果我即将引用的《麦克白》段落中存在某种氛围，那它必然是出于某种特定目的而营造的。在我看来，接下来这段文字是对文学作品最精彩绝伦的解读之一。如果我的语气听起来像比利·菲尔普斯（我指的是纯粹的评论，而非丁尼生！），我深感抱歉，但我确实也为此感到兴奋。

I think Empson is the funniest person who has ever written literary criticism, with the deadpan skill and perfect timing of a good stand-up comic. I enjoy reading him so much that when I was asked to write a book about him, I did so. I hope you enjoy him, too. He’s a page-turner, and his brilliance as a critic is really inseparable from the fun of reading him. I’m especially interested in the excerpt you have because of what he says there about “atmosphere.” This is his way of responding to “enthusiastic” or appreciative criticism. One of the tricks of “Q” and Billy Phelps and all the other authors and lecturers of the appreciative school was to say that they read for “atmosphere,” that there was something one just felt on one’s pulse when one encountered great literature, and their purpose as lecturers and as critics was to evoke the atmosphere of things. Empson responds that atmosphere certainly does exist and we should certainly talk about it; but after all, what is the use of atmosphere if it doesn’t serve an interpretive function? If there is atmosphere in the passage I’m about to quote from Macbeth, it must be atmosphere of a certain kind put there for a certain reason. What follows, it seems to me, is one of the most breathtaking riffs on a passage of literature that you’ll ever encounter. I’m sorry if I sound like Billy Phelps (talking about mere criticism, not Tennyson!), but I do get excited, too.

正如埃姆森所说，凶手们刚刚离开房间，麦克白百无聊赖地等待着天黑，因为班柯和弗林斯必须等到天黑才能被杀。于是，他自然而然地望向窗外，看看时间过得如何，然后他说了这样一番话：

As Empson says, the murderers have just left the room, and Macbeth is twiddling his thumbs, hoping it’s getting dark because it’s got to get dark before Banquo and Fleance can be killed. So naturally he looks out the window to see how the time is going, and this is what he says:

…
…
来吧，寂静的夜晚，
Come, seeling Night,
斯卡夫抬起可怜之日的柔嫩之眼
Skarfe up the tender Eye of pitiful Day
以及你那只沾满鲜血、看不见的手
And with thy bloodie and invisible Hand
取消并撕碎那伟大的邦德
Cancel and teare to pieces that great Bond
这让我脸色苍白！
That keeps me pale!

埃姆森没有提到最后一个词“苍白”，但与乌鸦和秃鼻乌鸦并置在一起时，我觉得这是这段文字中一个有趣的时刻。

Empson doesn’t mention that last word, “pale,” but in juxtaposition with the crows and rooks it strikes me that it is an interesting moment in the passage.

继续：

To continue:

光线渐浓，乌鸦
Light thickens, and the Crow
为新秀木队制造翅膀。
Makes Wing to th’ Rookie Wood.

埃姆森将这些句子用斜体标出，因为虽然他对文章的每一部分都有话要说，但这些句子才是他稍后要说的真正重点。

Empson italicizes those lines because while he has something to say about every part of the passage, they are going to be the true focus of what he’ll say later.

白昼的美好事物开始衰落，渐渐消逝。
Good things of Day begin to droope, and drowse,
当夜幕降临，黑衣特工们开始追捕他们的猎物时，一切都发生了改变。
While Night’s black Agents to their Prey’s do rowse.
你对我的话语感到惊讶，但请保持安静。（麦克白夫人走进了房间）
Thou marvell’st at my words, but hold thee still [Lady Macbeth has come into the room];
坏事始于恶，坏事愈演愈烈：
Things bad begun, make strong themselves by ill:
所以请跟我走吧。2
So prythee go with me.2

埃姆森对这段文字着迷，并在接下来的几段中，详细阐述了他着迷的种种原因。在他的论述中，他始终暗示，这就是人们谈论氛围时所指的。它不仅仅是一种能凭感觉感受到的东西，而是可以被描述和分析的。我只想谈谈他最后那句话。他说：“乌鸦群居，主要以素食为主。”——我忍不住要插话，指出埃姆森正是那个认为古舟子咏中，水手射杀信天翁是因为船员饥饿的人。在1798年版的《古舟子咏》中，硬饼干里进了虫子，所以埃姆森自然而然地写道：“据说，水手射杀的那种信天翁，熬出来的肉汤味道还不错。”
