Like the Russian formalists, Saussure is chiefly concerned with establishing the semiological project as a science. Also like the Russian formalists—and in a way like the New Critics, too—talking about their “academic” contemporaries, Saussure is vexed by the messiness and lack of system in the current study of linguistics. This is what he says in this first passage:

如果我们同时从多个角度研究语言，语言学的研究对象在我们看来就像是一团杂乱无章、互不相关的异质事物。
If we study speech from several viewpoints simultaneously, the object of linguistics appears to us as a confused mass of heterogeneous and unrelated things.

下图坐标系的横轴代表“言语”。如果我是一名语言学家，我会尽可能多地进行实证研究，而当我试图整理研究材料时，各种各样混乱的标准就会纷至沓来，令人烦恼。索绪尔继续说道：

The horizontal axis of the coordinates in the diagram below is “speech.” If I’m a linguist, I study as many speeches as I can empirically, and if I do so, all sorts of confused criteria jostle disturbingly for attention when I try to organize my material. Saussure continues:

[这一]程序为心理学、人类学、规范语法、语文学等几门学科打开了大门——这些学科与语言学不同，但鉴于语言学方法的缺陷，它们都声称言语是其研究对象之一。
[This] procedure opens the door to several sciences–psychology, anthropology, normative grammar, philology, etc.–which are distinct from linguistics, but which claim speech, in view of the faulty method of linguistics, as one of their objects.
依我看，解决上述所有困难只有一个办法：从一开始，我们就必须脚踏实地地运用语言，并将语言作为所有其他言语表现形式的规范。
As I see it, there is only one solution to all the foregoing difficulties: from the very outset we must put both feet on the ground of language and use language as the norm of all the other manifestations of speech.

我们立足于语言的范畴，而非言语，以便将其理解为符号间关系的系统。言语变化多端，在太多语境中得以体现，无法被纳入科学研究对象所需的限定领域。而语言则可以作为这样一个领域，围绕索绪尔的两个指导概念展开：符号的任意性以及符号与其他符号之间的否定同一性。

We put both feet on the ground of language, in contrast with speech, so that we can make it intelligible as a system of relations among signs. Speech is too protean, actualized in too many contexts, to be approached within the delimited field that a scientific object needs to inhabit. Language, on the other hand, can propose itself as such a field, organized around Saussure’s two guiding concepts: the arbitrariness of signs and the negative identity of signs in relation to other signs.

为了理解符号为何以及如何呈现负向差异，我们应该仔细思考语言中符号的各种理解方式——语言是我们的研究对象——所有这些理解都与特定符号在口语句子中的选择方式有关。以“船”这个词为例。作为一个能指，“船”在发音上与其他一些能指非常接近。我们在此不一一列举，以免出现弗洛伊德式的口误（例如，我们可能会用“船”来代替“船”），但我未提及的这些能指本身就构成了一个词簇。发音相近的符号构成了语言中一个由符号组成的联想网络，但“船”也有同义词：“bark”（树皮）、“boat”（船）、“bateau”（平底船）、“sailboat”（帆船）、“skiff”（小艇）、“ Schiff ” （小艇）（注意，后两个能指也属于发音相近的词簇）。同义词也构成一个词簇：这些词虽然发音大多不同，但发音仍然相近。此外，“船”也有反义词，因此与“火车”、“汽车”、“卡车”和“骡子”——这些替代交通工具——建立了联系。通过所有这些方式以及其他许多方式，“船”被归类，以便在我们说话时，能够从众多候选词中选择一个来表达我们试图阐明的含义。

In order to understand why and how signs are negatively differential, we should pause over the various ways in which we can think of signs in language—our scientific object—all of which have to do with the way a given sign might be chosen for a place in a spoken sentence. Take the word “ship.” As a signifier, “ship” is very closely related in sound to certain other signifiers. We won’t specify them for fear of a Freudian slip (“boat” may be replacing “ship” for this very reason), but what I have left unspoken amounts already to one cluster. Signs contiguous in sound constitute one associational network of clustered signs in language, but there are also synonyms for “ship”: “bark,” “boat,” “bateau,” “sailboat,” “skiff,” Schiff (note that these last two signifiers belong also in the sound cluster). Synonyms, too, exist in a cluster: words that don’t sound at all the same for the most part but are still contiguous. Furthermore, “ship” also has antonyms, hence enters into a relationship with “train,” “car,” “truck,” and “mule”—alternative modes of transportation. In all of these ways and many others, “ship” is clustered to make it available for choice from among other candidates to advance a meaning that we try to unfold when we speak.

如此一来，语言中每个符号都存在于一组符号群中，这些符号群与其他许多符号的符号群有所重叠，但最终又各自独一无二（没有其他符号完全属于同一组符号群），等待着被插入到正在展开的话语中的某个空缺位置。顺便一提，我之前随意地指出语言的基本单位是“词”，这显然过于简单化了。事实并非总是如此。语言学家可以从不同的抽象层次来研究语言。有时，基本单位是短语或句子；有时，基本单位是音素——不可分割的声音单位；如果研究的是作为书写系统的语言，那么基本单位可能是音节。同样，在书写研究中，基本单位也可能是字母，被理解为一种图形元素。语言学中研究基本单位或构成单位的方式多种多样，因此需要一个特殊的术语来涵盖所有构成单位：语素（tagmeme）。因此，无论选择哪个组成单元来构成给定系统中的符号，系统中符号之间的差异性关联都是语段性的。那么，任何系统中符号之间的关系，我们称之为语段性；为了体现这一系统术语，我们将图表的纵轴称为语段轴。

In this manner, each sign harbored by language sits in a set of clusters that overlaps with the cluster-set of many other signs but is ultimately unique to itself (no other sign belongs in exactly that set of clusters), waiting to be slotted into some vacancy in an unfolding utterance. By the way, I have grossly oversimplified in indicating casually that the basic unit of language is the “word.” That’s not at all necessarily the case. Linguists can work at different levels of abstraction with language. Sometimes the basic unit is the phrase or the sentence, but at other times the basic unit is the phoneme—the indivisible sound unit—or if one’s studying language as a system of writing, it might be the syllable. Again in the study of writing it could be the letter, understood as a graphic element. The multiple ways in which one can choose a basic or constituent unit for study in linguistics requires a special term to cover any and all constituent units: the tagmeme. Thus the differential association of signs in a system, no matter which constituent unit is chosen to constitute a sign in a given system, is tagmemic. The relationality of signs in any system, then, we call syntagmatic; in acknowledgment of this system-term, the vertical axis of our diagram is called the syntagmatic axis.

符号的负面差异性取决于其任意性。这就是为什么索绪尔和俄国形式主义者一样，对拟声词保持警惕。拟声词看起来和听起来都像一个自然符号，但索绪尔竭力表明，拟声词总是受制于词源的偶然性或方言的变迁，它并非能指与所指关系的内在组成部分或构成要素，而能指与所指关系始终是任意的。例如，狗叫声在每种人类语言中听起来都不同（汪汪，汪汪），这一事实只能解释为特定语言中这些声音与其他声音的相对位置，而不是能指中固有的模仿指令。人们或许会推测，英语中的“vow”（誓言）被用来指结婚，而德语中的“bow”（Bau）则专门用来指建造。

The negatively differential nature of signs hinges on their arbitrariness. That’s why Saussure, like the Russian formalists, is on his guard against onomatopoeia. An onomatopoetic word looks and sounds like a natural sign, but Saussure is at pains to show that onomatopoeia is always subject to transient accidents of etymology or vagaries of dialect, never intrinsic to or constitutive of the signifier-signified relation, which is always without exception arbitrary. The bark of a dog, for example, sounds different in every human language (bow-wow, vaow-vaow), a fact that can only be explained as the positioning of such sounds in relation to other sounds in a given language, not as a mimetic imperative that’s built into signifiers. One might speculate that in English “vow” is commandeered for getting married and in German “bow” (Bau) is reserved for building.

语言中能指的聚类简化了言语选择，限制了沿着我们图表中的“范式轴”（言语发展的轴线）从一个位置到另一个位置可用的能指数量。E.E. Cummings 大胆地挑战了这一原则，引起了语言学家 Dell Hymes 的注意。Cummings 写出了像“He danced his did”这样的句子，其中“did”显然不是一个你会认为会以任何方式参与相关联想簇的词。¹ “ He danced his did”：这在各个方面似乎都是一个失误，正如一种语言学派所称，而 Cummings 用这种“偏差”（语言学家称之为偏差）似乎是在对符号学嗤之以鼻。然而，只要具备一定的创造力，就能注意到“d”音或“duh”音与“danced”中的“duh”音重复，而且实际上有各种各样的组合压力引导卡明斯选择“did”而不是其他一些看似无关的词。

The clustering of signifiers in language streamlines the choices made in speech, limiting the number of signifiers available from slot to slot along the “paradigmatic axis” of our diagram, the axis on which speech goes forward. E. E. Cummings boldly challenged this principle, attracting the attention of a linguist named Dell Hymes. Cummings wrote sentences like “He danced his did,” where “did” is obviously not a word you would have supposed to be in any way involved in a relevant associational cluster.1 “He danced his did”: that seems in every sense a misfire, as one school of thinking about language would call it, and Cummings with such “deviations” (as the linguists call them) seems to be thumbing his nose at semiotics. Yet a certain amount of ingenuity is all that’s required to notice that the “d” sound or “duh” reiterates the “duh” sound in “danced,” and that in fact there are all sorts of combinatory pressures guiding Cummings to choose “did” as opposed to some other seemingly irrelevant word.

如果正如索绪尔所说，在边界的一侧，我们看着一头牛说“Ochs”（或“Kuh”），而在边界的另一侧，我们看着一头牛说“boeuf”，如果我们跨越一片相当大的水域，看着一头牛说“cow”，那么显然，事物与符号之间就不存在任何自然联系。因此，符号是任意的，也是差异性的。我必须能够区分我在任何交流序列中使用的所有符号。我该如何做到这一点？通过选择那些并非其他符号的符号。我并不肯定地知道任何构成单元；我不会指着它说，它本身就是符号x，即使我感觉自己好像就是这么做的。我否定地知道它。我之所以知道它，仅仅是因为它不是其他一切。它与相邻符号之间，无论基于相似还是差异，都绝非同一关系。它不是那个符号，当然也不是任何其他符号。这一点显而易见——即便仅限于口语——对于同音异义词尤其如此。“这里”和“听”只能通过语境来理解，我们绝不能妄想仅凭发音就能确定它们的含义。

If on one side of the border, as Saussure puts it, we look at a cow and say “Ochs” (or “Kuh”), and if on the other side of the border we look at a cow and say “boeuf,” and if we cross a considerable body of water, look at a cow, and say “cow,” plainly any natural relationship between the thing and the sign just doesn’t exist. Signs are arbitrary, then, and they’re also differential. I have to be able to distinguish among all the signs I use in any communicative sequence. How do I do it? By choosing signs that are not other signs. I don’t know any constitutive unit positively; I don’t point to it and say that, in and of itself, it is sign x, even though it feels as though that is what I am doing. I know it negatively. I know it only because it is not everything else. Its direct relationship with the sign that’s most closely adjacent to it owing either to similarity or dissimilarity can never be a relationship of identity. It’s not that other sign, and certainly not any other sign. This is clearly true—confining ourselves here to spoken language—even and especially of homonyms. “Here” and “hear” can be known only by their context, and we cannot pretend for a moment to know them positively by their sound.

我即将举一个例子来阐明我所说的“否定性认知”的含义，但首先我想引用索绪尔的几段话来重申这一点。第一段（845）：

I’m about to give an example that should clarify what I mean by negative recognition, but first a couple of passages in Saussure that reiterate the point. First (845):

语言是一个由相互依存的术语组成的系统，其中每个术语的价值完全取决于其他术语的同时存在。
Language is a system of interdependent terms in which the value of each term results solely from the simultaneous presence of the others.

我只能通过它与周围一切事物的不同之处来了解它。他接着说（847）：

I can’t know it except by the way in which it differs from everything that surrounds it. He goes on to say (847):

归根结底，语言片段的依据永远只能是它与其他部分的不一致。任意性和差异性是两个相关的特质。
[A] segment of language can never in the final analysis be based on anything except its noncoincidence with the rest. Arbitrary and differential are two correlative qualities.

然后，他又说（846）：“概念纯粹是差异性的，其定义并非基于其积极的内容，而是基于其与系统中其他术语的消极关系。” 正如我之前承认的，这很难凭直觉接受。我看着某物，告诉自己“我知道它是什么”，却忘记了我知道它是什么仅仅是因为身处一个语境之中，而这个语境并非它周围的事物——而且，它也不是任何那些不存在的事物，即使它们的存在会改变周围事物的格局。

And then again (846): “[C]oncepts are purely differential and defined not by their positive content but negatively by their relations with other terms of the system.” Again, as I’ve acknowledged, this is hard to accept intuitively. I look at something and tell myself that “I know what it is,” forgetting that I know what it is only because of a context in which it is not the things that surround it—and it is not, furthermore, any of the absent things the presence of which would alter the landscape of those surrounding things.

那么，这里就有一个例子，说明某个符号如何在不同的符号系统中流动，并且只能以否定的方式被认知。它既是语言单位，也属于其他符号系统。我的例子是红灯。对于红绿灯——这可能是我们拥有的最简单的符号系统——只有红、黄、绿三个变量——我们有两种思考红灯的方式。一方面，如果我们认为我们的认知是肯定的，我们会说红色就意味着停止。如果我们只能使用这一个符号系统，就很难抵制肯定的思维方式，因为我们会很快补充说“黄色”意味着“暂停”，“绿色”意味着“通行”。每个人都知道这些，当我接近一个红灯的十字路口时，我当然不会想“哦，不是黄灯，也不是绿灯”。我的思维方式并非如此。到目前为止，我似乎已经证实了“红灯就意味着停止”这一肯定的论断。但是，假设红灯出现在驯鹿的鼻子上或变成驯鹿的鼻子呢？在这种情况下，红灯就像一个信号灯，意思是“前进”、“走”、“跟我来”、“管他什么鱼雷”。我们听到红灯的指示就飞奔而去，这显然意味着“前进”。

Here, then, is an example of a sign that moves around among various semiotic systems and can be known only negatively. It’s a unit of language, but it also belongs to other sign systems. My example is the red light. Regarding a stoplight, which is probably the simplest semiotic system that we have—three variables, red, yellow, and green—we have two ways of thinking about the red light. If on the one hand we think that our knowledge is positive, we say red just means stop. If all we had to work with were this semiotic system alone, it would be hard to put up resistance to positive thinking, because we’d quickly add that “yellow” means “pause” and “green” means “go.” Everybody knows these things, and I’m certainly not thinking, when I approach an intersection where the light is red, “Oh, not yellow, not green.” My mind just doesn’t work that way. I seem so far then to have made good the positive claim that a red light just means stop. But suppose the red light appeared on or as the nose of a reindeer. In that case, the red light would be a beacon that means “forward,” “go,” “follow me,” “damn the torpedoes.” And we race off in response to the red light, which clearly means “go.”

在中国文化大革命期间，毛泽东夫人对红灯代表“停止”表示不满，因为红色在当时被视为进步的颜色。她想改变这一制度，但幸运的是，重新定义颜色被认为是不明智的。事实上，颜色的含义并非取决于任何颜色的内在价值，而是取决于当时普遍接受的颜色之间的区别。只要红色仍然代表“非绿灯通行”和“非黄灯暂停”，一切就都没问题。如果要让它代表其他含义（例如“通行”），就需要在一个完全不同的、根本不存在的系统中赋予它负面的含义。

During the Cultural Revolution in China, Madame Mao disapproved of the fact that red lights meant “stop” because red is, of course, the color of progress. She wanted to change the system, but fortunately, it was considered unwise to redefine the colors. Their meaning in fact depended not on the intrinsic value of any color but on the difference between the colors that was a universally accepted convention. As long as red means not-green-go, not-yellow-pause, everything’s fine. To make it mean anything else (“go,” for example) requires that it appear negatively in a completely different, nonexistent system.

现在来看另一种红灯：街门上的红灯表示“进去”、“进来”，它与相邻街门上的白灯（可能为了防盗而在夜间亮着，因此表示“停止”）之间存在着一种符号学上的否定关系。换句话说，只有在特定的符号学系统的“二元”（我们稍后会讨论这一点）框架内，红灯才能被理解。而礼堂门上的红灯则不表示“进来”，而是表示“出去”、“离开”。

Now for yet other red lights: a red light over a street door means “go in,” “come in,” existing as it does in a semiotic, that is, negative, relationship with a white light over the neighboring street door, which is probably kept on at night to keep burglars away, hence means “stop.” The red light is intelligible only, in other words, within the “binary” (we’ll come back to that) of that particular semiotic system. Over an auditorium door, the red light doesn’t mean “come in,” it means “go out,” “exit.”

我想，有些红灯既不表示“停止”，也不表示“通行”，但我们暂且只讨论表示运动或其反义词——静止的红灯。在情人节彩灯上，红灯表示“不要停止”。有趣的是，它在这里起到了一种作用：一方面否定了自身在另一个符号系统中的含义，另一方面又巧妙地强化了自身在另一个符号系统中的含义。在救护车或警车上——诚然，如今很多这类车辆的警灯都是蓝色的，但我们假设，按照传统，它们仍然是红色的——红灯表示“让开”或“停止”。这可能与交通信号灯的符号学意义有某种关联，让你产生“不要通行”的印象。但在这个例子中，同样重要的“让开”让开的含义变得复杂起来，它意味着通行，但方向却截然不同。许多司机对此感到困惑，这表明救护车灯光属于一个效率低下的符号系统。

I suppose there are red lights that mean neither “stop” nor “go,” but let’s confine ourselves still to the red lights that indicate locomotion or its binary opposite, stasis. On a light-up valentine, the red light means “don’t stop.” Interestingly here, it has the function of negating its own meaning in another semiotic system, and of course naughtily reinforcing its meaning in yet another. On an ambulance or a police car—admittedly, many of these lights are blue these days but let’s suppose, tradition prevailing, that they were still red—the red light means “get out of the way” or “stop.” It probably bears a distant relation to the semiotics of the stoplight, putting into your head the notion of “don’t go.” It’s a notion that’s complicated in this case by the equally imperative notion “get out of the way,” which means going, but going in a different direction. Many drivers are paralyzed by this perplexity, which shows that ambulance lights belong to a somewhat inefficient semiotic system.

最后，我们应该考虑圣诞树上的红灯。起初，我们或许会松一口气，认为它没有任何意义。我们想说，讨论红灯、绿灯、黄灯、白灯或蓝灯之间的负面关系显然毫无意义，因为它们都具有相同的价值。它们都明亮喜庆，仅此而已。所以，这里的红灯看起来并不像随意或与其他颜色的灯有任何区别。这是因为这盏红灯并不处于这个特定符号系统的基本构成单元层面。它本身根本不是一个符号。“明亮的灯光”才是相关的构成单元，而这个单元内各种颜色的差异被它们共同的意义所抵消——尤其是在圣诞树上或装饰其他被文化环境赋予相似价值的物品时。一旦你理解了这一点，一旦你理解了“圣诞树”的价值，而不是“红灯”（“红灯”或许是某些圣诞树的一部分），你就会发现你又回到了一个非常明显的符号系统：我们对圣诞树的认知是负面的，它不是烛台，不是宽扎节蜡烛，也不是那种毫无节日装饰的令人不快的象征。然而，这个问题或许还没有定论。即使我们不庆祝圣诞节，即使我们摆放的是宽扎节蜡烛，我们仍然知道圣诞树是什么；因此我们说这种认知并非“文化决定的”。但是，如果我们认为这种自由、自发的理解就证明了圣诞树作为一种符号既非任意也非差异性的，那就错了。因为我们完全可以想象这样一种情况：有人，比如来自火星的访客，可能不知道圣诞树是什么，这迫使我们尽管对它很熟悉，也需要去想象我们理解它的符号环境。

Then finally we should consider the red light on a Christmas tree. At first we are perhaps relieved to think, that has no meaning at all. Obviously it’s no use talking about the negative relationship between a red light and a green light and a yellow, white, or blue one, we want to say, because they all have the same value. They’re all bright and festive and that’s all there is to it. So here there’s a red light that doesn’t seem arbitrary and differential with respect to lights of other colors. Well, that’s because this red light is not at the level of the basic constituent units in this particular semiotic system. It is not in itself a sign at all. “Bright lights” is the relevant constituent unit, and the variety of the colors within this unit is neutralized by their common signification—particularly on a tree or festooning another object that cultural circumstance accords a similar value. Once you get that, once you get the value, “Christmas tree,” as opposed to “red lights,” “red lights” being perhaps a part of some Christmas trees, then you see that you’re back in a very obvious semiotic system: we know a Christmas tree negatively as not-menorah, not-Kwanzaa candles, not the bah-humbug absence of all festive decoration. The case is perhaps still not closed, though. We still know what a Christmas tree is even if we don’t celebrate Christmas, even if we put out Kwanzaa candles instead; hence we say that this knowledge can’t be “culturally determined.” But we’re mistaken to think that this sense of free, spontaneous understanding proves that as a sign the tree is neither arbitrary nor differential, because it’s very possible to imagine a circumstance in which someone, a visitor from Mars, wouldn’t know what it was, forcing us despite its familiarity to imagine the semiotic environment in which we understand it.

关于圣诞树上的红灯，我再说几句，然后就结束这个例子了。我们常说圣诞树上的红、黄、绿、蓝等等颜色之间没有区别，但这当然只适用于我们所谓的“冬至装饰”体系。毕竟，光谱也是一个符号系统，在这个系统中，我们当然可以根据一个方向的紫色和另一个方向的橙色来区分红色，或者，如果将这个系统简化为三原色，则可以根据蓝色或黄色来区分红色。在任何情况下，尽管从某种意义上说，我们可以通过与系统中所有非红色标志的对比来认识红色，但我们在此更应仔细观察一个在颜色系统中显而易见，但在更复杂的系统中却容易被忽略的原则：我们首先是通过与它最密切相关的标志（例如，昏暗城市街道上的白灯、驯鹿毛茸茸的棕色鼻子等等）的对比来认识红灯的。例如，当我们抽象地思考交通信号灯时，我们可以认同红色首先是“非绿”，其次才是“非黄”。换句话说，红色和绿色之间的关系，一种相互否定的关系，是二元的。但是，当我在十字路口遇到黄灯时，红色所代表的危险或警察逮捕的威胁，其作用二元性就变成了“非黄”。换句话说，二元关系在给定的系统中可以自由移动，但在分析中，总能分离出某个特定的二元关系，作为符号选择的主要驱动因素。符号出现的微分矩阵总是复杂的，但在这个矩阵中，二元关系是微分的基本不可分割的要素。换句话说，多个“此非彼”关系是相关二元关系的总和，而每个二元关系都是一个“此非彼”。

One more word about the red lights on a tree and then I’ll liberate you from this example. We say there’s no difference on a Christmas tree between red, yellow, green, blue, and so on, but of course that’s true only within the system that we might call “winter solstice decoration.” The color spectrum after all is also a semiotic system, and in that system of course we know red differentially in relation to shades of purple in one direction and shades of orange in the other, or, if the system is distilled to primary colors, in relation to blue or yellow. In every case, even though in one sense we can say we know red in contradistinction to all the not-red signs in the system to which it belongs, we should here look more closely to observe a principle that’s readily apparent in a system of colors but easy to lose track of in more multifaceted systems: we know a red light first and foremost in its opposition to the sign that is most closely interdependent with it (a white light on a dark city street, a brown fuzzy nose on a reindeer, and so on). When we think abstractly about a traffic light, for example, we can agree that red is primarily not-green, only secondarily not-yellow. The relation of red and green, in other words, a relation of mutual negation, is binary. But when I approach a yellow light at an intersection, then the operative binary for red, felt as the threat of danger or police arrest, is not-yellow. Binaries move around freely within a given system, in other words, but under analysis some particular binary can always be isolated as the primary motivating factor in sign selection. The differential matrix in which signs appear is always complex, but within this matrix binary relations are the basic indivisible moments of differentiation. The multiple “this-is-not-those,” in other words, is the sum of relevant binaries, each of which is a “this-is-not-that.”

在这样的课程中，我们常常似乎在说我们什么都不知道。但事实并非如此。我们此刻讨论的，正是我们如何认知事物。如果我们认真对待符号学，它会为我们提供一种相当精妙的方法来理解我们究竟是如何认知事物的，但同时又坚持认为，我们之所以认知事物，是因为它们的约定俗成。那么，就此而言，一个有趣的问题是：为什么我们有时会“不知道”或“不认识”某些事物呢？请注意，我们仍然将它们视为“非他物”；它们并非处于一种模糊不清的状态。换句话说，它们身份的系统性或情境性仍然清晰可见，但它们身份的本质仍然难以捉摸。不妨想象一下，一棵圣诞树让一位来自火星的访客感到困惑。访客清楚地看到它是一个符号，但仍然无法弄清楚它属于哪个符号系统。关键就在这里：当我们无法识别某个符号时，并非因为我们没有将其识别和处理为一个（差异化的、任意的）符号，而是因为我们无法识别出该符号得以被理解的符号系统。这反过来又表明，我们在更高层次上未能理解系统之系统，或者说，未能理解任何给定系统（作为构成其他系统单元的宏观单元）得以被理解的系统。

Much of the time in a course like this what we seem to be saying is that we can’t know anything. But that’s really never the case. What we’re talking about at this moment in particular is how we do know things. If we take semiotics seriously, it gives us a rather sophisticated means of understanding precisely how we know things, but insists at the same time that we know things because of their conventional nature. Interesting to ask in this regard why, then, we do not know, or recognize, things whenever that may occur. Note that we still know them as not-other-things; it’s not as though they’re in an undifferentiated blur. The systematicity or situatedness of their identity is still clear, in other words, yet the nature of their identity still eludes us. Think here of the Christmas tree puzzling a visitor from Mars. The visitor sees clearly that it’s a sign but still can’t figure out what system of signs it belongs to. That’s the key: when we fail to identify a sign, it’s not because we don’t recognize and process it as a (differential and arbitrary) sign but because we can’t identify the semiotic system in which the sign can become intelligible. This in turn suggests our higher-order failure to grasp the system of systems, as one might say, in which any given system, a gross constituent unit among other system-units, can become intelligible.

仅仅为了说“我们不认识语境”就大费周章？或许如此；但至少用符号学的术语来解释这个问题，能让我们对索绪尔声称已经创立一门科学的说法做出部分回应。“语境”在直觉上可以指引我们走得很远，甚至可以开创一些研究领域，但它也把我们推向了太多方向，就像索绪尔所说的对“言语”的研究一样，让我们​​——用他那不太雅观的比喻来说——无法真正站稳脚跟。

A lot of huffing and puffing merely to say “we don’t recognize the context”? Perhaps; but putting the matter in semiotic terms can at least allow us to meet the Saussurian claim to have founded a science half-way. “Context” can take us a long way intuitively, and can even authorize fields of research, but it pushes us in too many directions, like the study of “speech” according to Saussure, and doesn’t allow us—in his unlovely metaphor—to put both feet on anything in particular.

因此，符号系统的可理解性在于它们所共有的约定俗成性。正因如此，任何人都不可能随意将红灯改为“通行”的符号。同样，生态运动也使得任何人将绿灯改为“停止”的符号变得不可能。这些论述引出了另一个需要阐明的观点。正如索绪尔在讨论语言史中的“历时性变化”时所强调的，我们不能将个人意志强加于符号之上，符号的变化是通过用法的缓慢演变而非人为的命令来实现的。一个看似例外的情况是，有时个人似乎成功地运用影响力和声望，用新符号取代旧符号。杰西·杰克逊几乎凭借一己之力说服我们，即使“非裔美国人”这个表达冗长且音节繁多，我们也应该使用它。这似乎是一个有人抓住语言的衣领并将其改变的例子。然而，符号学家对此的解释是，这绝不可能是仅仅通过强加意志而发生的。这种改变必须得到认可。你需要使用语言惯例的社群认可这种用法的改变。记住，语言是共时存在的：它只存在于同时发生的瞬间。我们研究语言是历时性的——也就是说，我们研究它的历史，它随时间演变的过程。现在，根据符号学家的观点，这种演变过程的研究——这与俄国形式主义者的观点又有联系——并非将其视为语言从外部发生改变的方式，也就是蒂尼亚诺夫所说的“修改”，而是将其视为一系列共时性的切面。在每个切面，人们要么愿意以某种方式使用某个符号，要么不愿意。这才是关键：如果他们不愿意，符号的创新用法就无法确立，这证实了语言中没有任何东西可以通过个人意志来改变。

The intelligibility of sign systems, then, is their shared conventionality. That’s why it’s impossible for any individual to come along and make the red traffic light the symbol for “go.” The ecological movement has made it equally difficult for any individual to make the green light the symbol for “stop.” These remarks direct us to a further point that needs to be established. As Saussure insists in discussing “diachronic change” in the history of language, we cannot impose our individual will on signs, which change through glacial alterations of usage, not by fiat. A seeming exception is the fact that sometimes apparently individuals have successfully exerted influence and prestige to substitute new signs for old. Jesse Jackson almost single-handedly convinced us that we should use the expression “African American” even though it’s cumbersome and polysyllabic. That seems to exemplify somebody taking language by the scruff of the neck and changing it. The semiotician’s answer to this, though, is that it never could have happened simply as an imposition of will. It had to be acquiesced in. You need the community that makes use of linguistic conventions to acquiesce in a change of use. Remember, language exists synchronically: it exists only in a moment of simultaneity. We study language diachronically—that is to say, we study its history, its unfolding in time. Now according to the semioticians, this unfolding is studied—and here’s another link with the Russian formalists—not as the way language is changed from without, “modification” in Tynianov’s parlance, but rather as a sequence of synchronic cross-sections. At each cross-section, people are either willing to use a certain sign in a certain way or they’re not. That’s the crucial thing: if they’re not willing, the innovative use of the sign doesn’t take hold, which confirms the idea that nothing in language can be changed by individual fiat.

尽管做了这个最后的预告，共时性和历时性仍需进一步解释。我们将继续使用图表上的坐标，在这些坐标线上，共时性和历时性垂直于语言和言语，与句法和聚合，甚至隐喻和转喻平行。我们需要理解为什么纵轴上的很多内容都存在于虚拟空间，而横轴上的大部分内容却在实时中展开。所有这些，敬请期待。

Despite this last-minute preview, synchrony and diachrony remain to be explained. We’re going to keep using the coordinates on our diagram, along which the perpendiculars synchrony and diachrony are parallel, for example, to langue and parole, to the syntagmatic and the paradigmatic, even to metaphor and metonymy. We need to understand why so much that’s on the vertical axis is in virtual space while most of what’s on the horizontal axis unfolds in real time. All that’s to come.

 

 

第九章

CHAPTER 9

语言学与文学
Linguistics and Literature

阅读材料：

Readings:

列维-斯特劳斯，克劳德。“神话的结构研究。”载于《批判传统》，第 860-868 页。

Lévi-Strauss, Claude. “The Structural Study of Myth.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 860–868.

Jakobson, Roman. “语言学与诗学。”载于《批评传统》，第 871-874 页。

Jakobson, Roman. “Linguistics and Poetics.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 871–874.

雅各布森，罗曼。“两种类型的失语症和两种类型的语言障碍。”载于罗曼·雅各布森和莫里斯·哈勒，《语言基础》（海牙：穆顿出版社，1956 年），第 69-96 页。

Jakobson, Roman. “Two Types of Aphasia and Two Types of Language Disturbance.” In Roman Jakobson and Morris Halle, Fundamentals of Language (The Hague: Mouton, 1956), pp. 69–96.

为了准备对结构主义的讨论，我需要更详细地阐述共时性和历时性，也就是我们在上一讲结尾提到的二元对立概念。这对概念在我们的图表中分别对应纵轴和横轴，与俄国形式主义者关于文学史的思考特征相吻合。你可能还记得，形式主义者认为文学文本中某种修辞手法的“功能”有两个方面。一方面是共时功能，即该修辞手法与文本中所有其他修辞手法之间的关系；另一方面是自功能，即该修辞手法在文学史上持续存在和反复出现的方式，有时是主导性的，有时是潜在的或隐蔽的，但始终作为与其他变量相关的变量而存在。从共时功能的角度来看，三韵句有助于组织《神曲》，并在雪莱的《西风颂》和《生命凯旋》中通过对预言传统的暗示而再次出现。从功能上讲，三韵体在诗歌史上始终是一种潜在的或存在的诗节选择。

In preparation for a discussion of structuralism, I need to provide a fuller account of synchrony and diachrony, the binary pair with which we ended the last lecture. This pair, which maps onto the coordinates of our diagram as a vertical and a horizontal axis, corresponds with a feature of the Russian formalists’ thinking about literary historiography. You may remember from your reading that the formalists understood the “function” of a device in a literary text to have two facets. There is the syn-function, which is the relationship between that device and all of the other devices in a given text; but the same device has also an auto-function, which is the way in which the device persists and recurs throughout the history of literature, sometimes as the dominant, sometimes latent or recessive, but continuously present as a variable in relation to other variables. Syn-functionally, terza rima helps organize The Divine Comedy and resurfaces by way of allusion to a prophetic tradition in Shelley’s “Ode to the West Wind” and The Triumph of Life. Auto-functionally, terza rima is always either latent or present as a stanzaic option in the history of poetry.

在索绪尔语言学中，共时性和历时性之间的关系与俄国形式主义中的“同功能”和“自功能”之间的关系大体相似。将语言视为一个系统，意味着在特定时刻对其进行共时性考察。如果你关注的是语言随时间推移的发展和变化，你往往不会将语言视为一个系统。你会注意到，雅各布森似乎在符号系统的共时性分析中引入了时间因素，他认为必须同时考虑古老特征和创新特征，但要记住，在共时性横截面中，这些特征被标记为古老或创新，仅仅是相对于任何历史时刻的规范而言的（这种规范既向前又向后，但其本身并非时间性的），而不是相对于时间变化而言的。

In Saussurian linguistics, the relationship between synchrony and diachrony is largely parallel to that of syn-function and auto-function in Russian formalism. To consider language as a system is to consider it at a given moment synchronically. You tend not to think of language as a system if your focus is the way it develops and changes through time. Jakobson, you will notice, seems to introduce an element of time into the synchronic analysis of a semiotic system by saying that you’ve got to take into account both archaic and innovative features, but keep in mind that in a synchronic cross-section such features are simply flagged as archaic or innovative with respect to the norm of any historical moment (which looks both forward and backward without being itself temporal), not with respect to temporal change.

然而，一个系统在某一历史时期与前一个、后一个或任何其他历史时期的系统都不相同，这也是不争的事实。系统会随着时间而改变。符号系统、语言（langue ）、文学史、诗学史——无论是什么——都会随着时间而改变，当你反思这种随时间推移而发生的变化时，你就是在进行历时性的思考。

Yet it is also true that a system in one historical moment is not the same as that system in the previous, the next, or in any other historical moment. Systems change through time. A semiotic system, language (langue), the history of literature, the history of poetics—whatever it might be—changes through time, and when you reflect on that change through time you think of it diachronically.

索绪尔认为，从共时角度来看，某个事物（比如一个符号系统）各部分之间的关​​系并非必然，因为符号——系统的构成单元——是任意的，它们之间可能存在其他多种关系。但如果你从历时角度研究语言之类的符号系统，那么变化就是必然的，因为这种变化而非其他变化必然发生，且其原因并非其他。然而，历时变化虽然必然，却并非规律性的；它并非源于共时系统的结构，而是因为语言使用的某些方面由于各种难以概括的原因而发生了改变。当人们开始用“exuberant”（热情洋溢的）代替“gay”（快乐的），用“sinuous”（蜿蜒的）代替“plastic”（可塑的）时，这些变化反映了系统外部的各种压力，而这些压力与系统本身的结构无关。顺便一提，这种论点对传统语言学中的某些观点提出了挑战，例如大家可能都熟悉的“元音大移位”，它有时被认为是一种系统性的变化。然而，结构主义的语言观认为，元音大移位——即15世纪某个神秘的转折点上英语中所有元音音调都升高了一个音阶——表面上看似规律，但实际上是一种历时现象，或许与方言的地理迁移有关，因此不应被视为规律性的。所以，共时数据是规律性的，但并非必然；历时数据是必然的，但并非规律性的。

Saussure argues that the relationship among the parts of something viewed synchronically—a semiotic system, let’s say—are not necessary in the sense that—because the sign, the constituent unit of the system, is arbitrary—they might be any number of other relationships. But if you study a semiotic system such as language diachronically, change is necessary in the sense that that change and not some other change has perforce taken place for some reason and not for any other. Yet diachronic change, though necessary, is not regular; it doesn’t introduce itself with respect to the structure of synchronic system but rather because some aspect of language use has altered for any number of reasons that don’t lend themselves to generalization. When people start saying “exuberant” instead of “gay,” or “sinuous” instead of “plastic,” these modifications reflect various pressures on the system from without that don’t have to do with the system as a structure. This argument, by the way, poses a challenge to certain ideas in traditional linguistics such as the one you probably all know, “the Great Vowel Shift,” which is sometimes considered a systemic change. A structuralist’s view of language entails arguing, however, that the Great Vowel Shift, when every vowel sound in English went up a notch in pitch at some mysterious changeover moment in the fifteenth century, has only the appearance of regularity but is actually a diachronic phenomenon, perhaps having to do with the geographic movement of dialects, that should not be considered regular. So synchronic data is regular but not necessary; diachronic data is necessary but not regular.

在你的阅读中，当理论家们讨论如何从现有数据中推断语言系统或其他符号系统时，情况就变得有些复杂了，例如，我们如何从言语（parole）推断语言（ langue）。（实际上，我隐瞒了索绪尔引入第三个术语“语言”（langage）来指代所有言语的累积记录这一事实。我们暂且只讨论语言（langue）与言语（parole）之间的关系。）正如我们所说，语言（langue ）是一个被冻结在时间中的虚拟实体。正如我将在下文更详细地解释的那样，列维-斯特劳斯认为符号系统的场域可以在“可逆时间”中穿越，这意味着你可以在其中前后移动而不会改变其共时性特征。相比之下，言语（parole）在不可逆时间，或者说真实时间中展开，因为任何已说出的句子（无论是在言语中还是在完整的文本中）的开头必然先于结尾，并且逐个能指地在时间中展开。人们通常不会把言语视为历时性的，但严格来说，它就是历时性的。当人们在说话或写作过程中修改句子时，有时会回溯并重述某些内容，这种看似可逆的时间变化（语言学家称这种变化为“递归”），这种改变是必要的（它确实会发生），但并非规律性的（它的发生并非出于系统性的原因），并且最终会朝着听者或读者实时体验到的某个终点发展，因此，这种改变是历时的。即使是修改句子的人，在句子中也会回溯，但在实时时间中，它始终是向前发展的。

Matters are complicated somewhat on those occasions in your reading when theorists are talking about the way a system of language or other semiotic system is inferred from existing data, for example, the way we infer language, langue, from speech, parole. (I’m actually concealing from you the fact that Saussure brings in a third term, langage, to indicate the cumulative record of all speeches. We’ll stick to the langue-parole relation.) Langue as we have said is a virtual entity frozen in time. As I’ll explain more fully below, Lévi-Strauss says the field of a sign system can be traversed in “revertible time,” meaning you can move backward and forward within it without altering its synchronic character. By contrast, parole unfolds in nonrevertible time, or real time, in that the beginning of any uttered sentence (in speech or in a completed text) perforce comes before the end and unfolds, signifier by signifier, in time. One doesn’t ordinarily think of speech as diachronic, but strictly speaking that is what it is. When one changes a sentence in the course of speaking or writing, sometimes going back to restate something in what looks like revertible time (linguists call such changes “recursive”), this change is necessary (it happens) but not regular (it happens for a-systemic reasons) and builds toward an endpoint in real time experienced by an auditor or reader, hence diachronically. Even the person who revises goes back in the sentence but always forward in real time.

现在我们可以转向结构主义了。20世纪60年代初中期，当这一运动从法国传入美国时，许多人仿佛从教条的沉睡中醒来，几乎一夜之间意识到自己是理论家，或者渴望成为理论家。我在哈佛读研究生时就经历了这种情况，当时哈佛几乎无人关注结构主义。在耶鲁、约翰·霍普金斯和康奈尔，人们已经开始关注结构主义，但在哈佛，一位才华横溢的本科生查尔斯·萨贝尔（现为哥伦比亚大学社会科学和法学教授）引领我走进了结构主义的世界。我认为，他是剑桥唯一一个真正了解结构主义的人。

We can turn now to structuralism. When this movement arrived from France on the shores of the United States in the early and mid-1960s, many people awoke from their dogmatic slumbers and realized almost overnight that they were or wanted to be theorists. This happened to me when I was a graduate student at Harvard, where absolutely nobody else was paying any attention to structuralism. At Yale, Johns Hopkins, and Cornell, people were then taking notice, but at Harvard I was initiated into structuralism by a brilliant undergraduate, Charles Sabel (now a social science and law professor at Columbia), who was I think the only person in Cambridge who knew anything about it.

结构主义开启了文学理论蓬勃发展的诸多潮流，直至20世纪80年代末，其中包括美国人开始了解的法国精神分析（拉康的理论）以及路易·阿尔都塞等人的法国马克思主义。然而，令人惊讶的是，作为文学理论领域公认的重要贡献，结构主义竟然只持续了两年！在1966年约翰·霍普金斯大学举办的一次著名会议上（在我认识查尔斯·萨贝尔的几年前），雅克·德里达（我们接下来将要阅读他在那次会议上的发言）似乎彻底颠覆了结构主义，美国的理论界开始转向“解构”。尽管如此，说结构主义只持续了两年并不公平。结构主义深受符号学的影响，其深远的影响至今仍贯穿于整个文学理论领域。有很多影响深远的贡献，并非全部都发生在1964年（第一批结构主义著作被翻译成英文）到1966年（巴尔的摩会议召开）之间。罗兰·巴特的《论拉辛》是一部杰作。列维-斯特劳斯和雅各布森合著了一篇关于波德莱尔的论文《猫》（Les Chats）。人类学家埃德蒙·利奇对《圣经·创世记》进行了结构主义分析。事实上，他选择研究《创世记》并非偶然，这一点我稍后会提到。此外，语言学家尼古拉·特鲁别茨科伊、朱利安·格雷马斯、路易·叶尔姆斯列夫和埃米尔·本韦尼斯特也做出了重要的贡献。

Structuralism inaugurated all the trends that made literary theory a flourishing growth industry until the late 1980s, including French psychoanalysis as the Americans got to know Lacan and the French Marxism of Louis Althusser and others. Yet the amazing thing about it is that as an undisputed contribution to literary theory, structuralism lasted only two years! At a famous Johns Hopkins conference in 1966, several years before I met Charles Sabel, Jacques Derrida, whose contribution to that conference we’ll be reading next, appeared at least to have turned structuralism on its ear, and theory in the United States took up “deconstruction.” Nevertheless, to say that structuralism really only lasted two years is scarcely fair. The lasting effect of structuralism as it’s indebted to semiotics is something one still feels and senses throughout literary theory. The are many lasting contributions, not all of them between 1964, when the first structuralist texts were translated in this country, and 1966, when the conference in Baltimore took place. There’s a wonderful book called On Racine by Roland Barthes. There is an essay on Baudelaire, “Les Chats,” or “The Cats,” written conjointly by Lévi-Strauss and Jakobson. The anthropologist Edmund Leach wrote a structuralist analysis of Genesis in the Bible. Indeed, it’s no accident that he wrote about Genesis, as I will indicate later on. There is also important work by the linguists Nikolai Trubetzkoy, Julien Greimas, Louis Hjelmslev, and Emile Benveniste.

结构主义者最持久、最丰富的贡献或许体现在我们今天所知的“叙事学”领域。在结合弗洛伊德阅读彼得·布鲁克斯的著作时，我们会快速回顾一些叙事理论，但现在我只想提及罗兰·巴特在叙事学领域的重要著作：一篇名为《叙事的结构分析》的长篇论文，他在文中将詹姆斯·邦德小说视为一个二元对立系统；茨维坦·托多罗夫的重要著作，其中至关重要的是《十日谈的语法》 ；以及热拉尔·热奈特的《形象》系列著作，你会在即将阅读的保罗·德曼的著作中多次看到对热奈特的引用。所有这些著作以及叙事理论中的许多其他内容都直接受到结构主义思想的影响，或者本身就是结构主义思想的一个方面。

Probably the most lasting and rich contributions of the structuralists were in the field that we know as “narratology.” We’ll be passing some narrative theories in quick review when we read Peter Brooks’s text in conjunction with Freud, but for now I’ll just mention the key text in narratology by Roland Barthes: a long essay called “The Structural Analysis of Narrative” in which he approaches a James Bond novel as a system of binary pairs; important books by Tzvetan Todorov, crucial among them The Grammar of “The Decameron”; and a series of books called Figures by Gérard Genette, whom you will find quoted repeatedly in the work of Paul de Man that you’ll be reading soon. All of this work and a great deal else in the theory of narrative is directly indebted to or is an aspect of structuralist thought.

我曾承诺会阐述形式主义与符号学之间的关系，尤其是在克劳德·列维-斯特劳斯和罗曼·雅各布森等作家的著作中，这种关系是如何被阐明的。正如你从雅各布森——这位同时参与了这两个运动的人物——的著作中所看到的，结构主义从形式主义中汲取了“功能”的概念。同样，结构主义也从形式主义中衍生出共时功能和自功能之间的关系，它们分别对应着共时性和历时性。另一方面，符号学则带来了知识作为否定性差异的概念：例如，在列维-斯特劳斯对俄狄浦斯神话的分析中，不存在真实或原始的“版本”，不存在一个开创性的神话叙述，其他一切都只是它的衍生或变体，这种观点正是源于符号学中的否定时刻。这种将研究对象视为复合体、共时系统，而不是与某个特定词语相提并论，而是通过研究某一类对象的共同特征而产生的观念，是结构主义工作的基本前提。

I promised that I would describe the relationship between formalism and semiotics as it clarifies itself in the work of writers like Claude Lévi-Strauss and, in particular, Roman Jakobson. As you can see from reading Jakobson—the one figure who was involved in both movements—structuralism takes from formalism the idea of “function.” From formalism, too, structuralism derives the relationship between syn-function and auto-function, which become synchrony and diachrony. From semiotics on the other hand comes the concept of knowledge as negative differentiation: in Lévi-Strauss’s analysis of the Oedipus myth, for example, the notion that there is no true or originary “version,” no seminal account of the myth of which everything else is a derivative or variant, is inspired by the moment of negation in semiotics. This sense of the object of study as a composite, a synchronic system that is not to be identified with one particular parole but emerges from studying the common features of objects of a certain kind is the essential premise that characterizes the work of structuralism.

或许理解结构主义这一本质姿态的最佳途径，可以参考罗兰·巴特在《结构主义活动》（871）中的一句格言：“结构主义者获取现实，将其分解，然后重组。” 正是在这里，我们能够看到结构主义与形式主义的根本区别。形式主义并非为了重组而分解对象，而是将对象分解成各个组成部分，并展示它们彼此之间的功能关系。这种分析考察的是对象的“组合方式”——但这种结构只能从对象本身推导出来：例如果戈理的《外套》、塞万提斯的《堂吉诃德》、斯特恩的《项狄传》。而对于形式主义而言，数据可以积累，并且可以进行概括，例如，对陀思妥耶夫斯基的作品进行概括；但不存在根据对单个文本的观察来重新组合虚拟对象（例如“小说”）的问题。

Perhaps the best way to grasp this essential gesture of structuralism can be found in an aphorism by Roland Barthes in “The Structuralist Activity” (871): “Structural man takes the real, decomposes it, then recomposes it.” This is the moment in which you can see the radical difference between what structuralism is doing and what formalism is doing. Formalism doesn’t decompose its object in order to recompose it. It just breaks its object down into its respective devices, showing them functionally in relationship with each other. This sort of analysis considers the way the object is “put together”—but there’s no question of deducing this structure from anything other than that object: Gogol’s “Overcoat,” Cervantes’ Don Quixote, Sterne’s Tristam Shandy. For formalism, data does accumulate and one can generalize, for example, about the works of Dostoyevsky; but there’s no question of recomposing a virtual object, such as “the novel,” out of one’s observations of individual texts.

相反，正如巴特斯所说，“结构主义者将现实分解，然后重组。”他的意思是，将各种变体或版本汇集在一起​​，创造出一个数据体——不一定是所有数据，而是与任何给定的想法或概念相关的具有代表性的数据量——然后提出问题——列维-斯特劳斯正是在这里引入了“粗略构成单元”的概念——这些数据是否可以排列成一个有意义的模式，或者说“结构”。从这种构成特征的重新配置中产生的是一个虚拟对象，它重新组合了“现实”对象：在你读到的列维-斯特劳斯《结构人类学》的节选中，这个虚拟对象可以被称为俄狄浦斯神话的潜在意义。因此，结构主义像形式主义一样，将事物拆解开来，但并非仅仅为了了解它们的运作方式（就像拆解发动机的零件一样），而是为了将这些零件用于一种分析，从而揭示一个新的虚拟对象。

By contrast, as Barthes says, “Structural man takes the real, decomposes it, then recomposes it.” What he means is that you bring together variants or versions, you create a body of data, not necessarily all the data but a representative amount of the data relevant to any given idea or concept, and then you ask—and this is where Lévi-Strauss introduces the idea of gross constituent units—whether the data can be arranged in a significant pattern, or “structure.” What emerges from such a reconfiguration of constituent features is a virtual object recomposing the “real” one(s): in the case of the excerpt you have read from Lévi-Strauss’s Structural Anthropology, the virtual object might be called the underlying meaning of the Oedipus myth. Thus structuralism takes things apart, like formalism, not however just for the sake of seeing how they work, as when taking apart the parts of an engine, but rather in order to lend the parts to an analysis that reveals a new virtual object.

那么，让我们来看看列维-斯特劳斯关于俄狄浦斯神话的图表（如果你愿意这么称呼它的话）（864），并简单谈谈它。他考察了许多版本。我们暂且不去纠结究竟有多少个版本。顺便一提，他考察的版本数量远不及他研究北美印第安神话或他在田野调查期间作为人类学家研究的各种版本神话时那么多，但他确实考察了一些。其中一个是弗洛伊德的版本，一个是索福克勒斯的版本，还有其他一些。他注意到这些版本中存在一些反复出现的特征（事件、符号、词汇模式、仪式实践），并且它们可以归入不同的类别。这些特征可以排列成列，以表明共同的主题；而这些列又可以横向展开成行，以显示各列之间的相互关系。例如，有一系列事件、巧合和命名上的意外，可以归入“过度强调血缘​​关系”这一范畴。因此，当安提戈涅试图埋葬她的兄弟，并为此冒着生命危险，采取看似过激的极端手段时，这就是过度强调血缘​​关系的表现。然而与此同时，神话中也存在一系列行为——追溯到俄狄浦斯的祖先，并贯穿其后代的历史——这些行为却与对血缘关系的轻视有关。人们似乎并不像他们应该的那样重视血缘关系（在悲剧中，无知并非借口），结果酿成了悲剧，例如俄狄浦斯弑父与生母。

So let’s take a look at the Lévi-Strauss chart, if you want to call it that, of the Oedipus myth (864) and just say a word or two about it. He considers a lot of versions. Let’s not trouble ourselves with how many. He doesn’t have nearly as many versions by the way as he would have if he were studying a North American Indian myth or the sorts of myths that he did study in a variety of versions during his field work as an anthropologist, but he has some. One of them is Freud’s version, one is Sophocles’s, and there are others. He notes that there are recurrent features (events, symbols, lexical patterns, ritual practices) in these versions and that they fall into discrete categories. They can be placed in columns indicating a common theme; and these columns in turn can be cross-sectioned in horizontal rows that show how the columns interrelate. For example, there’s a cluster of events, happenstances, and accidents of naming that falls into a column called “over-determination of blood relations.” Thus when Antigone tries to bury her brother and risks everything in the attempt, going to extremes that seem excessive, that’s an overdetermination of blood relations. Yet at the same time, there’s a series of actions in the myth—reaching back into Oedipus’s ancestry and forward through the history of his offspring—that have to do with the undervaluation of blood relations. People don’t seem to care as much about blood relations as they should (ignorance being no excuse in tragedy), and bad things happen, as when Oedipus kills his father and sleeps with his mother.

然后还有一栏反映出——在所有版本中——一种对源于大地之物的奇特迷恋：卡德摩斯故事中散落在地上的怪物牙齿化作字母表；以及俄狄浦斯与斯芬克斯对峙时英雄们必须面对的各种怪物。所有这些怪物似乎并非由父母——两个生命体——所生，而是从它们所凶猛守护的大地中诞生。它们是地底的，或者如列维-斯特劳斯所说，“自生的”，意味着它们是从大地中自我诞生的。

Then there’s a column reflecting—in all the versions—a strange preoccupation with that which is born from the earth: the teeth of monsters that are scattered on the ground and spring forth as the alphabet in the story of Cadmos, and the variety of ways in which heroes have to confront monsters as Oedipus confronts the Sphinx. All of these monsters seem not to be born from parents—from two beings—but to have emerged rather from the earth of which they are fierce guardians. They are chthonic, or “autochthonous,” as Lévi-Strauss puts it, meaning they are self-born from the earth.

这个神话似乎对“自生性”有着一种奇特的执着，然而这种执着又被对它的强烈抵制所抵消（当然，也得到了强化），仿佛关键在于坚持认为存在着二元的亲子关系，这种关系孕育了我们，而“我们之中有一个人是由两个人所生”的观念则能让我们确信自身的人性。然而，这个神话也以截然相反的方式唤起了人们对“自生性”的思考。在俄狄浦斯的家谱中，许多人物的名字都以字母λ开头——例如拉布达库斯、拉伊俄斯等等——而λ这个字母在字符形式上看起来像一个跛脚的人。俄狄浦斯的意思是“肿胀的脚”、“跛脚的人”。第四栏所呈现的，是“自生性”的迹象不仅存在于怪物身上，也存在于我们自身的构成之中。我们跛行的原因在于我们脚底沾染了泥土，我们出生时所用的泥土的某些成分粘在我们身上，这在俄狄浦斯神话的展开中反复出现。值得注意的是，这是该神话传播到其他文化的少数几个例子之一。亚当，他的名字意为“红泥”，正是用取自大地的红泥创造出来的。

There seems to be a strange preoccupation with autochthony in this myth, yet this preoccupation is offset (but also of course reinforced) by the fierce resistance to it, as though the crucial thing were to insist on the binary parental relationship that produces us, to be reassured in our humanity by the idea that one of us is born from two. There are ways, however, in which the myth evokes autochthony in precisely the opposite way. Lambda, the letter that begins so many of the names of the figures in Oedipus’s genealogy—Labdacus, Laius, and others—in character form (λ) looks like a limping person. Oedipus means “swell foot,” “one who limps.” What emerges in the fourth column is the idea that there are signs of autochthony not just in monsters but within our own makeup. The reason we limp is that we have a foot of clay, that something of the earth from which we were born sticks to us, and this is a recurrent intuition in the unfolding of the Oedipus myth. Notice that this is one of those occasions on which the myth explodes into other cultures. Adam, whose name means “red clay,” is created from the red clay that has been taken from the earth.

所以，这就是四列：高估血缘关系、低估血缘关系、否认本土性以及坚持本土性。我暂时就说到这里，但我们稍后会回到这四列，探讨二与一在人类起源问题上的奇特关系。届时，我们会惊讶地发现——至少对我来说是这样！——列维-斯特劳斯的分析其实正是结构主义活动本身的寓言。当然，魔术师玩弄他的小卡片时，意义（而且是某种特定意义）的出现似乎具有必然性，这或许与分解重组的循环性有关，从而创造出一个虚拟的系统对象。请注意，我用虚线标出了这个对象的纵轴。你认为这四列是某种预先安排好的，这无可厚非。

So there you have your four columns: overvaluation of blood relations, undervaluation of blood relations, denial of autochthony, and persistence of autochthony. I’m going to leave it at that for now, but we’ll return to these columns to consider the curious issue of two versus one in relation to the problem of human origin, and at that point we’ll see to our astonishment—or at least to mine!—that Lévi-Strauss’s analysis turns out to be nothing other than an allegory of the structuralist activity itself. Of course the seeming inevitability with which not just meaning but meaning pointedly of a particular kind emerges from the games the magician plays with his little note cards may have something to do with the apparent circularity of decomposing in order to recompose, creating a virtual systemic object. Notice that I have made the vertical axis along which this object appears a dotted line. You cannot be blamed for thinking those four columns subject to some measure of prearrangement.

并非说列维-斯特劳斯的结论缺乏令人惊讶的力量。事实上，你可以通过思考他遗漏的、本可以轻松融入他所构建的框架中的一些内容来证实这些结论。伊俄卡斯忒上吊自杀，但他没有提及此事。它不在任何一列中，但显然与血缘关系的过度决定或决定不足有关——你可以自行选择。她因为犯了乱伦罪而感到内疚，因此她之前低估了血缘关系，现在却高估了它。俄狄浦斯出生时腿筋受伤，被遗弃在西塞隆山上。列维-斯特劳斯也没有提及此事，但显然这就是俄狄浦斯跛行如字母λ的原因。显然，他出生时腿筋受伤，并被发现于山上，仿佛他生于此地，这必然与本土性的持续存在有关。最后，在《俄狄浦斯在科罗诺斯》的结尾，俄狄浦斯死后被大地吞噬。你本​​是尘土，仍将归于尘土。这在俄狄浦斯神话中对应的是“我从哪里来，也将到哪里去”。因此，这张图表不仅适用于列维-斯特劳斯认为合适的内容，也适用于我们自己的思考。这应该让我们警惕，不要想当然地认为他排列这些卡片仅仅是随意之举。

Not that there isn’t a surprising amount of force in Lévi-Strauss’s conclusions. You can confirm them in fact by thinking of things he leaves out that would slip easily into the structure he has given us. Jocasta hangs herself, but he doesn’t mention that. It’s not in any of the four columns, yet obviously it has something to do—you can take your choice—with either the overdetermination or underdetermination of blood relations. She feels guilty because she committed incest, hence she underrated blood relations before and overrates them now. Oedipus at his birth is hamstrung and exposed on Mount Cithaeron. Lévi-Strauss doesn’t mention that either, but obviously that’s why Oedipus limps like the letter lambda. Plainly his hamstringing at birth and discovery on the mountain as though he had been born there must have something to do with the persistence of autochthony. Finally, at the end of Oedipus at Colonus, Oedipus is swallowed up by the earth when he dies. Dust thou art, to dust thou shalt return. The equivalent of this in the Oedipus myth is “where I came from is where I will go.” So the chart works not just for what Lévi-Strauss sees fit to mention but for what we can think of ourselves. That should put us on our guard against assuming that his arrangement of his note cards is just an arbitrary exercise.

当我转向雅各布森时，你可能会提出合理的异议：尽管我一直强调“分解以便重组”，但在《语言学与诗学》中却看不到这种做法。你或许认为雅各布森只是在进行形式主义论证。他将任何言语行为分解为六种功能。但雅各布森对诗歌功能（形式主义者称之为“文学性”）的概念做出了全新的贡献。我在此首次引用他的关键段落，并希望最终能将其解释为一种依赖于符号学的结构主义思想。这段话有点拗口（858）：“诗歌功能将等价原则从选择轴投射到组合轴。”那么，“等价原则”究竟是什么？它可以理解为雅各布森在《两种失语症》中所说的“隐喻”。1你可能还记得，在讨论符号学时，我提到过符号如何在图表的纵轴上聚集。“船”这个词在发音和意义上与某些词相似，在发音和意义上与另一些词截然不同，但它与某些词，例如“草地”，则没有特别密切的关系。某些符号，也就是说，会基于强烈的相似性或差异性，与其他某些符号聚集在一起，进入待选队列（记住，这就是“选择轴”）。这种聚集方式，使得一个符号可以隐喻地替代另一个符号，或者作为另一个符号的二元对立面，雅各布森称之为“等价原则”。

As I turn to Jakobson, it would be a fair objection on your part to remark that despite all this emphasis I’ve been throwing on “decomposing in order to recompose,” you don’t see that going on in “Linguistics and Poetics.” You may feel that Jakobson is just making a formalist argument. He breaks any speech act into six functions. But Jakobson has a decidedly new contribution to make to the notion of the poetic function, which the formalists would call “literariness.” I’ll just quote the key passage here for the first time and hope to explain it in the long run as a structuralist idea dependent on semiotics. It’s a mouthful (858): “The poetic function projects the principle of equivalence from the axis of selection into the axis of combination.” What, then, is “the principle of equivalence”? It can be understood as what Jakobson in “Two Types of Aphasia” calls “metaphor.”1 You’ll remember that in discussing semiotics I talked about how signs cluster in the vertical axis on our diagram. The word “ship” is similar to some words in sound and meaning and sharply dissimilar to others in sound and meaning, but has no particularly close relation to yet other words, such as “grassy,” for instance. Certain signs, that is, cluster with certain other signs in the queue to be selected (this is the “axis of selection,” remember) on the basis of strong similarity or dissimilarity. Those ways of clustering, so that one sign could substitute for another metaphorically or propose itself as the binary opposite of another, are what Jakobson calls “the principle of equivalence.”

如果这听起来过于模糊，或许最好完全避免使用差异或相似性这样的语言，而坚持使用近乎相同或对立的概念：几乎同义的符号，以及反义的符号，或因某种相互对立而彼此靠近的符号。当然，等价原则具有一定的弹性，正如韵律本身具有弹性一样。半韵可以替代全韵。因此，这些关系可以以各种方式延伸，但等价原则仍然是音素、词素或语素等符号彼此靠近的聚集方式。我们从语言中选择这类符号，并沿着“组合轴”将它们组合成语言的倾向，正是关注诗歌功能的人所关注的。如果口语或书面语似乎以各种等价关系为主，那么这种沿着组合轴展开的话语，是通过将等价原则（称之为隐喻，称之为相似或相异原则）从选择轴投射出来的：从语言作为一个系统所沿着的那个或许是虚拟的轴（再次注意虚线）投射到实际的组合轴，那个真实的轴——“真实”是因为没有人怀疑言语的存在——在这个轴上，语言不是一个系统，而是随着时间的推移而不断增强的符号的组合。

If that sounds too vague, maybe it’s better not to use the language of difference or similarity at all, but to insist on near-identity or opposition: signs that are virtually synonymous, and signs that are antonymic or brought into proximity by some other form of mutual opposition. Obviously, though, the principle of equivalence is somewhat elastic, just as versification is elastic. Slant rhyme can substitute for full rhyme. These relationships stretch in various ways, then, but the principle of equivalence remains the way in which signs understood as phonemes, lexemes, or tagmemes cluster in proximity to each other. The readiness with which we select signs of that kind from langue and combine them in the production of parole along “the axis of combination” is what a person attending to the poetic function looks for. If the spoken or written utterance seems to involve a predominance of equivalences of various kinds, then this utterance, which is unfolding on the axis of combination, results from having projected that principle of equivalence—call it metaphor, call it a principle of similarity or dissimilarity—from the axis of selection: from that perhaps virtual axis along which language is a system (note again the dotted line) to the actual axis of combination, that real axis—“real” because nobody doubts the existence of speech—along which language is not a system but a combination of signs augmented through time.

因此，诗歌功能，或者说将等价原则投射到组合轴上，赋予了原本属于转喻的组合过程以隐喻倾向。正如我们在阅读德曼的作品时将看到的，在这个词汇体系中，“转喻”有两个不同但相关的含义。在一种意义上，如果我组合一个陈述句，我所做的只是将一些词语并列在一起，因为它们在语法和句法上契合，但并没有特别注意意义上的平行或语音上的重复。还有一种修辞手法——你可能很熟悉——即用间接相关但并非同义词或隐喻的词语相互替代。转喻可以看作是一组广泛关联的符号，它们根据语法和句法规则以及逻辑规则恰当地并列在一起，同时也符合修辞手法的前提。如果我选择用“小屋”而不是“房子”来造句——我举的例子实际上出自雅各布森的《失语症》一文——比如我说“小屋很小”，那么它就隐含着与房屋、棚屋、豪宅和其他建筑物之间的转喻关系，但这种关系或许只能通过句子本身的组合逻辑来真正解决，正是这种逻辑促使我几乎是多余地说出“小屋很小”。因此，对于诗意功能并非主导的日常话语而言，组合过程——借用修辞术语“转喻”来指用一个符号替换一个不等价但相邻的符号——本质上就是转喻。

Thus the poetic function, or projection of the principle of equivalence onto the axis of combination, imposes metaphoric tendencies on a combinatory process that would otherwise be metonymic. Metonymy in this vocabulary, as we’ll see also when we read de Man, has two different but related senses. In one sense, if I put together a declarative sentence, what I’m doing is putting words next to each other because they are a smooth fit grammatically and syntactically but without special attention to parallels in meaning or repetition in sound. There’s also the rhetorical device—with which you’re probably familiar—whereby obliquely related but not synonymous or metaphoric words substitute for each other. Metonymy is a broadly connected group of signs, if you will, that go appropriately next to each other according to the rules of grammar and syntax and according to the rules of logic, but also in keeping with the premise of the rhetorical device. If I choose “hut” instead of “house” for my sentence—I’m using an example actually taken from Jakobson’s “Aphasia” essay—saying something like “The hut is small,” there is a metonymic relationship implied with houses, shacks, mansions, and other sorts of edifice, but which can only really be resolved, perhaps, by the combinatory logic of the sentence that moves me to say, almost redundantly, “The hut is small.” So for ordinary utterances in which the poetic function is not the dominant, combinatory processes—borrowing the rhetorical term “metonymy” as the substitution of one sign for a nonequivalent but adjacent sign—are basically metonymic.

现在让我们把雅各布森的六种功能放在一起来看。我认为这些观察并不难理解，而且我发现雅各布森对这六种功能的分析严密而全面。关于话语，似乎没什么可说的了。当然，在不同的语域中有很多可以讨论的内容，但按照雅各布森的分析精神，你对此几乎无可挑剔——或许只有一个例外，我稍后会提到。

Now let’s look at Jakobson’s six functions taken all together. I think these observations are by no means difficult, yet I also find Jakobson’s analysis of the six functions to be airtight and exhaustive. There isn’t much else to say about an utterance. Obviously in different registers there are lots of things to say, but in the spirit of Jakobsonian analysis there’s no possible complaint you can make about this—except possibly one, to which I’ll return.

为了证明任何话语都必须包含这六种功能，我费尽心思地找到了一句最无趣的表达。我的证明文本——请尽量克制住你的激动——是“下雨了”。你可以看到，在图中，我们有：一个指向说话者的情感集合；一个指向听话者的意动集合（试图命令或说服）；一个指向语境的指称集合；一个指向寒暄的交际集合（试探、一二三）；一个指向语码的元语言集合（母马指的是雌马）；以及一个指向信息本身的诗意集合。

For a proof text, I’ve been at some pains to find the most uninteresting possible expression in order to show that any utterance whatsoever must entail these six functions. My proof text—try to contain your excitement—is “It is raining.” You see on the diagram that we have a “set” to the addresser that is emotive, a set to the addressee that is conative (an attempt to command or convince), a set to the context that is referential, a set to the contact that is phatic (testing, one, two, three), a set to the code that is metalingual (a mare is a female horse), and a set to the message itself that is poetic.

假设我是一位浪漫主义抒情诗人，我说——如果我是一位诗人，这或许有些不合时宜——“下雨了。”我的意思是什么呢？嗯，可能是“我在雨中歌唱”或者“我的心中在下雨”。换句话说，我说“下雨了”这句话，表达了一种情感，实现了雅各布森所说的情感功能。

So let’s say I am an addresser who is a romantic lyricist. I say—probably ill-advisedly if I’m a poet—“It is raining.” What do I mean? Well, probably either “I’m singing in the rain” or “It’s raining in my heart.” In other words, I’m expressing something emotional in saying “It is raining,” fulfilling the sense of the expression in what Jakobson calls the emotive function.

现在，说话者正在对某人说话。信息的重点在于听话人。一个小女孩没穿外套就出门了，她的父母说：“下雨了”，意思是“穿上外套”。他们不一定非要说“穿上外套”，而是说“下雨了”，这样就满足了表达的意愿功能。

Now someone is being addressed. The thrust of the message is toward the addressee. A small child is going out the door without her coat on, and her mother or father says, “It is raining,” which means “Put your coat on.” They don’t necessarily say, “Put your coat on.” They say, “It is raining,” and that fulfills the sense of the expression in the conative function.

任何话语都有其现实语境。这一点我想我们都不会否认。我是一名气象学家。我看着图表，自信地对着麦克风宣布：“下雨了。”大家都认真对待我的话。“下雨了”这句话的指称功能在于传递信息。如果权威人士说这句话时，指称功能占据主导地位，我就会相信“下雨了”。我并不指望气象员在说“下雨了”的时候，暗含着高兴或不高兴的情绪。我所期待的——因此我听到的——仅仅是一个关于天气的事实。

There’s a real-world context for any utterance. This much I suppose none of us would think to disagree with. I’m a meteorologist. I look at my charts and announce confidently through the microphone, “It is raining.” Everybody takes me seriously. The referential function of “It is raining” is supposed to convey information. If the referential function predominates in the utterance when spoken by an authority, I believe that it is raining. I don’t expect the weatherman to be telling me covertly that he’s happy or unhappy when he says “It is raining.” All I expect—hence all I hear—is a fact about the weather.

现在来说说“建立联系”：雅各布森举了多萝西·帕克对约会的描述，里面有很多精彩的例子：嗯，我们在这儿，是啊，我们在这儿，是啊，我们当然在这儿，等等；换句话说，你处于一种极度紧张的状态，因为在约会却不知道该说什么，所以你胡乱地说话。于是你说：“下雨了。”对方当然会说：“是啊，下雨了。”你又说：“雨下得很大。”她又说：“嗯，是啊。也许一会儿就停了。”于是对话磕磕绊绊地进行着，这就是“寒暄”的功能，确认联系是否正常：你能听到我说话吗？你根本不在乎是不是在下雨；你只是想确认电路是否通畅。如果我是一位物理学家，和另一位物理学家约会，我说“E等于MC²”，我并不是在宣告或宣布“E等于MC²”，这几乎没有必要；我只是在用语言填充空气。这就是沟通的本质，任何信息在合适的语境下都具有这种功能，就像任何信息在合适的语境下都具有其他五种功能一样。

Now “the set to the contact”: Jakobson gives you wonderful examples from Dorothy Parker’s representation of a date: Well, here we are, yeah, here we are, yeah, we sure are here, and so on; in other words, you’re in a state of abject and acute nervousness filling the air with words because you’re on a date and you can’t think of anything to say. So you say, “It is raining,” and of course your interlocutor says, “Yeah, it’s raining,” and you say, “It’s raining hard,” and she says, “Well, yeah. Maybe it’ll stop soon.” So the conversation stumbles along, and that’s the “phatic” function, checking to make sure the contact is working: can you hear me? You don’t care at all whether it’s raining; you just want to make sure the circuitry is working. If I’m a physicist out on a date with another physicist and I say, “E equals MC-squared,” I’m not declaring or announcing that “E equals MC-squared,” which would scarcely be necessary; I’m filling the air with words. This is the set to the contact, and any message in the right speaking situation has that function, just as any message in the right speaking situation has any of the other five functions.

当我们不确定在特定场合下与他人是否理解某个词语的含义时，就会触发这种“代码设置”，所以我们会避免直接表达，而是先仔细斟酌，确保自己所说的内容清晰明确。比如，我说：“田里有一匹母马。” 有人问：“母马是什么？” 我说：“嗯，就是雌马。” 作为一种定义，这就是元语言功能。但我们的论证文本是“正在下雨”。这就变得很有意思了。这个“它”究竟是什么？它既可以是“正在下雨”的定义，也可以是雨的来源。其他语言也有类似的奇特现象：“Il pleut”（下雨），“Es regnet”（下雨）。“il”是什么？“es”是什么？“它”又是什么？是上帝吗？是木星普鲁维乌斯吗？是云层吗？也许它指的是云层，但我们感觉“它”指的并非如此。 “It”是一种语法和句法异常现象，即使是语言学家也很难分析和解释；所以，当我试图用“It is raining”来蒙混过关时，如果我和一个字面主义者交谈，我就可以预料到元语言功能会突然冒出来，狠狠地咬我一口。

The set to the code is when we’re not sure that we share the meaning of words with another person on a given occasion, so we back away from simply saying things to make sure that what we’re saying is clearly defined. I say, “There’s a mare in the field.” Somebody says, “What is a mare?” “Well, it’s a female horse.” As a definition, that is the metalingual function. But our proof text is “It is raining.” This is where it really gets interesting. What on earth is this “it” that is either the definition of “is raining” or the source of the rain? Other languages have this same weird phenomenon: “Il pleut,” “Es regnet.” What is “il”? What is “es”? What is “it”? Is it God? Is it Jupiter Pluvius? Is it the cloud canopy? Maybe it is the cloud canopy, yet we feel that that’s not what’s meant by “it.” “It” is a kind of grammatical and syntactical anomaly that is difficult even for linguists to analyze and to explain; so when I try to get away wth saying “It is raining,” if I am talking to a literalist I can expect the metalingual function to come running up and bite me in the shin.

与元语言功能不同，“It is raining”的诗意功能实在乏善可陈。这是这个例子唯一的不足之处。但即便如此，仍有值得探讨之处：“ih-ih”和“ raining ”中的双“ih” ，这些单音节强化了快速的宣告，随后又营造出一种持续感，就像人们望向窗外时所感受到的那样：“It is rainnnnnnning”，单词的延长传递了一种语义价值。即便有那么多“ i ”，要让诗意功能占据主导地位，对任何想要这样做的人来说都是一项艰巨的任务，正如我之前所说，如果一位浪漫主义抒情诗人说“It is raining”，那他/她就显得不够聪明。但我重申：任何话语中的任何功能，只要找到合适的语境，都可以成为主导功能。

Unlike the metalingual function, the poetic function of “It is raining” is unfortunately not very interesting. That’s the one drawback of this example. But there’s still something to say: “ih-ih” and the double “ih” in raining, the monosyllables reinforcing quick declaration followed by a sense of duration that one may have when looking out the window: “It is rainnnnnnning,” with the prolongation of the word conveying a kind of semantic value. To make the poetic function to be the dominant—even with all those i’s—would be taxing for anyone who wanted it to be, as I suggested when I said a romantic lyricist wouldn’t be very smart if he or she said, “It is raining.” But I repeat: any function in any utterance could be the dominant if the right situation were found for it.

这或许足以作为对雅各布森话语六重结构的分析。当诗性功能占据主导地位，从而产生雅各布森标题中“语言学中的诗学”时，它反映的是一种隐喻而非转喻的结构，因为我们观察到某种来自选择轴的压力，以及其等价原则，影响着组合的方式。还有什么比“下雨了”更平淡无奇的呢？然而，你突然会注意到那串“ i ”，重复的单音节词，以及其他一些细节。即使是最平庸的话语，其组合方式也能让我们观察到组合中的自指性（“与信息相契合”）。正如雅各布森所指出的，我们说“无辜的旁观者”而不是“漠不关心的证人”，是因为前者是一个双扬抑格；但如果我们说“漠不关心的旁观者”，我们或许会突然疑惑，为什么人群中所有这样的面孔都像是双音节诗。语言有一种奇妙的魔力，当它被运用到言语中时，便会变得诗意盎然。

This may suffice as an analysis of the sixfold structure of an utterance in Jakobson. When the poetic function dominates, giving rise to the poetics within the linguistics of Jakobson’s title, it reflects a metaphoric as opposed to a metonymic structure insofar as we observe some kind of pressure from the axis of selection, with its principle of equivalence, bringing itself to bear on the way in which the combination takes place. What could be more prosaic than “It is raining”? Yet all of a sudden you notice that string of i’s, the repetition of like monosyllables, and perhaps other things. The way even the most banal utterance is combined can lend itself to the observation of self-reference in the combination (the “set to the message”). As Jakobson points out, we say “innocent bystander” and not “unconcerned witness” because the former is a double dactyl; but if we said “unconcerned spectator,” we might suddenly find ourselves wondering why all such faces in the crowd are double dactyls. Language has an uncanny way of going poetic on us when speech makes use of it.

你或许会反驳说我没有展示雅各布森是如何“解构以重组”的。好吧，除了建议你读读他和列维-斯特劳斯合著的关于波德莱尔《猫》的文章（其中一首十四行诗被重构为一种深奥的、基于声音的主题，与诗歌逐行展开的论证几乎毫无关联）之外，我认为我可以说，雅各布森重组的是一种悬浮在组合轴之上和之内的、虚幻的选择轴。在构成能指的诗行中，尤其是在诗歌功能占据主导地位的情况下，我们可以将其视为一行，而每行诗行中都存在一个虚拟的“列”，由所有未被选中但本可被选中的、具有隐喻关联的能指组成。在《两种失语症：隐喻与转喻》一文中，隐喻一端的失语症使得组合轴成为选择轴一种经常不连贯的复制品。这的确是一种神经生理紊乱，但正如雅各布森经常提醒我们的那样，这也是诗人身上常见的倾向。

You may still object that I haven’t shown how Jakobson “decomposes in order to recompose.” Well, apart from urging you to read his essay with Lévi-Strauss on Baudelaire’s “Les chats” (in which a sonnet is reconstructed as a deep sound-based thematics having little or nothing to do with the unfolding of the poem’s argument from line to line), I think I can say that what’s recomposed in Jakobson is a phantom axis of selection hovering above and within the axis of combination. Everywhere along a composed line combining signifiers, which one can think of as a row, especially where the poetic function is the dominant, one senses above and below each new signifier the virtual column consisting of all the metaphorically related signifiers that were not selected but could have been. And in “Two Types of Aphasia: Metaphor and Metonymy,” the aphasic disorder at the metaphoric pole makes the axis of combination a kind of frequently incoherent duplicate of the axis of selection. This is indeed a neurophysiological derangement, yet it is also, as Jakobson frequently reminds us, a tendency that one finds in poets.

现在我终于可以提出一个异议了，一个微不足道的异议，雅各布森本人也试图反驳，但这确实引出了一个更普遍的问题。我想提请各位注意一个问题，在我看来，雅各布森在梳理六种功能方面，思路非常精妙，但却存在一个问题。他似乎在探讨诗歌功能和元语言功能之间的关系，以及信息集和代码集之间的关系时，有所停顿：

Now I’ve actually reached the point at which I could raise an objection, a niggling objection in itself that Jakobson actually attempts to counter but that does bring to mind a more general question. Let me call your attention to one problem in what seems to me otherwise to be a truly remarkable exercise of thought in sorting out the six functions. Jakobson pauses over the relationship between the poetic function and the metalingual function, between the set to the message and the set to the code:

或许有人会反对（是的，我们在此提出反对意见），元语言在将同义词组合成等式句时，也同样会按顺序使用等价单位：A = A（“母马是马的雌性”）。然而，诗歌和元语言恰恰相反：在元语言中，顺序被用来构建等式（换句话说，是为了证明一个术语可以用其他术语来理解），而在诗歌中，等式被用来构建顺序。
It may be objected [Yes, here we are objecting] that metalanguage also makes a sequential use of equivalent units when combining synonymic expressions into an equational sentence: A = A (“Mare is the female of the horse”). Poetry and metalanguage, however, are in diametrical opposition to each other: in metalanguage the sequence is used to build an equation [in other words, to prove that one term can be understood in terms of other terms], whereas in poetry the equation is used to build a sequence.

从某种意义上说，这当然没错。也就是说，我知道自己何时在说元语言，何时在说诗。也许你也知道，但雅各布森实际上触及了结构主义的痛点，因为他诉诸于意图：他认为元语言表达具有一种意图，而诗歌表达具有另一种意图。如果真是如此，那么话语就有了起源；它们源于一种意图意识，正如在非结构主义的传统中，甚至在那些与结构主义相悖的传统中，事物的起源在于先前的原因，而非两个事物之间的否定关系——二元对立。换句话说，如果结构主义本身就是对起源的批判，就像埃德蒙·利奇对圣经文本《创世记》的分析那样，就像列维-斯特劳斯对俄狄浦斯神话的理解那样（俄狄浦斯神话是由二而非一产生的） ——那么，如果结构主义是对起源的批判，当你必须根据其起源（即它们背后的意图）来区分系统中的两个实体，即诗歌功能和元语言功能时，会发生什么呢？

Now in one sense this is true, obviously. That is, I know when I’m speaking metalanguage and when I’m speaking poetry. Maybe you know it, too, but what Jakobson has actually done is exposed a structuralist nerve, because he has appealed to intention: he has said the metalingual expression has one intention and the poetic expression has another intention. If this is the case, utterances have a genesis; they have an origin in an intending consciousness, just as in traditions that are not structuralist, traditions indeed opposed to structuralism, things have origins in prior causes and not in the negative relationships between two things—binary pairs. In other words, if structuralism is in itself a critique of genesis, as is the case with Edmund Leach’s analysis of the biblical text Genesis, as is the case certainly with Lévi-Strauss’s understanding of the Oedipus myth, born from two and not from one—if structuralism then is a critique of genesis, what happens when you have to make a distinction between two entities in your system, the poetic function and the metalingual function, in terms of their genesis—that is, of the intention that stands behind them?

正如我所说，这个例子看似微不足道，因为我们都非常乐意同意雅各布森的观点，即我们一眼就能看出元语言功能和诗歌功能的区别，但他实际上并没有说我们一眼就能看出区别。如果他直接说任何人都能分辨出什么是元语言功能，什么是诗歌功能，或许会更稳妥一些。但他实际上是说，元语言功能的目的是使序列等式化，而诗歌功能的目的是使等式序列化。如果我是一匹会说话的马，正在给我的爱人写情书，我可能会热情洋溢地写道：“Mare is the female of the horse”：抑扬格-扬抑格-抑扬格，用相对的脚拥抱“女性”，并借用“mère”的同音词，暗示着俄狄浦斯情结，一举两得。

As I said, the example seems trivial because we’re all more than prepared to agree with Jakobson that we know the difference when we see it between the metalingual and the poetic functions, but he’s not actually saying we know the difference when we see it. Maybe it would have been safer if he had just said anybody can see what’s metalingual and what’s poetic. But what he says instead is that the metalingual is intended to do one thing, to make a sequence equational, and the poetic is intended to do another thing, to make it an equation sequential. If I were a talking horse writing a valentine to my sweetheart, I might very well rhapsodize, “Mare is the female of the horse”: dactyl-trochee-anapest, embracing the “female” with opposed feet, with an Oedipal suggestion thrown in by way of the homonym for “mère,” two for one.

然而，一旦我们看到了问题所在，我们可能就会对所有六种功能产生类似的怀疑。我站在你面前说：“下雨了。”你怎么知道我的意图？我是紧张地客套话；我是不高兴还是高兴；我是觉得你疯了，因为外面确实在下雨，但我没看到任何人穿外套；还是我其实是个伪装成英语教授的气象学家？你必须推断出我的意图。如果你这样做是为了做出这些区分，那么结构主义坚持认为知识是由结构决定的（这是否定的），而不是由基因决定的（这是肯定的），这种观点又该如何完整地保留下来呢？我把这个反问留给你们自己思考。

Once we see the problem, however, we may have a comparable doubt about all six functions. I stand here in front of you and say, “It is raining.” How do you know what I intend? Whether I’m nervous and just being phatic; whether I am unhappy or happy; whether I think you’re crazy because it is, in fact, raining outside and I don’t see any coats; or whether I am actually a meteorologist masquerading as an English professor? You have to infer an intention. If you do so in order to make these distinctions, how can the structuralist insistence on structural determination of knowledge (which is negative) rather than genetic determination of knowledge (which is positive) be preserved intact? I leave you with this rhetorical question to explore on your own.

对列维-斯特劳斯的批判我将推迟到下一讲，因为你们会发现你们正在阅读的德里达的文章《人文科学语言中的结构、符号和游戏》主要讲的是列维-斯特劳斯，所以自然而然地会过渡到解构主义，先回到列维-斯特劳斯论证的某些方面。

The critique of Lévi-Strauss I will defer until the next lecture because you’ll find that the essay by Derrida that you’re reading, “Structure, Sign, and Play in the Language of the Human Sciences,” is largely about Lévi-Strauss, so it will make a natural segue to deconstruction first to return to certain aspects of Lévi-Strauss’s argument.

 

 

第十章

CHAPTER 10

解构 I

Deconstruction I

雅克·德里达

Jacques Derrida

阅读：

Reading:

德里达，雅克。“人文科学话语中的结构、符号和游戏”和“差异”。载《批判传统》，第 915-925 页，932-939 页。

Derrida, Jacques. “Structure, Sign, and Play in the Discourse of the Human Sciences” and “Différance.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 915–925, 932–939.

本次讲座我们将探讨一位在阅读中最具影响力和最令人敬畏的人物。在雅克·德里达去世前后（2004年），他因转向伦理和政治议题而再次受到关注。他从未放弃早期的思想或他那出了名的晦涩难懂的文风，而是调整了这些标志性特征以迎合进步人文主义者的兴趣。尤其与意大利哲学家乔治·阿甘本一起，晚期德里达被认为是文学及其他领域理论研究中所谓的“伦理转向”的代表人物，而这一转向在当下尤为重要。因此，由于他晚期的著作，德里达的声誉——在20世纪80年代末期，随着解构主义在学术界（不再仅仅局限于公共报刊）遭受或多或少的理论攻击而一度岌岌可危——如今又重回巅峰。然而，我们本次讲座所阅读的材料则要早得多，属于他早期影响的范畴。

In this lecture we confront one of the most formidable and influential figures in our reading. In the years preceding and since his recent death (2004), Jacques Derrida has enjoyed a second vogue on the strength of having turned to ethical and political issues. He never repudiated his earlier thinking or his notoriously involuted style, but he adapted these signatures to the interests of progressive humanists. Together with the Italian philosopher Giorgio Agamben in particular, late Derrida is associated with what’s called “the ethical turn” in theoretical approaches to literature and other matters that is very much of the current moment. Hence owing to his latest books, Derrida’s reputation, endangered when deconstruction came under more or less theoretical attack during the late 1980s within the academy (no longer just in the broadsides of the public press), is very high again today. The materials that we are reading for this lecture date back much earlier, however, and belong to an earlier sphere of influence.

德里达的论文《人文科学语言中的结构、符号与游戏》发表于1966年约翰·霍普金斯大学举办的“人类科学”研讨会上。此次研讨会意在为克劳德·列维-斯特劳斯加冕，他的著作被视为一门“科学”，几年前才在美国学术界崭露头角。列维-斯特劳斯本人也出席了研讨会，他发表了演讲，也坐在听众席中；但德里达的演讲被广泛认为是对其的“废黜”，而非加冕，列维-斯特劳斯本人也持相同看法。列维-斯特劳斯于2009年去世，享年101岁。晚年，他对自己的著作被后来的发展所取代感到无比愤慨。

The essay “Structure, Sign and Play in the Language of the Human Sciences” was delivered during a conference about “the sciences of man” at Johns Hopkins University in 1966. The event was intended as a kind of coronation of Claude Lévi-Strauss, whose work, understood as a “science,” had burst upon the American scene only a few years earlier. Lévi-Strauss was there. He gave a talk, he was in the audience; but Derrida’s talk was widely viewed, not least by Lévi-Strauss, to be a dethroning rather than a coronation. Lévi-Strauss, who died in 2009 at the age of 101, expressed great bitterness in his old age about the displacement of his own work by what happened subsequently.

很容易将矛头指向德里达的演讲（我并不清楚列维-斯特劳斯是否曾这样做过），但思考这场演讲以及德里达的整体作品——乃至解构主义本身——所面临的诸多难题之一，在于如何判断它与结构主义的背离究竟有多彻底。在思考自身结构方法时，德里达表现出一种自觉，甚至带有反讽意味，这种自觉，我们在列维-斯特劳斯的作品中也经常看到，而德里达在他的文章中也坦然承认了这一点。德里达反复引用列维-斯特劳斯的论述来佐证自己的观点，但随后又指出，即使在列维-斯特劳斯最谨慎的表述中，也存在一些尚未被充分思考的内容，或者至少在其其他作品中没有被充分思考过。《结构、符号与游戏》绝非对列维-斯特劳斯的全面否定，甚至算不上是一次毁灭性的批判。我认为，德里达承认，他作为思想家，在多大程度上是站在列维-斯特劳斯的肩膀上的。

It is easy to blame Derrida’s lecture (I am not aware that Lévi-Strauss ever did), but one of the million complications in thinking about this lecture and about Derrida’s work in general—and, for that matter, about deconstruction—is deciding how absolute its departure from the work of structuralism really is. There is a self-consciousness, even irony, in thinking about his own approach to structure that we find frequently in Lévi-Strauss and that Derrida freely acknowledges in his essay. Again and again Derrida quotes Lévi-Strauss in confirmation of his own arguments, only then to point out that there is something in what Lévi-Strauss is saying even at his most circumspect that hasn’t quite been thought through, or at least not thought through elsewhere in his oeuvre. “Structure, Sign, and Play” is not anything like a wholesale repudiation or even a very devastating critique of Lévi-Strauss. Derrida, I think, supposes that he is acknowledging the degree to which he stands as a thinker on the shoulders of Lévi-Strauss.

无论如何，对于美国理论研究者而言，这一非同寻常的转折点事件几乎在一夜之间引发了一场从结构主义向解构主义的革命。这场革命——尽管伴随着广泛、多元且广为人知的敌意——在整个20世纪70年代和80年代初仍然是理论界的主导范式。德里达是这一时期两位关键人物之一，多年来他每年春季学期都会到耶鲁大学访问。当时一位评论家称之为耶鲁存在“诠释学黑手党”的说法，很大程度上源于德里达以及保罗·德曼、J·希利斯·米勒，还有与他们联系较为松散的杰弗里·哈特曼和哈罗德·布鲁姆的存在。

In any case, however, this extraordinary crossroads event for people thinking about theory in the United States did effect an almost overnight revolution away from structuralism toward deconstruction, a revolution that remained—amid widespread, diverse, and well-publicized hostility—the reigning paradigm in theory throughout the 1970s and the early 1980s. Derrida, one of the two key figures during this period, was for many years an annual visitor at Yale for part of the spring term. The notion that there was what one critic then called a “hermeneutical mafia” at Yale arose largely from the presence of Derrida together with Paul de Man, J. Hillis Miller, and—more loosely connected with them—Geoffrey Hartman and Harold Bloom.1

这个群体构成了所谓的“耶鲁学派”。它在某些圈子里产生了非凡的影响力，但同时也招致了前所未有的强烈愤怒。这与至今仍被称为“人文危机”的现象密切相关。如今，州议员和大学理事会比以往任何时候都更加坚信，解构主义从未消退，人文学科不应再获得资助，因为后结构主义的拥护者已经摧毁了西方文明的根本价值观。再加上对美国科学竞争力的恐慌，以及美国就业市场亟需补充科学家这一毋庸置疑的现实，这些因素共同导致了大学人文学科，乃至中学人文学科的严峻困境。

That group comprised the so-called Yale school. It generated extraordinary influence in some circles, while at the same time drawing down upon itself an outpouring of unprecedented anger. This had to do with what is still sometimes called “the crisis in the humanities.” State legislators and boards of trustees believe today more than ever that deconstruction has never gone away and that the humanities should no longer be funded because the apostles of poststructuralism have destroyed the foundational values of Western civilization. That together with panic about the competitiveness of American science and the undoubted need to restock the lagging American workplace with scientists has brought on severe hard times for the humanities in the universities, not to mention in secondary education.

所以你读完了一篇完整的文章和另一篇《差异》的一部分，觉得德里达的思想非常晦涩难懂。事实上，除了觉得他晦涩难懂之外，你可能还恼火地想，他为什么非要用这种方式写作。你明白他是一位富有挑战性的思想家，但怀疑他把自己搞得比实际需要的更难懂。你尤其不明白，他为什么不一次只说一件事。你甚至可能承认，这一切都是他有意为之，解构作为一种思维过程，是一种回避式的舞蹈，在这种舞蹈中，人们拒绝接受明确的立场，拒绝接受任何可能被一个笼统的术语所支配的结论——这正是《结构、符号与游戏》的核心所在——即被德里达常说的“先验所指”。但你仍然对他的写作风格感到不满。

So you have read all of one essay and part of another, “Différance,” and you’ve found Derrida very difficult. Indeed, in addition to finding him very difficult, you’ve probably wondered irritably why he has to write like that. You can see that he’s a challenging thinker but suspect that he’s making himself more difficult than he needs to be. You wonder in particular why he doesn’t just say one thing at a time. You may even acknowledge that it’s all deliberate on his part, that as a thought process deconstruction is a kind of evasive dance whereby one refuses to settle for distinct positions, for any sort of conclusion that could be governed—this is what “Structure, Sign, and Play” is all about—by a blanket term, by what Derrida often calls a “transcendental signified.” But still you frown at the style.

是的，德里达的散文风格，如同螃蟹般横着游离于常规论证之外，意在避免给人以源于某种明确指导概念的印象——这必然如此，因为解构恰恰在于拆解我们赖以建立思维的根基，即我们假定自身的思维可以源于某个或某些明确概念。他也拒绝承认写作风格可以被塑造以适应特定的文体。德里达与德曼之间的一个关键区别在于，德里达并非文学理论家。尽管他经常讨论我们称之为“文学”的文本，但他对写作（écriture）的看法却包含着这样的坚持：我们无法可靠地区分不同的文体。换言之，文体如同任何其他笼统的术语一样，都不适合作为先验的指称。因此，德里达是那些说服我们文学、法律文本、神学文本、哲学文本和科学文本之间并不存在，或者至少没有清晰界限的人之一。存在的只有“文本”，而思考文本领域就意味着思考一个充满差异的领域（更不用说我们稍后会提到的新词“差异”了） ——差异如此之多，如此之频繁，以至于无法被简单地归类。

Yes, Derrida’s prose style, a crablike, sideways movement away from the normal course of argumentation, is meant to avoid seeming to derive itself from some definite guiding concept—necessarily so, because deconstruction is precisely the dismantling of the grounds whereby we suppose our thinking can be derived from one or another definite concept. He also refuses to allow that a writing style might be shaped to fit a particular genre. One of the key distinctions between Derrida and de Man is that Derrida is not a literary theorist. Although he very often discusses texts that we call “literary,” his view of writing (écriture) entails the insistence that we can’t reliably discriminate among genres. In other words, genre is as unsuited to be a transcendental signified as any other blanket term. For this reason Derrida is one of the people who persuade us that there’s no such thing as, or at least no clear demarcation among, literature, legal texts, theological texts, philosophical texts, and scientific texts. There is only “text,” and to think about the field of texts is to think about something that is full of difference (not to mention the neologism différance, to which we shall return)—too much difference too constantly in play to be subject to the simplifications of category.

我之前一直在谈论困难和困惑，但鉴于我们所有人都对此感到高度紧张——我也很紧张，因为我不得不冒着背离德里达风格的风险去阐明这一点——我想提醒大家，在今天之前，我们已经进行过“解构”，而且解读德里达时遇到的许多问题也已经解释过了。让我们先从一份热身练习开始，这份练习可以基于我绘制的这些小图。我相信，当你们看到这些图时，会认出纵轴。（当我们讨论到女性主义理论时，我们会遇到一个截然不同的纵轴图示——当然，我不会妄自绘制。）
