I’ve been talking so far about difficulty and confusion, but in view of the fact that we’re all in a state of high tension about this—I’m in a state of tension, too, because I’m the one who has to risk betrayal of Derrida’s manner by trying to make it clear—let me remind us that before today we’ve already been “doing deconstruction,” and that much of what’s problematic in reading Derrida has already been explained. Let’s begin with a kind of warm-up sheet that we can anchor in these little drawings I’ve made. I trust that when you look at these drawings you will recognize the vertical axis. (When we arrive at feminist theory, we’ll encounter a rather different graphic for the vertical axis—which of course I won’t presume to draw.)

埃菲尔铁塔完美地展现了垂直轴的虚拟性。如果你见过一条竖立的虚线，那就是埃菲尔铁塔。它本身空无一物，透明无比。然而，如果你站在埃菲尔铁塔顶端的观景台上，整个巴黎仿佛瞬间呈现在你的脚下。你俯瞰着一条壮丽的组合轴线：巴黎圣母院、巴黎歌剧院、凯旋门，以及其他所有建筑，仿佛埃菲尔铁塔在行使着它的选择权。巴黎的地标，它的核心标志，以某种特定的顺序排列在铁塔脚下：如果从另一个选择轴线的视角来看，它们的排列顺序将会截然不同。正如罗兰·巴特在题为《埃菲尔铁塔》的文章中所述：

The Eiffel Tower offers a wonderful way of showing the degree to which the vertical axis is virtual. If you ever saw a dotted line standing upright, it’s the Eiffel Tower. There’s nothing in it. It’s transparent. Yet if you’re in the viewing station at the top of the Eiffel Tower, suddenly all of Paris is organized at your feet. It’s a splendid axis of combination that you’re gazing down upon, Notre Dame, the Opéra, the Arc de Triomphe, and the rest as the Tower exercises its power of selection. The landmarks of Paris, its key signs, lie at the feet of the Tower in a certain order: they would be combined in a different order from the vantage point of a different axis of selection. According to Roland Barthes in an essay called “The Eiffel Tower”:

莫泊桑经常去塔楼里的餐厅吃饭，尽管他并不特别喜欢那里的食物。“这是唯一一个，”他说，“我不用看到它的地方。”
[Guy de] Maupassant often ate at the restaurant in the tower even though he didn’t particularly like the food. “It’s the only place,” he said, “where I don’t have to see it.”2

关键似乎在于——再次借用索绪尔的话——如果我们“双脚稳稳地踏在”埃菲尔铁塔的“地面”上，我们就能摆脱它实际上是一种支配性存在的观念。如果我们真的置身其中，就不必再担心它如何将周围的一切组织成一个严谨的展开模式。毕竟，在某种意义上，我们确实是从周围环境中推断出埃菲尔铁塔的存在。它建于十九世纪。它绝非巴黎天际线的缔造者。它就像语言（langue）与言语（parole）的关系一样，是后发的。埃菲尔铁塔是一种虚拟的存在，它以一种可以说是任意的方式组织着事物。

The point appears to be—in the words of Saussure once again—that if we “put both feet squarely on the ground” of the Eiffel Tower, we’re liberated from the idea that it’s really a governing presence. If we’re actually there, we no longer have to worry about the way it organizes everything around it into a rigorous unfolding pattern. After all, there’s a very real sense in which we infer the Eiffel Tower from its surroundings. It was built in the nineteenth century. It by no means causes the skyline of Paris. It’s something that comes in belatedly just as langue comes in belatedly in relation to parole. The Eiffel Tower is a virtuality that organizes things, as one might say, arbitrarily.

作为对这些理念的反思，华莱士·史蒂文斯的一首诗或许能说明一些问题。我相信您一定认出我的画作描绘的是史蒂文斯诗作《陶罐轶事》中的陶罐。史蒂文斯写道，陶罐“使荒芜的荒野/环绕着它所在的这座小山”。因此，陶罐“无处不在”，如同文学文本中的“主导者”。正如德里达所说，它是它所创造的系统或结构的“中心”，但它实际上并非结构的一部分，而是在结构之外，如同一个从其创造物中抽离出来的创造者：“它没有像田纳西州其他任何东西那样，留下鸟儿或灌木。”陶罐被随意地放置在自然界自由玩耍的中心，这种自由玩耍充满了繁衍的活力，充满了令人愉悦的过剩，而这正是德里达强调“剩余”所暗示的：符号的剩余使用，符号的补充性。德里达在文章结尾处写到“痕迹的开创性冒险”时，也带有一种性高潮般的意味。无论如何，这个罐子就随意地矗立在那片蔓延的景象中央，组织着一切，却不参与任何事物的本质或再生产。换句话说，它是一个德里达式的中心，却又游离于结构之外：“一个非中心的中心”。稍后会详细讨论这一点。

As a reflection on these same ideas, there is a poem by Wallace Stevens. I am sure you recognize my drawing as the earthenware jar in Stevens’s “Anecdote of the Jar.” Stevens says the jar “made the slovenly wilderness / Surround [the] hill” on which it stands. Hence the jar “took dominion everywhere,” like “the dominant” in a literary text. It is the “center,” as Derrida puts it, of the system or structure that it creates, yet it is not actually part of the structure, it is outside the structure, a creator withdrawn from its creation: “It did not give of bird or bush, / Like nothing else in Tennessee.” The jar is arbitrarily placed in the middle of the free play of the natural world, a free play that is full of reproductive exuberance, full of a joyous excess that is part of what Derrida suggests in emphasizing what’s “left over”: the surplus usage of the sign, the supplementarity of the sign. There’s an orgasmic element, too, when Derrida writes of “the seminal adventure of the trace” toward the end of his essay. In any case, the jar just stands arbitrarily in the middle of that sprawl, organizing everything without participating in the nature, the reproductivity, of anything. It is, in other words, a Derridean center that is outside the structure: “a center which is not a center.” More of that in a minute.

现在说说双子塔。早在2001年之前我就开始用这个例子了，但它们当时所暗示的，正是我们今天在悲痛中才意识到的：垂直轴线的短暂性。双子塔在纽约的作用，正如埃菲尔铁塔在巴黎的作用。餐厅名为“世界之窗”（仿佛它与世界无关），可以俯瞰无与伦比的城市景观，一切都围绕着它而建。米歇尔·德·塞托（Michel de Certeau）一篇关于双子塔的精彩文章——同样，也是在2001年之前——对此论点进行了深入阐述。3

Now the Twin Towers. I started using this example long before 2001, but what they suggested even then was what today we realize in grief: the ephemerality of the vertical axis. The Twin Towers had the same function in New York that the Eiffel Tower has in Paris. The restaurant, called “Windows on the World” (as though it were not part of the world), afforded an incomparable view of the city, with everything organized at its feet. A very fine essay about the Twin Towers—again, long before 2001—by Michel de Certeau makes this argument in sustained form.3

因此，这些现实世界的例子印证了我们可能存在的这种不安感：推断某个空间瞬间，并以此断言经验的不可还原的时间性本质由此而来——推断某个脱离经验连续体而存在的瞬间是经验的必然原因——总是存在问题。认识到组织性观念的虚拟性，意味着承认其任意性，即便我们也承认，没有它，就没有组织性思维的基础。在非常重要的意义上，我们必须认识到，当我们进行思考时，我们离不开一个先验的所指，因此，正如德里达所说，我们必须将其“抹除”，即便我们承认它的必要性。德里达从未真正声称你可以舍弃它。如果你想要理解结构，你就必须运用某种此类推论；德里达承认，他自己几乎无法在不使用“符号”这一支配性概念的情况下写作，但最好给它加上引号，因为它的存在本身总是值得怀疑的，而且它绝不能被提升到创造性起源的地位。这一切我们最初都是从马克思关于商品拜物教的论述中学到的，此后我们一直铭记于心，例如我们用虚线来表示符号学和结构主义的纵轴。“结构、符号与游戏”在某种意义上正是对这条虚线的强调。

These, then, are real-world examples of the uneasy sense we may have that to infer a spatial moment from which we then say the irreducibly temporal nature of experience is derived—to infer a moment isolated from the continuum of this experience as a necessary cause of it—is always problematic. To realize the virtuality of an organizing idea is to recognize its arbitrariness even as we also recognize that without it there is no basis for organized thought. In a very important sense we must recognize that when we engage in thinking, we can’t do without a transcendental signified, hence must put it, as Derrida would say, “under erasure,” even while conceding its necessity. Derrida never really claims that you can do without it. If you want to get a sense of structure, you’ve got to work with some inference of this sort; Derrida admits that he himself can scarcely write without the governing concept of the “sign,” but it had better be in quotes because its very existence is always questionable, and it must not be promoted to the status of creative origin. All of this we learned at the outset from Marx on the commodity fetish, and we have reminded ourselves of it ever since when we represented the vertical axis of semiotics and structuralism as a dotted line. “Structure, Sign, and Play” is in one sense simply an insistence on this dotted line.

还有其他一些方式，我们已经暗示过你今天读到的内容。请看德里达引用列维-斯特劳斯关于神话本质的两段文字（921）。在依次引用这两段文字之后，我将回到列维-斯特劳斯对俄狄浦斯神话的分析，并说明德里达是如何既从列维-斯特劳斯的论述中获益，又同时能够批判列维-斯特劳斯的立场。首先：

There are other ways, too, in which we’ve already hinted at what you’ve been reading today. Consider the two passages (921) in which Derrida quotes Lévi-Strauss on the nature of myth. Once having quoted these passages in turn, I’ll return to Lévi-Strauss’s analysis of the Oedipus myth and show how it is that Derrida both benefits from what Lévi-Strauss has said and is enabled at the same time to criticize Lévi-Strauss’s position. First:

“与认知话语（即以某种原则、先验指称或统摄性术语为基础的话语——换句话说，在特定时刻，某种东西使得所有知识都可能由此而来）相反，关于神话的结构性话语——神话话语——本身必须是神话形态的。它必须具有它所谈论事物的形式。”
“In opposition to epistemic discourse [the kind of discourse that has some principle or transcendental signified or blanket term as its basis—in other words, something that in a given moment makes it possible for all knowledge to flow from it], structural discourse on myths—mythological discourse—must itself be mythomorphic. It must have the form of that of which it speaks.”

德里达接着说：

Derrida then says:

这是列维-斯特劳斯本人在其最著名的著作之一《生与熟》中所说的话。我只想引用这段话的结尾：“为了模仿神话思维的自发运动，我的尝试——既短暂又漫长——尚未能满足它的需求，也未能尊重它的节奏。因此，这本关于神话的书本身就是一个神话。”
This is what Lévi-Strauss [himself] says in [the following passage taken from one of Lévi-Strauss’s most famous books] The Raw and the Cooked. I just want to quote the end of that passage now: “In wanting to imitate the spontaneous movement of mythical thought, my enterprise, itself too brief and too long, has yet to yield to its demands and respect its rhythm. Thus is this book on myths itself and in its own way a myth.”

因此，在这里，列维-斯特劳斯承认——甚至引以为豪——了他自身作品中某些东西，而这些东西在他于《结构人类学》一书中对俄狄浦斯神话的分析中却并未承认。列维-斯特劳斯在《生与熟》中指出，他对神话的研究方法本身也只是神话的一种版本。也就是说，它参与了神话式的思维方式。它运用了他在《结构人类学》一书中称之为“神话主题”或“思维的粗略构成单元”的东西。它以我们之前讨论过的方式运用和操纵这些思维的粗略构成单元，但请注意列维-斯特劳斯在那篇文章中与德里达刚才引用的段落有何不同。列维-斯特劳斯在那里实际上是在说，他以条理分明的方式呈现给我们的神话形式是科学的，而非神话的。他用来得出这一“科学”结论的版本之一，是他所谓的弗洛伊德版的俄狄浦斯神话。弗洛伊德、索福克勒斯，以及他所掌握的所有其他版本，作为版本本身都同样有价值，但它们都无法提供对神话深层结构或意义的解释。神话的意义只能通过本文所呈现的科学方法才能发现。

Here, then, is a moment when Lévi-Strauss is admitting—even proud of—something about his own work that he is not admitting in his analysis of the Oedipus myth in the essay from Structural Anthropology. What Lévi-Strauss is saying in The Raw and the Cooked is that his approach to myth is itself only a version of the myth. That is, it participates in the mythic way of thinking about things. It uses what in the Structural Anthropology essay he calls “mythemes” or “gross constituent units” of thought. It deploys and manipulates those gross constituent units of thought in the ways that we reviewed, but notice what Lévi-Strauss is saying in that essay as opposed to the passage Derrida has just quoted. Lévi-Strauss says there, in effect, that the form of the myth he gives us in his columns and rows is scientific, not mythic. One of the versions he makes use of to arrive at this “scientific” conclusion is what he calls Freud’s version of the Oedipus myth. Freud, Sophocles, all of the other versions he has at his disposal have equal merit as versions, but none of them provide the deep structural explanation or meaning of the myth. The meaning of the myth is discoverable only in the science here presented.

弗洛伊德也自认为是一位科学家，他对神话的解读也被认为是科学的。那么，弗洛伊德对神话的解读究竟是什么呢？你猜对了，二选一！——换句话说，它关乎乱伦，关乎血缘关系过度决定和血缘关系决定不足的交汇点。简而言之，列维-斯特劳斯的结论在弗洛伊德那里就已经有所预示。此外，我们发现列维-斯特劳斯在这件事上做了什么？他否认了弗洛伊德的影响——这是我的神话，不是他的神话——这恰恰是弗洛伊德的原始部落中发生的事情。通过否定父亲，列维-斯特劳斯落入了弗洛伊德率先分析的神话模式之中。德里达批评列维-斯特劳斯的那些时刻，正是列维-斯特劳斯不加掩饰地宣称其作品具有科学性的时刻，也就是说，正如我们将看到的，用德里达的话来说，他的作品具有一个“中心”。但也有很多时候——德里达也一丝不苟地引用了列维-斯特劳斯的原话来佐证这一点——列维-斯特劳斯承认，他的观点会不稳定地融入被观察的对象之中。

Well, Freud, too, thought he was a scientist, and his reading of the myth was also supposed to be scientific. And what was Freud’s reading of the myth about? You guessed it, two or one!—in other words, it was about incest, the meeting point of the overdetermination of blood relations and the underdetermination of blood relations. In short, Lévi-Strauss’s conclusions are already anticipated in Freud. Furthermore, what do we find Lévi-Strauss doing on this occasion? He’s denying the influence of Freud—it’s my myth, not his myth—which is precisely what happens in Freud’s primal horde. In repudiating the father, Lévi-Strauss falls into the very mythic pattern that Freud had been the first to analyze. The moments for which Derrida is criticizing Lévi-Strauss are those moments in which Lévi-Strauss has unguardedly said that his work is scientific, which is also to say, as we’ll see, that in Derrida’s terms it has a “center.” But there are lots of occasions, too—and Derrida also scrupulously quotes Lévi-Strauss to this effect—when Lévi-Strauss concedes that his viewpoint disappears unstably into the thing viewed.

既然我们已经预料到了这一点，那么让我们来看一段德里达并非在谈论列维-斯特劳斯而是在谈论索绪尔的文字（917）。在这里，他重新审视了索绪尔对符号的基本定义，并对概念与声音意象——即所指与能指——之间所谓的关联感到困扰，而这种关联正是索绪尔科学的基础：所指与能指之间任意且差异化的配对，正是索绪尔赖以立足的根基。关于这种配对，德里达说道：

Now because we’ve anticipated this as well, let’s look at a passage where Derrida is talking not about Lévi-Strauss but about Saussure (917). Here he revisits Saussure’s foundational definition of the sign, and he is troubled by the alleged relationship between the concept and the sound image—the signified and the signifier—that is the basis of the science of Saussure: the arbitrary and differential pairing of signified and signifier that is the ground on which Saussure puts both feet. Concerning this pairing, Derrida says:

“符号”这一概念的意义一直以来都被理解和界定为“符号的符号”，即指称所指对象的能指，能指本身又不同于其所指对象。如果抹杀了能指与所指之间的根本区别，那么作为形而上学概念的“能指”一词本身就应该被抛弃。
[T]he signification “sign” has always been comprehended and determined, in its sense as sign-of, signifier referring to a signified, signifier different from its signified. If one erases the radical difference between signifier and signified, it is the word signifier itself which ought to be abandoned as a metaphysical concept.

这里我又回到了之前在讨论索绪尔时用问号限定的那张图。假设我把“所指”和“能指”之间的关系理解为两个术语之间的关系，而不是被表示事物和词语之间的关系——毕竟，表示“树”这个概念的一种方式就是写下“树”这个词，然后加上引号。如果我去掉引号，剩下的就只是这个词本身，没有任何迹象表明它是一个概念。请注意，这正是雅各布森所说的“元语言”关系。它暗示着“树”是“凉亭”的另一种说法。换句话说，这种关系并非指称与所指之间的关系，而是指称与指称之间的关系。如此一来，二元对立的关系便被打破，我们开始理解言语或文字的组合结构，它不过是一个指称引向另一个指称：德里达曾说过，我们不妨抛弃“指称”这个词，但他同样也可以对“所指”这个词做出同样的评价。当我“思考”一个指称（例如“树”，无疑受到了先前某个指称，如“榆树”）时，它会通过联想触发一个后续的指称（例如“凉亭”），而这个后续的指称又会触发另一个，如此往复。用解构主义的语言来说，这就是“链”，即能指链：它并非一种组织模式，而是一种不断自我复制、自我延伸的运动，它本质上是线性的，并通过一系列时间间隔的联想不断向前推进。德里达及其追随者称之为“指称链”。

Here’s where I come back to that diagram I already qualified with a question mark when I was talking about Saussure. Suppose I think of the relationship between “signified” and “signifier” not as the relationship between a represented thing and a word but as the relationship between two terms—because, after all, one way of indicating the concept “tree” is to write the word “tree” and put quotation marks around it. If I take away the quotation marks, all I have is the word with no indication that it’s a concept. Notice that this is now a relationship that Jakobson would call “metalingual.” What it suggests is that “tree” is another word for “arbor.” In other words, it’s a relationship not between a signified and a signifier but between a signifier and a signifier, so that the binarism of the relationship is broken down and we begin to understand the combinatory structure of speech or writing as just one signifier leading to another signifier: Derrida said above that we might as well jettison the word “signifier,” but he might as easily have said that about the word “signified.” When I “think” a signifier (“tree,” no doubt inspired by a previous signifier, such as “elm”), it triggers by association a subsequent signifier (arbor), which triggers another, which triggers another. That’s what gives us, in the language of deconstruction, “the chain,” the signifying chain: not an organizational pattern but an ever self-replicating and self-extending movement, irreducibly linear and pushing ahead through a sequence of temporally spaced associations. Derrida and his followers call this “the chain of the signifier.”

当你揭开概念/所指与声音意象/能指之间关系的神秘面纱时，你也揭开了存在于虚拟空间中的一系列联想与联想实际发生的方式（必然发生在时间之中）之间关系的神秘面纱。换言之，如果一个能指以链条的形式引出另一个能指，那么这就是索绪尔所描述的联想发生的维度。它们并非发生在系统性的空间中，而是发生在不断展开的时间之中。我们发现自己身处意义的洪流之中。所有可能性在我们出现之前就已经存在；因此，我们的联想过程如同顺流而下，被某种力量推动着。当我们引入“补充性”和“差异”的概念时，就能更精确地思考这种运动。

When you demystify the relationship between a concept/signified and a sound image/signifier, you also demystify the relationship between a set of associations, which exist in virtual space, and the way in which association actually takes place, which is necessarily in time. In other words, if one signifier leads to another in a chain, then that is the dimension in which the associations described by Saussure occur. They do not occur in a systemic space but in unfolding time. We find ourselves caught up in a stream of signification. All the possibilities existed before we came along; hence our associative process is moved, as down a stream, by—well, by something. When we take up “supplementarity” and différance, we can think of this movement more precisely.

德里达的文章从一开始就以另一种方式印证了我们一直在强调的观点，即结构主义的危机在于需要否认起源或原因。在结构主义中，如果某事物出现，它就出现在两个事物之间。它既不是这个也不是那个，或者说，它“出现”为既非此也非彼的事物。它并非源于某个先验的单一原因作为结果。它作为场域内的差异而出现。这正是德里达在《结构、符号与游戏》第一段（915）中以极其复杂的方式所指出的：

There’s yet another way Derrida’s essay from the very outset confirms a point we’ve been making, in this case about the crisis of structuralism being the need to deny the provenance of genesis or cause. In structuralism, if something emerges, it emerges from between two things. It’s not this and it’s not that, or it “emerges” as that which is not this, not that. It doesn’t derive from an antecedent single cause as an effect. It emerges as a difference within a field. That’s what Derrida is indicating with extraordinary intensity of complication in the first paragraph of “Structure, Sign, and Play” (915):

也许在结构概念的历史中发生了一些可以称之为“事件”的事情[ évênement，出现的事情，现在存在而以前不存在的事情]。
Perhaps something has occurred in the history of the concept of structure that could be called an “event” [évênement, something that comes forth, something that is there now and wasn’t there before].

在开篇的几句话中，德里达预示性地指出了结构主义面临的最大难题。当结构主义认为昨天的情况与今天不同时，它不得不说：昨天存在着某种共时性的数据横截面，而今天则存在着略有不同的共时性数据横截面。然而，结构主义在其共时性语境下，既无法也不愿解释昨天的数据是如何演变成今天的——换句话说，它无法解释变化本身。它看到的只是一系列连续的横截面，并将其称为“历史”。这并非“一件事导致另一件事”，而是正如阿诺德·汤因比对其竞争对手历史研究方法的轻蔑之言——“一件接一件的糟糕事”。

In those first words, Derrida proleptically announces the most problematic issue for structuralism. When structuralism considers that yesterday things were different from the way they are today, it has to say: yesterday there was a certain synchronic cross-section of data, and today there’s a slightly different synchronic cross-section of data. But structuralism in its synchronic register is unable and furthermore unwilling to say anything about how yesterday’s data turned into today’s data—in other words, to say anything about change. It sees successive cross-sections, and it calls that “history.” Not “one thing leads to another” but, in Arnold Toynbee’s dismissive remark about his rivals’ approaches to history, “one damned thing after another.”

德里达在第一段中就刻意对这个前提进行了探讨：

Derrida deliberately struggles with this premise in his first paragraph:

如果“事件”这个词本身没有蕴含某种意义，而结构主义思想——或者说结构论思想——恰恰旨在削弱或质疑这种意义，那么它就称得上是一个“事件”。但无论如何，我还是要谨慎地使用“事件”这个词，并赋予它引号般的含义。在这个意义上，这个事件将具有断裂的外在形式（如同火山喷发的熔岩）和重复（某种早已发生过的事情）。
an “event,” if this loaded word did not entail a meaning which it is precisely the function of structural—or structuralist—thought to reduce or to suspect. But let me use the term “event” anyway, employing it with caution and as if in quotation marks. In this sense, this event will have the exterior form of a rupture [the event as lava from a volcano] and a redoubling [something that has always already happened before].

正如鲍勃·迪伦所言，某些事情发生了，但并非什么新鲜事，它复制了你从未知晓却又一直存在的东西，琼斯先生。事件浮现，但同时又向我们强调它早已存在，一直都在那里。德里达暗示，这就是结构主义被迫得出的关于事件本质的结论。然而，他坚持认为，这个事件，结构主义本身的事件，难道不也是新的吗？如果是，它又是由什么产生的呢？

As Bob Dylan would say, something has happened, but it’s not something new, it replicates, Mr. Jones, what you never knew, yet was always there. The event emerges but at the same time presses on us its having already been there, always already been there. That, Derrida implies, is what structuralism is forced to conclude about the nature of an event. And yet, he persists, wasn’t this event, the event of structuralism itself, after all, new? And if so, engendered by what?

《结构、符号与游戏》是对“结构性”的批判。它绝不仅仅是对结构主义的批判。它质疑一切具有“中心”的事物。我观察一个结构，并说它有一个中心。我指的是一个概括性的术语，一个指导性概念，一个先验的能指，某种孕育结构的东西。德里达认为，正是这个中心使得结构内部存在有限的自由游戏。结构是有边界的；它可能是变形虫状的，但它仍然有边界，而边界总是限制结构内部的自由游戏。在现象学传统中，这种有限的自由游戏被称为结构的“意向性”。你还记得吗？康德称之为“目的性”：对象根据其内部动力组织的方式。

“Structure, Sign, and Play” is a critique of “structurality.” It’s not by any means just a critique of structuralism. It quizzes anything that has a “center.” I look at a structure and I say it has a center. I mean a blanket term, a guiding concept, a transcendental signified, something that engenders the structure. Derrida says that this center is also what allows for limited free play within the structure. A structure has boundaries; it may be amoeboid, but it still has boundaries, and boundaries always limit the free play within the structure. In the phenomenological tradition, this limited free play is called the “intentionality” of the structure. Kant, you remember, calls it “purposiveness”: the way the object is organized according to an internal dynamic.

但将意向性视为中心，与将产生意向性的人、作者、存在或观念视为中心，完全是两回事，因为这些起源与结构本身无关：它们是创世，是原因。那么，我们如何从意向性的作者推导出结构的意向性，反之亦然呢？正如德里达令人费解地告诉我们，中心“既是中心，又不是中心”。（顺便一提，基因双螺旋结构既是我们的创造者，也是我们体内的载体，就是一个很好的例子，说明在这个语境下，它并非一个中心。）中心通常被认为是组织结构，但实际上却不具备组织任何事物的资格，因为它并不在结构之内；它不参与结构，而是在结构之外，像一个饼干模具一样从外部强加自身。

But to speak of intentionality as a center is not at all the same thing as to speak of an intending person, author, being, or idea that brought it into existence as a center, because those origins are extraneous to the structure itself: genesis, a cause. But how do we get from an intending author to the intentionality of structure and back? A center is “both a center and not a center,” as Derrida maddeningly tells us. (By the way, the genetic double helix, which both produces us and is carried within us, is a good example of a center that is not a center in this parlance.) A center is typically conceived as that which organizes a structure yet isn’t really qualified to organize anything because it’s not in the structure; it’s not participatory but outside the structure, something that imposes itself from without like a cookie cutter.

在对“中心”做出这些初步论述之后，德里达将形而上学的历史描述为对中心——某种万物起源的基因冲动——的不断诉诸的历史。这份清单编排得非常巧妙（916）。它未必是按时间顺序排列的，但确实能让人感受到第一因概念的演变。我仅就清单的结尾部分进行探讨：“先验性、意识或良知、上帝、人，等等。”请注意，尽管这份清单并非严格按照时间顺序排列，但人确实接替了上帝。德里达思考的是西方文化的发展。在中世纪以及某种程度上在近代早期，我们生活在一个以神为中心的世界里。就人而言，如果他能够理解自己是“人”的话，那么人就将自己理解为神圣创造力的产物，是参与并受益于神圣临在的众多实体之一。启蒙运动的兴起也伴随着人类中心主义的兴起。到了启蒙运动鼎盛时期，从伏尔泰到布莱克，从马克思到尼采，所有人都认为不是上帝创造了人，而是人创造了上帝。人成为了超越性的所指。在这一历史时刻，一切都源于人类意识，所有概念，无论何种概念，都可以从这个角度来理解。

After these first remarks about the “center,” Derrida describes the history of metaphysics as a history of successive appeals to a center: to some genetic impulse from which everything derives. The list is very cunningly put together (916). It’s not necessarily chronological, but it does give you a sense of successive concepts of first causes. I’ll just take up the list toward the end: “transcendentality, consciousness, or conscience, God, man, and so forth.” Notice that though the list isn’t strictly chronological, man nevertheless does succeed God. Derrida is thinking about the development of Western culture. In the Middle Ages and to some extent in the early modern period, we lived in a theocentric world. Insofar as he understood himself as “man” at all, man understood himself as a product of divine creativity, as one entity among others that participate in and benefit from the divine presence. The ensuing rise of the Enlightenment is also the rise of anthropocentrism, and by the time the Enlightenment is in full cry, you get everybody from Voltaire to Blake to Marx to Nietzsche saying not that God invented man, but that man invented God. Man has become the transcendental signified. Everything derives now in this historical moment from human consciousness, and all concepts of whatever kind can be understood in that light.

但德里达在提到“人”之后，又意味深长地补充道：“等等”。在人之后，某种事物出现，而人作为中心仅仅存在于某个特定的历史时刻。德里达关于“事件”出现提出的论点是，一种新的先验所指实际上已经取代了人。随着结构主义的出现，世界不再以人类为中心，而是以语言为中心。最新的出现，这种断裂，这种具有变革意义的事件，就是语言作为符号系统的出现（同上）。

But then, having said “man,” Derrida adds, enigmatically, “and so forth.” Something comes after man, who exists as a center only at a certain historical moment. The argument Derrida is making about the emergence of the “event” is that a new transcendental signified has actually substituted itself for man. With the advent of structuralism, the world is no longer anthropocentric, it’s linguistic. The latest emergence, the rupture, the event that makes a difference, is the emergence of language understood as a system of signs (ibid.):

出现的时刻（事件）是语言入侵普遍问题的时刻（换句话说，是语言取代先前的先验所指，即人的时刻）；是在没有中心或起源的情况下，一切都变成了话语的时刻——如果我们能就这个词达成共识的话——也就是说，一切都变成了一个系统，在这个系统中，中心所指、原始或先验所指，永远无法在差异系统之外绝对存在。
The moment [of emergence, the event] was that in which language invaded the universal problematic [in other words, the moment in which language displaced the previous transcendental signified, which was man]; that in which, in the absence of a center or origin, everything became discourse—provided we can agree on this word—that is to say, when everything became a system where the central signified, the original or transcendental signified, is never absolutely present outside a system of differences.

因此，在结构主义话语中，新的起源——语言——在于否定起源本身。德里达一方面主张语言的存在，另一方面又抹杀语言。他痛苦地意识到，在某种意义上，语言就是新的上帝，新的人。（语言创造了我，正如我创造了上帝。）许多对解构主义的批判都认为，在其他主体缺失的情况下，解构主义赋予了语言以合法性，赋予其能动性，甚至意识，仿佛语言就是上帝或人。可以看出，德里达预见到了这种批判，并将其视为一种无法回避的双重困境。

The new origin, then, language in the discourse of structuralism, consists in the denial of origins. Derrida is making a claim for language while erasing it. He’s painfully aware that language is in one sense just the new God, the new Man. (Language produced me just as I produced God.) Many critiques of deconstruction take the form of saying that in the absence of other agencies, it authorizes language, gives it agency, even consciousness, as though it were God or man. You can see that Derrida anticipates this critique and views it as an inescapable double bind.

然而，德里达辩称，结构主义语言的“事件”确实以一种崭新且相对清晰的方式出现，因为此前形而上学中对起源的每一次解释都存在一个问题。我们总是说上帝内在于万物之中，人类意识渗透到它所遇到的一切——简而言之，我们谈论的是既是结构的一部分，又存在于结构之外的事物。上帝创造世界，然后，正如弥尔顿所说，“不受约束地退隐”。上帝不在那里，变成了隐藏的上帝（Dieu caché），既不在世界之内，又存在于世界的结构之中。同样的话也适用于人。人类思想创造了对世界本质的感知，然后置身事外，成为一个观察者。

Yet the “event” of structuralist language did occur in a new and comparatively clear-sighted way, Derrida says in its defense, because hitherto there had been a problem with each successive account of origins in metaphysics. We were always saying God is immanent in all things, human consciousness pervades everything that it encounters—in short, we spoke of something that is part of a structure yet is also outside of it. God creates the world and then, as Milton says, “uncircumscrib’d withdraw[s].” God is not there, becomes the Dieu caché, absent from the world yet also the structure of the world. The same thing can be said of man. Human thought brings the sense of what the world is into being, then stands aside as an observer.

德里达认为，语言并非如此运作，语言之所以特殊，是因为将其置于其参照框架之外进行讨论毫无意义。他承认“事件”即结构主义语言，并以此论证其对结构主义的核心批判。语言并非与言语（或更确切地说是“书写”，原因我们稍后会谈到）相异，它始终显现于言语（书写）之中，且仅存在于此。正如能指与所指之间的区别必须被抹去一样，语言与言语（书写）之间的区别也必须被抹去。然而，如果语言并非一个虚拟的符号系统，那么它究竟是什么？解构主义质疑语言与思想之间的区别，正是通过质疑能指与所指之间的区别来实现的，因此，语言并非完全是索绪尔式的，尽管正如德里达所说，若不借助索绪尔的词汇体系，就很难对其进行讨论。

Language doesn’t do that, Derrida says, language is different because it makes no sense to talk about it as standing outside of its frame of reference. Having acknowledged that, the “event” is structuralist language, he then develops this argument as his essential critique of structuralism. Language is not other than speech (or rather “writing,” for reasons we’ll get to), it is perpetually manifest in speech (writing) and only there. Just as the difference between signified and signifier must be put under erasure, so too must be the distinction between langue and parole (écriture). If it is not a virtual system of signs, however, what then is “language”? Deconstruction questions the distinction between language and thought in questioning the distinction between signifier and signified, so language is not quite Saussurian, even though, as Derrida says, it’s difficult to discuss it without a Saussurian vocabulary.

另一个问题，同样与对索绪尔的批判相关，在于其前提：内省的思维（索绪尔称之为“心理的”）是无需中介的，可以而且应该被表达出来，而将表达的表述保留给文字。值得注意的是，索绪尔将概念的表达称为“声音意象”。德里达认为，在索绪尔的传统中，语言的直接呈现被假定为声音，“声音”而非文字，言语而非书写。他声称，这种“将声音视为完全呈现的特权”是形而上学历史中一种隐蔽的偏见。毕竟，我们为什么要将语言视为言语的生产者，视为被表达之物的生产者？为什么我们将声音——如同神圣的逻各斯，即“道”：“太初有道”——视为一种完全呈现的同时性，既反映了语言的本质，也反映了其在言语中的显现？

Another problem, likewise related to the critique of Saussure, is the premise that the thinking that’s inward (Saussure calls it “psychological”) is something unmediated that can be voiced and indeed should be voiced, reserving for writing the representation of that voicing. Note that Saussure calls the utterance of a concept a “sound image.” According to Derrida, in the Saussurian tradition the unmediated presence of language is presumed to be sound, “voice” instead of script, speech instead of writing. He claims that this “privileging of voice as full presence” is a hidden bias in the whole history of metaphysics. Why, after all, should we think of language as a producer of speech, of that which is voiced? Why do we think of voice—as in the divine logos, the Word: “in the beginning was the Word”—as a fully present simultaneity that reflects the essence of language as well as its manifestation in speech?

德里达认为，写作与声音并无本质区别。声音同样是在时间中以组合的方式表达出来的。声音是铭刻在耳朵上的声音。这是德里达经常用来比喻言语的一种方式：耳朵上的文字。索绪尔试图区分的东西——德里达认为这是“形而上学的”——即某种原始的、直接的、非创生性的东西（声音）与某种仅仅是声音的再现的东西（即写作），这种区分需要受到质疑。德里达在他早期最具影响力的著作之一《论文字学》中对此进行了探讨。

Writing, Derrida argues, is very little different from voice. Voice, too, is articulated combinatorially in time. Voice is a noise inscribed on the ear. This is a metaphor for speech that Derrida frequently uses: a writing on the ear. The distinction that Saussure wants to make, which Derrida takes to be “metaphysical,” between something primary, something immediate and underivative—voice—and something merely reproductive of voice—namely, writing—needs to be questioned. Derrida does so in one of his most influential early books, Of Grammatology.

在德里达看来，言语和写作是彼此二元相关的，但德里达超越了这种二元对立，认为写作可以被理解为首要的，即便仅仅是为了消除对立的偏见。为了理解这一论点，我们需要先了解德里达用来支撑其对传统语言观念批判的几个关键术语。第一个是补充性概念。他指出，补充物要么是对不完整事物的补充，要么是对已完整事物的补充。例如，我服用维生素C。我也喝很多橙汁，所以我的维生素C摄入量很充足，如果我服用维生素C片，我就补充了已完整事物；如果我不喝橙汁，那么我的药片补充了不完整事物，但无论哪种情况，我们都称之为补充物。即使只是记住这两种补充物之间的概念差异，也是非常困难的。

Speech and writing for Derrida are binary correlates of each other, but Derrida argues beyond this contention, if only to offset opposed prejudices, that writing can be understood as primary. To follow that argument, we need to say something about a number of key terms that Derrida uses to sustain his criticism of traditional ideas about language. The first is the notion of supplementarity. A supplement, he points out, is something that either completes something that isn’t complete or adds to something that is already complete. For example, I take vitamin C. I also drink a lot of orange juice, so I’ve got plenty of vitamin C, and if I take a vitamin C pill I am supplementing something that’s already complete; if I don’t drink any orange juice, then my pill supplements what’s not complete, but either way we always call it a supplement. It’s very difficult even to keep in mind the conceptual difference between these two sorts of supplement.

传统意义上的符号是自足的、独立的。索绪尔将其视为科学对象，认为符号既是任意的又是差异性的；但从解构主义的批判视角来看，符号却是一个不断增殖、意义持续变化的实体，它并非静止不变，其本质也并非自足或独立。它不断地渗透或溢出到后续的符号中，从而持续留下德里达所谓的“痕迹”。当我们考察一个言语行为的展开过程时，我们会看到后续的符号是如何被先前的符号所污染和影响的。补充性正是理解符号在意义链中同时存在的自足性和自我溢出性的一种方式。

Now a sign as traditionally viewed is self-sufficient, self-contained. Saussure made it a scientific object by saying that it’s both arbitrary and differential; but a sign understood under the critique of deconstruction is something that is perpetually proliferating signification, something that doesn’t stand still, and something that can’t be viewed as self-sufficient or independent in its nature. It bleeds or spills into successive signs in such a way that it perpetually leaves what Derrida calls “traces.” As we examine the unfolding of a speech act, we see how successive signs are contaminated, influenced, by the signs that precede them. Supplementarity is a way of understanding the simultaneous self-sufficiency and self-overflow of signs in the chain of signification.

“差异”（Différance）在某种程度上是“补充性”（suppligarity）的同义词，但它也是一种谈论声音与书写之间差异的方式。声音与书写虽然有很多共同之处，但它们之间仍然存在差异。正如我所说，声音与书写并非稳定的二元对立关系。（在德里达的理论中，不存在稳定的二元对立关系。）声音与书写的区别在于，书写能够提供许多声音无法提供的差异信息。德里达坚持将“差异”（différence）拼写错误，其有趣之处在于，如果我们仅仅将语言视为发声的，我们就很难区分“差异”（différance）和“差异”（différence）。换句话说，Différance用 a 代替了a——还记得《Différance》一文中关于“a”作为金字塔、作为 alpha、作为起源以及作为弑君者的论述吗？因为记住，国王是超越的所指：“上帝、人等等”——Différance 中 a 的重要性，只有当我们把语言导向书面时才能体会到，因为在口语中，这些差异模式并不会显现出来。

Différance is in part a synonym for supplementarity, but it is also a way of talking about the difference between voice and writing. There is a difference between voice and writing even though they have so much in common. As I’ve said, voice and writing are not a stable binary. (There are no stable binaries in Derrida.) The difference between voice and writing is that writing can give us many indications of difference that voice can’t give us. Part of the interest of misspelling différence, as Derrida insists on doing, is that if we think of language merely as voiced, we can’t at all easily tell the difference between différance and différence. Différance, in other words, with its substitution of the a—and remember the riff in the essay “Différance” on “a” as a pyramid, as alpha, as origin, and as killing the king because the king, remember, is the transcendental signified: “God, man and so forth”—the importance of the a in différance is something that we can pick up only if we orient language toward writing, because in speech these modes of difference don’t register.

Différence（带e）其实就是索绪尔的语言系统，一个将差异理解为同时性的系统：它就像一个自助餐，供我们随意挑选。（然而，即使是“差异”这个词本身也与更概括的“对立”概念存在微妙的对比。）相比之下，Différance引入了延时性的时间概念，并提醒我们，差异——也就是说，我们对差异的理解，我们处理差异的方式——并非发生在空间中；它发生在时间中。当我感知到差​​异时，我是在时间上感知它。我不再将符号之间的关系视为同时性的问题。我希望将其视为一种空间关系，以便用科学的方法加以确定，但在我的意识流中，我却是在时间上把握差异。我延时差异。时间是符号相互渗透、相互补充的媒介，而要进入这个媒介，我需要Différance的概念。

Différence (with an e) is simply the Saussurian linguistic system, a system of differences understood as a simultaneity: available to us as a smorgasbord from which we pick and choose. (Yet even the word “difference” stands in subtle contrast with the more schematic notion of “opposition.”) Différance by contrast introduces the temporal idea of deferral and reminds us that difference—that is to say, our understanding of difference, our means of negotiating difference—is not something that’s actually done in space; it’s done in time. When I perceive a difference, I perceive it temporally. I no longer see the relation among signs as an issue of simultaneity. I want to see it as a spatial relation in order to pin it down scientifically, but in my actual stream of consciousness I grasp difference temporally. I defer difference. Time is the medium in which signs bleed into each other, supplement each other, and to enter this medium I need the concept of différance.

在下一讲中，我想谈谈德里达思想的特征性发展路径。我还会进一步阐述我刚才提到的那些棘手的关键词，以及它们与德里达语言观之间的关系。之后，我会讨论德曼。

There a couple of things I want to say in the next lecture about the characteristic moves of Derridean thought. I will also try to say something more about the troublesome keywords I have just introduced and their relation to Derrida’s understanding of language. Then on to de Man.

 

 

第十一章

CHAPTER 11

解构 II

Deconstruction II

保罗·德曼

Paul de Man

阅读材料：

Readings:

德曼，保罗。“符号学和修辞学。”载《批判传统》，第 882-892 页。

De Man, Paul. “Semiology and Rhetoric.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 882–892.

补充段落。

Additional passages.

我将放弃对我来说很有趣（但也许对你来说并非如此）的事情：对德里达《结构、符号与游戏》（926）结尾处那段惊人的文字进行解释，但我会引用它，以便你可以对此进行更深入的思考，考虑它是如何拾起早期主题、将文章带回开头并反思其自身隐喻的：

I’m going to forego what for me would have been fun, though perhaps not for you: an explication of the astonishing passage that concludes Derrida’s “Structure, Sign, and Play” (926), but I’ll quote it so you can think some more about it, considering how it picks up earlier motifs, returns the essay to its beginning, and reflects on its own metaphors:

这里存在一个问题，姑且称之为历史性的问题，我们今天只是窥见一斑：构思、形成、孕育、分娩。我承认，我使用这些词语时，目光投向了生育之事——但也投向了那些人，他们（我并不排除自己属于其中一员）面对那尚未命名之物视而不见，而这物正在宣告自身，并且只能以非物种的形态，以无形、无声、幼稚而又恐怖的怪物形态，在每次新生命即将诞生之际，如此宣告。
Here there is a sort of question, call it historical, of which we are only glimpsing today, the conception, the formation, the gestation, the labor. I employ these words, I admit, with a glance toward the business of childbearing—but also with a glance toward those who, in a company from which I do not exclude myself, turn their eyes away in the face of the as yet unnamable, which is proclaiming itself and which can do so, as is necessary whenever a birth is in the offing, only under the species of the non-species in the formless, mute, infant, and terrifying form of monstrosity.

好吧，这里有一句话，或许可以作为一篇评论的标题：“解构的怪诞之处”。

Well, there is a sentence for you, and perhaps a title for a commentary: “The Monstrosity of Deconstruction.”

我想简要地回顾一下德里达和列维-斯特劳斯之间的关系。我在上次讲座中提到，尽管《结构、符号与游戏》在某些方面是对列维-斯特劳斯的批判，但令人惊讶的是，无论德里达是否承认，它在很大程度上重复了列维-斯特劳斯的思想。例如，德里达引用了列维-斯特劳斯为马塞尔·莫斯关于语言的诞生、事件或出现所作的“导论”。从表面上看，他引用的内容似乎与德里达本人对语言的出现或诞生所持的保留和犹豫的态度如出一辙。德里达引用列维-斯特劳斯的这段话：

I want to go back briefly to the relationship between Derrida and Lévi-Strauss. I suggested in the last lecture that while in some ways “Structure, Sign, and Play” is a critique of Lévi-Strauss, to a remarkable degree, confessed or unconfessed, it repeats his thinking. There is the moment when he quotes from Lévi-Strauss’s “Introduction” to the work of Marcel Mauss on the subject of the birth, event, or emergence of language. What he quotes would seem, on the face of it, to have just the sort of reservation and hesitation about the emergence or birth of language that Derrida himself has. Lévi-Strauss writes, quoted by Derrida:

“无论语言在动物生命尺度上出现的时机和环境如何，它都只能一蹴而就。事物不可能逐步产生意义。在经历了一场转变之后——这场转变的研究并非社会科学的范畴，而是生物学和心理学的范畴——事物从一个毫无意义的阶段过渡到另一个万物皆有意义的阶段。”
“Whatever may have been the moment and the circumstances of its appearance in the scale of animal life, language could only have been born in one fell swoop. Things could not have set about signifying progressively. Following a transformation the study of which is not the concern of the social sciences but rather of biology and psychology, a crossing over came about from a stage where nothing had a meaning to another where everything possessed it.”

仿佛一声巨响，语言突然就出现了。符号系统瞬间形成，而在此之前——哪怕就在昨天或一分钟前——语言根本不存在。这并非暗示有人突然观察某物并赋予其意义，然后又观察另一物并赋予其意义，最终，语言就出现了。（如果你从中听到了梅尔·布鲁克斯和卡尔·雷纳的《两千岁老人》的影子，那绝非偶然。）这种重构之所以毫无意义，是因为列维-斯特劳斯想要论证的是，意义这一概念的出现，瞬间赋予了万物意义。语言并非逐渐产生，而是一次断裂。

With a big bang, all of a sudden you had language. There in place was a semiotic system, whereas before—yesterday or a minute ago—there was no language at all. There’s no suggestion that suddenly someone looked at something and assigned it a meaning, then looked at something else and assigned it a meaning, and in the long run, lo and behold, there was language. (If you hear echoes of Mel Brooks and Carl Reiner’s “2000 Year Old Man” in this, that’s no accident.) The reason this reconstruction makes no sense is that bringing into existence the very thought of meaning, Lévi-Strauss wants to argue, instantly confers meaning on everything. There is no gradual emergence of language; there is a rupture.

德里达对这种论点感兴趣，是因为他意识到它与他自己在谈论事件、诞生、涌现等等问题时的犹豫不决有着相似之处。同时，他以批判的口吻指出，如果假定昨天没有语言，事物只是无意义地存在，而今天有了语言——事物之所以有意义是因为我们称之为语言的符号系统已经存在——那就意味着文化必然是在自然之后才出现的。按照这种观点，一旦文化出现——正如列维-斯特劳斯在《忧郁的热带》一书中深刻论述的那样——我们便开始对自然的直接性产生强烈的怀旧之情，而这种直接性已被文化所疏远和腐蚀。然而，德里达指出，这种怀旧之情恰恰创造了我们所怀旧之物。如果没有文化赋予自然意义，自然便不复存在，而这种意义的一部分就包含着对自然消逝的惋惜。民族志学者怀有怀旧或遗憾之情，认为由于欧洲民族中心主义者在田野调查中的过度干预，野蛮的思维已不复存在，这种情绪与上述观点如出一辙。“野蛮的思维”（这一表达也是列维-斯特劳斯最具雄心的著作之一的书名）正是民族中心主义观察者所创造的概念。

Derrida is interested in this argument because he recognizes its affinity with his own hesitation in talking about events, births, emergence, and so on. At the same time, he points out by way of criticism that to suppose that yesterday there was no language, there were just things as they are without meaning, and that today there is language—that things have meaning because that semiotic system we call language is in place—means that culture must come after nature. On this view, as soon as culture emerges—as Lévi-Strauss argues poignantly in a book called Tristes Tropiques, we begin to feel overwhelming nostalgia for the immediacy of nature, which is distanced and corrupted by culture. Derrida points out, however, that this nostalgia brings into existence what we are nostalgic for. There is no nature unless there is culture to give it meaning, part of which is regret for its disappearance. The nostalgia or regret of the ethnographer who says that because of the obtrusive research of ethnocentric Europeans in the field there is no longer a savage mind is of the same kind. “The Savage Mind” (an expression that provides the title of one of Lévi-Strauss’s most ambitious books) is a concept that the ethnocentric observer brings into being.

但德里达或许早已在列维-斯特劳斯身上找到了类似的批判。《生与熟》的标题本身就体现了这种批判。“生”？如果亚当坐在伊甸园里吃胡萝卜，他会称之为“生”吗？当然不会，因为“生”的概念只有在与“熟”相对立时才有意义。“生”与什么相对？亚当会问。“熟”使“生”得以存在，正如文化使自然存在一样。

But Derrida could have found his critique already expressed in Lévi-Strauss. The Raw and the Cooked itself stages this critique in its very title. Raw? If Adam sits in the garden and eats a carrot, would he call it raw? Certainly not, because the concept “raw” is meaningless except in contrast with “cooked.” Raw as opposed to what? Adam would say. “Cooked” brings “raw” into being in exactly the way culture brings nature into being.

这种理论上的基本推论，我们以前见过，以后还会多次见到，它看起来像是二元对立关系中优先级的颠倒，但与其说是颠倒，不如说是在提醒我们，它们彼此不可分割。换句话说，批评一种状态从另一种状态中涌现出来的说法，本质上是在说——我很抱歉用如此简化的方式来解释，但我真的看不出这样说有什么歪曲之处——我们无法知道先有鸡还是先有蛋，但我们知道二者缺一不可。

This basic move in theory, which we’ve seen before and will see many more times, looks like an inversion of priority in a binary pair, but it’s not so much that as a reminder that they cannot exist apart from each other. In other words, criticizing the imputed emergence of one state of things from another state of things is basically saying—I’m sorry to be so reductive about it but I really can’t see the distortion in saying this—that we can’t know whether the chicken or the egg came first but we do know you can’t have the one without the other.

这或许是解构主义的核心步骤，但任何研习哲学和文学理论的人都会对此感到熟悉，从黑格尔到我们在后续阅读中遇到的后解构主义思想家，莫不如此——其中最杰出的当属性别理论家朱迪斯·巴特勒，例如，她认为，如果没有“同性恋”这一既定框架，“异性恋”的概念是不可想象的。这些概念的绝对相互依存性是巴特勒性别观的核心。

This is perhaps the essential move of deconstruction, but anyone who studies philosophy as well as literary theory will find it familiar, from Hegel right on through to the postdeconstructive thinkers we encounter in the rest of our reading—preeminent among them the gender theorist Judith Butler, who argues, for example, that the “heterosexual” is inconceivable without the established framework of the “homosexual.” The absolute interdependency of these concepts is central to Butler’s view of gender.

那么，关于德里达对书写（ écriture ）和言语的区分，我再补充一点。这种区分并非反直觉地暗示书写先于言语。德里达只是坚持认为，我们不能假定书写是为了再现、模仿或转录言语而姗姗来迟。书写和言语是相互依存的现象。上次我们谈到了“差异”（ différance）。我们说过，以“ e”开头的“différence”和以“ a”开头的“ différance”之间的区别无法用言语表达。这种差异，或者说“差异”（différance），恰恰是在书写中产生的，也只有在书写中，我们才能突然领悟到“差异”（différance）作为差异和延宕的双重本质。我想稍作停顿——这将会引出德曼的观点——先谈谈一个有趣的法语例子，英语中没有类似的例子，但我认为它非常具有启发性，值得引入：est / et。首先，在法语单词est中，书写的s（我们可以说它代表“意义”）在发音时被省略了， est读作“ eh”，表示“是”。那么，“eh”也是法语单词et （表示“和”）的发音。这两个词恰好用法语表达了德里达试图描述的“补充性”的双重含义。“是”在隐喻意义上——“这就是那个，A 就是 B”——是一种补充，它为整体增添了意义。它通过宣告 A（等待通过比较来实现）同时也是 B 来完善整体。

Just a bit more, then, in this regard, concerning Derrida’s distinction between writing (écriture) and speech. This distinction is not meant counterintuitively to suggest that writing precedes speech. Derrida insists only that we must not suppose writing to have come into being belatedly in order to reproduce, imitate, or transcribe speech. Writing and speech are interdependent phenomena. Last time we spoke about différance. We said that the difference between différence with an e and différance with an a can’t be voiced. It’s a difference, or différance, that comes into being precisely in writing, and it’s only in writing that we suddenly grasp the twofold nature of différance as difference and deferral. I’d like to pause—this will be my segue to de Man—over an interesting example in French that we don’t have in English but is, I think, so instructive that it’s worth bringing in: est/et. For one thing, the written s in est, the s that means “signification,” we might say, is dropped out of this word when you say it, est (eh), the word for is. “Eh,” then, is also the pronunciation of et, the word for and. These two words precisely express in French what Derrida is trying to describe as the double meaning of “supplementarity.” Is in the sense of the metaphor—“This is that, A is B”—is a supplement that adds to a whole. It’s a means of completing a whole through the declaration that A, which awaits fulfillment through comparison, is also, among other things, B.

但“ is”还有另一种非修辞意义。即使从比喻意义上讲，A是B，我们也完全清楚A不是B。A怎么可能是B呢？A就是A。事实上，A是否是A本身就是一个问题，但它肯定不是B。在语法意义上，比喻的神秘化并不适用。在语法意义上，这个词是谓述的手段或原则，通过它，我们说一件事是另一件事：例如，母马是雌马。请注意，修辞意义上的“ is”和语法意义上的“ is ”之间的关系，本质上就是雅各布森所说的“诗性功能”和“元语言功能”之间的关系。正如你将在德曼的著作中看到的那样，这个词的修辞意义（声称具有比喻性）和语法意义（不声称具有比喻性，而仅仅是在句子中确立谓述）之间存在着一种不可调和的张力。

But is has another sense that is not a rhetorical sense. Even though metaphorically A is B, we know perfectly well that A is not B. How can A be B? A is only A. In fact, it’s even a question whether A is A, but it’s certainly not B. In the grammatical sense, the mystification of the metaphor doesn’t enter in. In the grammatical sense, this word is the means or principal of predication whereby we say one thing is another thing: a mare is a female horse, for example. Notice that the relationship between the rhetorical is and the grammatical is is basically the relationship between what Jakobson calls the “poetic function” and the “metalingual function.” As you’ll see in de Man, there is an irreducible tension between the rhetorical sense of this word, which claims metaphoricity, and the grammatical sense of this word, which makes no such claim but is simply the establishment of predication in a sentence.

现在， est和et的重叠（后者隐含于est的语法意义中）强化了补充的概念，这种补充并非指对需要补充才能完整的事物的完成——即隐喻中意义的实现——而是指对已完成事物的添加。在and或et这样的表达中，意义的同位语式添加也与雅各布森所说的“转喻”非常相似：即对相邻事物的添加，并不像语法谓词那样声称是隐喻性的。因此，仅仅通过观察这两个发音相似的词语所产生的张力，就为我们提供了一个象征，它体现了德里达所说的“补充性”以及德曼所说的修辞与语法之间不可化约的冲突。在本次讲座中，我们将重点讨论这一冲突，以探讨德曼的思想。

Now the overlap of est and et, which latter is implied in the grammatical sense of est, reinforces the idea of the supplement, not as the completion of something that requires a supplement to be complete—the fulfillment of meaning in a metaphor—but rather in the sense of adding on to something that’s already complete. The appositional addition of meaning in the expression and or et is also very much like what Jakobson calls “metonymy”: the adding on of things that are contiguous, making no claim to be metaphorical, as in grammatical predication. So the tension that arises simply by looking at these two similarly voiced words gives us an emblem of what Derrida calls “supplementarity” and what de Man calls the irreducible conflict between rhetoric and grammar. This conflict will be the focus of what we have to say about de Man in this lecture.

在上一讲中，我提到了德里达和德曼在耶鲁大学的共同经历，以及J·希利斯·米勒和与他们关系密切的学者——杰弗里·哈特曼和哈罗德·布鲁姆——在20世纪70年代和80年代初的鼎盛时期，这一时期也被称为“耶鲁学派”。该学派在学术界备受推崇，但在学术界内外也饱受争议。在这一时期，学院派的文学思考对远超文学本身的诸多领域产生了深远的影响。解构主义的范式渗透到各个非科学领域，甚至包括法律和建筑等看似毫不相干的领域。

Now in the last lecture I mentioned the presence of Derrida and de Man together at Yale, together with J. Hillis Miller and scholars who were linked with them—Geoffrey Hartman and Harold Bloom—in a period of flourishing in the 1970s and early 1980s, elsewhere called “the Yale school,” subject to much admiration in the academy and much vilification both within and outside the academy. This was a moment in which academic thinking about literature had a strong influence on topics much broader than literature. The paradigms of deconstruction infiltrated every nonscientific discipline, including fields as unlikely as law and architecture.

20世纪80年代，米勒去了加州大学欧文分校，德里达也随之而来。1983年，保罗·德曼去世，解构主义运动开始让位于其他兴趣和潮流，无论是在耶鲁大学（布鲁姆和哈特曼在那里发展了新的研究方向），还是在其他地方。（不过，我应该指出，解构主义，或者如德曼所称的“修辞阅读”，至今仍被相当多的学者以严谨的态度和精湛的技巧进行实践，其中许多人是德曼的学生，或是德曼学生的学生。）随后，在他去世后不久，关于德曼的一个令人震惊的发现浮出水面——我们的编辑在《符号学与修辞学》的斜体序言中提到过——这本身就令人震惊，也使得人们再也无法用同样的方式解读德曼——但我不得不说，这恰恰是解构主义的敌人所期待的。事实是，德曼年轻时仍居住在比利时，是位杰出的社会主义政治家的侄子。他曾为一家纳粹资助的比利时报纸撰写了一系列带有反犹倾向的文化文章，其中一些甚至公开反犹。这些文章在种族和文化上都以欧洲为中心，主张将犹太人排除在欧洲的知识生活之外。这些文章被汇编成册，以“保罗·德曼的战时新闻报道”为名出版，引发了轩然大波，其程度堪比当年揭露海德格尔与纳粹政府关系的丑闻。尽管这些丑闻从未被彻底压制，但随着更多内幕被披露，舆论的声势却愈演愈烈。20世纪80年代末，在真正读过德曼作品的人和没读过的人之间，就此展开了激烈的公开争论。一些人反对他的作品，认为解构主义本身就是纳粹主义的毒瘤；而另一些人则竭力挽救他的作品，使其免遭全面批判，并力图维护解构主义的遗产。

In the 1980s, Miller went to UC Irvine and Derrida followed him there. In 1983, Paul de Man died, and the movement began to give way to other interests and trends both at Yale—where Bloom and Hartman developed new interests—and elsewhere. (I should mention, though, that deconstruction, or “rhetorical reading” as de Man called it, is practiced with integrity and skill by a considerable number of scholars, many of them de Man’s students and students of his students, to this day.) And then, shortly after his death there came a shocking revelation about de Man—mentioned by our editor in the italicized preface to “Semiology and Rhetoric”—that was horrible in itself and made it impossible ever to read de Man in quite the same way again—but that was also, I have to say, precisely what the enemies of deconstruction were waiting for. This was the fact that in his youth, de Man, still living in Belgium, the nephew of a distinguished socialist politician, wrote for a Nazi-sponsored Belgian newspaper a series of cultural articles that were anti-Semitic in tendency, several of them openly anti-Semitic. Racially and culturally Eurocentric, they argued for the exclusion of Jews from the intellectual life of Europe. These papers were gathered and published as “Paul de Man’s wartime journalism,” and there was a tremendous furor about them, similar to the outcry against revelations, which had never been completely repressed but grew in magnitude as more and more was known about them, concerning Heidegger’s association with the Nazi government. In the late 1980s, there was a furious public dispute among both those who had actually read de Man and those who hadn’t. Some were opposed to his work, finding the cancer of Nazism in deconstruction itself, and some scrambled to save his work from wholesale indictment and preserve the legacy of deconstruction.

这一切都有据可查，尽管我强烈反对“他的作品从头到尾都受到了污染”这种论断，但出于礼貌，我们还是应该停下来思考一个更为具体的问题：他的作品在多大程度上可以被视为他隐瞒过去的借口？在《阅读的寓言》（Allegories of Reading）一书中，你也能找到一篇名为《符号学与修辞学》（Semiology and Rhetoric）的文章，其中收录了德曼的一篇论文，而真正读过德曼作品的人最常以此文来指责他。这篇文章探讨了卢梭《忏悔录》中的一段文字：卢梭描述自己偷了一条丝带，想送给一位他心仪的女仆，结果当被问及是谁偷的时，他脱口而出她的名字——玛丽昂。德曼说这根本不是什么指控——事实上，这只是脱口而出的一句毫无意义的话——而且无论如何，根本不可能坦白，不存在任何真正的、主观的、能够用自己的声音肯定或否认罪行或责任的主体性。公众没有德曼晚年反犹主义的证据，反而倾向于关注他对过去的隐瞒和拒绝坦白，并将《被盗的丝带》视为一种自我辩护的寓言，一种在名为《阅读的寓言》的书中具有个人意义的寓言式解读。

All of this is a matter of record, and even though I am one of those who strongly oppose the contaminated-through-and-through thesis, decency requires that we pause to weigh the somewhat narrower question to what extent his work can be seen to excuse his concealment of the past. In the book Allegories of Reading, where you’ll find also a version of “Semiology and Rhetoric,” one of de Man’s essays that those who had actually read de Man pointed to most accusingly is called “The Purloined Ribbon.” It concerns the passage in Rousseau’s Confessions where Rousseau describes having stolen a ribbon in order to give it to a serving maid to whom he felt attracted and then, when asked who had done it, having blurted out her name, Marion. De Man says this really wasn’t an accusation—in fact, this is just a meaningless word blurted out—and that in any case there is no possibility really of confession, no authentic subjectivity that can, as it were in its own voice, affirm or deny guilt or responsibility. The public, which had no evidence of anti-Semitism in de Man’s later life to point to, was inclined to focus instead on his concealment of the past, his refusal to confess, and singled out “The Purloined Ribbon” as a kind of allegory in self-defense, an allegorical reading with a personal application in a book called Allegories of Reading.

无论如何，就像解读海德格尔一样，由于我们现在所了解的，我们很难再用以往的方式解读德曼。不过，我还要指出，无论是在德曼的著作中，还是在解构主义中，都不存在任何隐晦的右翼思想——无论是反犹主义还是其他形式的右翼思想。对于解构主义所谓的“不可判定性”（这当然是一种怀疑主义），有两种可能的回应方式。一种敌对的回应是，不可判定性会在理智和良知中造成一个空洞，狂热和暴政会趁虚而入。许多人持有这种观点。对不可判定性的积极回应——在我看来，考虑到世界各地的狂热都源于盲目信仰而非怀疑，这种回应更为合理——可以这样理解：不可判定性是对一切观点本身进行持续不断的警惕审视，其目的正是为了抵制和反抗那些最恶劣、最顽固的观点：狂热和暴政的观点。这并非我在本课程中第一次遇到这样的十字路口：你不可能同时选择两条路，却又难以抉择。或许，最终选择哪条路取决于个人的性情，这或许比我们愿意承认的要重要得多。但我确实认为，在这种情况下选择一条路比在诠释学中选择一条路要容易得多。

As with Heidegger, in any case, it has been very difficult to read de Man in the same way we did as a result of what we now know. Let me just say also, though, that there is no cryptically encoded rightism—anti-Semitic or otherwise—either in de Man or in deconstruction. There are two possible ways of reacting to what deconstruction calls “undecidability,” which is certainly a form of skepticism. The hostile response is to claim that undecidability opens a void in the intellect and in conscience, a void into which fanaticism and tyranny can rush. Many entertain this view. The positive reaction to undecidability—far more reasonable in my view when we consider that fanaticism everywhere in the world arises from unquestioning belief, not from doubt–takes this form: undecidability is a perpetually vigilant scrutiny of all opinion as such, precisely in order to withstand and to resist those most egregious and incorrigible opinions of all: the opinions of fanaticism and tyranny. This isn’t the first time in this course that I’ve paused at a crossroads where you can’t possibly take both paths but where it is difficult to make up one’s mind. More than one can say or care to admit, it may ultimately be a matter of temperament which path one chooses to take. Yet I do think that the choice of a path in this case is easier than the choice of a path in hermeneutics.

既然我们谈到了解构主义，在深入探讨德曼之前，我想补充一点，如果可以的话，还有另一种不批评解构主义的方式。人们普遍认为，解构主义否认文本之外任何现实的存在。在《论文字学》中，德里达曾说过一句名言：“文本之外什么也没有。”他的意思是，除了文本之外，别无他物。我们生活的整个组织、结构和本质——包括我们只能作为文本来认识的历史，包括记忆的文本——都只能作为文本来解读。他的意思绝不是说“某个”文本，或者说某种文本，包含了所有重要的东西，除此之外别无他物。然而，人们普遍认为他的意思正是如此。德曼在你附录中的一段文字里，再次对这种流行的假设提出了反驳：

While we’re on the subject of deconstruction in general and before we get into de Man, let me just add that there is one other way, if I may, not to criticize deconstruction. It’s always supposed popularly that deconstruction denies the existence of any reality outside a text. In Of Grammatology, Derrida notoriously said “there is nothing outside the text.” What he meant by that is that there’s nothing but text. The entire tissue, structure, and nature of our lives—including history, which we can only know as a text, including the text of memory—is readable as and only as a text. He didn’t mean at all that “the” text, some text, contains everything that matters and that nothing else exists. It is widely believed, though, that that is what he did mean. De Man, in a passage included in your appendix, returns to the attack against this popular supposition:

在真正的符号学以及其他以语言学为导向的理论中，语言的指称功能（注意这里对雅各布森的引用）并未被否定——恰恰相反；（换句话说，这并非约翰逊博士所反驳的那种唯心主义对现实的否定，他踢了一块石头，然后痛苦地跳开，说道：“我这样反驳它。”没有人会否认我们称之为石头的坚硬物体的存在。现实是既定的，无论它是什么，而指称功能则不断地试图唤起这种现实。）问题在于它对自然或现象认知的权威性……（也就是说，我们能否运用语言这一工具来认识事物是什么——不是事物存在，而是事物是什么？德曼接着提出了一个极具挑战性的观点：）我们所谓的意识形态，恰恰是混淆了语言现实与自然现实，混淆了指称与现象主义。换句话说，意识形态无非就是这样一种信念：语言，我的语言——我用语言所说的话和我所想的话——表达的是真理。
In genuine semiology as well as in other linguistically oriented theories, the referential function of language [notice the allusion to Jakobson here] is not being denied–far from it; [In other words, it’s not a question of the idealist denial of reality refuted by Dr. Johnson when he kicked a stone and leaped away in terrible pain saying, “I refute it thus.” Nobody denies the existence of that hard thing we call a stone. Reality is simply given, whatever it may be, and the referential function is perpetually trying to evoke that reality.] what is in question is its authority for natural or phenomenal cognition.… [That is to say, can we know what things are—not that things are but what things are—using the instrument of language? De Man goes on to say very challengingly:] What we call ideology is precisely the confusion of linguistic with natural reality, of reference with phenomenalism. [In other words, ideology is nothing other than the belief that language, my language—what I say and what I think in language—speaks true.]

解构主义从未否认既有事物的存在。但德里达指出，既有事物确实以文本的形式呈现在世人面前，供人反思。这意味着，它仍有待解读。

Deconstruction never says that what’s out there doesn’t exist. But what’s out there does present itself to reflection, Derrida says, as a text. All that means is that it remains to be deciphered.

德曼的第一本书《盲目与洞察》收录的文章主要受到法国存在主义的影响，尤其是让-保罗·萨特的《存在与虚无》 。尽管《盲目与洞察》的论证已然带有怀疑主义和辩证法的色彩，预示着他后来的著作，但其论述在很大程度上早于德曼后来对语言学的关注，以及他对语言本身无意义物质性的思考——奥波雅兹在1914年正是利用这种语言发现了声音的非指涉性。该书中的文章，特别是题为《批评与危机》的文章（其中包含一段我在附录中引用的文字），最好被解读为存在主义的；但德曼很快吸收了索绪尔在语言学和结构主义方面的影响，从此他的词汇也带有了这一传统的色彩。例如，我们今天在文章中探讨的词汇，就源于雅各布森对隐喻和转喻之间关系的讨论，我们将会看到这一点。

The essays collected in de Man’s first book, Blindness and Insight, were mainly influenced by French existentialism, in particular Jean-Paul Sartre’s Being and Nothingness. The argument of Blindness and Insight, while already both skeptical and dialectical in anticipation of the later work, for the most part precedes de Man’s later preoccupations with linguistics and what he sees as the unsignifying materiality of language as such, the same language in which OPOJAZ in 1914 discovered the nonreferential nature of sound. The texts in that first book, in particular the essay called “Criticism and Crisis”—containing a passage that I quote in the appendix—can best be read as existentialist; but soon de Man absorbed the influence of Saussure in linguistics and structuralism, and his vocabulary henceforth took on the coloring of that tradition. The vocabulary that we wrestle with in today’s essay, for instance, derives from Jakobson’s discussion of the relationship between metaphor and metonymy, as we’ll see.

与此同时，既然我们已经看到德里达和德曼都受到了索绪尔思想的影响，或许就应该借此机会谈谈他们之间的异同。他们的共同之处在于，都认为思考“开端”非常困难，但同时，人们又必须找到某种方法，某种准结构主义的方法，来认识到在某个共时时刻之前，存在着另一个共时时刻。因此，在附录中的一段引文中（我稍后会再提到），德曼说道：“可以说，文学理论是在……时产生的……”——这是德曼对德里达“事件”的诠释，同样充满了复杂性。他同意语言的产生与先前中心能指（“上帝、人等等”）的出现有着本质的区别。德里达和德曼都认为，语言的出现与之前所有出现方式之间的区别在于，语言并不声称独立于自身之外。语言始终处于其自身的系统性本质之中，它既是结构之外的中心，也是结构之内的中心，这与所有其他“事件”截然不同。

In the meantime, it’s probably on this occasion, once we see that they share the influence of Saussurian thinking, that we should say a little bit about the similarities and differences between Derrida and de Man. In common, they take for granted that it is very difficult to think about beginnings, but that at the same time, one has to have some way, some quasi-structuralist way, of realizing that before a certain synchronic moment there was a different synchronic moment. Thus in a quote found in the appendix, to which I’ll return in the end, we find de Man saying, “Literary theory can be said to come into being when …”—that is de Man’s version of Derrida’s “event,” and it is every bit as fraught with complication. He agrees that the coming into being of language differs qualitatively from the emergence of prior head signifiers (“God, man, and so forth”). What both Derrida and de Man say about the difference between the emergence of language and all those prior emergences is that language does not purport to stand outside of itself. Language is perpetually caught up within its own systematic nature, a center that is not outside the structure as well as in it, as all the other “events” were.

他们也认同二元关系的相互决定性。例如，德曼说道（891-892）：

They agree also on the interdetermination of binary relations. De Man, for example, says (891–892):

不难看出，这种表面上以真理之名对批评家哲学家的推崇，实际上是对诗人作为真理主要来源的推崇。
It is easy enough to see that this apparent glorification of the critic-philosopher in the name of truth is in fact a glorification of the poet as the primary source of this truth.

他的意思并非像弗洛伊德所说的那样——诗人先于他出现，在他之前就已洞悉他所知的一切——即诗人的思想先于批评家和哲学家的思想。他的意思体现在以下几个分句中：

Now he does not mean—as Freud meant in saying the poets came before him and knew everything he knows before he knew it—that poets’ ideas preceded critic-philosophers’ ideas. What he means is what he says in the following clauses:

如果真理是对某种错误的系统性特征的认识，那么真理就完全取决于这种错误的先前存在。
[I]f truth is the recognition of the systematic character of a certain kind of error, then it would be fully dependent on the prior existence of this error.

换言之，真理源于谬误。谬误并非偏离真理，也并非如柏拉图所言，是对事物进行诗意的阐释，从而削弱哲学家所认定的真理的完整性。恰恰相反，哲学正是在对既有谬误的充分认知中产生的。德曼正是以此方式来思考文学与其他言语形式之间的关系。文学提出谬误，而批评家兼哲学家则从中认识到谬误本身所蕴含的真理——其不可化约的必然性。

In other words, truth arises out of error. Error is not a deviance from truth. Error is not a poetic elaboration on things that undermines the integrity of the truth identified by philosophers, as Plato claims. On the contrary, philosophy is what comes into being as the full acknowledgment of a preexisting error. That is the way de Man wants to think about the relationship precisely between literature and other forms of speech. Literature propounds error, and the critic-philosopher then recognizes the truth—the irreducible necessity—of that error.

德曼对真假二元对立的处理方式，使我意识到他与德里达的分歧。正如我所说，德里达将所有话语都视为连续的语篇或话语性。我们身处语篇之中。诚然，我们可以暂时或启发式地将某种语篇形式与另一种形式区分开来——文学、法律、神学、科学等等——但这些区分都很容易被瓦解和揭开神秘面纱。德曼并不认同这种观点。相反，德曼认为存在一种“文学性”。在这方面，他比德里达更始终如一地遵循雅各布森的观点。德曼反复强调文学与其他语篇形式之间的区别，这实际上是一种“为诗歌辩护”的论证。

De Man’s treatment of the interdeterminate truth-error binary brings me to his divergence from Derrida. As I said, Derrida sees all utterance as a continuous tissue of discourse, or discursivity. We are awash in discourse. Yes, we can provisionally or heuristically speak of one form of discourse as opposed to another—literature, law, theology, science, and so on—but such distinctions are all easily undermined and demystified. De Man does not agree. De Man thinks, on the contrary, that there is such a thing as “literariness.” He follows Jakobson much more consistently in this regard than Derrida does. Again and again, in what amounts to a “defense of poetry,” de Man insists on the difference between literature and other forms of discourse.

以下这段文字（883）中，德曼的语气听起来很像一位俄国形式主义者，他谈论的是文学所缺乏的其他话语形式所不具备的特征。他说：

Here is a passage (883) in which de Man sounds very much like a Russian formalist talking about the characteristic of literature that is lacking in other forms of discourse. He says:

文学作品不能仅仅被视为一个明确的指称意义单元，可以被解码而不留下任何痕迹。其编码异常醒目、复杂且神秘；它本身就吸引了过多的关注，而这种关注必须发展成一种严谨的方法。对编码本身的关注是不可避免的，文学必然会孕育出其自身的形式主义。
[L]iterature cannot merely be received as a definite unit of referential meaning that can be decoded without leaving a residue. The code is unusually conspicuous, complex, and enigmatic; it attracts an inordinate amount of attention to itself, and this attention has to acquire the rigor of a method. The structural moment of concentration on the code for its own sake cannot be avoided, and literature necessarily breeds its own formalism.

然而，当我们思考这种与其他话语形式差异的意义时，德曼的论述听起来就不那么像形式主义者了。在他看来，文学的“残余”，即其“文学性”或“与信息相契合”，揭示了其他话语形式（它们自以为指涉事物）所无法察觉的必然错误。文学深知自身的虚构性。它并非基于任何事物，而是虚构的。（或许回顾一下我们之前对西德尼在《诗辩》中相关论述的阐述会有所帮助。）批评，作为“关于”文学的批评（例如德曼的批评），必然会将文学残余、文学性中不可避免地出现的指涉错误或失败视为真理。正因如此，批评以及所有其他形式的指涉话语才会永远忘记自身的错误。

It is when we consider the implications of this difference from other forms of discourse, however, that de Man sounds less like a formalist. The “residue” of literature, its “literariness” or “set to the message,” is in his view the disclosure of the necessary error that other forms of discourse, supposing themselves to refer to things, remain unaware of. Literature knows itself to be fictive. It is not based on something but is made up. (It may help you to remember our account of what Sidney says in the Apologie for Poesie here.) Criticism, which is “about” literature (de Man’s criticism, for example), perforce refers to, as a truth, the error or failure of reference that inevitably appears in the residue, the literariness, of literature. That is why criticism and all other forms of referential discourse perpetually forget the error of their ways.

德曼在附录中的一段文字中写道：“批评界对语言的论述——符号与意义永远不可能重合——恰恰是我们称之为文学语言的那种语言所默认的。文学不同于日常语言，它始于对这种认知的超越；它是唯一一种摆脱了未经中介的表达谬误的知识形式”——摆脱了这样一种谬误：当我作为气象学家说“下雨了”时，我一定是在说真话。当文学作品说“下雨了”时，它并非在向窗外观察。作者或许在向窗外观察，但文本无法做到这一点。它虚构天气。“我们所有人都知道这一点，”德曼继续说道，“尽管我们以一种误导的方式，即一厢情愿地断言相反的情况。然而，当我们称文学为虚构作品时，真理便在我们对文学真正本质的预知中显现出来。 ”

De Man writes accordingly (in a passage included in your appendix): “the statement about language [by criticism], that sign and meaning can never coincide, is what is precisely taken for granted in the kind of language we call literary. Literature, unlike everyday language, begins on the far side of this knowledge; it is the only form of knowledge free from the fallacy of unmediated expression”—free from the fallacy that when I say “It is raining” as a meteorologist, I must be saying something true. When literature says “It is raining,” it is not looking out of the window. The author may have been looking out of the window, but a text can’t do that. It makes up weather. “All of us,” de Man continues, “know this, although we know it in the misleading way of a wishful assertion of the opposite. Yet the truth emerges in the foreknowledge we possess of the true nature of literature when we refer to it as fiction.”

正因如此，在一段摘自斯特凡诺·罗索访谈的文字中，德曼愿意大胆地将自己的作品与挚友雅克·德里达的作品区分开来。他说：

This is why, in a passage taken from an interview with Stefano Rosso, de Man is willing to venture on a categorical distinction between his own work and that of his close friend Jacques Derrida. He says:

我倾向于赋予文本（他指的是文学文本）一种内在的权威，我认为这种权威比德里达愿意赋予它们的要强得多……从某种复杂的角度来看，我会坚持“文本自我解构（换句话说，文学是对其指涉性的不断否定），是自我解构的”这一说法，而不是被来自文本之外的哲学干预所解构（德里达用他那轻巧的重锤砸向每一种可以想象的表达形式，这是一种“哲学干预”）。
I have a tendency to put upon texts [and he means literary texts] an inherent authority, which is stronger, I think, than Derrida is willing to put on them.… In a complicated way, I would hold to the statement that “the text deconstructs itself [in other words, literature is the perpetual denial of its referentiality], is self-deconstructive,” rather than being deconstructed by a philosophical intervention [Derrida bringing his delicate sledgehammer down on every conceivable form of utterance is a “philosophical intervention”] from outside the text.

从历史角度来看，《符号学与修辞学》接近于《结构、符号与游戏》开启的解构主义研究的尾声。德曼的这篇文章发表于《阅读的寓言》一书中，其目前的版本可追溯到20世纪80年代初，而它早在1979年就以不同的形式和略有不同的结论性论点发表过。甚至在德曼去世以及他的过往经历被揭露之前，就已经有很多人挥舞着拳头，质问道：“历史呢？现实呢？”我之前已经指出，这种回应可能而且常常是一种天真的误解，但它当时仍然非常盛行，并且实际上决定了文学理论的未来走向，甚至包括解构主义内部的“伦理转向”。在这种回应的氛围下，德曼说道（883）：

Historically, “Semiology and Rhetoric” comes near the end of the investment in deconstruction that “Structure, Sign, and Play” inaugurates. De Man’s essay, published in Allegories of Reading, dates from the early 1980s in its presented form, having appeared in a different form and with a slightly different concluding argument in 1979. Even before the death of de Man and the revelations about his past, there were a lot of people shaking their fists and saying, “What about history? What about reality?” I’ve already suggested that this response can be and often has been a naive misunderstanding, but it was still very much in the air and actually determined the future course of literary theory, even the “ethical turn” within deconstruction itself. De Man says, in this atmosphere of response (883):

我们仿佛在说，文学形式的问题已经彻底解决，结构分析的技巧也已臻于完美，我们现在可以“超越形式主义”，去探讨我们真正感兴趣的问题，并最终收获审美上专注于技巧所带来的成果，这些技巧为我们迈出这一决定性一步做好了准备。
We speak as if, with the problems of literary form resolved once and forever and with techniques of structural analysis refined to near-perfection, we could now move “beyond formalism” toward the questions that really interest us and reap, at last, the fruits of the aesthetic concentration on techniques that prepared us for this decisive step.

从他的角度来看，他显然是在说，如果我们采取这种做法，如果我们超越形式主义，我们就忘记了俄国形式主义者的一条基本原则：即形式与内容之间没有区别，实际上，无论我们多么希望超越形式主义，我们都无法做到。这就是他在本文中展开的论证。这篇文章的任务是否定修辞和语法之间所谓的相互促进和互补关系，即便是在像热拉尔·热奈特、托多罗夫、巴特等人那样严谨的修辞分析中也是如此，而这些人“都已从雅各布森的严谨性中倒退”。德曼则持相反观点，认为在任何文本中，修辞和语法都不可避免地相互冲突。

From his viewpoint clearly he’s saying that if we make this move, if we move beyond formalism, we will have forgotten the cardinal rule of the Russian formalists: namely, that there’s no distinction between form and content, that we in effect cannot move beyond formalism no matter how much we may wish to do so. That’s the argument he develops in this essay. The task of the essay is to deny the supposed mutual reinforcement and complementarity of rhetoric and grammar even in rigorous rhetorical analysis like that of Gérard Genette, Todorov, Barthes, and others, all of whom have “regressed from the rigor of Jakobson.” De Man argues on the contrary that in any text, rhetoric and grammar are inescapably at odds.

我认为，这个论点与德里达的一篇题为《系词的补充》的文章有关，我之前在讨论“是”作为隐喻（修辞）和“是”作为谓词（语法）之间的不匹配时，就曾提到过这篇文章。前者强调同一性，而后者则表示主语和谓语之间的及物关系（男孩正在击球），或者表示主语和其属性之间的不及物关系（男孩很敏捷）。

This argument, I think, has something to do with an essay by Derrida called “The Supplement of Copula,” which I was alluding to earlier in discussing the misfit between “is” as a metaphor (rhetoric) and “is” as a predication (grammar). The former asserts identity while the latter indicates either transitive agency between a subject and a predicate (the boy is batting the ball) or the intransitive connection between a subject and its attribute (the boy is agile).

为了探究这种区别，德曼首先选取了当时一部热门情景喜剧《一家子》（All in the Family）。正如德曼所解释的，当阿奇·邦克（Archie Bunker）反问妻子伊迪丝（Edith）“有什么区别？”时，伊迪丝开始详细解释保龄球鞋鞋带朝上和朝下到底有什么不同，这让阿奇感到十分恼火。当然，这个反问句的意思是“我不在乎有什么区别”。但正如德曼所说，伊迪丝是一位思维极其简单的读者，她把这个反问句误解成了一个语法问题：“有什么区别？我很好奇。”阿奇对此无法忍受，因为在他看来，反问句就是反问句，这一点显而易见。

In pursuit of this distinction, de Man begins with a popular sitcom of the time, “All in the Family.” As de Man explains, Archie Bunker becomes exasperated when his wife Edith begins to tell him what the difference actually is between bowling shoes laced over and bowling shoes laced under in response to Archie’s rhetorical question, “What’s the difference?” Of course, the meaning of the rhetorical question was “I don’t care what the difference is.” But Edith, a reader of sublime simplicity, as de Man says, misinterprets the rhetorical question as a grammatical question: “What is the difference? I’m curious to know.” Archie can’t stand this because to him it’s perfectly clear that a rhetorical question is a rhetorical question.

然而，这一点也极其简单。德曼的观点是，如果不诉诸意图，一个问题既是修辞性的又是语法性的——而且，一个问题中蕴含的两个问题必然会有相互矛盾的答案。他随后转向叶芝的诗作《在学童之间》，使论点更加复杂，但并未改变。你还记得这首诗的结尾吗？“我们如何区分舞者和舞蹈？”这又是一个双重问题。这个修辞性问题完善了这首诗的通常解读。这个修辞性问题的答案是，我们无法区分舞者和舞蹈，因为它们在一个综合的、象征性的瞬间中融为一体，构成了这件艺术作品。 （请注意，反问句通常暗示某种隐喻意义上的同一性——“有什么区别？”——这正是它们具有反问性质的原因。）在对这首诗的这种解读中，所有前面提到的隐喻都指向了象征性统一的胜利感，而这正是艺术作品的本质——这种统一性包含着作者与文本、主体与行动的统一，以及文学理论解构的所有二元对立的统一。

That too, though, is sublimely simple. De Man’s point is that without appealing to intention a question is both rhetorical and grammatical—and that inevitably the two questions lurking within the one will have conflicting answers. He complicates without changing the argument by turning then to Yeats’s poem, “Among Schoolchildren,” which concludes, you remember: “How can we tell the dancer from the dance?” Another twofold question. The rhetorical question completes the usual reading of the poem. The answer to the rhetorical question is that we cannot tell the difference between the dancer and the dance because they are unified in a synthetic, symbolic moment that constitutes the work of art. (Note that rhetorical questions in general imply some metaphorical identity—“what’s the difference?”—which is what makes them rhetorical.) All the preceding metaphors in this reading of the poem lead up to this triumphant sense of symbolic unity as the essence of the work of art—a unity that entails among other things the unity of author and text, agent and action, the unity of all of those dualities that much literary theory deconstructs.

但德曼问道，假设这是一个语法问题，一个出于真诚（即便只是单纯）的好奇心而提出的问题呢？这个问题的答案似乎显而易见。这里是舞者，这里是表演的舞蹈，显然它们并非同一回事。德曼曾撰写过关于叶芝的博士论文，他随后列举了叶芝其他诗歌中的大量例证，表明叶芝显然理解语法差异的不可化约性。基于这些证据，德曼认为这首诗中蕴含着某种程度的反讽，使其免于陷入其表面所呈现的象征性迷雾之中。但他并非声称（正如他反复强调的那样）他的解释才是唯一正确的解释。他只是认为这种解释是存在的，并且可以从我们所谓的“证据”中推导出来，正如基于反问句的象征性解读同样存在，并且可以从证据中推导出来一样。因此，这两种解读无法调和，但也不能排除任何一种可能性。

But suppose this were a grammatical question, de Man asks, a question posed out of sincere, if simple, curiosity? The answer to that question seems painfully obvious. Here is the dancer and here is the dance that is performed and clearly they’re not the same thing. Then de Man, who had written a doctoral dissertation on Yeats, adduces an impressive array of examples from other Yeats poems showing that Yeats clearly grasps the irreducibility of grammatical difference. On this evidence de Man argues that there is a measure of irony in the poem that saves it from the symbolizing mystifications it appears to indulge in. But he’s not claiming, as he is at pains to point out, that his explication is the true one. He claims only that it is available and can be adduced from what we call “evidence” in the same way that the symbolic interpretation, based on the rhetorical question, is available and can be adduced from evidence. These two readings, then, can’t be reconciled, yet neither can be ruled out.

在所有以系词“是”为核心或暗示该系词的句子中——也就是说，在所有句子中——隐喻和谓语总是相互冲突的。隐喻是我们所说的诗意谎言。人人都知道A不是B。而谓语则通常服务于指称性，它是一种真理断言。但如果修辞性和语法性在所有句子中都并存，那么真理断言和谎言就永远相互矛盾，它们互相否定。当然，我们非常清楚伊迪丝和阿奇·邦克的意图，所以我们不会混淆他们所说的话的含义。但阿奇的问题确实包含两种含义，而伊迪丝却通过混淆它们来帮助澄清这两种含义。

In a sentence built around or implying the copula “is”—in all sentences, that is—metaphor and predication are always going to be at odds. A metaphor is what we call a poetic lie. Everybody knows A is not B. A predication, on the other hand, usually goes forward in the service of referentiality. It’s a truth claim of some kind. But if rhetoricity and grammaticality coexist in all sentences, the truth claim and the lie are perpetually at odds with each other, they belie each other. Of course, we know perfectly well what Edith intends and what Archie Bunker intends, so we don’t confuse the meaning of what they’re saying. But Archie’s question does harbor two meanings, and Edith helps clarify them by managing to confuse them.

但是，德曼继续他精彩的论述，假设阿奇·邦克是阿奇（希腊语意为“起源”）·德·邦克呢？假设阿奇·邦克是雅克·德里达，并提出“什么是差异？”这个问题呢？那将是完全不同的情况，不是吗？因为你根本无法判断这个问题是修辞性的还是语法性的。在这种情况下，就不可能援引意图，因为德里达引入的整个复杂过程恰恰在于提出这样一个问题：我们无法表达“差异”（隐喻）和“差异”（转喻）之间的差异，因此也无法判断阿奇是对的还是伊迪丝是对的。

But, de Man continues in a magnificent flight, suppose Archie Bunker were Arche (Greek for “origin”) Debunker? Suppose Archie Bunker were Jacques Derrida and put the question “What is the différance?” That would be an entirely different matter, wouldn’t it, because you would have absolutely no idea whether the question was rhetorical or grammatical. In that case, it wouldn’t be possible to invoke an intention because the whole complication introduced by Derrida is precisely to raise the question about not being able to voice the différance between différence (metaphor) and différance (metonymy) and not knowing therefore whether Archie is right or whether Edith is right.

在剩余的篇幅里，我只能略述德曼对普鲁斯特作品中马塞尔阅读寓言的解读。首先，德曼在文章开头就通过描写祖母总是把马塞尔赶到花园里，因为她无法忍受他阅读时的内心世界，从而为他对这段文字的高潮讨论埋下了伏笔。随后，德曼探讨了马塞尔如何将室外景象带入室内：他在凉爽昏暗的房间里阅读时，始终意识到阳光普照的花园里发生的一切，最终，在他沉浸于阅读的奇妙时刻，内外之间失去了界限。由此，一种对内外关系的修辞理解——一种将二者融合的隐喻——得以实现。然而，语法分析表明，这段文字的整体结构是叠加的，是对意象的复杂化和阐释，并不暗示任何同一性。德曼将这种更具时间性的展开称为转喻。

De Man’s reading of Marcel’s allegory of reading in Proust I can only skim in the space remaining. Remember to begin with that de Man sets up his climactic discussion of this passage at the beginning of the essay by talking about the grandmother who’s always driving Marcel out into the garden because she can’t stand the interiority of his reading. In the long run, de Man then discusses Marcel’s description of how he brought the outside inside, perpetually conscious while reading in his cool, darkened room of everything that was going on in the sun-drenched garden, so that ultimately, in the charmed moment of his reading, there was no difference between inside and outside. Thus a rhetorical understanding of the relationship between inside and outside, a metaphor conflating the two, has been accomplished. Yet grammatical analysis shows that the whole structure of the passage is additive, a complication and elaboration of the imagery with no implication of identity. This more temporal unfolding de Man calls metonymic.

我们不妨顺便承认，将修辞手法——转喻——与语法在组合层面上等同起来，或许会造成不必要的混淆。但正如我之前所说，雅各布森已经认可了这种将修辞滑入语法范畴的做法，一旦我们在解读普鲁斯特时遇到“语法的修辞化”，我们或许会觉得有必要默认这种混淆的存在。与此同时，为了避免我们仅仅因为觉得这段文字的结构最终符合语法就沾沾自喜，我们必须记住，整段描述都是由一个声音说出来的，是贯穿始终的统一的语气和态度。“这就是我所说的，”德曼说道，“语法的修辞化。”但他还没说完！那个声音并非作者的声音。说话者是马塞尔，他正施展着隐喻的魔力，但我们知道，作者普鲁斯特正以极其费力、精雕细琢的方式，一丝不苟地构建着这段描述，层层叠加意象，以一种符合语法（转喻）而非修辞的方式展开。此时此刻，我们已然抵达了“修辞的语法化”之处，而且丝毫没有想过会在此停留。室内阴冷黑暗，室外炎热明亮，两者皆寂静无声；但它们在马塞尔的“洪流” （如同清凉的水流）与其近义词“灼热”（torride ）交汇的听觉中融为一体。室内是隐喻的，室外是语法的；它们有时融合，有时分离——但始终无法确定。

We should concede in passing that a perhaps needless confusion arises in making a rhetorical device, metonymy, synonymous with grammar on the axis of combination. But as I said earlier, this slippage of rhetoric into grammar is already authorized by Jakobson, and once we encounter “the rhetoricization of grammar” in this reading of Proust we may feel the need to acquiesce in the confusion. In the meantime, lest we rest content feeling that the structure of the passage is grammatical after all, we must remember that the whole description is spoken by a voice, the overarching sameness of tone and attitude that unifies everything after all. “This is what I call,” says de Man, “the rhetoricization of grammar.” But he is not finished! That voice is not that of the author. The speaker is Marcel performing his metaphoric magic, but we know there is an author, Proust, painstakingly putting this description together in the most laborious, calculating way, building one image on another in a sequence that’s grammatical (metonymic), not rhetorical. We have arrived, without thinking for a moment by this time that we could remain there, at the “grammaticization of rhetoric.” The interior is cool and dark, the exterior is hot and bright, both are silent; but they merge in the audible confluence of Marcel’s word torrent (as of cool water) with its near-homonym torride. The interior is metaphorical, the exterior is grammatical; sometimes they merge, sometimes draw apart—but always undecidably.

最后要反驳的是对解构主义的最后一个批评是：“它使文学变得毫无意义。”德曼经常说，我希望这些例子能够表明，修辞解读并非否定意义，而是承认意义总是以过剩的形式存在，是至关重要的，是补充性的。意义永远不嫌多。

One last criticism of deconstruction to fend off: “it makes literature meaningless.” De Man often says, and I hope these illustrations show, that rhetorical reading is not a denial of meaning but an acknowledgment that meaning always exists in excess, seminally, supplementarily. You can never have enough of it.

 

 

作者（读者）和心灵

Author (Reader) and Psyche

 

 

第十二章

CHAPTER 12

弗洛伊德与小说
Freud and Fiction

阅读材料：

Readings:

布鲁克斯，彼得。“弗洛伊德的宏大情节。”载于《批判传统》，第 882-892 页。

Brooks, Peter. “Freud’s Masterplot.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 882–892.

弗洛伊德，西格蒙德。“梦的运作。”载于《批判传统》，第 500-508 页。

Freud, Sigmund. “The Dream-Work.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 500–508.

本次讲座标志着一个过渡阶段。我们已经完成了对以形式和语言为重点的理论概述。现在，我们将重点放在文学的心理特征上，并由此探讨文学的社会和文化决定因素。

In this lecture we mark a transition. We have completed our survey of theory that makes form and language its focus. We move now to an emphasis on the psychological profile of literature, and from there to the social and cultural determinants of literature.

到目前为止，我们已经探讨了论证思想和言语由语言产生，并且与它们的语言环境密不可分的各种方法。不过，我们将从语言决定的言语、话语和文学观念过渡到话语的心理决定论，过程将会非常顺利，因为我们将要探讨的两位理论家——彼得·布鲁克斯和雅克·拉康——虽然借鉴了弗洛伊德的理论，并以精神分析的视角审视他们的研究，但他们使用的仍然是我们现在非常熟悉的词汇。他们认为，意识与无意识的关系最好放在我们一直在研究的形式主义和符号学传统的语境中来理解。拉康曾说过一句名言（你很快就会再次听到），“无意识的结构就像一种语言”，而布鲁克斯显然也同意这一点。除了他对弗洛伊德文本的依赖，尤其是《超越快乐原则》（我将尝试概述这一语境），你会发现布鲁克斯的论述对你来说已经非常熟悉。顺便一提，他曾在耶鲁大学就读，正值耶鲁学派的鼎盛时期，此后也一直在那里。虽然他是我上次提到的圈子里一位受人尊敬、年纪稍短的成员，但我当时没有提及他，因为他的作品根植于结构主义和精神分析（在这方面与拉康相似），并且能够抵御解构主义的影响。等我们谈到拉康时——他的风格更接近德里达而非布鲁克斯——我会尝试阐明结构主义精神分析与解构主义究竟有何不同。
