So far we have reviewed ways of arguing that thought and speech are brought into being by language and are inseparable from their linguistic milieu. Our transition from language-determined ideas about speech, discourse, and literature to the psychological determination of discourse will be a smooth one, though, because Peter Brooks and Jacques Lacan, two of the theorists we’ll consider who borrow from Freud and view their projects in psychoanalytic terms, are nevertheless still using what is now for us an extremely familiar vocabulary. They maintain that consciousness in its relation to the unconscious is best viewed in the context of the formalist and semiotic traditions we have been studying. Lacan famously said, as you’ll hear again soon, “The unconscious is structured like a language,” and Brooks plainly does agree. Apart from his reliance on the texts of Freud, especially Beyond the Pleasure Principle, a context I’ll be attempting to sketch in, you’ll find Brooks writing on what for you is now familiar ground. He was at Yale, by the way, during the heyday of the Yale school and long thereafter. Although he was a respected, somewhat younger member of the circle I mentioned last time, I did not mention him then because his work is grounded in structuralism and psychoanalysis (like Lacan’s in that regard) and withstands the influence of deconstruction. When we get to Lacan, whose manner is much closer to Derrida’s than to Brooks’s, I’ll try to show just wherein structuralist psychoanalysis differs from deconstruction.

布鲁克斯在《阅读情节》节选中，借用了俄国形式主义者对“情节”和“故事”的区分，以此来解释叙事小说的本质。我最好还是先说明一下，克服了使用我甚至都念不出来的词汇的尴尬，这些概念在俄语中分别是“sjužet”和“fabula”，因为布鲁克斯用的就是这两个词。在我看来，它们有点反直觉，因为如果你试图在英语中寻找对应的同源词，你会认为“ sjužet ”应该是“主题”，这更接近于形式主义者翻译成英语的“故事”的意思；而你会认为“fabula ”很可能类似于“情节”或“小说”。但事实恰恰相反。“sjužet”指的是情节，即故事的构建方式；而“fabula”指的是构成“sjužet”的主题或素材。

Brooks begins the excerpt you have read from Reading for the Plot by borrowing the Russian formalist distinction between “plot” and “story” in an effort to explain what narrative fiction is. I had better let you know finally, overcoming my embarrassment about using words I can’t even pronounce, that the Russian words for these concepts, plot and story, are sjužet and fabula, respectively, because those are the terms Brooks uses. They’re a little counterintuitive, it seems to me, because if you try to find cognates for them in English you’d think that sjužet would be “subject matter,” something much closer to what the formalists translated into English mean by “story,” and you’d think that fabula might well be something like “plot” or “fiction.” But it’s just the opposite. Sjužet is the plot, the way a story is constructed, and the fabula is the subject matter or material out of which the sjužet is made.

此外，关于情节与故事的关系，布鲁克斯使用了我们在阅读雅各布森和德曼的著作后会熟悉的术语：“隐喻”和“转喻”。现代文学理论家们心照不宣地将古典修辞学的众多修辞手法简化为这两个术语。必要时，他们会添加一些其他修辞手法（肯尼斯·伯克在《动机语法》的附录中列出了四种，哈罗德·布鲁姆列出了六种，德曼本人也提到了寓言、反讽和拟人），但正如文学理论所言，古典修辞学的核心区别在于隐喻和转喻之间的区别。隐喻具有统一、综合和融合的作用，而转喻则使一个符号与另一个符号相连，但并不声称具有统一性或建立同一性。

In addition, concerning the relationship between plot and story, Brooks uses terms that are familiar after our reading of Jakobson and de Man: “metaphor” and “metonymy.” There’s a tacit agreement among modern literary theorists to reduce all the many tropes of classical rhetoric to just these two terms. When it’s necessary, they add a few (there are four in Kenneth Burke’s appendix to The Grammar of Motives, six in Harold Bloom, and de Man himself turns also to allegory, irony, and prosopopoeia), but the essential bifurcation in classical rhetoric, as literary theory sees it, is the distinction between metaphor, which unifies, synthesizes, and brings together, and metonymy, which makes one sign contiguous with another but makes no claim to unify or establish identity.

那么，彼得·布鲁克斯从弗洛伊德那里汲取了什么呢？他是一位杰出的弗洛伊德研究学者，对弗洛伊德的各个方面都抱有浓厚的兴趣。但就我们的目的而言，我们不妨说，他尤其从弗洛伊德那里汲取的是无意识中欲望的结构及其本质：就我们所能想象的，弗洛伊德对拉康的先见之明（拉康本人也确实声称弗洛伊德先于他），无意识的结构如同语言，但又是一种意志性的语言。毋庸置疑，当我们转向心灵时，我们又回到了意图的领域，只不过现在我们遇到的是类似无意识意图的东西。布鲁克斯希望将这一宏大的概念映射到虚构情节的构建上。

What, then, does Peter Brooks take from Freud? He is a distinguished Freudian scholar who has a deep interest in every aspect of Freud, but for our purposes let us say that what he takes in particular from Freud is the structuring of desire in the unconscious and the nature of that structuring: the idea, insofar as we can imagine Freud anticipating Lacan (Lacan himself certainly claimed that Freud anticipated him), that the unconscious is structured like a language but, as it were, a volitional language. In turning to the psyche, we are back in the realm of intention, needless to say, only now we encounter something like unconscious intention. Brooks wants to map this broad idea onto the construction of fictional plots.

亚里士多德告诉我们，情节有开头、中间和结尾。我们或许会认为这是哲学家提出的最不言自明的概念，但即便如此，我们也必须承认亚里士多德在情节方面的洞察力。当然，我们会抱怨，情节必须要有开头，而且除非像舍赫拉扎德那样拼命地维持故事发展，否则情节必须要有结尾。然而，我们不妨问问自己，为什么情节需要中间部分？中间部分相对于开头和结尾的作用是什么？而且不仅仅是任何中间部分：正如布鲁克斯引述的那样，亚里士多德为什么说情节应该“有一定的长度”？为什么情节不能更短或更长？中间部分究竟是如何揭示开头与结尾之间必然的联系的？毕竟，开头并非随意设定的起点（它有其前因，这些前因也可能成为开头），而是一个引发某种逻辑的时刻或事件，在中间部分完成其工作之后，最终以悲剧、喜剧或模棱两可的方式得到解决。那么，中间部分究竟是如何成为检验和探索这种逻辑的场域的呢？布鲁克斯认为，他可以用精神分析的术语来理解这些问题。

Aristotle tells us that a plot has a beginning, a middle, and an end. We are likely to think that the most self-evident concept ever posited by a philosopher, yet we must accord a degree of acumen even to Aristotle on plot. Well, of course, we grumble, it has to have a beginning, and we assume that unless we’re desperately keeping things going like Scheherazade, it has to have an end. Yet we might well ask ourselves, why does it have a middle? What is the function of the middle with respect to the beginning and the end? And not just any middle: Why does Aristotle say, as Brooks quotes him, that a plot should have “a certain magnitude”? Why shouldn’t it be shorter or longer? What in particular does the middle have to do with revealing to us the necessary connectedness of the beginning with the end? The beginning, after all, is not just an arbitrary starting point (it has antecedents that could have been a beginning) but a moment or event that precipitates a certain logic, a moment that is resolved in turn tragically, comically, or noncommittally by the end after the middle has done its work. How especially does the middle become a field in which this logic is tested and explored? Brooks believes that he can understand these questions in psychoanalytic terms.

布鲁克斯还借鉴了弗洛伊德的方法论思想，即可以根据弗洛伊德在《梦的解析》（1905）中对凝缩和置换的区分来思考情节结构。凝缩提取梦境的基本符号，并将它们提炼成一个过度决定的统一体，这样，如果研究梦的运作方式，就能看到梦中所表达的潜在愿望或欲望以特定的符号统一体或关联的形式显现出来。在置换中，梦中某些欲望的元素，可能是被压抑得最严重的那些，并没有以凝缩的符号形式表达，而是被置换到看似无关的想法、意象或活动中，而这些想法、意象或活动需要解释者去解读。置换是对解释性理解的一种延迟或绕道，而凝缩则是一种提炼，这种提炼或许过于压缩，以至于也对理解构成挑战。这两种运作方式同时进行。梦的运作方式同时凝缩和置换它既隐藏又努力显现为欲望对象的东西。

Brooks also borrows from Freud the methodological idea that one can think about plot structure in terms of the distinction Freud makes in The Interpretation of Dreams (1905) between condensation and displacement. Condensation takes the essential symbols of the dream and distills them into an overdetermined unity so that if one studies the dream work, one can see the underlying wish or desire expressed in the dream manifest itself in a particular symbolic unity or nexus. In displacement, certain elements of desire in the dream, probably the most severely repressed, are not expressed in condensed symbols but rather are displaced onto seemingly irrelevant ideas, images, or activities that the interpreter needs to decode. Displacement is a delay or detour of interpretive understanding, and condensation, on the other hand, is a distillation perhaps so extremely compressed that it too challenges understanding. These operations work simultaneously. The dream work simultaneously condenses and displaces what it is at once concealing and struggling to make manifest as its object of desire.

最早注意到弗洛伊德的凝缩和置换与雅各布森的隐喻和转喻之间可能存在富有成效的理论联系的人是雅克·拉康，布鲁克斯也引用了拉康的观点来佐证这一点。其前提是，在日常话语中，无论是在我们的对话中，还是在我们对梦境的描述以及我们向分析师讲述的其他内容中，欲望都是通过梦境运作的这两个方面（即修辞格）来表达的。凝缩以隐喻的方式运作，而置换则以转喻的方式运作。转喻是意义的延迟或持续的差异化。隐喻则是将试图沿着情节线表达自身的欲望凝结成一个清晰的瞬间。正如布鲁克斯所论证的，在小说中，我们观察到这两种修辞倾向是并存的。或许你能感受到德曼的《符号学与修辞学》在此背景下所蕴含的某种张力：隐喻和转喻是否和谐共存，是否最终导向统一，取决于你阅读的是哪位学者的作品。无论如何，它们的确以某种方式共存，以至于我们可以观察到虚构叙事的发展与梦境的形成之间存在相似之处。

The first person to notice that there might be a fruitful theoretical connection between Freud’s condensation and displacement and Jakobson’s metaphor and metonymy was Jacques Lacan, whom Brooks quotes to this effect. The premise is that desire in everyday discourse, in our conversation but also in our account of our dreams and in the rest of what we tell our analyst, expresses itself through the medium of these two aspects of the dream work understood as tropes. Condensation works metaphorically and displacement works metonymically. Metonymy is the delay or perpetual différance of signification. Metaphor is the gathering up in a crystalline moment of the desire that’s attempting to articulate itself along a plot line. In fiction, as Brooks argues, we observe that these two rhetorical tendencies coexist. You can perhaps feel an implied tension with de Man’s “Semiology and Rhetoric” in the background here: metaphor and metonymy may or may not work in harmony, may or may not conduce to an ultimate unity, depending whom you read. Be that as it may, though, they nevertheless do coexist in such a way that we can observe the resemblance between the development of a fictional narrative and the development of dreams.

如果布鲁克斯对弗洛伊德感兴趣的地方正是这类东西，我们应该立即意识到，他与我们可能倾向于刻板印象中的传统精神分析批评家截然不同。他不会到处寻找俄狄浦斯情结和阳具象征。当有人点燃雪茄或系领带时，他也不会（至少不会）长时间地停留。他在你摘录的结尾处也表达了这一点（1171）。

If this sort of thing is what interests Brooks in Freud, we should recognize immediately that he is not anything like what we may be tempted to caricature as a traditional psychoanalytic critic. He doesn’t go around looking for Oedipus complexes and phallic symbols. He doesn’t pause, at least for long, when somebody lights a cigar or wears a necktie. He says as much at the end of your excerpt (1171);

[T]可以对文本本身进行精神分析批评[他所做的，就是]，而这种批评不会像通常那样，变成对文本的心理发生（作者的无意识）、文学反应的动力（读者的无意识）或人物的隐秘动机（假设他们有一个“无意识”）的研究。
[T]here can be psychoanalytic criticism of the text itself [what he’s doing, that is] that does not become—as has usually been the case—a study of the psychogenesis of the text (the author’s unconscious), the dynamics of literary response (the reader’s unconscious), or the occult motivations of the characters (postulating an “unconscious” for them).

换句话说，布鲁克斯对发展一套关于作者、读者或人物的精神分析理论并不感兴趣。我说过，在本阶段的课程中，我们将重新回到意图的范畴，的确如此；但这是一种经过精心限定的意图，或许并非不会受到批评：它指的是语言本身或文本的能动性。

In other words, Brooks is not interested in developing a psychoanalytic theory of the author, of the reader, or of character. I said we were back in the realm of intention during this phase of the syllabus, and we are; but it’s a carefully confined sort of intention, perhaps not immune to criticism: it’s the agency of language itself, or of the text.

布鲁克斯在这段文字中并非对传统的弗洛伊德批评抱有居高临下的态度，至少并非全盘否定；他只是阐明了一个不同的目的。虽然本课程不会深入探讨传统的弗洛伊德批评，但它确实非常有趣：例如，弗洛伊德的弟子欧内斯特·琼斯曾撰写过一篇颇具影响力的莎士比亚《哈姆雷特》研究，他在文中指出哈姆雷特存在俄狄浦斯情结。如果你不注意到琼斯的论述颇有道理，就无法对这部剧做出真诚的回应；事实上，在莎士比亚戏剧的舞台和电影史上，劳伦斯·奥利弗爵士正是在欧内斯特·琼斯的影响下扮演了哈姆雷特一角，这已成为一段佳话。他饰演的哈姆雷特与格特鲁德的关系，清晰地展现了他俄狄浦斯情结的痛苦。此外，还有一些文学作品直接受到弗洛伊德的影响。在D·H·劳伦斯的《儿子与情人》中，主人公保罗·莫雷尔深受俄狄浦斯情结的折磨，无法自拔。时间快进到当代，我们将在后文探讨的文学理论重要人物哈罗德·布鲁姆，在其一系列著作（始于《影响的焦虑》）中，发展出一套关于作者的理论，将后世诗人与其前辈之间的关系视为父子之间的竞争。我本人也曾援引这种思路，论证列维-斯特劳斯对俄狄浦斯神话的解读暴露了他自身与弗洛伊德相关的俄狄浦斯情结。显然，带有此类倾向的弗洛伊德式批评十分普遍，时有出现，其对文学理论的影响不容忽视。

Brooks in this passage is not condescending toward traditional Freudian criticism, or certainly not all of it; he is just announcing a different purpose. Although we don’t linger over traditional Freudian criticism in this course, it can indeed be extremely interesting: just for example, Freud’s disciple Ernest Jones wrote an influential study of Shakespeare’s Hamlet in which he showed that Hamlet has an Oedipus complex. You can’t respond honestly to the play without seeing that there’s a good deal in what Jones is saying; in fact, famously in the history of the staging and filming of Shakespeare, Sir Laurence Olivier played the role of Hamlet under the influence of Ernest Jones. His Hamlet makes it painfully clear in his relations with Gertrude that he had an Oedipus complex. Again, there are actual works of literature written directly under the influence of Freud. In D. H. Lawrence’s Sons and Lovers, the central character, Paul Morel, is crippled by an Oedipus complex that he can’t master. Moving closer to the present, an important figure in literary theory whom we’ll be studying later, Harold Bloom, develops in a series of books, beginning with The Anxiety of Influence, a theory of the author that views the relationship between belated poets and their precursors as a rivalry between sons and fathers. I myself have invoked this pattern of thought in arguing that Lévi-Strauss’s version of the Oedipus myth betrays his Oedipus complex in relation to Freud. Plainly, Freudian criticism with these sorts of preoccupations is widespread, continues sometimes to appear, and cannot simply be discounted as an influence upon the theory of literature.

但正如我所说，布鲁克斯作品的奇特之处（或许也不算奇特）在于，尽管小说文本并非旨在向我们揭示作者、人物或我们自身隐秘的自我，但它本身却仿佛拥有作者或人物般的生命。情节的展开是为了表达某种欲望，确切地说是某种特定的欲望，但这并非作者的欲望，而是一种普遍存在于无意识中的欲望，它在情节的运作机制中得以展现。尽管这种欲望脱离了任何个人层面，布鲁克斯确实表示他心中怀有某种特定的欲望。我们不妨谨慎地称之为一种普遍的欲望。文本结构的功能在于满足这种欲望，即弗洛伊德在其分析著作中经常提到的“减少兴奋”：这种欲望在性方面可以与快乐原则相关联，或者与弗洛伊德在《超越快乐原则》中探讨的死亡愿望相关联，在这种愿望中，减少兴奋意味着以正确的方式实现死亡或终结。通过这两种渴望减少兴奋的形式（只有经历过兴奋才能实现——这两种形式能否共存，以及在多大程度上能否共存，还有待观察）——布鲁克斯诠释了情节“中间”所安排的延迟、曲折和结局的推迟。

But as I’ve said, the odd thing in Brooks’s work, or maybe not so odd, is that although the novelistic text is not there to tell us something about its author or its characters or our own secret selves, it seems in itself nevertheless to be alive like an author or a character. A plot unfolds to articulate desire, indeed some particular desire, yet it’s not the author’s desire, it’s a form of desire, broadly characteristic of the unconscious, that plays itself out in the mechanics of plot. Despite this abstraction from any individual profile, Brooks does say that he has a certain desire in mind. Let us hesitantly call it a universal desire. The function of the text’s structure is to fulfill this desire for what Freud in his analytic work frequently calls reduced excitation: this desire can be associated sexually with the pleasure principle or otherwise with the death wish that Freud explores in Beyond the Pleasure Principle, where the reduction of excitation would consist in achieving death, or closure, in the right way. Through these two forms of desiring reduced excitation that can only be achieved in having passed through excitation—and it remains to see whether, or to what extent, these two forms can coexist—Brooks interprets the delay, the arabesque, the postponement of the end that the “middle” of a plot orchestrates.

显然，无论是梦境还是故事，都不会直接满足这种欲望；它们还会通过维持引发欲望的兴奋感来延缓欲望的实现。我相信我们都曾有过这样的经历：醒来后感觉自己整晚都困在同一个梦境循环中，通常正处于某个重要事件即将发生的临界点。我们的许多梦境既不令人愉悦也不令人恐惧，反而像在跑步机上一样单调乏味，尽管某种兴奋似乎潜伏在梦境的边缘。小说优于梦境的原因或许在于，它的艺术性和结构性能够将这种延缓延长到令人愉悦的程度，但又不会过度延长。

Obviously, then, neither dreams nor stories simply blurt out the fulfillment of this desire; they also delay it by sustaining the excitation that prompts the desire. I’m sure we have all had the experience of waking up and thinking that we have been stuck in the same dream loop all night long, typically on the threshold of some signal event. Many of our dreams are neither pleasurable nor frightening but exhibit the tedium of a treadmill, even though some sort of excitement seems to lurk around the edge of them as a possibility. The superiority of fiction to the dream work may be that its art, its structure, protracts delay to a pleasurable degree but not unduly beyond that degree.

小说的中段不仅运用了诸如重复之类的拖延技巧，而且还有一种奇特的倾向，那就是反复提及令人不快的情节。没错，我们爱读的小说都“引人入胜”，但这并不意味着我们从中获得任何传统意义上的“乐趣”。混乱、灾难和悲伤潜伏在每一个角落，即使是喜剧小说也不例外。这一切都明显令人不快。我必须承认，近年来，我对小说的这种阅读方式越来越反感——它甚至影响了我观看电影的能力——以至于我对曾经如饥似渴的犯罪小说也失去了兴趣。但大多数读者，以及大多数情节的情感策略，并不会遇到我这样的问题。大多数读者都在进行一种心理上的平衡游戏。他们一边急切地翻页，一边又对坏消息感到畏缩。

Not only do the middles of fiction involve these techniques of delay, such as repetition, they also have a curious tendency to revisit unpleasurable things. Yes, everything we love to read is a “page turner,” but that doesn’t mean we’re having “fun” in any conventional sense. Mayhem, catastrophe, and grief lurk around every corner, even in comic fiction. It’s all distinctly unpleasurable. I should admit that this aspect of reading fiction has grown on me so much in recent years—it affects my ability to watch film even more—that I am losing my taste even for crime fiction, which in former days I read constantly. But most readers, and the affective strategies of most plots, just don’t have my problem. Most readers engage in a psychological balancing act. They wince away from the bad news even as they eagerly turn the page.

小说情节反复提及人生苦痛的原因之一，尤其是在布鲁克斯特别感兴趣的十九世纪现实主义经典作品中，在于人物总是执迷不悟地做出错误的选择。他们爱上不该爱的人，深陷困境无法自拔，原因可能是他们不够成熟，考虑不周，或者——就像哈代笔下那样——命运的阴影笼罩着他们，使他们无法做出更好的选择。无论如何，即使是最伟大、最激动人心的小说，其中段情节也往往充满痛苦。这又与驱动欲望的快乐原则有何关联呢？

One reason why plots revisit the agonies of life, especially in the monuments of nineteenth-century realism that particularly interest Brooks, is that the characters keep compulsively making bad object choices. They fall in love with the wrong person. They’re mired in sticky situations that they can’t get out of because they’re not mature enough, they haven’t thought things through, or because—as in Hardy—fate looms over the possibility of making a better choice. However the case may be, the experiences that flesh out the middles even of the greatest and the most exciting fiction do have a tendency to be unpleasurable. What can this possibly have to do with the pleasure principle that presumably fuels desire?

这正是弗洛伊德在布鲁克斯的论证文本《超越快乐原则》（1919）中提出的问题。该文本以对创伤受害者的探讨开篇。弗洛伊德的这本小册子写于第一次世界大战末期，他对创伤受害者的关注也为欧洲其他作家所共有。几乎与《超越快乐原则》同时期，英国也出现了一些小说，反映了机构心理学家对创伤受害者的研究成果。弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在《达洛维夫人》中将有自杀倾向的退伍军人塞普蒂默斯·史密斯塑造成一位遭受创伤的战争受害者；丽贝卡·韦斯特则创作了小说《士兵归来》，小说的主人公在失去记忆后回到了自己的庄园。弗洛伊德的《超越快乐原则》也呼应了这一战后主题。布鲁克斯喜欢将《超越快乐原则》的文本本身称为一个具有虚构氛围的“主线剧情”。或许这里暗示了德里达对文学与其他体裁之间关系的解构——正如《精神现象学》和《资本论》被誉为伟大的文化小说——但这并非布鲁克斯的主要论点。他从弗洛伊德的小册子中发现了一种与他所设想的情节结构特殊的关联，同时也找到了对这些结构的解释。它既是结构内部的核心，又是结构外部的核心。

That’s the question that Freud asked himself in Brooks’s proof text, Beyond the Pleasure Principle (1919), a text that begins with a consideration of trauma victims. Freud’s pamphlet was written at the end of the First World War, and its concern for trauma victims was shared by other writers in Europe. Almost contemporary with Beyond the Pleasure Principle, there are novels written in England that reflect the findings of institutional psychologists about trauma victims. Virginia Woolf treats the suicidal returned soldier Septimus Smith in Mrs. Dalloway as a traumatized war victim, and Rebecca West wrote a novel called The Return of the Soldier, the protagonist of which returns to his estate having lost his memory. Freud’s Beyond the Pleasure Principle contributes to this postwar theme. Brooks likes to refer to the text of Beyond the Pleasure Principle as itself a “master plot” with a fictive ambiance. Perhaps Derrida’s breakdown of the relation between literature and other genres is implied here—just as The Phenomenology of Mind and Capital have been called great novels of culture—but that is not Brooks’s main point. He finds in Freud’s pamphlet a special relation to the plot structures he has in mind and at the same time an explanation for those structures. It is a center that is both inside and outside of its structure.

弗洛伊德开篇便指出，他显然尚未意识到自己的最终结论，他注意到，他治疗过的创伤患者在讲述梦境或表现出神经质的重复行为（比如反复把烟灰缸放回某个特定位置）时，似乎会不由自主地重复最初导致他们前来就诊的创伤事件。他们并不回避，也并非严格意义上的压抑，而是不断地重温，但通常会以某种转喻的方式转移事件本身。因此，问题来了——一个令人不安的问题，它挑战了精神分析此前的基石——这种行为怎么可能与弗洛伊德一直认为的由快乐原则驱动的“愿望满足”相符呢？弗洛伊德之前的假设中隐含着我们现在所说的社会生物学前提，即生命的延续是为了确保性繁殖；性欲的转移或抑制——姑且称之为生命本能——在自我层面表现为渴望成功、自我提升、情感和智力成熟。所有这些都与快乐原则相关。但是，重返创伤事件的冲动又如何与快乐原则的运作机制相符呢？

Freud begins, quite obviously without yet knowing what his end will be, by remarking that the trauma victims he has treated seem, when recounting their dreams or exhibiting neurotically repetitive behavior (you know, returning the ash tray to some precise spot again and again), compulsively to repeat the traumatic event that brought them to him in the first place. They don’t shy away from it. They don’t in any strict sense repress it but keep circling back, ordinarily however displacing the event itself in some metonymic way. So the question was—a disturbing question that challenged what had hitherto been a cornerstone of psychoanalysis—how could such behavior possibly accord with the “wish fulfillment,” driven by the pleasure principle, that Freud had always considered the sole motivating force of the unconscious? Implicit in Freud’s previous assumption was what we would now call the sociobiological premise that the protraction of life is meant to ensure sexual reproduction; and that the displacement or inhibition of the sex drive—call it the life-instinct—takes the form in the ego of the desire to succeed, to improve oneself, to mature emotionally and intellectually. All of this we can associate with the pleasure principle. But how does the compulsion to return to a traumatic event in any way correspond to the workings of the pleasure principle?

然后他想起自己家里的一个例子：他刚出生不久的孙子小汉斯站在婴儿床里，把系着线轴的绳子扔出床外，喊着“ Fort！ ”，意思是“走开，别在这儿”，然后又把线轴拉回来，喊着“ Da！ ”，意思是“又回来了”：“ Fort！Da！ ”小汉斯到底为什么要这么做呢？弗洛伊德很快就明白，小汉斯是在表达他对母亲总是离开房间的沮丧。他玩这个游戏的成就感在于，他找到了用绳子拴住母亲的方法。没错，母亲会离开——我必须明白这一点：我知道母亲会离开——但你猜怎么着？我可以把她拉回来，她又回来了。正如弗洛伊德所说，布鲁克斯也赞同他的观点，这就是我们通过重复创伤事件而获得的“掌控感”。然而，这绝不仅仅是掌握了某种技巧那么简单，因为重返创伤之地显然只是其中的一半。仿佛那本身也是一种乐趣。

Then he remembers an example from his own home life: his infant grandson, little Hans, standing in his crib throwing a spool tied to a string out of the crib saying, “Fort!,” meaning “away, not here,” then reeling it back in and saying, “Da!,” meaning “here it is again”: “Fort! Da!” Why on earth is little Hans doing this? Well, Freud pretty quickly figures out that little Hans is expressing his frustration about the way his mother keeps leaving the room. The accomplishment of his game, then, is that he’s figured out how to keep her on a string. Sure, she goes away—I have to understand this: I know my mother goes away—but guess what? I can reel her back in and there she is again. This is the “mastery” of a traumatic event, as Freud puts it and as Brooks follows him in arguing, that we can acquire through the repetition of the event. Yet it can’t just be the achievement of mastery alone that’s involved, because the return to the trauma is so clearly only half the point. It is almost as though that, too, were a pleasure.

如果我们将其视为一种掌控的努力，那么弗洛伊德认为，这种强迫性重复的行为表现为通过预先演练来掌控死亡的必然性。生命中的创伤事件，以及那些死里逃生的经历，都预示着即将到来的死亡创伤。弗洛伊德提到，这类患者经常遭遇火车事故。他最终将这种强迫性重复视为对一个本身无法叙述的事件——至少对我们自己而言——的预先重复：那就是最终迫在眉睫的死亡事件。

If we think of it as an effort of mastery, the compulsion to repeat takes the form, Freud argues, of mastering in advance through rehearsal, as it were, the inevitability of death. The trauma of death that awaits has been heralded by the traumatic events in one’s life, the near escapes. Freud mentions the frequency of train accidents in such patients’ cases. He comes to see the compulsion to repeat as a repeating forward of an event that is itself unnarratable, at least to ourselves: the event of death, which ultimately looms.

但弗洛伊德开始思考，既然一切似乎都指向生长、繁衍和生存的意志，那么一个生物体为何会表现出这种行为呢？为何会对死亡如此渴望？他注意到（顺便一提，这一发现颇具争议，但却有助于他的论证），某些生物体，甚至包括分子生物体，其行为中都存在一种回归更简单、更早期的有机存在状态的倾向，回归到我们出现之前的状态。换句话说，我一直暗示的起始与终结之间的关系，正是死亡的共同特征。作为生物体，我们始于无生命，终于无生命，因此我们内心必然存在着回归本源的渴望。“一切生命的最终目的，”弗洛伊德接着说道，“就是死亡。”

But then Freud starts to wonder how it could be that a living organism would behave this way, when everything seems to point toward the will to grow, reproduce, and stay alive. Why this almost eager anticipation of death? He notices (controversially, by the way, but it helps his argument along) that in the behavior of certain organisms, even molecular ones, there’s an inclination to return to a simpler and earlier state of organic existence, to that which existed prior to our emergence into life. The relationship between the beginning and the end that I have been intimating, in other words, is the common denominator of death. As organisms we begin inanimate and end inanimate, hence there must be in us a desire to return to the beginning. “The aim of all life,” Freud then says, “is death.”

现在我们应该让布鲁克斯对这一非同寻常的断言（1166）发表评论，以便我们能够更接近将这些想法应用于虚构情节的结构：

We should now allow Brooks to comment on that extraordinary assertion (1166) so that we can move closer to an application of these ideas to the structure of a fictional plot:

目前，我们需要跟随弗洛伊德的脚步，更深入地探究重复强迫与本能之间的关系。答案在于“本能，或许也在于整个有机生命体的一个普遍属性”，即“本能是有机生命体固有的一种冲动，它促使人们恢复到先前的状态” 。
We need at present to follow Freud into his closer inquiry concerning the relation between the compulsion to repeat and the instinctual. The answer lies in “a universal attribute of instinct and perhaps of organic life in general,” that “an instinct is an urge inherent in organic life to restore an earlier state of things.”

基于此观点，布鲁克斯继续说道（1169）：“这种本能功能关乎所有生命体最普遍的努力——即回归无机世界的宁静。”仿佛终于迎来了“和平”——而弗洛伊德的推测之路上的一个障碍，便是挥之不去的疑问：死亡愿望本身是否也带来愉悦，甚至可能是一种受虐倾向。它仍然与快乐原则不同，因为其根本动机并非为了维持生命，但困扰弗洛伊德的那种矛盾感会因此有所减轻。

Building on this idea, Brooks continues (1169): “This function [of the drives] is concerned with the most universal endeavor of all living substance—namely, to return to the quiescence of the inorganic world.” “Peace at last,” as it were—and indeed one bump on the road of Freud’s speculation is the nagging question whether the death wish is not itself pleasurable, possibly a kind of masochism. It still wouldn’t be the same as the pleasure principle because its underlying motive wouldn’t be life-sustaining, but the sense of contradiction that so troubles Freud would be somewhat lessened.

但还有更多，这也是小说篇幅较长的原因：不长也不短——正如亚里士多德所说，篇幅要适中。还有更多，因为有机体并非只想尽快死去。有机体并非有自杀倾向。这或许是我们最初试图理解弗洛伊德所说的“死亡愿望”时所犯的错误。有机体更希望按照自己的意愿死去，在合适的时间以合适的方式死去，因此它拥有一套复杂的防御机制——弗洛伊德总是称之为“外层皮层”——试图抵御创伤的可能性，并将其与创伤隔离开来。创伤受害者会责怪自己不够警惕，未能抵御打击。强迫性重复行为所寻求的掌控感，正是建立起防御机制以防止创伤再次发生。

But there’s more, and this is why novels are long: not too long, but not too short—of a certain magnitude, as Aristotle said. There is more because the organism doesn’t just want to die as soon as possible. The organism is not suicidal. That’s the mistake we probably make when we first try to understand what Freud means by “the death wish.” The organism wants rather to die on its own terms, at the right time and in the right way, which is why it has an elaborate mechanism of defenses—“the outer cortex,” as Freud is always calling it—that attempt to withstand and to keep at arm’s length the possibility of trauma. Trauma victims blame themselves for not having been vigilant enough to ward off the blow. The mastery hoped for in the compulsion to repeat is the building up of defenses to prevent its recurrence.

所以，有机体只想按照自己的意愿死去。如果你想起蒂尼亚诺夫（Tynianov）在文学史中区分进化与修正的那段论述，我认为这种类比是恰当的。弗洛伊德笔下的有机体想要的是朝着自身消亡的方向进化，而不是被修正：它不想受到任何外在创伤或内在疾病的干扰。它想要拥有丰富而充实的生命，达到一定的规模，但最终目的是为了实现其渴望的终极目标，即按照自己的意愿回归到无机状态。如果一个故事被修正，那么它就不会有情节，或者情节不足。故事或许会有一个开头，但随后会突然戛然而止，阻止情节的展开，使其无法发展到合适的结局。

So the organism only wishes to die on its own terms. If you are reminded here of the passage by Tynianov in which he makes the distinction between evolution and modification in literary history, I think the parallel would be legitimate. What the organism in Freud wants to do is evolve toward its dissolution, not to be modified: not to be interfered with by anything from external trauma to internal disease. It wants to live a rich and full life, of a certain magnitude, but with a view to achieving the ultimate desired end, which is to return to an inorganic state on its own terms. If a story then were modified, there would be no plot, or not enough plot. There might be a beginning, but then you would have a sudden cutting off that prevents the arabesque of the plot from evolving to a proper end.

现在，布鲁克斯按照弗洛伊德的观点认为，随着情节构建过程的推进，快乐原则和死亡愿望相互配合（1166-1167）：

Now what Brooks argues following Freud is that as the emplotting process goes forward, the pleasure principle and the death wish cooperate (1166–1167):

因此，弗洛伊德得以带着某种傲慢提出这样的论断：“一切生命的最终目的都是死亡。 ”他描绘了一幅有机体的进化图景：外部影响所造成的张力迫使生命体“越来越偏离其原本的生命轨迹，并在最终走向死亡之前经历越来越复杂的迂回”。在这种观点看来，自我保护的本能确保有机体遵循其自身的死亡路径，并阻止任何并非有机体自身必然选择的回归无机状态的途径。换言之，“有机体只想以自己的方式死去”。它必须与那些可能通过某种“短路”方式帮助其过快实现死亡的事件（危险）作斗争。
Hence Freud is able to proffer, with a certain bravado, the formulation: “the aim of all life is death.” We are given an evolutionary image of the organism in which the tension created by external influences has forced living substance to “diverge ever more widely from its original course of life and to make ever more complicated détours before reaching its aim of death.” In this view, the self-preservative instincts function to assure that the organism shall follow its own path to death, to ward off any ways of returning to the inorganic which are not imminent to the organism itself. In other words, “the organism wishes to die only in its own fashion.” It must struggle against events (dangers) which would help to achieve its goal too rapidly—by a kind of short-circuit.

布鲁克斯接着说道（1169）：

Brooks then says further along (1169):

我们可以说，重复强迫和死亡本能服务于快乐原则；从更广义的角度来看，快乐原则监视着来自外部，尤其是来自内部的刺激的入侵，寻求释放这些刺激，从而服务于死亡本能，确保有机体能够恢复到静止状态。
[W]e could say that the repetition compulsion and the death instinct serve the pleasure principle; in a larger sense [though], the pleasure principle, keeping watch on the invasion of stimuli from without and especially from within, seeking their discharge, serves the death instinct, making sure that the organism is permitted to return to quiescence.

这样一来，这些看似矛盾的驱动力便能共存，并在某种程度上相互合作，从而发展出美好的生活和精彩的情节。

In this way, these apparently conflicting drives coexist and in some measure cooperate to develop the good life and the good plot.

正如我之前暗示的，对这一理论的一个致命质疑（弗洛伊德也承认这一点）在于，在我们称之为“人类”的运作系统中，将死亡和性完全区分开来极其困难。降低兴奋显然是快乐原则的核心。性的目的在于降低兴奋，消除欲望。弗洛伊德在1919年指出，死亡的目的也在于此。那么，我们如何区分二者呢？文学史中有大量篇章强调二者之间的密切联系。我们都知道早期现代情色诗歌中“死亡”的含义。我们都知道《特里斯坦与伊索尔德》中的“爱之死”，以及文学作品中其他充满性意味的死亡场景。文学作品中对二者的混淆显而易见且心照不宣——弗洛伊德总是说诗人先于他——这构成了一个难题。正如我之前所说，一种相反的观点是，重复痛苦经历、重温创伤的强迫行为可能是一种受虐倾向，毕竟它能带来愉悦感，从而无需建立死亡本能理论。弗洛伊德承认，区分这两种倾向很困难，但他认为他掌握的临床证据足以支持这种区分。他认为，受虐倾向的病因在于俄狄浦斯期的异常发展，而死亡本能作为一种重复的强迫行为，是为了抵御创伤的任意威胁，从而确保一个独立的结局。

As I’ve intimated already, an imperiling objection to this theory, one that Freud acknowledges, is that it’s awfully hard to keep death and sex separate in the functioning system we call human. The reduction of excitation is obviously what the pleasure principle is all about. The purpose of sex is to reduce excitation, to annul desire. The purpose of death, Freud finds himself saying in 1919, is to do the same thing. So how can we tell one from the other? There’s a rich vein of literary history that insists on their near connection. We all know what “to die” means in early modern erotic poems. We all know about “Liebestod” in “Tristan and Isolde,” with other moments of death in literature that are sexually charged. There is a manifest and knowing confusion of the two in literature—Freud always says that the poets preceded him in everything—that poses a problem. One countervailing thought, as I’ve said, would be that the compulsion to repeat nasty episodes, to revisit trauma, might be a form of masochism, pleasurable after all and obviating the need for a theory of the death drive. Freud admits that it’s hard to make the distinction, though he thinks he has clinical evidence that warrants it. Masochism, he would say, has its etiology in unusual developments at the Oedipal stage, whereas the death instinct, as a compulsion to repeat, builds up defenses against the arbitrary threat of trauma in order to secure an independent ending.

那么，让我们转向布鲁克斯（此处沿用拉康和小说理论家D.A.米勒的观点）笔下的小说情节：欲望以“可叙述之物”的形式出现或开始，它蕴含着情节的种子。那么，不可叙述之物又是什么呢？不可叙述之物是对生活的持续沉浸——拉康称之为“实在”，齐泽克称之为“污点”——它阻碍了秩序感或结构感的形成。如果我们没有开头、中间和结尾的概念来为其提供语境，那么任何事物都是不可叙述的。换句话说，可叙述之物必须能够融入某种结构。因此，萨特在《恶心》中对罗肯坦的沉思，以及布鲁克斯对此的引用（参见1163页），都指向可叙述的开端——可叙述之物始于进入某种欲望模式的瞬间，而这种模式可以启动情节。

Turning, then, to the plot of fiction according to Brooks (here following Lacan and the theorist of fiction, D. A. Miller): desire emerges or begins as the “narratable,” that which contains within it the seeds of a plot. What then might the unnarratable be? The unnarratable is the ongoing immersion in life—Lacan calls it “the real,” Zižek calls it “the blot”—that prevents a sense of order or structure. Anything is unnarratable if we don’t have a sense of a beginning, a middle, and an end to provide it as a context. The narratable, in other words, must lend itself to a structure. So the narratable beginning, which is meditated on by Sartre’s Roquentin in La Nausée and quoted to that effect by Brooks (cf. 1163)—the narratable begins in a moment of entry into a pattern of desire that can launch a plot.

当叙事内容演变为情节时，这种欲望的身份便通过隐喻显现出来，隐喻统一或“束缚”着情节，并支配着其各部分的连贯性。叙事理论几乎总是欣然指出，在小说中不存在无关紧要的细节。我们被告知，一切事物的存在都不是偶然的。这种关于细节不可或缺的正确性的感觉（当新批评最终将“细读”从诗歌引入小说领域时，马克·肖勒、鲁本·布劳尔和大卫·洛奇等人的著作便成为一种重要的阐释重点）被布鲁克斯视为在创作过程中施加于情节构建的隐喻压力。一切都围绕着一个动机而安排，即推动情节发展的潜在欲望。

When the narratable becomes a plot, the identity of this desire emerges through metaphor, which unifies or “binds” the plot and governs the coherence of its parts. Narrative theory nearly always remarks with satisfaction that there’s no such thing in fiction as irrelevant detail. Nothing, we are told, is there by accident. This feeling about the inescapable rightness of detail (a prominent interpretive emphasis when the New Criticism eventually imported “close reading” from poetry to fiction in books by Mark Schorer, Reuben Brower, and David Lodge) is represented by Brooks as the metaphoric pressure brought to bear on plotting in the course of composition. Everything is arranged with a motive, namely, the underlying desire that’s driving the plot forward.

然而，在某种程度上，与此相反，转喻发挥着延迟、迂回、繁复、拒绝结束的作用：做出糟糕的对象选择和其他不幸的结果，不愉快的事情再次出现，所有这些都发生在文学情节中“中间部分”的漫无目的的游荡之中。这并非意味着这些元素不连贯，与隐喻相悖；毕竟，情节将素材结合在一起，而隐喻和转喻可以说都是结合的形式。布鲁克斯说（1166）：“因此，谈论文学文本中的‘结合’，就是谈论任何形式化（这些形式化，就像结合一样，可能是痛苦的、阻碍性的），它们迫使我们在差异中认识到同一性，或者说，从故事素材中涌现出一个故事（sjužet）。”

To some extent by contrast, however, metonymy functions as the principle of delay, the detour, the arabesque, the refusal of closure: making bad object choices and other unfortunate outcomes, the return of the unpleasurable, all the things that happen in the excursive wandering of “middles” in literary plots. It’s not that these elements are incoherent, at odds with metaphorization; the plot, after all, binds material together, and both metaphor and metonymy are arguably forms of binding. Brooks says (1166): “To speak of “binding” in a literary text is thus to speak of any of the formalizations (which, like binding, may be painful, retarding) that force us to recognize sameness within difference, or the very emergence of a sjužet from the material of fabula.”

现在我想请托尼（你们想念他了吗？）来演示如何进行情节阅读。不过，我首先要说明的是，本次讲座的阅读材料选择不仅是为了探讨精神分析与文学及文学理论的关系，也是为了向你们这些喜爱小说的读者们介绍一些你们可能希望我们多了解的内容：叙事理论或“叙事学”。我建议你们阅读布鲁克斯节选的开头几页，他在那里回顾了一些叙事理论中最重要的著作，这些著作我在讨论结构主义时也提到过。罗兰·巴特、茨维坦·托多罗夫和热拉尔·热奈特是布鲁克斯在这一传统中重点提及的人物。

Now I want to turn to Tony (have you missed him?) to show how reading for the plot can take place. I should mention first, though, that the choice of reading matter for this lecture is not just a way into questions of psychoanalysis as they bear on literature and literary theory, but also a gesture toward something that those of you whose favorite reading is novels may wish we had a little more of: narrative theory or “narratology.” I refer you to the opening pages of the Brooks excerpt, where he passes in review some of the most important work in narrative theory, work that I mentioned when discussing structuralism. Roland Barthes, Tzvetan Todorov, and Gérard Genette are the figures Brooks singles out within that tradition.

总之，说说托尼拖车吧。在《超越快乐原则》的语境下，我们可以把这个故事重新命名为《通往成熟的坎坷之路》。它确实具备流浪汉小说的特质。故事发生在路上。情节的线性发展，事件的呈现方式如同流浪汉小说中常见的串珠一般（塞万提斯将堂吉诃德遇到的劳改队成员比作串珠），都赋予了叙事一种流浪汉小说的感觉。让我们快速地重读一遍，这次以散文的形式，而不是按行阅读：

Anyway, Tony the Tow Truck. In the context of Beyond the Pleasure Principle, we could retitle this story The Bumpy Road to Maturity. It certainly has the qualities of a picaresque fiction. It’s on the road. The linearity of its plot, its events laid out metonymically like beads on a string as in picaresque (Cervantes compares the members of a chain gang Quixote encounters to beads on a string), lends the feeling of picaresque to the narrative. Let’s quickly reread it, this time as prose, not broken up by line:

我是拖车托尼，住在黄色的小车库里。我专门帮助陷在泥里的车，把它们拖回我的车库。我喜欢我的工作。有一天，我陷住了。谁来帮帮我，拖车托尼呢？“我帮不了你，”尼托说，“我不想弄脏自己。”“我帮不了你，”斯皮迪说，“我太忙了。”我很难过。这时，一辆小车开了过来。是我的朋友，邦比。邦比推了我一把。他推啊 ... 【总之，这是故事的一部分，然后：】“谢谢你，邦比，”我回应道。“不客气，”邦比说。这才叫朋友。
I am Tony the Tow Truck. I live in a little yellow garage. I help cars that are stuck. I tow them to my garage. I like my job. One day I am stuck. Who will help Tony the Tow Truck? “I cannot help you,” says Neato the Car. “I don’t want to get dirty.” “I cannot help you,” says Speedy the Car. “I am too busy.” I am very sad. Then a little car pulls up. It is my friend, Bumpy. Bumpy gives me a push. He pushes and pushes [by the way, this text, I think, is very close to its surface a kind of anal-phase parable. In that parable, the hero is not Tony in fact but a character with whom you are familiar if you’re familiar with South Park, and that character is, of course, the one who says, “He pushes and pushes”] and I am on my way.” [In any case, that is part of the narrative, and then:] “Thank you, Bumpy,” I call back. “You’re welcome,” says Bumpy. Now that’s what I call a friend.

我说过，这个故事的情节带有流浪汉小说的风格。它线性的重复结构就像一道屏障，将开头和结尾拉开距离。过去，我们曾将这种特点称为布鲁克斯也提到的民间故事的三段式结构；但它也通过拉长开头和结尾之间的中间部分，来强调开头和结尾之间的关系。托尼来自一家黄色小修车厂，我们不禁会想——尽管这或许是无法叙述的部分——他是否会回到那里。我们知道他“正在路上”，但我们不知道他是要回到那家黄色小修车厂，还是——正如他“被困”在路上，车子抛锚了——要去废车场。

I’ve said that this plot is picaresque. Its linear repetitions are the delay that pries apart an origin and an end. In the past, we’ve spoken of this feature as the triadic form of the folk tale that Brooks also mentions; but it is also, in its dilation of the middle between the beginning and end, a way of putting pressure on the relation between beginning and end. Tony comes from a little yellow garage, and we can’t help wondering—though this may be part of the unnarratable—whether he is going back there. We know he’s “on his way,” but we don’t know whether he’s on his way back to the little yellow garage or whether—as being “stuck,” having broken down, would suggest—he’s on his way to the junkyard.

无论结果如何——是那间黄色小车库还是那片废品场——他都会按照自己的方式到达目的地，但不会像故事开头那样，以“我”开头，成为一个自恋的自我中心者。因为仅仅做一个独立自主的英雄是不够的。（顺便一提，弗洛伊德认为，白日梦的弊端就在于扮演超级英雄。）在你的旅程中，就像民间传说中那样，你需要一个帮手。小说的魅力之一就在于引入一个辅助英雄。与另一个像帮手一样的人进行建设性的交流，可以防止自恋的滋生，即使是像托尼这样善良的人，在故事开头也会表现出“我”、“我”、“我”的自恋倾向。最终，“我”只会在句子中出现，成为众多身份中的一员，而不是像卡车一样驱动故事的开篇自我。

In either case, no matter which the outcome—little yellow garage or junkyard—he’s going to get there on his own terms, but not as a me-first narcissist who begins every sentence in the first part of the story with the word “I,” because it’s not enough just to be an autonomous hero. (Freud says, by the way, that being a superhero is what’s unhealthy about daydreams.) On your journey, as in folklore, you need a helper. Part of the arabesque of fiction is its introduction of an ancillary hero. Constructively encountering another mind like the helper’s prevents the narcissism, even in a nice guy like Tony, that is manifest in the “I,” “I,” “I” at the beginning of the story. Eventually the “I” appears only when embedded in a line, an identity among others rather than an inaugural ego that drives the story like a truck.

故事的精妙之处在于它展现了人们如何面对并摒弃错误的选择：整洁、忙碌——顺便一提，这些选择本身就充满诱惑。我们都渴望整洁和忙碌，不是吗？但这个故事想要倡导的，作为人生——作为真正活到终点的人生——的相互尊重，并非整洁和忙碌的属性。故事的结局源于一个成熟的选择，它温和地推动着情节向前发展，但我们并不完全清楚它指向何方。不过，我们只能假设，它推动着我们走向一种状态：那间黄色的小车库和那座难以启齿的废品场（并非不可叙述）融为一体。

The arabesque of the plot is a matter of encountering bad object choices and rejecting them: neatness, busyness—choices which, by the way, offer temptations. We all want to be neat and busy, don’t we? But the mutuality of regard that this story wants to recommend as life—as life properly lived to its end—is not an attribute of neatness and busyness. Closure comes with a mature object choice that’s a gentle push forward of the plot, but we don’t quite know toward what. We have to assume, though, that it’s a push toward a state in which the little yellow garage and the unmentionable junkyard (it’s not unnarratable) are one and the same thing.

我们已经指出了许多转喻的要素，但其中有一个在主题层面发挥作用。这是一个关于汽车和其他机械物体的故事。有些会动，有些是静止的——还记得背景中那些皱着眉头和面带微笑的房子吗？——但它们都是机械物体，并非有机物。这是一个被转喻地视为缺乏有机性的世界，它仅仅与它所灌输的人类价值观相连。然而与此同时，这个故事在主题上也具有隐喻意义，它强调了我们所有人共同的人性：“这就是我所说的朋友。”许多动物故事以及类似的故事——例如它的原型《小火车头的故事》 ——其目的都是为了使世界人性化，使整个世界对孩子来说友好而充满吸引力。从隐喻的角度来看，托尼不是一辆拖车，而是一个人，他通过意识到自己需要朋友而认识到自己的人性，而尼托和斯皮迪却未能做到这一点，所以他们仍然是汽车。故事的统一性，与其通过机械论进行的转喻式移位形成对比，在于机械论最终的人性化，以及我们在阅读故事时感受到的并非与机械为伴，而是与人为的陪伴。尼特和斯皮迪继续前行，托尼依然在那里，邦比则在他身后默默守护。托尼从车库门走出，来到这个世界，他经历了耽搁、绕路，最终才抵达终点。

We’ve pointed out many elements of metonymy, but there’s one that functions at the level of theme. This is a story about cars and other mechanical objects. Some move and some are stationary—remember the frowning and smiling houses in the background— but they’re all mechanical objects. They’re not organic. This is a world viewed metonymically as that which lacks organicity, which is only contiguous to the human values it inculcates. Yet at the same time the story is thematically metaphoric, asserting the common humanity of us all: “That’s what I call a friend.” The whole point of so many animal stories and other stories like this one—its prototype The Little Engine That Could, for example—is to humanize the world, to make the whole world friendly and inviting to a child. Metaphorically, Tony is not a tow truck but a human being, and he realizes his humanity in recognizing the need for a friend, something Neato and Speedy fail to do, so they remain cars. The unity of the story, in contrast with its metonymic displacements through the mechanistic, is the triumphant humanization of the mechanistic and the fact that as we read the story, we feel that we are not in mechanical company but in human company. Neat and Speedy move on, Tony is still there, and Bumpy has his back. Having emerged from his garage door into the world, Tony is delayed, detoured, then pulls ahead to the end.

接下来，我们将着手处理理解拉康这项艰巨的任务。

Next we turn to the formidable task of understanding Lacan.

 

 

第十三章

CHAPTER 13

雅克·拉康理论
Jacques Lacan in Theory

阅读：

Reading:

拉康，雅克。“无意识中的文字能动性。”载《批判传统》，第 1129-1148 页。

Lacan, Jacques. “The Agency of the Letter in the Unconscious.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1129–1148.

我们之前评述的彼得·布鲁克斯的作品与拉康的这篇论文《无意识中的文字能动性》之间存在着显而易见的联系，我想首先强调这一点。这篇论文涉及拉康论证中你或许在了解结构主义之后最容易理解的部分，并且可能为理解拉康对文学理论的意义提供了最佳途径。

There is an obvious link between the work we reviewed of Peter Brooks and this particular essay of Lacan, “The Agency of the Letter in the Unconscious,” that I’d like to begin by emphasizing. It concerns the part of Lacan’s argument that is probably most accessible to you after your tour through structuralism and offers perhaps the best means of understanding the relevance of Lacan for literary theory.

布鲁克斯将虚构叙事中趋于圆满的“阿拉伯式花纹”视为欲望通过一系列迂回曲折的延续，这些曲折曲折包括冒险尝试和规避不恰当或不合适的终点，从而使欲望得以延续，直至达到一个恰当的结局——这个结局与弗洛伊德提出的有机体渴望以自身的方式而非受外部因素改变或压力而死亡的观点相符。布鲁克斯将叙事情节展开过程中的这一系列迂回曲折称为转喻，此时我们应该意识到，它指的是雅各布森所描述的沿着组合轴排列的符号序列。但布鲁克斯也指出，与此同时，这一系列符号——就情节而言，是一系列事件——之间存在着某种联系。这种联系产生了一种统一的效果，他将这种效果称为“隐喻”。雅各布森所谓的“诗性功能”之类的东西，以某种方式叠加在转喻的组合轴线上，使得统一感，即符号中同一性的反复出现，成为我们铭记于心的印象，并且可以通过诠释加以证实。隐喻甚至在情节的曲折延宕中也保持着整体的统一。当然，在婚姻情节中，这种实现的延迟最为明显，也最容易理解——但情节有很多种，它们都阐述了一种欲望。

Brooks treated the arabesque toward completion in fictional narrative as the sustaining of desire through a series of détours, inadequate or improper endpoints risked and avoided, resulting in a continuation of desire until a proper ending is reached—an ending that corresponds to what Freud posited as the desire of the organism to die in its own way and not according to the modification or pressure of something from without. This sequence of détours in the elaboration of a narrative plot Brooks called metonymy, which by this time we should recognize as what happens in the sequencing of signs along the axis of combination as described by Jakobson. But Brooks remarks also that at the same time there is a binding of this sequence of signs—of events in the case of a plot. There is an effect of unity, and this effect he calls “metaphor.” Something like what Jakobson calls the “poetic function” has been superimposed on the metonymic axis of combination in such a way that the feeling of unity, the sense of the recurrence of identity in the signs used, is an impression we carry away with us but can also confirm exegetically. Metaphor unifies the plot even through the zigs and zags of its delay. The delay of fulfillment is most obvious, of course, in a marriage plot and most immediately intelligible there—but there are many sorts of plot, all of which elaborate a form of desire.

我之所以停下来回顾布鲁克斯的观点，是因为我认为无论你对拉康有何不满，都能看出，同样的根本对比也塑造了拉康对无意识的理解。对拉康而言，实现的延迟——在他看来，这种延迟可能是无限的——也是他思想的核心。与布鲁克斯一样，拉康也追溯了弗洛伊德提出的、并由雅各布森完善的凝缩与隐喻、置换与转喻之间的联系。欲望对象的延迟，以及对拉康而言永远无法实现对某种“他者”（我将在本次讲座中尝试阐明）的欲望，被理解为转喻，正如布鲁克斯再次将转喻的运用理解为一种维持情节发展的迂回或对终点的延迟。

I pause in this way to review Brooks because I think you can see—whatever frustration you may be feeling with Lacan—that the same basic contrast shapes Lacan’s approach to the unconscious. The deferral of fulfillment for Lacan, in his case potentially an endless deferral, is central as well to his thinking. Like Brooks, Lacan harkens back to the connection made by Freud and as it were completed by Jakobson between condensation and metaphor and displacement and metonymy. The deferral of desire’s object, and for Lacan the impossibility of ever realizing one’s desire for a certain kind of “other” that I’m going to be trying to identify during the course of this lecture, is understood as metonymy, just as Brooks, again, understands the movement of metonymy as a plot-sustaining détour or deferral of the end.

另一方面，拉康将隐喻视为他所谓的转喻链的“缝合”，即连接一系列不同能指的“纽扣”，它突然将一系列不同的能指连接在一起，从而实现符号的替代而非置换。稍后，当我们试图理解拉康对维克多·雨果诗作《睡着的波阿斯》中“他的麦捆既不吝啬也不恶毒”这句诗的解读时，我们会再次回到这一点。与此同时，拉康对欲望的解读与布鲁克斯的解读不同，实际上也与任何其他以精神分析术语思考这些结构主义问题的人的解读不同，因为拉康并不相信存在一个合适的结局。他认为我们永远无法得到我们渴望的东西。他毫不怀疑我们可以得到我们所需的东西，而我们自身也需要牢记拥有我们渴望的东西和拥有我们所需的东西之间的这一根本区别。这种区别通常被这样描述——当你阅读斯拉沃热·齐泽克的作品时，你会发现他对此着墨颇多——即“大他者”（big Other）与“小客体”（ objet petit à ）之间的区别。大他者永远无法被占有，因为它始终难以捉摸；而小客体则并非真正的欲望对象，它只是为了满足需求而存在。从社会生物学的角度来看，你可以得到你需要的；而从精神分析的角度来看，你无法得到你渴望的。

Lacan views metaphor, on the other hand, as what he calls at one point “the quilting” of the metonymic chain, the point de capiton or “quilting button” that suddenly holds together a sequence of disparate signifiers in such a way that a substitution of signs rather than a displacement of signs can be accomplished. We’ll come back to this later when attempting to grasp what Lacan says about the line from Victor Hugo’s poem “Boaz Asleep”: “His sheaves were neither miserly nor spiteful.” In the meantime, what makes Lacan’s reading of desire different from Brooks’s, and indeed what makes his reading of desire different from that of anyone else who thinks of these structuralist issues in psychoanalytic terms, is that Lacan really doesn’t believe in a suitable ending. He doesn’t think we can ever have what we desire. He has no doubt that we can have what we need, and for our part we need to keep in mind this fundamental distinction between having what we desire and having what we need. The distinction is often put—and when you read Slavoj Žižek soon you’ll find much made of this—as the distinction between the “big Other,” which one can never appropriate as an object of desire because it is perpetually and always elusive, and the “objet petit à,” the little object at hand, which is not really an object of desire at all but is available to satisfy need. Sociobiologically, you can get what you need. Psychoanalytically, you cannot get what you desire.

这里最明显的典故就是滚石乐队。如果拉康是滚石乐队，他会稍稍改写那句著名的歌词，说：“你永远得不到你想要的，但有时如果你尝试”——而你必须尝试。即使是你真正需要的，你也必须尝试，你不能只是坐在那里——“有时如果你尝试，你就能得到你需要的。”拉康谈到欲望对象的不可实现性，因为欲望的转喻结构遵循他所谓的“渐近线路径”。“渐近线”指的是曲线弯曲，趋向于它想要到达的直线，却永远无法到达，这其中蕴含着隐藏症状的双关含义。唯一能够揭示症状的，是那些缝合的时刻，是缝合点，正如拉康在你的文章中两次提到的，隐喻揭示症状的时刻。这就是你永远无法得到自己想要的东西时会发生的事。我怀疑米克·贾格尔是否真的深入研究过拉康的理论才得出这个重要的结论，但下次当你对欲望和需求之间的区别感到困惑时，你或许应该记住这个概念。

Now the obvious gloss here is the Rolling Stones. If Lacan had been the Rolling Stones, he’d have slightly rewritten the famous refrain by saying, “You can’t ever get what you want, but sometimes if you try”—and you’ve got to try. Even for what you need, you’ve got to try, you can’t just sit there—“Sometimes if you try you’ll get what you need.” Lacan speaks of the impossibility of realizing an object of desire, because the metonymic structure of desire follows what he calls “an asymptotic course,” “asymptotic” meaning the line that curves toward the line it wants to meet but never reaches it, with the punning sense of concealing the symptom. The only thing that can reveal the symptom is those moments of quilting, the moments at the point de capiton when metaphor, as Lacan says on two different occasions in your essay, reveals the symptom. So this is what happens when you can’t ever get what you want. I doubt that Mick Jagger made a close study of Lacan in order to make that important distinction, but it’s still one that you might want to salt away the next time you feel confused about the distinction between desire and need.

如果我们能就此止步就好了，但我们必须更深入地研读文本，并尝试弄清楚，为什么在拉康提出的这些术语——既包括结构主义的术语，也包括精神分析的术语——中，我们迄今为止引入的概念会向如此多的方向延伸——甚至可以说是爆炸式增长。不过，我首先应该顺便提几点。

It’d be great if we could just stop there, but we do have to get a little closer to the text and try to figure out why in these terms given to us by Lacan, terms both structuralist and psychoanalytic, the concepts we’ve introduced thus far ramify—not to say explode—in so many directions. I should first say a couple of things in passing, though.

首先，拉康那种极其晦涩、含糊、并列的风格，令人恼火地将许多事物视为常识，或许会让你想起德里达；而拉康开篇关于徘徊于言语与文字之间的论述，可能暗示我们又回到了德里达对书写与言语之间关系的复杂化探讨，某种程度上来说，的确如此。他们二人都刻意追求晦涩难懂，而且原因也大同小异。他们都认为，规范散文的线性结构和清晰的组织方式与他们的研究目标相悖，而他们的共同目标是展现语言如何以多层次、迷宫般的方式颠覆言语的交际意图。“我喜欢以晦涩的方式切入，”拉康在其文章的开头如是说，而所有读过德里达《结构、符号与游戏》开篇段落的人都知道，他不会反对这种观点。对他们二人而言，开端和起源都值得怀疑，都需要被颠覆。

First, the enormously allusive, diffuse, and appositional style of Lacan, which maddeningly takes so many things for granted as common knowledge, perhaps reminds you of Derrida; and Lacan’s opening gambit about lingering somewhere between what was spoken and what is written may suggest that we’re back with Derrida’s complication of the relation between writing and speech, as in a way we are. Certainly they both cultivated difficulty, and for much the same reason. Both felt that the linearity and clear organization of normative prose were at odds with their projects, which were, in common, the representation of the multilayered and labyrinthine way in which language subverts the communicative ambitions of speech. “I like the way in to be difficult,” intones Lacan near the beginning of his essay, and all you survivors of Derrida’s opening paragraph in “Structure, Sign, and Play” know that he would not disagree. Beginnings and origins are suspect for both and need to be subverted.

然而，这两位法国理论巨匠之间存在着一个重要的区别，我在此只能略作提及。拉康在其《论“失窃的信”》研讨会上论证道，除了杜宾之外，这封信在所有人眼皮底下消失，象征着潜意识对某种症状的隐藏；但最终显露出来的东西，如同信件本身及其内容的含义，却类似于某种真理。德里达对此的回应是一篇题为《真理的传播者》的文章，意指拉康，不出所料，这篇文章解构了爱伦·坡和拉康对真理意义的理解。尽管无法详尽阐述双方的论点，但我们仍能清晰地看到解构主义和结构主义精神分析之间的区别。

Yet there is an important difference between these two titans of French theory, one that I can only touch on here. In his “Seminar on ‘The Purloined Letter,’ ” Lacan had argued that the disappearance of the letter from under the nose of everyone but Dupin corresponds to the concealment of a symptom by the unconscious, but that what stands revealed in the end, like the letter itself and the implications of its contents, is something like a truth. Derrida’s response to this was an essay called “The Purveyor of Truth,” meaning Lacan, which not unsurprisingly deconstructs the conditions of what truth might mean in Poe and Lacan alike. Without doing justice to either argument, we can see clearly here the difference between deconstruction and structuralist psychoanalysis.

对于人文专业的学生来说，雅克·拉康并非只有一种解读。在文学研究领域，我们面前的文本很好地展现了拉康的一面，尽管他的一些重要思想在这里只是略有提及。例如，我们在这里完全没有听到他关于实在界、想象界和象征界的三元区分。仅凭这篇文本，我们无法真正深入探讨这一区分，尽管我们可以谨慎地指出（这一点我们之后还会再次提及），想象界是转喻的，而象征界是隐喻的。在文章的结尾，也只是略微提及了我刚才提出的“大他者”和“小客体”之间的区别。我们将有充足的时间来思考这个问题，因为它是齐泽克文章的核心；但再次强调，对于专注于拉康结构主义遗产的文学研究而言，这篇文本堪称典范。但还有一种或许更贴近当代的拉康，即使在今天，电影研究和女性研究领域的你们当中也有人对此有所了解。这是关于“凝视”的拉康，是关于“凝视”的复杂辩证法，它确实涉及对现实、想象和象征之间区别的探讨。正如我所说，由于我给你们的阅读材料有所选择，我们只能间接地接触到这种拉康。

For students of the humanities, there is more than one Jacques Lacan. There is a Lacan for literary studies who is very well represented by the text we have before us, even though some of his most important ideas are only hinted at here. For example, we hear nothing here about his triadic distinction among the Real, the Imaginary, and the Symbolic. This is something we can’t really explore with only this text before us, although it might be fair to remark cautiously, in a vein that we’ll in fact circle back to, that the imaginary is metonymic and the symbolic is metaphoric. There is only the slightest hint at the very end of the essay of the distinction I have just made between the “big Other” and the “objet petit à.” We’ll have lots of time to think about that because it’s central to the essay of Žižek; but again, for literary studies when focused on the structuralist legacy in Lacan, this is an exemplary selection. But there’s also a perhaps more current Lacan, one better known even now to some of you in film studies and women’s studies. This is the Lacan of “the gaze,” the complicated dialectic of “the gaze,” which does very much involve negotiating the distinctions among the real, the imaginary, and the symbolic. As I say, this Lacan we shall only be able to approach obliquely, owing to the selectivity of what I’ve given you to read.

我还要顺便提一点，希望能解释这篇指定论文颇为奇特的语气。你会注意到，拉康的语气充满了敌意和居高临下，仿佛随时准备挑起争端。在我们阅读的所有自负之人中，他的傲慢无疑是最甚的。我们必须习惯这一点，并逐渐意识到，拉康的居高临下并非主要针对听众和读者的愚昧。更确切地说，他针对的是他认为国际精神分析协会（其中许多成员是所谓的美国自我心理学家）的同僚们对弗洛伊德遗产的歪曲。

The other thing I should say in passing will I hope explain the quite curious tone of the assigned essay. You’ll notice that Lacan is fairly bristling with hostility and condescension, spoiling for a fight. Of all the swelled heads on our list of reading, his is by far the biggest. We just have to get used to it and come to realize that Lacan’s condescension isn’t mainly directed toward the stupidity of his auditors and readers. It’s aimed more particularly at what he takes to be the distortion of Freud’s legacy by his psychoanalytic contemporaries in the International Psychoanalytic Association, many members of which were the so-called American ego psychologists.

自我心理学家如同拉康一样，以弗洛伊德著名的分析程序纲要“Wo es war soll ich sein”（我本该在何处）为出发点。换言之，自我（或称“我”）应从无意识中的本我——“它”、“是”——的原始素材中产生，作为人类意识通过升华力比多驱力而成长成熟的能力。换句话说，根据自我心理学家的观点，本能驱力与人类或成人意识的适当抑制之间的关系可以而且应该是一个渐进的过程；精神分析的目的，即帮助人们超越各种婴儿期阶段或某种神经症的束缚，正是为了巩固和强化自我。拉康讨厌这种想法，因为所宣称的稳定成熟的自我的出现，是以存在稳定的人类主体性为前提的：换句话说，是以存在自主意识为前提的，我们的交流、语言和其他符号系统正是在这种意识的权威下发展起来的。

An ego psychologist is somebody who begins as Lacan does with Freud’s famous agenda for the analytic procedure, “Wo es war soll ich sein”: “Where it was, there I should be.” In other words, out of the raw materials of the id—“it,” “es”—in the unconscious, the ego or ich should arise as the capacity of human consciousness to grow into its maturity through the sublimation of libidinal drives. In other words, the relationship between instinctual drives and the proper inhibitions of human or adult consciousness according to the ego psychologists can and should be a progressive one; and the purpose of psychoanalysis, the purpose of bringing people beyond their entrapment in the various infantile stages or in some form of neurosis, is to shore up the emergence and strengthening of the ego. Lacan hates this idea, because the proclaimed emergence of a stable and mature ego is presupposed by the idea that there is such a thing as stable human subjectivity: in other words, that there is such a thing as autonomous consciousness, under the authority of which our communicative and linguistic and other semiotic systems develop.

拉康对意识持有截然不同的观点。他在这篇文章中最为强烈的敌意（以蔑视的形式表达）源于这样一个问题：我们每个人是否都拥有稳定且（由此推论）独一无二的主体性？拉康在这些问题上的怀疑并非在于我们彼此之间没有差异。我们几乎不可能假定自己就是彼此，或者参与到某种普遍的潜意识思维连续体中（这与荣格的观点有些相似）。事实上，作为伦理学家，我们抱怨的是彼此之间的孤立。但对拉康而言，内在症状与外在语言之间的关系，构成了一个核心谜题，它驳斥了任何关于“我”假定自身与“它”决定我之关系的简单结论。在这篇文章中，你会发现，拉康的论证出现了一种转变，他确实持有一种有限的心理个体化观念，至少将其视为一种可能性：这种个体化绝不能为自主主体性或自由意志的概念提供任何依据，而仅仅因为无意识的符号复杂性，我们每个人都仿佛栖居于这种复杂性的不同形式之中。然而，他却对这样一种观点嗤之以鼻：一个由此产生的“主体”能够通过分析或仅仅通过成熟而获得稳定、连贯、组织良好的自我意识和身份认同。

Lacan takes a completely different view of consciousness. The source of his most intense hostility throughout this essay, expressed as contempt, concerns the question of whether there is for each of us a stable and, by implication, unique subjectivity. The point of Lacan’s skepticism in these matters is not that we don’t differ from each other. We can scarcely suppose ourselves to be each other, or to participate in some universal continuum of subliminal thought (which was something like Jung’s idea). As ethicists we in fact complain of our isolation from each other. But for Lacan the relationship between interior symptomology and the apparent externality of the language that inscribes itself upon it constitutes the central enigma that defeats any facile conclusions about what “I” suppose myself to be in relation to what “it” determines me to be. In this essay you will find, as a kind of turn in his argument, that Lacan does entertain a limited sense of psychic individuation, at least as a possibility: nothing that can by any means authorize notions of autonomous subjectivity or free will, but a sense that, owing simply to the semiotic complexity of the unconscious, each of us, as it were, inhabits a somewhat different form of that complexity. He scoffs, though, at the idea that a “subject” thus brought into being could ever emerge from analysis or simply through maturation with a stable, coherent, well-organized sense of self and identity.

那么，让我们从拉康唯一一项严肃的临床工作——“镜像阶段”的概念——开始谈起。这个概念最初于20世纪30年代提出，是关于婴儿对自身倒影的反应的假设，并在拉康的整个学术生涯中不断抽象化，最终成为心理功能的一个永久性方面。拉康的精神分析哲学很大程度上是思辨性的，而他也非常倾向于这种思辨。他深入研究哲学和文学材料，从不拘泥于分析师的座位。他对他的分析对象缺乏耐心，并且对那些要么是捷径，要么是“没完没了”（正如弗洛伊德在其晚期论文《分析的终结与终结》中所描述的那样）的分析程序抱有异端般的兴趣。但镜像阶段是一个临床概念，它确实衍生出了许多拉康在思辨方向上扩展的思想体系。

Let’s start, then, with the one piece of serious clinical work that Lacan ever did, the concept of the “mirror stage,” first put forward in the 1930s as a hypothesis about infants’ responses to their reflections and abstracted increasingly for the rest of his career into a permanent facet of psychic functioning. Lacan’s psychoanalytic philosophy is largely speculative, as he very much preferred it to be. He worked in depth with philosophical and literary materials and was never glued to the analyst’s chair. He was impatient with his analysands and took a heretical interest in analytic procedures that were either shortcuts, on the one hand, or, on the other hand, “interminable”—as described in Freud’s late essay, “Analysis Terminable and Interminable.” But the mirror stage is a clinical concept, one that actually does generate much of the system of ideas that Lacan expands in speculative directions.

从临床角度来说，镜像阶段是指婴儿不再感受到与母亲乳房的融合，因而开始意识到自我与他者之间的差异，并开始在镜子中观察自己的时刻。在六到十八个月大的时候，婴儿敏锐地意识到自己缺乏对身体的控制和协调能力，然而当他们用双手扶着镜子，勉强支撑起身体直立时，看到的却是一幅完整无缺的画面。自这一现象被首次研究以来，关于婴儿何时以及是否真的能在镜中认出自己的争论一直存在，但这种批评至少忽略了部分要点。对于拉康而言，尤其是在他随后几十年对这一问题的思考中，关键在于婴儿对自身身体的感知与他所凝视的那幅完美挺拔的影像之间那种令人沮丧的对比——尽管这种对比只是隐约暗示。

The mirror stage, clinically speaking, is the moment when a baby who no longer feels at one with the breast of the mother, hence has become aware of some difference between self and otherness, views itself in the mirror. At six to eighteen months, it is acutely aware that it lacks control and coordination in its own body, yet what it sees when it hoists itself up, holding itself erect with its hands on the mirror, is a picture of unfragmented wholeness. There has been controversy from the time this phenomenon was first studied about when and whether infants actually recognize themselves when they look in the mirror, but arguably this criticism misses at least part of the point. For Lacan, especially as he thought about the matter over the ensuing decades, the point of interest was the frustrating contrast, however vaguely intimated, between the infant’s sense of its own body and the gloriously upright image it gazes upon.

或许婴儿会欣喜若狂地认为自己如此英俊（假设它认出了自己），一定是母亲渴望的对象。这或许并非事实，但我们推测，紧随这一欣喜时刻之后发生的事情似乎更为合理。拉康在《无意识中的文字作用》一书中引用的达·芬奇的精彩题词正是关于此的。在想象另一个主体——一个需要谓词的主体——的主体位置时，婴儿便进入了语言的范畴，在那一刻，它不再将自己视为理想的“我”——用弗洛伊德的话来说就是“理想自我”。它意识到，它所目睹的笔直的垂直姿态属于另一个主体；镜中的影像如同能指般矗立在它面前，象征着它所不是的东西。襁褓中的婴儿（婴儿：“因为捆绑你的人不会听懂你的语言，你也不会听懂他们”）逐渐意识到自己甚至没有名字，更遑论身份。它拥有“父亲的名字”，这个能指既指代他者，又指代他者本身，但它没有父亲的阳具，或者说，它并非作为父亲的阳具。它开始意识到欲望中的竞争。然而，父亲，同时也是父亲的名字，这个未被占有的能指，诉说着语言，它仅仅是象征意义上的父亲。在拉康的理论中，欲望的对象可以是任何事物，这取决于欲望所遵循的转喻序列的解构；但归根结底，这个出发点是俄狄浦斯情结，因此，孩子进入承载其命运的语言的入口被称为“父亲的名字”（le nom du père）。

There may be an exultant moment in which the baby thinks it’s so handsome (supposing it to have recognized itself) that it must be the object of the mother’s desire. That may or may not be the case, but what we may suppose to follow upon this exultant moment seems more plausible. The rather wonderful epigraph from Leonardo da Vinci with which Lacan begins “The Agency of the Letter in the Unconscious” is all about this. In imagining the subject position of another—a subject that requires predication—the baby falls into language, and in that moment it no longer sees itself as the ideal I—“das Ideal-Ich” in Freud’s language. It knows that the upright verticality it has witnessed belongs to another; the image in the mirror stands before it as a signifier, as what it is not, and the infant still in swaddling clothes (infans: “ ‘for those who bind you will not understand your language nor will you understand them’ ”) awakens to the recognition that it doesn’t even have its own name, let alone an identity. It has “the name of the father,” the signifier of and as another, but it doesn’t have the phallus of the father, or rather it is not the phallus as the father, and it begins to recognize competition in desire. But the father, which is at the same time the name of the father, the unpossessed signifier bespeaking language, is only symbolically the father. In Lacan the object of desire can be just absolutely anything depending on the unraveling of the metonymic sequence that desire follows; but this point of departure is, after all, the Oedipal phase, so the entry point of the child into the language that harbors his destiny is called le nom du père.

在拉康对弗洛伊德的修正中，欲望的永恒动力源于一种必要的缺失。然而，这种缺失并非物质性的。它并非指阴茎！恰恰相反，它本质上是象征性的，是自我理想（镜中完美的形象），却不再是自身，也永远无法在自我观察中被发现。这种缺失由此呈现出令人眼花缭乱的各种——我们姑且称之为——“以阴茎为中心的”形式。在电影批评领域，你们中的一些人或许读过劳拉·穆尔维的拉康式论文，其中，观众欲望或凝视的女性对象，身着紧身连衣裙，实际上就像那个婴儿，就像任何其他直立的物体。我一直将这种“阴茎”称为垂直轴，并将其描述为虚拟的，我的虚线表明它仅仅存在于假设之中。但就其本身而言，正如拉康所说，它“字面上”是支配精神生活的“字母”，它存在于无意识之中或坚持自身作为无意识中的一种力量。

It is a necessary lack, in Lacan’s revision of Freud, that perpetually motivates desire. Yet this lack is not at all physical. It’s not the penis! It is, on the contrary, something that is by nature symbolic, something that is an ego ideal (that figure of perfection in the mirror) yet no longer oneself and never again to be discoverable in one’s self-observation. This lack henceforth takes a bewildering variety of—let’s just say—“phallogocentric” forms. In film criticism, some of you may know the Lacanian essay by Laura Mulvey in which the female object of the spectator’s desire or gaze, dressed in a sheath dress, is actually just like that baby, just like anything else that’s upright. This “phallus” is what I have been calling the vertical axis and characterizing as virtual, my dotted line suggesting that it only hypothetically exists. Except, that is, insofar as it is itself “literally,” as Lacan puts it, the “letter” that governs the psychic life, seated in or insisting upon itself as an agent in the unconscious.

总之，为了回答一个你记得德里达在《结构、符号与游戏》中非常谨慎地探讨过的问题：语言是如何扮演如此决定性的角色的？语言究竟有什么特质导致了这种无法弥补的问题？拉康在文章开头就对弗洛伊德的无意识做出了一番论断，他声称这番话出自《梦的解析》，弗洛伊德在书中谈到了梦境运作中凝缩与置换之间的关系，我们都知道这一点。拉康说：“无意识的结构就像语言一样。”我认为这是人们从拉康那里得到的唯一概括，因为它是我们理解他思想的基础。

In any case, to address a question that you remember Derrida addressed with great circumspection in “Structure, Sign, and Play”: how is it that language comes to play such a determinate role? What is it about language that introduces this problematic that’s beyond repair? Lacan begins the essay with a declaration about the Freudian unconscious, taken, he claims, from the part of The Interpretation of Dreams where Freud speaks, as we know, of the relationship between condensation and displacement in the dream work. Lacan says, “The unconscious is structured like a language.” That’s the single expression that people take away from Lacan, I think rightly so, because it is foundational for what we need to understand if we’re to get along with him.

“无意识的结构就像一种语言。”顺便一提，他并没有说“无意识就是一种语言”，也没有说他指的是无意识的结构完全像人类语言。更准确地说，他的意思是无意识的结构就像一个符号系统。他还借鉴了弗洛伊德的《梦的解析》，认为梦的运作方式类似于谜语——一种谜题，如果你能弄清楚如何将图画、数字和音节组合起来，就能找到隐藏的句子——换句话说，它是一系列来自不同符号系统的符号，可以被解码成人类语言。“我‘爱’纽约”，“4u，‘鹿’”，等等。

“The unconscious is structured like a language.” He doesn’t say, “The unconscious is a language,” by the way, and he doesn’t say that he means the unconscious is structured exclusively like human language. He means, to put it as precisely as possible, that the unconscious is structured like a semiotic system. He also draws from Freud’s Interpretation of Dreams the idea that the way the dream works resembles a rebus—one of those puzzles in which you can find a hidden sentence if you figure out how to put together drawings, numbers, and syllables—in other words, a sequence of signs taken from different semiotic systems that can be decoded as human language. “I ‘heart’ New York,” “4u, ‘deer,’ ” and so on.

如果无意识的结构如同语言，那就意味着它不再能被视为本能的无言、未分化的居所。这一点上，拉康与大多数其他精神分析实践者之间存在着巨大的鸿沟。无意识并非先于——或者说更为原始地——那些我们通常称之为“语言”的衍生表达形式。因此，如果无意识类似于语言，那么它——本我，即本我——本身必然是能指，是“字母”，是欲望的晦涩对象，永远被排除在意识之外。但这绝非意味着无意识为思想服务。正如我们阅读的许多其他著作一样，拉康否认语言是一种媒介，它作为思想的促进者或外衣发挥作用。相反，语言构成思想；它使思想产生，并且与思想密不可分。

If it is structured like a language, this means the unconscious cannot any longer be considered the speechless, undifferentiated seat of the instincts. Here there is an enormous gulf between Lacan and most other practitioners of psychoanalysis. The unconscious does not precede—being more primitive—those derivative forms of articulation that we’re accustomed to call “language.” In resembling a language, then, it—the id, es—must itself be the signifier, the “letter,” that is the obscure object of desire, ever barred from consciousness. This is not at all to say that the unconscious works in the service of thought. Like many others in our reading, Lacan denies that language is a medium functioning as the facilitator or clothing of thought. Rather, language constitutes thought; it brings thought into being and is really inseparable from thought.

你或许能看出，这里不仅与其他形式的精神分析存在冲突，而且与整个哲学传统也存在冲突。如果你是唯物主义者——例如马克思主义者——并且认为事物先于意识而存在，意识次于事物，意识只是指涉和回应事物的工具——也就是说，意识、意识形态，或者随便你怎么称呼它，都是由现有的物质环境决定的——那么你就很难认为现有的物质环境是由语言产生的。同样地，如果你是实证主义者，如果你认为关于事物的观念是由语言表达的，而语言的存在正是为了表达事物，那么你同样将事物以及对事物的指涉置于思想的范畴之上。拉康实际上以一种相当巧妙的迂回方式抨击了马克思主义传统（参见1130页），同时也抨击了实证主义者（1132页）。如果仅仅是马克思与黑格尔之争，正如马克思本人所希望的那样，拉康坚持语言的优先性，赋予语言某些力量和能量，这可能会让人想起精神，这无疑使他从广义上讲成为一个黑格尔主义者。

You can probably recognize here the conflict not just with other forms of psychoanalysis but with a whole philosophical tradition. If you are a materialist—a Marxist, for example—and believe that things come first and consciousness comes second to refer to them and react to them—that consciousness, ideology, or call it what you will, is determined by existing material circumstances—you can’t very well think that existing material circumstances are produced by language. If by the same token you’re a positivist, if you believe that ideas about things are expressed by language, which exists for that purpose, then you are likewise giving priority to things and the reference to them that is the province of thought. Lacan actually attacks both the Marxist tradition in a rather brilliant sideways blow (cf. 1130) and the positivists (1132). If it were just a question of Marx versus Hegel, as Marx himself wanted to stage the quarrel, Lacan’s insistence on the priority of language, according language certain powers and energies that may remind one of Geist, certainly does make him, very broadly considered, a Hegelian.

那么，究竟是本我（id）还是存在（es）？这个通常与“本能驱力”、未经调和的欲望能量联系在一起的本我究竟是什么？拉康认为它就是能指（1130）：“我们该如何理解这里的‘字母’？很简单，字面理解。”意识的原始基础就是字母。还记得列维-斯特劳斯在德里达引用的文本中说过的话吗？语言并非一点一点地产生。今天没有语言，明天就有了语言：突然间，就有了赋予事物意义的方式，用符号学的术语来说，这最好理解为任意符号之间的区分。语言带来了符号的任意性以及索绪尔著作中着重探讨的符号之间的差异关系。拉康也持同样的观点。字母并非为了表达事物而诞生，并非自我雇佣来约束和驯服本我的警察，而是本我本身。也就是说，它是开端。“太初有道”，即字母，它通过自身所提供的符号系统传播意识。

So what is it, id, or es? What is this thing, the id, which is normally associated with “the instinctual drives,” the unmediated, unruly energy of desire? Well, Lacan says it is nothing other than the signifier (1130): “[H]ow are we to take take this ‘letter’ here? Quite simply, literally.” The primordial basis of consciousness is the letter. Remember Lévi-Strauss saying in the text quoted by Derrida that language doesn’t come into being just a little bit at a time. One day there is no language, and the next day there is language: suddenly there is a way of conferring meaning on things, best understood in semiotic terms as differentiation among arbitrary signs. Language brings with it the arbitrary nature of the sign and the differential relations among signs that are featured in the work of Saussure. So it is for Lacan. The letter is not that which comes into being to express things, not a policeman hired by the ego to discipline and civilize the id, but rather the id itself. That is merely to say, it is the beginning. “In the beginning was the word,” the letter, which disseminates consciousness through the signifying system that it makes available.

我其实希望，在阐述这些观点时，你会发现我其实是在重复一些枯燥乏味的事情。拉康的这部分理论，尽管有时显得有些奇怪，却反复强调着许多你现在应该已经习以为常的内容。拉康运用结构主义模型来阐释无意识如何支配意义。他接受了雅各布森对隐喻和转喻的区分，并且像雅各布森一样，在无意识的话语、日常生活中的精神病理以及失语症中，都看到了隐喻和转喻的协同构建。请记住，雅各布森不仅将隐喻和转喻分别与“诗歌”和“散文”联系起来，还将它们与精神障碍联系起来。正如拉康也指出的那样，在语言实践中，隐喻和转喻的极端形式会导致两种根本性的失语症或词语处理障碍。

I actually hope that in saying these things you’ll find me rather dully repeating myself. This is the part of Lacan that repeats, albeit strangely at times, a good deal of what you must be getting used to by now. Lacan activates a structuralist model to show how the unconscious dictates signification. He accepts Jakobson’s distinction between metaphor and metonymy and sees the cooperative building-up of metaphor and metonymy in the discourse of the unconscious and in the psychopathology of everyday life and of the aphasias in much the way that Jakobson does. Remember Jakobson associates metaphor and metonymy not just with “poetry” and “prose,” respectively, but also with mental disorders. In its extreme forms, metaphor and metonymy in linguistic practice take the form of two fundamental aphasias or word processing disorders, as Lacan, too, points out.

当然，拉康也借鉴了索绪尔的理论，但正如编辑在脚注中正确指出的那样，拉康对索绪尔符号图式的运用方式相当具有颠覆性。索绪尔的“所指/能指”变成了拉康的“S/s”。在拉康的理论中，巨大的能指笼罩着胆怯的所指，因为所指几乎不参与想象界的转喻话语。毕竟，你永远无法跨越这道屏障到达它，或者即使能指“滑过”了这道屏障，它也会用自身取代所指。在索绪尔的理论中，这道屏障将符号的两个部分连接在一起；而在拉康的理论中，这道屏障则是它们之间的深渊，是它们之间的屏障。索绪尔的图表与拉康所谓的算法实际上只有一点共同之处：即能指与所指、或所指与能指之间的关系是任意的，无法通过唤起所指本性中任何能指的自然属性来跨越。在这一点上，他们达成了一致；但在“什么产生什么”的问题上，他们似乎存在分歧。索绪尔暗示，在不可分割的联系中，这个问题毫无意义；而拉康则坚持认为，大S（能指）产生小s（所指）——任何把握所指的可能性都源于此。

Of course, Lacan draws likewise on Saussure, but as your editor rightly points out in a footnote, the algorithm Lacan uses for Saussure’s diagram of the sign is quite revisionary. Saussure’s “signified/signifier” becomes Lacan’s “S/s.” In Lacan we have the big looming signifier over the timid little signified, because the signified scarcely participates in the metonymic discourse of the imaginary. After all, you can never cross the bar to get to it, or if the signifier does “slide under” the bar, it displaces the signified with itself. In Saussure the bar binds the two parts of the sign together; in Lacan the bar is the abyss between them, the bar between them. Saussure’s diagram has in common with Lacan’s so-called algorithm only in fact the bar itself: the fact that the relationship between signifier and signified, or signified and signifier, is an arbitrary one that can’t be crossed by evoking anything natural in the nature of the signified that calls forth the signifier. There they agree, but as to what produces what, they appear to be divided. Saussure implies that in an indissoluble linkage the question is meaningless, whereas Lacan seems to insist that the big S is what generates the little s—is that from which any possibility of grasping a signified arises.

让我们回到我之前在介绍符号学时提到的门上的红灯的例子来说明这种区别，因为我认为，在这种情况下，我们也能感受到这种延续性。门上的红灯是一个与欲望相关的能指。这一点我们习以为常。在其他语境中，红灯与欲望无关，但“门上的红灯”这个能指却迎合了欲望。但欲望究竟指向什么呢？我们当然认为自己知道，但仔细看看这个能指。它位于门上方，仿佛这扇门是阻挡门后事物的屏障。门是所指吗？当然不是。但如果不是，既然其他一切都不可见，那么这个能指又如何能在二元对立的互惠关系中与所指锁定在一起呢？欲望的对象就在门后，被越来越厚重的屏障所遮蔽——毕竟，我们始终要假设，考虑到欲望和需求的区别，欲望的对象确实存在。你并不渴望那扇门，就像拉康故事里的男孩和女孩并不渴望写着“男士”和“女士”字样的门一样。小女孩说：“我们到了‘先生’那里。”小男孩说：“我们到了‘女士’那里。”嗯，这看起来相当健康！我们正朝着某种异性恋规范的欲望发展。但是，我们该如何确定这些欲望的对象呢？

Let’s exemplify this difference by going back to what I said about the red light over a door when introducing semiotics, because in this case, too, I think, we’ll have continuity. The red light over a door is a signifier that has to do with desire. This we take for granted. The red light in other contexts has nothing to do with desire, but the signifier “red light over a door” caters to desire. But desire for what? Well of course we think we know, but then look at the signifier. It is over the door as though the door were a bar to what’s behind it. Is the door the signified? Hardly. But if it is not, nothing else being visible, how then can the signifier lock itself into place, in the mutuality of binarism, with a signified? What’s desired is behind the door, concealed by a thickening opacity of the bar—always supposing, after all, given the difference between desire and need, that what’s desired is even there. You don’t desire the door, any more than the boy and the girl in Lacan’s anecdote desire the doors on which hommes and femmes are written. The little girl says, “We’ve arrived at Gentlemen,” and the little boy says, “We’ve arrived at Ladies.” Well, that seems to be quite healthy! We’re on our way to something like hetero-normative desire. But where can we say the objects of these desires are located?

这些门后唯一的吸引力在于重拾个人舒适的机会。如果可见的所指仍然存疑，我们甚至无法像在红灯下的门那样，暂时断言门本身就是所指的屏障——在能指链中，它们是隐蔽的能指，而非所指。更复杂的是，在拉康的轶事中，还有铁轨，对他而言，铁轨构成了一道更为真实的屏障。小男孩和小女孩端庄地坐在那里，彼此面对面，禁忌的屏障横亘在他们之间，他们心知肚明地讽刺着男人和女人试图表达任何事物的荒谬。他们自身的能指链或组合轴从男人和女人身边滚落，消失在夜色中。这对男孩和女孩就像是从纳博科夫的《阿达》中走出来的精彩人物，在《阿达》中，乱伦禁忌被打破。我不知道你们当中是否有人读过那本小说，但小说里的男孩范·维恩是个魅力十足又令人讨厌的小天才，就像拉康一样，而他的妹妹艾达则更甚。“白痴”是艾达和拉康笔下的小女儿都喜欢用的昵称（希腊语中“idiotes”的意思是“未分化的”）。拉康笔下的小男孩和小女孩被拒之门外，因为他们带着一种百无聊赖的自知之明，发现自己正朝着某种类似异性恋规范的欲望表达方式前进。但这根本不是欲望的表达，而是需求的表达，因为他们被禁止去代表能指所指涉的欲望对象。

The only attraction behind these doors is the chance to restore your personal comfort. And were the visible signified to remain in question, we cannot even say, as we could say provisionally in the case of the door under the red light, that the doors are themselves the bar over the signified—covertly signifiers, not signifieds, in the signifying chain. To complicate the matter further, in Lacan’s anecdote there are the railroad tracks, which for him constitute a truer bar. The little boy and girl sit there primly, facing each other, the bar of a taboo between them, quite knowingly ironic about the absurdity of the effort made by hommes and femmes to signify anything whatsoever. Their own chain of signification or axis of combination rolls past hommes and femmes into the night. This boy and girl are wonderful characters right out of Nabokov’s Ada, where the incest taboo is violated. I don’t know whether any of you know that novel, but the boy, Van Veen, is a charmingly obnoxious little genius, like Lacan, and his sister Ada is even worse. “Idiot” is a term of endearment favored both by Ada and by Lacan’s little girl (idiotes in Greek means undifferentiated). Lacan’s little boy and girl are barred because, with a bored knowingness, they find themselves on track toward something like the hetero-normative expression of desire. It’s not an expression of desire at all. It’s an expression of need because they are barred from representing the object of desire indicated by the signifier.

因此，欲望是对那些无法在话语的转喻运动、梦境或无意识运作方式中被指称之物的无尽延宕。我认为，拉康非常巧妙地向我们展示了我们如何从一个能指过渡到另一个能指：换句话说，他所谓的能指链是如何运作的。你会看到一系列同心圆，但每个圆环又由许多更小的同心圆环组成，这些小圆环以不同的方式与周围的圆环相连。这个意象非常精妙地重现了索绪尔对纵轴联想结构的理解：在语言的共时时刻，一些能指自然地与其他能指聚集在一起，并非只与一个群体聚集，而是与许多具有不同属性的群体聚集。但它们并非自然地与任何或所有能指聚集；因此，在选择轴上会出现联想簇，而这些簇则由链中链来指示。

Desire, then, is the endless deferral of that which cannot be signified in the metonymic movement of discourse, of dreaming, or of the way in which the unconscious functions. Lacan is very ingenious, I think, in convincingly showing us how it is that we get from one signifier to another: in other words, how what he calls the chain of the signifier works. You have a series of concentric rings, but each ring is made up of a lot of little concentric rings that hook on to surrounding rings in variable ways. This image very nicely rediagrams Saussure’s sense of the associative structure of the vertical axis: of the synchronic moment of language within which some signifiers naturally cluster with other signifiers, not just with one group but many groups with different properties. But they don’t at all naturally cluster with just any or all signifiers; hence you get associative clusters on the axis of selection, and they are indicated by these chains within chains.

隐喻的可能性偶尔会出现。在拉康看来，这是一个值得庆祝的时刻，因为正如他所说，它是“诗意的”，而且正如他所说，它是症状的一种显现，也是唯一可能的显现。症状之所以会引起我们的注意，是因为它让我们意识到欲望对象的缺失，这种缺失是公开表达的，而不是在转喻的喋喋不休中无休止地转移。我们可以看到它，但无法完全把握它，不过我们可以看到，它正是被意义行为本身所转移的东西。隐喻就出现在这些连接点上。被子的填充物是转喻的话语（在莎士比亚时代，被子的填充物被称为“浮夸”），而连接点则将其固定到位。

Now every once in a while the possibility of metaphor arises. It’s a moment to be celebrated in Lacan because, as he says, it’s “poetic,” and it is also, as he says, a manifestation, the only possible manifestation, of the symptom. A symptom calls itself to our attention as an awareness of lacking the object of desire that is expressed openly, not endlessly displaced in the babble of metonymy. One can see it. One can’t grasp it, but one can see it as that which has been displaced by the very act of signification. Metaphor appears at these points de capiton. The stuffing of a quilt is the discourse of metonymy (in Shakespeare’s time, quilt stuffing was called “bombast”), and the points de capiton hold it in place.

拉康列举了几个诗歌隐喻的例子。我将重点讨论雨果的作品，因为它比瓦莱里的作品更简洁。我很高兴拉康使用了“火花”这个词。你还记得我之前谈到沃尔夫冈·伊瑟时，我说过火花塞需要保持一定的间隙，两点之间必须有一定的距离才能产生火花。如果距离太近，就会短路；如果距离太远，什么也产生不了。拉康所指的火花是波阿斯和他的麦捆之间的关系，正如诗句“他的麦捆既不吝啬，也不恶毒”所表达的那样；麦捆本身慷慨地奉献，因此当然不是吝啬或恶毒的——由此你会认为，从转喻的角度来看，由于麦捆与波阿斯的关联，波阿斯也必然如此。

Lacan gives several examples of poetic metaphor. I shall focus on the Hugo because it’s more compact than the Valéry. I am delighted that Lacan uses the word “sparks.” You remember that when I was talking about Wolfgang Iser, I spoke of the need to gap a sparkplug, to have a certain distance between two points in order for the spark to happen. If it’s too close, you just short out, but if it’s too distant nothing happens either.
