The spark Lacan identifies is the relationship between Boaz and his sheaves in “his sheaves were neither miserly nor spiteful”; the sheaves themselves, which give of themselves freely, are certainly not miserly or spiteful for that reason—hence you would think that metonymically, by dint of their association with Boaz, Boaz must be like that, too.

他慷慨的收成既非吝啬也非恶意，然而，正如拉康所指出的，吝啬和恶意却在“他的”这个词中再次出现：如果他是这捆麦穗的拥有者，那么波阿斯就受制于资本主义或达尔文式竞争的精神，而这种精神既包含节俭，也包含竞争性的嫉妒或恶意，这些似乎已经从句子中被排除掉了。从比喻的角度来看，波阿斯被“他的麦捆”所取代。根据雅各布森所谓的等价原则中的差异性，所有格意味着波阿斯与那些被他用转喻方式粗略描述为的事物截然相反；然而与此同时，在这个比喻中，象征阳具的麦捆本身恰恰是他在俄狄浦斯情结阶段或原始部落中所扮演的角色，也正是如果一个婴儿将他物化后会成为的样子。我常常觉得济慈的《异乡玉米地里的路得》就像普桑的《秋》中那样，在波阿斯脚下卑躬屈膝，就像一个婴儿。

His munificent crop is neither miserly nor spiteful, and yet, as Lacan points out, miserliness and spitefulness come back in that word “his”: if he is a possessor of the sheaf, Boaz is subject to the spirit of capitalism or Darwinian competition that entail both the thrift and competitive envy or spite that appeared to have been banished from the sentence. Metaphorically speaking, Boaz is substituted for by the expression “his sheaves.” The possessive means, on the basis of what Jakobson would call dissimilarity within the principle of equivalence, that Boaz is the opposite of the things that he’s loosely said to be metonymically; yet at the same time within the metaphor, the phallic sheaves themselves are precisely what he has been in the Oedipal phase or primal horde, precisely what he would be if objectified by a baby looking at him. I often think that Keats’s “Ruth amid the alien corn,” suppliant at the feet of Boaz as in Poussin’s “Autumn,” is just such a baby.

我认为，在这里你可以看出拉康对隐喻或转喻之间关系的理解介于雅各布森或布鲁克斯与德曼之间，因为对这句诗的两种解读之间似乎存在着一种潜在的、无法化解的张力。它似乎同时且无法确定地表明：波阿斯慷慨无私，而他之所以吝啬刻薄，仅仅是因为他拥有财产。但这并不意味着否认雅各布森对拉康关于组合轴的思考方式产生了主要且核心的影响。隐喻在组合轴上的出现，以及我们能够沿着其表面识别出绗缝纽扣的方式，正是雅各布森所说的，诗歌的功能是将等价原则从选择轴转移到组合轴。

Here I think you can see Lacan’s sense of the relation between metaphor or metonymy hovering between that of Jakobson or Brooks and that of de Man, because there seems to be an underlying irreducible tension between the two readings of the line. It seems to say all at once, and undecidably, that Boaz was generous and free of spite and that he was just necessarily miserly and spiteful because he was a property owner. But this is not to deny that Jakobson is the primary and central influence on Lacan’s way of thinking about the axis of combination. The appearance of metaphor on the axis of combination, the way in which we can identify quilting buttons along its surface, is nothing other than what Jakobson said and meant when he said that the poetic function is the transference of the principle of equivalence from the axis of selection to the axis of combination.

总而言之，拉康认为语言是一种谜语，他指出，能指在任何符号学层面上的运动，即欲望的运动，都是对匮乏的表达。能指无法依附于任何所指（如果它“滑过横梁”，就会取代所指），这便是欲望对象无法实现的体现。

To sum up, Lacan says language is a rebus, and he says the movement of the signifier in whatever semiotic register, the movement of desire, is the articulation of a lack. The impossibility of attaching the signifier to any signified (if it “slides under the bar” it displaces the signified in doing so) is the impossibility of realizing an object of desire.

对“文字”优先性的理论化，其最显而易见的后果（这并非我们第一次或最后一次在各种词汇和语境中遇到这种含义）是意识到“语言思考我”。例如：“我在我不在的地方思考，因此我在我不思考的地方存在”（1142）。构成我思想的事物并非呈现于我自身。它就是它，文字本身。我并非呈现于我自己，因为呈现于我的自我通过话语而产生的方式，然而这种方式却无法识别我。它既无法将我识别为主体，也无法——在自恋阶段，假设我能以某种方式在镜像阶段重新想象自己——将我识别为欲望的对象。

The most obvious consequence of theorizing the primacy of “the letter,” and this isn’t the first or last time we will have encountered this implication in various vocabularies and contexts, is the realization that “language thinks me.” For example: “I think where I am not, therefore I am where I do not think” (1142). That which constitutes my thought is not present to me. It is it, the letter. I am not present to myself because what is present is the way my self comes into being through discourse, which nevertheless cannot identify me. It cannot identify me either as subject or—in a phase of narcissism, supposing I could somehow reimagine myself in the mirror phase—as an object of desire.

关于欲望与需求的区别，还有更多值得探讨之处，尤其是在我们所接触的文本中。仔细想想，这并非意味着我们对仅仅需要的东西感到不满。显然，我们确实感到满意，但我们在生活中，正如电影——以及虚构作品所营造的幻象世界——所反映的那样，意识到这种区别及其伴随的悲情，数百年来一直存在。齐泽克的论文《宫廷爱情》基于拉康发表的一篇“研讨会”文章，解读了一系列电影，这些电影中，种种障碍阻碍了男女主角与“大他者”的结合，但最终却揭示出他们实际上对这种可能性的回避。

There’s more to say about desire and need as the distinction appears in texts that we encounter. As we think about it, it’s not that we’re not happy with the things that we merely need. Obviously we are, yet we recognize in our lives as reflected in the magical world of film—the world of illusion promoted by film and also fiction—that the distinction with its attendant pathos has been prominent for hundreds of years. The essay by Žižek called “Courtly Love” and based on one of Lacan’s published “Seminars” features readings of a series of films in which barriers prevent consummation with the Big Other yet turn out to mask an actual avoidance of the possibility.

 

 

第十四章

CHAPTER 14

影响
Influence

阅读材料：

Readings:

艾略特，TS “传统与个人才能。”载《批评传统》，第 537-541 页。

Eliot, T. S. “Tradition and the Individual Talent.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 537–541.

布鲁姆，哈罗德。“关于优先性的思考。”载于《批判传统》，第 1156-1160 页。

Bloom, Harold. “A Meditation upon Priority.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1156–1160.

那些主要熟悉《如何读诗》、宗教著作以及《莎士比亚与人的发明》的读者，或许会惊讶地发现哈罗德·布鲁姆的名字出现在文学理论的课程大纲中；但始于20世纪70年代的《影响的焦虑》、《误读地图》、《诗歌与压抑》等一系列著作，使布鲁姆置身于当时激烈的理论争论之中。他与所谓的耶鲁学派关系密切，尽管当时他对同事们的许多工作都表示不满，但他仍然愿意编辑并参与撰写一本名为《解构与批评》的文集。

Those of you who are chiefly familiar with How to Read a Poem, the books on religion, and Shakespeare and the Invention of the Human may be surprised to find Harold Bloom on a literary theory syllabus; but the great outpouring of work that began with The Anxiety of Influence, A Map of Misreading, Poetry and Repression, and many other books in the 1970s put Bloom in the very midst of the theoretical controversies then swirling. He was associated with the so-called Yale school, and although even at the time he expressed disaffection with many aspects of his colleagues’ work, he was willing to edit and also to contribute to a volume that was called Deconstruction and Criticism.

即使阅读你眼前的这些内容，你也能看出布鲁姆与解构主义的关联相对较少，尽管从广义上讲，我们可以将诗人之间的防御性斗争视为一种否定，从而将其视为对大多数文学理论反实证主义倾向的又一贡献。自《影响的焦虑》出版以来，尽管他从未公开放弃其影响理论，但他已不再运用“六种修正比例”来解读诗歌。我并不强求你理解这些比例，但我认为欣赏“clinamen”（斜向性）、“tessera”（镶嵌）、“kenosis”（虚己）、“askesis”（苦行）、“demonization”（妖魔化）和“apophrades”（否定）的动态变化——熟悉这些概念并将它们作为实践批评的工具——是一件令人兴奋的事情。稍后我会更详细地探讨其中的一些修正比例。

Even in reading what you have before you, you can see how relatively little Bloom has to do with deconstruction, although perhaps broadly speaking one can think of the defensive struggle between poets as negation, hence as another contribution to the anti-positivist thrust of most literary theory. Since the period of The Anxiety of Influence, although he has never openly renounced his theory of influence, he has stopped reading poems through the machinery of “the six revisionary ratios.” I’m not going to insist that you understand these, yet I do think it exciting to appreciate the dynamic of clinamen, tessera, kenosis, askesis, demonization, and apophrades—to become acclimatized to these ideas and actually to use them as a machinery for practical criticism. I’ll have more to say about at least some of the revisionary ratios later.

我认为布鲁姆对文学理论最重要的贡献在于他提出的思想体系，正是这些思想使他成为一位重要的文学史学家。布鲁姆与我们之前阅读过的蒂尼亚诺夫和雅各布森，以及后来的汉斯·罗伯特·尧斯和弗雷德里克·詹姆逊等人一道，提出了一套极具挑战性的文学史理论。这一点却鲜为人知。事实上，人们普遍认为布鲁姆，尤其是在20世纪80年代之后，完全不关心历史，对历史漠不关心，也不关心现实世界如何影响文学。这种评价在很大程度上是合理的，布鲁姆也将其视为一种优点而引以为豪；但布鲁姆作为理论家——正如蒂尼亚诺夫一样——真正有趣的地方在于他对文学史的理解，而非历史本身。 （应该指出的是，布鲁姆在探讨非文学主题时所展现的历史知识广博而详尽。）他提出了一个关于诗歌传统中诗歌传承逻辑的有力论证，我认为作为诠释者，我们若忽视这一论证将付出惨痛的代价。该论证的结构是精神分析式的，但任何将其视为仅仅是传记式论证的人，都会像布鲁克斯的论证一样，将其过度简化。布鲁姆关注的是“诗人作为诗人”的心理，并将此与任何关于“诗人作为人”的考量截然区分开来。

I would say that Bloom’s most important contribution to literary theory is the sets of ideas that make him an important literary historiographer. Together with figures like Tynianov and Jakobson earlier in our reading and Hans Robert Jauss and Fredric Jameson later, Bloom offers a challenging theory of literary history. This hasn’t often been remarked upon. As a matter of fact, the common attitude toward Bloom, especially in retrospect since the 1980s, takes for granted that he’s hopelessly ahistorical, caring nothing about history or about the way in which the real world impinges on literature. To a considerable extent, this judgment is fair, and Bloom proclaims it proudly as a virtue; but what’s interesting in Bloom as a theorist—as in Tynianov—is his view of literary history, not history. (It should be said that the historical knowledge on display when Bloom works on a nonliterary topic is broad and detailed.) He offers a powerful argument about the logic of succession among poems in a tradition, an argument that as interpreters I think we ignore at our peril. The argument is psychoanalytic in structure, though it is much oversimplified, like Brooks’s argument, by anyone who thinks it is merely biographical. Bloom focuses on the psyche of “poets as poets,” distinguishing this focus sharply from any consideration of “poets as men.”

在我们的阅读三阶段中，我们首先探讨了语言生成论，即语言如何产生文学作品。现在，我们正在回顾心理生成论的概念，即人类心理如何产生文学作品。很快，我们将转向社会政治生成论，即社会、经济、政治和历史因素如何产生文学作品。很好，但你可能已经注意到，我们在过渡到“心理”生成论时遇到了多少困难。我们一直说我们已经到达那里，而我甚至已经开始说我们即将离开，但实际上，正如你肯定已经注意到的，我们仍然在使用语言学模型。拉康告诉我们，无意识类似于语言，它的结构也像语言；布鲁克斯告诉我们，正是隐喻和转喻之间的关系所产生的语言结构构成了叙事文本。我们仍在等待有人来阐述文本的心理生成论。

In the tripartition of our reading, we first considered logological genesis, the production of literature by language. We are now reviewing concepts of psychological genesis, the production of literature by the human psyche. We will turn soon to sociopolitical genesis, the production of literature by social, economic, and political and historical factors. Well and good, but you may have noticed how much trouble we’ve had moving to “psychological” genesis. We keep saying we’ve arrived there, and I’m already starting to say we’re about to leave, yet we actually continue to be working with linguistic models, as I’m sure you’ve noticed. We’ve had Lacan telling us the unconscious resembles a language, that it’s structured like a language, and Brooks telling us that it’s the verbal structure arising out of the relationship between metaphor and metonymy that constitutes a narrative text. We’re still waiting for somebody to say something about the psychological genesis of the text.

布鲁姆确实让我们更接近真相，尽管究竟接近到什么程度还有待观察。当他谈到“诗人中的诗人”时，他关注的是他所谓的“对抗”，即迟来的诗人与先行诗人之间发生在心理层面（或许是本能层面）的心理斗争。然而，即便布鲁姆本人，最终也无非是在谈论文本与文本之间的关系，因为他找不到其他证据来支持他所描述的这种心理动态。他描述的这些关系，他更倾向于从主题的角度来探讨，但这些关系必然源于语言线索。他总是对探寻语言影响的做法嗤之以鼻，称之为“发霉的无花果语文学”。但我认为，当你研究《影响的焦虑》、《误读地图》及其后续著作中关于文学影响的例证时，你会发现，其中仍然存在对语言回响的依赖，尽管他理论的强版本尽力抵制这种依赖，但实际上却又不可或缺。我想就“影响力”这个主题展开一般性的探讨，实际上，我想谈谈基于心理或现实世界的影响力概念与基于语言的影响力概念之间的区别有多么模糊。

Well, Bloom brings us closer, though it remains to be seen how close. When he speaks of “the poet in the poet,” he is concerned with describing what he calls an “agon,” a psychological struggle between the belated poet and the precursor poet that takes place at a presumably instinctual layer of the psyche. Yet even Bloom, of course, is finally talking about the relation of text to text, having no other source of evidence for the dynamic he describes as psychological. He describes relations that he prefers to consider thematically but that must perforce arise from verbal cues. The search for verbal influence he always professes contempt for, calling it “moldy fig philology.” But I think that as you study the examples of literary influence in The Anxiety of Influence, A Map of Misreading, and their successors, you will see that there remains a dependence on verbal echo, which the strong version of his theory resists as best it can but does nevertheless require. I want to move into a general exploration of the topic of influence by talking, in fact, about how slippery the distinction is between an idea of influence that is, let’s say, psychological or world-based and an idea of influence that is word-based.

在讨论影响力时，人们常常混淆心理因素和语言因素，这种混淆在模仿这一传统概念中体现得尤为深刻。柏拉图和亚里士多德都认为诗歌是模仿。他们都说，诗歌是“对自然的模仿”。柏拉图认为诗歌写得不好，亚里士多德则认为写得很好，但他们都认同诗歌是对自然的模仿。最终，这种模仿自然（mimesis）的概念发生了转变。在罗马文学的白银时代，拉丁语达到文采巅峰，昆体良、西塞罗等修辞理论家不再讨论模仿（mimesis），而是将注意力——当然是用拉丁语——集中在模仿（imitatio）上，尽管两者表面上看起来是同一个概念。这不再是模仿自然的问题，而是模仿文学典范的问题：模仿（imitatio）指的是模仿语言，这一主题使得白银时代和亚历山大时期的批评家能够通过思考特定诗人与其所源自的文学表达传统之间的关系来建立经典。因此，模仿是一种基于语言的影响理论，它源于一种基于自然的影响理论。这种情况的出现，是因为文学传统不断延伸，像荷马和埃斯库罗斯这样的原始典范（可以说，他们除了自然之外别无模仿对象）被像维吉尔和塞内卡这样对过去抱有高度“文学性”态度的中间派作家所取代。

There’s a long tradition of the confusion between psychological and the linguistic factors in discussing influence, a confusion that runs deepest within the very traditional concept of imitation. Plato and Aristotle agree that poetry is imitation. It is, both of them say, an “imitation of nature.” Plato thinks it’s done badly, Aristotle thinks it’s done well, but both agree that poetry is an imitation of nature. Eventually this idea of mimesis, the imitation of nature, was transformed. During the Silver Age of Roman literature, a high-water mark of elegance in the Latin language, rhetorical theorists like Quintilian, Cicero, and others no longer discuss mimesis but instead focus their attention—in Latin, of course—on imitatio, which is only seemingly the same idea. It’s no longer a question of the imitation of nature but rather of the imitation of literary models: imitatio is the imitation of language, a topic that enables Silver Age and Alexandrian critics to establish canons by thinking about the relationship between particular poets and the tradition of literary expression from which they emerge. Imitatio, then, was a language-based theory of influence arising out of a nature-based theory of influence. This took place as literary traditions elongated themselves and originary models like Homer and Aeschylus (of whom one could say that they had nothing to imitate except nature) were succeeded by intermediary authors, highly “literary” in their attitude toward the past, like Virgil and Seneca.

在亚历山大·蒲柏的《论批评》中，他探讨了维吉尔与模仿自然的关系。文章认为，荷马直接模仿自然，即便只是因为当时没有文学范本可供借鉴。维吉尔起初也认为自己可以模仿自然，创作属于自己的民族史诗，但后来他开始研究荷马。起初他感到很沮丧，因为荷马似乎已经把一切都表达完了。在《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》之后，似乎已经没有什么可说的了。然而，维吉尔解决这个问题的办法是：既然他不能模仿自然（因为荷马已经做到了），那么他仍然可以模仿荷马。

During the course of Alexander’s Pope’s “Essay on Criticism,” the relation of Virgil to the imitation of nature is touched upon. Homer, the argument goes, imitated nature directly, if only because there were no literary models to imitate. Virgil began by supposing that he could just write his own national epic, imitating nature, but then he started looking at Homer. At first he felt terrible because Homer seemed to have said it all. After The Iliad and The Odyssey, there seemed to be nothing left to say. Well, the solution to this problem for Virgil was that if he couldn’t imitate nature because Homer had done that, he could still imitate Homer:

但当他仔细审视每一部分时，他发现[荷马作品的每一部分，以及他自己创作史诗时的每一部分]
But when t’ examine ev’ry part he came [every part of Homer’s compositions, together with every part of his own composition as he undertook to write his own epic]
他发现，自然与荷马是同一回事。
Nature and Homer were, he found, the same.

因此，这里逐渐浮现出这样一种观点：模仿自然和模仿艺术——模仿人物、历史事件和模仿语言——是同一过程的组成部分，密不可分。要做其中之一，就必然要做另一个。这就是我所说的，我们仍在努力摆脱文学的语言起源，转向其心理起源。即使在最传统的关于影响如何运作的论述中，例如蒲柏的理论，我们仍然很难区分自然和艺术。在蒲柏之后五十年，塞缪尔·约翰逊宣称“没有什么能取悦大众，或长久取悦大众，唯有对普遍自然的描绘”，他正徘徊在两种观点之间：一种观点认为艺术代表世界，另一种观点则认为艺术代表的是经得起时间考验的、公认的模仿世界的规范。

So here you have emerging the idea that to imitate nature and to imitate art—to imitate people and historical events and to imitate language—is part and parcel of the same process. To do one, you necessarily have to do the other. That’s what I mean in remarking that we’re still struggling to get away from the linguistic origins and move on to the psychological origins of literature. Even in the most traditional accounts of how influence works, like Pope’s, we still find it very difficult to distinguish between nature and art. When Samuel Johnson, fifty years after Pope, pronounces that “Nothing can please many, or please long, but just representations of general nature,” he is poised between the idea that art represents the world and the idea that art represents agreed-upon norms for imitating the world that withstand the test of time.

那么，如果我们再来看你为本次讲座阅读的两篇文本——它们都是关于影响的理论——你会发现，T·S·艾略特对于这两种模仿之间的关系也有些含糊不清。在艾略特看来，个体的才能在面对传统时，必须应对他所谓的“欧洲的思维”（539）。我将朗读一段较长的文字，这段文字是对艾略特观点最易于理解的概括之一：

If we turn, then, to the two texts that you’ve read for this lecture, both of which are theories of influence, you can see that T. S. Eliot, too, is somewhat unclear about the relationship of these two sorts of imitation. For Eliot the individual talent that confronts tradition has to cope with what he calls “the mind of Europe” (539). I’ll read a fairly extensive passage that provides one of the most accessible summaries of what Eliot has to say:

诗人必须清楚地意识到一个显而易见的事实：艺术本身永远不会进步，但艺术的素材却永远不会一成不变。他必须明白，欧洲的思想——他自己国家的思想——这种思想，他终将明白，远比他个人的思想重要得多……
[The poet] must be quite aware of the obvious fact that art never improves, but that the material of art is never quite the same. He must be aware that the mind of Europe—the mind of his own country—a mind which he learns in time to be much more important than his own private mind …

我先停一下，说说这似乎与布鲁姆的风格截然不同，因为布鲁姆这位浪漫主义者颂扬个体精神，或者至少推崇个体精神为从众多争夺关注的先行者中脱颖而出而进行的斗争。这种斗争在艾略特身上似乎并不存在。艾略特似乎坚持自我消融，认为欧洲的集体精神比个人的精神更为重要，并且如果一个人想要以个人才能为传统做出任何贡献，那么这种贡献必须建立在对自身并非自身以及自身无法成为的一切都极其敏锐的认知之上。

Let me just stop there and say that this seems as much unlike Bloom as it can possibly be because Bloom, the Romantic, celebrates the individual mind, or in any case honors the struggle of the individual mind to distinguish itself from all of those minds jostling for attention that precede it. This sort of struggle seems to be absent from Eliot. Eliot seems to insist on self-effacement, the recognition that the mind of Europe is more important than one’s own mind, and that if one is to contribute anything as an individual talent to tradition, that contribution has to be grounded in the acutely sensitive awareness of everything that one is not, and not capable of being, oneself.

继续这段文字：

To continue the passage:

欧洲人的思想是不断变化的，这种变化是一种发展，它不会抛弃任何既有的东西，也不会使莎士比亚、荷马，或是马格德林岩画的作者们的作品过时。这种发展，或许是精炼，也肯定是复杂化，但从艺术家的角度来看，这并非一种进步。
[The mind of Europe is] a mind which changes, and that this change is a development which abandons nothing en route, which does not superannuate either Shakespeare, or Homer, or the rock drawing of the Magdalenian draftsmen. That this development, refinement perhaps, complication certainly, is not, from the point of view of the artist, any improvement.

个人的才能必须融入文学、哲学和其他各种表达方式的庞大矩阵之中，这个矩阵不断变化，却从未真正改变自身，当然也不能被理解为朝着某个伟大目标的宏伟征程或进步，因为没有什么会消失，也没有什么根本性的创新会被引入。

The individual talent must enter into a vast matrix of literary, philosophical, and other sorts of expression that changes and yet never really transforms itself and certainly can’t be understood as a grand march or progress toward some great goal, because nothing is ever lost and nothing radically innovative can ever be introduced.

我希望你能从这段文字中看到我们之前讨论过的许多内容：伽达默尔认为传统需要对延续性的认知，需要愿意与过去达成某种妥协，需要找到一种融合的视野，使过去与现在能够以一种真实的方式彼此对话；又如俄国形式主义的观点，认为任何文学文本的主导元素和辅助元素始终存在，只是在不同的文本中不断互换位置。简而言之，根据这类历史理论，所有可能的文学形式始终存在，而一个人进入这片广阔的表达可能性海洋的过程，永远无法展现出浪漫主义传统所追求的那种原创天才。从艾略特的这种传统主义视角来看，我们或许会认为布鲁姆的观点必然与之截然不同。

I hope you see in this passage a good deal that we’ve passed through already: Gadamer’s sense of tradition as something that requires the awareness of continuity, the willingness to meet the past halfway, finding a merger of horizons in which the past and the present can speak in an authentic way to each other; or the Russian formalist idea that the dominant and the recessive elements of any literary text are always present at any time but change places with each other in successive texts. In short, according to historical theories of this kind, the whole gamut of literary possibility is always already present, and one’s own entry into this vast sea of expressive possibility can never display the sort of original genius that the Romantic tradition looks for. From this traditionalist perspective of Eliot we would imagine that Bloom must diverge sharply.

相反，我想论证的是，艾略特和布鲁姆之间实际上存在着大量的延续性，而布鲁姆否认这种影响恰恰是对他前辈的严重误读。我不想详细展开这个论点，以免被认为过于执着，但我想就此提出几点看法，因为这些看法本身就能有效地阐释《影响的焦虑》一书的论点。布鲁姆一直否认《传统与个人才能》的影响。他确实承认受到一些影响：爱默生、尼采、弗洛伊德、伟大的浪漫主义诗人，以及近代的莎士比亚。但在我看来，至少在框架和暗示层面，布鲁姆的所有思想都已在艾略特的《传统与个人才能》中有所体现。

I want to argue, on the contrary, that actually there is a tremendous amount of continuity between Eliot and Bloom, and that in order to deny this influence Bloom is a strong misreader of his precursor. I don’t want to develop this argument in full detail for fear of being considered obsessive, but I’d like to make a few points about it, because these points will exemplify the argument of The Anxiety of Influence itself as effectively as anything else I could say. Bloom has always denied the influence of “Tradition in the Individual Talent.” He does acknowledge influences: Emerson, Nietzsche, Freud, the great Romantic poets, and more recently Shakespeare. But it seems to me that at least in skeletal form, in suggestion, Bloom is all there already in Eliot’s “Tradition and the Individual Talent.”

例如，布鲁姆不遗余力地展现了新事物如何重构旧事物。他指出，《丁登寺》的先驱文本是《利西达斯》。或许还有其他诗歌影响了《丁登寺》，例如柯勒律治的《午夜霜冻》，但《丁登寺》真正与之抗衡的诗歌是《利西达斯》。布鲁姆阐明了华兹华斯如何重新审视并修正了弥尔顿对挽歌主题的最终诠释。关键在于，一旦一位杰出的诗人创作了后世的文本，我们就再也无法用同样的眼光解读先驱文本。换句话说，华兹华斯对先驱文本的深刻误读如此有力，以至于它也成为了我们自身的深刻误读。读过《丁登寺》之后，我们便无法再用同样的视角看待《利西达斯》。我们现在发现，华兹华斯反思自己身上已经失去的某种品质，这种品质体现在弥尔顿身上，已故的爱德华·金现在代表了弥尔顿自身诗歌创作生涯的危机。

Just for example, Bloom is at pains to show the way in which the new reconstitutes the old. The precursor text for “Tintern Abbey,” he says, is “Lycidas.” Perhaps there are other poems that may have influenced “Tintern Abbey,” such as Coleridge’s “Frost at Midnight,” but the poem with which “Tintern Abbey” struggles is “Lycidas,” and Bloom is able to show how Wordsworth revisits and revises the subject matter of elegy as Milton had definitively presented it. But the point here is that once the belated text is written by a strong poet, we can never read the precursor text the same way again. Wordsworth’s strong misreading of the precursor text is so powerful, in other words, that it becomes our own strong misreading. We just can’t think about “Lycidas” in the same way on this view after we’ve read “Tintern Abbey.” We now find Wordsworth’s reflection on a former quality in himself that he has lost already to be present in Milton, with the deceased Edward King now standing proxy for a crisis in Milton’s own poetic vocation.

如果这听起来难以置信，或许你可以通过一两个例子来理解。最明显的例子，虽然远非最符合布鲁姆式的论述，是博尔赫斯的小说《皮埃尔·梅纳尔，堂吉诃德的作者》。这篇轶事讲述的是一位法国人在十九世纪末（如果我没记错的话）用西班牙语写了一部小说，结果发现这部小说与塞万提斯的《堂吉诃德》一字不差。只不过，这不是塞万提斯的《堂吉诃德》，而是皮埃尔·梅纳尔的《堂吉诃德》。想想这有多么不同。这是一位法国人在不久前用西班牙语写作。这相当令人印象深刻，可以说比塞万提斯仅仅用他自己的语言和时代写作更令人印象深刻。梅纳尔的小说堪称技艺精湛的演绎，它为堂吉诃德的故事引入了一个截然不同的历史视角。塞万提斯自认为是在讽刺他所处的历史时期——记录骑士精神的消亡等等——但想想看，几个世纪之后，当一个人带着如今所知的一切，以某种叠加的、重新审视的方式去写作时，他对那个历史时期的讽刺意味又该如何体现？我们又怎能用同样的眼光去解读塞万提斯的《堂吉诃德》呢？这似乎有些天真。然而，得益于这部姗姗来迟的文本，我们现在得以认识到，塞万提斯其实已经完成了皮埃尔·梅纳尔的壮举：将一种历史视角叠加在另一种视角之上（他自己的视角叠加在堂吉诃德的视角之上），并且以一个西班牙人的身份“书写”着由摩尔人西德·哈梅特·贝南杰利从阿拉伯语翻译而来的文字。

If this seems implausible, you may at least see the point by considering an example or two. The most obvious, though far from the most Bloomian, is the Borges story called “Pierre Menard, Author of Don Quixote.” This is an anecdote about a Frenchman at the end (as I recall) of the nineteenth century writing a novel in Spanish that turns out to be, word for word, Cervantes’s Don Quixote. Only it’s not Cervantes’s Don Quixote; it’s Pierre Menard’s Don Quixote. Think how different it is. This is a Frenchman writing in Spanish not so long ago. That’s pretty impressive, much more impressive, you might say, than Cervantes merely writing in his own language and his own time, and as a virtuoso performance Menard’s novel introduces a completely different historical perspective on the Quixote story. Whereas Cervantes thinks he’s being ironic about his own historical moment—chronicling the death of chivalry and so on—think how ironic one can be about that historical moment when writing several centuries later, with everything that one knows now a sort of layering of second thoughts. How can we ever read Cervantes’s Don Quixote in the same way? It seems naive. Yet with the benefit of the belated text we are now enabled to recognize that Cervantes has already performed Pierre Menard’s feat: superimposing one historical perspective on another (his own on Quixote’s), and “writing,” as a Spaniard, words translated from the Arabic by a Moor, Cide Hamete Benengeli.

想想乔伊斯的《尤利西斯》。我们都知道，《尤利西斯》和维吉尔的《埃涅阿斯纪》前半部分一样，都是以《奥德赛》为基础，并且沿用了《奥德赛》中的一些情节；但它似乎用错了角度来解读《奥德赛》。它将原诗的英雄主义视角拉低到对现代社会日常生活的平淡描述中。乔伊斯正是通过对《奥德赛》的借鉴，来消解《奥德赛》的英雄气概。有了这样的视角，读过《尤利西斯》之后，我们很难再用同样的眼光去解读《奥德赛》。然而，《奥德赛》对《尤利西斯》中所有卑鄙无耻的东西都提出了反驳，更重要的是，奥德修斯变化莫测、适时求生的本能，为未来的地中海商人树立了榜样，预先勾勒出了利奥波德·布鲁姆的性格轮廓。

Think of Joyce’s Ulysses. We all know that Ulysses, like the first half of Virgil’s Aeneid, is based on The Odyssey and that it recycles the episodes of The Odyssey; but it seems to be looking at The Odyssey through the wrong end of a telescope. It’s dragging the heroic outlook of the poem down into an unheroic account of everyday life in recent society. Precisely in following The Odyssey, Joyce debunks the heroic scale of The Odyssey. With this perspective, it’s hard to read The Odyssey in the same way again after we’ve read Ulysses. Yet The Odyssey offers its countercommentary on everything that’s sordid and mean in Ulysses, and, more importantly, the protean, time-serving survival instincts of Odysseus, modeling for the future the seagoing Mediterranean merchant, furnish in advance the outlines of Leopold Bloom’s character.

现在必须指出，哈罗德·布鲁姆本人肯定也会这么说，《尤利西斯》并非对《奥德赛》的强烈误读，因为它完全清楚自己的意图。这是一种刻意的误读，但它也有其他优点。我举的两个例子都不是心理上的对抗。因此， 《尤利西斯》并非强烈误读的典范，但它与布鲁姆的理论以及艾略特关于个人才能与传统之间关系的观点，共同之处在于它重构了传统。它并非仅仅是创新，而是让我们以一种不同的方式看待传统本身。艾略特说（538）：

Now it has to be said, and Harold Bloom would certainly say this himself, that Ulysses is not a strong misreading of The Odyssey because it’s perfectly conscious of what it’s doing. It’s a deliberate misreading that has other virtues. Neither of the examples I have given are psychologically agonistic. Ulysses is not an exemplar of strong misreading, then, but what it does have in common with Bloom’s theory and also with Eliot’s idea about the relationship between the individual talent and tradition is that it reconstitutes tradition. It doesn’t just innovate. It makes us see tradition itself in a different way. Eliot says (538):

现有的古迹彼此构成了一种理想的秩序，而新的（真正意义上的）艺术作品的引入则改变了这种秩序。在新的作品出现之前，现有的秩序是完整的；为了使秩序在新事物出现后得以延续，整个现有的秩序必须做出改变，哪怕只是微小的改变。
The existing monuments form an ideal order among themselves which is modified by the introduction of the new (the really new) work of art among them. The existing order is complete before the new work arrives; for order to persist after the supervention of novelty, the whole existing order must be, if ever so slightly, altered.

我们再也无法用同样的眼光看待它了。因此，传统与个人才华之间，或者说强大的先驱者与后起之秀之间，似乎存在着一种动态的、相互依存的关系。

We can’t quite see it the same way again. So it’s a dynamic, mutual relationship that exists between tradition and the individual talent or between the strong precursor and the belated poet that seems to be in play.

在布鲁姆看来，后起之秀对先驱的强烈误读——否认先驱早已表达过如今所表达的内容——凸显了后起之秀的自我中心主义：我正在做新的事情，我正在去往无人涉足之地。我的创新如此强劲，以至于我怀疑在我出现之前是否真的存在过这样的人。这种俄狄浦斯式的对父亲的超越正是后起之秀的力量所在。然而，正如我们所见，强大的先驱实际上早已表达了后起之秀所要表达的一切。布鲁姆的理论强调一种字面意义上的原创性修辞，即“第一”，同时承认之前的诗人早已表达过一切。是弥尔顿笔下的撒旦，而非伟大的浪漫主义者，曾说过他不知道自己何时不再是现在的样子。因此，布鲁姆的文学史学同时重视创新和保守，或者说传统。与倾向于保守或传统的伽达默尔，以及倾向于创新的伊瑟尔或俄国形式主义者不同，布鲁姆既认可传统是永恒不变的——这正是“早已被说过”的逻辑——也认可传统是不断被重塑或至少被重新思考的。我必须说，这与T·S·艾略特之前的观点非常相似。

In Bloom, the belated poet’s strong misreading of the precursor, denying that the precursor already said what’s being said now, asserts the egoistic priority of the belated poet: I’m doing something new, I’m going where no one has ever gone before. I’m innovating so powerfully that I doubt whether there actually was anybody before I came along. This Oedipal overgoing of the father is the strength of the belated poet. Yet as we have seen, the strong precursor turns out already to have said everything the belated poet says. Bloom’s theory emphasizes a rhetoric of literal originality, in the sense of being first, while acknowledging that earlier poets have always already said everything. It was Milton’s Satan, not the great Romantics, who said that he knows no time when he was not as now. Thus Bloom’s literary historiography places a premium on innovation and on conservation, or tradition, at one and the same time. Unlike Gadamer leaning toward the conservative or traditional, and Iser or the Russian Formalists, who lean toward the innovative, Bloom simultaneously countenances the idea of tradition as unchanging—such is the logic of “always already said”—and also the idea of tradition as what is constantly being remade or at least rethought. That, I have to tell you, is very similar to what T. S. Eliot had said already.

于是，我们便引出了艾略特那句著名的格言（539）：“有人说：‘逝去的作家与我们疏远，因为我们比他们知道得更多。’正是如此，他们就是我们所知道的。” 我觉得这话说得相当精辟，布鲁姆或许也会以他自己的方式表达类似的观点。过去是我们所知道的，但如果我们足够强大，我们就不会意识到自己知道过去。换句话说，当我写这首迟来的诗时，我写的是过去，但我认为我做的是不同的事情。在第一个修正比例（clinamen）中，我偏离了过去：我向外向下偏转，我找到了属于自己的空间，就像卢克莱修笔下的原子。卢克莱修说，如果原子不偏转，它们最终都会落到同一个地方，这描述了迟来的诗人对自己与前人之间关系的理解。他实际上还是落在同一地点，但这种转向的力量，这种转向的修辞手法，如此强烈，以至于我们感觉自己仿佛被带入了另一个世界。我们再次感受到这位新诗人作品中的创新性以及必要的保守性，或者说是传承的一面。

We come, then, to the famous aphorism of Eliot (539): “Someone said: ‘The dead writers are remote from us because we know so much more than they did.’ Precisely, and they are that which we know.” Rather good, I think, and something that Bloom, in his own way, might very well say. The past is what we know, but if we’re strong, we’re not aware of knowing it. In other words, I write the past when I write my belated poem, but I think I’m doing something different. In the first revisionary ratio, clinamen, I am swerving from the past: I swerve out and down, I find my own space like a Lucretian atom. Lucretius says that all the atoms would fall in the same place if they didn’t swerve, and that describes the belated poet’s sense of what he’s doing in relation to the precursor. He’s actually falling in the same place, but the strength of that swerve, the rhetorical gesture of the swerve, is so powerful that we do feel that we have been transported. Once again we feel both the innovation and the necessary conservatism, or preservational aspect, of the new poet’s composition.

然而，艾略特对诗人非人格化的强调，以及对逃离人格的渴望（541），无疑与布鲁姆的理念背道而驰：“当然，只有那些拥有人格和情感的人才知道想要逃离这些东西意味着什么。”进入艺术的世界，意味着放弃那种认为个人心理痛苦才是最重要的观念（或者至少希望如此：艾略特的诗人只想逃离人格），意味着以诗人和创作者的身份——如果还能保留这个称谓的话——沉浸于远比自身广阔无垠的宇宙之中。

Surely, however, nothing could be less Bloomian than Eliot’s emphasis on the poet’s impersonality, on the wish to escape personality (541): “But, of course, only those who have personality and emotions know what it means to want to escape from these things.” To enter the world of art is to abandon the sense that what’s important is one’s personal psychological agony (or at least to hope to do so: Eliot’s poet only wants to escape from personality), to immerse oneself as a poet and creator, if one can still retain this term, in that which is infinitely more vast than one is oneself.

嗯，这听起来不太像布鲁姆的理论，但请看布鲁姆的第五个修正比例——苦行（askesis，1150）。他谈到的是，迟来的诗人为了给自己留出空间，为了使自己与众不同而采取的行动。你可能会认为答案是让自己比任何人都更强大。华莱士·史蒂文斯有一首精彩的诗，叫做《兔子是幽灵之王》，诗中兔子不断膨胀，或者自认为膨胀，直到它变得如此巨大，占据了所有空间。我总是把这只兔子想象成布鲁姆所说的迟来的诗人，但苦行（askesis）却带来了截然不同的结果，尽管最终目的可能相同。

Well, that doesn’t sound very Bloomian, but look at Bloom’s fifth revisionary ratio, askesis (1150). He’s talking about what the belated poet does in order to find space for himself, to make himself different from other people. You’d think the answer would be to make yourself bigger than anybody. Wallace Stevens has a wonderful poem called “Rabbit as King of the Ghosts,” in which the rabbit swells, or thinks it swells, until it is so big that it takes up all space. I always think of that rabbit as Bloom’s belated poet, but with askesis something very different happens, though perhaps to this same end.

在对“苦行”（askesis）的定义进行到一半时，布鲁姆说道：“（诗人）放弃了一部分自身的人性天赋和想象力。”换句话说，他克制自己；他让自己变得不如他本可以成为的那样——当然，是为了超越他曾经的成就。他放弃了一部分自身的人性天赋和想象力，以便将自己与他人（包括先驱者）区分开来。因此，在苦行（askesis）中——顺便一提，在虚己（kenosis）中也是如此——对于这些针对先驱者的强烈误读而言，都存在着一种自我收缩或自我消解。换句话说，这不仅仅是兔子作为幽灵之王的问题。这也不是一个巨大的自我膨胀到占据所有空间的问题。它比这复杂得多，而正是这种复杂性，坦率地说，更像艾略特的风格。

About halfway through the definition of askesis, Bloom says, “[The poet] yields up part of his own human and imaginative endowment.” In other words, he curtails himself; he makes himself less than he might have been—in order, to be sure, to be more than he has been. He yields up part of his own human and imaginative endowment so as to separate himself from others, including the precursor. Thus in askesis—and also in kenosis, by the way—there is a self-shrinking or self-effacement on the part of these particular moves of strong misreading with respect to the precursor. It’s not, in other words, just a question of the rabbit as king of the ghosts. It’s not a question of a massive ego swelling to the point where it fills all space. It is more complicated than that, and in being more complicated it is frankly more Eliot-like.

顺便一提，布鲁姆从未为使用男性代词而道歉。他会说，或者说，一个精通性别语言的辩护者会说（当然，我们稍后会再谈到性别问题），诗人的性别是男性化的，但任何女性都可以成为诗人。例如，布鲁姆就认为艾米莉·狄金森是一位杰出的诗人。这种理论的男性化性别设定是基于俄狄浦斯情结的理念，即父子之间的竞争，而弗洛伊德本人也一直因此受到批评。

The masculine pronoun, by the way, is something that Bloom has never apologized for. What he would say, or what an apologist who speaks the language of gender would say (we’ll be coming back to gender, of course), is that a poet is gendered masculine but that any woman can be a poet. Bloom does think of Emily Dickinson, for example, as a strong poet. The masculine gendering of the theory is modeled on the idea of Oedipal conflict, a father-son rivalry that Freud himself is always likewise being criticized for.

现在直接谈谈布鲁姆，不再过多地与其他诗人比较：他的创作生涯始终贯穿着诗人之间关系的斗争感。在他早期的作品——雪莱的《神话的创造》、布莱克的《启示录》和《幻象公司》——中，这种斗争的理念体现在布鲁姆所谓的“新教主义”之中。他认为，他所感兴趣的传统兴起于宗教改革时期，正如我在诠释学简史中所述，人们开始在与《圣经》和上帝的联系中感受到某种个人化的体验。这也是人类个体性开始变得重要的时期——许多人将其与资产阶级的兴起联系起来。在那一刻，新教主义的理念——正如劳伦斯·达雷尔笔下的一个人物所说，“我对此表示抗议”——营造了一种氛围，在这种氛围中，每位诗人都感到自己独立于以往的文学模式之外。在布鲁姆早期作品中，“新教徒”一词逐渐被“修正主义者”所取代，后者是他主要在《远见卓识的公司》一书中使用的词汇。在弗洛伊德的帮助下，“修正主义”又进一步演变为“误读”。

Turning now to Bloom directly, no longer so much in comparison with others: his career has always involved a sense of struggle in the relationship among poets. In his earliest work—Shelley’s Mythmaking, Blake’s Apocalypse, and The Visionary Company—the idea of struggle was embodied in what Bloom called Protestantism. He saw the tradition that interested him arising in relation to the Reformation, that time when, as I said in my thumbnail history of hermeneutics, people began to feel something personal in their connection to the Bible and to God. This was the time also when human individuality came to matter—the time associated by many others with the emergence of the bourgeoisie. In that moment, the idea of Protestantism—purely in the sense, as a character in Lawrence Durrell says, “that I protest”—creates an atmosphere in which each poet feels independent of previous literary models. The word “Protestant” gives way in early Bloom to the word “revisionary,” the word he uses primarily in The Visionary Company. With the aid of Freud, revisionism gives way in turn to “misreading.”

令人惊讶的是，布鲁姆并非首次提出作家之间存在俄狄浦斯情结的冲突这一概念，这一点我们可以通过回顾批评史中一些相关的段落来观察。前两段出自朗基努斯之手，他可能是公元二世纪一位罗马青年的导师，我引用他的《论崇高》一文：

Surprisingly enough, the notion of Oedipal struggle among authors is not new to Bloom, as we can observe in reviewing a few passages taken from the whole span of the history of criticism. The first two are by Longinus, probably a second-century tutor of a Roman youth, whose On the Sublime I quote:

仿佛本能地（在崇高之时），我们的灵魂被真正的崇高所提升。（到目前为止，这应该是每个人都会说的话。）它骄傲地飞翔，充满喜悦和自豪（而这正是令人惊讶之处），仿佛它自己创造了它所听到的东西（斜体字为笔者所加）。
As if instinctively [this is in the moment of the sublime] our soul is uplifted by the true sublime. [Thus far that’s what you would expect anybody to say.] It takes a proud flight and is filled with joy and vaunting [and this is where the surprise comes] as though it had itself produced what it has heard [italics mine].

当他者占据我们时，一种外在的声音将我们带入其中，这种占据在心理上却被体验为对他者的占有。在我的幻想中，那是我自己的言语。一个孩子在看球赛，有人打出了本垒打，孩子欣喜若狂，挥舞着想象中的球棒，仿佛那是他自己击出的。他是英雄。朗吉努斯说，文学中的崇高也是如此，这给布鲁姆产生了强烈的影响。

A possession by the other takes place, as an external voice transports us, yet this is experienced psychologically as possession of the other. In my fantasy, it’s my own speech. A child watches a ball game, somebody hits a home run, and the child in his exultation starts swinging an imaginary bat as though he had hit it himself. He is the hero. Longinus says it’s the same with literary sublimity, exerting thereby a strong influence on Bloom.

我认为朗吉努斯在下一段话中的观点确实很有道理：柏拉图不断地贬低荷马，然而，要证明荷马的伟大事迹乃至比喻如何塑造柏拉图的思想，却易如反掌。这是一个引人入胜的话题，而朗吉努斯的观点在我看来完全正确：“如果柏拉图没有全心全意地与荷马争夺首位，他的哲学理论就不会如此臻于完美。”朗吉努斯甚至用布鲁姆式的思维来思考，即即使内心深处知道自己屈居第二，仍然渴望成为第一。柏拉图为了争夺首位而奋斗，“或许过于热衷于争论，与荷马如同断矛一般，但即便如此，他也从这场较量中获益匪浅；正如赫西俄德所说，‘这种斗争对凡人有益。’”

I think that what Longinus says in the next passage is actually quite true: Plato is constantly abusing Homer, yet nothing can be easier than to show how the great Homeric actions and even tropes help shape Platonic thought. It’s a fascinating topic, and Longinus, it seems to me, is exactly right about it: “There would not have been so fine a bloom of perfection on Plato’s philosophical doctrines unless he had with all his heart and mind struggled with Homer for primacy.” Longinus even thinks in Bloomian terms of wanting to be first even though in some part of your mind you know you’re second. Plato struggles for primacy, “showing perhaps too much love of contention and breaking a lance with [Homer], as it were, but deriving some profit from the contest nonetheless; for as Hesiod says, ‘This strife is good for mortals.’ ”

更常见的例子来自圣伯夫的著名文章《何谓经典？》，这同样是布鲁姆理论的雏形。关于“何谓经典？”的文章由来已久，艾略特在1944年就写过一篇佳作，这些文章都对影响理论做出了重要贡献。圣伯夫写道：

The more commonplace example, taken from a famous essay by Sainte-Beuve called “What Is a Classic?,” is again proto-Bloomian. There’s a tradition of essays called “What Is a Classic?” Eliot wrote a great one in 1944, and they’re all important contributions to the theory of influence. Sainte-Beuve writes:

歌德说得没错，拜伦虽然才华横溢，诗意盎然，却害怕莎士比亚在人物塑造和实现方面比自己更胜一筹（的确，拜伦总是贬低莎士比亚）。他本想否认这一点。莎士比亚那种超脱于自我之外的境界令他感到恼火（这是歌德的说法）。他觉得，一旦靠近莎士比亚，自己就永远无法自在地展现自我。他从未否认过蒲柏，因为他并不畏惧蒲柏。他知道，蒲柏（你知道蒲柏个子矮）不过是他身旁的一堵矮墙。
Goethe spoke the truth when he remarked that Byron, great by the flow and source of poetry, feared that Shakespeare was more powerful than himself [it’s true, Byron was always abusing Shakespeare] in the creation and realization of his characters. He would have liked to deny it. The elevation so free from [this is Goethe talking] egoism irritated him. He felt when near it that he could never display himself at ease. He never denied Pope because he did not fear him. He knew that Pope was [and you know how short Pope was] only a low wall by his side.

换句话说，拜伦选择了一个他认为不如自己（至少在创作力上不如自己）的人作为他的文学典范（他称此人为“安妮女王的小人物”），同时不断否认莎士比亚对他的强大影响，并持续与莎士比亚、对莎士比亚的崇拜以及对《哈姆雷特》的过誉争论不休。他选择了一个较弱的先驱，而不是一个强大的先驱。

In other words, Byron chose as his literary model somebody he supposed inferior to himself, at least in creative energy (“the little Queen Anne’s man,” he called him), while constantly denying a very powerful influence, quarreling constantly with Shakespeare, bardolatry, and the overrating of Hamlet. He chose a weak precursor instead of a strong precursor.

除了词汇和思想的哲学广度之外，布鲁姆论证的复杂性还在于我一开始提出的问题：即影响的传统观念，即艺术与自然的问题，而布鲁姆对此非常清楚。从某种意义上说，影响危机关乎人们对自然的取向；而从另一个意义上说，这显然是布鲁姆更关注的层面，危机则关乎人们对其他文本的取向。但请注意，布鲁姆并非始终都想把问题仅仅归结为文本本身（1157）：“弗洛伊德的弟子奥托·兰克更深刻地意识到艺术家与艺术的斗争，以及这种斗争与艺术家与自然的对立斗争之间的关系。”换句话说，自然即死亡。如果作者无法在对自然生命周期的优先性和优越性的主张中站稳脚跟，那么他最终将以死亡的形式回归自然。

What complicates Bloom’s argument, apart from the vocabulary and the philosophical range of his thought, is the issue I began with: the traditional idea of influence as an art-nature problem, of which Bloom is very much aware. In one sense, the crisis of influence concerns one’s orientation to nature, and in another sense, apparently the more prominent sense in Bloom, the crisis concerns one’s orientation to other texts. But notice that Bloom really doesn’t want to say at all times that it’s just about texts (1157): “Freud’s disciple, Otto Rank, show[s] a greater awareness of the artist’s fight against art, and of the relation of this struggle to the artist’s antithetical battle against nature.” In other words, nature is death. Nature is that into which the author will fall back in the form of death should he fail to sustain himself in the triumph of his assertion of priority and superiority to the life cycle in nature.

布鲁姆想要强调的是，迟来的诗人所追求的，部分原因在于不朽。作为先行者，对前人一无所知，意味着你也将是最后的，意味着你将永生，意味着你不属于寻常的人生轨迹。你是一种超越历史的力量、天才或能量。正如布鲁姆所说，这正是诗人“对抗时间的谎言”，他们既在抗拒死亡，又坚持认为，人既不受优先顺序的约束，也不受起源的束缚。

Bloom wants to insist that in part what the belated poet struggles for is immortality. Part of what it means to come first and to know nothing that was there before you is to suppose that you are also going to be last, that you’re going to be immortal, that you don’t belong in an ordinary trajectory of life. You are a force, genius, or power that transcends history. Here we find the poets’ “lie against time,” as Bloom calls it, holding off death while insisting, too, that one is touched neither by priority nor even genesis.

为了快速说明这一点，我们不妨看看华兹华斯，这位对弥尔顿作品理解有误且成书较晚的诗人。他在一首我们现在称之为《致“隐士”的序言》的许愿诗中写道，他对创作《失乐园》毫无兴趣。对他而言，《失乐园》不过是陈旧过时的东西。他声称对弥尔顿所关注的事物漠不关心：“一切力量——一切恐惧，无论是单个的还是成群的，/ 曾经以人格形式展现的，/ 耶和华——带着他的雷霆，带着/ 天使的合唱，带着帝王的宝座——/ 我都毫不畏惧地走过。”《失乐园》，对他来说不过是玩弄玩具兵罢了。与华兹华斯本人即将做的事相比，这简直微不足道：“混沌，/ 即使是最黑暗的厄瑞玻斯深渊，/ 也绝非梦境所挖掘出的/ 盲目的空虚—— 也无法孕育出如此的恐惧和敬畏，/ 当我们审视自身，审视人类的心灵时，/ 便会涌上心头——/ 我的栖息之地，我歌唱的主要领域。” 上帝、天堂、地狱、战争、神话、古老的英雄主义——所有这些都让位于真正且唯一的主题——“人类的心灵”，它不会带来重蹈自然界饥渴世代覆辙的风险，因为这不是我的心灵，而是心灵本身，它在我的歌声中不受时间的影响。

To illustrate this very quickly, let’s turn to Wordsworth, the key strong misreader and belated poet with respect to Milton, who writes in a promissory poem that we now call “The Prospectus to ‘The Recluse’ ” that he is not interested in writing Paradise Lost. Paradise Lost for him is just archaic, a thing of the past. He claims indifference to the things Milton cares about: “All strength–all terror, single or in bands,/ That ever was put forth in personal form,/ Jehovah– with his thunder, and the choir/ Of shouting angels, and the imperial thrones–/ I pass them unalarmed.” Paradise Lost, that’s just playing with toy soldiers. It’s nothing compared with what Wordsworth himself is going to do: “Not chaos,/ Not the darkest pit of lowest Erebus,/ Nor aught of blinder vacancy, scooped out/ By help of dreams–can breed such fear and awe/ As fall upon us often when we look/ Into our minds, into the mind of man–/ My haunt, and the main region of my song.” God, heaven, hell, war, myth, archaic heroism—all these give way to the true and only subject, “the mind of man,” which doesn’t entail the risk of falling back into the hungry generations of nature because it is not my mind, it’s the mind, immune to time in my voice.

啊，但看看那破旧不堪的古老《失乐园》：这里有撒旦的三段宣言。布鲁姆继布莱克和雪莱之后（他们也曾提出过同样的观点），认为华兹华斯的有力先驱与其说是弥尔顿，不如说是撒旦：“心灵自有其境，它本身/能将地狱化为天堂，将天堂化为地狱。”显然，撒旦正在撰写《隐士》的序言，因为这正是华兹华斯的主张。“我们不知何时，”撒旦对堕落的亡灵们说，“我们与现在截然不同。”这正是这位迟来的诗人一直努力想要表达的。最后，“我即地狱。”这话说起来令人不安，但这仍然是鬼王之王——兔子——在说话：“我的栖身之处，我歌唱的主要领域”，心灵即万物。

Ah, but look at tatty old, archaic Paradise Lost: here are three proclamations by Satan. Following Blake and Shelley, who had made the same claim, Bloom says it’s not so much Milton who is Wordsworth’s strong precursor, it’s Satan: “The mind is its own place and in itself/ Can make a heaven of hell, a hell of heaven.” Apparently, Satan is writing “The Prospectus to ‘The Recluse,’ ” because that’s Wordsworth’s claim. “We know no time,” Satan tells the fallen legions, “when we were not as now.” That’s what the belated poet always strives to say. And finally, “Myself am hell.” That’s rather an uncomfortable thing to say, but still, it’s the rabbit as king of the ghosts talking: “my haunt and the main region of my song,” it is the mind that is all things.

因此，华兹华斯严重误读了《失乐园》，误以为自己在创作全新的作品，却揭示了这位伟大的先驱诗人早已写出了后继诗人所能写的一切。这种在传承与创新之间动态博弈的现象，在任何反映出影响焦虑的时刻都存在。

Wordsworth, then, has strongly misread Paradise Lost in order to think he’s doing something completely new, while revealing that the strong precursor poet has always already written anything that the successor poet can write. The dynamic interplay between conservation and innovation is present in any moment that reflects the anxiety of influence.

是时候重温托尼拖车的故事了。对拉康而言，托尼拖车代表着意识安于“小客体”（ objet peti tà），也就是小汽车邦比。邦比虽不完美，却乐于助人，是个朋友——“这才叫朋友”——而欲望的对象，比如尼托和斯皮迪，嗯，它们可不是什么好车。正如布鲁克斯所说，这些欲望对象表面上看是不恰当的选择。美国自我心理学家也会这么说，但用布努埃尔式的语言来说，尼托和斯皮迪是模糊的欲望对象，它们在路上行驶，对托尼而言根本就不是选择的对象。所以，尼托和斯皮迪是“大他者”，而邦比则是“小客体”。

High time we returned to Tony the Tow Truck. For Lacan, Tony the Tow Truck represents consciousness settling for the objet peti tà, little Bumpy the Car, an imperfect being but a helpful one and a friend—“that’s what I call a friend”—whereas the objects of desire, Neato and Speedy, well, those are bad cars. As Brooks would say, these objects of desire are improper object choices on the face of it. That’s what an American ego psychologist would say, too, but Neato and Speedy are, in a more Buñuelesque way of putting it, obscure objects of desire as they motor on down the road, simply unavailable to Tony as object choices at all. So Neato and Speedy are the big Other, and Bumpy is the object petit à.

在哈罗德·布鲁姆看来，《拖车托尼》是对《小火车头的故事》的严重误读。最明显的例子是，在《小火车头的故事》中，真正的英雄是邦比，而不是托尼。这种对原著的误读，将托尼塑造成了需要邦比帮助的英雄。从民间故事的角度来看，邦比成了帮助者而非英雄，但我们仍然可以看到，故事的核心叙事模式——弱者凭借毅力和活力完成强者未能完成之事——反映了强者和弱者之间的关系。邦比出现之后，我们再也无法用同样的眼光看待托尼这个角色了，然而邦比正是《小火车头的故事》中的英雄，而托尼在这部作品中却占据了这一主角的位置。因此，这种关系又是一种对抗关系，涉及英雄主义从一个角色的焦点转移到另一个角色的焦点，同时——正如任何给孩子读过这两个故事的人都能认识到的那样——只是以一种《小火车头的故事》完全预料到的方式重写了故事。

For Harold Bloom, Tony the Tow Truck is a strong misreading of The Little Engine That Could. This is clearest in that Bumpy, not Tony, plays the role of the hero of The Little Engine That Could. The misreading of the belated text involves making Tony the hero in need of Bumpy’s help. In folkloric terms, Bumpy becomes the helper and not the hero, but we can see nonetheless that the essential narrative model—the model of the weak doing with perseverance and energy what the strong fail to do—reflects on the strong and the weak. We can’t ever read the character Tony in quite the same way again after the appearance of Bumpy, yet Bumpy is nothing other than the hero of The Little Engine That Could, a subject position that has been appropriated by Tony in this text. So the relationship is again an agonistic one involving the transposition of heroism from one character focus to another while at the same time—as anybody can recognize who has read both stories to their kids—simply rewriting the story in a way that The Little Engine That Could completely anticipates.

在下一讲中，我们将回到拉康的领域，学习德勒兹、加塔利，特别是斯拉沃热·齐泽克。

We shall return now to more Lacanian pastures when we study Deleuze and Guattari and especially Slavoj Žižek in the next lecture.

 

 

第十五章

CHAPTER 15

后现代心理
The Postmodern Psyche

阅读材料：

Readings:

德勒兹，吉尔，和费利克斯·加塔利。“导论：根茎。”载于《千高原：资本主义与精神分裂症》。明尼阿波利斯：明尼苏达大学出版社，1987 年。

Deleuze, Gilles, and Félix Guattari. “Introduction: Rhizome.” In A Thousand Plateaus: Capitalism and Schizophrenia. Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press, 1987.

齐泽克，斯拉沃伊。“宫廷爱情。”载于《批评传统》，第 1181-1197 页。

Žižek, Slavoj. “Courtly Love.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1181–1197.

本次讲座我们仍将聚焦于个体意识，即便你们阅读的作者以其政治参与而闻名。我们仍将探讨文本或电影的心理起源，将其视为文本符号模式的场所或模型——这在齐泽克的作品中无疑如此，在德勒兹的作品中也有一定程度的体现。这实际上是我们对心理学重点的告别，之所以如此安排——并将齐泽克与拉康区分开来——是因为当今的作者们确保我们理解，艺术和阐释中蕴含着政治意义。

In this lecture, we’re still focused on individual consciousness, even though the authors you read are known for their political engagements. We shall still be considering the psychological genesis of the text or film as the site, or model, for the symbolic patterning of a text, undoubtedly in the case of Žižek, to some extent also in that of Deleuze. This is actually our farewell to the psychological emphasis, and it is so arranged—with the consequence of separating Žižek from Lacan—because today’s authors make sure we understand that there are political stakes in art and interpretation.

例如，齐泽克在其对《哭泣的游戏》的精彩解读中指出，情节的最终转折并非仅仅是个人放弃了对爱尔兰共和事业的责任。这位士兵并非只是离开了他在革命活动中的角色；他已在私生活中——在他意识的情欲维度中——发现了内心深处革命的必要性。他必然以一种与支持爱尔兰共和运动所需的思维颠覆同样激进且密切相似的方式颠覆了自己的思维。因此，最终与“大他者”的悲剧性遭遇与主人公行为的政治含义密不可分。

In his brilliant reading of The Crying Game, for example, Žižek argues that the final twist of plot isn’t just an individual’s abdication from responsibility for the Irish Republican cause. The soldier has not merely walked away from his role in revolutionary activity; he has discovered in his private life—in the erotic dimension of his consciousness—the need for revolution from within. He has necessarily disrupted his own thinking in ways equally radical to and closely parallel to the disruption of thinking that’s required to support the Republican movement in Ireland. Thus the ultimately tragic encounter with the Big Other is inseparable from the political implications of the protagonist’s behavior.

或许我们应该对这种说法稍作思考。正如编辑在其斜体字的前言中所指出的，这种对晦涩难懂甚至超凡脱俗的欲望对象的迷恋，对个人而言固然存在诱惑，但对社会心理而言也同样存在诱惑。如果将政治理想视为遥不可及之物，这无疑会令人沮丧，尽管或许并非不切实际。此外，齐泽克的作品中也展现出一种令人惊讶的对宗教的友好态度。毕竟，信仰，或者说对信仰的追求，无疑是一种努力，试图与自己渴望却无法面对面接触的事物建立有意义的联系。然而，问题在于齐泽克承认，无论是宗教还是政治，都存在着令人兴奋之处，但沉迷于宏大理念也可能带来潜在的危险。尽管他总体上属于左翼，并深受马克思的影响，但他有时也会坦言自己的政治思想存在一定程度的不稳定性。然而，他清楚地看到，任何形式的进步集体主义，包括法西斯主义，都带有禁忌愿望的魅力。简而言之，齐泽克意识到，他从拉康那里借鉴的思路，在政治领域带来了令人眩晕的危险可能性。（我最终会再谈到希区柯克的《迷魂记》。）

Perhaps one should be given pause, at least momentarily, by this claim. As your editor points out in his italicized preface, there are temptations entailed for the individual in this fascination with an obscure or even perhaps transcendent object of desire, but there are temptations also for the social psyche. It would be discouraging, arguably, though perhaps not unrealistic, if a political ideal were considered precisely what one cannot have. There is also in Žižek’s work a rather surprising friendliness toward religion. After all, faith, or the struggle for faith, certainly counts as an effort to enter into a meaningful relationship with what one desires yet cannot meet face to face. But what remains problematic is Žižek’s recognition that in both religion and politics there is excitement but also potential danger in becoming fascinated by a big idea. There are moments when he confesses to a measure of instability in his own political thinking, even though he is by and large on the left and heavily influenced by Marx. He sees clearly, however, that any form of progressive collectivity, including fascism, brings with it the charisma of a forbidden wish. Žižek is aware, in short, that the train of thought he borrows from Lacan brings with it a vertigo of dangerous possibilities in the political arena. (I’ll be coming back to Hitchcock’s Vertigo eventually.)

德勒兹的思想中也蕴含着强烈的政治维度。（我通常会用“德勒兹”而非“德勒兹和加塔利”——费利克斯·加塔利是他的长期合作者——正如我用“温萨特”而非“温萨特和比尔兹利”一样。）你现在读的是他的著作《千高原》的第一章，在这一章中，他提出了一种思想实验，这一建议也体现在本章的结构之中。德勒兹指出，我们需要在思想层面进行一场所谓的“内在革命”，但正如齐泽克所言，其对政治的影响却有些模糊不清。也就是说，这种“根茎式”的思维模式——我们稍后会再谈到——它彻底地去中心化，从而有利于多元化的、渐进民主的事业，但它或许也更倾向于民主之外的自由主义，而非法西斯主义或共产主义。

There is also an emphatic political dimension in Deleuze. (For the most part, I shall be saying “Deleuze” rather than “Deleuze and Guattari”—Félix Guattari was his frequent collaborator—just as I said “Wimsatt” rather than “Wimsatt and Beardsley.”) You are reading the first chapter of his book, A Thousand Plateaus, in which he proposes a kind of thought experiment, a recommendation to the reader that is echoed by the organization of the chapter itself. Deleuze indicates the need to perform in thought what you might call a revolution from within, but the implications for politics, as in Žižek, are somewhat ambiguous. That is to say, the “rhizomatic” mode of thinking—we’ll come back to that—which is radically decentering and thereby lends itself to pluralistic, progressively democratic causes, may lend itself likewise not so much perhaps to fascism or communism as to libertarianism at the far side of democracy.

德勒兹确实谨慎地指出，根茎式思维既有好的一面，也有坏的一面。老鼠是根茎，马唐草也是根茎。换句话说，任何没有主根、以分散方式组织自身的事物，无论如何，都是根茎式的。不过，总的来说，正如我稍后会更详细地解释的那样，在德勒兹看来，根茎式思维总体上是有益的。无论如何，齐泽克和德勒兹都在引入新的思维可能性——截然不同的可能性——并且坦诚地承认，他们并不完全清楚这些可能性会将他们引向何方。除了暗示某种程度的解放之外，他们并没有说明成功进入他们的思维世界会带来哪些影响或后果。

Deleuze is indeed careful to point out that rhizomatic thinking takes place both for the best and worst. Rats are rhizomes. Crabgrass is a rhizome. In other words, everything that organizes itself dispersively without a taproot is rhizomatic, no matter what. On the whole, though, as I’ll try to explain more carefully later, rhizomatic thinking is for the good in Deleuze’s view. In any case, however, both Žižek and Deleuze are introducing new possibilities of thought—very different possibilities—and are candid enough to admit that they don’t quite know where these possibilities are taking them. Beyond implying a measure of liberation, they don’t say what the implications or consequences of successfully entering their thought worlds might be.

我即将探讨这两位思想自由、甚至可以说是特立独行的思想家之间的理论联系，但此刻我需要强调他们之间巨大的差异。德勒兹的思想实验源于树状或“树状”的思维模式（有趣的是，他必须努力避免在其隐喻中使用“激进”一词的根本含义）；而齐泽克则有时关注欲望和需求的符号学穷尽之后所剩下的东西，他想要发展他关于“污点”的奇特概念——叙事话语中无法解释、无法被赋予意义的元素。很难找到任何共同点。（我这样阐述齐泽克的计划，部分借鉴了布鲁克斯的观点——布鲁克斯通过拉康与D.A.米勒关于“可叙述性”的理论建立了联系——但对齐泽克而言，拉康关于“实在”的理论则处于次要地位。）由此可见，他们之间存在着分歧；人们很容易会说这是不可通约之处。但请注意，这两个项目都在努力接近一种超越某种乏味或可预测性的现实，这种乏味或可预测性侵蚀着常规的意义模式：例如，与德里达的“先验所指”不无关联的树状结构，或是迷失在陈词滥调和既定观念丛林中的想象的组合逻辑，甚至是拉康的象征性。德勒兹和齐泽克共同提出了当代陌生化的形式。

I’m about to suggest what the connection is in theory between these two very free spirits, not to say loose cannons, but for the moment I need to stress the enormous differences between them. Deleuze’s thought experiment departs from the tree or “arboresque” model of thinking (interesting, perhaps, that he must strain to avoid the root sense of “radical” among his metaphors); while Žižek, focused at times on what is left over when the semiotics of desire and need is exhausted, wants to develop his curious notion of the blot—the element in narrative discourse that can’t be interpreted, can’t be said to have meaning. Hard to find any common ground there. (I partly invoke Brooks in putting Žižek’s project this way—with Brooks’s intermediary link to Lacan, D. A. Miller on “the narratable”—but for Žižek, Lacan on “the real” stands in the background.) There are points of divergence here, then; one is tempted to say points of incommensurability. But notice that both of these projects are striving to approximate a reality beyond a certain tedium or predictability that infects normal modes of signification: the arboresque, which is not unrelated to the “transcendental signified” in Derrida, or the combinatory logics of the imaginary, lost in a thicket of cliché and received ideas, and even the symbolic in Lacan. In common, Deleuze and Žižek are proposing latter-day forms of defamiliarization.

当你阅读这两篇文风轻快活泼的文章时，你会发现它们在情绪、立场或对批评和理论先例的态度上有着共通之处。它们似乎都出自同一时代。你甚至可以想象，如果仅仅从风格上看，这两篇文章出自同一人之手。当然，也许并非如此；然而，从这两篇文章中感受到的那种高能量、略带亢奋的氛围，或许会让你不禁思考，这种奔放不羁的风格究竟属于哪个历史时期。

As you read the rather bouncy and frantic prose of both these texts, you can see that they also share a mood, a stance or orientation toward critical and theoretical precedents. They seem to be of the same moment. You could even imagine these two texts being written—if it was just a question of their style—by the same person. Well, perhaps not quite; yet the kind of high-energy, too-caffeinated feeling that you get from the prose of both may cause you to wonder just what historical moment this rambunctiousness belongs to.

你或许已经准备好告诉我它属于哪个时期：没错，“后现代主义”。德勒兹和齐泽克正是这一概念的典型代表，而这一概念无疑是过去二三十年来文化史所面临的最难以捉摸的难题。喜欢它的人会说它灵活多变；不喜欢它的人则会说它晦涩难懂。当我们停下来思考“后现代主义”时，不妨将目光聚焦于这两篇文章。

You may be ready to tell me what moment it belongs to: yes, “postmodernism.” Deleuze and Žižek are exemplars of what is by far the most slippery concept to which cultural history been exposed in the last twenty or thirty years. If one likes it, one wants to say it’s flexible; if one doesn’t like it, one wants to say it’s murky. We can bring both essays into focus as we pause over “postmodernism.”

我们或许可以很快就后现代主义在艺术表达中的含义达成共识。尤其是在视觉艺术领域，但我认为，正如小说、戏剧和诗歌中的某些趋势所反映的那样，后现代主义是一种对过去的折衷主义取向。从某种意义上说，它是对过去的回归，是对传统和历史表达方式的文本可能性的开放，而现代主义由于强调自主形式，曾认为这些传统和历史表达方式已经过时并被弃置一旁。在建筑领域，许多对过去的折衷主义借鉴的例子都非常出色，但也有许多非常丑陋。十五到二十年前，几乎每个商业街都进行了翻新。在此之前，它们都是狭长的扁平盒子，但后来，以后现代主义的名义，翻新者们给这些盒子加上了小山墙，这些山墙本身就很丑陋，而且比例失调——更糟糕的是，这些设计一夜之间就过时了。最可怕的事情发生在郊区牧场住宅上，这一切都打着盲目、平庸地回归传统的旗号，尤其是对帕拉第奥式新古典主义的肆意破坏和拙劣模仿。

Probably we can agree quickly about what postmodernism is in artistic expression. Especially in the visual arts, but I think as reflected in certain trends in fiction, drama, and poetry as well, postmodernism is an eclectic orientation to the past. In a limited sense, it’s a return to the past, an opening up of textual possibility to traditions and historical moments of expression that modernism, with its emphasis on autonomous forms, had supposed obsolete and set aside. In architecture, many examples of eclectic poaching on the past are quite extraordinary, but many are quite hideous. There was a point fifteen or twenty years ago when every strip mall was renovated. Until then they had been long flat boxes, but then in the name of the postmodern, the renovators came along and put little gables on the boxes, intrinsically ugly and out of scale—but what’s worse, old news overnight. The most awful things were done with suburban ranch houses, all in the name of a blind, bland return to tradition, especially to ransack and travesty Palladian neoclassicism.

但后现代主义在其他领域，例如绘画，发挥了不同的作用。自后现代主义兴起以来，纽约的艺术界并非由单一的、占据主导地位的抽象绘画流派相互取代。艺术界的后现代主义绝非对早期运动（例如现实主义）的全盘回归，尽管现实主义也包含在内；它融合了各种元素，包括质疑架上绘画、平面画面等的尖端概念艺术、行为艺术和数字艺术（“杜尚式”）。艺术家们一直执着于自身在艺术史上的地位，但我们在后现代主义旗帜下看到的，并非仅仅是艺术家群体试图将自身置于艺术史的某个特定时期。一种关于艺术本质的无政府主义式的独立思考已经走向全球，并影响了诸如阿瑟·丹托等艺术哲学家的重要著作。

But the postmodern has done its work differently in other fields, such as painting. Since the advent of postmodernism, the New York scene hasn’t consisted in single dominant schools of abstract painting superseding each other. The postmodern in the art world is not at all a wholesale return to earlier movements such as realism, although they’re accommodated; it’s a mixture of everything, including the cutting-edge concept, performance, and digital art (the “Duchampian”) that questions easel art, the flat picture plane, and so on. Artists have always been obsessed with their place in art history, but what we have seen under the banner of the postmodern is not just groups of artists wanting to place themselves with respect to this or that moment of art history. There’s an anarchic independence in thinking about what art is that has gone global and informs such important work in the philosophy of art as that of Arthur Danto.

在哲学中，后现代主义不仅反映了对知识基础的怀疑（例如理查德·罗蒂的观点——我们在本课程中一直在讨论的那种普遍存在的怀疑），而且尤其反映了对部分与整体之间关系的怀疑。我能确定我的腿是我身体的一部分，同时它又是一个整体，而我的脚又是这个整体的一部分吗？我如何才能以任何稳定的方式知道什么是部分或整体，或者说，什么是研究领域（我希望你们能想起德勒兹）？举一个更有趣的例子——这出自维特根斯坦的《哲学研究》——想想法国国旗，它被称为三色旗。它由蓝、白、红三色条纹组成。作为一个整体，它们具有象征意义。然而，蓝、白、红三色并非仅仅局限于这块布料上它们作为一个整体的共生关系。那条细细的白条纹是白色的一部分，是白色概念的一部分。如果你在不了解三色旗的构成的情况下观察它，又怎能断言白色是整体的一部分呢？你可以说白色是一个独立的实体，碰巧被人与蓝色和红色缝合在一起。我们不禁要问，我们究竟是如何知道一个实体是什么的呢？

In philosophy, postmodernism reflects doubt not just about the grounds of knowledge, as in, say, Richard Rorty—the widespread sorts of doubt that we have been discussing more or less continuously in this course—but doubt in particular about the relationship between or among parts and wholes. Can I be sure that my leg is part of my body when at the same time it is a whole of which my foot is a part? How is it that I know in any stable way what a part or a whole is, or what therefore a field of inquiry is (here especially I hope you’re reminded of Deleuze)? To take a more interesting example—this is from Wittgenstein’s Philosophical Investigations—consider the French flag, which is called the tricolor. It’s made up of three color stripes: blue, white, and red. As a composite, they have symbolic value. Yet blue, white, and red aren’t confined to their symbiosis on this piece of cloth, viewed as a whole. The little stripe of white is part of whiteness, the concept of white. And if you look at the tricolor without knowing what it is, how can you say in any case that the white is part of a whole? You could say that the white is an autonomous entity that somebody happens to have sewn together with the blue entity and the red entity. We have to wonder how we know what an entity is.

哲学思考深受视觉隐喻的影响。我们假定自己对现实有清晰的感知，因为我们能够看到它。但我们是如何看到它的呢？眼睛的聚焦能力，以及由此导致的“事物”（被认为是独立实体）轮廓的模糊和清晰呈现，都值得我们铭记。如果你过于仔细地观察某物，比如一张脸，你所看到的只是点，就像自然界中的毛囊或屏幕上的像素，一幅视网膜上的马克·托比画作；如果你离得太远（正如我们所说，“远到无法分辨”），你所看到的只是一片模糊，或者齐泽克所说的“污点”。如果你看着某物然后闭上眼睛，它也会变成一幅视网膜上的马克·托比画作。如果你坐在喷气式飞机上向下看，你看到的景象当然看起来有形状和结构，但这与你站在地面上看到的景象截然不同，即使你站在平坦的平原上，视野几乎和从飞机上看到的一样开阔。这根本不是“视角”的问题，也不是“从多个角度观察同一事物”的问题。你的视觉呈现的是完全不同的“事物”。

Philosophical thinking is dominated by metaphors of vision. We assume that we have a clear sense of reality because we can see it. But how do we see it? The focusing capacities of the eye, resulting in the arbitrariness with which “things” (presumed to be independent entities) come in and out of clear outline, is worth remembering. If you look too closely at something, a face, for example, all you can see is dots, follicles in nature or pixels on-screen, a retinal Mark Tobey painting; if you are too far away (“too far away to discriminate,” as we say), all you can see is a blur, or Žižek’s “blot.” If you look at something and close your eyes, that too becomes a retinal Mark Tobey painting. If you’re in a jet looking down, what you see certainly looks like it has form and structure, but it’s a completely different form and structure from what you’re seeing if you’re standing on the ground, even if you’re on a flat plain and can see almost as much looking out to the horizon as you could see from the jet. It’s not at all just a question of “perspective,” of looking at “the same thing from more than one angle.” Your vision is constituting entirely different “things.”

我继续这段冗长的题外话，希望它并非真正的题外话，而是对今天阅读内容的一种解释。部分与整体的混淆也困扰着科学史。在直线加速器的黄金时代，亚原子粒子之间的关系发生了逆转：人们曾认为的基本单元粒子，在加速器的轰击下，竟然被发现其内部包含着另一个基本单元，而它本身也是这个基本单元的一部分！

I continue this long digression in hopes that it’s not really a digression but a way of accounting for today’s reading. Part-whole confusions also beset the history of science. During the golden age of the linear accelerator, the relationship between subatomic particles reversed itself: the particle that was thought to be the fundamental unit turned out to have within it, revealed by bombardment in the accelerator, a fundamental unit of which it was a part!

我们难以界定“整体”的含义，这会带来一些后果。当我们想到“整体”时，我们往往会联想到统一性。如果我们连整体都难以识别，那么我们是否就走错了方向，才会认为事物的本质是统一的、相互融合却又结构清晰的呢？德勒兹本人就对统一性避而不谈。他的思想实验的全部意义就在于使事物去中心化，从而使人们无法再谈论统一性、整体或孤立的实体。德勒兹想要强调的是共存、融合、分离、重聚，以及实体（如果它们还能被称为实体的话）的动性或运动。

The difficulty that we have deciding what a whole is has consequences. When we think of a whole, we infer unity. If then we have trouble identifying wholes, might we not be on the wrong track in considering the nature of things to be unified, interfused yet firmly articulated structure? Deleuze for one wants nothing to do with unity. The whole function of his thought experiment is the decentering of things such that one can no longer talk about unities or wholes or isolated entities. It’s the being together, merging together, flying apart, reuniting, and kinesis or movement of entities, if they can even be called entities, that Deleuze wants to emphasize.

后现代主义的另一个方面，是后现代哲学家让-弗朗索瓦·利奥塔（Jean- François Lyotard）所称的“非人性”，或者说是人类的非人化。¹我认为选择这个词很奇怪，从某种角度来看甚至有些不妥，因为利奥塔的倾向并非反人道主义。尽管它确实强调了非人化的历史暴行（毕竟，这正是选择这个词的原因），但“非人性”实际上是一种重新认识人类的方式。你会注意到，德勒兹——不仅在这段摘录中，而且在他的所有作品中——都谈到了“没有器官的身体”（这也是为什么他在这里对此解释甚少的原因）。这或许会让你感到困惑。它暗示着，正如德勒兹所说，我们是机械的，而非有机的。如果以中心视角看待事物的问题在于它将一切都视为树木，视为一棵根深蒂固的大树，那么这个问题在某种程度上源于我们认为树木的各个部分都具有人体器官的特征。根和枝是肌肉和循环系统；树叶是毛细血管；花朵是生殖器；树冠或树荫是树木伸向天空的心灵，是树木的精神。同样地，如果我们把自己的身体想象成树木，我们就会认为身体的某些部分具有认知功能，而其他部分则具有自主性，能够做事。如果是这样，那么我们就会认为以中心视角、最终以生殖器或基因为基础的身体理解是富有成效的。

Another aspect of the postmodern is what the postmodern philosopher Jean-François Lyotard, in particular, has called “the inhuman,” or the dehumanization of the human.1 This is a weird term to choose, I think from one viewpoint an unfortunate one, because Lyotard’s drift is not at all anti-humanistic. Although it does keep in focus the historical atrocities of dehumanization (and this is, after all, why the term is chosen), “the inhuman” is really a new way of appreciating the human. Deleuze, you’ll notice—not just in this excerpt but everywhere in his work, which is why he has so little to say about it here that’s explanatory—talks about “bodies without organs.” That may have brought you up short. What it suggests is that we are, as Deleuze would put it, machinic rather than organic. If the problem with centered thought is that it approaches everything as arboresque, as a rooted tree, that problem has to some extent to do with the fact that we consider a tree to have human organs for parts. The roots and branches are muscles and circulation; the leaves are capillaries; the blossoms are genitals; the crown or canopy of leaves is the mind of the tree reaching up to the sky, the mentality of the tree. By the same token, if we think of our own bodies as arboreal, we think of certain parts of those bodies as cognitive, other parts as having agency, as doing things. If that’s the case, then we think of a centered and ultimately genital or genetic understanding of the body as being productive.

德勒兹希望将身体视为一种互动的存在。在德勒兹看来，身体无处不在，又无处可寻，它游离于其他流动性之中，对周围环境的各个方面都保持着敏感和功能性的互动。为了实现这一点，身体（无器官的部分）与其他事物之间的交互必须是主动的，无需操纵性的意志，也无需认知意图，例如“我思故我在，我是我而非他者，世界是我所想”。简而言之，后现代主义的非人化并非否定人的重要性，而是重新思考人与其他身体和事物之间的关系。

Deleuze wants to think of the body as interactive. The body in Deleuze is everywhere and nowhere, unsituated among other fluidities, sensitive and functionally interactive at all points with a far-reaching environment. In order for this to happen, the interface with other things of the body without organs has to be active without manipulative will, and also without cognitive intention, such as “I think, therefore I am, myself and not another, and the world is what I think it to be.” In short, the dehumanization of the postmodern results not in denying the importance of the human but in rethinking the human among other bodies and things.

显然，这种强调凸显了一种融入他者性的过程，一种主体与客体之间的连续性，在这种连续性中，最终，内在的、构成我真实自我或不可或缺的本质，与外在的事物之间的差异变得完全渗透和可互换。十九世纪末的作家兼美学哲学家沃尔特·佩特在其著作《文艺复兴》的结论中，预见了德勒兹的许多观点。佩特实际上是说，我们太习惯于认为自己身处“此处”，而其他一切都在“彼处”，并且，不知何故，我们对“彼处”的视角是一种拯救性的隔离，它赋予我们客观性的力量。然后，佩特转述道，我们实际上与外部世界进行着一种生物化学的交换，这种交换能够渗透到事物的分子层面。用他的话说，我们内在的东西也是“使铁生锈，使玉米成熟”的东西。

Plainly, this emphasis stresses a dissolve into otherness, a continuity between subject and object in which the difference, ultimately, between what is inside me, what is authentic or integral to my being me, and what’s outside me become completely permeable and interchangeable. The late nineteenth-century author and aesthetic philosopher Walter Pater, in the conclusion to a book called The Renaissance, anticipated much of what Deleuze has to say. Pater said in effect that we are too much used to thinking that we’re in here, that everything else is out there, and that, somehow or another, our perspective on everything out there is a saving isolation that enables our power of objectivity. Then Pater says, in paraphrase, that we actually subsist in a biochemical interchange with what’s outside of us, permeable to the molecularity of things. What is inside us is also what “rusts iron and ripens corn,” in his words.

德勒兹和加塔利用他们自己激动而跳跃的方式来表达这些概念，但你可以看出，认为我们夸大了意识与其环境的客观隔离，这种说法其实并不新鲜。这种根茎状的、去中心化的思维方式，其关注点正是内外之间的双向渗透性。现在，如果我们回到垂直和水平坐标系，可以说，德勒兹，就像我们读过的许多其他人一样，对将垂直轴虚拟化，甚至消除垂直轴感兴趣：将树的中心、树冠或树形结构（即构成水平轴上展开的一切——无论是语言，还是像语言一样结构的无意识）虚拟化或抹去。

Deleuze and Guattari have their own excited, jumpy way of putting these things, but you can see that it’s not really new to say that we exaggerate the objectifying isolation of consciousness from its surroundings. It is the two-way permeability of inside and outside that this kind of rhizomic, decentered thinking is meant to focus on. Now if we go back to our vertical and horizontal coordinates, we could say that Deleuze, like so many others we’ve read, is interested in rendering virtual, or possibly even eliminating, the vertical axis: rendering virtual or putting under erasure that center or head or crown of the tree, the arboresque, which constitutes everything that unfolds on the horizontal axis—whether it be language or the unconscious structured like a language.

但如今水平轴还剩下什么呢？德勒兹与解构主义的不同之处就在于此，解构主义认为言语，尤其是写作，完全是语言性的。我将仅就这一点，将他与拉康进行比较。你还记得吗？在拉康的《文字的能动性》一文中，他不仅将组合轴描述为一系列同心圆，每个同心圆又由更小的同心圆组成，他还将语言中想象或欲望的组合能力比作五线谱。符号的组织，就其彼此间的邻近性而言，既可以是旋律性的，也可以是和声性的，可以沿着水平轴进行水平和垂直的标记。

But what now remains of the horizontal axis? Here is where Deleuze differs from deconstruction, for which speech and especially writing are exclusively linguistic. I’m going to compare him in this one respect, and only in this respect, with Lacan. You remember that in Lacan’s “Agency of the Letter” essay, he doesn’t just talk about the axis of combination as a series of concentric circles, each of which is made up of little concentric circles. He also compares the combinatory powers of the imaginary in language, or of desire, with a musical staff. The organization of signs, in their contiguity with each other, can be either melodic or harmonic, notated both horizontally and vertically along the horizontal axis.

为了表达这种沿着组合轴线的多层次性，德勒兹和加塔利引入了“高原”的概念。您摘录的这段文字出自一本名为《千高原》的书。最终，对他们而言，高原甚至比根茎更为重要，但当他们引入高原的概念时，他们同样——就像引入根茎一样——将注意力从单一的支配概念转移到多个同时存在的概念上。然而，高原并非仅仅是语言中的多种意义或符号系统。德勒兹和加塔利强调“编码的多元性”，这种思维不仅发生在语言中，而且在语言、图像、音乐、电影以及其他各种编码之间穿梭。这一点也与拉康——以及在拉康看来与弗洛伊德——存在联系。弗洛伊德曾说梦的运作就像一个谜语，拉康便以此作为他语言符号学的模型。这听起来很像德勒兹的“编码的多元性”。

To express this multilayeredness along the axis of combination, Deleuze and Guattari introduce the concept of “plateau.” The book in which your excerpt appears is called A Thousand Plateaus. Ultimately, the plateau is even more important to them than the rhizome, but when they introduce the concept of plateau they’re likewise—as with the rhizome—drawing attention away from a single governing concept to many simultaneous concepts. The plateaus are not, however, simply multiple meanings or sign systems within language. Deleuze and Guattari emphasize “multiplicity of coding,” thinking that does not just take place in language but careens among the verbal, the pictorial, the musical, the filmic, and yet other codes. Here, too, there is a link with Lacan—and with Freud in Lacan’s opinion. Freud having said the dream work is like a rebus, Lacan makes Freud’s observation his model for the semiotics of speech. That sounds a lot like Deleuze’s “multiplicity of coding.”

德勒兹与我们读过的所有人物之间的关系确实相当复杂，尤其是与精神分析的拥护者们。他的前作《千高原》名为《反俄狄浦斯》，是对弗洛伊德“将军”的持续抨击。正如你所料，德勒兹否定俄狄浦斯情结并非因为其本身存在缺陷（这方面有很多其他理论），而是因为它是一种树状的组织原则。德勒兹试图揭示精神分析专注于某一特定议题的局限性及其对精神分析遗产造成的遗憾。你可能会认为，德勒兹会更认同博学多才的拉康，但他是这样评价拉康的（34）：“精神分析的命运与语言学的命运紧密相连，这并不令人惊讶。”乍一看，我们很难判断——或许并非偶然——德勒兹在这里究竟是在影射弗洛伊德还是拉康，因为他是否认真对待了拉康关于无意识结构如同语言的观点，而弗洛伊德在《梦的解析》中也持此观点。但我认为德勒兹只是在回避争论。大家都认同拉康对语言学的关注是对弗洛伊德零散观察的一次大规模（有些人甚至认为是不合理的）修正，而在我看来，德勒兹的真正目标显然是拉康。

Deleuze’s relationship with all the figures we have been reading is rather problematic, really, but it is especially so with the proponents of psychoanalysis. The book preceding A Thousand Plateaus was called Anti-Oedipus, a continuous attack on Freud “the General.” As you can guess, Deleuze rejects the Oedipus complex not so much because it’s flawed in itself (there are plenty of others to do that), but because it’s an arboresque organizational principle. Deleuze sets out to show how limiting and unfortunate for the legacy of psychoanalysis focusing on a particular issue has been. You would think, then, that Deleuze would feel a lot closer to the polyvalent Lacan, but here is what he says about Lacan (34): “[I]t is not surprising that psychoanalysis tied its fate to that of linguistics.” It’s impossible to say on the face of it—probably not by accident—whether Deleuze alludes here to Freud or Lacan if he takes seriously Lacan’s implication that the unconscious is structured like a language because Freud says it is in The Interpretation of Dreams. But I think Deleuze is just avoiding a fight. All agree that Lacan’s focus on linguistics is a massive (some would say unjustified) revision of scattered observations by Freud, and it seems clear to me that Deleuze’s target really is Lacan.

此外，德勒兹的目标超越了精神分析本身，直指语言学。他想以一种在他看来语言学尚未成功容纳的方式来概念化语言。他不断提及诺姆·乔姆斯基，乔姆斯基可以说是本文的反派，正如弗洛伊德是前一本书的反派一样。德勒兹对乔姆斯基的观点——即心灵天生具有一种普遍的、树状的“深层结构”，这种结构是所有语言共有的——抱有敌意，这并不难理解。但我仍然认为，让乔姆斯基代表整个领域，只不过是为了避免谈论索绪尔，从而避免激怒包括拉康在内的所有结构主义者。毕竟，用德勒兹的话来说，索绪尔的问题也在于，他对二元性、对符号任意性的关注同样是树状的，这与德勒兹对符号之间以及符号与其他代码之间相互渗透的兴趣背道而驰。

Additionally, the target beyond psychoanalysis is linguistics itself. Deleuze wants to conceptualize language in a way that no linguistics has successfully accommodated as far as he’s concerned. He keeps talking about Noam Chomsky, who is arguably the villain of this essay, just as Freud was the villain of the previous book. Deleuze’s hostility to Chomsky’s notion that the mind is hardwired for a universal, arboresque “deep structure” common to all languages is not hard to understand. But I still think that making Chomsky stand proxy for the whole field is just a way to avoid talking about Saussure and angering all those structuralists, including Lacan. In Deleuzean terms, after all, the problem with Saussure, too, is that his focus on the binary, on the arbitrary nature of the sign, is likewise arboresque, at odds with Deleuze’s interest in the seepage of signs into each other and into other codes.

那么，我们如何才能认出根茎呢？无论德勒兹的文章给你带来多少困惑，我猜想，从长远来看，你最终会对根茎的概念有相当清晰的认识。如果你还有任何疑问，不妨想想流感。德勒兹称之为“根茎型流感”。这种疾病是从他人那里传染的，而且因为我们几乎都在期中考试前后感染，所以它的传播方式是根茎式的：我们易感，它就找到了传染源。这与黄蜂和兰花之间的关系类似。黄蜂就像病毒一样，在花朵间飞来飞去，落到兰花上，传播花粉。与流感不同的是，还有遗传性疾病——这种疾病潜伏在我们体内，因为我们的基因里就预设了它。德勒兹将这种疾病与树状结构联系起来。它源于某种起源，某种根本原因。根状群落内部各种张力的相互作用——老鼠互相翻滚、洞穴迷宫、马唐草蔓延——这一切都是随机且不可预测的。这是一种自由活动，但不受中心控制，因此不属于结构性活动。

How then do we know a rhizome when we see it? Whatever frustrations Deleuze’s essay puts in your path, I suspect that in the long run you’re pretty clear on what a rhizome is. If you have any doubt, just think about the flu. Deleuze calls it “rhizomatic flu.” It’s something we get from other people, and because we all come down with it around midterm period, the circulation of this disease is rhizomatic: we are vulnerable, it finds its way to us. It parallels the relationship between the wasp and the orchid. The wasp, like the virus, flits about from blossom to blossom, descends, and spreads pollen. By contrast with the flu, there is hereditary disease—that which lurks in us because we’re hardwired for it genetically. This form of disease Deleuze associates with the arboresque. It comes from an origin, a root cause. The give and take of tensions within rhizomatic colonies—the rats tumbling over each other, the maze of the burrow, the spreading of crabgrass—all of this is random and unpredictable. It is free play but not governed by a center, hence not structural.

再次强调，围绕这些比喻的价值体系并非一成不变。它并非简单的“树状结构不好，根茎状结构好”。他的观点已经非常接近这种倾向，但他正如我所说，也承认根茎状结构的弊端。至于树状结构，他通过区分书籍中不同类型的根系，在某种程度上挽救了它。一种是他所谓的“根系书籍”，即传统的书籍，它提出一个主题，并系统地展开论述，同时注重子主题的逻辑顺序。另一种是他所谓的“分册书籍”，其根系错综复杂，但仍然追溯到主根。他将这种书籍与现代主义联系起来。分册书籍就像乔伊斯的《尤利西斯》，包罗万象，无所不包。它乍看之下似乎完全是根茎状的，但实际上却由一个单一的、聚焦的作者意识凝聚而成（想想德曼的“语法修辞化”），因此仍然是一本分册式的书籍，比根茎状的书籍更值得称道，但还称不上突破性的创新。而现在，通过某种宣言，《千高原》将成为一本根茎状的书籍。它是合作的产物，它摒弃了顺序，转而采用层次丰富的结构，它兴高采烈地一次性表达一切，在隐喻之间看似随机、不可预测地穿梭——并非为了唤起某个核心理念或执念，而是为了模仿排列组合本身。至于他们是否成功，就由你来评判吧。

Again, the value system surrounding these metaphors is not fixed. It’s not quite “arboresque bad, rhizomatic good.” He’s coming pretty close to that, but he acknowledges the perils of the rhizomatic, as I’ve said. As to the arboresque, he rescues it in some degree by distinguishing, in speaking of books, between kinds of roots. One is what he calls the “root book,” the traditional book that announces a theme and develops it systematically, with due attention to a logical sequence of subtopics. Then there is what he calls the “fascicle book,” with complicated offshoots of roots that still trace back to a taproot. This is what he associates with modernism. The fascicle book is like Joyce’s Ulysses, containing everything including the kitchen sink. It looks as though it were totally rhizomatic, but it is brought into coherence by a single focusing authorial consciousness (think of de Man’s “rhetoricization of grammar”), hence remains a fascicle book, more commendable than a root book but not quite a breakthrough. And now, by proclamation, A Thousand Plateaus is going to be a rhizomatic book. It’s collaborative, it rejects sequencing for layering, it cheerfully says everything at once, scrambling unpredictably and seemingly at random from metaphor to metaphor—not in order to evoke one root idea or hobby horse but to imitate the permutation of permutation itself. You can decide whether they succeed.

因此，齐泽克可以帮助我们理解拉康，也让我们有机会重新审视彼得·布鲁克斯。虽然你在《宫廷爱情》一文中对齐泽克如何运用叙事来阐释欲望冲突的例子非常精彩，而且我认为这些例子本身就足以说明问题，但最好的例子实际上出自齐泽克的一本书，名为《你想知道的关于拉康的一切（但你不敢问希区柯克）》 。在那本书中，他对《迷魂记》进行了大量的分析。不妨把《迷魂记》看作是齐泽克所讨论的那种情节的一个变体。它可以被视为对“不满足于小客体”的一种病态研究。斯科蒂的朋友，艺术家米奇，一直爱着他，而他却对她的吸引力视而不见，对自己的需求漠不关心，一心只想着神秘的玛德琳/卡洛塔/朱迪。他渴望的对象不仅遥不可及（他想与她缠绵，却总能找到无数借口推脱），而且还十分神秘。最终揭开她的真实身份，不仅摧毁了她本人，也彻底瓦解了她对斯科蒂的吸引力。在灾难发生之前，还有一系列痛苦的场景：他痴迷地将朱迪改造成玛德琳的翻版，只有当“另一个”的每一根头发都到位后，他才能真正拥有她。然而，就在这一切完成的那一刻，“另一个”本身也被揭露为虚假，她只是对原本完美却并不存在之物的复制品，斯科蒂那段如梦似幻的爱情也随之彻底崩塌。

Žižek, then, can help us understand Lacan, and he also allows us to revisit Peter Brooks. Although the examples of the way the conflictedness of desire in narrative works for Žižek in your essay, “Courtly Love,” are excellent and I think largely self-explanatory, the best example of all is actually in a book by Žižek called Everything You Wanted to Know about Lacan (but Were Afraid to Ask Hitchcock). In that book, a lot of attention is paid to Vertigo. Just think about Vertigo as an instance of the kind of plot Žižek is talking about, with one variant. It could be considered a pathological study of not settling for the objet petit à. Scottie’s friend who is in love with him, the artist Midge, is continuously available, yet he is oblivious to her attractions, indifferent to need, throughout his obsessive pursuit of the enigmatic Madeleine/Carlotta/Judy. The object of his desire is not just distant (he wants to make love with her but finds a million excuses not to), she is also obscure, the final discovery of her identity destroying both her and her allure for Scottie all at once. Preceding the catastrophe are the painful scenes in which he fetishistically remakes Judy into an exact replica of Madeleine, unable to possess her until every hair of the Other is in place. At just the moment when this is accomplished, the Other herself is exposed as inauthentic, herself a replica of what was perfect because nonexistent, and Scottie’s courtly love disintegrates altogether.

或许，思考齐泽克作品中欲望的难以捉摸与彼得·布鲁克斯作品中情节的延展之间的关系会很有帮助。布鲁克斯描述了情节中段如何通过一系列片段不断延伸，而这些片段都体现出某种需要反复纠正的失衡。由于现实主义小说的典型情节是婚姻，因此许多这样的迂回都与不恰当的对象选择有关。但这种错误的转向，就像齐泽克的《哭泣的游戏》那样，也可能同时涉及不恰当的政治对象选择。不妨以此为例来思考亨利·詹姆斯的《卡萨马西玛公主》的情节。可怜的海辛斯·罗宾逊在这两方面都以类似的方式遭遇了失败。他在政治上站错了队，像康拉德笔下的人物一样，把社会主义和无政府主义混为一谈；在爱情上也步了后尘，变幻莫测的克里斯蒂娜·莱特对他而言是一个遥不可及的“大他者”，就像她在詹姆斯的第一部小说中对同名主人公罗德里克·哈德森那样。（克里斯蒂娜·莱特最终以公主的身份出现，这与她名字本身就蕴含着宗教启迪的寓意，尽管詹姆斯的小说与现实世界的期望相悖——作为公主，她并非神圣的启示，而是一座大宅，casamassima——这一童话般的结局使她在齐泽克的“宫廷爱情”传统中占有一席之地。）

It’s useful, perhaps, to think about the relationship between the elusiveness of desire in Žižek and the dilation of plot in Peter Brooks.
