Brooks describes the way middles in plots protract themselves through episodes, all of which manifest some sort of imbalance in need of corrective repetition. Because the characteristic plot of realist fiction is the marriage plot, many of these détours have to do with inappropriate object choice. But such wrong turns, as in the case of The Crying Game in Žižek, may also, and perhaps at the same time, involve inappropriate political object choices. Consider the plot of Henry James’s Princess Casamassima in that regard. Poor Hyacinth Robinson strikes out on both counts in parallel ways. He ends up on the wrong side in politics, confusing socialism with anarchism like a character out of Conrad, and on the wrong side of love, the mercuric Christina Light being a decidedly inaccessible Big Other, as she had been, too, for the eponymous Roderick Hudson in James’s first novel. (That Christina Light persists as a princess, a fairy-tale outcome linked to a woman whose given name even promises religious enlightenment despite the real-world expectations of James’s fiction—as a princess she is not sacred illumination but a big house, casamassima—secures her a place in Žižek’s “courtly love” tradition.)

总之，对布鲁克斯而言，情节走向恰当结局的平衡是通过降低兴奋感来实现的，甚至可能以死亡的形式出现。这让人想起弥尔顿的净化，即“心境平静，激情消退”。齐泽克则更具后现代主义色彩。他追随拉康的观点，认为欲望的对象是渐近的，最终且永远是不可及的；或者说，即便它变得可及——或者说几乎可及——这反而会带来与它看似消除的问题一样多的问题（1193）：

In any case, for Brooks the navigation of a plot toward a suitable end reaches equilibrium through the reduction of excitation, possibly even in the form of death. One thinks again of the Miltonic catharsis, “calm of mind, all passion spent.” Žižek is more postmodern. Following Lacan, he sees the object of desire as asymptotic, as being ultimately and always inaccessible; or if it becomes accessible—or one might say almost accessible—this gives rise to as many problems as it seems to eliminate (1193):

或许，在宫廷爱情中，期待已久的最高满足时刻，当夫人向她的仆人施以仁慈时，并非夫人的臣服，并非她对性行为的同意，也不是某种神秘的入会仪式，而仅仅是夫人爱的象征，是“奇迹”——对象回应了她的请求，向恳求者伸出了手。
[P]erhaps, in courtly love itself, the long-awaited moment of highest fulfillment, when the Lady renders Gnada, mercy, to her servant is not the Lady’s surrender, her consent to the sexual act, nor some mysterious rite of initiation, but simply a sign of love on the part of the Lady, the “miracle” that the Object answered, stretching its hand out towards the supplicant.

换句话说，客体变成了主体。在这一交流、相互认同，或者说，在这一刻——齐泽克将这位女士与虐待关系中的女主人联系起来——她变得人性化、并给予爱，客体也因此变得更加容易接近。此时，臣服的可能出现了，然而，随着她变得更加容易接近，欲望的能量也面临着消散的威胁。换句话说，在齐泽克看来，封闭是对欲望能量的威胁，而非对欲望满足的威胁。根据齐泽克的观点，欲望内在于语言；它是语言的特征性运动，而满足则威胁着它。女士说：“当然，为什么不呢？我不介意。”她的“仆人”彻底被打乱了计划，拒绝了他长期以来视为梦想答案的行为，因为在满足之后，就再无欲望可言了。欲望变成了需要，仅仅是满足欲望的问题，而不再是维持我们作为人的东西的问题：文字的无尽动力或能动性。

The object, in other words, has become subject. In this moment of exchange, mutuality of recognition, or becoming human on the part of the lady—whom Žižek has associated with the dominatrix in a sadistic relationship—in this moment of becoming human and of offering love, the object becomes more accessible. There is now the chance of surrender, yet as she becomes more accessible, the energy of desire is threatened with dissolution. In other words, closure in Žižek is a threat to the energy of desire, not the fulfillment of it. Desire inheres in language, according to Žižek; it is the characteristic movement of language, and it is threatened by fulfillment. The lady says, “Sure, why not? Don’t mind if I do,” and her “servant” is thrown off his game completely, refusing the act he has so long represented to himself as the answer to his dreams, because in fulfillment there’s nothing more to desire. Desire becomes need, merely a matter of gratification and no longer a question of sustaining that which makes us human: the endless propulsion, or agency, of the letter.

小汉斯·霍尔拜因，《大使们》（1533 年）。

Hans Holbein the Younger, The Ambassadors (1533).

但真实存在的、无法叙述的事物又该如何看待呢？不妨看看汉斯·霍尔拜因的《大使们》。画中两位外交官中间隔着一张桌子。他们可能正在商讨亨利八世的某桩婚事，而这桩婚事交织着政治与爱情，或许意义非凡。这幅画描绘的是一个欲望的对象，而这个对象却缺席了，最多只是隐约提及。在前景中，有一个东西。它像影子一样斜向我们，但它并非画中任何事物的影子、镜子或负像。如果你从侧面观察，它开始像一个骷髅头。事实上，学者们几乎一致认为，这可能是一个扭曲变形的骷髅头的影子或象征。这个骷髅头以如此倾斜的视角出现在那里究竟有何意义，很难说，但或许并非不可能。这是一个“死亡纪念”的时代，霍尔拜因几乎将其扭曲得面目全非，以此提醒我们，我们并非总是记得死亡，但死亡却如影随形，如同降胆固醇药广告中那具想象中的担架。从精神分析的角度来看，正如我们一直在研究的叙事理论的公理，我们发现自己观察到一种死亡愿望与快乐原则相互依存的模式。死亡的阴影也是阳具的阴影，这块污渍无疑也与之相似。毕竟，这是一场婚姻谈判。所以，我们当然可以说些什么。但即便如此，这块污渍也始终是对礼仪的亵渎。就其作为我们自身死亡的阴影而言——死亡是无法叙述的，正如它对大使们、亨利以及他最新的未婚妻而言一样——这颗头骨或其他什么东西以一种不合时宜的方式，斜着身子，闯入了人生的情节之中。我们可以将其解读为象征性的（阳具、“字母”），或是想象性的（头骨作为传统的记忆辅助工具）。然而，正因为它无法被解读，正因为它挑战了所有既定的表征惯例，它才是真实的，是在我们赋予它意义之前，它本身并无意义。

But what about the real, the unnarratable? Consider Hans Holbein’s The Ambassadors. There are the two diplomats with a table between them. They are negotiating probably over one of Henry VIII’s marriages, and as a crossing between politics and love that is perhaps not insignificant. The painting then concerns an object of desire, and that object is absent, implied at most. In the foreground, there is this thing. It angles toward us like a shadow, but it is not a shadow, a mirror or negative reflection, of anything in the painting. If you look at it from the side, it begins to resemble a skull. Indeed, there’s something approaching a consensus among scholars that it may be a weirdly distorted shadow or representation of a skull. What the skull is doing there in such oblique perspective is hard to say, though perhaps not impossible to say. This is the age of the memento mori, which Holbein distorts almost beyond recognition to remind us that we do not always remember death yet death still follows us around like the imaginary stretcher in an ad for pills that lower cholesterol. Psychoanalytically, and as an axiom in the theory of narrative we have been studying, we find ourselves observing a model of the death wish and the pleasure principle as mutual presences. The shadow of death is also the shadow of the phallus, which surely this blot resembles as well. It is, after all, a marriage negotiation. So certainly there are things we can say. But still, this blot must always be a breach of decorum. Insofar as it is the shadow of our own death, which is unnarratable, as it is, too, for the ambassadors, for Henry, and for his latest fiancée, the skull or whatever it is obtrudes in untimely fashion, at an oblique angle, in the very midst of the plot of life. We can interpret it in the register of the symbolic (the phallus, the “letter”), or the imaginary (the skull as conventional memory aid). Insofar as it cannot be interpreted, though, insofar as it obtrudes on any and all conventions of representation, it is the real, that which has no meaning until we give it one.

在关于希区柯克的书中，齐泽克几乎在希区柯克的每一部电影中都发现了类似的东西；在霍尔拜因的画作中，齐泽克也称之为“污点”。在小说中，我们会称之为无关紧要的细节。我们觉得在小说中，任何事物都能找到形式上的作用或功能。天气、桌上的鲜花、路上的尘土：我们可以赋予它们形式上的意义，但在小说中，或许存在着某种难以解释的存在，而这正是齐泽克所说的“污点”。

Both in the book on Hitchcock, where he finds something like this in just about every film Hitchcock ever made, and also in Holbein’s painting, Žižek calls this “the blot.” In fiction, we would call it irrelevant detail. We feel that we can find a formal role, a function, for absolutely everything in fiction. The weather, the flowers on the table, the dust in the road: we can place these formally, but there may be something in fiction that is simply an unaccountable presence, and that’s the blot for Žižek.

现在谈谈语言中的欲望：齐泽克的文章中有一部分内容你可能觉得有些离题。他突然谈到了J.L.奥斯汀的日常语言哲学，以及语言学家奥斯瓦尔德·杜克罗的谓词概念。但对齐泽克而言，真正重要的是奥斯汀所说的任何话语中都存在的“施为性”要素，以及杜克罗所说的谓词对整个句子的支配作用。奥斯汀的“施为性”和杜克罗的“谓词”概念占据了语言领域的大部分，尽管它们原本只应涵盖语言的一部分。奥斯汀最初区分了施为性陈述和陈述性陈述；但从长远来看，《如何以言行事》的论证表明，语言中只有施为性陈述，因为任何类型的陈述都包含施为性要素。杜克罗特也同样赋予谓语一种能量，它接管了语法主语，并在句子中构成了一种表演——在这两种情况下，“表演”都意味着“欲望”，即在表达某种愿望时，自我的一种呈现。当我承诺做某事时，我便展现了履行承诺的欲望。当我陈述某事时，我便通过自身的行动展现了希望该事成真（而非虚假）的欲望。这些论证阐明了齐泽克为何坚持认为欲望在语言中不可避免，以及欲望如何渗透到我们彼此交流的一切，当然也渗透到齐泽克所举电影例子的情节——或者如电影研究领域所说的“叙事”——之中。

A word now about desire in language: there’s a part of Žižek’s essay that you may have found digressive. He’s suddenly talking about J. L. Austin’s ordinary language philosophy, together with the linguist Oswald Ducrot’s idea of predication. But what’s relevant for Žižek is the element of performance one finds in any utterance according to Austin, and the dominance of an entire sentence by predication according to Ducrot. Performance in Austin and predication in Ducrot take over the field of language even though they were supposed to cover only a part of it. Austin began by distinguishing between performatives and constatives; but in the long run, the argument of How to Do Things with Words suggests that there are only performatives, as statements of any kind harbor elements of performance. Ducrot similarly ascribes to the predicate an energetic agency that simply takes over the grammatical subject and constitutes a kind of performance within the sentence—where performance in both cases means “desire,” a staging of the self in the act of speaking with respect to some wish. When I promise to do something, I enact the desire to fulfill the promise. When I predicate something, I enact the desire that that something be the case—rather than false—through my own instrumentality. These arguments then illustrate what Žižek means in insisting on the inescapability of desire in language, and the way desire permeates everything we can say to each other and certainly permeates the plot—or, as they say in film studies, the “diegesis”—of the film examples that Žižek gives us.

我们或许已经开始怀疑自己是否还能在阅读中翻开新的一页（该死的语言障碍），但下次我们会再试一次。

We have perhaps grown skeptical about whether we can ever turn a new page in our reading (dwat that pesky langwidge), but next time we’ll try again.

 

 

社会背景

The Social Context

 

 

第十六章

CHAPTER 16

读者与文本的社会渗透性
The Social Permeability of Reader and Text

阅读材料：

Readings:

Jauss, Hans Robert. “文学史对文学理论的挑战。”载《批评传统》，第 981-988 页。

Jauss, Hans Robert. “Literary History as a Challenge to Literary Theory.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 981–988.

巴赫金，米哈伊尔。“小说中的异质性。”载《批评传统》，第 588-593 页。

Bakhtin, Mikhail. “Heteroglossia in the Novel.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 588–593.

现在我们转向主要关注文学社会语境和环境的理论，首先要讨论的是一对或许和德勒兹与齐泽克一样奇特的组合：米哈伊尔·巴赫金和汉斯·罗伯特·尧斯。今天这两位作者之间最显著的区别在于，巴赫金主要关注的是文本产生的社会生活，而尧斯主要关注的是文本被接受的社会生活，或者更准确地说，是一系列社会生活。然而，我认为从阅读这两段摘录中，以及在接下来的阅读材料中，你们都能看出，一旦将社会环境纳入考量，文学的生产和接受就远没有你们想象的那么容易区分了。在所有话语交流中，例如对话，我们都意识到听者同时也是说话者，读者同时也是作者。在布鲁姆等文学影响理论中，作者就是读者，从某种意义上说，我认为尧斯的理论也是如此。但从更广义的角度来看，我们也会发现，文学的生产和消费这两个主题很难割裂开来。在文学史中，作者既是读者，也是与过去存在关联的人；而读者反过来又扮演着将文本传播到未来的角色，从某种意义上说，他们本身或许也是一位作家。读者表达观点、传播价值观、使文本保持在畅销书排行榜上，甚至可能有助于其名垂青史。

As we turn now to theories that are concerned chiefly with the social context and milieu of literature, we begin with a pairing that’s perhaps as odd as that of Deleuze and Žižek: Mikhail Bakhtin and Hans Robert Jauss. The most egregious difference between your authors for today is that Bakhtin’s primary concern is with the life world that produces a text, and Jauss’s primary concern is with the life world, or perhaps better succession of life worlds, in which a text is received. I think you can tell from reading both excerpts, however, and will find in the materials ahead in our reading, that once you factor in a social setting the production and reception of literature are not as easy to tell apart as you might have supposed. In all discourse exchanges, such as conversation, we recognize that the listener is also a speaker and the reader an author. In theories of literary influence like Bloom’s, the author simply is the reader, and in a sense I think this is true of Jauss as well; but in broader senses, too, we’ll come to see that the production and consumption of literature are difficult to separate as topics. In literary history, the author is a reader who stands in relation to the past; and the reader in turn, who plays a role circulating texts for the future, is perhaps even in concrete terms a writer. He or she expresses opinions, circulates values, keeps texts on the best seller list, and perhaps contributes to their lasting reputation.

尽管雅斯并未如此表述，但我始终认为，他的读者实际上几乎和布鲁姆的读者一样，都是作家。任何一位读者，只要其对一部作品在文学史上的延续或影响力负有责任，就必然在某种意义上表达过自己的观点。十九世纪图书馆的借阅活动，甚至书店的购书行为，都只是昙花一现：一本书的命运取决于评论、口碑和口口相传。如今，博客、在线读者反馈、读书俱乐部和讨论小组比以往任何时候都更加印证了这一点。作为品味引领者的读者，本身也是一位作家。或许有必要强调一个尚未被提及的观点：如果布鲁姆关于“强误读”的理论——作为文学史编纂原则之一——可以被理解为作家作为读者、读者作为作家之间的关系，那么在雅斯看来，读者也是作家，作家也是读者，这在某种意义上同样适用。布鲁姆和雅斯都对文学史编纂做出了卓著的贡献。

Although Jauss does not say this, I’ve always felt that of necessity his reader is almost as much a writer as Bloom’s is. Any reader responsible for the continued presence, or influence, of a text through literary history must in some sense have expressed an opinion. Silent participation in the nineteenth-century lending libraries or even purchases at the bookseller’s are going to be ephemeral: the fate of a book is dictated by reviews, buzz, word of mouth. Our blogs, online reader feedback, book clubs, and discussion groups make this truer today than ever before. The reader as tastemaker is also a writer. Perhaps to belabor a point that has not been acknowledged: if Bloom’s theory of strong misreading as a principle of literary historiography can be understood as a relationship between writers as readers and readers as writers, there is a sense in which for Jauss, too, the reader is a writer and the writer is a reader. Both of them, Bloom as well as Jauss, have made plausible contributions to literary historiography.

不过，让我们回到正题，记住这次讲座标志着我们阅读的一个过渡时刻。或许我们还会时常质疑，我们是否真的在向前迈进，或者我们是否需要承认，“形式主义”尽管表面上对历史和世界漠不关心，但实际上它一直在谈论的是“生活”。什克洛夫斯基希望文学性不仅能使语言陌生化，还能使历史和社会现实陌生化。理查兹说，诗歌能够拯救我们。克林斯·布鲁克斯说，诗歌的用途之一是使我们成为更好的公民。在雅各布森看来，任何话语都具有指涉功能。德里达谈论“事件”的奥秘，德曼谈论普鲁斯特式的氛围。那么，我们如何才能就过去的内容和现在要读的内容之间至少暂时的区别达成共识呢？我们可以这样说——虽然不确定这种区分是否站得住脚，但我们仍然觉得我们需要这种区分——迄今为止，文本构成了一个世界，而从现在开始，世界存在于文本之中。文本不再是微观世界，而是现实世界传递的媒介。它仍然是一种扭曲的媒介，但它不再是一个具有独立本体论地位的可分离实体（请注意，这同样源于德里达的前提，即在正确理解的文本之外不存在任何东西）；文本是世界中的一个对象，由社会力量产生、维系和瓦解。

Let us return, though, to remembering that this lecture marks a moment of transition in our reading. There may be times, again, when we wonder whether we’re really moving ahead or whether we do perhaps need to acknowledge that “formalism,” for all its alleged and apparent indifference to history and the world, was after all talking about “life” all along. Shklovsky hoped that literariness would defamiliarize not just language but historical and social reality. Richards said that poetry is capable of saving us. Cleanth Brooks said that one of the uses of poetry was to make us better citizens. For Jakobson there is no utterance that lacks a referential function. Derrida speaks of the mystery of the “event,” de Man of Proustian atmospheres. So how can we agree upon at least a provisional difference between what went before and what we’ll read now? We shall say, not sure whether the distinction will hold up but still with the sense that we need one, that hitherto the text has constituted a world but that henceforth the world lives in the text. The text is no longer a microcosm but a medium through which the real world passes. It is as much as ever a distorting medium, but it is no longer a separable entity with a discrete ontological status (note that this follows equally from Derrida’s premise that there is nothing outside the text, properly understood); the text is an object in the world, produced, sustained, and undone by social forces.

到目前为止，我们一直将语言视为一种符号代码，同时又怀疑这种代码可能只是虚拟的。我们一直强调我们在与语言的关系中处于被动状态，甚至被语言“说话”。换句话说，在我们思考这些问题的过程中，语言通过我们说话这一观点始终存在；然而，我们却一直对我们可能拥有的任何感觉保持着一种奇怪的沉默，即这种语言不仅仅是一种代码，不仅仅是在任何特定历史时刻虚拟存在的东西，而实际上是由其他人的语言构成的代码：它不仅是抽象的语言，而且是流通的语言。这使得它或许更接近索绪尔意义上的“语言” （langue ），而不是他所说的“语言”（langage），即所有流通话语的总和。拉康也认为语言是继承的，当然，是“父辈”的语言，无论我们多么不想说，我们都会说；但显然，这种说法是对一种更为弥散和多面的继承进行的精神分析式提炼。

So far we have been thinking of language as a semiotic code, while suspecting that this code may be only a virtual one. We have been emphasizing the degree to which we are passive in relation to, even “spoken by” this language. In other words, it has been a constant in our thinking about these matters that language speaks through us; yet we have exercised so far a curious reticence about any sense we may have that this language is not just a code, not just something that exists virtually at any given historical moment, but is in fact a code made up of other people’s language: it is language not just in the abstract but in circulation. This makes it perhaps less a langue, in Saussure’s sense, and closer to what he called langage, the sum of all speeches in circulation. Lacan, too, sees language as inherited, to be sure, the language “of the father” that we speak no matter how much we wish we didn’t; but clearly that way of putting it is a psychoanalytic distillation of a far more diffuse and multifaceted inheritance.

因此，我们仍在思考语言，以及我们学会区分语言和言语，但如今的语言不再是脱离现实的抽象概念；它是一种在现实中流通的语言，是社会交换的工具。在我们看来，语言现在以及今后都是一种社会制度。在文学理论中，这种新的、制度化的语言观与个体言语之间仍然保持着我们在语言学和精神分析形式主义中观察到的那种确定性关系，但我们现在开始理解语言以一种新的方式与我们对话这一论断。我的声音——“声音”一词在这里显然承受着巨大的压力，尽管没有人会说它会消失——我的声音渗透着我周围世界中语言的所有沉淀、语域、层次和方向。就我的言语而言，其能动性在于我从他人那里汲取语言。当我即兴发挥，仅凭几张笔记讲课时，语言的社会流通性在我所说的话中比平时更加​​显著。当你听我即兴发挥、不看稿子的时候，你听到的是互联网，是报纸标题，是俚语。你听到的是“你听到了”，一个节奏重复的短语，其韵律你肯定在讲坛和政治演说中听过，就像跷跷板或摇摇马一样，如果我在写作，我大概会想办法去掉它。正如我们将要了解到的，写作的确是一种掌控语言、使其为己所用的努力，但写作本身也从未停止过用他人的语言表达。

So we are thinking of language still, and of the distinction we have learned to make between language and speech, but now it’s not a language abstracted from reality; it’s a language that circulates within reality as an instrument of social exchange. Language is now and henceforth in our reading a social institution. In literary theory, this new, institutional sense of language retains the same determinate relationship with individual speech that we have observed in linguistic and psychoanalytic formalism, but we now begin to understand the claim that language speaks to us in a new way. My voice—and the word “voice” is obviously under heavy pressure here, even though nobody ever quite says it goes away—my voice is permeated by all the sedimentations, registers, levels, and orientations of language in the world that surrounds me. Insofar as my speech retains agency, it is in the sense that I take language from other people. When I lecture ad-lib from a few notes, the social circulation of language is even more pronounced in what I say than it might be otherwise. When you listen to me blather on without a script, you’re hearing the internet, you’re hearing newspaper headlines, you’re hearing slang. You’re hearing the expression “you’re hearing,” a rhythmically repeated phrase in the cadence you’ll recognize from pulpit and political oratory, a kind of seesaw or rocking-horse effect that I’d probably try to get rid of if I were writing. As we’ll learn, writing is indeed an effort to take possession of language, to make it do one’s bidding, but writing too never stops being voiced in the language of others.

“外在的”事物会逐渐融入我们的内心，不知不觉中，它就成了个人日常表达模式的一部分，甚至成为最独特言​​语的组成部分。至于这种情况究竟在多大程度上存在，是绝对如此还是仅仅是个人言语构成中的一个因素，这始终是一个值得探讨的话题。稍后我们会举几个例子。但无论如何，我们可以看到，语言与言语之间的关系结构本身并没有改变——事实上，随着时间的推移，这种结构也不会真正改变——但当我们把语言视为一个社交网络而非一个虚拟系统时，这种关系的本质以及我们谈论它的方式却发生了巨大的变化。

What’s “out there” gets to the point where it’s in here, and the next thing you know, it becomes part of the ongoing patter of an individual, the grain as it were of even the most idiosyncratic speech. I suppose the extent to which this might be the case, where it is absolutely so or only one factor in the makeup of individual speech, is always subject to debate. Soon we’ll take up a couple of examples. But in any case, you can see that without the structure of the relationship between language and speech having changed—and in fact it won’t really change as we continue along—the substance of this relationship and the way we talk about it is very much changed when we think of language as a social network rather than a virtual system.

为了更具体地了解这种变化如何在本次讲座所读的两位作者的作品中体现，我想引用几段文字。第一段出自巴赫金，他的理论根植于俄国形式主义。这段文字探讨了他认为的形式主义对双声的理解与“真正的异质性”之间的关系。传统的双声概念体现在反讽的概念中，即说话者的意思与听话者通常能够达成共识的意思不符。但巴赫金想要引起我们注意的是一种不同的现象：

In order to see more concretely how this change appears in the work of the two authors we read for this lecture, I want to quote from a couple of passages. The first is from Bakhtin, whose roots are in Russian formalism. The passage concerns the relationship between what he takes to be a formalist understanding of double-voicedness and “genuine heteroglossia.” A conventional sense of double-voicedness is reflected in the notion of irony as not meaning what one says in a way that in most cases speaker and hearer can agree upon. But Bakhtin wants to call a different phenomenon to our attention:

修辞往往局限于对文字、对意识形态权威的纯粹语言上的胜利。[我们可以通过反讽等修辞手法来颠覆那些对思想施加专制权威的既定观念。] 当这种情况发生时，修辞便沦为形式主义的语言游戏。但我们重申，当话语脱离现实时，对词语本身而言也是致命的。词语变得苍白无力，失去语义的深度和灵活性，失去了在新的语境中扩展和更新其意义的能力。[当坏事发生时，我们会说“太好了！”我们已经这样说了好几代，这种表达方式已经失去了活力。] 它们本质上已经作为话语消亡，因为具有意义的词语超越了自身而存在；也就是说，它通过向外投射其目的性而存在。双声性，仅仅是语言上的，并非建立在真正的异质性之上，而仅仅是建立在声音的多样性之上。
Rhetoric is often limited to purely verbal victories over the word, over ideological authority. [These are the ways we can subvert received ideas that exert tyrannical authority over thought by submitting them to figures of rhetoric such as irony.] When this happens rhetoric degenerates into formalistic verbal play but, we repeat, when discourse is torn from reality it is fatal for the word itself as well. Words grow sickly, lose semantic depth and flexibility, the capacity to expand and renew their meanings in new living contexts. [Something bad happens and we say “great!” We have done this for several generations and the expression doesn’t have much oomph any more.] They essentially die as discourse, for the signifying word lives beyond itself; that is, it lives by directing its purposiveness outward. Double-voicedness, which is merely verbal, is not structured on authentic heteroglossia but on a mere diversity of voices.

它是一种声音的多样性，也就是说，可能不超过两种声音，由一个人操控。换句话说，双声性没有考虑到意义的可能性和语域之间存在的复杂叠加，这种叠加依赖于不同的语言社群共同构建话语的各个方面，并迫使我们思考话语的语境，才能理解其声音的运用。

It is a diversity of voices, that is, probably no more than two, manipulated by an individual. In other words, double-voicedness doesn’t take into account the way in which there are complex overlays among the possibilities and registers of meaning, depending on diverse speaking communities coming together to forge any aspect of discourse and forcing us to think about the life world of an utterance in order to understand its play of voice.

我们可以指出汉斯·罗伯特·尧斯对形式主义的回应与之类似。与巴赫金一样，尧斯深受俄国形式主义者的影响。这种影响在你手中的文本中并未完全体现，而是在尧斯最著名的文章——篇幅仅一页的《文学史作为对文学理论的挑衅》中有所体现。在尧斯关于文本与生活世界关系的理论中，他将俄国形式主义史学（尤其是雅各布森和蒂尼亚诺夫的理论）的某些方面与马克思主义关于文学作品的营销、接受和消费的视角结合起来。这两组思想在尧斯关于文学接受的论述中并存，我们将在讲座的最后部分再次讨论这一点。

We can point to a comparable response to formalism on the part of Hans Robert Jauss. Like Bakhtin, Jauss is strongly influenced by the Russian formalists. This influence is not enunciated fully in the text that you have but rather in Jauss’s best known essay, the pamphlet-length “Literary History as a Provocation to Literary Theory.” In his theory of the relationship between the text and the life world, Jauss stitches together aspects of Russian formalist historiography, particularly that of Jakobson and Tynianov, with a Marxist approach to the marketing, reception, and consumption of literary production. These two sets of ideas function side by side in Jauss’s thesis about literary reception, to which we’ll return at the end of the lecture.

第二段文字中，雅斯试图与这两种影响保持一定距离，内容如下：

The second passage, in which Jauss attempts to distance himself somewhat from both of these influences, goes as follows:

早期马克思主义和形式主义方法通常将文学事实置于生产和再现美学的封闭循环中。这样做，它们剥夺了文学不可分割的维度，即文学的接受和影响维度，而这一维度既是其审美特征，也是其社会功能。
Early Marxist and formalist methods in common conceive the literary fact within the closed circle of an aesthetics of production and representation. In doing so, they deprive literature of a dimension that inalienably belongs to its aesthetic character as well as to its social function, the dimension of its reception and influence.

换句话说，文本在时间长河中传播的方式，它在读者眼中的变化，以及随着时间推移而增长或衰落的方式——这是一个社会过程，但其动态和轮廓只能通过一系列集体审美和阐释判断来描绘。正如我们将看到的，在社交媒体或网络中发生的一切——即“接受”过程——是一个评价和阐释的问题。

In other words, the way in which a text makes its way forward in time, the way it changes in the eyes of readers and grows or diminishes as time passes—this is a social process, but its dynamics and contours can be charted only as a matter of successively collective aesthetic and interpretive judgments. What takes place in the social medium or network—the process of “reception”—is a matter of evaluation and interpretation, as we’ll see.

当我们试图更深入地探究这种思维方式与形式主义传统之间的联系时，不妨思考一下巴赫金在讨论文学“戏仿”（参见589页）时所用的狭义概念，即对某些著名文学范例或文本的戏仿。他暗示，广义上的戏仿理论主要属于俄国形式主义文学史学，其中区分新文本与旧文本的创新原则就被称作戏仿。因此，让我们稍作停留，探讨“戏仿”这一概念：如果我们仅仅从狭义的角度来理解它，就无法充分把握对话或异质语体如何以复杂的方式调节、影响并丰富文学话语的表象。狭义的戏仿概念再次将我们局限于二元对立的框架：前一个文本是这样那样的，后一个文本以一种我们可以称之为戏仿的方式对前一个文本进行模仿，但这仍然是一种二元互动。它只是将一篇文本与另一篇文本联系起来，而忽略了贯穿连续文本的多种声音的涌现。

As we try to get closer to the connection between thinking of this kind and the formalist tradition, consider where Bakhtin discusses (cf. 589) literary “parody,” here in the narrow sense of a spoof of some well-known literary model or text. He implies that the theory of parody understood in a broader sense belongs primarily to Russian formalist literary historiography, where the innovative principle that distinguishes a new text from an old one is just called parody. To pause over “parody,” then: if we conceive of it only in the narrow sense, we cannot have a sufficient grasp of the complexity with which the dialogic or the heteroglossal modulates, ripples, and makes complicated the surface of literary discourse. Parody narrowly conceived once again leaves us confined to a binarism: the previous text was such and such, the successive text plays off that previous text in a way that we can call parodic but that remains a binary interaction. It’s one text in relation to another and leaves out the flooding of multiple voices that pervades successive texts.

这种修正隐含着对文学史的否定，即拒绝将其置于社会史之外，另辟蹊径。巴赫金坚持认为文学和社会的声音密不可分。尧斯也持同样的观点。在下文引述的段落中，你会发现他直接回应了蒂尼亚诺夫论文《论文学演化》结尾处的那段话，我们之前也讨论过。你还记得蒂尼亚诺夫区分了演化和修正。演化指的是一系列文本的变异方式，或者说，后续文本（再次）戏仿或改变先前文本的方式；修正指的是非文学因素对文本的外部影响，这种影响仍然会导致文本的变化。蒂尼亚诺夫认为，无论对于历史研究还是文学史研究而言，将二者清晰区分开来都至关重要。

Implicit in this revision is the refusal to allow a separate track, isolated from social history, for literary history. Bakhtin insists that literary and social voices are inseparable. Jauss makes the same refusal. In a passage quoted below, you will find him directly responding to that passage at the end of Tynianov’s essay, “On Literary Evolution,” which we have discussed before. You remember Tynianov makes the distinction between evolution—the way a sequence of texts mutates, as one might say, the way successive texts (again) parody or alter what preceded them—and modification, which is the outside influence on texts by nonliterary factors that still bring about textual change. Tynianov says that it’s important both for the study of history and also for the study of literary history that the two be kept clearly distinct from each other.

Jauss对这一论断的回应或许更多是修辞上的而非实质性的，但这仍然再次标志着语言观念向社会性转变的趋势，而这正是我一直想要强调的。Jauss说道：

Jauss’s response to that claim is perhaps more rhetorical than substantive, but it nevertheless once again does mark the shift toward conceiving of language as social that I’ve been wanting to begin by emphasizing. Jauss says:

文学发展与社会变迁（即社会中那些会且确实会改变文本的特征）之间的联系，并不会因为二者的否定而消失。新的文学作品是在日常生活经验的背景下被接受和评判的。
The connection between literary evolution and social change [that is to say, those features in society that would and do modify texts] does not vanish from the face of the earth through its mere negation. The new literary work is received and judged against the background of the everyday experience of life.

需要注意的是，这是对蒂尼亚诺夫的一种相当初级的误读。蒂尼亚诺夫认为，作品在其历史进程中的相互更替方式，以及作品在日常生活中被评判的方式，是截然不同的两件事。但我们仍然可以合理地认为，蒂尼亚诺夫的区分是脆弱的，并且在研究文学接受史时，尤其是在考虑作者态度和文本关系的情况下，很难站得住脚。作者在创作新作品时，除了文学惯例之外，还会重塑先前作品中的许多方面——例如，重塑其观点。此外，区分形式创新和本质上由社会压力产生的创新，既不容易，甚至是不可能的。社会主义现实主义中对隐喻的回避，表面上看起来只是一种形式选择。审美因素和社会因素相互渗透，正如巴赫金的“异质语”理论中，人类声音的各种语域和沉淀相互交融一样。

Note that this is a fairly elementary misreading of Tynianov, who thinks the way works replace each other within their history and the way they’re judged in relation to the everyday are very different matters. But it may still be fair to argue that Tynianov’s distinction is fragile and certainly difficult to maintain when studying literary reception, especially if one takes authorial attitudes as well as textual relations into account. An author in creating a new work reshapes many things in a prior work besides its literary conventions—reshapes its opinions, for example. Also, there is no easy or even possible way to distinguish between formal innovations and those sorts of innovation that are produced by essentially social pressures. The avoidance of metaphor in socialist realism only looks like a formal choice. Aesthetic and social factors seep into one another in exactly the same way that all the registers and sedimentations of human voices interact and seep into one another in Bakhtin’s heteroglossia.

以上便是巴赫金和尧斯对形式主义思想的共同修正，这些修正在我们迄今为止所研究的大部分（如果不是全部）文学理论中都扮演了重要角色。在回到尧斯之前，我想先谈谈巴赫金。巴赫金有时称之为“异质语言”（Heteroglossia）或“言语多样性”，他认为这是“风格的基础”（592）。风格的基础并非规范性共享语言的统一性，也并非作者的独特之处，而是言语的多样性。当我与你交谈时，我并非在用官方的语调。我并非在说标准英语。事实上，按照这种观点，根本不存在所谓的标准英语，不存在一个可以指称的孤立、提炼的实体。某些封闭的环境，例如一端封闭的贵族阶层，以及另一端社会光谱上的某些孤立场所，在巴赫金看来就是“单语的”。 （巴赫金可能不会同意任何底层阶级的语言都是单一语言的，因为他认为所有这类语言环境都处于抗议和反抗的动荡之中。）但我们大多数人的语言也是许多其他人的语言。

These, then, are Bakhtin’s and Jauss’s shared revisions of formalist ideas that have played a prominent part in most, if not all, of the literary theory that we have studied until now. I’d like to discuss Bakhtin for a while now before turning back to Jauss. Heteroglossia, or diversity of speech as Bakhtin calls it sometimes, is what he singles out to be “the ground of style” (592). It is the diversity of speech and not the unity of a normative shared language or that which is distinctive in an author that is the ground of style. When I speak to you, I’m not speaking in an official voice. I am not speaking the King’s English. In fact, on this view there’s really no such thing as the King’s English, no such isolated, distilled entity that one can point to. Some hermetically sealed environments, like that of an inward-looking aristocracy at one extreme and perhaps some isolated settings at the opposite end of the social spectrum, are what Bakhtin would call “monoglossal.” (Bakhtin probably would not agree that the language of any underclass is monoglossal because he takes all such speech environments to be in a ferment of protest and resistance.) But the language of most of us is the language of many others.

如果真是如此，那么独特的风格是如何形成的呢？我们谈论风格时，仿佛它仅仅是作者的签名：“哦，我一眼就能认出这种风格。”柯勒律治曾说，如果他在沙漠中偶然读到华兹华斯的几行诗，他一定会喊出“华兹华斯！”的确，我们能够识别出某种风格——例如简·奥斯汀的风格。或许有人会认为《傲慢与偏见》的第一句话是约翰逊博士的风格，但大多数人会认为这是简·奥斯汀的风格。然而，正如我们稍后将看到的，这种风格是由许多声音交织而成的，这些声音最终很难被剥离出来并彼此区分开来。

If this is true, how is a distinctive style generated? We speak of a style as though it were purely a question of an authorial signature: “Oh, I would recognize that style anywhere.” Coleridge said of a few lines of Wordsworth that if he had come across those lines in the desert, he’d have cried out “Wordsworth!” And certainly it is true that we do recognize a style—the style of Jane Austen, for example. I suppose arguably you could think that the first sentence of Pride and Prejudice is the style of Dr. Johnson, but most people would recognize it as the style of Jane Austen. At the same time nevertheless, as we’ll see in a minute, it is a style made up of many voices that are very difficult finally to factor out and distinguish from each other.

将文体视为言语沉淀的复合体这一观点，似乎会动摇作者声音的概念。这或许会让我们进一步追问：如果我们认同社会方言是通过个人方言来表达的，认同所有人的语言实际上就是表达我言语的语言——那么，我们是否又一次不得不面对那个令人沮丧的话题：作者之死？我认为并非如此，至少在巴赫金的论述中并非如此。巴赫金赋予了我们一种相当振奋人心的作者重要性感悟（593）：

The idea of a style as a composite of speech sedimentations would seem to put the notion of an authorial voice in jeopardy. That might lead us to ask in turn whether agreeing that the sociolect speaks through the idiolect, that the language of everyone is, in fact, the language that speaks my speech—whether agreeing to this once again brings us face to face with that dreary topic, the death of the author. I don’t think so, not quite anyway, and certainly not in Bakhtin, who gives us a rather bracing sense of the importance of the author (593):

仿佛作者没有自己的语言，却拥有自己的风格，一种有机且统一的法则支配着他玩弄语言的方式[因此，风格或许是作者调和并分配影响其表达的各种声音的独特方式]，以及他自身真实的语义和表达意图如何在其中折射。[巴赫金在此援引统一意图原则，以及我们如何在任何一部小说的语篇中识别这一原则，从而拯救或保留了作者。] 当然，这种对语言的玩弄（以及他常常完全缺乏直接的语言表达）绝不会削弱作品整体上普遍存在的、根深蒂固的意图性，也不会削弱其总体的意识形态概念化。
It is as if the author has no language of his own, but does possess his own style, his own organic and unitary law governing the way he plays with languages [so style is perhaps one’s particular way of mediating and allocating the diversity of voice that impinges on what one’s saying] and the way his own real semantic and expressive intentions are refracted within them. [And here Bakhtin saves or preserves the author by invoking the principle of unifying intention and the way we can recognize it in the discourse of any given novel.] Of course this play with languages (and frequently the complete absence of a direct discourse of his own) in no sense degrades the general, deep-seated intentionality, the overarching ideological conceptualization of the work as a whole.

所以，这并非像我们阅读之初福柯或巴特等人所引发的“作者之死”问题，尽管在某些方面它似乎如此。我们迄今为止所讨论的关于多元声音的一切，都可以在大量的长篇小说中找到体现。小说是巴赫金最为关注的体裁。我认为，就此而言，我或许有些过于简化，但他解读小说的历史、其兴起和发展时，是将其置于他认为是单一声音的体裁背景下：史诗，它仅仅表达了贵族传统的单一声音；抒情诗，它仅仅表达了孤立的浪漫主义唯我论者的单一声音。与之相对的是多元声音，小说中丰富多样的声音。正如我所说，我认为这种体裁对比有些过于简单，因为没有什么比将史诗和抒情诗都视为异质声音的体现更容易理解、也更具启发性的了。想想《伊利亚特》。如果你真的相信它是单语的，那么你打算如何解释那些心怀不满的忒耳西忒斯人的演说呢？你可以说他们是例外，证明了霸权规则，但事实仍然是，他们的声音并非暴躁如神的阿喀琉斯的声音，而阿喀琉斯的声音也并非古板守旧的官僚阿伽门农、意识形态相对主义者萨尔佩冬或狡猾的奥德修斯的声音。

So this is not, though it may seem to be in certain respects, a question of the death of the author as provoked by, let’s say, Foucault or Barthes at the start of our reading. Everything that we’ve been saying so far about plurivocality can be seen at work in a vast array of novels. The novel is the privileged genre for Bakhtin. I think somewhat oversimplifying in this regard, he reads the history of the novel, its emergence and flowering, against the backdrop of genres he considers to be monoglossal: the epic, which simply speaks the unitary voice of an aristocratic tradition; the lyric, which simply speaks the unitary voice of the isolated romantic solipsist. Over against that, you get the polyglossal, the rich multiplicity of voice in the novel. As I say, I think that the generic contrast is somewhat oversimplified because nothing is easier and more eye-opening than to read both epic and lyric as manifestations of heteroglossia. Just think of The Iliad. If you really believe that it’s monoglossal, what are you going to do with the speeches of the malcontent Thersites? You could say they’re an exception proving a hegemonic rule, but the fact remains, they’re not the voice of the peevishly godlike Achilles, which in turn after all is not the voice of the stuffy official Agamemnon, the ideological relativist Sarpedon, or the wily Odysseus.

尽管如此，我认为异质语言的基本概念既丰富又重要。让我们用《傲慢与偏见》的第一句话来尝试一下，我相信你们大多数人都熟悉这句话：“凡是有钱的单身汉，都渴望娶妻，这是一条举世公认的真理。” 总的来说，这正是巴赫金所说的“通用语言”（“这是一条举世公认的真理”，因为每个人都在谈论它）与某种类似作者反思的东西（巴赫金在其他地方称之为“内在说服性话语”）之间微妙平衡的一个例证。

Despite this caveat, however, I think the basic idea of heteroglossia both rich and important. Let’s try it out with the first sentence of Pride and Prejudice, which I’m sure most of you know: “It is a truth universally acknowledged that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.” Generally speaking, this is an example of the precarious balance between what Bakhtin calls “common language”—“It is a truth universally acknowledged” because everybody speaks of it—and something like authorial reflection—what Bakhtin elsewhere calls “internally persuasive discourse.”

按照传统的说法，这段话会被认为是反讽的，而巴赫金在本文第一段中正是对这种反讽修辞进行了批判。我们很容易得出结论：简·奥斯汀自己都不相信她所说的话。这不过是些老生常谈的“客厅智慧”，她这句话里的每一句话都指向了其中显而易见的错误之处，即便她称之为真理：“普遍”指的是那一千个重要的、愚蠢的人，而不是那几千个既不承认也不关心这种事的人。当然，认为“一个拥有丰厚财富的单身汉”，或者说，一个没有财富的单身汉，除了“想找个妻子”之外别无他事，这种说法本身就显得夸张。因此，我们可以得出结论：奥斯汀是在讽刺那些客厅里的闲谈。

In traditional parlance, this would be considered a speech that manifests irony, the rhetoric of irony against which Bakhtin sets himself in the first passage on your sheet. We easily conclude that Jane Austen doesn’t believe what she says. It’s drawing-room wisdom, and everything in her sentence points to the ways in which it’s obviously wrong, even while it’s being called a truth: “universally” means the thousand silly people or so who matter, not the thousands who neither acknowledge nor care about any such thing. Then, of course, the idea that “a single man in possession of a good fortune,” or indeed otherwise, has nothing to do but to be “in want of a wife” is on the face of it exaggerated. Hence we conclude that Austen is being ironic at the expense of drawing room chatter.

但现在，我们开始让这些对简单讽刺的证实变得复杂起来。请记住，小说的情节证实了第一句话的“真相”，尽管我们似乎并不想认同这个真相。达西和宾利，这两个“拥有丰厚财富”的人，最终都渴望娶妻，并在小说结尾如愿以偿。当然，还有“想要”这个词。它的含义取决于说话的人。我们最近一直在思考“想要”这个词，因为我们刚刚经历了一段心理分析的时期。这位单身汉究竟想要什么？“想要”这个词本身就蕴含着微妙的双关，它既可以表示“渴望”，也可以表示“缺乏”。毕竟，如果我缺乏某样东西，我未必渴望它，我只是恰好没有它。另一方面，如果我想要某样东西，没错，我也可以说我渴望它。那么，究竟是哪一种呢？是某种社会压力试图填补的缺失（“他早就该结婚了，考虑到他这么富有，却还没结婚真是奇怪”），还是欲望？如果是欲望，那么拥有巨额财富就很难解释这种渴望。这部小说中存在一些爱情情节的元素——与婚姻情节略有不同——恰恰引出了这个问题。欲望并不在意银行存款，尽管它对皇室成员情有独钟。奢华、便利、社会认可、舒适：所有这些都与财富有关，但我们认为欲望的本质有所不同。这句话的复杂性实际上在于这些词语在社会语境中的含义如何在句子中传递，并让我们意识到，我们之前对奥斯汀与社交圈保持讽刺距离的自信推断，实际上受到各种微妙倾向的制约，正如我之前所说，她的情节也印证了这一点。我们需要巴赫金的帮助才能明白，仅仅归因于讽刺对于解读奥斯汀的作品来说过于简单粗暴。

But now we start to complicate these confirmations of a simple irony at work. Bear in mind that the plot of the novel confirms the “truth” of its first sentence, even though it is a truth that we seem not to be intended to endorse. Darcy and Bingley, both of them “in possession of a good fortune,” do turn out to have been in want of a wife and procure one by the end of the novel. Then, of course, there is this word “want.” What it means depends on who’s speaking it. We’ve been thinking a lot about want lately because we have just gone through our psychoanalytic phase. What exactly does this single man really want? There’s a subtle pun in the word “want,” which means both “to desire” and “to lack.” If I lack something, after all, I don’t necessarily desire it, I just don’t happen to have it. On the other hand, if I want something, true enough, I can also be said to desire it. Well, which is it? Is it a lack that social pressure of some sort is calculated to fill (“high time he was married, odd that he isn’t considering how rich he is”), or is it desire? If it’s desire, then possessing a good fortune is scarcely what accounts for the want. There are elements of a romance plot in this novel—not quite the same as a marriage plot—that raise precisely that question. Desire ignores mere bank accounts, though it likes royalty. Luxury, convenience, social acceptability, comfort: all of those things have to do with fortune, but desire we suppose to be of a somewhat different nature. The complication of the sentence has to do actually with the way the meanings of these words as they are used socially circulate through the sentence and make us see that our confident inference about Austen’s ironic distance from the drawing room is qualified by all sorts of tempered allegiances, borne out as I’ve said by her plot. We need Bakhtin’s help to see that the ascription of irony is too blunt an instrument for reading Austen.

理解巴赫金的“共同语言”概念也至关重要。这个概念本身并没有特定的价值取向。“共同语言”有点像根茎，它既可以是好的，也可以是坏的。它可以是（我这里指的是巴赫金关于“狂欢节”的著作）一种拉伯雷式的、狂欢式的、颠覆性的、充满活力的底层声音，推翻权威的既定模式和垂死社会秩序的陈规陋习。它可以是这样的，但同时它本身也可能是权威的、反动的、盲目的。共同语言可能会唤起那种令人沮丧的普遍吸引力，这种吸引力似乎为未经反思的、条件反射式的回应提供了合法性，例如在竞选活动中。共同语言涵盖了所有这些方面。

It is also important to grasp Bakhtin’s idea of common language. This is not a concept that is supposed to have one particular value attached to it. “Common language” is a little like a rhizome; it could be good, it could be bad. It could be (I allude here to Bakhtin’s book on “carnival”) a Rabelaisian, carnivalesque, subversive, energetic body of voices from below overturning the apple carts of authority and the fixed ways of a moribund social order. It could be that, but at the same time it could itself be authoritative, reactionary, mindless. Common language could call forth that depressing universality of appeal that seems to authorize unreflected, knee-jerk responses to what one observes and thinks about, for example, on the campaign trail. Common language covers this whole range.

关键在于它的存在，在于它流通，在于它与巴赫金所谓的“内在说服性话语”——换句话说，在于各种语言的过滤组合最终形成某种我们认为真实的东西。我们感受到一种反思的力量，一种语言各层面之间关系的构建，使得它们能够以说服的方式表达，这种表达方式未必是我们认同的，而是我们能够识别出构成我们仍然称之为“作者”的连贯意识的方式——在某种意义上，我们赋予这种意识以权威。在《傲慢与偏见》第一句（每个词都是“日常用语”）与整部小说情节之间那种奇特的自嘲关系中，我们感受到了某种内在的说服力，某种话语的连贯性。

The important thing about it is that it’s out there and that it circulates and exists in relation to what Bakhtin calls “internally persuasive discourse”—in other words, the way in which the filtering together of these various sorts of language result in something like what we feel to be authentic. We sense a power of reflection, a posing of relations among the various strata of language, such that they can speak persuasively, not necessarily in a way that we agree with but in a way that we recognize to constitute that coherent consciousness that we still do call “the author”—and to which we ascribe, in some sense, authority. In the peculiar self-mocking relationship between the first sentence of Pride and Prejudice—every word of which is “common language”—and the plot of Pride and Prejudice as a whole, we feel something like the internal persuasiveness, the coherence of the discourse.

为了总结我对巴赫金的论述，我想引用您文集中收录的另一篇长文节选，我强烈建议您阅读。这篇文章名为《小说中的话语》，我只想引用其中的一段（580）：“人的意识形态形成……是一个有选择地吸收他人话语的过程。”任何人的思想连贯性都源于从他人的话语中选择出某种类似自主世界观的东西。小说强调教育和发展，是巴赫金眼中典型的社会文本，而小说中“内在说服力的话语”（正如巴赫金在分析狄更斯的讽刺风格时所展示的那样，是通过对常用语言的复杂并置而实现的）正是选择他人语言并最终形成可辨识的声音的场所。

To sum up these remarks on Bakhtin, I want to quote from the other long excerpt that you have in your anthology, which I would encourage you to read. It’s called “Discourse in the Novel,” and I just want to quote this part of it (580): “The ideological becoming of a human being … is the process of selectively assimilating the words of others.” The achieved coherence of anyone’s mind results from selecting out of the words of others something like an autonomous world view. The novel, with its emphasis on education and development, is the social text par excellence for Bakhtin, and its “internally persuasive discourse,” achieved through the complex juxtaposition of common languages as demonstrated in Bakhtin’s examination of Dickens’s satiric style, is the site on which the selection of other people’s languages becomes a recognizable voice.

汉斯·罗伯特·尧斯通过伊瑟尔，将我们带回了伽达默尔。我相信您已经注意到，尧斯关于期待视域及其破坏的论述，与伊瑟尔对读者在填补文本中留下的想象空白中所扮演角色的阐述密切相关。这些空白是由偏离传统预期而造成的，需要读者去协商。尧斯对期待视域的论述，实际上是一种思考伽达默尔所说的“视域融合”得以实现的条件的方式。但对尧斯而言，并非仅仅是读者自身的视域与文本的视域需要相互交融。这种融合的发生或失败，取决于一系列视域的演变，而这些视域又会随着历史环境对文本的审美和阐释方式的改变而变化。

Hans Robert Jauss takes us back, by way of Iser, to Gadamer. You’ve noticed, I’m sure, that Jauss’s talk about horizons of expectation and the disruption of expectation has a great deal to do with Iser’s account of the role of the reader in filling imaginative gaps that are left in the text, gaps caused by departures from conventional expectations that need to be negotiated. What Jauss has to say about horizons of expectation is a way of thinking through the conditions in which Gadamer’s “merger of horizons” is possible. But for Jauss it’s not just one reader’s horizon and the horizon of the text that need to meet halfway in mutual illumination. Such mergers take place or fail to do so along a succession of horizons that change as modes of aesthetic and interpretive response to texts are mediated by historical circumstances.

这不仅仅是文本曾经具有某种身份，而如今读者对其理解发生了改变，因此需要从自身的视角重新审视。更重要的是，我们需要探究文本在过去和现在被接受的方式发生了哪些变化。文本拥有生命，经历了各种变迁，而这些变迁需要根据伽达默尔在《真理与方法》历史部分中描述的诠释学理解的三个阶段来理解。雅斯在其文章开头提到的十八世纪对“理解”（intelligere）、“阐释”（explicare）和“应用”（ applicare）的区分，正是为了区分任何读者或读者群体在文本接受史的任何阶段所面临的诠释学理解的三个阶段。

It’s not just that the text once had a certain identity that readers now conceive differently, hence need to reconsider from their own horizon. It’s rather a matter of deciding what has happened, studying changes in the way the text has been received between that other time and one’s own. The text has had a life. It has passed through life changes, and these life changes have to be understood at each successive stage in terms of the three moments of hermeneutic grasp as described by Gadamer in the historical section of Truth and Method. The eighteenth-century distinction between intelligere, explicare, and applicare—understanding, interpretation, and application—that Jauss talks about at the beginning of his essay exists to distinguish the three moments of hermeneutic understanding for any reader or reading public at any moment in the history of the reception of a text.

雅斯非常重视区分对文本的审美反应和随后的、反思性的诠释反应。这或许会让人有些困惑，因为他确实像海德格尔等人一样承认（正如我们之前指出的），你不可能对任何事物做出不经反思的自发反应。总有一种意义上的“你已经知道它是什么”，也就是说，总有一种意义上的“你已经诠释了它”。然而，雅斯确实非常重视区分这两个阶段——审美（他将其与理解联系起来）和诠释（他将其与诠释学传统中的“阐释”联系起来）。我们需要理解他所说的“审美”究竟是什么意思。一个文本之所以能够进入历史的流通，并持续出现在历史长河中不同读者的视野中，是因为它受到了审美上的赞赏。审美是滋养文本在历史长河中保持活力的养分。人们不断地表达他们喜欢这个文本。如果读者不喜欢一本书，那么就根本不存在解读或历史传承的问题，因为它终将消失。正如约翰逊博士所说：“读者丢弃的书，其价值也毫无意义。”换句话说，从解读的角度来看，一本书或许确实很好，无可争议的好——但如果它不能取悦读者，不能带来愉悦，不能通过取悦读者的方式在审美上与读者建立联系，那么后续的一切都无从谈起。

Jauss makes a considerable point of distinguishing between the aesthetic response to the text and a subsequent, reflectively interpretive response to the text. This may seem a little confusing because he does admit with Heidegger and others, as we’ve indicated ourselves in the past, that you can’t just have a spontaneous response to anything without reflection. There’s always a sense in which you already know what it is, which is to say a sense in which you’ve already interpreted it. Yet Jauss does make a considerable point of distinguishing between these two moments—the aesthetic, which he associates with understanding, and the interpretive, which he associates with explicare in the hermeneutic tradition. We need to understand what he means by “the aesthetic.” A text enters historical circulation and remains before the gaze of successive audiences in history because it has been admired aesthetically. Aesthetics is the nourishment that keeps the text alive through history. People continue to say that they like it. If they don’t say they like it, there will never be a question of interpreting it or transmitting it historically, because it’s going to disappear. As Dr. Johnson said, “That book is good in vain which the reader throws away.” In other words, from the standpoint of interpretation, a book may have been good, just incontestably good—but if it didn’t please, if it didn’t give pleasure, if it didn’t attach itself to a reading public aesthetically by means of pleasing, none of what would have followed could ever take place.

基于对读者和阅读群体在特定历史时期行为方式的理解，接受史研究（雅乌斯及其康斯坦茨大学的同事，包括伊瑟尔，称之为“接受史”）向我们揭示了任何特定时刻的审美和阐释接受在多大程度上受到其前后影响。换言之，文本会因其接受而逐渐改变；如果我们不研究接受史，就会天真地认为时间流逝，对过去文本的阐释变得困难，但这种困难与历史变迁本身无关。事实上，文本经历了一系列阐释的展开过程，其间发生了翻天覆地的变化：它变得不那么受欢迎，又变得更受欢迎；被阐释得更加丰富，又被阐释得更加匮乏；但它始终在不断演变，偏离最初的感知，以至于各种各样的附加含义和愉悦来源得以呈现，尽管某些含义也可能随之消失。英语领域近期兴起了一门名为“中世纪主义”的研究，它探讨了几个世纪以来中世纪观念的演变，包括赦罪僧在酷儿研究中的新生命、巴斯妇作为女权主义者的新身份、随着人文学科社会地位的兴衰，教士声誉的变迁（他是智者还是寄生虫？），以及磨坊主的故事如何以狂欢式的视角反驳骑士的故事，这种“对话式”的强调日益凸显。接受史研究了此类变化，无论它们出现在哪里——其中最常见的例子（几乎人人都知道）或许是人们对莎士比亚《亨利五世》的态度与当时民族好战或和平主义情绪之间的关联。

With this understanding of how readers and reading publics behave within a given horizon, the historical study of reception (what Jauss and his colleagues at the University of Konstanz, including Iser, called “reception history”) is what shows us the degree to which any particular moment of aesthetic and interpretive reception is mediated by what has gone before it and what comes after. In other words, a text gradually changes as a result of its reception, and if we don’t study reception, we are left naively supposing that time has passed and that interpretation of a past text has become difficult but that the difficulty has nothing to do with historical change itself. The fact is, there has been an unfolding process of successive interpretations whereby a text has gone through sea changes: it has become less popular, more popular, more richly interpreted, and less richly interpreted, but tends to keep eddying out from what it was sensed to be originally, to the point where all sorts of accretive implications and sources of pleasure may become available to us, though perhaps also lost. A recently emergent field in English called “Medievalisms” studies successive ideas of the medieval over the centuries, including the Pardoner’s new life in queer studies, the Wife of Bath’s new life as a feminist, the vicissitudes of the Clerk’s reputation (is he a sage or a sponger?) as the social cachet of advanced humanistic studies waxes and wanes, and of course the increasingly “dialogic” emphasis on the carnivalesque ways in which the Miller’s story rebuts the Knight’s story. Reception history considers such changes wherever they appear—perhaps the commonest instance of which (nearly everyone is aware of it) being the correlation of attitudes toward Shakespeare’s Henry V with bellicose and pacifist national moods.

如今，或许比“接受史”更具影响力的是另一位伽达默尔的学生尤尔根·哈贝马斯提出的“公共领域”概念。哈贝马斯研究了启蒙运动时期思想传播和接受的新环境，并将这一概念广泛应用于媒介变迁的研究，尤其是印刷文化的兴起。尽管雅斯的许多接受史案例都聚焦于单一视野内的异常现象（例如，他在《文学史作为对文学理论的挑衅》一文中对福楼拜的《包法利夫人》和欧内斯特-艾梅·费多的《芬妮》的接受情况进行了富有启发性的对比），但我在此更倾向于将他视为文学史理论的贡献者。另一个密切相关的领域，通常与受众研究相结合，是“媒介史”，尤其是文学研究中的书籍史。书籍史以流通的物质对象（手稿、书籍、病毒式博客）为出发点来理解阅读受众。

Perhaps more influential today than “reception history” is the concept of the “public sphere” introduced by another student of Gadamer, Jürgen Habermas, who studied this new milieu for the circulation and reception of ideas as a feature of the Enlightenment in the eighteenth century, but whose concept has been rather broadly adapted to the study of media shifts, especially the rise of print culture. Although many of Jauss’s examples of reception history focus on anomalies within a single horizon (as in his illuminating contrast between the reception of Flaubert’s Madame Bovary and the reception of Ernest-Aimé Feydeau’s Fanny in “Literary History as a Provocation to Literary Theory”), I assign him in preference here as a contributor to the theory of literary history. Another and closely related field, often combined with audience studies, is “media history,” especially the history of the book in literary scholarship, which takes the material object circulated (manuscript, book, viral blog) as its point of departure for understanding reading audiences.

因此，接受史研究两方面内容：首先，是不断变化的预期视野，即读者在特定时期必须理解文本中既有的惯例及其违背之处，并区分新颖之处与陈旧之处——这种视野并非仅在当下发生一次改变，而是随着时间的推移而不断演变。这一考量主要属于美学范畴。接受史还涉及语义可能性的变化，或者说，意义可能性的变化：文本在特定时期对读者群体而言为何重要？这一考量主要属于诠释范畴。

The history of reception, then, studies two things: first, changing horizons of expectation whereby a reader in a given moment has to come to terms with conventions and their breach in any given text, discriminating between what’s new and what’s merely culinary—horizons that don’t just change once in the here and now but have changed successively through time. This consideration is largely aesthetic. Reception history also involves changing semantic possibilities or, if you will, changing possibilities for and of significance: why does the text matter to a reading public at given times? This consideration is largely interpretive.

举例来说，要说明对历史语境的敏锐感知如何在当下发挥作用，不妨看看最近百老汇复排的音乐剧《该死的扬基佬》（ Damn Yankees）。这部老音乐剧讲述的是一个棒球运动员为了击败扬基队而出卖灵魂的故事，而它首演时，扬基队还被视为不可战胜的劲旅。如今，扬基队不再拥有不可战胜的声誉，人们不禁会想到，《该死的扬基佬》的复兴是否与类固醇丑闻以及众多运动员为了胜利和辉煌的职业生涯而出卖灵魂的现象有关。正是在这种社会和文化谴责的氛围下，我们突然又对《该死的扬基佬》产生了兴趣。 《拖车托尼》（Tony the Tow Truck）诞生于20世纪80年代初，那是一个繁荣的时代，人们需要对富裕带来的种种弊端进行一番批判。或许托尼拖车会再次流行起来，因为在如今经济低迷的时期，像尼托那样富有或光鲜亮丽，或者像斯皮迪那样自私地忙碌，显然都已过时，无关紧要，甚至偏离了主题，真正重要的是小人物之间的互助。如果托尼真的再次流行起来，每个蹒跚学步的孩子都会听到他的声音，父母们也会从中获得乐趣，甚至英语教授们也会用各种应用程序（例如applicare）来解读他的作品。他将在历史上继续存在下去，实现雅斯所设想的三种接受方式。

Just to take examples of how alertness to the historical moment of reception might work in the here and now, there was recently a Broadway revival of Damn Yankees, an old musical about a baseball player who sells his soul to beat the Yankees, produced at a time when the Yankees were considered an invincible machine. One can’t help but think now that the revival of interest in Damn Yankees, at a time when the Yankees no longer have the reputation of invincibility, has something to do with the steroid scandals and the way so many athletes do sell their souls in order to win and to have good careers. It is in this atmosphere of social and cultural censure that we’re suddenly interested in Damn Yankees again. Tony the Tow Truck appeared in the early 1980s, prosperous times when the vices of affluence needed a dressing down. Perhaps there will be a revival of Tony the Tow Truck because now, in the economic downturn, obviously to be rich or glamorous like Neato or selfishly busy like Speedy seems obsolete, more or less irrelevant and beside the point, and what really matters is little guys helping each other. Should this revival occur, Tony will be heard by every toddler, give pleasure to parents, and find itself interpreted (with applications: applicare) by English professors. It will survive to live another day historically, fulfilling the three moments of reception specified by Jauss.

 

 

第十七章

CHAPTER 17

法兰克福学派批判理论
The Frankfurt School of Critical Theory

阅读材料：

Readings:

本雅明，瓦尔特。“机械复制时代的艺术作品。”载《批评传统》，第 1233-1248 页。

Benjamin, Walter. “The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1233–1248.

霍克海默，马克斯，和西奥多·阿多诺。“文化工业。”载《批判传统》，第 1255-1262 页。

Horkheimer, Max, and Theodor Adorno. “The Culture Industry.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1255–1262.

阿多诺的段落。

Passages from Adorno.

当我们开始探讨文学和艺术的社会视角时，你可能会问自己：“为什么是马克思？为什么如此强调马克思？为什么似乎只有马克思才支持这样一种观点：对艺术进行社会批判是研究这一主题的最佳且最相关的方法？” 原因在于，无论马克思主义思想在历史上最终的结论如何，它仍然是对社会错觉最深刻的批判，因为它既启发又制约着艺术作品的历史发展。在下一讲中，我们将讨论弗雷德里克·詹姆逊，而现在我们已经开始探讨瓦尔特·本雅明，我们将看到，马克思主义思想以“政治无意识”的形式揭示了我们对现实的认知以及我们对自身在世界中位置的理解背后的根源。我们首先探讨了语言无意识，或者说语言的预设，然后是精神分析无意识；现在，正如詹姆逊著作的标题所示（我们将在下一讲中阅读该书的节选），我们将探讨政治无意识。

As we move into social perspectives on literature and art, you may ask yourself, “Why Marx? Why so much Marx? Why is it Marx who seems to stand behind the idea that the social criticism of art is the best and most relevant way to approach this subject matter?” Well, it’s because whatever the outcome of Marxist thought may have proven to be or yet prove to be historically, it remains nevertheless the most devastating critique we have of social delusion as it both inspires and conditions works of art historically. When we turn to Fredric Jameson in the next lecture, and already in considering Walter Benjamin now, we’ll see that Marxist thought reveals what stands behind our conception of reality and our understanding of our place in the world in the form of a “political unconscious.” We have first considered a linguistic unconscious, or in any case linguistic preconditioning, then a psychoanalytic unconscious; and now, following the title of Jameson’s book from which we’ll read an excerpt for the next lecture, we arrive at a political unconscious.

对文学和艺术进行社会批判的方法不止一种。在保守派阵营，列奥·施特劳斯关于阿里斯托芬的著作堪称杰作，此外，他对传统政治哲学文本的解读也极具影响力，尤其是从《理想国》入手，并着重强调苏格拉底对诗歌的批判。同时，自由主义的批评传统也十分强大，尤其体现在公共领域的新闻报道中。从社会视角出发的自由主义艺术批评的杰出倡导者或许是莱昂内尔·特里林，特别是他所著的《自由主义的想象》一书中的文章。因此，在政治光谱的其他位置，也存在着以社会为导向的文学研究方法，但迄今为止，文学理论中最普遍的社会批判模式仍然是马克思主义的。当我们继续关注文学时，我们的关注点仍将主要集中在马克思主义美学上。

There are other ways of approaching the social criticism of literature and art. On the conservative front, there is an extraordinary book by Leo Strauss on Aristophanes, together with his influential readings of the traditional texts of political philosophy, beginning with The Republic and laying strong emphasis on Socrates’s critique of poetry. And there is, as well, a very strong liberal tradition of criticism, particularly in the journalism of the public sphere. Perhaps the most notable proponent of a liberal criticism of art undertaken from a social point of view was Lionel Trilling, especially in the essays collected in The Liberal Imagination. So there are and have been socially oriented approaches to literature from other points along the political spectrum, but by far the most pervasive mode of social critique in literary theory remains the Marxist one. As we go on trying to keep at least one eye on literature, our concern will remain primarily with Marxist aesthetics.

与此同时，关于马克思，我们需要了解些什么呢？我希望在这样的课程中，你们大多数人都对思想史和西方文化有所了解，因此对马克思的认识应该与对弗洛伊德的了解相当（福柯所说的这两位都是“话语的奠基人”）。对我们而言，尤其重要的是“意识形态”这个含义模糊的概念，因此值得我们稍作探讨。

In the meantime, what do we need to know about Marx? I hope I can take for granted in a course of this kind that most of you have some familiarity with the history of ideas and with Western culture, hence have some notion of Marx comparable to what you know about Freud (two of Foucault’s “founders of discursivity”). Of special importance to us, hence worth a pause, is the slippery notion of “ideology.”

在马克思和恩格斯的著作以及所有后世马克思主义著作中，意识形态这一概念从未达成过完全一致的共识。这一传统中关于意识形态的分歧主要在于，它是否应该被恰当地归因于对世界的有意识的先入之见，以及无意识的先入之见。如果我从心底里确信月亮是由绿奶酪做成的——我完全意识到这个观点，能够流畅地进行推理，并且能够像堂吉诃德证明风车是巨人一样无可辩驳地证明它——那么问题就来了：我的这种认知是否可以被揭示为意识形态？同样地，一位落魄的贵族准备捍卫等级制度和特权对社会有益的观点，他完全清楚这是一个不受欢迎、或多或少受人尊敬的观点，但他仍然坚持己见，并准备引用权威学者的论证来为其辩护。我们再次面临这样的问题：“这还是意识形态吗？”

In the writings of Marx and Engels and all the Marxist writing that has succeeded them, ideology is a concept about which there has never been wholehearted agreement. The disagreement concerning ideology in this tradition chiefly concerns whether it ought properly to be ascribed to conscious as well as to unconscious preconceptions about the world. If I know to the very core of my being that the moon is made of green cheese—I am fully conscious of this opinion, can reason fluently about it, and can prove it as indubitably as Quixote can prove a windmill is a giant—the question arises whether this knowledge of mine can be demystified as ideology. Just so, a belated aristocrat is prepared to defend the idea that hierarchy and privilege are beneficial to society, perfectly conscious that this is an unpopular, more or less disgraced idea, but committed to it nonetheless and prepared to cite learned authorities in its defense. We again face the question, “Is this still ideology?”

尤其在恩格斯的著作中，甚至可能比在马克思的著作中更甚，答案总体上是肯定的，它仍然是意识形态。我们可以将意识形态定义为一种信念，无论这种信念是有意识的还是无意识的，即持有某种观点就等同于认识真理。意识形态决定了，从我自身意识的物质和经济基础出发，事物呈现的方式不仅是它们呈现的方式，而且是它们实际存在的方式。根据马克思的观点，这种信念模式在不同的历史上依次成为各个统治阶级的特征。随着资本主义的兴起及其向所谓晚期资本主义的演变，这种信念模式被称为“资产阶级意识形态”。在资产阶级的思想中，那些使中产阶级生活得以繁荣发展的理念——职业道德、家庭观念、某些道德行为准则——是所有阶级在任何情况下、任何历史时期都适用的最佳理念。因此，意识形态认为，适合某一组物质条件的思想和行为基础也适合所有物质条件。

Particularly in the writings of Engels, indeed perhaps more than in the writings of Marx, the answer by and large is yes, it is still ideology. We can define ideology as the belief, whether conscious or unconscious, that holding a point of view is knowing the truth. Ideology dictates that the way things appear from the materially and economically grounded standpoint of my own consciousness is not just the way they appear to me but the way they actually are. Now according to Marx, this is a mode of belief that in successive historical periods has characterized each dominant class in turn. With the rise of capitalism and its evolution into what’s called late capitalism, this mode of belief is what’s called “bourgeois ideology.” In the bourgeois mind, the ideas that have enabled middle-class life to flourish—the work ethic, the idea of family, certain codes of moral behavior—are the best ideas for all classes in all circumstances at all historical times. Thus does ideology suppose that the ideas and foundations of behavior suited to one set of material conditions are suited to all.

课程伊始，我们引用了马克思《资本论》中关于商品拜物教的论述。马克思指出，人们往往不假思索地认为，一件商品的劳动价值——即由于投入的劳动量及其相应的实际用途而产生的价值——被一种被认为内在于商品本身的价值所取代，仿佛商品本身就是其存在的主体。这种价值重估同样适用于艺术，本雅明在将艺术的商品化描述为艺术的“光环”时，也暗示了这一点。如果我们忘记了艺术是被生产的——忘记了其生产过程中投入了一定的劳动——而仅仅全神贯注地沉思冥想，仿佛艺术作品本身就具有客观价值——其真实性的光辉——而无需考虑其生产过程，那么我们所做的就是将艺术作品“商品化”。换句话说，从本雅明的角度来看，被艺术作品的光环所诱惑，就是从意识形态上将作品体验为一种商品。

We began the course with the quotation from Marx’s Capital on commodity fetishism. There Marx shows how it is just spontaneously supposed, without reflection, that the labor value of something that’s produced—the value that can accrue to it because of the amount of labor that has gone into it and the accordant amount of practical use that can be derived from it—is superseded by a value that’s thought to be inherent in the product itself as though it were itself the agent of its being. This transvaluation applies as well to art, and it’s something to which Benjamin alludes when he characterizes the commodification of art as its “aura.” If we forget that art is produced—that a certain quantum of labor has gone into its production—and if we then simply address ourselves to the work of art with rapt contemplative absorption as though it had objective value—the glow of its authenticity—apart from having been produced, then what we’re doing is “commodifying” the work of art. From Benjamin’s point of view, in other words, to be seduced by the aura of the work of art is to experience the work ideologically as a commodity.

那么，回到马克思主义批评的美学目标这一问题：我们需要梳理各种不同的传统，这符合一种“有根基的”论述方式；但基本上，马克思主义有四种选择来确定艺术美学的真正本质。从每个角度来看，需要考虑的因素包括：艺术应该如何反映社会？它应该如何构成对社会的批判？它应该如何预测一个理想的、正在形成的、乌托邦式的社会？所有这些问题都是美学问题，因为艺术表达社会的方式——与政治论著不同——必然是美学的。社会表达是通过形式、体裁、风格来实现的——所有这些都被理解为受物质因素制约的生产方式。

To return, then, to the whole question of the aesthetic objectives of Marxist criticism: one needs to sort through a varied tradition, as befits a “founded” discursivity; but there are basically four Marxist options for determining what the aesthetics of art ought actually to be. Factors to be taken into account from every standpoint are, how should art reflect society? How should it constitute a critique of society? How should it predict an ideal, emergent, utopian society? All of these questions are questions of aesthetics because the way art does express the social—as opposed to a political treatise, say—is necessarily aesthetic. Social expression is mediated by form, genre, style—all understood as modes of production that are conditioned by material factors.

马克思和恩格斯自身的审美观——我们首先考虑的——是现实主义的，但他们的现实主义冷静分析，而且相当精妙。当一些怀揣梦想的作家，一心想着要为无产阶级的进步而写作，给恩格斯写信——我想到了费迪南·拉萨尔、米娜·考茨基等人——寄去他们“社会主义现实主义”小说的手稿时，恩格斯并不赞同，他回应说，没有义务歌颂无产阶级，也没有必要以这种方式展望未来。他说，他的通信者应该努力做的，是观察当下社会动态的本来面目——以现实主义而非偏颇的方式理解世界。恩格斯的文学偶像是巴尔扎克，一个保皇派反动分子，但他却成功地描绘了社会的种种复杂性，尤其是阶级结构，恩格斯认为他是现实主义写作的最佳典范。

The aesthetics of Marx and Engels themselves—our first option—was realist, but their realism was dispassionately analytic and quite sophisticated. When aspiring writers, already caught up in the idea that they ought to be writing for the advancement of the proletariat, would write to Engels—I’m thinking of Ferdinand Lassalle, Minna Kautsky, and others—sending him manuscripts of their “socialist realist” novels, Engels disapproved and responded that there was no obligation to glorify the proletariat, no need to project the future in this way. What his correspondents should attempt to do, he said, is to see the social dynamic as it exists in the present moment—to understand the world realistically but not tendentiously. Engels’s literary hero was Balzac, a royalist reactionary who nevertheless successfully evoked society in all of its manifold complexities, especially its class structure, and whom Engels considered the best model for realist writing.

这种美学在马克思主义早期充满活力的时期，包括俄国革命初期，都广泛盛行。1927年，艾肯鲍姆发表了《形式方法论》，海德格尔出版了《存在与时间》 ，本雅明也访问了莫斯科。同年，文学哲学家格奥尔格·卢卡奇写了一本书，名为《历史小说》 。卢卡奇曾是黑格尔主义者，在转向马克思主义思想之前，他写过一部精彩的形而上学沉思录，名为《小说理论》 （1920）。 《历史小说》读起来就像是从恩格斯的信件中摘录出来的。它一方面抨击了卢卡奇认为的现代主义（尤其是乔伊斯和普鲁斯特）的自恋式内省，另一方面，它的论点也与恩格斯在给弟子的信中推荐巴尔扎克的方式如出一辙。卢卡奇推崇沃尔特·斯科特爵士的小说，斯科特像巴尔扎克一样是一位政治反动派，他笔下高地与低地、封建与商业、苏格兰与英格兰、旧社会秩序与新社会秩序之间宏大的辩证平衡，被卢卡奇视为看清阶级关系本质的完美例证。

This aesthetic prevailed widely in Marxism through its early energetic years, including the early years of the Russian Revolution. In 1927, the year of Eikhenbaum’s “Theory of the Formal Method,” of Heidegger’s Being and Time, and of Benjamin’s visit to Moscow, the literary philosopher Georg Lukács wrote a book called The Historical Novel. Lukács had been a Hegelian and had written a brilliant metaphysical meditation called The Theory of the Novel (1920) before he turned to Marxist thought. The Historical Novel reads as though it were taken from Engels’s letters. It’s partly an attack on what Lukács took to be the narcissistic inwardness of high modernism, particularly Joyce and Proust, but its thesis is also argued along the lines chosen by Engels to recommend Balzac in his letters to disciples. Lukács champions the novels of Sir Walter Scott, a political reactionary like Balzac, whose grand dialectical balances between Highland and Lowland, feudal and mercantile, Scotland and England, the old social order and the new Lukács took to be perfect instances of seeing class relations as they really are.

但差不多在《历史小说》问世的同时，随着斯大林的崛起，那些曾经给恩格斯写信的人——考茨基、拉萨尔——的思想开始在苏联思想界​​占据主导地位。一位名叫安德烈·日丹诺夫的文学评论家阐述了社会主义现实主义理论，这一理论在马克西姆·高尔基的作品中得到了充分体现，并在1934年的苏联国际作家大会上被确立为官方理论。这是第二种美学选择。你可能听过这个笑话：男孩遇见拖拉机，男孩弄丢了拖拉机，男孩进城寻找拖拉机，把拖拉机带回乡下，从此过上了幸福的生活。这个基本情节，显然是婚姻情节的变体，但也涉及本雅明所说的“机械复制”，在苏联文学中盛行，形式和意识形态上的偏差都受到审查，直到1989年铁幕落下。

But more or less at the time of The Historical Novel, alongside the rise of Stalin, the ideas of all those people who used to write to Engels—Kautsky, Lassalle—began to prevail in Soviet thought. A literary critic named Andrei Zhdanov articulated a doctrine of socialist realism that was showcased in the writings of Maxim Gorky and espoused as official doctrine at the International Soviet Writer’s Conference in 1934. That was the second aesthetic option. You probably know the joke: boy meets tractor, boy loses tractor, boy goes to the city to find tractor, takes tractor back to the countryside and lives with it happily ever after. This fundamental plot, obviously a variant on the marriage plot but engaged also in what Benjamin would call “mechanical reproduction,” prevailed in Soviet writing, with formal as well as ideological deviations subject to censorship, until the Iron Curtain fell in 1989.

因此，这些是人们通常认为与马克思主义批评和文学创作联系最紧密的现实主义形式。然而，自二十世纪卢卡奇以来，或许最具活力的批评家们已经认识到，现实主义本身就是一种修辞，一种意识形态，已被资产阶级所挪用。还有谁会“实话实说”？还有谁会不断提醒你“现实世界”的存在？还有谁会在餐桌上宣称自己是“现实主义者”？正如中产阶级攫取一切一样，他们也挪用了现实主义的理念，并使其变得庸俗不堪，审美过时。因此，正如我们将在后文中阐述的那样，第三种和第四种选择分别背离了现实主义，转向了形式主义和乌托邦式的浪漫主义。

So those are the forms of realism that are most often identified with Marxist criticism and literary production. Yet probably the most dynamic criticism since Lukács in the twentieth century has recognized that realism is a rhetoric, an ideology in itself, that has been appropriated by the bourgeoisie. Who else “tells it like it is”? Who else keeps reminding you about “the real world”? Who else proclaims around the dinner table that he or she is a “realist”? Just as it commandeers everything else for itself, the middle class has appropriated the idea of realism and made it banal, aesthetically outmoded. Hence, as we shall explain over time, the third and fourth options turn away from realism toward formalism and utopian romance, respectively.

瓦尔特·本雅明既不拥护上述两种可能性，也不支持其他可能性，但他同样敏锐地意识到现实主义的局限性。他认为现实主义是晚期资本主义将灵光商品化的一种形式，是资产阶级艺术和鉴赏的最后挣扎。然而，本雅明并不主张背离现实（这也是我没有将他的观点列为第五种选择的原因）；他敦促人们沉浸于现实之中。对他而言，现实主义的平庸需要用一种参与式美学来对抗：日常生活中碎片化的感知和注意力分散正是这种美学的一部分，但这绝非意味着要背离现实。相反，参与式的艺术家和观众是共同的劳动者，他们参与到将艺术作品带入现实世界的生产方式中。我们将在探讨本雅明的《艺术作品》一文时展开这些讨论。

Walter Benjamin espouses neither of these possibilities, yet he too is acutely conscious of the limits of realism, which he grants to be a late capitalist form of commodifying the aura, a last gasp of bourgeois art and appreciation. Benjamin does not however advocate a departure from the real (which is why I don’t describe his as a fifth option); he urges immersion in it. For him the banality of realism needs to be counteracted with a participatory aesthetic: the fragmentary perceptions and the distracted attention span of daily life are part of this, yet there is no question of turning away from the real. The participatory artist and audience are, on the contrary, communal workers engaged with the very mode of production that ushers the work of art into the real world. We’ll develop these topics when we turn to Benjamin’s “Work of Art” essay.

或许，马克思主义批评家最不寻常的审美倾向体现在阿多诺身上（第三种选择）。西奥多·阿多诺所推崇的，恰恰是卢卡奇在《历史小说》中所批判的那种高度现代主义美学。他推崇文学上的贝克特，音乐上的勋伯格、贝尔格和韦伯恩。（阿多诺接受过音乐学训练，并将大部分写作生涯投入到关于音乐和音乐史的论文和专著中。）这些现代主义者是阿多诺心目中的英雄，这引发了一个问题：那些对社会关系并无深刻见解、主要关注自身创作媒介、似乎对整个历史进程漠不关心（除了他们创作媒介的历史之外）的艺术家，怎能成为马克思主义批评家的审美标杆？这个问题的答案在《论音乐中的拜物教特征与聆听的倒退》一文中有所阐述，我在附录中摘录了其中的两段。我想就此稍作停留，因为我认为阿多诺的文章深刻地区分了艺术形式所提供的整体性或完整性，以及现代霸权政府形式所强加的总体化或极权主义——无论是显而易见的极权主义，还是像他专门论述的“文化工业”（你读过的那篇文章就是对此的论述）那样隐蔽的极权主义。

Perhaps the most unusual aesthetic move for a Marxist critic is the one that you will find in Adorno (the third option). Theodor Adorno was devoted to precisely what Lukács had attacked in The Historical Novel, namely, the high modernist aesthetic. He admired Beckett in literature, Schönberg, Berg, and Webern in music. (Adorno was by training a musicologist and devoted much of his writing career to essays and treatises on music and the history of music.) These modernists were heroes in Adorno’s pantheon, provoking the question of how artists who have nothing striking to say about social relations, who are largely preoccupied with the medium they work in, and who seem to be indifferent to the whole course of history (apart from the history of their medium) can be the aesthetic benchmarks of a Marxist critic. The answer to this question is worked out in “On the Fetish-Character in Music and the Regression of Listening,” from which I’ve given you two excerpts in the appendix. I want to pause over them because I think Adorno’s essay incisively distinguishes between the totality, or wholeness, that’s offered by artistic form and the mere totalization or totalitarianism that’s imposed by modern hegemonic forms of government—whether obviously totalitarian or insidiously totalitarian, like the “culture industry” to which he devotes the essay that you’ve read.

这就是阿多诺在这两段文字中所说的。他描述了那些受文化产业影响、自以为是地欣赏音乐的人是如何完全沦为花腔局部效果的受害者的，你可以称之为——阿多诺憎恶的指挥家——托斯卡尼尼效应：强调作品中的某个特定片段，将其发挥到极致，却牺牲了整体，以及所有炫技的技巧，这些技巧展现了阿多诺在其他地方所说的“令人垂涎的悦耳之声”；换句话说，就是为了追求局部音响的完美而牺牲对整体作品的理解。他在第一段文字中写道：

So this is what Adorno says in these two passages. He’s describing the way people who enjoy, or think they enjoy, music under the sway of the culture industry are completely victimized by coloratura local effects, what you might call—this is a conductor whom Adorno hated—the Toscanini effect: the highlighting of a particular moment in a composition, riding it into the ground at the expense of the whole, and all the virtuoso turns that show off what Adorno elsewhere calls “lip-smacking euphony”; in other words, cultivating the perfection of local sound at the expense of comprehending the total composition. So he says in the first passage:

当下的愉悦和表面上的欢愉成为一种借口，使听者得以逃避对整体的思考，而整体的意义恰恰在于正确的聆听。听者沿着阻力最小的路径（毕竟，聆听如此美妙），最终沦为默许的购买者。局部不再像现代主义中那样，对整体进行批判（换句话说，不和谐本身就是对我们通常认为与整体性相关的那种宏大和谐的批判。因此，从某种意义上说，部分可以被理解为对整体的批判，而无需挑战或破坏整体。）；相反，它们暂停了成功的审美整体对社会缺陷所施加的批判。 [斜体为笔者所加]
The delight in the moment and the gay façade become an excuse for absolving the listener from the thought of the whole, whose claim is comprised in proper listening. The listener is converted, along his line of least resistance [because after all, it’s so beautiful to listen to], into the acquiescent purchaser. No longer do the partial moments serve as a critique of the whole [as they sometimes do in Modernism. Dissonance, in other words, is in and of itself a critique of that overarching harmony that we associate with wholeness. So there’s a real sense in which the parts can be understood as a critique of the whole without challenging or breaking down the whole.]; instead, they suspend the critique which the successful esthetic totality exerts against the flawed one of society. [italics mine]

换言之，唯有艺术作品中真正达到的完整性才能批判社会整体的虚假性。这两种“整体”概念之间的差异，恰恰构成了批判的领域，它或许——仅仅是或许——能够唤醒文化产业的受害者，使他们从安于现状的顺从和默许中醒来。

In other words, nothing can criticize the inauthenticity of the bad totalities of society except the authenticity of genuinely achieved wholeness in a work of art. The difference between these senses of the whole is precisely the zone of critique that might—just might—awaken the victim of the culture industry from the slumbers of happy conformism and acquiescence.

现在来看第二段，只是为了进一步说明这一点：

Now the second passage, just to reinforce this:

像贝尔格、勋伯格和韦伯恩这样的伟大现代主义作曲家被其他马克思主义批评家，以及那些不喜欢卢卡奇所谓的“形式拜物教”（即以牺牲社会指涉和表达为代价来物化形式）的人称为个人主义者，然而他们的作品不过是与那些摧毁个性的力量进行的一场对话——这些力量的“无形阴影”巨大地投射在他们的音乐之上。在音乐中，集体力量也在消灭一种无法挽救的个性，但只有个体才能自觉地代表集体的目标，与之抗衡。
Great Modernist composers like Berg, Schönberg and Webern are called individualists [by other Marxist critics, by people who don’t like what Lukács would call “fetishization of form,” reification of form at the expense of social reference and expression], and yet their work is nothing but a single dialogue with the powers that destroy individuality—powers whose “formless shadows” fall gigantically on their music. In music, too, collective powers are liquidating an individuality past saving, but against them only individuals are capable of consciously representing the aims of collectivity.

艺术作品的整体性——即已实现的、成功的、真实的整体性——以一种任何当今国家虚假的整体性都无法企及的方式，模拟了集体国家的理想整体性。换言之，阿多诺认为，纯粹的形式中蕴含着一种进步的政治理念。纯粹形式的实现，归根结底，是由各个部分组成的，它模拟了集体社会的实现。

The totality—the achieved, successful, authentic totality—of the work of art models the utopian totality of a collective state in ways that none of the false totalities of current states can even approximate. In other words, there is an implicit progressive politics, Adorno argues, in pure form. The achievement of pure form, which is, after all, a collection of parts, models the achievement of a collective society.

这是一种引人入胜的思维转变。它略显理想化，因为很难想象它会带来实际的结果。试想一下，有人听了勋伯格的音乐后说：“天哪，也许我应该成为一名共产主义者。”但这仍然是对马克思主义思想所假定的西方文明主流美学——对整体性的迷恋——的一种具有挑战性的辩证逆转（阿多诺或许是自黑格尔以来最精妙的辩证法学家）。想想新批评如何强调诗歌的统一性，强调将离散的本体论对象视为一个统一的整体。这正是马克思主义批评通常抨击的陈词滥调，而阿多诺却将离散的本体论对象视为集体性的典范，而非自恋式个体性的典范，这着实令人赞叹。

This is a fascinating turn of thought. It’s somewhat quixotic because it’s hard to imagine a practical result. Imagine somebody listening to Schönberg and saying, “Gosh, maybe I should become a communist.” But it is still a challenging dialectical reversal (Adorno is perhaps the most subtle dialectician since Hegel) of what Marxist thought supposes to be the mainstream aesthetic of Western civilization: the fetishization of wholeness. Think of the New Criticism laying stress on the unity of the poem, on the discrete ontological object as a unified whole. This is the commonplace typically attacked by commonplace Marxist criticism, and it’s quite wonderful that Adorno sees the discrete ontological object not as a model of narcissistic individuality but of collectivity.

马克思主义的最后一个美学选择，也是下一讲的部分内容，令人惊讶。它源于恩斯特·布洛赫的三卷本著作《希望的原则》（1938-1947）。布洛赫在书中论证——在这方面很大程度上预示了阿多诺——在我们所处的晚期资本主义世界中，希望已然破灭。布洛赫用一种观点反驳了这种悲观的看法：尤其是在民间艺术、民俗、口头文化和大众文化中——也就是说，在被剥夺者和被压迫者的作品中所表达的渴望中——存在着一种乌托邦主义、一种浪漫情怀，以及一种并非是对过去事物的怀念（尽管它看似怀旧），而是对现实世界中根本不可能实现的未来的一种投射。

The last aesthetic option for Marxism, in part the subject of the next lecture, is another surprising one. It goes back to a three-volume work by Ernst Bloch called The Principle of Hope (1938–1947) in which Bloch essentially argues—in this respect largely anticipating Adorno—that in the late capitalist world as we inhabit it there is no longer any hope available. This dark outlook Bloch counters with the idea that especially in folk art, folkways, oral culture, and popular culture—that is, in the expressions of longing one finds in the work of the dispossessed and the oppressed—there is a kind of utopianism, a romance, and a sense not so much of wishing for something past, even though it seems to take the form of nostalgia, but rather of projecting a possibility on the future that is simply unavailable in the real world.

我能想到的最佳例子是《大岩糖山》，这首歌由劳改营的囚犯唱着，歌颂着酒水顺着山坡流淌成溪，以及一切如他们所愿的美好景象。弗雷德里克·詹姆逊认真地采纳了布洛赫的观点，这并非体现在你即将读到的《政治无意识》节选中，而是体现在该书导论章节的前半部分。在那部分中，他探讨了浪漫主义在取代破产的现实主义美学方面的重要作用，它在一个看似绝望的世界中表达了被压迫者和被剥夺者的希望。

The best example I can think of is “The Big Rock Candy Mountain,” sung by people on chain gangs about liquor running down the sides of mountains in rivulets and everything else just as they wish it to be. Bloch’s idea is picked up and taken very seriously by Fredric Jameson, not so much in the excerpt from The Political Unconscious that you’ll be reading but in an earlier part of that introductory chapter in which he discusses the important role of romance in replacing the bankrupt aesthetic of realism, expressing in a seemingly hopeless world the hopes of the oppressed and the dispossessed.

然而，今天我们将聚焦于本雅明的参与式美学和阿多诺的现代主义整体论。你会发现它们之间存在着冲突。阿多诺的《恋物癖人物》（1938）实际上是对本雅明《艺术作品》一文的一种友好回应；但《文化工业》在某种程度上也是一种回应。阿多诺是本雅明的挚友，两人曾通信反驳《艺术作品》一文的观点——这些信件后来发表在1973年的《新左派评论》上，对于任何想要探究他们之间争论背后有趣含义的人来说，都值得一读。

Today, however, we zero in on the participatory aesthetic of Benjamin and the modernist totality of Adorno. You can see the way they conflict with each other. Adorno’s “Fetish Character” essay (1938) was actually a response, in friendly disagreement, to Benjamin’s “Work of Art” essay; but “The Culture Industry,” too, is in its way a response. Adorno was a close friend of Benjamin’s and exchanged letters with him disputing the claims of the “Work of Art” essay—letters that were republished in the New Left Review of 1973 and are well worth reading for anyone who wishes to pursue the interesting implications of their disagreement.

阿多诺和本雅明同为法兰克福社会研究所（又称“法兰克福学派”）的成员。该学派的成员在逃离纳粹魔爪（许多人移居美国）之前，创作了大量重要的辩证思想著作，融合了马克思和弗洛伊德的洞见，并着重探讨极权主义的根源（例如阿多诺的论文《权威人格》和《反犹主义与法西斯宣传》）。其中最著名的作品是与马克斯·霍克海默合著的《启蒙辩证法》，您引用的正是出自该书。在20世纪60年代和70年代的美国，这一学派最著名的代表作是赫伯特·马尔库塞的《爱欲与文明》。除了霍克海默之外，弗里德里希·波拉克和西格弗里德·克拉考尔（他的“大众装饰”理论探讨了文化拜物教，阿多诺亦是如此）也发表了与我们主题相关的重要著作。我在上一讲中提到的该学派的一位年轻成员，也是当今最杰出的代表人物，是尤尔根·哈贝马斯。然而，他的观点更接近自由人文主义，而非其导师和同事们最终走向非革命性的辩证唯物主义。

Adorno and Benjamin were members together of the Frankfurt Institute for Social Research, or “Frankfurt School,” which—before its members fled the Nazis, many emigrating to the United States—produced volumes of important dialectical thought combining the insights of Marx and Freud and focused on the roots of totalitarianism (as in Adorno’s essays, “The Authoritarian Personality” and “Anti-Semitism and Fascist Propaganda”). The best known of these works is The Dialectic of Enlightenment, written with Max Horkheimer, from which your excerpt is taken. In this country during the 1960s and 1970s the best-known work emanating from this circle was Herbert Marcuse’s Eros and Civilization. In addition to Horkheimer, Friedrich Pollak and Siegfried Kracauer (whose theory of the “mass ornament” explores the cultural fetish, as does Adorno) published important work of relevance to our subject. A younger member of this school whom I mentioned in the last lecture, and who is the most prominent of them all today, is Jürgen Habermas, whose viewpoint, however, is closer to liberal humanism than to the ultimately nonrevolutionary dialectical materialism of his mentors and colleagues.

本雅明在20世纪30年代曾短暂地成为一名坚定的马克思主义批评家。此前，他更感兴趣的是卡巴拉文献和黑格尔哲学传统，即使在30年代，他也常常在两种可能性之间摇摆不定。莫斯科之行后，他对苏联世界仍然充满活力，或者至少与他自身文化截然不同的文化产生了浓厚的兴趣。在魅力四射的阿斯娅·拉西斯的引荐下，他还与马克思主义剧作家贝托尔特·布莱希特建立了密切的友谊，布莱希特的影响在他的《艺术作品》一文中清晰可见。但另一位同样对他影响深远的挚友是犹太神学家格尔绍姆·肖勒姆，这位犹太复国主义者移居耶路撒冷，并希望本雅明能与他一起在那里学习卡巴拉。本雅明从肖勒姆、他自身博采众长的学识，或许也间接地从布洛赫那里汲取了“弥赛亚式”存在的概念，这种存在可以在历史中辨识出来，并可能拥有救赎历史的力量——这一概念在他最后的著作《历史哲学提纲》中得到了精辟而精彩的阐述。（1940年，本雅明试图移民美国，但西班牙政府决定将他所在难民营的所有人遣返回维希法国，他最终自杀身亡。）

Benjamin was only for a brief period in the 1930s a committed Marxist critic. He had hitherto been much more interested in Kabbalistic literature and in the Hegelian tradition of philosophy, and even in the 1930s he was famously torn between two possibilities. After his Moscow visit, he had become interested in what was still a vibrant or in any case strikingly different culture in the Soviet world.
