Thanks to the intercession of the charismatic Asja Lacis, he had also formed a close friendship with the Marxist playwright Bertolt Brecht, whose influence can be felt in the “Work of Art” essay. But another very close and equally influential friend was the Jewish theologian Gershom Scholem, a Zionist who emigrated to Jerusalem and wanted Benjamin to join him studying the Kabbalah there. From Scholem, from his own eclectic learning, and perhaps distantly from Bloch, Benjamin absorbed the idea of a “messianic” presence, discernable within history, that may have the power to redeem history—an idea worked out epigrammatically and brilliantly in his last work, “Theses on the Philosophy of History.” (While attempting to emigrate to the United States in 1940, Benjamin committed suicide when the government in Spain decided to send everyone in his refugee camp back to Vichy France.)

《艺术作品》一文是本雅明最著名的、系统阐述马克思主义思想的作品，但他1936年发表的一篇题​​为《作为生产者的作者》的短文也同样值得关注。在这篇文章中，本雅明探讨了他在《艺术作品》一文中曾略微提及的一个问题：在俄国，人们评判一个人，不仅看他能否胜任工作，还看他能否谈论工作本身，能否就此撰写宣传册或给报社写信，能否参与其中；不仅要参与劳动，还要参与对劳动的反思，这使得每个生产者同时也能成为作者。本雅明在《艺术作品》一文中，很大程度上是通过暗示的方式，建议人们以这种方式参与其中——当然，如果说他真的提出了什么建议的话。

The “Work of Art” essay is Benjamin’s best-known piece of sustained Marxist thinking, but a shorter essay of 1936 called “The Author as Producer” is also of interest. Here Benjamin takes up an issue he mentions in passing in “The Work of Art” essay: his observation that in Russia everybody is judged not just for being able to do a job but for being able to talk about doing the job, to write a brochure or a letter to the paper about it, to participate; to be engaged not just in the labor force but also in reflections on the labor force, enabling everyone who is a producer to be an author as well. To become involved in this way is what Benjamin recommends, largely by implication, in the “Work of Art” essay—insofar, that is, as he can be said to recommend anything.

任何读过《机械复制时代的艺术作品》的人都会注意到，本雅明对“灵韵”怀有强烈的怀旧之情，而这种灵韵恰恰是进步艺术及其侵入性装置旨在摒弃的艺术属性。对于本雅明来说，要打破灵韵，代之以机械复制中可能具有解放意义的亲身参与，并非易事。他尤其钟情于维多利亚时代摄影师如朱莉娅·玛格丽特·卡梅隆的柔焦肖像作品，这些作品近乎颓废地追求着灵韵。

No one reading “The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction” can fail to notice that Benjamin evinces strong nostalgia for the “aura,” the very attribute of art that progressive art with its invasive apparatus is meant to jettison. It’s not an easy thing for Benjamin to say we have to tear down the aura and replace it with hands-on involvement, liberatory as that may be, in mechanical reproduction. He had a particular weakness for the soft-focus portraits of such Victorian photographers as Julia Margaret Cameron, which are an almost decadent effort to cultivate the auratic.

谁又能责怪他呢？上世纪六十年代，我还是个学生的时候，在伯克利校园里的一家美术用品和画框店断断续续地打工。所有学生都需要画来装饰房间，所以我们店里堆满了梵高的《向日葵》和马蒂斯的《舞者》，还有一些其他的热门作品，都是18乘24英寸的尺寸，我们称之为“笔触版画”。它们被裱在硬纸板上，上面压着一台巨大的压印机，在版画上压出笔触的纹理。如果你在学期初眯起眼睛仔细看，就能看到这些版画堆的高度逐渐降低，就像延时摄影一样。等到这些版画堆都被收起来，你就能确定数百名学生的房间里都挂满了梵高的《向日葵》和马蒂斯的《舞者》。这难道就是机械复制的产物吗？这种现象作为一种美学价值，又能从中发现什么呢？

And who could blame him? When I was a student in the 1960s I worked on and off in an art supply and picture framing store on the Berkeley campus. All the students needed pictures for their rooms, so we had huge stacks of Van Gogh’s Sunflowers and Matisse’s Dancers and a few other surefire hits, all of them eighteen-by-twenty-four, which we called “brushstroke prints.” They were mounted on cardboard, and a huge stamping machine of some kind had come down on top of them, embossing the prints with the appearance of brushstrokes. If you squinted at the beginning of a semester you could see the stacks of prints diminishing in height, as in time-lapse photography. When the stacks were gone you knew for a fact that hundreds of students’ rooms were festooned with Van Gogh’s Sunflowers and Matisse’s Dancers. Was this the fruit of mechanical reproduction? What value could anyone find in this phenomenon as an aesthetic?

没错，这确实把艺术品从博物馆里带了出来。人们不必再花钱排长队，透过别人巨大的帽子瞥一眼《蒙娜丽莎》。但是，用那些小小的笔触版画来代替对艺术史的深入了解，又怎能算是进步呢？这些看似是对本雅明论点的挑战，但我举这个例子的重点在于，本雅明并非对此一无所知。他非常清楚，他所倡导的美学的最大威胁在于它很容易被资本主义劫持，而且很可能真的会被劫持。我有点跑题了，因为这正是阿多诺反驳他论点时所要探讨的，我之后也确实想谈谈阿多诺，但现在我还是先回到本雅明的话题上来吧。

Yes, it takes the work of art out of the museum. Nobody has to pay to wait in a long line and get a peep at the Mona Lisa around somebody’s enormous hat. But how can the substitution of those little brushstroke prints for a decent acquaintance with art history be considered progressive? These may seem like challenges to Benjamin’s thesis, but it has really been the point of my anecdote that Benjamin is not unaware of them. He knows very well that the greatest threat to the aesthetic he propounds is that it can easily be hijacked by capitalism and probably will be. I’m getting ahead of myself, because that’s precisely what Adorno retorts in opposing his argument and I do wish to turn to that, but I shall return for now to Benjamin.

本雅明1933年后定居巴黎，而阿多诺则去了美国，他厌恶美国。阿多诺在美国时期的著作，例如《最低限度的道德》 ，所展现的悲观世界观，与其说是源于他在魏玛共和国时期所经历的脆弱的民主形式（尽管这些经历令人不安），不如说是源于纳粹主义的兴起（因为他从未怀疑过纳粹主义的出现）；他作为社会观察家所感受到的最深切的悲观，源于他对美国文化的接触。他觉得我们的流行文化令人难以忍受。他无法忍受“爵士乐”。要知道，当时还没有比波普爵士乐的时代，我一直觉得，如果阿多诺再多待一段时间，或许就能接受不再是保罗·怀特曼（指挥家）所代表的那种爵士乐了；但即便如此，也令人怀疑。阿多诺也厌恶电影，这种厌恶程度甚至让他与电影爱好者本雅明产生了分歧，尽管本雅明在“好莱坞”问题上与他持相同观点。 《艺术作品》一文赞扬了电影的进步潜力；《恋物癖角色》一文则以对电影的些许讽刺回应，但它对本雅明的批判却显得迂回，因为它聚焦于音乐的衰落。不过，我们还是能猜到阿多诺的想法。我刚看了一部叫《1940年的百老汇旋律》的电影，弗雷德·阿斯泰尔和埃莉诺·鲍威尔在里面跳踢踏舞。阿斯泰尔和他的搭档乔治·墨菲原本默默无闻，却被选中成为埃莉诺·鲍威尔的舞伴。这简直就是塞缪尔·斯迈尔斯式的成功故事，充满了朗朗上口的旋律，以及两位男主角高尚的资产阶级自我牺牲精神。这部电影相当精彩，但它的拍摄目的显然是为了激怒阿多诺。

Benjamin lived in Paris after 1933, and Adorno had gone to the United States, which he hated. Adorno’s gloomy view of the world in books of the American period like Minima Moralia is not so much the result of his experience of the weak forms of democracy in the Weimar Republic, ominous as those experiences were; not even so much the rise of Nazism because he had never doubted that would happen; the deepest gloom he felt as a social observer resulted from his exposure to American culture. He found our popular culture unbearable. He couldn’t stand “jazz.” Remember this was not yet the age of bebop, and I’ve always felt that maybe if Adorno had hung around a little longer he could have been reconciled to what was no longer the jazz of the aptly named conductor Paul Whiteman; but even that is doubtful. Adorno disliked the movies, too, to an extent that put him at odds with the cineaste Benjamin, who agreed with him in any case about “Hollywood.” The “Work of Art” essay had celebrated the progressive potential of film; the “Fetish Character” essay responds with a few sideswipes at film but renders its critique of Benjamin oblique by focusing on the degradation of music. Still, one knows what Adorno thought. I just saw a film called “Broadway Melody of 1940” with Fred Astaire and Eleanor Powell tap dancing. Astaire and his sidekick, George Murphy, are snatched out of obscurity to be the dance partners of Eleanor Powell. It’s a perfect Samuel Smiles success story, replete with catchy tunes and the need for nobly bourgeois self-sacrifice on the part of both male leads. This film, which was quite enjoyable, was made to incur the wrath of Adorno.

阿多诺预见了20世纪五六十年代社会学中那种痴迷于美国式顺从的潮流。他将个人主义的衰落归咎于文化产业的压迫，后者审视我们所有的怪癖、奇特之处和细微的原创性，以寻找市场价值。孩子们说的最古怪的话都能找到市场，很快，每个古怪的个性都变成了其他人的翻版。在阿多诺看来，人们无法摆脱文化产业的监视和支配。与此相反，阿多诺异想天开地探讨了艺术整体性的力量——只要它不被炫技的表演元素所玷污。例如，他认为音乐作品应该停留在脑海中，就像国际象棋大师脑海中的一盘棋；而且，即使要为非保守的听众演奏，也应该用听起来普通的乐器演奏，不加任何修饰。

Adorno anticipated that whole trend in the sociology of the 1950s and 1960s that was obsessed with American conformism. He ascribes the eclipse of the individual to the oppressive thumb of the culture industry, which scrutinizes for market value our very eccentricities, our very quirks and little originalities. A market is found for the darndest things kids say, and soon every madcap personality is a simulacrum of all the others. For Adorno there is no sideways escape from the surveillance and dominance of the culture industry. Against all that, Adorno quixotically ranges the forces of artistic totality—as long as it is not contaminated by the bravura elements of performance. He felt, for example, that musical compositions should be suspended in the mind, like a chess match in the mind of a grandmaster; and that, when they are performed at all for nonregressive listeners, they should be played colorlessly on ordinary-sounding instruments.

正如我之前所指出的，《机械复制时代的艺术作品》一文深受1934年以前俄罗斯艺术的影响，尤其是吉加·维尔托夫的电影——在这些电影中，路人和从事各种工作的人们构成了连续场景的内容；此外，还有其他一些作品也将观众置于参与者的位置。在这样的语境下，本雅明可以毫不含糊地断言，艺术作品的基座已被移除。我们不再像过去那样双手合十，如痴如醉地膜拜，而是与艺术作品融为一体；我们成为了它们的一部分。

“The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction” is influenced, as I’ve suggested, by the promise of Russian art before 1934: the films of Dziga Vertov in particular, where passersby and persons performing tasks are the content of successive scenes, and by other examples that cast the spectator as a participant. In such contexts, Benjamin can unequivocally affirm the removal of the pedestal from beneath the work of art. We no longer clasp our hands in rapturous adoration but become engaged with works of art; we become part of them.

在这篇文章中，参与主要通过表征机制对被表征领域的介入而实现。本雅明用这个复杂的概念来表达的是，观众是从生产方式的角度来观看对象，观看所讨论的领域——也就是说，观众通过加入生产过程而参与其中。最显而易见的是，当我观看一部电影时，我——当然是必然地——是从摄影机的角度来观看这部电影；换句话说，我的眼睛与摄影机的眼睛融为一体。在战前出版的《柏林故事集》中，克里斯托弗·伊舍伍德将其中一个故事命名为《我是一台摄影机》。我常常觉得，伊舍伍德关于“成为一台摄影机”的概念与柏林人本雅明的作品中出现的这一概念之间存在某种联系——这无疑是一种巧合。

In this essay, participation takes place primarily through the intrusion of the representational apparatus into the represented field. What Benjamin means by this complicated idea is that the spectator sees the object, sees whatever the field in question is, from the standpoint of the mode of production—that is to say, the spectator participates by joining the process of production. Most obviously this means that when I watch a film, I see the film—necessarily of course—from the standpoint of the camera eye; my eye, in other words, joins that of the camera. In his prewar Berlin Stories, Christopher Isherwood entitled one story “I Am a Camera.” I have often thought there’s some sort of bond between Isherwood’s notion of being a camera and the way in which this notion appears—by a happy coincidence, no doubt—in the work of the Berlin native, Benjamin.

共享镜头视角会带来什么后果？首先，观众因此变成了评论家。本雅明不断将镜头视角比作“测试”，甚至比作职业能力测试。这就好比舞台上的试镜——在导演面前表演、背诵剧本台词——被电影演员在镜头前永无休止的“试镜”所取代。摄像机记录着演员的表演，并可以选择在后期舍弃不满意的部分。因此，镜头前的演员就像求职者参加职业能力测试一样，不断地接受着考验和试镜。

What is the consequence of sharing the camera’s eye? For one thing, the spectator by this means becomes a critic. Benjamin keeps comparing the eye of the camera with a “test.” He even compares it with a vocational aptitude test. It’s as though what would count as an audition on the stage—appearing before the director, reciting certain lines of the script—were substituted for by the perpetual auditioning of the film actor before the camera. The camera records what the film actor is doing and has the option of throwing out what isn’t any good later on. Thus the actor in front of the camera is constantly being tested and auditioned in just the way that you might be tested or auditioned if you took a vocational aptitude test for a job.

如果观众换位思考，以摄像机的视角观看电影，她自己就成了评论家，就像体育迷一样。本雅明从布莱希特那里借用了体育迷的比喻。他丝毫没有假装成为这种评论家就等同于成为一名优秀的评论家；完全不是。本雅明并非有意贬低电影，但他同意那些比他更不屑一顾的人的观点：我们去看电影只是为了消遣，因为我们很累。事实上，他认为，我们通常都是心不在焉的。因此，我们是评论家，是积极的参与者，但同时我们又是处于心不在焉状态的评论家。德语中有一个词是“Zerstreuung”。我们心不在焉，即使以摄像机的视角观看事物，也无法真正集中注意力。

If the spectator then takes the camera’s eye position, she herself becomes a critic, like a sports fan. Benjamin takes the sports fan analogy from Brecht. He doesn’t pretend for a moment that to become a critic of this kind is to become a good critic; not at all. Without intending disparagement of film, Benjamin agrees with people who say more disdainfully than he that we go to the movies when we’re tired and just want to be entertained. In fact, he argues, we are characteristically distracted. We are critics, then, hence active participants, yet at the same time we are critics in a state of distraction. The German word is Zerstreuung. We are zerstreut, not quite paying attention even while we are seeing things from the camera-eye point of view.

我稍后会再谈到分心的问题，但首先，从相机视角观察事物是一种特权，因为它揭示了我们通常不会注意到的现实层面：慢动作、不寻常的角度等等。本雅明曾评论过这些效果（1235）：“借助某些技术，例如放大或慢动作，摄影复制可以捕捉到自然视觉无法捕捉到的影像”；后来他又给这些效果命名（1245）：“相机让我们接触到无意识的光学现象，正如精神分析让我们接触到无意识的冲动一样。” 通过揭示光学的无意识，相机打破了我们的固有观念，提醒我们事物的本来面目并非我们所见。这并不是说我们用幻觉取代了现实。相机本身也可能存在偏见。慢动作是一种显而易见的偏见，加速也是一种显而易见的偏见；但我们逐渐意识到，我们观察事物的速度也是一种偏见。精神分析中的无意识也并非揭示真相。梦境并不会揭示与意识所审视的神秘世界截然不同的现实。梦境对意识提出的挑战来自无意识中唤起的世界；它并不提出何为真实、何为虚幻的问题。这和摄像机的视角如出一辙，只不过我们体验它的方式并不十分复杂。

I’ll come back to distraction in a minute, but first, to see things from the camera-eye point of view is a position of privilege because it exposes aspects of reality that we wouldn’t otherwise notice: slow motion, unusual angles, and so on. Benjamin remarks upon these effects (1235): “photographic reproduction, with the aid of certain processes, such as enlargement or slow motion, can capture images which escape natural vision”; then later he gives these effects a name (1245): “The camera introduces us to unconscious optics just as does psychoanalysis to unconscious impulses.” In exposing an optical unconscious, the camera demystifies our ideology by reminding us that things as we see them aren’t necessarily the way things are. It’s not that we trade illusion for reality by this means. The camera, too, may have its bias. Slow motion is an obvious bias, speed-up is an obvious bias; but we are made to realize that the speed at which we see things is a bias, too. The psychoanalytic unconscious doesn’t tell the truth either. Dreams don’t expose a reality in contrast with the mystified world surveyed by consciousness. The dream poses a challenge to consciousness from the world evoked in the unconscious; it doesn’t pose the question of what’s real and what isn’t real. Well, it’s the same with the camera’s-eye point of view, with the added complication that we don’t experience it in a very sophisticated way.

记住，观众是分心的——zerstreut。那么，接下来呢？关键在于：分心与震撼之间存在着一种辩证关系，本雅明认为，这种关系对于任何渐进式的审美启示都至关重要。或许最好的比喻就是扫罗前往大马士革的路上。你肯定知道这个故事：扫罗骑着马小跑，心不在焉。他分了神，突然从马上摔了下来。这是一种震撼，一种依赖于先前分心的震撼，正是这种震撼促使扫罗皈依了基督教。他站起身，拍拍身上的尘土，从此改名为保罗。分心是启示的震撼得以发生的氛围或媒介，因此，对于观众兼批评家来说，漫不经心地吞下爆米花是一件好事——尽管阿多诺对此感到恐惧。

Remember, the spectator is distracted—zerstreut. Well, what then? The point is this: there is a dialectic between distraction and shock that is crucial, Benjamin thinks, for any progressive aesthetic revelation. Perhaps the best analogy is Saul on the road to Damascus. You know how the story goes: Saul is trotting along on his horse and not paying a lot of attention. He’s distracted, and all of a sudden he falls off his horse. That’s a shock, a shock dependent on a prior distraction, such a shock indeed that Saul is converted to Christianity. He stands up, brushes himself off, and his name is Paul. Distraction is the atmosphere or medium in which the shock of revelation can take place, and that’s why it’s a good thing—though horrifying for Adorno to contemplate—for the spectator-critic to be swallowing popcorn inattentively.

我们或许是那种在电影院里全神贯注的人，因此很难被震撼。然而，本雅明令人信服地指出，有一种艺术形式，我们大多数人都是在心不在焉的状态下接受的。我们仅仅是路过建筑，便能感受到它的存在。我每天都在耶鲁英国艺术中心工作，因此我早已不再关注这座建筑本身。换句话说，我是在心不在焉的状态下“接受”路易·康的两座最伟大的建筑之一，但这并不意味着它不是我审美体验的一部分。这表明，审美以及我们处理世界形态的方式，可以在多种注意力状态下被吸收。从某种意义上说，欣赏作为庇护所的建筑，是与生俱来的。但与此同时，除非我们是惊叹于泰姬陵的游客——本雅明确实考虑到了这一点——除非我们处于那种特定的状态，否则我们接受我们住所的形式，就处于一种你可以称之为建设性分心的状态——所有这些都促成了本雅明的参与美学。

We may be the sorts of people who actually pay a lot of attention at the cinema, hence can’t be shocked. Benjamin convincingly shows, though, that there’s one art form that all of us receive most of the time in a state of distraction. We receive architecture simply by passing through it. I work in the Yale Center for British Art every day, hence I’ve long since ceased to pay any attention to the British Art Center as a building. I “receive” one of Louis Kahn’s two greatest buildings, in other words, in a state of distraction, but that doesn’t mean it’s not part of my aesthetic experience. What it shows is that the aesthetic and the ways in which we process the forms of the world can be assimilated in more than one state of attention. It is in one’s bones, in a certain sense, to appreciate architecture as shelter; yet at the same time, unless we are tourists gaping at the Taj Mahal—and Benjamin does take this into account—unless we are in that particular mode, we receive the forms of our dwellings in a state of what you might call constructive distraction—all of which contributes to Benjamin’s aesthetic of participation.

接下来我们转向詹姆逊，他早期对法兰克福学派思想，特别是阿多诺思想的研究，可以在一本名为《马克思主义与形式》的书中找到。

We turn next to Jameson, whose early studies of Frankfurt School thought, especially that of Adorno, will be found in a book called Marxism and Form.

 

 

第十八章

CHAPTER 18

政治无意识
The Political Unconscious

阅读材料：

Readings:

詹姆逊，弗雷德里克。“政治无意识。”载于《批判传统》，第 1291-1306 页。

Jameson, Fredric. “The Political Unconscious.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1291–1306.

摘自詹姆逊和马克思的段落。

Passages from Jameson and Marx.

上次我探讨了马克思主义文学艺术美学的四种可能选择。我着重讨论了现实主义，包括符合恩格斯和卢卡奇品味和历史议程的客观现实主义，以及在苏联世界，尤其是在1934年之后盛行的倾向性现实主义。我还探讨了瓦尔特·本雅明在1936-1937年间提出的参与式美学，认为它为倾向性现实主义增添了理论意义。之后，我提到了两种摆脱现实主义的方法，因为现实主义已经成为资产阶级意识形态的基石。第一种是阿多诺尤其推崇的“整体”的高级现代主义美学；第二种是转向浪漫主义，其思想脉络从恩斯特·布洛赫一直延续到当今的关键人物弗雷德里克·詹姆逊。（请注意他的名字拼写，即使是詹姆逊的追随者发表的文章也常常拼错。）

Last time I reviewed four possible options for an aesthetics of Marxist approaches to literature and art. I paused over realism, both objective realism as it accorded with the tastes and historical agendas of Engels and Lukács, and also tendentious realism as it pervaded the Soviet world, especially after 1934, with the participatory aesthetic of Walter Benjamin in 1936–1937 considered as a way of lending theoretical interest to tendentious realism. I then mentioned two ways of turning away from realism once it has become a cornerstone of bourgeois ideology. The first of these is the high modernist aesthetic of the “whole” embraced particularly by Adorno, and the second is the turn to romance in the line of thought that descends from Ernst Bloch to the key figure for today, Fredric Jameson. (Please note the spelling of his first name, which even prose published by Jameson’s acolytes manages to get wrong most of the time.)

詹姆逊对浪漫主义的论证早先出现在《政治无意识》导论章节“魔幻叙事”中。这与诺思罗普·弗莱关于浪漫主义在社会中作用的观点非常契合——在弗莱看来，浪漫主义在社会中扮演着宗教角色——詹姆逊提出，一种包含民间传说、民间故事、童话以及各种民间表达形式的浪漫主义美学，作为一种神奇的解决冲突的手段，是应对晚期资本主义阶级冲突中看似无法克服的矛盾的最有效途径。例如，右翼政治势力很容易通过诉诸于与自身经济利益脱节的文化和宗教价值观上层建筑，来说服劳动力投票反对自身的经济利益。我下面引用的“魔幻叙事”中的长篇段落旨在推广浪漫主义美学，同时也对如果坚持现实主义美学会对进步思想造成何种后果提出批判。詹姆逊写道：

Jameson’s argument favoring romance appears earlier in the introductory chapter of The Political Unconscious under the heading “Magical Narratives.” Very much in keeping with the thinking of Northrop Frye about the role of romance in society—in Frye’s case the religious role of romance in society—Jameson proposes that an aesthetic of the romance that entails folklore, the folktale, the fairy tale, and various forms of folk expression as a magical resolution of conflicts that can’t otherwise be resolved is the most constructive means of combating the seemingly insuperable contradictions of class conflict in late capitalism—for example, the ease with which the political right can persuade the labor force to vote against its own economic interests by appealing to an out-of-sync superstructure of cultural and religious values. The long passage I quote below from “Magical Narratives” is meant to promote the romance aesthetic and also to mount a critique of what the consequences would be for progressive thought if one clung to a realist aesthetic. Jameson writes:

让斯科特、巴尔扎克和德莱塞作为现代现实主义兴起的非时间顺序的标志（别忘了巴尔扎克是恩格斯最喜欢的作家；斯科特是1927年卢卡奇最喜欢的作家；而来自所谓自然主义运动的美国小说家西奥多·德莱塞也恰好可以列入其中）；这些早期伟大的现实主义作品的特点在于其素材的根本性和令人振奋的异质性，以及与之相应的叙事技巧的多样性。在这样的时刻，对现实的体裁限制（如果你是现实主义者，你唯一需要做的就是如实描述事物）对文本的语域产生了一种悖论式的解放作用，并释放出一系列异质的历史视角——斯科特的过去、巴尔扎克的未来、德莱塞的商品化过程——这些视角通常被认为与关注历史当下相矛盾。事实上，这种多元的时间性往往会被封闭并重新纳入“高度”现实主义和自然主义之中[换句话说，它开始变得过于简单，表现和唤起现实的公式开始僵化为矫饰主义]，其中完善的叙事机制（特别是作者去人格化[即自由间接引语的叙述风格]、视角统一以及对场景再现的限制这三重要求）开始赋予“现实主义”选项一种令人窒息的自我惩罚的意味。正是在晚期资本主义这种逐渐物化的背景下，浪漫主义再次被视为叙事异质性和摆脱现实原则的场所。
Let Scott, Balzac, and Dreiser serve as the [and remember that Balzac is the favorite author of Engels; Scott is the favorite author of Lukács in 1927; and the American novelist Theodore Dreiser from the so-called naturalist movement is an appropriate figure to add to this list] non-chronological markers of the emergence of realism in its modern form; these first great realisms are characterized by a fundamental and exhilarating heterogeneity in their raw materials, and by a corresponding versatility in their narrative apparatus. In such moments, a generic confinement to the existent [the only thing you have to do if you’re a realist is talk about things as they are] has a paradoxically liberating effect on the registers of the text and releases a set of heterogeneous historical perspectives—the past for Scott, the future for Balzac, the process of commodification for Dreiser—normally felt to be inconsistent with a focus on the historical present. Indeed, this multiple temporality tends to be sealed off and recontained again in “high” realism and naturalism [in other words, it starts getting too easy, and the formulas of representing and evoking the real begin to harden into mannerism], where a perfected narrative apparatus (in particular the threefold imperatives of authorial depersonalization [i.e., the speaking voice in style indirect libre], unity of point of view, and restriction to scenic representation) begin to confer on the “realistic” option the appearance of an asphyxiating self-imposed penance. It is in the context of this gradual reification in late capitalism that the romance once again comes to be felt as the place of narrative heterogeneity and freedom from the reality principle.

从某种意义上说，最后这一点是对弗洛伊德将现实原则奉为建构疗法目标的讽刺；但与此同时，詹姆逊也承认，弗洛伊德也对未经审视的道德准则感到日益绝望，即资产阶级英雄必须像枪手一样直面日益严峻的现实。当现实变成束缚的枷锁，那座诱人的糖果山便再也无法召唤他们了。

In a way, this last is a jab at Freud’s enshrinement of the reality principle as the goal of constructive therapy; but at the same time, Jameson is acknowledging that Freud participates in a growing despair over the unexamined moral imperative that the bourgeois hero confront an increasingly grim reality face to face, like a gunslinger. When reality becomes a straightjacket, the big rock candy mountain can no longer beckon.

在深入分析詹姆逊的三个视域或同心圆式的阐释视角之前，我想先从三个层面探讨一下他的浪漫主义美学，作为热身。我们当然指的是“政治”、“社会”和“历史”层面：政治层面，指的是在虚构的语境下，由某个个体构建的、类似编年史的事件连续记录；社会层面，指的是詹姆逊所谓的“意识形态”（ideologemes）——即不同阶级表达的、相互冲突的世界观——之间的冲突，或者说对自身冲突的认知；最后是历史层面，詹姆逊称之为“必然性”。在本章结尾，他说历史是“令人痛苦的”，但就文学分析而言，正如我们将看到的，“历史”指的是理解生产方式的交叠更迭，以及与之相应的上层建筑的滞后（就像今天无产阶级反动派的现状一样），这一切都在历史时间中展开。顺便一提，我们稍后会更详细地讨论“生产方式”，但我们的基本三个视野——我现在要着重探讨浪漫主义美学——正是詹姆逊所说的政治、社会和历史。

Before we venture very far upon an analysis of Jameson’s three horizons or concentric circles of interpretation from other points of view, I thought it would be interesting, as a warm-up, to find his romance aesthetic at all three levels. We’re talking, of course, about the “political,” the “social,” and the “historical”: the political, which is the chronicle-like record of successive happenings in a fictive context, constructed as a plot by some individual voice; the social, which is the conflict—or awareness of its being a conflict—between what Jameson calls “ideologemes” or ways of thinking about the world as expressed by disparate and conflicting classes; and finally the historical, which Jameson calls “necessity.” At the end of the chapter, he says that history is “what hurts,” but in terms of literary analysis, as we’ll see, “history” is a matter of understanding the overlapping succession of modes of production, with corresponding superstructures lagging behind (as they do today, again, for proletarian reactionaries), as it all unfolds in historical time. We’ll have more to say about “modes of production,” by the way, but our basic three horizons, then—where I am now going to single out the romance aesthetic—are what Jameson calls the political, the social, and the historical.

詹姆逊有时称它们为同心圆，这一点很重要，因为你必须明白，当你从诠释学的角度沿着三个视域或分析阶段前进时，你不会遗漏任何东西。政治包含在社会之中，社会也包含在历史之中。读者所经历的一切，都旨在从每个更具包容性的视域的角度重新思考、重新审视——詹姆逊有时称之为“重写”。

It’s important that Jameson does sometimes call them concentric circles, because you have to understand that as you advance hermeneutically through the three horizons or stages of analysis, you’re not leaving anything behind. The political is contained within the social, and the social is contained within the historical. Everything the reader passes through is meant to be rethought, reconsidered—Jameson sometimes says “rewritten”—from the standpoint of each more inclusive horizon.

那么，创作行为的政治意义何在？詹姆逊借用肯尼斯·伯克的说法，称之为“象征行为”。作为一名作家，我试图以象征性的方式化解矛盾——这里的矛盾指的是任何阶级在自身需求和欲望以及与其他阶级的冲突中所处的视角。政治层面的象征行为旨在化解现实世界中无法解决的虚构矛盾。换句话说，它是一种幻想，一个关于公主和乞丐的童话故事。它是一个强加于现实中根本不可能存在幸福结局的境况之上的武断的幸福结局。简而言之，它是对世界的浪漫化重构。

What, then, is the political moment of the creative act? Well, it’s what Jameson, borrowing from Kenneth Burke, calls “the symbolic act.” As an individual writer, I undertake to resolve a contradiction symbolically—contradiction here entailing the perspective of any class as it exists in conflict both with its own needs and desires and with other classes. The symbolic act at the political level is designed to resolve a contradiction in fiction that has no resolution in the real world. In other words, it’s a fantasy, a fairy tale about the princess and the pauper. It is an arbitrary happy ending tacked onto a situation for which in reality there can be no happy ending. In short, it is a romance revision of the world.

《贫民窟的百万富翁》就是一个有趣的例子。这是丹尼·博伊尔执导的一部作者电影，换句话说，这是一部个人作品，它巧妙地运用整个宝莱坞体系，化解了其中的矛盾。印度教徒和穆斯林之间、本土贫民窟生活与全球化之间、种姓制度之间，矛盾比比皆是，而这些矛盾都无法通过现实手段解决。但一个象征性的奇迹却能奏效：你中了彩票。你奇迹般地赢得了巨额奖金，成为了百万富翁。谁想成为百万富翁呢？我们都想，但只有一个人，通过一系列匪夷所思的巧合，最终实现了这个梦想——而且还抱得美人归。

“Slumdog Millionaire” is an interesting example. It’s an auteur film made by Danny Boyle, an individual act in other words that magically resolves a contradiction through the whole Bollywood apparatus that it brings to bear on it. Contradictions are rife between Hindu and Muslim, between indigenous slum life and globalization, between castes, and none of those contradictions can be resolved realistically. But a symbolic fiat can do the trick: you hit the Lotto. Against all odds you win a prize that makes you a millionaire. Who wants to be a millionaire? Well, we all want to be millionaires, but only one of us, magically, through a series of completely implausible happenstances, is able to become one—and get the girl in the bargain.

但请注意：这并非不可能发生。确实有人中了彩票，也确实有人赢得了价值64000美元的谜题或其他类似的奖项。然而，需要记住的关键是——我认为这才是影片结尾火车站那场盛大集体舞蹈的真正讽刺之处——即便赌博奇迹真的在现实中发生，也无法解决任何矛盾。你的生活或许会改变，甚至可能被完美地安排好（金钱和美人）；但整个世界不会为了你的梦想成真而为你服务，在你身后翩翩起舞；被不愉快的现实，其中一些甚至是充满掠夺性的现实所包围，必然会损害你未来童话般的生活。正如许多令人悲伤的报道所证实的那样，中彩票也可能是一场悲剧。无论如何，我们已经从詹姆逊所理解的政治层面，将浪漫元素单独剥离出来。

But notice this: it’s not that it can’t happen. People do hit the Lotto. People do win the $64,000 question or whatever it may be. The point to be kept in mind, however, is—and I think this is finally the ironic point of that extravagant communal dance in the railroad station at the end of the film—that even were a gambling miracle to happen in reality, it wouldn’t resolve any contradictions. Your life would change, perhaps even scripted to perfection (the money and the girl); but the whole world is not going to fall into line with your dream come true, dancing behind you; and being surrounded by unhappy realities, some of them predatory, is bound to impair your fairy-tale life to come. It can be tragic to hit the Lotto, as many sad reports confirm. In any case, we have thus isolated the romance element at the political level of interpretation as understood by Jameson.

第二层面，即社会层面，揭示了这种童话式的冲突解决方式中所蕴含的颠覆性元素，而这种冲突原本是无法通过其他方式解决的。第二层面还有许多其他因素需要考虑，但请记住，在探讨其他因素之前，我首先要探索这三个层面中的浪漫美学。在第二层面，詹姆逊引用了布洛赫（1297）：

The second level, the social, brings to the surface the element of subversion that’s entailed in this same fairy-tale resolution of a conflict that can’t otherwise be resolved. There are all sorts of other factors to consider at the second level, but remember that at this point I’m discovering the romance aesthetic in all three levels before turning to other factors. At the second level, Jameson acknowledges Bloch (1297):

例如，布洛赫对童话的解读，其中充满了神奇的愿望实现和乌托邦式的富足幻想，以及科卡涅之乡（顺便一提，“大岩糖山”是美国的科卡涅之乡），通过将其展现为对史诗霸权贵族形式的系统性解构和破坏，从而恢复了这种“形式”的对话性和对抗性内容。
Thus, for instance, Bloch’s reading of the fairy tale, with its magical wish-fulfillments and its Utopian fantasies of plenty and the pays de Cocagne [“The Big Rock Candy Mountain” is an American pays de Cocagne, by the way], restores the dialogical and antagonistic content of this “form” by exhibiting it as a systematic deconstruction and undermining of the hegemonic aristocratic form of the epic.

换句话说，童话故事不仅仅是一种象征性的幻想，更是一种社会姿态。它蔑视霸权势力，是一种对抗行为，而这种对抗恰恰源于它承认解决或和解的不可能性。在第二个层面，即社会层面，不同阶级和视角的意识形态声音公开冲突，你甚至无法得到一个有意为之的任意解决方案。你所得到的是颠覆和反抗，一种旨在揭露冲突而非解决任何问题的声音张力。

In other words, the fairy tale is not just a symbolic fantasy, it is a social gesture. It thumbs its nose at hegemonic forces. It is an act of antagonism arising precisely from its recognition of the impossibility of resolution or reconciliation. At the second level, the social level, in which the ideological voices of various classes and perspective are openly in conflict, you don’t get even a knowingly arbitrary resolution. What you get is subversion and reaction, a tension of voices that is not meant to resolve anything but is meant, rather, to lay bare the conflicts.

然而，通过这种颠覆性的表达，一种狂欢式的底层起义涌现出来，詹姆逊也将其与浪漫主义联系起来：这是一种释放压力、畅想乌托邦可能性的方式，发生在有人被尊称为“混乱之王”的那一天；在那一天，整个社会秩序颠倒过来；底层民众被提升到权力地位，并被授予城市钥匙。在这一天，狂欢节或盖伊·福克斯日，冲突得以表达，但并未得到解决，因为每个人都知道明天一切又将恢复原状，这场活动是统治阶级精心策划的，旨在释放压力。但浪漫主义的元素依然存在，这是民众表达愿望的方式，类似于第一层政治层面的愿望，但如今不再是个人的，而是集体的。在这个层面上，我们可以重新审视《贫民窟的百万富翁》的宝莱坞舞蹈结尾，不再将其视为个人财富“恰好落入其中”的不太可能的现象，而是将其视为对那些除了荒谬的解决方案之外别无他法的问题的一种集体讽刺和痛苦的表达。

Through this voicing of subversion, however, there emerges a carnivalesque uprising from below that Jameson also associates with romance: it is a letting off of steam, entertaining the possibility of utopia, that takes place on that day when someone is called the Lord of Misrule; the entire social order for that one day is inverted; the low are elevated to positions of authority and for that one day receive the keys to the city. On this day, a carnival or Guy Fawkes day, conflict is expressed but not resolved because everybody knows that tomorrow it’s going to be the same-old same-old, the occasion having been orchestrated by the ruling class as a safety valve. But the romance element is still there, the folk expression of a wish, a wish similar to what’s expressed at the first political level but now expressed no longer individually but collectively. At this level, we could reconsider the Bollywood dance finale of “Slumdog Millionaire” not as an improbable “falling into place behind” an individual fortune but as a collective expression of ironic bitterness about problems that suggest nothing better than absurd solutions.

第三层级，即历史层级，揭示了在任何时间框架内，一种占主导地位的生产方式与其他生产方式之间的关系。生产方式是指由某种总体性的社会或经济安排所产生的生产体系​​（包括思想和商品的生产）。詹姆逊在他的著作中列举了各种生产方式。我们稍后会回到这个列表，并思考其中的一些术语。詹姆逊举了一个生产方式重叠的绝佳例子：在十八世纪后期，启蒙运动成为新兴的、受过良好教育的资本家资产阶级的主要表达形式。推动工业化和资本发展的价值观，是对封建和贵族理想的反动，后者更注重仪式化的编码，不那么“现实”，更不切实际，也更理想化，不太关注在现实世界中有所作为。启蒙运动被理解为一种新兴生产方式的表达：资本主义取代了封建主义。

The third level, the historical level, exposes for any time frame a dominant mode of production in relation to others. A mode of production is a system of manufacture (of ideas as well as goods) generated by an overarching social or economic arrangement. Jameson lists them in his text. We’ll come back to the list and think about some of its terms. Jameson gives an excellent example of overlapping modes of production: in the latter part of the eighteenth century, the Enlightenment came to be the dominant form of expression for an emergent, quite well-educated capitalist bourgeoisie. The values that drove the development of industrialization and capital circulated in reaction against feudal and aristocratic ideals that were more ritually encoded, less “realistic” and more quixotic, less concerned with getting things done in the world. The Enlightenment is understood as an expression of an emerging new mode of production: capitalism as it succeeds feudalism.

但詹姆逊指出——而浪漫主义也正是在此发挥作用——除了启蒙运动之外，还存在两种抵抗或抗争模式。一方面是浪漫主义，在这种语境下，它可以被解读为（而且通常也确实如此）对贵族和封建理想主义的返祖式回归，试图在启蒙时代重新诠释浪漫主义时代的理想主义，包括骑士精神和其他类型的理想主义，因为这些理想主义当时已显得过时。因此，从这个角度来看，浪漫主义是一种反动的生产模式，它与主流生产模式重叠，或者通过主流生产模式表达自身。然而，与此同时，民众也对启蒙运动日益机械化的趋势进行抵抗。民众反对政治经济学的教条，反对社会工程的兴起以及与功利主义相关的各种社会组织形式，这种反弹可能在政治和社会层面造成破坏性影响，例如“打破框架”、干预劳动活动、抗议工厂的工作标准。这种活跃的氛围也带有返祖的意味，如同浪漫主义（这两种抵抗形式在约翰·克莱尔的生平和诗歌中交织在一起），因为它坚持早期的农业和工业生产方式（例如家庭手工业）。由此可见，在浪漫主义和民众对工业化的抵抗中，启蒙运动与表达浪漫情怀的重叠生产方式并存。生产方式之间的张力，正是第三个层面——历史层面——分析的重点，它再次揭示了乌托邦式的怀旧情结作为一种希望的原则。

But Jameson points out—and here’s where romance comes in—that alongside the Enlightenment, there are two modes of resistance or contestation. On the one hand, there is Romanticism, which can be read in this context (and often is) as an atavistic throwback to aristocratic and feudal idealism, an effort to recode in an age of Enlightenment the idealism of the age of romance, chivalric and otherwise, that had come to seem outmoded. Romanticism, then, on this view is a reactionary mode of production overlapping with or expressing itself through the dominant one. At the same time, however, there is folk resistance to the increasing mechanization of the Enlightenment. Against the doctrines of Political Economy, against the rise of social engineering and the various forms of social organization associated with utilitarianism, there is popular backlash that can be politically and socially disruptive: “frame-breaking,” interference with labor activity, protest against factory work standards. This ferment of activity is also atavistic, like Romanticism (and the two forms of resistance come together in the life and poems of John Clare), because it insists on earlier forms of agricultural and industrial production (the cottage industry, for example). Here too, then, in the forms of Romanticism and popular resistance to industrialization, the Enlightenment coexists with overlapping modes of production that express romance longings. The tension among modes of production, which is the focus of analysis at the third, historical level, once again reveals utopian nostalgia as a principle of hope.

至此，詹姆逊或多或少明确的美学论述就告一段落了。现在我们转向这样一个问题：从这三个层面进行文学分析，其阐释意义何在？詹姆逊认为，这三个层次或同心圆式的分析旨在揭示“政治无意识”的某个要素。正如解构主义和弗洛伊德的理论一样，这种关注点揭示了与日常意识相悖的事物，它颠覆了我们对事物的传统理解，而在这传统理解之下，存在着我们需要理解的规律、原因和动力。然而，就此而言，这里所指的无意识既非语言的，也非心理的。除了其他决定因素之外，用马克思主义的术语来说，政治无意识作为它们的“物质基础”也存在于此。我们之所以会做我们所做的事情，而不是做其他事情，是出于我们可能并不完全意识到，甚至根本意识不到的政治原因；因此，我们需要推断出一种政治无意识的存在。

So much, then, for Jameson’s more or less explicit aesthetic. We turn now to the question, what is the interpretative payoff of undertaking literary analysis at these three levels? Jameson argues that each of these three tiers or concentric circles of analysis is meant to lay bare an element of the “political unconscious.” As in deconstruction, as in Freud, such a focus exposes or reveals something that is antithetical to ordinary consciousness, something that undermines our conventional understanding of things, beneath which there are laws and causes and dynamics at work that we need to understand. In this case, however, the unconscious in question is neither linguistic nor psychological. Alongside these other determinations and underlying them as their “material base,” in Marxist terms, there is the political unconscious. We do what we do, rather than doing other things, for political reasons of which we may not be fully aware, or aware at all; hence the need to infer a political unconscious.

那么，就这三个层面而言：在“政治”层面，个体的象征行为揭示了政治无意识的哪些要素？詹姆逊举了一个来自结构主义的精彩例子，从中可以看出，他非常依赖结构主义来理解叙事形式本身如何表达无意识的愿望。他让我们思考卡杜维奥的脸部彩绘。列维-斯特劳斯在《野性的心灵》和《忧郁的热带》中都提出了这样的问题：我们如何解释这幅画作中某种程度上的过度复杂性？为什么脸部线条在垂直和水平方向上呈现出一种奇特的张力？为什么水平线条中尤其蕴含着一种既有美感又有紧张和复杂之感？

With respect to the three levels, then: at the “political” level, what element of the political unconscious is revealed by the individual symbolic act? Jameson gives a wonderful example taken from structuralism, on which you can see that he leans very heavily for his understanding of the way narrative form itself expresses unconscious wishes. He asks us to consider Caduveo face painting. Lévi-Strauss asks, both in The Savage Mind and in Tristes Tropiques, how we can account for the somehow excessive complexity of this painting. Why the curious tension in the marks on the faces between the vertical and the horizontal? Why is there a feeling of tension, of aesthetic beauty but also of tension and complication, in the horizontal lines especially?

因此，詹姆逊的论点——我认为他比列维-斯特劳斯表达得更明确，尽管列维-斯特劳斯也表达了类似的观点，他将卡杜维奥人的面部彩绘与邻近部落（如博罗罗人）的面部彩绘进行了对比——是：卡杜维奥人是一个等级森严的社会，其中存在着公开且显而易见的不平等形式，作为部落成员，每个人都必须意识到这一点；但邻近部落（这或许是卡杜维奥部落自身也能观察到的）通过交换部分财产来找到一种看似解决等级制度固有矛盾的方法：例如列维-斯特劳斯所讨论的亲属礼物、结婚礼物等等。这种部分财产的交换似乎在现实生活中，以实际的方式，为这些社会秩序强加了一种使社会看起来比实际情况更加平等的机制。是的，它仍然是等级森严的，但与此同时，财富得到了分配，每个人都有某种方式来维护尊严和自我价值。

So Jameson’s argument—which I think he enunciates more unequivocally than Lévi-Strauss, though Lévi-Strauss does say much the same thing, contrasting Caduveo face painting with that of neighboring tribes like the Bororo—is that the Caduveo are a hierarchical society in which there are open and obvious forms of inequality that one must perforce be aware of as a member of the tribe, but that neighboring tribes (and this is something that probably the tribe itself can observe) work out a way of seeming to resolve the contradictions inherent in hierarchy by the exchange of moieties: the kinship gifts, wedding gifts, and so on that Lévi-Strauss discusses. This exchange of moieties seems to impose on these social orders in real life, in real terms, a way of making society seem more equal than perhaps it is. Yes, it’s still hierarchical, but at the same time wealth is distributed and each person has some means of asserting dignity and self-worth.

卡杜维奥人没有这样的安排可以依靠。列维-斯特劳斯和詹姆逊指出，卡杜维奥人从未建立起一套礼物交换体系，因此他们只能维持一种简单的等级组织形式。根据列维-斯特劳斯和詹姆逊的观点，脸部彩绘是卡杜维奥人象征性地解决问题的一种方式，他们通过引入水平标记，在艺术层面（这种表达必须局限于此）表达了其他部落如何通过更平等地分配财富和声望来成功地抵消等级制度。其他部落能够在现实生活中以实际行动实现的象征性行为，卡杜维奥人则以个体的方式完成，每个女性都将脸部彩绘视为一种象征性的行为，我们可以将其理解为表达政治无意识——因为我们推测，这并非任何个体意识到的动机。因此，正如詹姆逊所描述的那样，政治无意识在理解的第一层面，即政治层面，以个人象征行为的形式展现出来。

The Caduveo have no such arrangements to fall back on. Lévi-Strauss and Jameson remark that the Caduveo never worked out a system of gift exchange, so they’re stuck with a simple form of hierarchical organization. Face painting, then, according to Lévi-Strauss followed by Jameson, is the Caduveo way of symbolically resolving the problem by introducing horizontal marks—expressing at the artistic level (to which such expression must be confined) the ways in which other tribes have successfully offset hierarchy by distributing wealth and prestige more equally. The symbolic act that other tribes were able to accomplish in real life, in real terms, the Caduveo accomplish individually, with each individual woman painting her face as a symbolic act, one that we can take to express the political unconscious—because this is not a motive, we suppose, of which any individual is aware. That, then, is the way in which the political unconscious, as Jameson describes it, is brought out at the first, political, level of understanding as an individual symbolic act.

在第二层面，即社会层面——正如詹姆逊所言，文本的自我重写并非个体行为，而是巴赫金式的异质话语表达——在此层面，政治无意识必须被理解为“意识形态模因”（ideologemes）的相互作用。詹姆逊再次提出这一术语，并将其与结构主义联系起来，类比于列维-斯特劳斯的“神话主题”（mythemes），即神话的粗略构成单元。换言之，人们或许在不知不觉中，反射性地表达的不仅是“自我”，还有反映其经济和社会阶层的观点和意见。他们的生活境遇决定了他们会持有某些观点，成为詹姆逊认为至少部分无意识的意识形态模因的代言人。换句话说，人们并不知道，自己如此热切地表达和虔诚地信仰的观点，实际上是受到自身所处社会环境制约的观点。因此，文学就变成了意识形态的戏剧，是未解决的冲突的体现，这种冲突体现在各种不同的、情境化的声音中。

At the second level, the social—in which the text, as Jameson says, rewrites itself not as an individual act but as a heteroglossal expression of voices very much in the spirit of Bakhtin—at this level the political unconscious must be understood as an interplay of “ideologemes,” a term Jameson coins again in relation to structuralism, on analogy with Lévi-Strauss’s “mythemes,” or gross constituent units of myth. In other words, perhaps unbeknownst to themselves, people reflexively express not just “themselves” but views and opinions that reflect their economic and social class. It follows from their situation in life that they will hold certain views, speaking as mouthpieces for ideologemes that Jameson considers to be at least in part unconscious. One doesn’t know, in other words, that the opinions one so fervently expresses and so devoutly believes in are opinions conditioned by the social circumstances in which one finds oneself. Literature, then, becomes a drama of ideologemes, a representation of unresolved conflict that manifests itself in the variety of situated voices that are brought together.

你可以看出，詹姆逊的著作在此处与巴赫金最为接近，也最清晰地反映了我们之前已经接触过的巴赫金的一些关注点。詹姆逊举了一个很好的例子来说明这种冲突是如何运作的，他解释说，这些冲突的奥秘之一在于它们总是出现在一个共同的准则框架内。詹姆逊在此讨论了17世纪英国骑士党和圆颅党之间激烈的宗教冲突，以及围绕克伦威尔统治时期、查理二世复辟和当时发生的剧烈动荡（主要是宗教动荡）的所有争议；但对于任何马克思主义者——克里斯托弗·希尔是运用马克思主义视角最清晰地阐释这一时期历史的领军人物——这种冲突都蕴含着一种潜在的政治无意识：其最终动机是对权利的主张和阶级观点的表达。再次强调，阶级斗争的对话是两种对立的话语在一个共同准则的总体统一性框架内展开的较量。例如，在17世纪40年代的英国，宗教的共同准则成为了霸权神学的主流论述被重新诠释和论战性修改的场所。英国国教代表着——这也是当时使用的词语——“建制”，既包括政治建制，也包括宗教建制。圆颅党的观点、各种形式的清教主义以及其他形式的宗教反叛都反对建制，但它们都被纳入了基督教的论述框架之中。它们必须在同一个战场上展开较量。

You can see that this is the point at which Jameson’s work is closest to Bakhtin’s and most clearly reflects some of the preoccupations of Bakhtin as we have encountered them already. Jameson gives a good example of the way this conflict works, explaining that part of the mystery of these clashes is that they always present themselves within a shared code. Jameson here discusses the violent religious controversies of the seventeenth century in England between Cavalier and Roundhead, with all the controversies surrounding the interregnum of Cromwell, the restoration of Charles II, and the tremendous ferment—largely religious—taking place during that period; but for any Marxist—and Christopher Hill is the leading historian who has made this period most clearly intelligible in these terms—this conflict has an underlying political unconscious: its ultimate motives are an assertion of rights and an expression of class views. Again, the dialogue of class struggle is one in which two opposing discourses fight it out within the overarching unity of a shared code. Thus, for instance, the shared master code of religion becomes in 1640s England the place in which the dominant formulations of a hegemonic theology are reappropriated and polemically modified. The Church of England stands for—and this is the word that was then used—“establishment,” political as well as religious. Roundhead points of view, various forms of Puritanism, and other forms of religious rebellion, are antiestablishment, yet they are all coded within the discourse of the Christian religion. They have to fight it out on a common battlefield.

更贴近我们这个时代，不妨思考一下上世纪六七十年代在共同伦理话语准则内部发生的争论。例如，想想性革命。同样，这里存在一个共同点，即对性行为在人类生活中核心地位的共同认知；而代际冲突所反映的，并非一套全新的价值观，而是对现有价值观的简单重新评价。一方认为不好的东西，另一方却重新评价并奉为圭臬。人们所警惕的，恰恰是人们争相拥抱的。因此，我们再次看到，一场源于共同准则并参与其中的未解决的冲突。这就是社会对抗在第二层面上的表现形式。

Closer to our own time, consider the battle fought in the 1960s and 1970s within the common code of ethical discourse. Think, for example, of the sexual revolution. Again there is a common ground, a shared sense of the centrality of sexual conduct to human life; and what gets reflected in the conflict of generations on this topic is an inversion of values, not a new set of values exactly but a simple transvaluation of the values that exist. Everything that one faction considers bad, another faction transvalues and considers good. The very thing against which one is warned is the thing that one rushes to embrace. So once again you can observe an unresolved clash that arises from and participates in a common code. That’s the way social antagonism expresses itself at the second level.

在第三层面，我们目睹了不同生产方式之间为争夺历史地位而展开的紧张关系。正如詹姆逊所言，将生产方式视为一系列霸权的延续，其危险之处在于，每一种生产方式都可能被视为一个凝固在时间中的同步瞬间。如果你身处资本主义社会，你可能会误以为不存在其他生产方式；同样，如果你身处“父权制”社会（詹姆逊列举的生产方式之一），也会产生类似的错觉。然而，正如詹姆逊所指出的，企业等级制度与父权等级制度之间的紧张关系——这种紧张关系常常在马克思主义和女权主义观点的论战中造成分歧——反映了不同时代生产方式的共存：一种是当代的，另一种则被认为是过去的，但它们仍然存在，并且以“玻璃天花板”的形式与当代的生产方式相互交织。

At the third level, we witness the tension among modes of production jockeying for position historically. As Jameson puts it, the danger of thinking about modes of production as a succession of hegemonies is that each mode of production in turn might seem like a synchronic moment frozen in time. If you’re in capitalism, you may be lulled into thinking that no other mode of production exists, and likewise if you’re in “patriarchy,” to cite one of the terms on Jameson’s list of successive modes of production. Yet as Jameson points out, the tension between corporate hierarchy and patriarchal hierarchy—the tension that has often driven a wedge in polemic between Marxist and feminist points of view—is a reflection of the coexistence of modes of production from different eras: one contemporary, one supposedly a thing of the past, yet persisting and still overlapping, in the form of “the glass ceiling,” with a mode of production that is contemporary.

所有这些都只是历史记录的一部分，但当我们在文学分析中开始以更正式的术语思考第三层面时——我将以雪莱的著名诗歌《西风颂》为例——我们可以看到，诗歌形式的选择本身就是詹姆逊所说的“形式意识形态”的一个例证，它表达了不同创作方式之间的冲突。雪莱的《西风颂》共有五节，每一节的形式都完全相同。每一节既是十四行诗，又是——在结尾对句之前的十二行——一系列三韵句。这两种形式被融合为一个诗节，却以截然不同的方式被编码，各自承载着不同的意识形态。三韵句被编码为“预言”，因为它源于但丁的传统。《神曲》正是以三韵体写成，这首诗由三部分组成，在第三章《天堂篇》中，通过神圣的三位一体，最终化解了所有矛盾。（注意民间传说中的三位一体的关联。）因此，三韵体表达了雪莱的愿望：西风将借由他吹响政治预言的号角。如果冬天来了，春天还会远吗？革命即将到来，一切都将美好。

All that is simply part of the historical record, but when in literary analysis we begin to think of the third level in more formal terms—and I’ll be taking as an example Shelley’s famous poem, “Ode to the West Wind”—we can see the very choice of verse form as an instance of what Jameson calls “the ideology of form” expressing the conflict of modes of production. Shelley’s “Ode to the West Wind” has five strophes, each exactly the same in form. Each is simultaneously a sonnet and—in the first twelve lines before the concluding couplet—a succession of terza rima stanzas. Now these two forms, synthesized as a single strophe, are coded in entirely different ways, each with its own ideology. Terza rima is coded “prophecy” because it is in the tradition of Dante. It’s the verse form in which The Divine Comedy is written, a three-part unit that carries the poem toward the resolution of all contradiction through the divine Trinity in the third canto, The Paradiso. (Note the relevance of the folkloric triad.) Thus terza rima expresses for Shelley the hope that the west wind will be through him the trumpet of a political prophecy. If winter’s here, can spring be far behind? Revolution is in the offing, everything’s going to be great.

但与此同时，这首诗也弥漫着一种悲观主义——或者说，现实主义：一种对预言这种概念相当牵强的认知。风为什么要听从雪莱的安排？风只是风而已，它并非灵感。因此，几乎全程采用三韵体（terza rima）的诗节，实际上是一首十四行的十四行诗。尤其是第一节，它不仅被编码为一首十四行诗，而且还特意引用了莎士比亚的第七十三首十四行诗，这首诗以“你或许能从我身上看到那一年一度的景象”开头。我老了，头发都掉光了，我就像一座光秃秃的破败唱诗班，昔日甜美的鸟儿曾在此歌唱，而这一切却无能为力。在诗的结尾，诗人心中的火焰即将熄灭。换句话说，寒冬已至，春天不会到来。没有预言的可能，只有逝去生命的轨迹。这些人生真相，正如十四行诗所表达的那样，也是政治中的现实，是理想主义——或者如詹姆逊在其他地方所描述的浪漫主义——无法凌驾的。

But at the same time, the poem is shot through with a kind of pessimism—or, if you will, realism: an awareness that this notion of prophecy is rather far-fetched. Why should the wind do Shelley’s bidding? The wind is just wind. It’s not inspiration. Therefore, the very strophe that is written until almost the end in terza rima is written at the same time as a sonnet of fourteen lines. The first stanza in particular is coded not just as a sonnet but as an allusion specifically to one sonnet, Shakespeare’s seventy-third, which begins, “That time of year in me thou mayest behold.” I’m getting old, I don’t have any hair left, I’m just a bare ruined choir where late sweet birds sang, and there’s nothing to be done about it. At the end of the poem, the embers of the speaker’s fire are about to be snuffed out. In other words, winter’s here and no spring is coming. There is no prophetic possibility, only the trajectory of a spent life. These facts of life, as the sonnet form codes it, are realities in politics as well that idealism—that Romanticism as Jameson describes it elsewhere—cannot override.

因此，雪莱的诗歌形式体现了一种思想上的张力：一方面是封建和神权中心主义世界中根深蒂固的预言性思想，另一方面是启蒙运动时期商业阶级冷酷的现实主义（莎士比亚常被认为是启蒙运动的先驱人物）；另一方面也是形式上的张力，即三韵体和十四行诗。因此，“形式的意识形态”反映了两种相互冲突的生产方式：封建的和启蒙的。它们反映了与这些生产方式相关的态度。雪莱是一位极具自省意识的诗人，深受马克思及其圈子的推崇，因此，或许我们最好不要用“政治无意识”来形容他，而只需说，在他的诗歌中，我们可以观察到一种政治“准意识”，这种意识在詹姆逊的第三层分析中得以体现。

So what you get in Shelley’s verse form is a tension between ideas, the prophetic idea at home in a feudal and theocentric world in conflict with the tough-minded realism of a mercantile class whose heyday is the Enlightenment (Shakespeare is often thought of as a proto-Enlightenment figure), which is also a tension between forms, terza rima and the sonnet. Thus “the ideology of form” reflects conflicting modes of production, feudal and Enlightenment, respectively. They reflect attitudes that one can associate with those modes of production. Shelley was an incredibly self-conscious poet, much admired by Marx and his circle, so perhaps we had better not speak of a political unconscious in his case, but just say that in his poem a political “quasi-consciousness” can be observed expressing itself at Jameson’s third level of analysis.

从形式上看，我们可以将第一层面（政治层面）的核心批判任务理解为主题化：一个个体象征行为的情节结构试图表达什么主题？这个象征行为解决了什么矛盾？在第二层面，我们运用的形式原则是巴赫金的异质性概念：声音的冲突以及声音从个体到社会的转变。在第三层面，我们发现了詹姆逊所说的“一系列手法”，我已在雪莱的例子对此进行了阐述。

In formal terms, we can think of the essential critical task at the first or political level as thematization: what theme is the plot structure of an individual symbolic act trying to express? What contradiction is being resolved in this symbolic act? At the second level, the formal principle that we bring into play is the Bakhtinian idea of heteroglossia: the clash of voices and the transformation of voice from the individual to the social. At the third level, we find what Jameson calls “a repertoire of devices,” on which I have reflected in the example from Shelley.

让我再举一个例子，同样来自浪漫主义时期，这与詹姆逊的观点相呼应，即启蒙时代不同创作模式的交融尤为引人注目。浪漫主义继承了品达式颂歌的悠久传统。华兹华斯在创作《不朽的暗示》时仍然沿用了这一传统，但与此同时，他和柯勒律治也发展出了一种新的颂歌形式，我们称之为“对话诗”：柯勒律治的《午夜霜冻》和《这菩提树荫下是我的牢笼》，以及华兹华斯的《丁登寺》（他在诗的注释中将其比作一首颂歌），都是对话诗的杰出代表。

Let me just add another example, also taken from Romanticism, in keeping with Jameson’s reminder that the overlap of modes of production is particularly interesting in the age of Enlightenment. Romanticism inherits the long tradition of the formal Pindaric ode. Wordsworth is still making use of that tradition in writing his “Intimations of Immortality,” but in the meantime he and Coleridge have developed a new kind of ode, if you will, which is called the “conversation poem”: Coleridge’s “Frost at Midnight” and “This Lime-Tree Bower My Prison” together with Wordsworth’s “Tintern Abbey” (which he compares with an ode in a note to the poem) are notable examples of the conversation poem.

我们可以轻易地将这些颂歌类型之间的差异视为生产方式的冲突。正式颂歌最终源于品达对希腊贵族赞助人在奥林匹克运动会上胜利的颂扬，它再次被赋予了封建贵族的特征；而对话诗，正如其描述性术语所示，则非常属于新兴的公共领域。尽管在形式上（尽管场景本身也很有趣，我们稍后会谈到），对话诗营造了一种咖啡馆的氛围，人们在那里彼此交谈，交换意见。这些诗歌是写给某个人的；它们会在某个时刻转向那个人，有时甚至会征求对方的意见。因此，从正式颂歌到对话诗的转变本身就可以被理解为生产方式之间的转变——或者用詹姆逊的话来说，是由生产方式的剧变所带来的“文化革命”。然而，对话诗仍然处于一种介于两者之间的状态：它是一种独白，对话者保持沉默，只能在浪漫的孤独和内省氛围中被暗示存在。对话诗并不反映某种特定创作模式——公共领域——的胜利，而这种胜利体现在例如狄德罗的《拉莫的外甥》中生动的意见交流中。

We can easily see the difference between these types of ode as a conflict of modes of production. The formal ode, derived ultimately from Pindar celebrating the Olympic victories of aristocratic patrons in Greece, is coded once again as feudal-aristocratic, whereas the conversation poem belongs very much, as the descriptive term suggests, to the emergent public sphere. In mode though not in setting (that in itself is of interest, as we’ll see), this is the atmosphere of the coffeehouse, where people address each other and exchange views. These are poems addressing an individual person; they turn to that person at a certain point, sometimes even soliciting an opinion. Hence the very transition from the formal ode to the conversation poem is itself intelligible as a transition between—or what Jameson calls “a cultural revolution” brought about by a seismic shift in—modes of production. Yet the conversation poem is still betwixt and between: it is a monologue, its interlocutor remaining silent and only to be inferred as a presence in atmospheres of romantic solitude and inwardness. The conversation poem does not reflect the triumph of a particular mode of production—the public sphere—that we find in the lively give and take of opinion in, say, Diderot’s Rameau’s Nephew.

以上便是运用詹姆逊三层次理论的一些方法。詹姆逊本人也提醒我们注意其中的危险。如果我们仅仅将叙事视为一种象征行为，就很容易要么过分强调结构主义的潜台词而忽略其现实基础，要么过分强调正在解决的社会矛盾而忽略形式的存在。正如詹姆逊所说，第一层次的两种危险分别是结构主义的危险和庸俗唯物主义的危险。相反，分析象征行为的关键在于维持文本中形式要素和社会要素之间的平衡或综合。第二层次的问题在于，如果我们开始从不可调和的阶级冲突的角度思考问题，我们的分析就会变得僵化，仿佛阶级视角没有发生转变，仿佛一种视角不会取代另一种视角成为霸权：换句话说，仿佛变革从未发生，阶级冲突仅仅是生活的一部分。老板总会贬低员工，员工也总会在背后嘲笑老板。事情就是这样。

These then are some ways to put Jameson’s three levels to work. Jameson himself reminds us of the dangers. If we settle into thinking of a narrative as a symbolic act, we are much too prone either to forget that it’s based on reality by emphasizing the structuralist subtext or else to forget that form is involved at all by emphasizing the social contradiction that’s being resolved. As Jameson says, these two dangers at the first level are the danger of structuralism and the danger of vulgar materialism, respectively. The point in analyzing the symbolic act, on the contrary, is to sustain a balance or a synthesis between formal and social elements within the text. At the second level, the problem is that if we start thinking in terms of irreconcilable class conflict, our analysis can become static, as though class perspectives didn’t shift, as though one perspective might not succeed another as the hegemonic: in other words, as though change didn’t take place and class conflict were a mere fact of life. The boss is always going to speak demeaningly of the worker, and the worker is always going to laugh at the boss behind his back. That’s just the way it is.

最后，在第三层面，存在着以僵局思维来思考的危险——例如，将晚期资本主义视为一种根本无法逾越的僵局。想想阿多诺对文化产业的极度悲观。阿多诺的理论中似乎没有多少希望，不是吗？毕竟，你也可以说詹姆逊本人或许对历史的必然性、历史的“痛苦”有些过于戏剧化，因此他自己也难逃这种僵局感。正因如此，我引用马克思在其《关于费尔巴哈的第十一条论纲》中那句铿锵有力的提醒，正如马克思主义批评家们经常做的那样：“哲学家们只是用不同的方式解释世界而已。然而，问题在于改变世界。”

Finally, at the third level, there is the danger of thinking in terms of impasse—late capitalism, for example, as an impasse that simply can’t be surmounted. Think of Adorno’s incredible gloom about the culture industry. There isn’t much hope in Adorno, is there? And you could, after all, argue that Jameson himself is maybe a tad melodramatic about history as necessity, history as “what hurts,” hence subject to this sense of impasse himself. This is why I quote for you, as Marxist critics themselves so often do, the ringing reminder of Marx in his Eleventh Thesis on Feuerbach: “The philosophers have only interpreted the world in various ways. The point, however, is to change it.”

让我们简要地再来谈谈托尼。如果采用詹姆逊在开头我引用的那段长文中批判的那种将托尼视为物化的现实主义视角，就会发现尼托和斯皮迪什么事也没发生。他们明明是反派，却什么事都不会发生。他们在社会秩序中各司其职：一个是讲究的贵族或势利眼，不愿弄脏自己；另一个则完全致力于生产力、打卡和职业道德，是个典型的资产阶级斯皮迪。他们就那样存在着，反映了两种相互冲突的生产方式，却无人能改变。他们对托尼并不友好，但除了我们读者义愤填膺的谴责之外，没有人会对他们进行任何惩罚。

Let’s revisit Tony briefly. A reified realist approach to Tony, the kind that Jameson criticizes in the long passage I quoted at the outset, would point out that nothing happens to Neato and Speedy. They are manifest villains, yet nothing can happen to them. They simply have their place in the social order: one of them is a fastidious aristocrat or snob who doesn’t want to get dirty; the other is completely committed to productivity and the time clock and the work ethic, a bourgeois Speedy. There they are, reflecting conflicting modes of production, with nothing to be done about it. They’re not nice to Tony, but there is no recrimination against them apart from our indignant disapproval as readers.

但从第一层面来说，如果我们把最终解决的情节理解为一种象征性的行为，那么原本看似无解的冲突最终是通过友谊——邦比和托尼之间的友谊——得以化解的。托尼说：“就算我只是个普通上班族也没什么不好，因为我有哥们儿。我们一起喝啤酒，一起玩乐，生活很美好。阶级结构带来的侮辱也无关紧要。我很开心，”托尼实际上是在说，“我喜欢我的工作。”当然，这句话本身就是一种预先解决冲突的方式，避免了故事中可能出现的其他冲突。

But then at the first level, if we understand the resolved plot as a symbolic act, the resolution of what would otherwise be a hopeless conflict comes about through friendship—the friendship of Bumpy and Tony. It’s perfectly okay if I’m just a working guy because I’ve got my buddies. We drink beer, we have a good time, life is great. It doesn’t matter that the class structure leaves insults in its wake. I’m happy, Tony says in effect. “I like my job.” That claim in itself, of course, is a resolution in advance of any conflicts that the story might otherwise reveal.

在第二层，我们看到的是意识形态的话语。“我帮不了你，”尼托汽车说，“我不想弄脏自己。”“我帮不了你，”斯皮迪汽车说，“我太忙了。”“我可以帮你，”邦比说；但请注意，这些回应都出自同一个共享的语境，正如话语的平行性所表明的那样。在这个单一的语境中，这些无法调和的意识形态争夺着权威。

At the second level, you get the discourse of ideologemes. “I can’t help you,” says Neato the car. “I don’t want to get dirty.” “I can’t help you,” says Speedy the car. “I am too busy.” “I can help you,” says Bumpy; but notice that these responses are all made within a single, shared code, as the parallelism of the utterances indicates. Within a single code, these ideologemes, which can’t be resolved, struggle for authority.

最后，关于第三层级的生产方式：尼托和斯皮迪同时出现在同一个故事中，这本身就表明封建和资产阶级之间存在着某种张力，但这种张力并没有以任何动态的方式自行消解。在我看来，这里需要注意的是拉和推之间的冲突。托尼是一种生产方式，一辆拖车。很有意思的是——我以前也说过——拉的东西需要被推。这对托尼来说一定很有教育意义。邦比就像《小火车头》里的那辆小火车一样，是对早期一种动力不足、效率低下、机械效率也较低的生产方式的回归。他必须推。想想过去人们是如何砌墙的：在起重机和滑轮发明之前，预制墙需要一群人推上去。在能够拉东西的技术出现之前，推是建筑劳动的重点。之后，你就可以用起重机，放下吊钩，把墙拉到合适的位置。在这里，当我们看到托尼在一位老前辈的帮助下向前迈进时，我们看到了詹姆逊第三层分析（即历史分析）中新旧生产模式的交汇。

Finally, then, as to modes of production at the third level: the very existence of Neato and Speedy in the same story suggests that there is a tension between the feudal and the bourgeois, but it’s not a tension that works itself out in any way dynamically. The important thing to notice here, it seems to me, is the conflict between pulling and pushing. Tony is a mode of production, a tow truck. It’s quite interesting—and I’ve said this before—that something that pulls needs to be pushed. It must be educational for Tony. Bumpy, like the Little Engine That Could, is a throwback to an earlier, less energized and powerful, less mechanically efficient mode of production. He has to push. Think of the way walls were put up in the past: a prefabricated wall before the invention of the crane and the pulley had to be pushed up by a bunch of people. Pushing was the focus of construction labor before the kind of technology arose that made it possible to pull something. After that, you have a crane, you let the hook down and just pull the wall up into place. Here then, as we watch Tony being helped forward by a throwback, we find the overlap of older and newer modes of production at Jameson’s third or historical level of analysis.

我们将在下一讲讨论新历史主义时再回到托尼身上，并借此机会看看我们是否也能将本雅明和阿多诺与托尼联系起来。

We’ll come back to Tony in the next lecture when we discuss the New Historicism and seize the chance at that point to see whether we can map Benjamin and Adorno onto Tony as well.

 

 

第十九章

CHAPTER 19

新历史主义
The New Historicism

阅读材料：

Readings:

格林布拉特，斯蒂芬。“形式的权力。”载于《批评传统》，第 1443-1445 页。

Greenblatt, Stephen. “The Power of Forms.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1443–1445.

麦甘，杰罗姆·J.“济慈与历史方​​法。”载于《语调之美：历史方法与理论中的文学研究》。纽约：牛津大学出版社，1988年。

McGann, Jerome J. “Keats and Historical Method.” In The Beauty of Inflections: Literary Investigations in Historical Method and Theory. New York: Oxford University Press, 1988.

本次讲座，我们将探讨一种席卷学术界的文学批评方法，即新历史主义。这种批评方法始于20世纪70年代末，贯穿80年代和90年代。它起源于加州大学伯克利分校，或者至少其最初的学术中心位于此，由斯蒂芬·格林布拉特（Stephen Greenblatt）发起。格林布拉特等人（托马斯·拉克尔、斯韦特兰娜·阿尔珀斯、霍华德·布洛赫）创办了一份名为《表象》（Representations）的期刊，至今仍是文学研究领域最重要、最具影响力的期刊之一，也是新历史主义思想的中心。这一群体对历史方法（“旧历史主义”）的新态度，最早聚焦于早期现代时期，也就是所谓的“文艺复兴”时期。

In this lecture, we turn to a way of doing literary criticism that swept the academy, beginning in the late 1970s, through the 1980s and into the 1990s, that is called the New Historicism. It began, or at least had its first intellectual center, at the University of California at Berkeley under the auspices of Stephen Greenblatt. Greenblatt and others (Thomas Lacqueur, Svetlana Alpers, Howard Bloch) founded a journal, still one of the most important and influential journals in the field of literary study, called Representations, which has always been a headquarters for New Historicist thought. The new attitude taken by this group toward historical (“old historicist”) methods took for its earliest focus of attention the early modern period, otherwise known as the “Renaissance.”

实际上，新历史主义本身就促成了“文艺复兴”一词被“早期现代”所取代。近年来，许多领域或时期都进行了重新命名，用时间跨度取代了所谓的思想特征（例如用“漫长的十八世纪”取代“新古典主义”，用“十八世纪末至十九世纪初”取代“浪漫主义”），其目的是为了提醒学者，各个时期都充满了变革和多样性，足以抵消某种主流思想潮流的影响。所有这些变化都源于历史主义倾向，即便并非总是严格意义上的新历史主义倾向。

The New Historicism is itself, in effect, responsible for the replacement of the term “Renaissance” with the term “early modern.” There has, in fact, been a lot of field or period renaming in recent years, substituting time spans for alleged intellectual characteristics (“long eighteenth century” for “neoclassicism,” “late eighteenth and early nineteenth century” for “Romanticism”), with the intention of reminding scholars that periods are full of ferment and diversity that offset this or that dominant intellectual trend. These changes have all followed from historicist, if not always strictly New Historicist, inclinations.

新历史主义的方法论迅速扩展到其他领域，在某些领域甚至比在其他领域更为显著。我之所以说“至今”，是因为新历史主义在今天仍然根深蒂固。该运动的基本前提依然存在，尽管在关注点、研究对象以及修辞力度上，它已失去了些许锋芒。无论如何，或许值得专门讲一讲（但我并不打算讲），来解释为什么某些领域似乎比其他领域更容易接受新历史主义的研究方法，但如今所有领域都已受到新历史主义的关注。不过，我认为可以公平地说，除了近代早期之外，受新历史主义影响最大的三个领域是十八世纪、英国浪漫主义（请原谅我使用了略显过时的术语）以及从殖民时代晚期到共和时期的美国研究。最后一个时期——以印刷文化的兴起、活跃的公共领域对报纸和连载文章的讨论为特征——已从新历史主义的视角进行了深入研究，并取得了令人振奋的成果，同时又通过媒介史的视角进行了更新。在讨论杰罗姆·麦克甘的文章时，我将着重谈谈麦克甘对浪漫主义研究的影响。

The method of the New Historicism quickly extended to other fields, to some fields perhaps even to this day more than to others. I say “to this day” because the New Historicism is very much with us today. The premises of the movement are still in evidence, although in focus, subject matter, and also in the lowered decibel level of its rhetoric it has lost some of its edgy profile. In any case, it might be worth a lecture that I’m not going to give to explain why certain fields seem to lend themselves more readily to New Historicist approaches than others, but by this time all have had their share of attention. I think it’s fair to say, though, that in addition to the early modern period, the three fields that have been influenced the most by the New Historicism are the eighteenth century, British Romanticism (forgive the outmoded nomenclature), and Americanist studies from the late colonial through the republican period. This last era—featuring the emergence of print culture, a lively public sphere engaged in the discussion of newspapers and feuilletons—has been studied with galvanizing results from New Historicist points of view, updated by way of media history. When we discuss Jerome McGann’s essay, I’ll say something about how McGann in particular has influenced Romantic studies.

新历史主义在20世纪70年代末至90年代初这段时期之所以如此流行并产生如此巨大的影响，很可能是因为学术思想日益政治化。新历史主义既是对外部压力的回应，也是对内部相关压力的回应。正如詹姆逊所言，历史越来越成为“伤痛之源”，在这种学术氛围下，一种日益强烈且被公开宣扬的道德失范感油然而生：文学研究某些形式将文学文本与历史潮流割裂开来。从新批评时期，到解构主义时期，再到拉康等人的精神分析学派的晦涩论述，尤其是在年轻学者中，普遍存在一种感觉，鉴于紧迫的社会问题——后越战时代、敏感的身份认同问题、权力分配和全球资本问题——这种感觉在学术文学研究中可谓是一种罪恶感，即必须改变研究方向。这股愧疚浪潮导致了“回归历史”。人们感到，道德的转折点已经到来，那些曾经盛行的分析模式需要被新的分析模式所取代，在新的分析模式中，历史以及人们行为的政治含义变得突出和核心。

What probably accounts for the remarkable popularity and influence of the New Historicism in the period roughly from the late 1970s through the early 1990s was the increasingly politicized sensibility of academic thought. The New Historicism was a response to pressures from without and to related pressures from within. History was increasingly “what hurt,” in Jameson’s expression, and in that atmosphere within the academy there was an increasing and loudly proclaimed sense of ethical failure in the isolation of literary texts from historical currents by literary study as it was allegedly practiced in certain forms. Beginning with the New Criticism through the period of deconstruction and the recondite discourse of Lacan and others in psychoanalysis, there was a feeling widespread among younger scholars in particular, in view of pressing social concerns—post-Vietnam, sensitive identity concerns, concerns about the distribution of power and global capital—a feeling amounting to what one can only call a guilt complex in academic literary scholarship that a change of direction was required; and that wave of guilt resulted in the “return to history.” It was felt that an ethical tipping point had been arrived at and that the modes of analysis that had been flourishing needed to be superseded by those in which history and the political implications of what one was doing became prominent and central.

我必须指出，这类辩论中总是充斥着大量的空谈，或许双方都有。正如我曾多次指出的那样，所谓孤立的研究方法在很多方面并非真正孤立。例如，第二代解构主义始终关注伦理和历史，并试图将其研究方法应用于各种可能的历史研究途径。而新历史主义则表现出对形式和文本细节问题的关注，这无疑源于其之前的学科，但我认为，这种关注并非总是得到充分的认可。正如我们即将探讨的许多其他方法一样，尤其是那些受社会身份驱动的方法，新历史主义在很大程度上挪用了理论先锋派的语言（或者更广义地说，是借用了从敌方继承而来的理论话语，以此作为体面的外衣），并且吸收了一些有用的结构主义思想：例如，自我与他者之间以及社会群体之间的二元关系。简而言之，新历史主义正是在学术界普遍存在自我怀疑的论战氛围中兴起的。

I have to say that in debates of this kind there’s always a lot of hot air, perhaps on both sides. In many ways, as I’ve tried to indicate from time to time, it’s just not the case that the so-called isolated approaches really were isolated. Deconstruction in its second generation wrote perpetually about ethics and history and tried to orient its techniques to possible ways of approaching history, just to give one example. The New Historicism for its part evinced a preoccupation with issues of form and textual detail that certainly followed from the disciplines that preceded them, not always, I think, with sufficient acknowledgement. As is true also of a good many other approaches that we’re about to investigate, approaches driven by social identities in particular, to a large degree the New Historicism appropriated the language of the theoretical avant-garde (or, to speak more broadly, the language of theory-speak inherited from the enemy as a cloak of respectability) and also took over some useful structuralist ideas: for example, the binary relationship between self and other and among social groups. In short, it was in a polemical atmosphere and at a moment of widespread self-doubt in the academic literary profession that the New Historicism came into its own.

新历史分析的程序遵循一种模式，这种模式既易于识别又引人入胜，格林布拉特的简短导论就精彩地阐释了这一点，我请各位阅读了这篇导论。这种模式以一个轶事开篇，这个轶事通常与最终在文章论证中涉及的文学问题看似毫不相干。例如：一个浑身沾满面粉的磨坊主漫无目的地走在路上，遇到了一位当地电网的官员——姑且称他为法警吧。这次偶遇引出了一些法律问题，然后话题就转到了《李尔王》上。这种巧妙而迂回地切入文学主题的方式，主要归功于格林布拉特的精湛技艺，以及路易斯·蒙特罗斯和其他许多人的贡献，其中包括像卡洛·金兹伯格和娜塔莉·泽蒙·戴维斯这样受过历史学训练的学者。这种技法成为了新历史主义的标志，但它也极易被戏仿，因此在很大程度上已被弃用，这实在令人惋惜。

The procedure of New Historical analysis fell into a pattern, a quickly recognizable and very engaging one, which is wonderfully exemplified in the brief introduction by Greenblatt that I have asked you to read. The pattern begins with an anecdote that’s often rather far afield, at least apparently far afield, from the literary issues that are eventually turned to in the argument of a given essay. For example: a flour-covered miller was walking down the road, thinking about nothing in particular, when he encountered some functionary on the local power grid, call him—probably a him—a bailiff. From this encounter certain legal issues are raised, and the next thing you know we’re talking about King Lear. This rather marvelous, oblique way into literary topics was owing to the brilliance in handling it of Greenblatt, in particular, together with Louis Montrose and many others, including historians by training like Carlo Ginzberg and Natalie Zemon Davis. This technique became a hallmark of the New Historicism, so vulnerable to parody indeed that it has been abandoned for the most part, which is rather a pity.

无论是否带有戏仿意味，这种轶事式的引子都揭示了新历史主义思维运作方式的重要特征。福柯实际上是他们话语体系的奠基人。今天我不会过多赘述这一点，除非我很快会在性别研究的语境下再次探讨福柯，届时我们将一起讨论福柯和朱迪斯·巴特勒——但我还是要简要指出，福柯的著作，尤其是他后期的著作，关注的是他所谓的“权力”在社会秩序中的流通。新历史主义追随福柯，关注权力的分配。这一思想流派进行历史研究的部分目的，正是为了揭示权力体系。

Parodied or not, though, this sort of anecdotal entrée shows you something important about how New Historicist thinking works. Foucault is really their founder of discursivity. I won’t say as much about this today as I might feel obliged to say if I weren’t soon to return to Foucault in the context of gender studies, when we take up Foucault and Judith Butler together—but I will say briefly that Foucault’s writing, especially his later writing, concerns the circulation through social orders of what he calls “power.” Following Foucault, the New Historicism is interested in the distribution of power. The study of history is undertaken by this school of thought in part to reveal systems of power.

然而，重要的是要理解，即使在福柯的理论中，权力也不仅仅是既得利益者的权力、国家认可的暴力或自上而下的暴政。尽管权力可以包含这些要素，而且往往确实如此，但在福柯看来，权力更普遍、也更隐蔽地体现在知识在文化中的传播方式：我们认为合适的思考方式——即可接受的思考方式——是如何在社会网络或系统中通过一些大多不可见的力量进行分配的。我们可以说，这种权力不同于意识形态，因为意识形态是对社会和经济利益的反思性表达，而权力则是思想对感知到的（尽管不一定是强制性的）社会压力的顺从或趋同。在福柯看来，权力即知识，或者换句话说，它是某些知识形式得以盛行的原因——顺便一提，“知识”并不一定是指对真理的认知。在这里，我要引用我最喜欢的一句格言，这句话出自美国幽默作家乔什·比林斯，他是威尔·罗杰斯的同代人：“大多数人的问题不在于他们的无知，而在于他们知道太多不真实的事情。”福柯和他的追随者——新历史主义者——正是这一朴实真理的科学家。

It is important to understand, however, that even and especially in Foucault, power is not just the power of vested authorities, of state-sanctioned violence, or of tyranny from above. Although it can be those things and frequently is, power in Foucault is much more pervasively and also insidiously the way in which knowledge circulates in a culture: the way what we think that it is appropriate to think—acceptable thinking—is distributed by largely unseen forces in a social network or system. This sort of power differs from ideology, we can say, because whereas ideology is the reflexive expression of social and economic interest, power is the conformance or conformism of thought to perceived, though not necessarily coercive, social pressures. Power in Foucault is knowledge, or to put it another way, it is the reason why certain forms of knowledge come to prevail—“knowledge,” by the way, being not necessarily the knowledge of something that’s true. Here I get to quote my favorite motto of all, courtesy of the American humorist Josh Billings, a contemporary of Will Rogers: “The trouble with most folks isn’t so much their ignorance, it’s knowin’ so many things that ain’t so.” Foucault and his followers the New Historicists are the scientists of this down-home truth.

因此，这些初步的轶事才显得尤为重要。尽可能从与你最终要讨论的主题——莎士比亚、斯宾塞或伊丽莎白时代假面剧中的某些文本或主题问题——相距甚远的地方入手。之所以要尽可能远离这些主题，正是为了展现某种思维习惯或法律观念的普遍性，某种社会约束或自由限制的普遍性，从而揭示福柯式权力的本质——一种网络或系统，一种潜移默化、无处不在的知识传播模式。所有这些都隐含在，有时也明确地体现在新历史主义的文学和文化研究方法中。

Hence the interest of those preliminary anecdotes. Start as far afield as you possibly can from what you will finally be talking about, which is probably some textual or thematic issue in Shakespeare or Spenser or the Elizabethan masque. Start as far afield as you possibly can from that, precisely in order to show the pervasiveness of some habit of thought or legal idea, the pervasiveness of some social constraint or limitation on freedom, that reveals Foucauldian power to be a grid or system, an insidious and ubiquitous mode of circulating knowledge. All of this is implicit, sometimes explicit, in New Historicist approaches to literary and cultural studies.

因此，福柯的权力论是至关重要的先决条件。在福柯的影响下，文学作为一种假定的特殊话语形式，往往会回归到更广泛或更一般的“话语”概念之中，因为权力正是通过话语来传播知识的。然而，在此，我们必须指出，新历史主义对福柯进行了修正，因为我所提及的文学训练，即便有时被忽视，也培养了一种对表达细节的关注，这种关注不仅关乎形式，也关乎体裁——但与精深的马克思主义批评一样，它也理解形式和体裁本身就是权力的产物。尽管新历史主义试图将我们带回现实世界，但它必须承认，这种回归是受制于语言的。正是通过语言，现实世界才得以塑造自身。正因如此，新历史主义者才如此强调文学与历史之间相互依存的关系。

Foucault on power, then, is the crucial antecedent. Under Foucault’s influence, literature as a supposed specific kind of utterance tends to collapse back into the broader or more general notion of “discourse,” because it’s by means of discourse in general that power circulates knowledge. Here, though, it’s proper to say that the New Historicism modifies Foucault, because the literary training of which I have spoken, even when it’s being shrugged off, fosters an attention to expressive detail that accounts not only for form but for genre—with the understanding, however, in common with sophisticated Marxist criticism, that form and genre are themselves effects of power. Despite the fact that the New Historicism wants to return us to the real world, it must acknowledge that that return is language-bound. It is by means of language that the real world shapes itself. That’s why the New Historicist lays so much emphasis on the idea that the relationship between literature and history is reciprocal.

是的，历史决定了文学在特定时代能够表达什么。历史是理解特定时期某些话语价值的重要途径。正如格林布拉特所谓的“旧历史主义”一直以来所论证的那样，历史是话语或文学的背景。但新历史主义想要强调的是截然不同的东西。文学本身具有历史能动性，拥有影响历史的话语力量。这正是格林布拉特开篇轶事的要点。“我就是理查二世，你难道不知道吗？”伊丽莎白女王在埃塞克斯起义的威胁下，得知莎士比亚的《理查二世》正在公共街道和私人住宅中上演时，如此说道。她认为，凡是有叛乱的地方，凡是有人想要推翻她，拥立埃塞克斯伯爵一伙取而代之的地方，都会上演《理查二世》 。这令伊丽莎白女王感到恐惧，因为她既是戏剧的支持者，又不敌莎士比亚，她深知《理查二世》讲述的是一位拥有诸多美德却也性情软弱的国王——正是这种软弱让他常常坐在地上，讲述历代君王的悲惨遭遇——最终，未来的亨利四世篡夺了他的王位，以新王朝取代了旧王朝。因此，伊丽莎白女王不得不假定她的敌人正在上演这出戏，意在将她与理查二世相提并论，以此为借口废黜她，甚至可能以惯常的治国之道处死她。她自然忧心忡忡，而令她忧心的，竟是一出戏。

Yes, history conditions what literature can say in a given epoch. History is an important way of understanding the valency of certain kinds of utterance at certain times. As what Greenblatt calls the “old historicism” had always argued, history is the background of discourse or literature. But the New Historicism wants to emphasize something quite different. Literature itself has historical agency, the discursive power to influence history reciprocally. This is the point of Greenblatt’s opening anecdote. “I am Richard II, know you not that?” says Queen Elizabeth when, at the time of the threatened Essex Uprising, she gets wind of the fact that Shakespeare’s Richard II is being performed, as she believes, in the public streets and in private houses. Wherever there is sedition, she thinks, wherever there are people who want to overthrow her and replace her with the faction of the Earl of Essex, Richard II is being performed. This is terrifying to Queen Elizabeth because, as a supporter of the theatre and no enemy to Shakespeare, she knows that Richard II is about a king who has many virtues but also a weakness of temperament—the kind of weakness that makes him sit upon the ground and tell sad tales about the death of kings—a king whose throne is usurped by the future Henry IV, replacing an old dynasty with a new one. Hence Queen Elizabeth has to assume that her enemies are staging this play to compare her with Richard II in preparation for deposing her and probably executing her in the bargain for the usual reasons of state. Naturally she’s worried, and what she’s worried by is a play.

所以，文学也会伤人！文学具有话语权，能够影响历史进程。当文学“公之于众”时，它就更加危险，因为格林布拉特认为，剧院曾被认为具有一种调解作用，能够化解或至少降低煽动叛乱的可能性。人们在剧院观看文学作品——或者在既定的界限内接受任何形式的文学作品——时，或许会带着某种程度的客观性，而当利益相关方利用同一文本并将其搬上舞台以煽动叛乱时，这种客观性就完全消失了。简而言之，文学影响历史进程，历史也影响文学。

So literature hurts, too! Literature has a discursive agency that influences the course of history. Literature is even more dangerous when it is “out there,” because the playhouse, Greenblatt argues, was thought to have a mediatory effect that defused or at least reduced the possibilities of sedition. One views literary representation in the playhouse—or receives any sort of literature within preestablished boundaries—with a measure of objectivity, perhaps, that is absent altogether when interested parties take up the same text and stage it for the purpose of fomenting rebellion. Literature, in short, influences the course of history as much as history influences literature.

格林布拉特有力地论证了新历史主义与旧历史主义的区别就在于此。除了这一区别之外，还必须认识到，旧历史主义扭曲了其研究对象，通过宣称一种虚假的客观性，正中现代真理体制（福柯有时称之为权力体制）的下怀。约翰·多佛·威尔逊是一位备受尊敬的传统莎士比亚学者，格林布拉特选择他作为例证来刻画旧历史主义。我即将引用的观点带有讽刺意味地转述了约翰·多佛·威尔逊的观点，指向了过去关于文学与历史关系的共识（1443年）：

It is in this respect, Greenblatt argues effectively, that the New Historicism differs from the old historicism. In addition to this difference, it is necessary to see that the old historicism distorts its subject, playing into the hands of modern regimes of truth (as Foucault sometimes calls power) by laying claim to a false objectivity. John Dover Wilson, a highly respected traditional Shakespeare scholar, is the case in point Greenblatt chooses in order to characterize the old historicism. The view I’m about to quote ironically paraphrases that of John Dover Wilson, pointing toward a former consensus about the relationship between literature and history (1443):

现代历史学（即旧历史主义）向伊丽莎白保证，她无需担忧：理查二世并非颠覆之作，而是对都铎王朝秩序的颂歌。该剧非但没有煽动叛乱，反而将废黜合法国王视为“亵渎神明”的行为，认为这会将国家拖入“混乱的深渊”；J·多佛·威尔逊宣称，“莎士比亚及其观众将博林布鲁克视为篡位者，这一点毋庸置疑。” 但在1601年，伊丽莎白女王和埃塞克斯伯爵对此却并不确信。
Modern historical scholarship [meaning old historicism] has assured Elizabeth that she had nothing to worry about: Richard II is not at all subversive but rather a hymn to Tudor order. The play, far from encouraging thoughts of rebellion, regards the deposition of the legitimate king as a “sacrilegious” act that drags the country down into “the abyss of chaos”; “that Shakespeare and his audience regarded Bolingbroke as a usurper,” declares J. Dover Wilson, “is incontestable.” But in 1601 neither Queen Elizabeth nor the Earl of Essex were so sure.

格林布拉特胜出。格林布拉特的过人之处在于他选择的例子如此有力且无可辩驳。我们知道伊丽莎白女王当时感到恐惧，这足以证明约翰·多佛·威尔逊认为理查二世对她没有威胁是错误的。反驳的重点并非威尔逊对当时人们对理查二世的普遍态度判断正确。他当然是对的，博林布鲁克当然被认为是篡位者，理查被废黜也的确被认为是悲剧。但这并不意味着文本不会被曲解和颠覆，而伊丽莎白女王认为这种情况确实发生了，即便她所认为的威胁远没有她想象的那么严重。王室惶恐不安，而文学作品也无济于事。

Greenblatt wins. It’s the genius of Greenblatt to choose examples that are so telling and so incontrovertible. We know Queen Elizabeth was scared on this occasion, which makes it merely obvious that John Dover Wilson was wrong to suppose that Richard II was no threat to her. It’s not at all a point to be made in rebuttal that Wilson was right about the general attitude toward Richard II. Certainly he was right, certainly Bolingbroke was considered a usurper, and certainly it was thought tragic that Richard was deposed. But that doesn’t mean the text can’t be hijacked and made subversive, which is what Elizabeth believed to have happened even if the threat was less severe than she supposed it to be. Uneasy sits the crown, and literature doesn’t help.

威尔逊对此视而不见，因为他认为历史与文学的关系仅仅是历史影响文学，而非反之。旧式的历史主义将当时关于君主制合法性、君权神授、英国国教认可的继承权等等广泛的政治或意识形态共识——而事实上，在这些历史剧创作之时，所有这些意识形态的束缚正在逐渐减弱——视为此类剧作被接受的背景，仿佛它们所能做的仅仅是反映一种共识。然而，事实上，任何人都可以篡改剧情，颠覆其价值观，从而对既有权力构成真正的威胁。

Wilson doesn’t acknowledge this because his view of the relationship between history and literature is only that history influences literature, not the other way around. The old historicism points to a broad political or ideological consensus at that time about the legitimacy of monarchy, the divine right of kings, authorized succession under the sanction of the Church of England, and all the rest of it—all of which was in fact loosening its ideological stranglehold when these history plays were being written—as a background to the reception of such plays, as though all they could do was reflect a consensus. This despite the fact that anyone could take the plots and reverse their values, posing real threats to established power.

正如我前面提到的，旧历史主义和新历史主义的另一个区别在于，旧历史主义者从未承认历史学家主观观点的作用。格林布拉特说，历史“不被认为是历史学家诠释的产物”（1444）。请注意，这里我们又回到了伽达默尔的观点。请记住，这正是伽达默尔对历史主义（格林布拉特称之为旧历史主义）的批判：它认为我们可以排除自身的历史视野，消除所有历史偏见，从而客观地理解过去——正如一个世纪前一位颇具影响力的历史学家利奥波德·冯·兰克所说，“如其本来面目”。

As I suggested above, another way in which the old historicism and the New Historicism differ is that the old historicists never acknowledged the role of the historian’s subjective views.
