History was “not thought,” says Greenblatt, “to be the product of the historian’s interpretation” (1444). Notice that at this point we’re back with Gadamer. Remember that this was Gadamer’s accusation against historicism (what Greenblatt calls the old historicism): its belief that we can bracket out our own historical horizon, eliminating all of our own historical prejudices in order to understand the past objectively—“as it really was,” as an influential historiographer of a century before, Leopold von Ranke, had put it.

格林布拉特也认为，认为自己对自己的研究对象没有既得利益的想法是天真的。格林布拉特的论证巧妙地引用了约翰·多佛·威尔逊在1939年向一群德国学者发表的关于理查二世的观点。希特勒不仅即将成为，而且实际上已经成为了德国的博林布鲁克，他所建立的政权虽然不像理查二世那样充满毒害，却也同样存在着理查二世性格上的弱点。我们推测，约翰·多佛·威尔逊希望他的听众通过他对莎士比亚作品的解读得出这样的结论：他们拥有一个脆弱的民主制度，但仍然是一个他们绝不能失去的民主制度。既然大势已去，他便能如此令人安心地发表这番言论，其目的仅仅是为了证实他坚信伊丽莎白时代的英国政权的合法性是稳固的。

Greenblatt, too, says it’s naive to suppose that one has no vested interest in one’s subject. The reminder that John Dover Wilson delivered himself of these opinions about Richard II before a group of German scholars in 1939 is wonderfully placed in Greenblatt’s argument. Hitler is not only about to be, but really already is, the Bolingbroke of Germany, succeeding upon less poisonous regimes that had all of Richard’s temperamental weaknesses. We assume John Dover Wilson wanted his audience to conclude, in response to his version of Shakespeare, that they have a weak democracy, but still a democracy that they must not lose. That horse already having escaped from the barn, he can speak thus reassuringly with no motive more than to confirm his belief that legitimacy was secure in Elizabethan England.

相比之下，新历史主义者充分意识到研究选择背后所蕴含的主观投入。格林布拉特出于某种原因，对权力作为知识的流通表现出浓厚的兴趣，并将之视为既得权威与异议之声之间策略博弈的结果。在新历史主义看来，世界本质上是一场围绕权力展开的动态冲突，是既得权威网络与颠覆势力之间争夺表达权的斗争——而这种颠覆本身也是一种权力。寻找颠覆的途径之一，就藏身于那些精心维护权威的文本之中。例如，伊丽莎白时代的假面剧，以精心编排的方式展现了宫廷与朝臣、访客以及追随者之间的关系，其多语种的运用，使其结构中蕴含了颠覆的元素。

The New Historicist by contrast is fully cognizant of the subjective investment that leads to a choice of research. Greenblatt’s personal interest, for reasons best known to him, was the circulation of power as knowledge, viewed as a contest of strategies between vested authority and voices of dissidence. The world as the New Historicism sees it is essentially a dynamic skirmish about power, a struggle for expression between networks of vested authority and subversion—which in circulation is also a kind of power. One place to look for subversion is within the very texts that ceremoniously shore up authority. The Elizabethan masque, for example, which stages the relation of court to courtier, to visitor, and to hanger-on in carefully orchestrated ways, is a means—because it’s polyglossal—of containing within its structure the elements of subversion.

我不确定杰罗姆·麦克甘是否曾将自己视为新历史主义者。虽然有人这样称呼他，但我认为至少在他研究早期现代时期时，他与格林布拉特及其同事的研究重点存在一个相当重要的差异。麦克甘并不像他们那样强调历史与文学的相互作用。他感兴趣的是，我们所阅读的文本，或者更确切地说，是学术界出于选择性而引导我们阅读的文本，其字里行间所蕴含的历史、社会乃至个人因素。在你读过的那篇文章中，他主要关注的是文本研究，即学术版本编纂者和课堂选集选材的编辑们如何塑造我们对作者作品的理解。他本人是拜伦新标准作品集的编辑，也为斯温伯恩的作品集做出了类似的贡献，并且在围绕文本研究的深奥辩论中，他一直是一位颇具影响力的发言人，代表着一种鲜明的观点：文本研究是否应该出版一部融合了各种现有手稿和印刷文本的文本？它所呈现的文本是否应该是作者最后也是最好的思想？——这显然是对麦克甘在这篇文章中所持立场的简化——或者它是否应该是作者最初的灵感迸发？后一种观点或许值得商榷，但所有偏爱华兹华斯《序曲》早期版本的批评家（例如，我也在内）至少在这一点上会支持它。总之，我们应该将麦克甘关于济慈和历史方法的文章理解为对文本批评的贡献，它发表在一本名为《语调之美》的书中，而这本书主要探讨的正是此类问题。

It’s not clear to me whether Jerome McGann has ever thought of himself as a New Historicist. He has been so designated by others, but I think there is one rather important difference in emphasis, at least between what he’s doing and what Greenblatt and his colleagues do in studying the early modern period. McGann doesn’t put as much emphasis as they do on the reciprocity of history and literature. He is interested in the presence of historical, social, and also personal circumstances in the very grain of the texts we read, or rather the texts we are directed to read by scholarly selectivity. His attention in the essay you have read is devoted chiefly to textual scholarship, to the way the makers of scholarly editions and editors who select materials for classroom anthologies shape our understanding of an author’s work. He himself is the editor of the new standard works of Byron, he has performed a comparable service for Swinburne, and he has been an influential spokesperson for a strong point of view within the recondite debates surrounding textual scholarship: Should textual scholarship publish a text that amalgamates a variety of available manuscripts and printed texts? Should the text it produces be the last and best thoughts of the author?—that’s an oversimplification of the position that McGann takes in this essay—or should it be the author’s first burst of inspiration? This last position seems dubious, perhaps, but all the critics who prefer the earliest versions of Wordsworth’s Prelude, for example (I include myself), would side with it at least on that occasion. In sum, we should understand McGann’s essay on Keats and the historical method to be a contribution to textual criticism, published in a book called The Beauty of Inflections that’s largely concerned with such matters.

因此，对麦克甘影响最大的与其说是福柯，不如说是巴赫金，他承认巴赫金是某个学派的成员：

The primary influence on McGann, then, is not so much Foucault as it is Bakhtin, whom he acknowledges as the member of a school:

以下内容是对所谓巴赫金学派批评理论中某些关键思想的总结和阐述。巴赫金学派是由一小群来自苏联的马克思主义批评家组成，他们早期就对诗歌的形式主义方法提出了挑战。巴赫金学派的社会历史方法将所有语言表达——包括诗歌——都视为具有具体起源和历史特征的现象。
What follows is a summary and extrapolation of certain key ideas set forth by the so-called Bakhtin School of criticism, a small group of Marxist critics from the Soviet Union who made an early attack upon formalist approaches to poetry. The Bakhtin School’s socio-historical method approaches all language utterances—including poems—as phenomena marked with their concrete origins and history.

这些现象的多样性被用来动摇传统的浪漫主义观念。麦克甘认为，如果用巴赫金的视角去聆听历史，就会发现浪漫主义中孤独个体的声音并非真正意义上的声音，而是各种视角交织融合而成的多元声音。

In their diversity, these phenomena are invoked to undermine standard notions of romanticism. If one listens to history with the attunement of Bakhtin, on McGann’s view, one realizes that the voice of the romantic solitary individual is not really that voice at all but a polyglossal infusion of various perspectives.

麦克甘对20世纪70年代和80年代历史复兴运动最具影响力的贡献是一本名为《浪漫主义意识形态》的小册子。该书抨击了当时广为流传的关于英国浪漫主义诗人的观点——例如M·H·艾布拉姆斯和耶鲁学派的观点——但其本质是对浪漫主义本身的批判。正如麦克甘所言，现代批评家的问题在于他们“仍然沉浸在浪漫主义之中”。《浪漫主义意识形态》融合了两个标题。其中一个是德国诗人、有时也自诩为浪漫主义者的海因里希·海涅早期对浪漫主义的重要批判著作《浪漫主义学派》 （ Die romantische Schule ）。该书强调并批判了浪漫主义诗人的主观性，甚至是唯我论，以及他们与社会关怀和历史进程的脱节。麦克甘书名中的“浪漫主义”（Romantic）一词便源于此。它引用的另一个标题是马克思的小册子《德意志意识形态》，该书内容广泛，但尤其关注那些自诩进步的咖啡馆知识分子，他们却像黑格尔一样认为思想创造物质环境，而非反之：简而言之，这些人是唯心主义者，因此，按照这种批判，他们也同样是浪漫主义者。在麦克甘关于济慈的文章中，所谓的耶鲁学派仍然受到抨击。保罗·德曼以及杰弗里·哈特曼关于济慈《致秋》的著名文章尤其受到批判，理由是，如果我们积极参与政治，并致力于融入社会共同体，那么我们对浪漫主义的解读必然是一种反浪漫主义的批判。

McGann’s most influential contribution to the return to history that marked the 1970s and 1980s was a short book called The Romantic Ideology, which is an attack on widely received ideas about the British romantic poets—those of M. H. Abrams and the Yale school, for example—but is really at bottom an attack on romanticism itself, the trouble with modern critics being, as McGann puts it, that they are “still in romanticism.” The Romantic Ideology is an amalgam of two titles. One is the important early critique of romanticism by the German poet and sometime romantic Heinrich Heine called Die romantische Schule, or The Romantic School, in which the subjectivity, even solipsism, and the isolation from social concern and from unfolding historical processes of the romantic poets is emphasized and criticized. That’s where the word “Romantic” comes from in McGann’s title. The other title it draws on is Marx’s pamphlet The German Ideology, which is about many things but in particular about coffeehouse intellectuals who consider themselves progressive but who think with Hegel that thought produces material circumstances rather than the other way around: people, in short, who are idealists and therefore, under this indictment, likewise romantic. The so-called Yale school is still under attack in McGann’s Keats essay.. Paul de Man, together with Geoffrey Hartman’s well-known essay on Keats’s “To Autumn,” are singled out for particular scorn, on the grounds that our reading of romanticism, if we are politically engaged and invested in the world as a social community, must necessarily be an anti-romantic critique.

我已经解释过，麦克甘在这篇文章中主要探讨的是文本研究方面的问题。他捍卫了济慈最后的深思熟虑的选择，并为此论证了1820年《指示报》出版的《无情的美人》版本才是济慈最后的深思熟虑之作，或者至少是他的最佳选择，而非蒙克顿·米尔恩斯于1848年出版的济慈遗作版本。麦克甘关于文本历史性、关于文本深受其创作环境和社会压力影响的论述，令人耳目一新，也很有价值。认为文本会凭空出现——如果有人曾经有过这种想法的话——显然站不住脚，而相反的观点，即文本是在复杂的社会和历史环境的交织下产生的，则无疑是合理的。至于麦克甘对“浪漫主义”的解读是否正确，则是一个更为复杂的问题。如果关于这些诗人的刻板印象成立，任何优秀的评论家都不可能愉快地阅读他们的作品，而麦克甘本人也对这些刻板印象是否成立持保留态度。他撰写的关于济慈的文章总体上旨在将济慈从这些刻板印象中解救出来。问题在于，如果我们认真对待格林布拉特关于诚实历史批评的主观性的坦率观点，这或许并不令人惊讶：麦克甘在这篇文章中对他选取的文本所做的所有论述，都相当容易受到反驳。

I have explained that McGann is engaged primarily in talking about issues of textual scholarship in this particular essay. He defends Keats’s last deliberate choices, and to this end he argues that the 1820 Indicator text of “La Belle Dame Sans Merci” is Keats’s last deliberate choice, or in any case his best choice, not the posthumous 1848 text published by Monckton Milnes. McGann’s general pronouncements about the historicity of texts, about the saturation of texts by the circumstances of their production and by social pressures, are bracing and worthwhile. The idea that a text just falls from a tree—if anybody ever had that idea—is plainly not a tenable one, and the opposite idea that a text emerges from a complex matrix of social and historical circumstances is certainly a good one. Whether McGann is right about “romanticism” is a more complex question. Certainly no good critic could ever happily read these poets if the stereotypes about them were valid, and McGann himself is on the fence about whether they are. The Keats essay is on the whole meant to rescue Keats from such stereotypes. The trouble is, and this is perhaps not surprising if one takes Greenblatt’s candor about the subjectivity of honest historical criticism seriously, that everything McGann says about the texts he has extracted for attention in this essay is quite consistently vulnerable to counter-argument.

以《无情的美人》为例。首先，谁说我们只能读1848年的版本？学术版本——麦克甘主要抨击的对象是杰克·斯蒂林格的济慈学术版本——会提供校勘记。当然，普通版本会用粗体字标出特定文本，但会将异文放在脚注中，有时甚至放在对页。它不会对读者隐瞒异文。人人都知道1820年的指示文本。“你这可怜的家伙，究竟有什么难处？”至少对我这个浪漫主义者来说，和“你这武士，究竟有什么难处？”一样熟悉——后者是1848年版本的开头；坦白说，有多少非浪漫主义者会认真思考这两个版本呢？

Take, for example, “La Belle Dame Sans Merci.” In the first place, who says we only read the 1848 text? A scholarly edition—and McGann’s main object of attack is Jack Stillinger’s scholarly edition of Keats—gives you a variorum apparatus. Sure, a typical edition gives you a particular text in bold print, but it gives you the variant text in a footnote, sometimes even on a facing page. It doesn’t conceal the variant text from you. Everybody knows the 1820 Indicator text. “What can ail thee, wretched wight?” is at least as familiar to me, as a romanticist, as “What can ail thee, knight at arms?”—which is how the 1848 text begins; and frankly, how many people who aren’t romanticists think a great deal about either text?

浪漫主义者们丝毫不会被这种针对1820年《指示者》文本的所谓历史阴谋所蒙蔽，而非浪漫主义者们也对此漠不关心。麦克甘的论点是，1820年的版本更好，因为它讲述的是一个普通男子（“wight”）和一个女孩相遇并发生性关系，但结局并不美好的故事。换句话说，它反映的是现实世界。它并非浪漫爱情诗；而1848年版本中的“你为何如此，骑士？”——以及它的所有其他变体，例如“四吻”等等——则是一首不加修饰的浪漫幻想诗，它秉持着中世纪关于女性的观念，既将女性奉为神明，又惧怕她们，因为她们可能会让那些值得尊敬的年轻绅士失去理智。为什么1848年版本中这种糟糕的意识形态会占据主导地位呢？因为保存了那个版本的查尔斯·布朗对女性的行为卑鄙无耻，而且不喜欢范妮·布朗，又因为 1848 年版的实际编辑蒙克顿·米尔恩斯是一位情色作品收藏家。

The romanticists are not in any way hornswoggled by this alleged historical conspiracy against the 1820 Indicator text, and people who aren’t romanticists don’t care. McGann’s argument is that the 1820 version is better because it’s a poem about an ordinary guy (a “wight”) and a girl who meet up and have sex and it doesn’t turn out so well. In other words, it’s about the real world. It’s not a romance; whereas “What can ail thee, knight at arms?” in the 1848 version—and all of its other variants, the “kisses four” and so on—is an unself-conscious romance fantasy subscribing to medieval ideas about women, simultaneously putting them on a pedestal and fearing them because they might take the sap out of deserving young gentlemen. Why did the bad ideology of the 1848 version prevail? Because Charles Brown, who saved that version, behaved despicably toward women and didn’t like Fanny Brawne, and because Monckton Milnes, the actual editor of the 1848 edition, was a collector of erotica.

除此之外，谁又能断言1848年的版本不是济慈的最后构思呢？ 1820年《指示者》版出版时，他已身患重病。他那时已接近思维能力的极限，难以清晰地思考自己的作品，也无暇顾及作品的出版方式或是否出版；与此同时，我们也不知道布朗何时收到了济慈的版本。我们不能假设布朗只是简单地重写了一遍，如果他没有重写，那么济慈一定是把1848年的版本交给了他。谁又能断言那不是济慈的最后构思，即便不是他最好的作品呢？毕竟，标题取自阿兰·夏蒂埃的中世​​纪民谣《无情的美人》（La Belle Dame Sans Merci），印证了“骑士，你为何如此？”（What can ail thee, knight at arm?）的版本。这首诗讲述的是摩根勒菲的故事。无论好坏，无论我们从意识形态上如何看待它，如果标题正确的话，这首诗描绘的是 1848 年版本中描绘的那种女性，而不是 1820 年版本中不那么生动的那种女性。

Apart from that, who’s to say the 1848 text wasn’t Keats’s last thought? He was already ill when the Indicator text was published in 1820. He was close to the end of his ability to think clearly about his own work and to worry very much about how or whether it was published; and at the same time we don’t know when Brown received his version of the text. We can’t suppose Brown just sat down and rewrote it, and if he didn’t rewrite it, then Keats must have given it to him in the 1848 form. Who’s to say that wasn’t his last thought, if not his best? After all, the title, taken from a medieval ballad by Alain Chartier, “La Belle Dame Sans Merci,” bears out the “What can ail thee, knight at arms?” version. It’s about a Morgan Le Fay. For better or worse, whatever we think of it ideologically, if the title is right, the poem is about the kind of woman who is evoked in the 1848 version, not the less colorful one in the 1820 version.

因此，1848 年版与两个版本中出现的标题更为一致，尽管 1848 年版的标题显然不那么带有明显的讽刺意味。此外，尽管我们可以对济慈严谨的才智赞不绝口（换句话说，如果浪漫意味着愚蠢，那么这与“浪漫”毫无关系），但实际上，我们没有任何理由赞赏他记录在案的关于女性的观点。麦克甘恩试图为济慈的文本注入一种令人愉悦的政治正确性。从我们自身的历史视角来看——格林布拉特强调这是任何历史学家都必须考虑的问题——我们不希望济慈以如此贬低女性的方式思考问题。但他的信件和其他诗歌表明，他的确有过这样的想法。因此，你或许可以得出结论：1848 年版才是他真正想要并偏爱的版本。或者更确切地说，既然两个版本都存在，并且各有其价值，那么我们就把它们都保留下来吧，毕竟各种版本都提供了这两种选择。

So the 1848 version is simply more consistent with the title one finds in both versions, though the title is certainly less knowingly ironic in the 1848. The additional point to be made is that while there are all sorts of things to say about the scrupulous intelligence of Keats (nothing to do with “romantic” in other words if romantic means stupid), there is in fact no reason to admire his recorded opinions about women. McGann wants to infuse Keats’s text with a pleasing political correctness. From our own historical horizon—which Greenblatt for his part emphasizes as part of any historian’s agenda—we don’t want Keats to have thought in that demeaning way about women. But his letters and his other poems suggest that he did. Therefore, you might feel free to conclude, the 1848 text is the one he intended and preferred. Or rather, since both texts do exist and offer different sorts of interest, let’s just have both of them, which the various editions after all do give us.

对于麦克甘对其他他着重提及的诗歌的解读，同样存在各种各样的反对意见。这些论点精妙绝伦，也确实引人深思，但它们并不像麦克甘所希望的那样具有决定性。它们旨在证明某种观点的正确性。正如格林布拉特充分承认的那样，所有历史主义批评都带有倾向性，它既是文本的创造者，也是文本的创造者，而他自己的批评恰恰因其坦诚地承认这一点而澄清了这一点。

The same variety of objections can be made to McGann’s readings of the other poems he singles out. They are ingenious arguments, and certainly provoke reflection, but they are not as conclusive as McGann wants them to be. They argue for victory. All historicist criticism is tendentious, as Greenblatt fully acknowledges, producing and reproducing texts as much as it is produced by them, and his own criticism clears the air in being openly so.

让我快速回顾一下从巴赫金到新历史主义的托尼，略过詹姆逊对托尼的解读，因为我们在上一讲结尾已经讨论过了。先从巴赫金说起，你会发现《拖车托尼》的第一部分完全充斥着第一人称单数：我做这个，我做那个，我喜欢我的工作，我被困住了——我，我，我，我。然后，随着阅读的深入，你会发现“我”消失了，或者即使出现，也出现在一行中间，被其他音节环绕，而不是在开头。对自我的强调——无论我多么迷人，我都优先——随着故事的展开，逐渐被故事的社会性所取代。我不再是作为浪漫个体的“我”。我是一个朋友的“我”，我定义着一个朋友，甚至“称呼”一个朋友（这才是真正的朋友）：一个与他者的关系构成其身份认同的人。在这种互惠互利的友谊中，第一人称单数消失了。换句话说， 《拖车托尼》中最终呈现的并非个体主观的声音，而是社会团结的声音。然而，这种改变后的声音与那些不变的声音形成了鲜明的对比。一丝不苟的声音和工作狂的声音都带有不可渗透的自我中心主义，第一人称单数永远是第一位的。

Let me turn quickly to review Tony from Bakhtin to the New Historicism, gliding over Tony according to Jameson, because we did that at the end of the last lecture. Starting then with Bakhtin, you can see that the first part of Tony the Tow Truck is completely saturated with the first person singular: I do this, I do that, I like my job, I am stuck—I, I, I, I. Then as you read along, you see that the “I” disappears, or if it still appears, it’s in the middle of a line, cozily surrounded by other sounds, rather than at the beginning. The emphasis on the self—me first, however charming I may be—is gradually subsumed by the sociality of the story as it unfolds. I am no longer “I” defined as a romantic individual. I am “I” defined as a friend and defining a friend, even “calling” a friend (now that’s what I call a friend): a person whose relation with otherness is what constitutes his identity. In that mutuality of friendship, the first-person singular disappears. What is spoken in Tony the Tow Truck, in other words, is not in the long run the voice of individual subjectivity but the voice of social togetherness. Yet this altered voice is pitched polyglossally against voices that don’t alter. The fastidious voice and the workaholic voice share an impermeable egoism, the first-person singular always singularly first.

在雅斯看来， 《拖车托尼》的关键在于它与《小火车头》的故事截然不同。每一代读者都会重新审视、反思和重组当时盛行的审美标准。新的审美视野由此出现，文本的构成方式也随之改变，这与俄国形式主义者的观点颇为相似，只是雅斯认为文学变革背后存在着确定的历史因素。《小火车头》讲述的是弱者和强者之间的权力颠倒，弱者帮助强者，角色发生了彻底的反转，正如圣经中的先知以赛亚所言，山谷被填平，高山被夷平。而《拖车托尼》的故事则并非如此。弱者自身也需要帮助。他需要另一个弱者的帮助。小与大之间存在着一种互惠关系，这种关系并非辩证的对立，而是相互促进、逐步增强。这正是《小火车头》和《拖车托尼》之间视角转变的体现。沃蒂·派珀的《小火车头》取材于1910年的故事，但其新版本很快成为经典。该书出版于1930年，正值经济大萧条的深渊。马克思主义的风席卷全球，革命的气息弥漫在空气中。相比之下， 《拖车托尼》则反映了晚期资本主义的困境，即使对詹姆逊来说，也难以想象如何克服。小人物和大人物就像夜航的船只，小人物互相帮助，因为没有人会伸出援手。

According to Jauss, the important thing about Tony the Tow Truck is that it is not the same story as The Little Engine That Could. In each generation of reception, the aesthetic standards that prevail at a given time are reconsidered and rethought, reshuffled. A new aesthetic horizon emerges, and texts are constituted in a different way, much also as the Russian formalists had said, only with the sense in Jauss of determinate historical issues behind literary change. The Little Engine That Could concerns the inversion of power between the little guy and the big guy, so that the little guy helps the big guy in a definite reversal of roles, demonstrating, with the prophet Isaiah in the Bible, that the valleys have been raised and the mountains made low. That’s not the way Tony the Tow Truck works. The little guy himself needs help. He needs the help of another little guy. There is a reciprocity that is not dialectical between little and big but a mutual reinforcement of little by little, and that is the change in horizon that one can witness between The Little Engine That Could and Tony the Tow Truck. Watty Piper’s Little Engine, itself drawing on a story of 1910 but quickly canonical in its new form, appeared in 1930, the depths of the Depression. Winds of Marxist doctrine circled the world, and revolution was in the air. Tony, by contrast, reflects the impasse of late capitalism, so hard to imagine surmounting even for Jameson. Little guys and big guys are like ships in the night, and little guys help each other because nobody else will.

在本雅明看来，关键在于叙述者即是“装置”这一概念。换句话说，我们是从“装置”的视角来看待事物。正如电影观众从摄影机的视角观看事物一样，我们也从拖车托尼的视角来看待这个故事。结果如何呢？正如摄影机的视角使所见之物如本雅明所说“摆脱了设备”，同样地，如果我们从“装置”的视角来看待事物，我们便会注意到故事的寓意：换句话说，我们会注意到故事的人性，以及它所传达的寓意——工具化，将他人简化为纯粹的工具，是一件坏事。换句话说，在所有这些“装置”的包围下，我们所看到的，正是摆脱了“装置”的、纯粹人性的现实。通过我们与机械化世界的认同，我们实现了机械化世界的人性化，这正是《拖车托尼》所讲述的故事。因此，拖车托尼的运作方式与本雅明的机械再生产理论相符。然而，在阿多诺看来，机械再生产装置默许其卑微的服务角色——在阶级关系的不平等中一遍又一遍地拖拽——这种默许一如既往地遭到尼托和斯皮迪的反对，这证明本雅明理论所假定的独立于文化工业运作的装置，最终必然会被文化工业收买，为己所用。

In Benjamin, the important thing is the idea that the narrator is the apparatus. We see things, in other words, from the point of view of the apparatus. Just as the filmgoer sees things from the point of view of the camera, so we see Tony the Tow Truck from the point of view of the tow truck. And what happens? Just as the camera-eye point of view leaves that which is seen, as Benjamin puts it, “equipment-free,” so, oddly enough, if we see things from the standpoint of equipment, we are pointed toward the moral of the story: in other words, toward the humanity of the story, with its moral that instrumentalization, the reduction of others to mere equipment, is a bad thing. What we see, in other words, surrounded by all of this equipment, is nothing other than the equipment-free, purely humanized aspect of reality. The humanization of a mechanized world, through our identification with it, is what takes place in Tony the Tow Truck. So Tony the Tow Truck works in a way that is consistent with Benjamin’s theory of mechanical reproduction. For Adorno, however, the acquiescence of the apparatus of mechanical reproduction in its abject service role, towing again and again and again, in the inequity of class relations, rejected as always by Neato and Speedy, proves that the apparatus Benjamin’s theory supposes to be independent of the machinations of the culture industry can be and inevitably will be suborned by the culture industry for its own purposes.

传统历史主义对托尼的解读重申了一种现状：美德清晰，恶行清晰，二者毋庸置疑，一切都一成不变——换句话说，这种现状反映了一种永恒的社会动态。新历史主义的解读或许也会止步于此，因为它似乎无可避免。但我想最后提出一点：如果文学影响历史，那么拖车托尼的故事或许可以解释为什么我们今天提倡节能汽车。托尼是对油老虎、SUV和小型货车的抨击——别忘了，那辆说着“我太忙了”的车可能是一位家庭主妇。如果我们淘汰悍马，如果我们缩小现有车型的尺寸，使其更加人性化，或许正是因为托尼和他的朋友邦比。由此可见，这又是一部既影响历史又受历史影响的文本。

The old historicist reading of Tony reconfirms a status quo in which virtue is clear, vice is clear, both are uncontested, and nothing changes—in other words, a status quo that reflects a timeless social dynamic. The New Historicist approach might stop short with this reading as well, as it certainly seems inescapable. But let me just conclude by suggesting that if literature influences history, Tony the Tow Truck might well explain why today we’re promoting fuel-efficient cars. Tony is an attack on the gas guzzler, the SUV and the minivan—remember the car that says “I am too busy” may be a soccer mom. If we get rid of the Humvee, if we downsize and streamline the available models to a more human scale, maybe it’s because of Tony and his friend Bumpy. Here, then, is yet another text influencing history as much as we have shown it to be influenced by history.

关于托尼拖车，有一点需要说明，那就是车里没有女性，至少在街上没有，而这正是我们接下来要讨论的问题。

One thing that needs to be said about Tony the Tow Truck is that there are no women in it, at least not on the street, and that is the issue that we’ll be taking up next.

 

 

第二十章

CHAPTER 20

古典女权主义传统
The Classical Feminist Tradition

阅读材料：

Readings:

伍尔夫，弗吉尼亚。“奥斯汀-勃朗特-艾略特”和“雌雄同体的视野”。载《批评传统》，第 602-610 页。

Woolf, Virginia. “Austen-Brontë-Eliot” and “The Androgynous Vision.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 602–610.

Showalter, Elaine. “走向女性主义诗学。”载于《批评传统：经典文本与当代趋势》，David H. Richter 编（第 2 版：波士顿：Bedford，1998 年），第 1375-1386 页。

Showalter, Elaine. “Toward a Feminist Poetics.” In The Critical Tradition: Classic Texts and Contemporary Trends, ed. David H. Richter (2nd ed.: Boston: Bedford, 1998), pp. 1375–1386.

本次讲座的大部分内容都是预备知识，但就像文学作品中称为“预叙”的修辞手法一样，这些预备知识首次涵盖了以后将要重新探讨的主题。

Quite a bit of this lecture consists in preliminaries, yet like the rhetorical device called “prolepsis” in literary texts, they are preliminaries that cover for the first time topics to be revisited later.

首先，必须指出的是，在本课程中，当我们进入以特定人类身份为理论焦点的阶段时，我们将接触到一些在实践中极其丰富且富有成效的批判方法。正如乔纳森·库勒所言，“以女性的视角阅读”，或以非裔美国人的视角阅读，或以任何其他“主体位置”阅读，都会彻底改变一切，这着实令人惊叹。身份批判的实践价值远超其本身。

First, let it be said that in entering upon the phase of this course that concerns particular human identities as theoretical focal points, we shall find ourselves engaged with critical approaches that are, in practical terms, remarkably rich and productive. It is simply amazing how, as Jonathan Culler once put it, “reading as a woman,” or reading as an African American, or reading in any other “subject position” transforms everything. The practical payoff of identity criticism is more than considerable.

正如我们上次所见，斯蒂芬·格林布拉特的轶事以伊丽莎白女王的一句话开篇：“我就是理查二世，你们难道不知道吗？”格林布拉特当时并没有打算从女性主义批评的角度，或者从性别理论的角度来解读这种说法（我们稍后会讨论性别理论）；但即便如此，伊丽莎白女王说出这样的话仍然令人震惊，不是吗？这表明，作为一名女性，她不仅会恐惧女性传统上所遭受的苦难和危险，还会恐惧男性角色所面临的苦难和危险，这是多么非凡。她的说法更加复杂，因为她非常清楚，尽管女性“成为”理查二世的情况极为罕见，但也并非闻所未闻。伊丽莎白本人就曾拥立苏格兰女王玛丽为理查二世。她囚禁并斩首了玛丽，正如她担心埃塞克斯伯爵也会囚禁并斩首她一样。因此，当我们从性别经验的角度来思考这句话——“我是理查二世，你难道不知道吗？”——时，它的意义就与新历史主义轶事中的含义截然不同了。

As we saw last time, Stephen Greenblatt’s anecdote begins with Queen Elizabeth saying, “I am Richard II, know you not that?” Greenblatt wasn’t at the time concerned to read a pronouncement of that sort from the standpoint of feminist criticism, or indeed from the standpoint of gender theory, to which we’ll be turning on a later occasion; but still, it’s quite an amazing thing for Queen Elizabeth to say, isn’t it? It shows how remarkable it is that she, a woman, would find herself fearing not only the kind of suffering and peril that her own sex has traditionally endured but fearing in addition the suffering and peril that one would experience in a masculine role. Her claim is complicated yet more because she knows full well that despite the rarity of a woman “being” Richard II, it’s not unheard of. Elizabeth herself has made a Richard II of Mary Queen of Scots. She has imprisoned and beheaded Mary, just as she fears the Earl of Essex will imprison and behead her. So this remark—“I am Richard II, know you not that?”—comes to life in a completely different way from its life in a New Historicist anecdote when we think about it as a question of a gendered experience.

在上一讲的结尾，为了做个铺垫，我撒了个小谎。我说《拖车托尼》里没有女性角色，当然，如果只看文字，确实没有女性。里面只有几辆男性汽车在说话。但是，如果你把之前提到的插图和文字结合起来，就会发现除了汽车之外还有其他角色。房子们脸上既有皱眉，也有微笑。当邦比终于出现并推了托尼一把时，不仅是汽车们为之高兴，就连背景里那些之前一直对尼托和斯皮迪的自私行为表示不满的房子们也露出了笑容。当邦比帮助托尼时，房子们都露出了赞许的神情，认为这是件合乎道德的事情。

At the end of the last lecture, by way of further preliminary, I told a little fib. I said that there were no women in Tony the Tow Truck, and of course in looking only at the prose there are no women. There are just male cars talking. However, if to the prose text you add the illustrations that I’ve told you about, you can see that there are characters other than the cars. There are frowns and smiles on the faces of the houses. It’s not just the cars that are happy about what’s going on when Bumpy finally comes along and pushes Tony, it’s also the houses in the background, which until now have been expressing disapproval at the selfishness of Neato and Speedy. When Bumpy helps Tony, the houses beam their approval that the morally correct thing is being done.

但她们自身却无法成为道德主体。她们无力地被束缚在家庭生活的场所中。在维多利亚时代——我认为托尼拖车在这方面确实可以追溯到维多利亚时代——有一位名叫考文垂·帕特莫尔的诗人，他其实是一位不错的诗人，却因写了一首长诗而在女权主义传统中声名狼藉。诗中他将女性描述为“家中的天使”。你可能熟悉这个表达。安·道格拉斯大约三十五年前出版的巨著《美国文化的女性化》也体现了这一观点。这本书认为，在十九世纪的美国，道德、审美和文化价值观在客厅和茶桌旁落入了女性（以及神职人员）手中，她们向社会各界人士——而这些人全是男性——规定了在处理事务时应有的礼仪规范。换句话说，天使在家中的职责不仅仅是做饭和照顾孩子，尽管这始终是其重要组成部分。天使在家中的职责还包括评判家庭内外的道德问题，而这些房子显然正是如此，它们受到天使的指引，时而微笑，时而皱眉。所以，说到底，拖车托尼家也有女性成员。

But they have not been able to perform as moral agents themselves. They are helplessly fixed in place as sites of domesticity. In the Victorian period—and I do think Tony the Tow Truck in this regard hearkens back to the Victorian period—there was a poet named Coventry Patmore, not really a bad poet, who became notorious in the feminist tradition for having written a long poem in which he describes woman as “the angel in the house.” You’re probably familiar with that expression. It’s an idea that’s embodied also in a monumental book of some thirty-five years ago by Ann Douglas called The Feminization of American Culture. This book argues that in nineteenth-century America, moral, aesthetic, and cultural values passed into the hands of women (and clergymen) in the drawing room and at the tea table, dictating to the agents of society—all of whom were male—what a proper decorum in the conduct of affairs ought to be. In other words, the role of the angel in the house was not just to cook the meals and take care of the kids, although that has always been a big part of it. The role of the angel in the house is also to adjudicate the moral aspect of life at the domestic level and beyond, and that’s exactly what these houses are doing, obviously inspirited by angels that make them smile and frown. So after all, there are women in Tony the Tow Truck.

转向身份认同的视角并非我们阅读中的一个十字路口。它并非像从语言到心理再到社会那样，因为我们显然仍然处于社会层面。事实上，我们并非此前从未接触过社会视角这一概念。显然，我们以各种方式接触过它；但尤其是在巴赫金或詹姆逊的著作中，我们了解到阶级冲突是如何以对话的形式在文学作品中表达出来的，并且需要结合身份认同的概念——在本例中是阶级身份认同——来解读文学文本，才能真正理解其含义。

The transition to an identity focus is not exactly a crossroads in our reading. It’s not like moving from language to the psyche to the social, because obviously we’re still very much in the social. In fact, it’s not as though we haven’t hitherto encountered the notion of social perspective. Obviously we have in all sorts of ways; but particularly in the work of Bakhtin or Jameson, we’re introduced to the way class conflict is expressed in literary form dialogically and needs to be read with notions of identity in mind—in this case class identity—if the literary text is to be understood.

但这里却隐藏着一个问题。我曾指出，在我们的阅读过程中，某些时刻会让人走到十字路口，无法同时选择两条路。理论层面上的身份认同问题之所以复杂，尽管在实践层面未必如此，是因为这种十字路口是不可避免的。当我们关注身份认同时，我们开始感受到各种进步观点之间日益激烈的竞争。在接下来的讨论中，我会不时地指出这一点，但从一开始就存在一个至今仍棘手的竞争根源：马克思主义视角（其关注阶级）与其他身份认同视角（包括女权主义视角）之间的关系。身份认同和意识的根本决定因素是什么？例如，是阶级还是性别？这并非我们今天才因某种迟来的深刻理解而偶然发现的新话题。不妨听听弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在《一间自己的房间》（600）中的论述：

But herein lurks a problem. I have pointed out certain moments in our reading in which one arrives at a crossroads and simply cannot take both paths. What complicates considerations of identity at the theoretical level, though not at all necessarily at the practical level, is that such crossroads moments are inescapable. As we turn our attention to identity, we begin to feel an increased competitiveness among admirably progressive perspectives. I’m going to be pointing this out from time to time in the sequence of discussions that we now undertake, but from the very beginning there is a source of competition that remains problematic to this day: the relationship between the Marxist perspective, with its focus on class, and other sorts of identity focus, including the feminist one. What is the underlying determination of identity and consciousness? Is it class or gender, just for example? This is not a new topic that we stumble upon today as a result of some belated sophistication we have achieved. Listen to Virginia Woolf in A Room of One’s Own (600):

像莎士比亚那样的天才，并非诞生于劳苦、未受教育、卑微的人民之中。它并非诞生于英国的撒克逊人和不列颠人之中。它也不是诞生于当今的工人阶级之中。那么，这种天才又怎能诞生于那些女性之中呢？特里维廉教授指出，她们几乎在离开育婴室之前就开始工作，她们被父母强迫，并受到法律和习俗的种种约束。然而，正如天才必然存在于工人阶级之中一样，女性之中也必然存在某种天才。
For genius like Shakespeare’s is not born among labouring, uneducated, servile people. It was not born in England among the Saxons and the Britons. It is not born today among the working classes. How, then, could it have been born among women whose work began, according to Professor Trevelyan, almost before they were out of the nursery, who were forced to it by their parents and held to it by all the power of law and custom? Yet genius of a sort must have existed among women as it must have existed among the working classes.

值得注意的是，面对她所揭示的问题，伍尔夫在这里有所保留。她并没有说阶级优先于性别，也没有说性别优先于阶级，尽管她承认，当我们考察女性受压迫的历史或女性表达形式受限的历史时，阶级和性别可能是相互竞争的解释模式。像玛丽·卡文迪什或凯瑟琳·菲利普斯（“无与伦比的奥琳达”）这样的贵族女性的境遇与伍尔夫笔下的“朱迪思·莎士比亚”有所不同——尽管并非完全不同。 《一间自己的房间》的标题将我们的注意力引向一个至少部分涉及阶级的问题，如果我们仅仅将这本小册子视为早期女权主义的一次尝试，这或许会令人惊讶。伍尔夫后来关于女性在进步社会运动中可能发挥的作用的小册子《三枚金币》的标题则更明显地体现了阶级导向。这些标题都根植于物质环境。伍尔夫站在牛津剑桥女学生面前，说她只有一句话要说：如果你想在写作或任何其他摆脱父权制禁令的活动中有所作为，你真的需要每年有 500 英镑和一间属于自己的房间。

Notice that in the face of the problem she has uncovered Woolf is pulling her punches here. She is not saying class has priority over gender or gender has priority over class, even as she admits that they could be rival modes of explanation when we consider the history of the oppression of women or the history of the limits on the forms of women’s expression. Things were different for aristocratic women like Mary Cavendish or Katherine Phillips (the “matchless Orinda”) than they were for Woolf’s “Judith Shakespeare”—though not wholly different. The title of A Room of One’s Own calls our attention to a problem that touches at least in part on class, surprisingly, perhaps, if we think of this pamphlet solely as an early feminist salvo. Even more clearly class-oriented is the title of Woolf’s later pamphlet about the possible scope of activity for women in progressive social movements, Three Guineas. These titles are grounded in material circumstances. Woolf stands before her audience of Oxbridge women and says she has just one thing to say: if you expect to get anything done in the way of writing or any other activity that frees itself from patriarchal prohibition, you really need to have 500 pounds a year and a room of your own.

事实上，当你通读《一间自己的房间》的六个章节时，你会发现，尽管每一章都充满了丰富而富有印象派风格的洞见，但伍尔夫的笔触总是会回到这个特定的主题上。如果你不是简·奥斯汀，如果你不是一个天才作家，坐在客厅里，每当仆人或亲戚进屋时，就把正在创作的小说藏在针线活下面，那么你就必须拥有500英镑和一间属于自己的房间。我认为，即使在《一间自己的房间》——即便不是最伟大的，也绝对是迄今为止最雄辩的关于女性写作状况的女权主义论著——中，阶级视角也占据了一定的优先地位。如果不采取措施重新分配金钱和权力，性别将继续受到金钱和权力的影响。

In fact, as you read through the six chapters of A Room of One’s Own, you find that after the wide array of impressionistic insight that enriches each chapter, Woolf is always pulled back to this one particular. If you’re not Jane Austen, if you’re not a genius sitting in the family parlor whisking your novel-in-progress under a piece of needlework every time a servant or relative comes into the room, then you simply must have 500 pounds and a room of your own. I think one could show that even in A Room of One’s Own—which is, if not the greatest, certainly the most eloquent feminist treatise on the conditions of women’s writing ever written—there is a measure of priority given to the perspective of class. Gender will continue to be conditioned by the effects of money and power if something isn’t done to redistribute money and power.

这类紧张关系不仅持续困扰着女性主义批评，也困扰着其他基于身份认同的批评形式，直至今日。以身份认同视角为主题的会议通常会演变成围绕这一问题的辩论。这类会议上最机智的辩手往往是那些能抢占先机的人，他们会说，在场的所有人都天真地以为会议所宣布的身份认同主题就是根本问题。虽然马克思主义牌在这种场合出现的频率很高，但并非总是如此。你几乎总能预料到，最后总会有人抛出这样一番话，让在场的所有人都开始反思，他们究竟应该思考的是女性——例如——还是其他什么问题。正如我希望在讲座结束时已经阐明的那样，“经典女性主义批评”需要补充其他方面的关注，或许可以借鉴德里达的理论，例如这里提到的阶级考量和性别理论。在讲座结束时，我将开始解释后一种补充内容可能包含哪些内容，然后在几节课后讨论朱迪斯·巴特勒和米歇尔·福柯时再回到这个问题。

These sorts of tension continue to haunt not just feminist criticism but other forms of criticism grounded in identity to this day. Conferences featuring identity perspectives typically develop into debates on precisely this issue. The cleverest debaters at such conferences are the ones who get in the last word and say that everyone present has been naive to suppose that the announced identity topic of the conference is the basic issue. It’s not always the Marxist card that’s played in this setting, although it frequently is. You can nearly always count on a last word of this kind that sends everybody off to wonder whether they were supposed to have been thinking about women—for example—or about something else. As I hope to have made clear by the end of the lecture, “classical feminist criticism” needs to be supplemented, perhaps in the Derridean sense, by other emphases, one of which is the consideration of class mentioned here and one of which is gender theory. At the end of the lecture, I’ll begin explaining what this latter supplement might entail, and then come back to it when we discuss Judith Butler and Michel Foucault a few lectures from now.

《一间自己的房间》是一部令人惊叹的杰作，也是我最喜欢的书之一。我把它当作小说来读，在很多方面它的确是一部小说。伍尔夫研究学者喜欢称它为“小说散文”。然而，即便如此，这种毫无争议的说法本身也可能引发一个问题：如果夏洛蒂·勃朗特因为其作品中带有倾向性，因为公开抱怨她所感受到的压迫而受到指责，而这种倾向性又是否妨碍了她小说的充分表达？也就是说，正如弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫正确指出的那样，如果我们疑惑为什么在简·爱抱怨自己想旅行、想开阔眼界之后，格蕾丝·普尔突然出现，并且意识到格蕾丝·普尔显得格格不入，是因为简·爱的抱怨在叙事结构中造成了裂痕：如果对夏洛蒂·勃朗特的这种批评是公平的，那么它也可以被用来批评《一间自己的房间》中叙事和抗议的交织——尽管毫无疑问，伍尔夫比勃朗特更擅长用讽刺的溶剂将叙事和抗议融合在一起。

A Room of One’s Own is an amazing tour de force. It’s one of my favorite books. I read it like a novel, and in many ways it is a novel. Woolf scholars like to call it a “novel-essay.” Yet to make this uncontroversial claim about it may already raise a question. If Charlotte Brontë is to be called to account for tendentiousness, for complaining openly of perceived oppression, and if Charlotte Brontë’s tendentiousness gets in the way of the full expression of her novel; if, that is, as Virginia Woolf rightly remarks, we wonder why Grace Pool suddenly appears after Jane’s diatribe about wishing that she could travel and that her horizons were broader, and we realize that Grace Pool is out of place because Jane’s complaint has made a rift in the narrative fabric: if this criticism of Charlotte Brontë is fair, then it could also be turned against the interspersing of narrative and protest in A Room of One’s Own itself—though undoubtedly Woolf is more deft at blending narrative and protest with the solvent of irony than Brontë was.

只有读完《一间自己的房间》的全部六章，你才能真正体会到这一点。我强烈建议你读完，因为它真的很有趣。叙述者说：“你想叫我什么都行”，这与梅尔维尔笔下的叙述者说“叫我以实玛利”如出一辙。叫我玛丽·贝顿、玛丽·塞顿、玛丽·卡迈克尔都行。其实都无所谓，但我的确经历过一些奇遇，而作为读者或听众的你或许会认为这些经历是虚构的。叙事本身就刻意地将自己置于虚构的世界中。

This could only strike you forcefully if you read the whole of A Room of One’s Own, all six chapters, which I urge you to do because it’s so much fun. The speaker says, “call me anybody you like,” not unlike Melville’s speaker saying, “Call me Ishmael.” Call me Mary Beton, Mary Seton, Mary Carmichael. It doesn’t really matter, but I’ve had certain adventures and you the reader or listener may suppose that they are fictitious. The narrative shelters itself quite by design in the world of fiction.

事实并非如此，正如她在第一章中告诉我们的那样，她，玛丽·贝顿，坐在河边，苦思冥想着究竟该如何向这些年轻女士们讲述女性与小说，最终她灵光一闪。这就像从河里捞出一条鱼，鱼儿在她脑海里游来游去。她兴奋不已，径直穿过草地。这时，一位身着学院长袍、气宇轩昂的执事站了起来，指着碎石小路，告诉她，作为一名未经许可的女性，她应该走这条路，因为草地只供与大学有关联的男性使用。她心事重重地去了图书馆，却被一位老先生告知，由于她是女性，需要一封介绍信才能进入。于是，她虚构的思考日——思考究竟该如何向这些年轻女性讲述女性与小说——就这样开始了，对她而言，这并非愉快的一天，而是一个女人讲述一个女人遭受不公待遇的故事。

It really isn’t true, as she tells us in the first chapter, that she, Mary Beton, has been sitting by the river wondering what on earth she’s going to tell these young ladies about women and fiction when finally she gets a little idea. It’s like pulling a fish out of the river, and the fish starts swimming around in her head. She becomes quite excited and she walks off across the grass. At that point a beadle rises up, a formidable person wearing college gowns and pointing at the gravel path where she, as an unauthorized woman, should be walking, as the grass is intended only for the men affiliated with the university. She goes to the library in this preoccupied state, only to be told by an elderly gentleman that since she’s a woman she needs a letter of introduction to get in. And so her fictitious day of thinking about what on earth she should say to these young women about women and fiction begins, unpleasantly for her character, as a presented fiction by a woman about a woman treated unfairly.

午餐很愉快。她受邀来到校园，身份是一位杰出的作家。只要不惹是生非，身为小说家的女性也无妨。她正是以这个身份，或许也因为认识在场的某位人士，才受邀参加这场午餐。午餐很愉快，因为是由男士买单，而且氛围也完全是为男士设计的。之后，她去拜访一位在虚构的女子学院任教的女性朋友。她在学院的餐厅与朋友共进晚餐，晚餐简陋乏味。晚餐后，她们去了朋友的房间，开始谈论这所学院的建造条件。十九世纪，一群女性竭尽全力筹集了三万英镑，学院的建设简朴无华，没有任何花哨的装饰。她们当时身无分文，也没有任何大笔捐款，所以草坪无人修剪，砖墙也朴素无华。

It continues with a very pleasant lunch. She’s been invited to the campus as a distinguished writer. It’s okay to be a woman who is a novelist as long as you don’t rock the boat too much. In that capacity and no doubt as an acquaintance of someone present, she has been invited to such a lunch, which is very pleasant because it’s paid for by men in an atmosphere that is designed for men. Then she goes to visit a woman friend who is teaching at the fictitious women’s college. She has dinner with the friend in that college’s dining hall, the dinner is inferior and plain, and then they go to the friend’s rooms and start talking about the conditions under which this college was built. A group of women in the nineteenth century did all they could do to raise 30,000 pounds, no frills, thank you very much. None of them had any money, there have been no major donations, so the grass never gets cut and the brick is plain and unadorned.

第二天，主人公来到伦敦大英图书馆的主阅览室（女性可以进入），因为她决定一定要弄清楚人们对女性的看法。尽管被要求讨论女性，她却不知道“女性”究竟是什么，她带着一种恶毒的谦逊坦白道，所以最好还是去咨询专家。她发现成百上千的男人写过关于女性的书：论及女性的低劣、女性的道德敏感、女性缺乏体力等等，不胜枚举。她把这些书都列入了图书馆的目录。这真是一个绝妙的讽刺机会，既滑稽又带有讽刺意味。人们感觉，她不会让夏洛蒂·勃朗特就这么算了。弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫想说，夏洛蒂·勃朗特必须克制自己的愤怒，才能将她心中所有的想法表达出来。嗯，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的语气听起来并不愤怒，她很清楚不该显得愤怒；但我们知道她是在用喜剧的方式发泄愤怒，这也不足为奇。

The next day the protagonist goes to the main reading room of the British Library in London (where women are allowed) because she decides she really must find out what people think of women. She doesn’t know what a woman is even though she’s been asked to discuss women, she confesses with malicious humility, so she’d better consult the experts. She finds out that hundreds and hundreds of men have written books about women: on the inferiority of women, the moral sensitivity of women, the lack of physical strength of women, on and on and on. She lists them as items in the library catalogue. It’s an occasion for delicious satire, hilarious yet still tendentious. She wouldn’t let Charlotte Brontë get away with that, one feels. Charlotte Brontë has to suspend her anger, Virginia Woolf wants to say, if she’s going to get the whole of what’s on her mind expressed. Well, Virginia Woolf doesn’t sound very angry, she knows better than to sound angry; yet we know she is venting her anger in comic effects, as well she might.

《一间自己的房间》的其余部分都发生在叙述者的书房里，也就是她自己的房间里。她大致按照时间顺序从书架上取书。在文学史的早期，她查看书架上本应摆放女性作家作品的地方，却发现一本也没有；后来，确实出现了一些女性作家，其中不乏小说家。而到了近代，女性作家的活动空间略有扩大，但她们仍然要与那些令人反感的男性作家争夺书架上的一席之地。

The rest of A Room of One’s Own takes place in the speaker’s study, the room of her own, where she pulls books off the shelf more or less in chronological order. For the earliest periods in literary history, she looks on the shelf where the women writers ought to be and there aren’t any; then later, yes, there are women writers, quite a few novelists. More recently yet, women writers get a little more scope for their activity, yet still struggle for shelf space with objectionable male writers.

这就是《一间自己的房间》的整体结构，我在此提供情节概要，希望你们能亲自阅读。这种游走于小说、文学评论和社会批判之间的写作手法并非没有先例。奥斯卡·王尔德的《WH先生的画像》就是一个典型的例子。这是一部带有思辨色彩的中篇小说，以莎士比亚十四行诗为主题，但它本身也是一部关于文学的文学作品。正如你们所能想象的，伍尔夫对夏洛蒂·勃朗特的评价在后来的女性主义批评中引发了争议。女性主义批评家认为弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的观点存在诸多误区或需要补充，而这只是其中之一。总的来说，女性主义批评家认为夏洛蒂·勃朗特，或者任何其他作家，都有权持有自己的观点；她们从伍尔夫对勃朗特的反应中看出，她不假思索地接受了现代主义——以及男性主导的——关于自主统一的美学（正如我们所见，这种美学在新批评中仍然未受质疑）。我们将进一步探讨弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的雌雄同体标准，该标准部分要求避免以任何一种性别的方式思考。与此同时，大多数女性主义批评认为，雌雄同体并非女性散文应追求的理想，无论它如何体现优雅、都市风范和精雕细琢的艺术，因此，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫批评夏洛蒂·勃朗特，实际上是表明了她对唯美主义的忠诚，并因此受到批评。

That’s the structure of A Room of One’s Own overall, which I give you as a plot summary in hopes that you’ll read it for yourselves. There were precedents for the kind of writing that hovers between fiction, literary commentary, and social criticism. Oscar Wilde’s Portrait of Mr. W. H. offers one precedent in particular. That’s a speculative, novella-like reflection on Shakespeare’s sonnets, but it, too, is literature that’s about literature. As you can imagine, what Woolf says about Charlotte Brontë has been controversial in subsequent feminist criticism. There are a number of ways in which feminist critics feel that Virginia Woolf is misguided or needs to be supplemented, and this is one of them. By and large, feminist critics feel that Charlotte Brontë, or any other writer, has the right to be tendentious; and they see in Woolf’s reaction to Brontë her unthinking acceptance of the modernist—and male-driven—aesthetic of autonomous unity (still unquestioned, as we’ve seen, in the New Criticism). We’ll have more to say about Virginia Woolf’s criterion of androgyny, which in part calls for the avoidance of thinking like either sex. Most feminist criticism in the meantime has argued that androgyny isn’t the ideal toward which women’s prose ought to be aspiring, however much it may realize the ideal of elegance, urbanity, and highly wrought polish, and takes Virginia Woolf to task therefore for having signaled her allegiance with aestheticism in criticizing Charlotte Brontë.

尽管基于这些理由批评《一间自己的房间》当然是可能的，但与此同时，我们也应该认识到弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的论点是如何完全预示了后来的女性主义批评史的。我只想指出其中的几个方面。正如伊莱恩·肖瓦尔特所指出的，现代女性主义批评的第一阶段主要关注男性在小说中对女性的描写。玛丽·埃尔曼的《思考女性》（1968）和凯特·米利特的《性政治》（1970）这两本书都聚焦于那些性别歧视的男性小说家，认为他们贬低女性的行为需要被记录下来。在肖瓦尔特的论述中，这种批评被她更倾向的“女性主义批评”或“女性主义批评家”所取代。女性主义批评与其说是关注男性在小说中对女性的刻画，不如说是关注女性作为作家在文学史上的地位，以及作为人物——无论她们是出现在男性小说还是女性小说中，或者仅仅是作为独立个体——在小说史上的地位。女性主义批评在20世纪60年代末和70年代初将女性主义批评的重点从男性压迫的历史转向对女性传统的历史、重构和拓展。

Although it is certainly possible to criticize A Room of One’s Own on such grounds, one should recognize at the same time how completely Virginia Woolf’s arguments anticipate the subsequent history of feminist criticism. I just want to point out a few of the ways in which they do. As Elaine Showalter points out, the first phase of modern feminist criticism primarily paid attention to men’s treatment of women in fiction. Mary Ellmann’s Thinking about Women (1968) and Kate Millett’s Sexual Politics (1970) are both books that focused on sexist male novelists whose demeaning treatment of women needed to be recorded. This criticism was superseded in Showalter’s account by what she prefers, “gynocriticism” or “the gynocritics.” Gynocriticism is not so much concerned with men’s treatment of women in fiction as with the place of women as writers in literary history and as characters—regardless of whether they are characters in men’s or women’s novels or treated simply in their own right—in the history of fiction. Gynocriticism turns the emphasis of feminist criticism in the late 1960s and early 1970s from the history of oppression by men to the history, reconstruction, and amplification of what is known about a female tradition.

现代女性主义批评中体现的这种兴趣演变在伍尔夫的作品中已然充分显现。她也想探讨女性作家的可能性，探讨女性作家如何能够并且必须感受到她们并不孤单。然而，与此同时，她以辛辣的讽刺来强调女性视角，讽刺男性贬低女性、将她们束缚在男性的位置上——就像她假装在大英图书馆发现的那些撰写女性题材书籍的男性一样。所有这些都与肖瓦尔特所认为的以埃尔曼和米勒为代表的现代女性主义批评的第一阶段相吻合。伍尔夫的论述方式包容性体现在她能够将两种现代传统联系起来，并非像肖瓦尔特所呈现的那样按时间顺序排列，而是将其视为一种同时性，在这种同时性中，对男性边缘化女性的强调和对女性意识及传统的强调可以同时提出，并且在某种程度上可以被视为彼此的衍生。

This succession of interests reflected in modern feminist criticism is already fully present in Woolf. She, too, wants to talk about the possibilities for women writers, about how women writers can and must feel that they’re not alone. At the same time, however, she frames this emphasis on the woman’s perspective with her grim satire on men demeaning women and keeping them in their place—men like the ones who wrote books about women, as she pretends to have discovered in the British Library. All of this corresponds to that first phase of modern feminist criticism that Showalter identifies with Ellmann and Millett. You can see the capaciousness of Woolf’s approach in her ability to bridge both sorts of modern tradition, not chronologically as Showalter presents them but as a kind of simultaneity in which the emphasis on men’s marginalization of women and the emphasis on women’s consciousness and traditions can be set forth at the same time and seen in certain ways as giving rise to each other.

此外，正如在谈到《简·爱》时一样，这次是以一种间接的方式提及这部小说，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫预见了桑德拉·吉尔伯特和苏珊·古巴尔合著的引人入胜的著作《阁楼上的疯女人》。《简·爱》中阁楼里的疯女人伯莎，在吉尔伯特和古巴尔的著作之后，作为“疯女人”主题的一部分，被纳入了女性主义批评的范畴：由于女性无法公开地以作家或其他艺术家的身份进行创作，她们被迫将自己的创造力引导到颠覆性的、狡猾的，或许甚至是心理上自我毁灭的形式中，正如夏洛特·珀金斯·吉尔曼的《黄色壁纸》所展现的那样。你会发现伍尔夫已经在作品中触及了这一“疯女人”主题（600）：

Also as it happens in reference to Jane Eyre, this time in oblique reference to that novel, there is Virginia Woolf’s anticipation of the fascinating book by Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar called The Madwoman in the Attic. Bertha, the madwoman in the attic of Jane Eyre, is made available for feminist criticism after Gilbert and Gubar as its madwoman thesis: the idea that because women could not openly express themselves creatively as writers or as artists in other media, they were forced to channel their creativity into subversive, devious, and perhaps psychologically self-destructive forms, as exemplified in Charlotte Perkins Gilman’s The Yellow Wallpaper. You find Woolf already touching on this madwoman theme (600):

然而，当人们读到女巫被浸入水中、女人被魔鬼附身、女巫售卖草药的故事时，[她当然还补充道]甚至读到一位非常了不起的男人，他的母亲……
When, however, one reads of a witch being ducked, of a woman possessed by devils, of a wise woman selling herbs, [and then of course she adds] and even of a very remarkable man who had a mother …

换言之，在这种情况下，人们强烈怀疑存在着一个创造力受到压制，并不幸被引导至非社会或反社会方向的人。伍尔夫虚构的“莎士比亚的妹妹”被耻辱地埋葬在十字路口，便是她这一典型例证。肖瓦尔特的女性主义批判视角要求学者们熟悉女性史以及女性写作史，同样也必须承认诸如巫术、疯狂和草药学等形式的压迫。

In such cases, in other words, one strongly suspects that there is a person whose creativity has been oppressed and unfortunately channeled in unsocial or antisocial directions. Woolf’s invention, “Shakespeare’s sister,” buried ignominiously at a crossroads, is her full-dress case in point. Showalter’s gynocritical perspective, which expects scholars to become familiar with the history of women as well as the history of women’s writing, must likewise entail the recognition of such forms of repression as witchcraft, madness, and herbalism.

伍尔夫当时也十分关注女性批评的本质任务：强调传统的重要性，指出女性作家面临的一大困境和缺陷在于，尽管涌现出一些伟大的作家——那些总是被提及的名字，比如简·奥斯汀、勃朗特姐妹、乔治·艾略特——但却缺乏一个持续发展、彼此契合的写作传统。伍尔夫谈到“男人的句子”（606），谈到连自己的语言都没有，更遑论拥有一个属于自己的空间。“或许她提笔写作时首先会发现，根本没有现成的句子可供她使用。”所有小说散文的范式都带有男性色彩，因为写作的氛围——这一点我们稍后会谈到——甚至写作本身，用笔在纸上涂鸦，都带有男性特有的光环。

Also very much on the mind of Woolf already is the essential task of gynocriticism: to insist that one needs a tradition, that one of the great difficulties and shortcomings facing the woman writer is that, yes, there are a few greats—the ones who are always named, Austen, the Brontës, George Eliot—but there is no sense of an ongoing, developing tradition within which one could write companionably. Woolf talks about “the man’s sentence” (606), the difficulty of not having even a language of one’s own, let alone a room. “Perhaps the first thing she would find, setting pen to paper, was that there was no common sentence ready for her use.” All the models of novelistic prose are gendered male, because the atmosphere of writing—and this is a point that we’ll be getting to soon—the very fact of writing, poking a pen about, has a male aura attached to it:

这是一句男人的句子（她刚刚引用了一句长句）；从中我们可以看到约翰逊、吉本等人的影子。这句话不适合女人使用。夏洛蒂·勃朗特，尽管拥有卓越的散文天赋，却也因这句笨拙的句子而失手。乔治·艾略特用这句形容乞丐的句子犯下了滔天罪行。简·奥斯汀看着它，嘲笑了一番，然后构思出一个自然流畅、优美动人的句子，并始终坚持使用。因此，尽管她的写作天赋不如夏洛蒂·勃朗特，却表达得更加深刻。（606）
That is a man’s sentence [she has just quoted a long sentence]; behind it one can see Johnson, Gibbon and the rest. It was a sentence that was unsuited for a woman’s use. Charlotte Brontë, with all her splendid gift for prose, stumbled and fell with that clumsy weapon in her hands. George Eliot committed atrocities with it that beggar description. Jane Austen looked at it and laughed at it and devised a perfectly natural, shapely sentence proper for her own use and never departed from it. Thus, with less genius for writing than Charlotte Brontë, she got infinitely more said. (606)

顺便说一句，这种说法值得商榷。当然，我们完全可以理解简·奥斯汀的散文风格源于塞缪尔·约翰逊，或许还有塞缪尔·理查森。不过，伍尔夫的观点是，奥斯汀能够摆脱那种想表达某些东西却发现找不到合适的语言来表达的困境。她想以女性的身份写作，表达女性想表达的东西，但她所能用的却只有男性的语言。这就是伍尔夫的观点，当然，它有着诸多深远的影响。

By the way, this claim is disputable. Surely it’s possible to understand Jane Austen’s prose style as emerging from that of Samuel Johnson and perhaps Samuel Richardson. Still, Woolf’s point is that Austen was able to shake herself free from the problem of wanting to say something but finding that one doesn’t have one’s own language for saying it. One wants to write as a woman, to say the things that a woman wants to say, but all one has for the purpose is a man’s sentence. That’s Woolf’s point, and of course it has many and long ramifications.

我一直暂且不谈伍尔夫关于“女性”和“男性”写作的言论所受到的批评——这些批评自1980年以来就一直受到女性主义批评和性别理论的挑战。但与此同时，我提到的这些影响却被我们称之为“法国女性主义”的、理论上非常精深的女性主义批评分支所强化，这很有意思。你们当中有些人可能了解露西·伊里加雷和海伦·西苏的作品。这类作家坚持认为，存在一种女性语言。女性写作时不仅用头脑和性器官，而是用整个身体。她们写的不是精心构建的周期性句子，而是线性的、并列的、印象式的、离题的、即兴的句子：没有自我意识的句子——因为在这种意义上，缺乏结构或多或少等同于没有自我意识。我们稍后会在肖瓦尔特的论述中再谈到这一点，但与此同时，法国女权主义愿意确立并推广一种关于女性写作的理念，以及——隐含在这种理念背后——关于女性本质的理念，而这种理念却遇到了另一种困境。将女性与某种特定类型的句式联系起来，同时也意味着将她们排除在其他句式之外。

I’m holding at bay the criticism of Woolf’s remarks about “women’s” and “men’s” writing that has been leveled at them by feminist criticism and gender theory roughly since 1980, but in the meantime the ramifications I mentioned are interestingly reinforced by the theoretically very sophisticated wing of feminist criticism that we call “French feminism.” Some of you may know the work of Luce Irigaray and Hélène Cixous. Writers of this kind insist that there is such a thing as women’s language. Women write not just with their heads and their phalluses but with their whole bodies. They don’t write carefully constructed periodic sentences, but linear, paratactic, impressionist, digressive, ad hoc sentences: sentences without ego—as lack of structure on this account more or less corresponds to being without ego. We’ll come back to this in Showalter, but in the meantime French feminism was willing to settle upon and promote an idea of women’s writing and—implicit behind this idea—an idea of what a woman is that runs into a different kind of trouble. The identification of women with a certain kind of sentence is at the same time their banishment from other kinds.

为什么女性就不能写出好的周期句呢？毕竟，简·奥斯汀写的不就是这种句式吗？如果女性真的可以自由地做自己想做的事，为什么她们就不能写出不带性别色彩的句子呢？换句话说，为什么女性的写作就必须是女性的写作呢？

Why can’t a woman write a good periodic sentence? After all, that’s the kind of sentence that Jane Austen did, in fact, write. Why can’t a woman, if she is really free to be whatever she wants to be, write a sentence that isn’t necessarily of this gendered sort that the French call écriture feminine? Why does women’s writing, in other words, have to be women’s writing?

可以说，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在提出她那或许同样危险的“雌雄同体”概念时，预示了对法国女权主义的一种潜在批判。这种思维既具有男性特质又具有女性特质，其写作方式恰恰是在不再思考自身性别身份的那一刻才得以充分表达自我——这种高度发达的思维不再书写男性的句子，也不再书写女性的句子。尽管有人可能会认为伍尔夫的“雌雄同体”概念预先否定了法国女权主义，并暗示在精神或实践层面，并不需要存在某种本质实体来被认定为“女性”，但与此同时，我们也应该意识到弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫对性别的明确身份抱有矛盾的态度。伍尔夫对中性写作的理想——一种不受束缚的表达——与她坚持认为简·奥斯汀之所以能充分表达自我，是因为她摆脱了男性话语的束缚，以自己的方式写作，这之间存在着一种可以原谅的矛盾，这是不同修辞场合造成的。我们无法确定伍尔夫是否认为存在某种可以被定义为“女性写作”的东西，或者更确切地说，是否存在某种可以被定义为“女性”的东西。

You could say it is a possible critique of French feminism that Virginia Woolf anticipates when she embarks on her perhaps equally perilous idea of androgyny. The kind of mind that is both male and female and writes in a way that’s fully self-expressive precisely in the moment when one no longer thinks of being male or female—this advanced mind no longer writes a man’s sentence or a woman’s sentence. Although it could be argued that Woolf’s concept of “androgyny” rejects French feminism in advance, and suggests also that there need not exist, in spirit or practice, some essential entity to be identified as “woman,” at the same time we should recognize an ambivalence on Virginia Woolf’s part about the distinct identity of the sexes. There is a forgivable inconsistency, the effect of differing rhetorical occasions, between her ideal of androgynous writing as untethered expression and her insistence that Jane Austen expressed herself fully because she shrugged off the tyranny of the man’s sentence and wrote like herself. We can’t know for sure whether Woolf thinks there is something identifiable as “women’s writing” or whether for that matter there is something identifiable as woman.

肖瓦尔特探讨了女性小说发展史上的三个阶段。首先是“女性化”阶段，在这个阶段，女性试图像男性一样写作（或者至少表面上如此），尽可能地迎合男性价值观——或许是将一种“天使般的”文化仁慈融入到原本冷漠无情的男性视角中，尽管这些视角本质上与男性视角并无二致。这些女性作家经常使用男性笔名，例如柯勒·贝尔、阿克顿·贝尔、埃利斯·贝尔、乔治·艾略特等等，她们很少就女性在社会中的地位展开激烈的辩论。肖瓦尔特接着指出，这一阶段被小说史上的“女权主义”时期所取代，在这个时期，像伊丽莎白·盖斯凯尔晚期作品这样的小说开始带有强烈的倾向性，女性的地位和角色成为小说的主题。这些分类无疑是模糊的：夏洛蒂·勃朗特属于肖瓦尔特所谓的“小说史上的女性阶段”，但伍尔夫早已在勃朗特身上发现了某种原始的女性主义，这种女性主义破坏了《简·爱》的质感。肖瓦​​尔特也对小说中的倾向性感到担忧，她的历史观倾向于用“女性小说”取代女性主义小说。“女性小说”理所当然地认为女性视角是真实且合法的，并从这一视角出发进行写作，摒弃了早期小说中存在的愤怒或对抗意识等因素。

Showalter discusses three phases in the history of the women’s novel. First there is the “feminine,” the phase in which women try to write as though they were men (or at least appear to do so), by deferring to male values as much as possible—perhaps introducing a kind of “angel in the house” cultural benevolence into perspectives of men that would otherwise be cold and unfeeling but are nonetheless the same perspectives. These women writers frequently assumed male pen names such as Currer Bell, Acton Bell, Ellis Bell, George Eliot, and so on and rarely entered polemically into controversy about the place of women in society. Showalter then says this is a phase supplanted by a “feminist” moment in the history of the novel in which novels like the late work of Elizabeth Gaskell, for example, become tendentious, and the place and role of women become the dominant theme. The categories are no doubt porous: Charlotte Brontë belongs to what Showalter is calling “the feminine phase” in the history of the novel, but Woolf had already found in Brontë a proto-feminism that damages the texture of Jane Eyre. Showalter, too, is nervous about tendentiousness in fiction, and her history favors the supplanting of the feminist novel by the “female” novel, which simply takes for granted the authenticity and legitimacy of the woman’s point of view and writes from that point of view, having shaken off the elements of anger or adversary consciousness in earlier novels.

这部小说史与非裔美国文学批评家对小说历史的梳理有部分相似之处，与肖瓦尔特所记录的近期女性主义批评的各个阶段颇为相似，尽管其中只有两个阶段：首先是她所谓的“女性主义阶段”，主要关注男性在小说中对女性的刻画；其次是“女性主义批评阶段”，即女性文学传统的拓展。肖瓦尔特指出，当时最重要的女性主义学术成果，尤其是20世纪70年代的成果，致力于发掘和拓展女性写作的经典，特别是非虚构类作品。在19世纪的大部分时间里，小说仍被视为一种轻浮低级的文体，新闻界勉强允许女性以小说的形式表达她们的写作欲望，但与此同时，人们却断言她​​们不应该创作诗歌和戏剧。肖瓦尔特认为，经典作品的扩展和深化是一种至关重要的反驳。正如她所说，我们需要追溯女性写作的历程，跨越数十年，而不是仅仅关注一部部经典作品，从而构建一个与男性传统相媲美的传统，供创作者思考、借鉴和汲取养分。因此，无论是肖瓦尔特的小说史，还是她所著的现代女性主义批评史——或者更准确地说，是现代女性主义批评史——都止步于一个问题：女性视角的真实性究竟如何？

This history of the novel, which finds partial parallels in historical outlines of the novel offered by African American literary critics, is quite similar to the phases of recent feminist criticism as Showalter chronicles them, though there are only two of these: first the feminist, as she calls it, when the treatment of women by men in fiction is the main focus, and then the gynocritical, which is the development for women of a literary tradition. Showalter points out that much of the most important work of then-recent feminist scholarship, the work of the 1970s, is devoted to the unearthing of and expanding the canon of women’s writing, especially that which is not fiction. There had been a time—much of the nineteenth century—when the novel, still viewed as a frivolous and inferior mode, was conceded to women journalistically as an outlet for their compulsion to write, a concession accompanied by the sovereign assertion that they shouldn’t, on the other hand, write poetry and plays. The expansion and deepening of the canon Showalter sees as a crucial counterassertion. As she puts it, we need to trace women’s writing from decade to decade and not from great book to great book, creating a tradition comparable to the male tradition that one can think about, think within, and draw on as a creative writer oneself. So both Showalter’s history of the novel and her history of modern feminist criticism—or modern gynocriticism, one had better say—end at a point when it is still a question of authenticating the woman’s perspective.

但这引出了一个我之前已经提及的问题，这个问题始终萦绕在我们对这类问题的思考之中。当我们从批评和理论的角度探讨其他身份认同视角时，我们会反复遇到这个问题。如果我说女性的写作，或者说女性的写作总体上属于某种类型，如果我以某种我认为可以辨识的方式去定义一位女性——比如直觉敏锐、想象力丰富、印象派、敏感、不合逻辑、反理性、拒绝我们通常与男性写作联系在一起的那种周期性句式——如果我像法国女权主义者那样，把这种身份挪用给女性，这难道不就是在颂扬《一间自己的房间》第二章中男性对女性的居高临下的态度吗？如果男性把理性、科学、逻辑等等都据为己有，声称头脑高于情感，那么除了宣称情感高于头脑之外，他们又取得了什么成就呢？父权制的范式依然完好无损。这就是理论问题所在。它呼应了朱迪斯·巴特勒式的人们在理论上乐于宣扬的观点：根本不存在“女人”这种东西。如果我们努力追求一个美好的愿景：女性终有一天能够自由地成为她想成为的任何人（当然，也包括成为贤妻良母），那么或许对她来说，最好的选择就是什么都不是，除了她自己塑造的自己。艾米莉·狄金森曾说：“我什么都不是。你又是谁呢？”

But this raises a question I’ve already touched on that has to haunt thinking of this kind. We’ll encounter it again and again as we move through other identity perspectives in criticism and theory. If I say that a woman’s writing or women’s writing in general is of a certain sort, if I identify a woman in a way that I take somehow to be recognizable—as intuitive, imaginative, impressionistic, sensitive, illogical, opposed to reason, a refuser of that periodic sentence that we associate with men’s writing—if I appropriate this identity for women like the French feminists, isn’t that simply to make a celebration out of men’s condescending attitudes toward women in the second chapter of A Room of One’s Own? If men keep for themselves reason, science, logic, and all the rest of it, saying the head is higher than the heart, has anything been accomplished except to claim that on the contrary the heart is higher than the head? The paradigms of patriarchy remain intact. This is where the theoretical problem arises. It calls for what people who work in the mode of Judith Butler are quite willing to say in theory: there is no such thing as a woman. If we work toward the hope that a woman will someday be free to be whatever she wants to be (including, of course, an angel in the house), then it is perhaps best for her to be nothing at all except what she makes of herself. I’m nobody, said Emily Dickinson. Who are you?

当然，这步棋非常棘手，有时甚至会在女权主义思想中造成分裂。现实生活中，女性的确存在。女性受到法律的压迫，也受到那些与法律本质相同的男性的压迫。世界各地都需要警惕地保护女性的权利和生命。认为“女性”这种概念根本不存在的理论在现实生活中是站不住脚的。然而与此同时，身份政治论战中常被称作“本质主义”的那些含义——即把“女性”定义为某种特定事物（通常与男性一直以来对女性的认知极其相似）——仍然不利于我们更深入地理解性别及其可能性，即便是在实践层面。当我开始讲授这些课程时，我就对“实践不过是应用理论”这种经常主导此类课程的假设表示保留意见。我们稍后会谈到斯坦利·菲什，他曾被拍到穿着一件T恤，上面写着“实践中行得通，但理论上行得通吗？”身份政治的困境表明，这不仅仅是一个玩笑。

Now, of course, this is a very tricky move, one that unhappily proves divisive at times in feminist thought. In real life, there certainly are women. Women are oppressed by laws and by the men who are for the most part the same as the laws. The rights and the very lives of women need to be protected with vigilance around the world. The theoretical idea that there’s no such thing as a woman cannot for a moment be sustained in life. Yet at the same time, the implications of what the polemics of identity politics are always calling “essentialism,” the implications of saying “woman” is one particular thing (often something dangerously similar to what men have always thought her to be), remain detrimental to a more sensitive understanding, even at the practical level, of gender and its possibilities. When I began these lectures, I expressed reservations about the supposition, frequently governing courses like this one, that practice is nothing but applied theory. Stanley Fish, whom we’ll be discussing soon, was once seen wearing a T-shirt that said “It works in practice, but does it work in theory?” The dilemma of identity politics shows why that isn’t just a joke.

凭直觉、感性、印象派固然很好，但关于这一点，我想说两点。首先，男人如果想这样做，难道不应该如此吗？其次，为什么女人就一定要这样呢？很明显，在这两种情况下，都存在着远超常人的例外情况，而这些例外恰恰证明了规则。

It’s all very well to be intuitive and emotional and impressionistic, but one wants to say two things about that. In the first place, a guy gets to be that, too, if he wants to be, no? In the second place, why does a woman have to be that? It’s perfectly clear in both cases that there are exceptions that go vastly beyond the exception that proves the rule.

正如我认为肖瓦尔特的文章所揭示的那样，这是1980年前后女权主义批评界尚未达成共识的难题。请注意肖瓦尔特在文章结尾对马克思主义和结构主义的敌意，理由是它们都自诩为“科学”。当然，我也曾在讲台上对这些理论以及许多其他理论提出过同样的批评。但现在的问题在于，男性范式将这些方法性别化为男性化的，而女权主义却接受了这种性别化。我们不想与马克思主义和结构主义有任何瓜葛，因为它们就像弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫笔下的教堂执事，披着一层薄薄的外衣，再次抬头告诫我们不要踏入女性禁区。我们对此嗤之以鼻。肖瓦尔特在文章结尾（参见1385-1386页）实际上指出，我们需要的是一种避免科学伪装的批评；这种批评形式关注文本的现实和文本传统，但它——呃，好吧，还能怎么说呢？——不会纠结于理论问题。

As I think Showalter’s essay illustrates, this is a bind that feminist criticism around 1980 had not found a consensus solution for. Notice Showalter’s animus, at the end of her essay, toward Marxism and structuralism on the grounds that both of them present themselves as “sciences.” Of course, I’ve made the same complaint about those and many other theories from my lectern. But now the trouble is that male paradigms have gendered these approaches male and that feminism accepts this gendering. We want nothing to do with Marxism and structuralism because they are Virginia Woolf’s beadle in thin disguise, raising his ugly head again and telling us not to walk on the grass which is off-limits to women. None of that, thank you. Showalter says in effect at the end of her essay (cf. 1385–1386) that what’s needed is a criticism that avoids scientific pretension; a form of criticism that engages with the reality of texts and the textual tradition but that doesn’t—er, well, but how else to put it?—trouble its pretty head with theoretical matters.

这个结论似乎让女性主义批评处于一种令人愉悦的被殖民状态，只要不理性，它就可以随心所欲。实际上，这并非坏事，我倾向于同意，因为我自己也对理性的雄性激素持怀疑态度。但需要注意的是，这无疑会限制女性主义批评——这些限制是无害的还是束缚性的，或许值得商榷，但无论如何，它们都是限制。亨利·路易斯·盖茨（Henry Louis Gates）在一定程度上受到巴赫金的影响，他将以一种非常有趣的方式展现，一旦边缘化的少数群体批评摆脱了主流批评的前提和术语，它们就能获得怎样的发展空间。我希望你们在阅读盖茨的文章时，特别牢记这一建议。我们将在讨论性别理论，特别是朱迪斯·巴特勒的性别理论时，再回到女性主义批评，回到1980年以来女性主义批评的一个方面。

This conclusion would seem to leave feminist criticism in the pleasantly colonized position of doing anything it likes as long as it’s not rational. Not a bad thing, actually, I’m inclined to agree, being rather skeptical about the testosterone of reason myself, but as a caveat it would certainly impose limits on feminist criticism—whether harmless limits or a straightjacket may be open to question, but limits nonetheless. Henry Louis Gates, partly through the influence of Bakhtin, will have a very interesting way of showing what’s available for a marginalized minority criticism once it avoids the premises and terms of mainstream criticism. I want you to read Gates’s essay with that suggestion particularly in mind. We’ll return to feminist criticism, to one aspect of feminist criticism since 1980, when we discuss gender theory, especially that of Judith Butler.

 

 

第21章

CHAPTER 21

非裔美国人批评
African American Criticism

阅读材料：

Readings:

盖茨，亨利·路易斯，小。“写作、‘种族’及其带来的影响。”载于《批评传统》，第 1891-1902 页。

Gates, Henry Louis, Jr.. “Writing, ‘Race,’ and the Difference It Makes.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1891–1902.

莫里森，托尼。“在黑暗中玩耍。”载于《批评传统》，第 1791-1800 页。

Morrison, Toni. “Playing in the Dark.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1791–1800.

非裔美国文学传统源远流长，底蕴深厚。正如亨利·路易斯·盖茨所言，这一传统中首位重要的诗人菲利斯·惠特利生活于美国殖民时期。奴隶叙事文学的兴盛始于十八世纪，并延续至十九世纪。二十世纪，尤其是在哈莱姆文艺复兴时期，以及整个世纪以来不断积累的文学作品，在各个体裁中都涌现出了大量杰出的创作。这一绵延不绝的传统与同样丰富但起步较晚的非裔美国文学理论与批评传统形成了鲜明的对比。

The African American literary tradition is rich and long-standing. As Henry Louis Gates tells you, the first important poet in the tradition, Phillis Wheatley, lived during the American colonial period. The flourishing of the slave narrative form begins in the eighteenth century and continues into the nineteenth. In the twentieth century, most conspicuously in the Harlem Renaissance but throughout the century in gathering volume, there has been remarkable work done in all genres. This extended tradition contrasts in duration with the equally rich but also very recent tradition of African American literary theory and criticism.

诚然，从杜波依斯和休斯时代起，批评和美学领域就涌现出不少贡献，但直到盖茨那一代，理论方面才真正有所建树。或许，最初人们回避理论，是因为黑人知识分子内部存在着明显的紧张关系。黑人批评和黑人女性主义批评从一开始就意识到，作为不同的思想流派，它们的诉求并不完全相同。像芭芭拉·克里斯蒂安、芭芭拉·史密斯、黑兹尔·卡比和贝尔·胡克斯这样的批评家强烈批判非裔美国男性形象，而男性批评家们也发现，他们只关注种族问题而忽略性别问题，其效果会受到这些观点的制约。然而，自20世纪80年代以来，双方的分歧已基本得到缓解，非裔美国文学理论也基本摆脱了这些顾虑的束缚，得以向前发展。

Certainly there were contributions in criticism and aesthetics from the time of Du Bois and Hughes forward, but very little in the way of theory emerged until the generation of Gates himself. Theory was perhaps avoided at first because of a marked tension within the black intelligentsia. Black criticism and black feminist criticism from the beginning saw that as schools of thought they didn’t have quite the same agenda. Critics like Barbara Christian, Barbara Smith, Hazel Carby, and bell hooks were strongly critical of the African American male persona, and male critics for their part found that their attention to race without attention to gender was somewhat limited in effectiveness by these views. For the most part, since the 1980s a sufficient détente has been achieved, however, and African American literary theory moves forward largely unfettered by these concerns.

在我看来，亨利·路易斯·盖茨在非裔美国人批评领域扮演的角色堪称典范。尽管你读到的那篇文章中有些措辞相当尖锐，这些尖锐之处我将在后文详述，它们或许暗示着盖茨的思想存在某种程度的过度扩张。这正是我最后要权衡的问题，毫无疑问，我会为此感到恼火，并反复斟酌正反两方的观点。总的来说，他展现出的形象并非尖锐刻薄。他不仅是一位重要的调解者和富有洞察力的声音，更是一位杰出的管理者和项目构建者。他离开耶鲁大学前往哈佛大学时，成功招募了安东尼·阿皮亚、康奈尔·韦斯特等人，组建了一个庞大的系。其他人大多因为与当时的校长不和而离开了哈佛，但盖茨本身就是一个庞大的学术帝国，所以这或许无关紧要。你们在本次讲座中读到的，是他早期的一些作品，这些作品与哈丽雅特·威尔逊的小说的重新发现一起，为他奠定了声誉。他声称这部小说是一部虚构的奴隶叙事作品，是对我们了解十九世纪非裔美国文学的重要贡献，这进一步巩固了他的声誉。

The role of Henry Louis Gates in African American criticism is, it seems to me, exemplary, although there are some rather harsh moments in the essay you’ve read, moments that I will to take up in the long run, that may or may not suggest an element of overreach in Gates’s thinking. That’s the question I’ll weigh in conclusion and no doubt maddeningly take both sides about. Harshness is not at all the image that he has projected in general. Not only is he an important mediatory and nuanced voice, he is a superb administrator and program builder. When he left Yale for Harvard, he was able to recruit Anthony Appiah, Cornel West, and others to form a megadepartment. The others have, for the most part, left Harvard owing to friction with the university president at the time, but Gates is an empire unto himself, so perhaps it scarcely matters. Some of his earliest work is what you’ve been reading for this lecture, and it established his reputation together with the rediscovery of a novel by Harriet Wilson, bolstered by his claim that it was a novel, a fictitious slave narrative and an important contribution to our knowledge of nineteenth-century African American literature.

盖茨原本就是一位优秀的作家，但不知何故，他突然间成为了一位文风大师。他开始为《纽约客》撰稿，在他职业生涯的这一阶段，除了创作自传（讲述他在西弗吉尼亚州的成长经历）之外，盖茨还成为了公共领域中促进种族和种族派别间相互理解的代言人。他一直保持着温和的立场，从未被指责为出卖原则，尽管他与休斯顿·贝克多年来的辩论——正如您在文集中看到的——或许会让人产生相反的印象。在蒂娜·布朗担任主编期间，盖茨为《纽约客》撰写的文笔优雅而睿智的文章，与亚当·戈普尼克的巴黎来信一起，构成了该杂志当时最优秀的作品。

Gates was a perfectly good writer in the first place but somehow suddenly became a master stylist. He started writing for the New Yorker, and during this phase of his career, when among other things he produced an autobiography about growing up in West Virginia, Gates became a spokesperson in the public sphere for mutual understanding among races and racial factions. He has been a voice of moderation without incurring any imputation of selling out, although his debates with Houston Baker over the years, as reflected in the exchange you’ll find in your anthology, might suggest otherwise. Gates’s urbane and judicious contributions to the New Yorker during Tina Brown’s editorship were, together with Adam Gopnik’s letters from Paris, the best work in that incarnation of the magazine.

因此，对于盖茨而言，正如伊莱恩·肖沃尔特以及她之前的伍尔夫一样，我们可以看出，困扰身份范畴的概念性问题依然存在。身份虽然是那些渴望在文学和文化领域占有一席之地的人们的重要思考锚点，但它至少在理论上仍然会导致一些问题。其中有两个问题尤其困扰着身份问题。一个是“本质化”，我稍后会谈到；另一个问题可以称之为身份队列：我是一个来自巴勒斯坦的工人阶级黑人女同性恋女权主义者。这给了我很多身份选择，但问题在于我必须弄清楚哪个身份优先。哪个身份具有潜在的决定性力量，能够激励和塑造我如何看待其他身份？一旦我选择了我的“原始身份”，其他身份就需要相应地被排在队列的后面。

For Gates, then, as for Elaine Showalter and for Woolf before her, you can see that the conceptual problems bedeviling the category of identity persist. Identity, despite being an important anchor for the thinking of people who feel the need for a place in the literary and cultural firmament, leads nevertheless at least potentially to certain problems in theory. Two problems in particular dog the issue of identity. One of them is “essentializing,” which I’ll take up in a moment; and there is also the problem of what might be called the identity queue: I am a working-class black lesbian feminist whose nation is Palestine. That gives me a lot of identity options to choose from, but the trouble is that I have to figure out which of them has priority. Which of those identities has the underlying determinate force that motivates and shapes the way I inhabit my other identities? Once I have chosen my ur-identity, the others need accordingly to be placed farther back in the queue.

关于这个问题我之后还会再谈，但与此同时，还有一个被广泛认可的问题，那就是本质化，正如其反对者在所有涉及文化史或身份认同的理论辩论中所称的那样。盖茨非常清楚地指出了将本质特征归于任何群体或种族的危险性（1893）：

I shall have more to say about this problem, but in the meantime there is the more widely acknowledged problem of essentializing, as its opponents call it in every theoretical debate that concerns cultural history or identity. Gates is very clear on the dangers of ascribing essential characteristics to any group or race (1893):

在“种族”一词的流行用法中定义的差异感，既被用来描述和体现语言、信仰体系、艺术传统、“基因库”以及各种所谓的“自然”属性（如节奏、运动能力、思维能力、高利贷和忠诚）方面的差异。
The sense of difference defined in popular usages of the term race has been used both to describe and inscribe differences of language, belief system, artistic tradition, “gene pool,” and all sorts of supposedly “natural” attributes such as rhythm, athletic ability, cerebration, usury, and fidelity.

对正面和负面特质进行刻板印象的划分对任何人都没有好处，因为被单独挑出来作为独特特征的，总是隐含着所缺乏的东西：例如，“思考”在这里是书呆子的代名词。

Stereotyping for positive and negative traits alike does nobody very much good, because what is lacking is always implied in what is singled out as a distinctive trait: for instance, “cerebration” here is code for nerdy.

在文章开头，盖茨认为现代种族意识史在两种极端之间摇摆不定：一方面是尴尬地避而不谈种族问题，另一方面则是直白的种族主义决定论及其伴随的刻板印象。与吉姆·克劳时期温文尔雅的评论家们对种族问题的巧妙回避形成鲜明对比的是，伊波利特·泰纳在19世纪末的著作——该书认为“种族”、“环境”和“文化时刻”是任何艺术或文化作品的关键决定因素——在盖茨看来，即便其中也包含刻板印象，也明显更胜一筹。盖茨欣慰地看到，至少种族问题终于开始被人们讨论，但与此同时，他自然而然地对那些可以追溯到泰纳乃至孟德斯鸠的种族主义思想感到反感。 （与许多人一样，我区分了种族主义和种族歧视。种族主义是指基于种族的刻板印象——盖茨在上面列出的“自然”属性中有所提及——而种族歧视则是指对某个种族的歧视。）正如盖茨所说，20世纪对种族问题的沉默对艺术规范的影响在于，它让我们相信我们都属于一个“伟大的传统”（用F.R.利维斯的话来说），所有有价值的艺术都属于这个传统，任何拒绝、忽视甚至与这些作品格格不入的作品都可以被搁置和忽视。正如约翰·吉洛里所指出的，正是这种对反映“普世”价值（但实际上是近年来占据主导地位的阶级和群体的价值观）的核心规范的坚持，使得知识分子和政治右翼在近几十年的“文化战争”中形成了统一的论战。

At the beginning of his essay, Gates sees the modern history of race consciousness vacillating between the embarrassed unwillingness to talk about race at all and straightforward racialist determinism with accompanying stereotypes. In contrast with the decorous erasure of race by genteel critics during Jim Crow, the late nineteenth-century work of Hippolyte Taine, arguing that “race,” “milieu,” and “cultural moment” are the key determining issues in any kind of artistic or cultural production, seems distinctly preferable to Gates, stereotypes and all. Gates is relieved that at least race is being talked about while at the same time he naturally winces away from the racialist thinking that can be traced back from Taine to Montesquieu. (With many others, I distinguish between racialism, which is stereotyping by race—alluded to in Gates’s list of “ ‘natural’ attributes” above—and racism, which is discrimination against a race.) As Gates says, the effect of twentieth-century reticence about race on artistic canons was the idea that we all belong to a “great tradition,” in the expression of F. R. Leavis, that all worthwhile art belongs within that tradition, and that anything that rejects or ignores or even stands apart from these works can be set aside and neglected. As you will find John Guillory pointing out, it is this commitment to a central canon reflecting “universal” values (but really the values of lately dominant classes and groups) that has united the polemics of the intellectual and political right during the “culture wars” of recent decades.

然而，本质化的问题依然存在。假设你赋予了别人眼中的刻板印象以正面价值。正如盖茨（Gates）在1901年所说，塞内加尔诗人利奥波德·桑戈尔（Léopold Senghor）在描绘黑人文化运动时就做到了这一点：

Yet the problem of essentializing doesn’t go away. Suppose you ascribe positive value to what another person might call a stereotype. This is what the Senegalese poet Léopold Senghor did in representing the Négritude movement, as Gates says (1901):

当我们试图通过颠倒种族概念来挪用它，将其作为某种本质的象征时，例如像黑人文化运动那样（桑戈尔曾论证非洲人“我们感受，故我们存在”），我们就放弃了太多东西，例如人类共同的基础。正如安东尼·阿皮亚所观察到的，这种做法是徒劳且危险的，因为它会进一步强化新的、怪诞的刻板印象。
When we attempt to appropriate, by inversion, race as a term for an essence, as did the Negritude movement, for example (“We feel, therefore we are,” as Senghor argued of the African), we yield too much, such as the basis of a shared humanity. Such gestures, as Anthony Appiah has observed, are futile and dangerous because of their further inscription of new and bizarre stereotypes.

所以你可以看出，在讨论种族问题时有很多需要避开的雷区，而盖茨对此非常敏感。

So you can see there are landmines to be avoided in negotiating the discourse of race, and Gates is extremely sensitive to them.

回到这个问题，还有身份队列的问题。盖茨本人可能偶尔也会遇到一些困难，因为在他职业生涯的早期阶段，他仍然身处非裔美国批评传统中与女权主义之间那种微妙的缓和关系之中。例如，在一段似乎涉及身份队列的、颇具争议的文字中，他写道（1894）：

There’s also the problem, to return to this, of the identity queue. Gates himself may have a little difficulty with this, at least from time to time, because in this early phase of his career he still works within the uneasy détente with feminism in the African American critical tradition. So, for example, in a somewhat problematic passage in which the identity queue seems to be at issue, he says (1894):

简而言之，性别差异中所蕴含的生物学意义，在谈论“种族差异”时并不成立，也永远不可能成立。然而，我们却常常不加思索地使用语言，将这种自然差异的概念强加于我们的表述之中。
The sanction of biology contained in sexual difference, simply put, does not and can never obtain when one is speaking of “racial difference.” Yet we carelessly use language in such a way as to will this sense of natural difference into our formulations.

他声称，从生物学角度来看，两性之间确实存在差异，但从生物学角度来看，所谓“原始种族”之间未必存在差异。按照这种观点，至少在女权主义传统中谈论男女时，人们必须直面实际差异的问题，这种差异仿佛是生物学固有的本质主义；而当人们在种族话语的传统中谈论黑人和白人时，实际上根本不是在谈论真正的差异。因此，在这两种话语中，更有说服力的话语是那些仅仅关注短暂差异的话语，这些差异被种族主义夸大并被赋予了决定性意义；而另一种话语则关注本质差异，无论人们如何看待这些差异，无论人们想要如何解读它们。

In biological terms, there’s definitely a difference between the sexes, he claims, but in biological terms there is not necessarily a difference among the so-called primary races. On this view, the result would be that at least when one speaks of women and men in the feminist tradition, one has to come face to face with the problem of actual difference, an essentialism as it were built in by biology; whereas when one speaks of black and white in the traditions of discourse about race, one isn’t actually talking about a genuine difference at all. Therefore the discourse with the stronger justification of the two is the one that concerns merely ephemeral differences, exaggerated and rendered determinate by racism, as opposed to the discourse that is about essential differences, whatever one thinks of them and whatever one wants to make of them.

当我们重新审视女性主义批评，特别是朱迪斯·巴特勒的性别理论时，我们会发现，关于性别的生物学基础——即两性之间的生物差异，这种差异将性本质化为繁衍手段——的整个问题都受到了深刻的质疑，这不仅是因为所谓的跨性别问题，还因为我们自身的性身份也是我们建构的。简而言之，关于两性差异的说法，归根结底，与关于种族差异的说法一样充满争议。

When we return to feminist criticism, particularly the gender theory of Judith Butler, we’ll see that the whole question of the biological basis of sex, the biological difference between the sexes that essentializes the role of sex as the means of reproduction, is profoundly in question, and not just because of so-called transgender issues but also because our very sexual identity is something that we construct. In short, the allegation of difference between the sexes is, after all, as controversial as the allegation of difference between races.

在这里，我们可以看出我请大家阅读的托妮·莫里森的文章的重要性。我们当然最熟悉的是她作为小说家的身份，但她同时也是一位杰出的评论家和一位颇具影响力的文学编辑。在我看来，她的思考为我们提供了一个摆脱我之前一直在讨论的困境——本质主义问题和身份认同困境——的迂回途径。莫里森借鉴了黑格尔《精神现象学》中关于主奴辩证法的论述，她想表达的是，身份认同与其说是“是什么”的问题，不如说是“不是什么”的问题。她说，关注“身为黑人”是一回事，而思考“身为黑人”是如何被铭刻在白人传统中的则是另一回事。在这种语境下，“身为黑人”意味着“不属于白人” ：黑人代表着缺失、否定或消极，而这正是定义“白人”的要素。对于白人身份的构建，对于美国文化传统的起源和发展而言，非裔美国人，尤其是奴隶，必须以缺席或缺失的形式存在。

Here we can see the importance of the essay that I’ve also asked you to read by Toni Morrison. We know her best, of course, as a novelist, but she’s also a distinguished critic as well as an influential literary editor. It seems to me that her reflections give us a sideways exit from the predicaments I have been talking about thus far, the problem of essentialism and the problem of the identity queue.
