What Morrison wants to say, borrowing from the discussion of the master-slave dialectic in Hegel’s Phenomenology of Mind, is that identity isn’t so much a question of what something is as a question of what it is not. It is one thing to be preoccupied with what it is to be black, she says, but another to consider the way being black is inscribed within the white tradition. To be black in that context is to be what white is not: black is the absence, the negation or negativity, that defines whiteness. For the construction of white identity, for the origins and development of the American cultural tradition, it has been necessary for there to be, as an absence or lack, the African American and, more particularly, the slave.

正如莫里森（1795年）所说：

As Morrison says (1795):

在对黑人身份和奴役的建构中，不仅蕴含着不自由，也包含着“非我”的投射。其结果为想象力提供了广阔的舞台。而为了缓解内心的恐惧并为外部剥削辩护，一种源于集体需求的非洲主义应运而生——一种由黑暗、他者性、警觉和欲望交织而成的虚构混合物——它独具美国特色。
In that construction of blackness and enslavement could be found not only the not-free but also the projection of the not-me. The result was a playground for the imagination. And what rose up out of collective needs to allay internal fears and rationalize external exploitation was an Africanism—a fabricated brew of darkness, otherness, alarm and desire—that is uniquely American.

她进一步指出，尽管她的研究对象是美国传统，但欧洲也存在一种非洲主义，其在殖民文学中也有对应的体现。为了佐证自己的观点，她举了一个引人注目的例子，这或许会让你想起福克纳笔下的托马斯·萨特本。历史人物威廉·邓巴并非出身于沼泽，而是来自苏格兰启蒙运动时期，他来到美国后，据历史学家伯纳德·贝林（莫里森引用）所述，邓巴成为了一名奴隶主，并彻底改变了自己的人生。莫里森将贝林的记载总结如下（1796年）：

She points out further that although her subject is the American tradition, there also exists a European Africanism with its counterpart in its own colonial literature. To reinforce her argument, she takes a remarkable example that must have reminded you at least in some ways of Faulkner’s Thomas Sutpen. The historical character William Dunbar rose up not from the swamp but from the Scottish Enlightenment and came to the United States, where according to Bernard Bailyn, the historian Morrison cites, Dunbar became a slaveowner and a completely transformed person. Morrison summarizes Bailyn’s information as follows (1796):

我认为邓巴这个人物简洁地描绘了美国人作为新一代白人男性是如何形成的。这种形成带来了一些诱人的结果，所有这些结果都在贝林对邓巴性格的总结中有所提及，并体现在邓巴“内心”的感受中——“一种力量，一种他以前从未体验过的自由感”。
I take [Dunbar] to be a succinct portrait of the process by which the American as new, white, and male was constituted. It is a formation that has several attractive consequences, all of which are referred to in Bailyn’s summation of Dunbar’s character and located in how Dunbar feels “within himself”—“a power, a sense of freedom he had not known before.”

这在某种程度上与古希腊文化中对奴隶制的合理化有相似之处。希腊人总是说，他们拥有奴隶是为了获得自由，这样统治阶级才能从维持生活的日常琐事中解放出来，从而进行更深入的思考。在希腊城邦的哲学家公民看来，自由就是摆脱劳作。

This is in some ways parallel to the rationalization of slavery in ancient Greek culture. The Greeks always said that the reason they had slaves was so they could be free, so the governing population could be liberated from performing the practical daily activities that sustain life in order to think deep thoughts. To be free according to the philosopher-citizen of the Greek polis is to be free from work.

但对邓巴而言，正如对萨特本而言一样，自由并非真正意义上的免于劳作。它是一种更广泛、更隐蔽的自由：免于承担责任，免于承认“他者”也是人——换句话说，免于爱丁堡和伦敦旧式文明所施加的种种束缚：在这片边疆、这片荒野、这片沼泽中，可以随心所欲地做任何你想做的事。而这种自由，却是建立在黑奴的血汗之上的。正如我所说，它在某些方面与古希腊奴隶制的合理化相似，但它既更加险恶，也如莫里森所设想的那样，更具辩证性。她提出了这样一个问题：如果没有一个被物化为“不自由”的黑人对立面，一个人是否能够成为白人？这个对立面就像弹簧盒里的弹簧，让白色的木偶能够从盒子里跳出来，正是因为被压在下面的东西。

But freedom for Dunbar, as for Sutpen, is not really a freedom from work. It’s a broader and more insidious idea of freedom: freedom from responsibility, freedom from the need to acknowledge otherness as human—freedom, in other words, from the sorts of constraint imposed by old world civility in Edinburgh and in London: freedom on this frontier, in this wilderness, in this swamp, simply to be whatever one wants to be. That freedom is achieved on the backs of black slaves. It is in some ways similar, as I say, to the rationalization for slavery in Greece, but it is both more sinister and, as Morrison conceives it, more dialectical. She puts the question of whether a person could become white without the availability of a black opposite, objectified as not-free, which functions like the spring in a jack-in-the-box, allowing the white puppet to leap out of the box because of what has been crushed beneath it.

这一论点为莫里森对《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》颇具争议的解读奠定了基础，而我认为这种解读极具说服力，远比因书中出现的“N字”而导致该书在许多学区被禁的争议更具说服力——尽管我们稍后会再次探讨究竟谁拥有使用“N字”这类词语的权利。莫里森认为，小说结尾处吉姆未能获得解放的悲剧本应是世上最简单的事情，因为汤姆和哈克只需指出河流的正确岔路口即可。然而，这种失败对于汤姆、哈克以及马克·吐温本人而言，却是他们作为白人唯一可用的自我认同的必要条件。我们知道，吐温一直苦于找不到合适的结尾。这部小说在他的书桌上搁置了很久，最终他才想出了这个令人沮丧的结局。托妮·莫里森认为这是唯一可行的结局，因为哈克和吉姆之间感伤的情感——这种情感如此强烈，以至于另一位评论家莱斯利·菲德勒在一篇题为《哈克，亲爱的，回到木筏上来吧》的文章中探讨了他们之间的同性恋情——掩盖了马克·吐温小说中基本的意识结构：吉姆必须保持奴隶的身份。如果吉姆获得了自由，那么白人就无法通过与“他者”的对立来定义自身的自由。

This thesis colors Morrison’s controversial reading of Huckleberry Finn, which I find strongly compelling, much more compelling indeed that the “N-word” controversy that got the book banned in many school districts—even though we’ll return ourselves to question who owns the right to speak words like the “N-word.” Morrison argues that the depressing failure to liberate Jim with which the novel concludes would have been the easiest thing in the world because all Tom and Huck had to do was point out the correct fork in the river, yet this failure is an absolute necessity for the only self-definition as a white person that’s available both to Tom and to Huck and by implication to Mark Twain himself. We know that Twain couldn’t figure out how to end the novel. It lay on his desk for a long time, then he finally came up with this dismal ending. Toni Morrison says it’s the only ending available because the sentimentality of the relationship between Huck and Jim, which is so strong that it caused another critic named Leslie Fiedler to talk about a homoerotic relation between them in an essay called “Come Back to the Raft Ag’in, Huck, Honey,” has obscured the basic structure of consciousness in Twain’s novel: it’s imperative that Jim remain a slave. If Jim is free, then there is no otherness over against which whiteness can define itself as free.

你可以看出，莫里森的论证与列维-斯特劳斯所说的“没有熟食就没有生食”的传统非常契合。这是一种基于否定的二元论证，我们通常将其与结构主义联系起来，但它同样也属于可以追溯到黑格尔的辩证法传统。这是理论中最有力、最具代表性的论证之一，我们将在朱迪斯·巴特勒的论述中再次看到它。巴特勒对性别差异非本质性的看法与我们引用的盖茨的观点有所不同。那么，让我们回到盖茨的论述上来。

You can see that Morrison’s argument belongs very much to the tradition in which Lévi-Strauss says there can be nothing raw without something cooked. It’s a binary argument grounded in negation that we have associated largely with structuralism, but it belongs equally to the dialectical tradition that goes back to Hegel. It is one of the strongest and most characteristic moves of theory, and we’ll see it again in Judith Butler, whose sense of the inessentiality of sexual difference differs from that of Gates in the passage we cited. Let’s return, then, to Gates.

然而，在回到身份建构（而非“所有权”）这一关键问题之前，我想先探讨一下盖茨等人对非裔美国文学和批评传统发展阶段的论述。首先，盖茨和伊莱恩·肖瓦尔特都认同批评传统基本上是一个两阶段或两部分发展的进程。肖瓦尔特曾说过，女性介入文学批评的第一波浪潮是她所谓的“女权主义”时期，凯特·米利特和其他一些作家开始探讨男性作品中女性遭受的贬低和不公待遇；第二波浪潮则是“女性主义批评”，即女性对文学传统的挪用，她们的档案研究使得女性文学经典不再仅仅是从一个伟大作家跳到另一个伟大作家，而是以十年为单位不断发展演变。盖茨认为非裔美国批评的发展也大致相同。他并没有按时间顺序排列这两个阶段，但如果你愿意，可以将它们与肖瓦尔特的论述对应起来。他说（1896 年）：“我引用这些……被过度使用的术语（他特别指的是‘他者’）的意思正是如此：黑人在文学中是如何出现的，以及黑人是如何参与创作他们自己创作的文学作品的。”

Before moving back, however, to the key issue of identity construction (as opposed, say, to “ownership”), I want to discuss the account given by Gates and others of the stages of development in the African American literary and critical traditions. First of all, the grasp of the critical tradition as basically a two-step or two-part progression is something that he shares with Elaine Showalter. You remember Showalter says that the first wave of women’s interventions in literary criticism is the moment that she calls “feminist,” the moment of Kate Millett and other authors who talk about the degradation and unfair treatment of women in male books, the second wave being “gynocritical criticism,” or women’s appropriation of literary traditions for themselves, the archival work that makes the canon of women’s literature not just a matter of leaping from great name to great name but a development from decade to decade. Gates sees much the same development in African American criticism. He doesn’t put the two options chronologically, but you could map them onto Showalter’s sequence if you wished. He says (1896): “What I mean by citing these … overworked terms [he’s talking about “the other” in particular] is precisely this: how blacks are figures in literature, and also how blacks figure, as it were, literature of their own making.”

正如肖瓦尔特所论证的那样，文学传统的问题比篇幅较短的批评传统更为复杂，因为它经历了更多阶段。女性从早期写作开始就拥有的自我表达能力经历了不止两个阶段，非裔美国文学亦是如此。盖茨的论述与耶鲁大学同事迈克尔·库克几乎同时期在其著作《二十世纪非裔美国文学：亲密关系的成就》（1984）中的观点有很多共同之处。库克认为，非裔美国文学史基本上经历了四个阶段。它始于“自我遮蔽”时期：这是人们首次尝试写作的时期。盖茨指出，在这个阶段，写作实际上是将自己融入人类社会，因为写作能力——南方奴隶正是因此被禁止学习——被视为人类身份的证明。无论如何，最早尝试写作的人都以白人为榜样。菲莉丝·惠特利或许是在“表达某种含义”（我们稍后会谈到这个关键词），但从表面上看，她的写作风格却像亚历山大·蒲柏。因此，她属于库克所说的“自我掩饰”的第一阶段。

As Showalter argued, too, the question of the literary tradition is more complicated than that of the shorter critical tradition because it passes through more stages. The powers of self-expression available to women from their earliest writings passed through more than two stages, and the same thing is true of African American literature. Gates’s account has much in common with work done almost simultaneously by a Yale colleague named Michael Cooke in a book called Afro-American Literature in the Twentieth Century: The Achievement of Intimacy (1984). Cooke argued that the history of African American literature passes essentially through four stages. It begins with “self-veiling”: the period in which people attempted for the first time to write at all. Of this stage Gates remarks that writing is really writing oneself into the human community, since the ability to write, which slaves in the South were prohibited from learning for this very reason, was considered a proof of being human. In any case, the people who first attempted to write used white models. Phillis Wheatley may have been “signifyin’ ”—we’ll come to this keyword soon—but outwardly she wrote like Alexander Pope. She is an instance, then, of the first phase, which Cooke calls “self-veiling.”

库克称之为“孤独”的第二阶段，继续沿用白人的散文和叙事模式，但以种族自我认同为中心主题。在这里，你可以想到弗雷德里克·道格拉斯以及奴隶叙事，这些叙事强调的是被白人教导，但其中也蕴含着对压迫的反抗，指向自我解放。第三阶段，库克称之为“亲缘关系”，这是一种非裔美国人彼此联结的文学，他们将自己视为一个社群，而非为自由而奋斗的个体。库克将这一阶段与方言实验以及强调语言差异的叙事和诗歌创作方式联系起来。兰斯顿·休斯的诗歌以及哈莱姆文艺复兴时期创作的许多其他作品都属于这一阶段。

The second phase, which Cooke calls “solitude,” continues to use white models of prose and narration but takes racial self-definition for its central theme. Here you might want to think of Frederick Douglass and of slave narratives in general, where the emphasis is on being taught by white people, but where nevertheless there is a resistance to subordination that points toward self-liberation. Third, there is what Cooke calls “kinship,” a literature in which African Americans reach out to each other, identifying themselves as a community, not as individuals struggling to be free. Cooke links this phase to experimentation with dialect and to ways of narrating and poetizing that emphasize verbal and linguistic difference. The poems of Langston Hughes and much else that’s written during the Harlem Renaissance belong to this phase.

当我们谈到最后一个阶段时，库克和盖茨之间也出现了分歧，因为盖茨认为我们还没有到达最后一个阶段，尽管我猜想他也认为这是一个值得追求的结果。库克将最终阶段称为“亲密性”。这指的是可以自由地挪用任何模式，不再局限于反映种族传统的审美和主题选择，而是以一种后种族的方式进行写作，这与伍尔夫的雌雄同体理想有几分相似。例如，埃里森的《看不见的人》是晚期现代主义的杰作。它自由地从任何现成的传统中汲取灵感，以完成埃里森想要创作的作品。库克或许有些乐观地将这种美学（显然没有体现在主题上）等同于他所谓的“亲密性”：即各种传统最终融合，以至于正如伍尔夫所论证的那样，人们不再需要以代言人的身份写作。

When we come to the last phase, we come also to a point of disagreement between Cooke and Gates because Gates doesn’t think we’ve reached the last phase, though I’d imagine that he, too, sees it as an outcome to be desired. Cooke calls the culminating phase “intimacy.” This consists in the freedom to expropriate any and all models, not to confine oneself to the aesthetic and thematic choices reflecting a racial tradition but to write as it were postracially, somewhat in parallel with Woolf’s ideal of androgyny. Ellison’s Invisible Man, for example, is a masterpiece of late modernism. It takes freely from whatever traditions are ready to hand for the work Ellison wants to do. Cooke identifies this aesthetic (which is clearly not reflected in theme) perhaps rather optimistically with what he calls “intimacy”: with a finally achieved merger of traditions such that, as in Woolf’s argument, one no longer has to write as a spokesperson.

我认为盖茨的观点是正确的，我们尚未达到亲密的境界，这也是为什么我在谈到库克第四阶段写作模式的挪用时，特意使用了“挪用”这个词。问题在于，如果我使用自身传统之外的模式，我并非凭空捏造，而是带着某种精心策划的目的。我们尚未完全达到亲密的境界，因为自我定义在我转向世界主义的过程中仍然是一个问题。你可以尽情谈论《看不见的人》的晚期现代主义甚至后现代主义，但这部小说仍然探讨的是身为黑人的意义，甚至在美学选择上也蕴含着某种程度的反抗。

Gates I think rightly feels that we haven’t arrived at intimacy, and that’s why I deliberately used the word “expropriate” in talking about the way models of writing are taken over in Cooke’s fourth phase. The trouble is that if I use models other than those made available by my own tradition, I’m not just pulling them out of the air. I’m using them with a calculated purpose. We’re not quite at intimacy because self-definition is still at issue in my very turn to cosmopolitanism. You can talk about the late modernism or even postmodernism of The Invisible Man all you like, yet that novel is still about what it means to be black, with a measure of defiance entailed even in the choice of aesthetic.

盖茨认为，自我定义仍然是问题的关键。我们借鉴其他模式，但我们需要将它们内化为己用。否则，我们最终只会沦为它们的殖民者，一切又回到了原点。菲利斯·惠特利曾使用白人模特，她渴望成为一位诗人，而不是一个异域奇观——一个会押韵的年轻黑人女奴。她希望自己可以随心所欲地写作，比如理查德·威尔逊画作中尼俄柏的眼泪。但问题显而易见。如果亲密关系，即不同传统的冷静融合，在第四阶段得以实现，那只不过是菲利斯·惠特利在第一阶段所追求的目标的实现；但它真的完全实现了吗？借用的表达方式仍然是他者的语言；因此，正如盖茨所坚持的，我们必须承认，身份盲视尚未到来，这当然是有充分理由的。

As Gates sees it, self-definition continues to be the issue. We use other models, but we need to make them our own. Otherwise we’re just colonized by them, and then after all we’re back in phase one. Phillis Wheatley used white models, aspiring indeed to the idea that she was a poet, not that exotic spectacle, a young black slave woman who could rhyme. She could write about anything she wanted to write about, she hoped—the tears of Niobe, for example, in the painting by Richard Wilson. But you can see the problem. If intimacy, the dispassionate merger of traditions, is achieved in the fourth phase, well, that’s just the realization of what Phillis Wheatley wanted in the first phase; but is it fully realized? A borrowed expression is still the language of the other; hence we have to admit, as Gates insists, that identity blindness is not yet at hand, and certainly for good reason.

这就引出了盖茨的核心概念：挪用他人的传统，尤其是白人的传统，意味着什么？这样做又有什么好处？至少目前来看，盖茨主要思考的是批评，而非文学。他问道，我们如何用白人的语言进行理论和批评？我们如何才能将白人的语言、术语和理论据为己有？盖茨引用巴赫金的一段非凡的题词，强调了为己所用的必要性。顺便一提，这段话对于理解巴赫金至关重要，其重要性不亚于我们之前研读巴赫金著作时所学的任何内容。我希望你们记下这段话，因为它有助于我们理解当时的讨论。在盖茨引用的这段题词中，巴赫金（1891）说道：

This brings us to Gates’s key concept: what does it mean to expropriate other people’s traditions, more particularly the white tradition, and what is the advantage of doing so? Here at least for the moment, Gates is thinking primarily about criticism, not about literature. How, he asks, can we do theory and criticism in the white man’s language? How can we appropriate for ourselves the white man’s language, terms, theories? The necessity of bending language to one’s own purposes is what is emphasized in the remarkable epigraph that Gates takes from Bakhtin. This is a central passage for an understanding of Bakhtin, by the way, as much so as anything that we studied when we were actually reading Bakhtin, and I’d like you to make note of it because I think it can shed light on what we said then. In Gates’s epigraph, Bakhtin says (1891):

对于个体意识而言，语言处于自我与他者的边界。语言中的词语一半属于他人。只有当说话者赋予它自己的意图和语调（你可以听出盖茨想要强调“语调”这个词），当他挪用词语，使其符合自身的语义和表达意图时，它才成为“自己的”。在此挪用之前，词语并不存在于中立且客观的语言中（毕竟，说话者并非从字典中获取词语！），而是存在于他人的口中，存在于他人的语境中，服务于他人的意图：正是从那里，人们必须汲取词语，使其成为“自己的”。
language, for the individual consciousness, lies on the borderline between oneself and the other. The word in language is half someone else’s. It becomes “one’s own” only when the speaker populates it with his own intention, his own accent [and you can hear Gates wanting to emphasize that word “accent”], when he appropriates the word, adapting it to his own semantic and expressive intention. Prior to this moment of appropriation, the word does not exist in a neutral and impersonal language (it is not, after all, out of a dictionary that the speaker gets his words!), but rather it exists in other people’s mouths, in other people’s contexts, serving other people’s intentions: it is from there that one must take the word, and make it “one’s own.”

在文章中，盖茨也引用了德里达的话，呼应了巴赫金的这种观点：“正如德里达所写，我们必须掌握‘如何在不放弃（我们）自己语言的情况下说别人的语言’”（1901）。

During the course of his essay, Gates echoes this sentiment of Bakhtin by quoting Derrida, too; “We must master, as Derrida wrote, ‘how to speak the other’s language without renouncing (our) own’ ” (1901).

如何做到这一点？如何着手掌控你所拥有的语言？这不仅仅是协商种族差异的问题，而是我们所有人作为语言使用者彼此之间关系的问题。正如巴赫金在你已读过的文章中所说，大多数时候我们都在说别人的语言。我们很少能像创作作家那样，自认为已经将别人的语言从传统用法中解放出来，使其成为我们自己的语言，并稍加改写，使其带有我们自己的印记。更广泛地说，这就是一个不愿重复他人观点的理论事业所面临的挑战。

How to do this? How do you set about taking over the language you are given? This isn’t just a question of negotiating racial difference. It’s a question for all of us in relation to each other as speakers. As Bakhtin says in what you have already read, most of the time we’re speaking other people’s languages. It is rare indeed that we can say, feeling very much like creative writers when we do so, that we have wrenched other people’s language out of conventional usage and made it our own, slightly rewritten it so it bears our signature. More broadly speaking, this is the challenge that faces a theoretical enterprise that doesn’t want to repeat what other folks have already said.

盖茨和肖沃尔特一样，都意识到符号的概念很可能是白人男性文学理论的基石。他认识到必须对符号进行挪用，并以此为目的，选择探讨如何对某事物进行符号化。他以一种非常平静的方式引入了这一观点，似乎只是顺带提及（1900）：“根据休谟的说法，写作是区分动物和人类的最终符号，因此这些作家实际上是在对锁链本身进行符号化。” 注意这里用巴赫金的术语来说的“重音”。你不一定非要发出g音：这些作家是在对锁链进行符号化。当然，等级森严的“存在之链”与锁链帮的锁链截然不同，同样也与解构主义中的能指之链截然不同。思想史中的链条（A.O.洛夫乔伊的“存在之链”）和横轴上的链条，与最初将奴隶和后来被监禁的自由人联系在一起的链条截然不同。批评家通过提醒人们该术语也包含着一些未被言说、未被低语的内容，从而“赋予”该术语新的意义。至少在表面上看来，在白人男性理论传统中，“能指”只不过是语言差异博弈中的一个占位符，而黑人对该术语的挪用则能为这场博弈引入新的维度。

Gates recognizes, as does Showalter, that the notion of the sign is probably the cornerstone of white male literary theory. He recognizes that one must expropriate the sign, and with this end in view he elects to talk about the way one can signify on something. He introduces this move very quietly, seemingly just in passing (1900): “Since writing, according to Hume, was the ultimate sign of difference between animal and human, these writers implicitly were Signifyin(g) upon the figure of the chain itself.” Notice the “accent,” to use Bakhtin’s term. You don’t necessarily pronounce the g: these writers were signifyin’ on the chain. Of course, the Great Chain of Being, which is hierarchical, is very different from the chain of the chain gang and, likewise again, from the chain of the signifier in deconstruction. The chain in intellectual history (A. O. Lovejoy’s great chain of being) and the chain on the horizontal axis are very different from the chain that binds first slaves and later jailed freedmen together. The critic “signifies on” a term by introducing a reminder that the term also means something that has gone unspoken, unwhispered. At least allegedly, the “signifier” in the white male theoretical tradition is no more than a placeholder in a play of linguistic differences, and the black appropriation of the term can introduce a new dimension to this play.

但“象征”究竟是什么意思？这个表达源自何处？它来自​​非洲。盖茨从非洲的“骗子”传统中汲取了这一概念，这种传统讲述的是弱者往往更聪明，猴子或蜘蛛一次又一次地戏弄强大的恶棍，比如大象或狮子。所有恶棍都会上当受骗，因为他们更愚蠢，而弱者总能瞒过他们，让他们浑然不觉。这种关于象征的表达方式属于非裔美国人的民间传说传统，我最初是在一首由拟声吟唱歌手小奥斯卡·布朗创作并演唱的歌曲《象征猴子》（Signifyin' Monkey）中听到的。这首歌被许多器乐组合翻唱，成为20世纪五六十年代灵魂爵士乐的经典曲目。总之，奥斯卡·布朗二世对“符号猴子”的戏仿启发了盖茨的想法，即把别人的话语从其语境中抽离出来，并将其弯曲成非裔美国人的语境，这种语境是自己的语境，而不仅仅是别人赋予的语境。

But what does it mean to “signify on” something? Where does the expression come from? It comes from Africa. Gates takes the concept from the trickster tradition, the tradition of African storytelling in which the weaker is also the smarter, and the monkey or the spider tricks the big, bad guys, the elephant or the lion, over and over again. All of the bad guys get tricked because they are stupider, and the little guy is always able to lie to them without their realizing what’s going on. This way of talking about signifying belongs to the tradition of African American folklore, then, and first came to my attention in a song written and sung by the scat singer Oscar Brown Jr. called “Signifyin’ Monkey.” It was picked up by various instrumental groups and was a soul jazz staple of the 1950s and 1960s. In any case, Oscar Brown Jr.’s riff on the signifyin’ monkey helps inspire Gates’s idea of taking somebody else’s discourse out of its context and bending it to an African American context, a context that is one’s own and not just the context one is given.

“指称”（signifyin'）或“对称称”（signifyin' on）最终不仅仅是对白人思想的挪用，在这里，其目的是为了用白人素材建立一种真正的黑人文学理论；它也是一种对权威人士的戏弄。当A在B面前与C谈论B，而B却不知情，实际上被欺骗时，这就是“指称”的社会动态。B是一位白人文学理论家，A和C是黑人文学理论家，他们在B的期刊上发表文章，也阅读B的期刊（盖茨的文章发表在芝加哥大学著名的理论期刊《批判性探究》上）。他们开了一个关于“对能指进行指称”的玩笑，将链条中一个虚拟的声音（充满喧嚣和愤怒，却毫无意义）变成了一种打破链条的实际社会戏法，而B却没有意识到，随着这种打破，理论游戏的规则已经改变。这不是“亲密”。

Signifyin’, or signifyin’ on, finally, is not just the takeover of a white idea, here in the interest of founding an authentic black literary theory out of white materials; it is also a trick played on the Man. When A talks to C about B in the presence of B without letting B know he’s being talked about and in effect lied to, that’s the social dynamic of signifyin’. B is a white literary theorist, A and C are black literary theorists who publish in and read B’s journal (Gates’s essay appeared in the University of Chicago’s hallowed journal of theory, Critical Inquiry). They share a joke about signifyin’ on the signifier, turning a virtual sound in a chain (full of sound and fury, signifying nothing) into an actual social trick that breaks the chain, without B realizing that with this break the rules of the theory game have been changed. That’s not “intimacy.”

盖茨在《紫色》中举的最后一个例子——关于“把男人从你的眼里赶走”的对话——也体现了“象征意义”的运用。但正如我一开始所说，即使在非裔美国人的传统中也存在着同样的问题。正如盖茨所指出的，惠特利以及后来的丽贝卡·杰克逊都从白人男性身上汲取了教育和自我发展的模式，这些白人男性教会了她们阅读。在这两种情况下，这都是有害的，因为白人男性形象的存在仍然深深地影响着她们。你必须把男人从你的眼里赶走，至少根据盖茨引用的《紫色》中的对话是这样的。没错，但显然，舒格说的“男人”指的不仅仅是白人男性。 《紫色》所展现的女权主义，正努力摆脱男性主导的社会建构，而这种建构并非仅仅由种族构成。盖茨说得对，“男人”这个词，我们都明白它是“白人”的简称（就像“比尔”可以是任何人的名字，但过去被潮人用来指代“名字很土的白人”），它也可以变成一个令人厌恶的词，一个令人反感的污点：“把那家伙从你眼前赶走”。然而，在女权主义传统中，它也可以被用来指代所有男性，以一种重叠且略有不同的方式表达谴责：“男人”指代所有男性。这里我们再次看到了它与非裔美国女权主义批评之间的微妙张力，它反映了某种程度的缓和，但仍然需要我们选择侧重点。

Another example of “signifyin’ on” appears in Gates’s culminating example from The Color Purple, the conversation about “gettin’ the man out of your eye.” But here there resurfaces the problem that exists, I began by saying, even within the African American tradition. As Gates has been pointing out, Wheatley and later Rebecca Jackson take their models of education and self-development from white male figures who have taught them how to read. In each case, this is pernicious because the existence of the white male figure is very much still in your eye. You got to get the man out of your eye, at least according to the dialogue Gates quotes from The Color Purple. Yes, but plainly Shug doesn’t just mean the white man when she says “the man.” The Color Purple sustains a feminism struggling to free itself from social constructions of male dominance that aren’t just defined by race. Gates rightly says that “the man,” which we all recognize as shorthand for “the white man” (just as “Bill” could be anyone’s name but used to be signified on by the hipsters as “white man with a square name”) can be signified on to become a term of disgust, a speck as well as an offense to the field of vision: “get the man out of your eye.” Yet it can be signified on, too, by the feminist tradition, making it a term of opprobrium in an overlapping and partially different way: “the man” as all men. Here again we find the slight tension with African American feminist criticism, reflecting détente yet still requiring a choice of emphasis, one way or the other.

最后，我想谈谈我认为本文中最具争议性的例子。盖茨一直在谈论新农业主义运动，这场运动涌现出许多与新批评相关的代表人物，其中包括罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦。沃伦很早就否定了新农业主义者的观点，并在自己的作品中展现出进步的政治立场。你们可能读过他的《国王的人马》以及他的诗歌。沃伦是新批评发展史上的核心人物，我们之前也简要地探讨过新批评。

Finally I want to take up what to me is the most controversial example in this essay. Gates has been talking about the New Agrarian moment out of which there emerged a number of figures associated with the New Criticism, including Robert Penn Warren, who quite early on repudiated the New Agrarians and became politically progressive in his own writing. You have probably read All the King’s Men and his poetry as well. Warren was a central figure in the development of the New Criticism, which we have briefly studied.

沃伦写了一首名为《池塘森林》的诗，诗中一个黑人逃犯躲在沼泽里，逃避私刑暴徒的追杀，一只秃鹫嘲笑他。黑人评论家斯特林·布朗回应了秃鹫的一句台词（盖茨称之为“罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦的宣言”），即“黑鬼，你们这群人不懂形而上学”，反驳道：“白人，你们这群人不懂诠释学。” 我认为盖茨不应该效仿布朗（参见1893年）。他所谓的“罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦的宣言”就像《尤利西斯》里的迪西先生说“莎士比亚怎么说？‘把钱放进你的钱包里。’” 莎士比亚没这么说，是伊阿古说的。秃鹫正得意洋洋地栖息在树上，等着逃犯死去。所以，我们想说的是，布朗的解读对这首诗的作者沃伦来说是完全不公平的，沃伦用感人的笔触描绘了在这种可怕的、令人不知所措的恐慌状态下，作为一名逃犯的感受。

Warren wrote a poem called “Pondy Woods” in which a black fugitive is hiding in a swamp from a lynch mob and is mocked by a vulture. The black critic Sterling Brown answered a line spoken by the vulture (Gates calls it “Robert Penn Warren’s statement”), “Nigger, your breed ain’t metaphysical,” with the retort, “Cracker, your breed ain’t exegetical.” I don’t think Gates should have followed Brown here (cf. 1893). His “Robert Penn Warren’s statement” is like the schoolmaster Mr. Deasy in Ulysses saying “What does Shakespeare say? ‘Put but money in thy purse.’ ” Shakespeare doesn’t say that, Iago says it. The buzzard is sitting exultantly in a tree, waiting for the fugitive to die. So what one wants to say is that Brown’s reading is completely unfair to the author of the poem, Warren, who is writing a movingly sympathetic evocation of what it’s like to be a fugitive in this state of terrible and overwhelmed panic.

然而，尽管我不禁认为这是一种带有偏见的误读，但我非常清楚地理解了它的观点，并且觉得这一点在某种程度上需要得到承认。盖茨的观点无疑是对我在此提出的批评的一种预先反驳。正如我之前提到的，盖茨一直在讨论新批评主义从新农业主义中兴起的过程。这种经常被引用的谱系本身就有些误导性，但毫无疑问，一些批评家，例如艾伦·泰特（他和沃伦一样也是一位诗人），以及克林斯·布鲁克斯（程度不如泰特），确实保留了他们参与撰写的新农业主义宣言《我将坚持我的立场》中的社会保守主义思想。盖茨则认为，反动性是新批评思想不可避免的组成部分，并以沃伦与布朗的对话为例来说明这一点。当我抱怨布朗的回应对沃伦不公平，因为这位诗人把冒犯性的台词给了秃鹫时，我其实是在援引新批评的原则，正如盖茨或许预料到有人会这么做一样。正是新批评——罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦也对此有所贡献——告诉我们，不应该把说话者和作者混为一谈。

And yet, while I can’t help thinking this a tendentious misreading, I can see the point of it very clearly and feel that this point needs in some measure to be conceded. Part of Gates’s point is undoubtedly an attack in advance on the criticism I have been making here. Gates has been discussing the emergence of the New Criticism from the New Agrarianism, as I mentioned. This frequently cited genealogy is itself somewhat misleading, but unquestionably some critics such as Allen Tate, also a poet like Warren, and Cleanth Brooks (to a lesser degree than Tate) did retain the social conservatism of the New Agrarian manifesto to which they had contributed, I’ll Take My Stand. Gates is saying for his part that being reactionary is inescapably in the grain of New Critical thought, and gives the “Warren”-Brown exchange as an instance of it. When I then complain that Brown’s response is unfair to Warren because the poet gave the offensive line to a buzzard I am invoking a New Critical principle, as Gates perhaps anticipated someone would. It’s the New Criticism, to which Robert Penn Warren contributed, that tells us we shouldn’t confuse speakers with authors.

多亏了新批评，这种看似合理的教条在我们阅读诗歌时已成为理所当然。对我们而言，所有诗歌在某种程度上都是戏剧独白，如同勃朗宁和其他十九世纪诗人的作品。然而，我们也可以反驳说，如果一位作者脑海中有一个说话者，那么这个说话者就是他的一部分，是其他人无法想象的虚构。沃伦的脑海中潜藏着那只秃鹫。精明的商人莎士比亚的脑海中也潜藏着伊阿古给罗德里戈的忠告。正是这种警告让我们重新审视了广为人知的《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》争议，或许比我们这些作者超脱论的信奉者更加犹豫。我们确实需要扪心自问，作为能指本身，或许也作为“被能指”的能指，“谁有权使用‘N字’？”如果有的话。尽管在许多非裔美国人的社交网络中，这个词常被戏谑地用来描述和问候朋友，但非裔美国教师强烈反对这种做法，因为这个词的污名太深，无法挽回。在他人眼中，它代表着卑贱和堕落，这种程度的污名根本无法用非裔美国人的语言来表达，也无法从白人的仇恨和蔑视中被拯救出来。或许由此可以得出一条不成文的原则：那些无法用非裔美国人的语言来表达的词语，就应该被禁用。我们想把马克·吐温和约翰·沃伦排除在外，因为我们欠他们太多，也因为我们不喜欢焚书。但如果托妮·莫里森是对的呢？吐温无法指引吉姆走向自由，沃伦也无法帮助他的逃亡者逃离庞迪森林。

Thanks to the New Criticism, this plausible dogma is something we just take for granted when we read poems. All poems for us are to some degree dramatic monologues on the model of Browning and others in the nineteenth century. And yet it’s possible to reply that if an author has a speaker in his head, that speaker is part of him, an invention that would have been impossible for someone else to envision. Somewhere in Warren that buzzard lurked. Somewhere in the mind of the canny businessman Shakespeare, Iago’s advice to Roderigo lurked. This caveat brings us back to address the well-publicized Huckleberry Finn controversy with perhaps greater hesitation than we might have exercised as believers in authorial detachment. We really do need to ask, as signifiers ourselves and perhaps also as signifiers “on,” “Who has the right to use the ‘N-word’?” If anyone. Despite the fact that in many African American social networks the word is used with jocular fondness in the description and greeting of friends, this practice is strongly discouraged by African American teachers because the word is too badly soiled to be reclaimed. It signifies abjection and degradation in the eyes of others to an extent that simply cannot be signified on, or borrowed back and rescued from white hatred and contempt. Perhaps the rule of thumb emerges that words that can’t be signified on should be off-limits. We want to exempt Twain and Warren because we owe them so much and also because we don’t like book burning. But suppose Toni Morrison were right? Twain couldn’t point Jim toward freedom, and Warren couldn’t help his fugitive out of the Pondy Woods.

 

 

第22章

CHAPTER 22

后殖民批评
Postcolonial Criticism

阅读材料：

Readings:

萨义德，爱德华。“东方学导论。”载于《批判传统》，第 1801-1813 页。

Said, Edward. “Introduction to Orientalism.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1801–1813.

巴巴，霍米·K.“被视为奇迹的迹象。”载于《批判传统》，第 1875-1899 页。

Bhabha, Homi K. “Signs Taken for Wonders.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1875–1899.

在本课程的这一部分，后殖民研究无疑是我们所探讨的身份认同领域中最为多元的：这种多元性既源于其涵盖的材料和文化的丰富多样性，也源于后殖民研究（或简称“后殖民”）内部纷繁复杂的争议。本次讲座我们将聚焦于后殖民研究的一个发展脉络，即从爱德华·萨义德到霍米·巴巴的思想演进。这一演进可以被视为两种截然不同的学术议程之间的对比，而这两种议程又各自产生了深远的影响。

Postcolonial studies is by far the most varied of the identity fields we review in this part of the course: necessarily varied because of the immense variety of the materials and cultures covered, but also because of controversies that swirl within postcolonial studies, or “po-co,” as it’s affectionately known. In this lecture we are concentrating on one developmental strand in postcolonial studies, a progression from the work of Edward Said to that of Homi Bhabha that can be presented as a matter of contrasting intellectual agendas, each widely influential in turn.

我应该顺便提一下一些并非完全无关的话题，这些话题最终不会成为我们研究的重点，但如果您对这个领域感兴趣，或许可以考虑一下。例如，您可能会问：谁说“后殖民”？谁说我们必然摆脱了殖民主义？仅仅因为地方总督收拾行囊返回欧洲，并不意味着所谓的后殖民环境下发生了翻天覆地的变化，所以谈论“殖民研究”或许仍然有意义。此外，还有一个问题：如何定义那些在冷战期间（在很大程度上已经是一个“后殖民”时期）被超级大国或其棋子剥削的文化？如今，冷战至少在表面上已经结束。实际上，就这两个问题而言，随着国家领土的衰落和全球资本主义领土的扩张，世界殖民地的地位究竟发生了怎样的变化？如果有变化，又是如何变化的？

I should mention in passing certain not unrelated topics that won’t finally form part of our emphasis, but that you might want to consider if you do have an interest in this field. You might well ask, for example: who says, “postcolonial”? Who says we’re necessarily out of coloniality? Just because the provincial viceroy packed up and went back to Europe doesn’t mean that things changed all that much in the so-called postcolonial setting, so it might still make just as much sense to speak of “colonial studies.” There’s also the question of defining those cultures that have been exploited by superpowers or pawns of superpowers during the Cold War (already for the most part a “postcolonial” period), now that the Cold War at least allegedly no longer exists. With respect really to both questions, as national territoriality declines and global capitalist territoriality increases, how has the status of colonized parts of the world changed, if at all?

换个角度来问这个问题——这也更贴近我们今天的重点——就是：第三世界的社会、经济和政治危机是否必然要从殖民主义的角度来理解？仅仅是因为地球上的某些地区过去曾被殖民，就决定了它们现在的样子，并在第一世界强权和学者眼中定义了它们的身份吗？萨义德在试图弄清为什么19世纪的德国东方主义与法国东方主义如此相似时，就探讨了这个问题。尽管德国在中东并无殖民利益。尤其是在整个19世纪早期，德国东方主义几乎与法国东方主义如出一辙，关注点相同，利益诉求也相同。萨义德不禁疑惑，为什么法国人的观点似乎无疑受到了殖民利益的影响，而德国人却没有任何殖民利益，至少在中东是如此。

Another way to put this question—and this does bring us closer to our emphasis today—is to ask whether social, economic, and political crises in the third world are always necessarily to be understood in terms of coloniality. Is it solely the fact that certain parts of the globe were colonized in the past that constitutes them as they are and determines their identity in the eyes of first-world powers and scholars? Said addresses this question when he tries to figure out how it is in the nineteenth century that German Orientalism so very closely resembles French Orientalism, even though the Germans had no colonial interests in the Middle East. During the whole of the early nineteenth century in particular, when German Orientalism is practically indistinguishable from the French equivalent, taking up the same concerns and expressing the same interests, Said wonders how it can be that the French seem undoubtedly to be influenced in their views by their colonial interests, whereas the Germans have no colonial interests at all, at least in the Middle East.

萨义德最终自圆其说地解决了这个难题。他的答案是，德国东方学源于当时法国东方学的研究成果，并简单地烙上了法国思想的烙印。毫无疑问，他所掌握的资料也印证了这一论断。尤其是让-多米尼克·维旺·德农受拿破仑资助的《埃及史》，对整个欧洲大陆产生了深远的影响。然而，萨义德也可以提出另一种观点：某种对待第三世界的特定态度，借用詹姆逊的说法，即一种“意识形态”，仅仅是欧洲中心主义的一个方面，而与其中是否涉及殖民利益无关。

Said solves this puzzle to his own satisfaction. His answer is that German Orientalism derives from the contemporary scholarship of French Orientalism and simply takes on the stamp of French thinking. No doubt the sources at his disposal bear out this claim. Jean-Dominique Vivant Denon’s Napoleon-sponsored Histoire de l’Égypte in particular exerted a strong influence all over the Continent. Yet Said could have argued, alternatively, that a particular attitude toward the third world, an “ideologeme,” to borrow Jameson’s term, is simply an aspect of Eurocentrism, regardless whether there happen to be colonial interests involved.

然而，所有这些论点都未能解答这种态度是如何盛行的。近年来，人们一直在国家利益和商业利益之间摇摆不定，猜测它们才是其根源所在。真相仍然扑朔迷离，因为正如怀疑论者所言，殖民主义的经济基础通常被国家层面或多或少真诚维护的虚假意识所掩盖：解放人民、维护国家安全、为民主创造安全的世界等等。早在后殖民时代之前，这种关于东方主义双重成因的反复出现就体现在英国东印度公司的历史中。早在现代之前，东印度公司既是帝国主义者，又是全球资本化的先驱；而这段历史在现代从殖民主义向第三世界投资的转型过程中被改写，更使其引人入胜。我们不禁要问：究竟是什么驱动着东方主义？是领土扩张，是都市中心对地方空间的侵蚀，还是全球化中的跨国利益？我们又该如何区分这些动机？仅仅说民族主义不再重要，全球化才重要，虽然这或许很诱人，但还远远不够。一种表面上仁慈、被包装成“美国价值观”的民族主义，仍然主导着美国的外交政策，至少在两党温和派中，这种民族主义得到了广泛的政治认同。然而，关于美国反恐和反独裁行动在多大程度上是为促进全球利益而设的幌子，质疑之声却一如既往地高涨，甚至可能更加强烈。

All such arguments, however, leave unanswered the question of how such an attitude comes to prevail. In recent times, speculation has hesitated between national and business interests as root causes. The truth remains uncertain because, as skeptics would argue, the economic basis for coloniality is typically veiled by more or less honestly maintained forms of false consciousness at the national level: liberation of a people from oppression, national security, making the world safe for democracy, and so on. Even before postcolonial times, this recent repetition of the twofold causes for Orientalism was distilled in the history of the British East India Company, which was both imperialist and a pioneer in global capitalization long before the modern era; that this history has rewritten itself during the modern transition from colonization to third-world investment makes it all the more fascinating. What drives Orientalism, we persist in asking? Is it always territoriality, the encroachment of a metropolitan center on a provincial space, or is it transnational interests in globalization, and how and when can these motives be separated? It’s not enough to say, though perhaps it’s tempting, that nationalism isn’t important anymore and globalization is. An ostensibly benevolent nationalism packaged as “American values” continues to drive American foreign policy, sustained by the broad political agreement at least of moderates in both parties, with as much skeptical debate in the air as ever, perhaps more, about the degree to which our anti-terrorist and anti-dictatorial interventions are pretexts to promote global interests.

后殖民研究领域，尤其是在那些代表世界各地被殖民民族的学者中，经常讨论的另一个话题是盖亚特里·斯皮瓦克提出的问题：“底层民众应该如何发声？”斯皮瓦克的潜台词是：“底层民众究竟能否发声？”萨义德也提出了这个问题，但这个问题还有另一个方面需要注意：“底层民众应该用哪种语言发声？”也就是说，假设底层民众能够发声。例如，假设恩古吉·瓦·提昂戈能够写一部小说——而他确实能够做到。那么，这部小说应该用哪种语言写成呢？恩古吉曾反对用英语写作，并敦促其他非洲作家用他们的母语而不是殖民者的语言写作。这种观点在后殖民研究中经常得到肯定，但也经常遭到反对，理由是文学影响的传播依赖于国际出版，而国际出版需要使用广泛使用的语言。

Another topic that circulates in postcolonial studies—especially among those who represent the various colonized peoples of the world, addresses the question of Gayatri Spivak: “How should the subaltern speak?” Spivak’s subtext is, “Can the subaltern speak at all?” and Said raises that question, too, but there is another aspect of the question to keep in mind: “Which language should the subaltern speak in?” Suppose, that is, that the subaltern can speak. Suppose Ngugi wa Thiong’o, for example, can write a novel, as indeed he can. What language should it be written in? Ngugi has campaigned against writing in English and urged other African writers to write in their native languages and not in the language of the colonizer. This opinion is often affirmed in postcolonial studies, but it is just as often resisted on the grounds that the circulation of literary influence, which depends on international publishing, requires the use of languages that are widespread.

我希望，在不完全忽略这些问题的前提下，我们现在转向从萨义德到巴巴的思想轨迹。在开始思考萨义德时，我想我们应该再次从弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫入手。在《一间自己的房间》第二章中，叙述者坐在大英图书馆里，试图弄明白学者们对女性的看法。她以为只要找到几本书就万事大吉了。然而，她却被如雪崩般涌来的资料淹没了。“女性”原来是一个男人们孜孜不倦地书写的话题。当然，这些数不胜数的男性作为一个整体，其组织方式在图书馆目录或数据库中体现得最为清晰：

Without forgetting these issues altogether, I hope, we turn now to the trajectory of thought that carries us from Said to Bhabha. In beginning to think about Said, I thought we’d approach him by thinking instead, once again, about Virginia Woolf. In the second chapter of A Room of One’s Own, the speaker is sitting in the British Library, trying to figure out what scholars think about women. She thinks she’ll just find a couple of books and she’ll be all set. Instead she is overwhelmed by an avalanche of material. “Women” turns out to be a topic on which men have scribbled incessantly. Naturally these countless men as an aggregate can be seen to have organized their topic in ways that become visible most clearly in a library catalog or database:

中世纪的状况；斐济群岛的习俗；被奉为女神；道德感较弱；的理想主义；更强的责任心；南太平洋岛民的青春期年龄；吸引力；作为祭品献给；大脑体积小；更深的潜意识；体毛较少；精神、道德和身体上的劣势；对孩子的爱；更长的寿命；较弱的肌肉；强烈的情感；虚荣心；高等教育；莎士比亚对的看法；伯肯黑德勋爵对的看法；英格院长对的看法；拉布吕耶尔对的看法；约翰逊博士对的看法；奥斯卡·勃朗宁先生对的看法。
condition of Middle Ages of; habits in the Fiji Islands of; worshipped as goddesses by; weaker in moral sense than; idealism of; greater conscientiousness of; South Sea islanders age of puberty among; attractiveness of; offered as sacrifice to; small size of brain of; profounder sub-consciousness of; less hair on the body of; mental, moral and physical inferiority of; love of children of; greater length of life of; weaker muscles of; strength of affections of; vanity of; higher education of; Shakespeare’s opinion of; Lord Birkenhead’s opinion of; Dean Inge’s opinion of; La Bruyère’s opinion of; Dr. Johnson’s opinion of; Mr. Oscar Browning’s opinion of.

如果我们用“女性主义”这个词来指代男性记录的所有这些事实，我们很快就会明白爱德华·萨义德的“东方主义”一词的含义。

If we coined the term “female-ism” for all these factoids recorded by men, we’d quickly see what Edward Said’s term, “Orientalism,” is getting at.

“东方主义”远非无知的刻板印象。它是一套浩瀚的信息体系，其中一些颇具学术性，主要针对那些被统称为“东方”的民族，尤其是在十九世纪的传统中，而这些信息并非由这些民族自身编纂而成。萨义德主要关注中东民族，但他令人信服地表明，“东方主义”（或许会让我们联想到远东）仍然是描述十九世纪学术和语言学传统的恰当术语。即使在今天，正如我们所知，“东方”和“西方”也并非总是地理意义上的描述性术语，而且我们完全可以像现在这样说：没有“西方”，就没有“东方”。无数图书馆的书架上堆满了关于东方的多卷本专著，几乎所有这些著作都是西方人撰写的，探讨的是萦绕在西方想象中的这个“他者”。正如萨义德（1811年）所说：“东方主义的前提是外在性，也就是说，东方学家、诗人或学者让东方开口说话，描述东方，将其奥秘向西方阐明。”文学也做出了大量贡献，最初取材于《一千零一夜》和拜伦等真实旅行家的传说（夜莺唱着“bul-bul”为爱自焚，精灵从瓶子里蹦出来，苏丹造访后宫），后来又取材于爱德华·菲茨杰拉德的《鲁拜集》。

“Orientalism” is more than just ignorant stereotyping. It is a vast body of information, some of it scholarly, about peoples called “Oriental” by and large, especially in the nineteenth-century tradition, none of it compiled by those peoples themselves. Said’s main concern is the peoples of the Middle East, but he shows convincingly that “Orientalism” (perhaps suggesting to us the Far East) is nonetheless an appropriate term to use for that tradition of scholarship and philology in the nineteenth century. Even today, as we know, “East” and “West” are not always geographically descriptive terms, and we can certainly say, in the manner we’re getting used to, that there is no “east” without “west.” There are endless library shelves groaning under multivolume treatises on the East, nearly all of them written in the West about this “other” that haunts the Western imagination. As Said says (1811): “Orientalism is premised upon exteriority, that is, on the fact that the Orientalist, poet or scholar, makes the Orient speak, describes the Orient, renders its mysteries plain for and to the West.” Literature also makes plenty of contributions, drawing first from the Arabian Nights and the lore of actual travelers like Byron (the nightingale that sings “bul-bul” impales itself on a thorn as a sacrifice for love, the genie pops out of the bottle, the sultan visits the harem), and later from Edward Fitzgerald’s Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam.

在深入探讨您引用的萨义德的段落之前，我想先解释一下我所说的萨义德和巴巴代表后殖民话语的不同阶段是什么意思。我特别指的是伊莱恩·肖瓦尔特对女性主义批评和女性主义批评的区分，正如我们在盖茨的文章中看到的，这一区分也有其推论。首先，存在一种批评，其关注点在于男性作家在文学作品中对女性的描写；其次，则存在一种批评，其关注点在于女性文学传统。将后殖民研究叠加到这一发展进程中，我们可以看出萨义德处于第一阶段。而霍米·巴巴则将注意力集中在被殖民者、底层民众的主体位置上。当然，他并没有忽略殖民者的主体位置，因为他认为两者之间存在着根本性的关联，但他更强调被殖民人民自身的传统，尤其是他们的防御策略，这使他处于第二阶段。

Before edging closer to your excerpt from Said, let me explain what I mean in saying that Said and Bhabha represent stages of postcolonial discourse. I’m thinking in particular of Elaine Showalter’s distinction between feminist and gynocritical criticism, a distinction that has its corollary, we saw, in Gates’s essay. First there is criticism in which the treatment of women in literature by men is the focus of attention, then you get criticism in which a women’s literary tradition is the focus. Superimposing postcolonial studies on this progression, you can see that Said is in phase one. Homi Bhabha, in turn, focuses his attention on the subject position of the colonized, of the subaltern. He doesn’t leave out the subject position of the colonizer, certainly, because he sees the two as radically interrelated, but much of his emphasis is on the traditions and above all the defensive strategies of colonized peoples themselves, which puts him in phase two.

萨义德和巴巴都没有强调的一个问题是，白人男性文学理论需要重新定位以服务于其他目的。对于这种与肖沃尔特和盖茨观点上的明显差异，或许存在一些肤浅的解释。第三世界的知识分子历来都在精英云集的大都市学府接受教育，这里指的当然主要是牛津和剑桥。在某种程度上，他们认同并参与了殖民者的教育议程——这与巴巴关于混合性的论述不无关联。这纯属推测，而且必须承认，作为一种背景，它与女权主义者和非裔美国知识分子的教育环境并没有太大区别。巴巴（如果不是萨义德的话）无论如何都有自己对“西方”文学理论进行“突袭”的方式，因为他们两人都分别利用了西方文学理论的结构主义和解构主义的元素，而且正如我们将看到的，巴巴引入了一个与“意义”概念非常相似的概念。

An issue that is not emphasized in either Said or Bhabha is the need to reorient white male literary theory for alternative purposes. There are various, perhaps superficial, ways to explain this apparent difference from Showalter and Gates. Third-world intellectuals have always been educated in high-octane metropolitan institutions, by which of course one means primarily Oxford and Cambridge. To some limited degree, they come to identify—in ways not unrelated to Bhabha’s argument about hybridity—with the educational agenda of the colonizer, and to participate in it. That’s pure speculation, and as a background scenario it isn’t so very different, it must be admitted, from the educational circumstances of feminist and African American intellectuals. Bhabha if not Said, too, may in any case have their own ways of staging raids on “Western” literary theory, as both certainly do make use of its structuralist and deconstructionist moments, respectively, and Bhabha introduces a concept, as we’ll see, that’s not unlike the concept of “signifyin’.”

从我刚才所说的“分别地”一词，我们可以推断出身份理论中普遍存在的另一种两阶段发展模式。萨义德的东方主义理论以结构主义为前提。它主要关注自我与他者之间相互依存的二元对立——包括他者性的建构同时也是自我建构的一种手段，在本例中，这种自我建构指的是西方身份的建构。萨义德观点的根本二元论此后经常受到批评，其中最常见的批评来自巴巴的立场，巴巴参与了德里达式的二元论解构。巴巴的“双重意识”概念并非仅仅是两种视角的融合或混淆，而是对视角本身的动摇。正如我所说，这里也存在一种在不断演进的身份理论中普遍存在的阶段一-阶段二的趋势。古典女权主义基于一种被性别理论动摇的男女二元论，而我们也讨论过在种族理论中固守黑白二元论的问题。

From the “respectively” in what I just said, we infer another two-stage development that’s shared across identity theories. Said’s Orientalism works through structuralist premises. Its primary concern is the mutual and interdependent binary opposition of self and other—including the way the construction of otherness is at the same time a means of constructing selfhood, in this case the identity of Being Western. The fundamental binarism of Said’s viewpoint has often since been criticized, most often from the standpoint of Bhabha, who participates in the Derridean deconstruction of binarism. Bhabha’s concept of “double consciousness” is not just a merger or confusion of two perspectives but an unsettling of perspective as such. Here too, as I say, there is a phase one–phase two tendency that’s shared among evolving identity theories. Classical feminism works with a male-female binary that is unsettled by gender theory, and we have discussed the problematic of settling for accepted views of black and white in theories of race.

接下来谈谈萨义德，我们先来谈谈“真理”这个词。你可能还记得，在结构主义者拉康和德里达对拉康的批判——《真理的传播者》——中，真理正是拉康和德里达争论的焦点。萨义德不遗余力地提醒他那些同情他的读者，他所审视的对象——对阿拉伯世界的丑化甚至妖魔化——并非全然是谎言。可以说，其中很多内容，尤其是在受过训练的学者和“波斯老手”的论述中，在某种程度上是真实的。萨义德对此的语气略有不同，总的来说，他确实对东方主义的研究成果持怀疑态度，但对他而言，根本问题不在于东方主义是说谎还是说真话（1802）：

Turning then to Said, let’s begin with a word or two about “truth,” the word that was at issue, you’ll recall, between the structuralist Lacan and Derrida in his critique of Lacan, “The Purveyor of Truth.” Said is at pains to remind his sympathetic readers that his object of scrutiny, the caricature and even the demonization of the Arab world, cannot be dismissed as a mere pack of lies. Much of it is, as one might say, especially in the case of trained scholars and “old Persia hands,” true as far as it goes. Said’s tone varies somewhat about this, and in balance he does distrust the findings of Orientalism, but it remains clear that for him the fundamental issue is not whether Orientalism lies or tells the truth (1802):

我们绝不应假定东方主义的结构仅仅是谎言或神话的堆砌，一旦真相大白，这些谎言或神话就会不堪一击。我个人认为，东方主义作为欧洲-大西洋对东方权力的象征，其价值远大于其作为关于东方的真实论述的价值……然而，我们必须尊重并努力理解的是东方主义话语本身所蕴含的强大力量。
One ought never to assume that the structure of Orientalism is nothing more than a structure of lies or myths which, were the truth about them to be told, would simply blow away. I myself believe that Orientalism is more particularly valuable as a sign of European-Atlantic power over the Orient than it is as a veridic discourse about the Orient.… Nevertheless, what we must respect and try to grasp is the sheer knitted-together strength of Orientalist discourse.

确实存在大量精心编纂的特定知识，而且这些知识由来已久，例如我之前提到的德农的十卷本《历史》。其中一些知识确实属实，但仅限于其本身。因此，萨义德区分了真理和价值。东方主义话语本身并非必然为真或为假。然而，无论如何，它都会潜移默化地贬低其关注的对象。萨义德并未将其隐含的欧洲中心主义视为一种刻板印象。然而，即使是最严谨的研究者，即便著作浩如烟海，也仍然会误导读者，因为他们假装自己是洞察现实的客观窗口（1812）：“因此，我对东方主义文本的分析强调的是，这些表述仅仅是表述，而非对东方的‘自然’描述，而这些表述绝非不可见。”

A great deal of painstakingly compiled knowledge of a certain kind does exist and has long existed, like the ten volumes of Denon’s Histoire that I mentioned earlier. Some of it is true, again, as far as it goes. Said draws on a distinction, therefore, between truth and value. It’s not that Orientalist discourse is necessarily true or false. It is the case, though, that either way it insidiously devalues its object of attention. Its implicit Eurocentrism Said does not go so far as to consider in all cases a form of stereotyping. Yet even the most meticulous researchers in their very voluminousness still mislead in pretending to be unselective windows on reality (1812): “My analysis of the Orientalist text therefore places emphasis on the evidence, which is by no means invisible, for such representations as representations, not as ‘natural’ descriptions of the Orient.”

我们最好在那段文字上稍作停顿，以便进行批判性思考，因为在萨义德《东方学导论》的结尾，你会注意到他拒绝说明如何才能做得更好，尽管他仍然保留了说真话的可能性。他没有解释为什么一位阿拉伯学者对阿拉伯世界的描述会比他一直在批判的那些描述更“自然”而非“再现”。他也没有讨论，一个人是否可以预期别人在描述自己时所表现出的偏见会大于自己对自身的偏见——即自己的先入之见和成见。他承认，他并没有一套先进的理论能够保证某种形式的描述是真实可靠的，而另一种形式的描述则是带有偏见的、不真实的（1814）。

We had best pause for critique at that passage because at the end of his introduction to Orientalism, you’ll notice that Said declines to say how it could be done better, while nevertheless holding open the possibility of speaking true. He does not explain how it is that an account of the Arab world by an Arab scholar would be less a “representation” and more “natural” than what he has been criticizing. There is no discussion of whether one can expect the bias of somebody else writing about me to be greater than my own bias–my preconceptions and prejudices–about myself. He admits that he doesn’t have an advanced theory that can secure one kind of representation as true or authentic and another kind of representation as biased and inauthentic (1814):

或许最重要的任务是……探讨如何从自由主义的、非压迫性和非操纵性的视角来研究其他文化和民族。但这又需要我们重新思考知识与权力这一复杂的问题。遗憾的是，这项研究在这些问题上都未能得到充分的探讨。
Perhaps the most important task of all would be to … ask how one can study other cultures and peoples from a libertarian, or a nonrepressive and nonmanipulative, perspective. But then one would have to rethink the whole complex problem of knowledge and power. These are all tasks left embarrassingly incomplete in this study.

不禁让人疑惑，究竟哪里才能找到“自然”的文本？正如我们所了解的，符号是任意的，它不可避免地将我们置于表征的领域，让我们不得不权衡不同表征的价值，同时抹杀真理的标准。

It remains to wonder where the text might be that is “natural.” The sign being arbitrary, as we’ve learned, it does locate us inescapably in the realm of representation, left to value one representation more than another while leaving the criterion of truth under erasure.

萨义德公开阐述了自己的思想框架，值得我们停下来思考一下对他影响最大的两位学者兼理论家——米歇尔·福柯（其“知识与权力”的论述出现在上文引用的段落中）和意大利马克思主义者安东尼奥·葛兰西——所共同持有的观点。萨义德在1803年解释他对葛兰西的借鉴时说道：

Said openly announces his own intellectual framework, and it’s worth pausing over an idea shared by the two scholar-theorists who matter most to him, Michel Foucault (whose “knowledge and power” gets into the passage cited above) and the Italian Marxist Antonio Gramsci. Said explains his debt to Gramsci as follows (1803):

当然，文化是在公民社会中运作的，在公民社会中，思想、制度和其他人的影响不是通过统治，而是通过葛兰西所说的同意来发挥作用的。
Culture, of course, is to be found operating within civil society, where the influence of ideas, of institutions and of other persons works not through domination but by what Gramsci calls consent.

你可以看出这与福柯的理论之间的联系：真理体制并非强加于人的观念或法律，而是知识和意识形态的流通，这种流通通过共识确立了某些偏见态度。这正是葛兰西所区分的两种方式：一种是人们被实际权力和权威所强加的方式，另一种是人们被詹姆逊所谓的“意识形态”流通所强加的方式。

You can see the connection with Foucault: regimes of truth are not a matter of having ideas or laws forced down your throat, but a circulation of knowledge, of ideology, which through consent establishes certain attitudes of bias. This is the distinction that Gramsci makes between the way one is imposed on by actual power and authority and the way one is imposed on by the circulation of what Jameson calls “ideologemes.”

接续萨义德的论述：“在任何非极权社会中，某些文化形式会凌驾于其他文化形式之上，正如某些思想比其他思想更具影响力一样；这种文化领导形式正是葛兰西所说的霸权。”这是一个你会经常遇到的术语，尤其是在马克思主义批评中，但它也与大多数大西洋盆地读者更熟悉的福柯著作中的“权力”一词密切相关，有时也与“权力/知识”相关。正如你将在下一讲阅读的福柯节选中了解到的，福柯和葛兰西一样，区分了两种权力：一种是警察、法律或独裁者实施的单纯强制，另一种是整个社会结构如何使某种被视为知识的形式具有霸权和权威性的权力。因此，葛兰西和福柯都区分了绝对权力与霸权或权力/知识。萨义德认为，按照这些话语建构者的思路，西方东方主义是一种霸权形式。

To continue the passage from Said: “In any society not totalitarian, then, certain cultural forms predominate over others, just as certain ideas are more influential than others; the form of this cultural leadership is what Gramsci has identified as hegemony.” This is a term that you will frequently encounter, particularly in Marxist criticism, but it is also closely related to what for most Atlantic Basin readers is more familiar from the work of Foucault, the term “power,” or sometimes “power/knowledge.” As you will learn in the excerpt from Foucault that you’ll read for the next lecture, Foucault like Gramsci makes a distinction between power as mere coercion by the police or the law or the dictator and power as the way the entire structure of society makes some form of what passes for knowledge hegemonic and authoritative. Both Gramsci and Foucault, then, make the distinction between absolute power and hegemony or power/knowledge. For Said, following these founders of discursivity, Western Orientialism is a form of hegemony.

在萨义德看来，霸权性观点建构了后殖民世界，同时也强化了这些观点制造者的权威（福柯所反对的“作者身份”）。然而，萨义德在某一方面与福柯存在分歧，即关于作者身份的影响力。我不确定福柯是否会否认，如果我们允许作者拥有这种权威，他们最终会变得极其危险。因此，我认为萨义德夸大了福柯认为所有作者即使作为影响范围也微不足道的观点。但萨义德的观点仍然值得引用，因为它体现了他认为权力即使没有棍棒也能造成毁灭性的压迫（1813）：“福柯认为，一般来说，单个文本或作者的影响力微乎其微；就东方主义而言，或许在其他任何地方，我都发现情况确实如此。”

For Said, hegemonic opinions construct the postcolonial world and simultaneously reinforce the authority (the being-an-author resisted by Foucault) of those who generate the opinions. Said does, however, disagree with Foucault in one respect, precisely concerning the influence of authorship. I’m not sure Foucault would disagree that authors are, after all, dangerously authoritative if we allow them to be, and feel therefore that Said exaggerates the degree to which Foucault supposes all authors to be negligible even as spheres of influence, but Said’s opinion is still worth citing as an index of his sense that power is crushingly oppressive even without a truncheon in its hand (1813): “Foucault believes that in general the individual text or author counts for very little; empirically [that is to say, “based on my experience”], in the case of Orientalism, and perhaps nowhere else I find this not to be so.”

换句话说，这里的“作者”指的是那些对世界这一地区进行了大量著述的语言学家、社会历史学家、探险家和人口学家，他们向我们灌输了大量信息，而这些信息却完全不受任何先验知识的质疑。他们是无可匹敌的先知，可以肆无忌惮地进行威逼利诱。因此，就东方主义而言，问题不在于潜意识里反复出现的某种观点——当我们说“他们说……”时，“他们又说了什么”——而这正是福柯所关注的那种现象。

In other words, the “author” is in this case the philologists, social historians, explorers, and demographers who have written so extensively on this part of the world and filled our heads with information that goes completely unchallenged by any prior knowledge of any kind. They are unrivaled oracles who can browbeat with impunity. In the case of Orientalism, it is not a question, therefore, of a subliminal drumbeat of opinion expressing itself over and over again—what “they say” when we say that “they say that …”—which is the sort of phenomenon that interests Foucault.

因此，作为一种权力流通，东方主义对欧洲中心主义思维的影响最终是萨义德所关注的。他强调这一点带有几分反问意味，因为显然他也同样关注东方主义对相关民族的影响。为了进一步阐明他的担忧，他甚至像托妮·莫里森和其他一些我们之前接触过的学者那样，声称东方主义甚至可以说塑造了欧洲中心主义的思维（1806）：“我的真正论点是，东方主义是——而不仅仅是代表——现代政治知识文化的一个重要维度，因此，它与东方的关系远不如与‘我们’的世界的关系密切。”

So as a circulation of power, the effect of Orientalism on the Eurocentric mind is what ultimately concerns Said. He insists on this point somewhat rhetorically because it obviously does concern him, too, that Orientalism also has an effect on the peoples in question. In pressing home his concern, he goes so far as to claim, in the vein of Toni Morrison and others we have encountered, that Orientalism can even be said to construct the Eurocentric mind (1806): “[M]y real argument is that Orientalism is—and does not simply represent—a considerable dimension of modern political-intellectual culture, and as such has less to do with the Orient than it does with ‘our’ world.”

回想一下莫里森说过的话。如果我们研究的是美国文学和文化史，那么“黑人”作为一种缺席的存在，必须被理解为构建“白人”身份的手段，它将“白人”从原本会使其停滞不前的种种束缚中解放出来。或许既然这个主题开始反复出现，我应该谈谈黑格尔《精神现象学》第四章中的主奴辩证法。黑格尔阐述了这样一个观点：在互惠的结构中，主人和奴隶是彼此绝对必要的。如果没有奴隶的存在，主人就不是主人，也无法将自己定义为自由或优越的，因为奴隶的反抗精神使他得以征服。（黑格尔在这里想到的是封建德国男爵们嗜血的勇气。）奴隶为了在从属地位中生存，学会了各种狡猾的手段，这其中涉及复杂技能的发展，这意味着很快主人就会依赖于奴隶，因为奴隶在技术和文化上已经变得比主人更胜一筹。在一个阶级颠倒的寓言故事中，奴隶变成了主人，这种颠倒的局面不断发生。这种阶级关系哲学既构成了莫里森关于种族关系的论证基础，也构成了萨义德关于东西方关系的论证基础。

Recall what Morrison said. If we are studying the history of American literature and culture, the existence of black as absence needs to be understood as the means of constructing whiteness, liberating whiteness from the forms of constraint under which it would otherwise languish. Perhaps since this motif is starting to recur, I should tell you something about the master-slave dialectic in the fourth chapter of Hegel’s Phenomenology of Mind. It’s clear as Hegel develops the idea that master and slave are absolutely necessary to each other in a structure of mutuality. The master isn’t the master, can’t define himself as free or superior, without the existence of the slave, whom he has subdued because of his willingness to fight. (Hegel thinks here of the bloodthirsty courage of the feudal German barons.) The trickiness that the slave learns from the need to survive in the position of subordination, which involves the development of complex skills, means that soon enough the master depends on the slave, who has become technologically and culturally superior. The slave becomes master in a fable of class reversal, a situation that reverses itself again and again. This is a philosophy of class relations that structures Morrison’s argument about race relations and also structures Said’s argument about West and East.

我想在此过渡到巴巴的理论，因为很明显，这种辩证法是一种二元论。正如索绪尔传统中那样，这两个能指彼此需要。我无法简单地说红灯是什么。我只能在它与非红灯事物的关系矩阵中认识它。在交通信号灯中，如果没有黄灯和绿灯，红灯就毫无意义。在这个符号系统中，红灯既不是黄灯也不是绿灯。要完全了解它，就必须了解它在两种不同的二元关系中的角色。简而言之，我只能将一个概念，甚至我自己的概念，作为其他一个或多个概念的否定来呈现。

I want to make the transition to Bhabha here, because obviously this dialectic is a form of binarism. The two signifiers need each other as they do in the Saussurian tradition. I can’t simply say what a red light is. I know it only in a matrix of relations with what it is not. In a traffic light, red would be nothing were it not for yellow and green. In this semiotic system, red is not-yellow and also not-green. To know it fully is to know its role in two different binaries. I can represent a concept to myself, in short, even the concept of myself, only as the negation of some other concept or concepts.

索绪尔传统中二元对立的基本概念塑造了萨义德等人的论证。我们否定性地将自身视为“非他者”，这是支撑这一论证的理论原则。然而，当萨义德将他的定向主义论题视为一种积极的社会批判时，它并不带有结构主义的意图。萨义德运用结构主义思想来组织他仍然认为是经验性的研究。他知道自己持有结构主义思想，但他相信自己能够将其直接映射到现实世界（他并非像巴特所说的那样先解构再重组），因为他已经看到这种思想在文化政治领域中得以体现。

This basic notion of the binary in the Saussurian tradition is what shapes arguments like Said’s. That we know ourselves negatively as the not-other is the theoretical principle that undergirds the argument. Nevertheless, Said’s thesis about Orientialism does not have a structuralist agenda when presented as an activist social critique. Said uses a structuralist idea to organize what he still considers to be empirical research. He knows he has a structuralist idea, but he believes he can map it directly onto the real world (he is not decomposing in order to recompose, as Barthes put it) because he has seen it play itself out as a reality in the sphere of cultural politics.

然而，其前提仍然是结构主义的。巴巴公开批评这种二元论，事实上，他将这种论证方式与黑格尔（1879）的观点联系起来：

The premise, however, is still structuralist. Bhabha openly criticizes binarism of this kind, and in fact identifies this sort of argument with Hegel (1879):

正是这种矛盾心理（参与者对自己的自我认知所感受到的矛盾心理）使得殖民“立场性”的边界——自我/他者的划分——以及殖民权力问题——殖民者/被殖民者的区分——既不同于黑格尔的主人/奴隶辩证法，也不同于现象学的他者投射。
It is this ambivalence [felt by participants concerning their self-conception] that makes the boundaries of colonial “positionality”—the division of self/other—and the question of colonial power—the differentiation of colonizer/colonized—different from both the Hegelian master/slave dialectic or the phenomenological projection of Otherness.

在这里，巴巴尽可能清晰地将自己与萨义德的理论体系区分开来。这段文字以“矛盾心理”一词开头。我们将尝试理解巴巴对这个词的理解，并尝试据此深入他错综复杂的思考。我希望通过一个历史例子来尽可能地阐明这一点。殖民者对被殖民者抱有矛盾心理，被殖民者自身也抱有矛盾心理；驱动殖民的并非只有一种态度。例如，在东印度公司的历史经验中，存在两个截然不同的阶段，这两个阶段在整个二十世纪反复交替。第一个阶段发生在十八世纪，当时东印度公司由沃伦·黑斯廷斯领导。黑斯廷斯热衷于我们所谓的“融入当地文化”，并鼓励他所有的省级官员也这样做。用萨义德的话来说，黑斯廷斯对东方化的他者有着深刻的理解。他精通当地所有语言和方言，熟知当地风俗。显然，他对这片异域风情充满好奇，或许在某种程度上甚至抱有敬意。然而，他仍然是一位冷酷无情的总督，一位从未放松对权力铁腕掌控的殖民者。黑斯廷斯体现了巴巴所强调的矛盾心理：他从未让步，却又似乎与权力融为一体，毫无疑问，他正暗自嘲笑那些对印度一无所知的英国游客。

Here is a moment in which Bhabha is distinguishing himself as clearly as he can from the project of Said. This passage begins with the word “ambivalence.” We shall try to grasp what Bhabha means by this term and see whether we can work our way into his intricately qualified thinking accordingly. I hope to make things as clear as possible by starting with a historical example. There is the ambivalence of the colonizer toward the colonized as well as the subaltern’s ambivalence; it’s not just one attitude that drives colonization. In the historical experience of the East India Company, for example, there are two distinct phases, phases that have actually succeeded each other repeatedly throughout the twentieth century. The first phase, in the eighteenth century, was the period when the East India Company was governed by Warren Hastings, who had an interest in what we might call “going native” and encouraged all of his provincial administrators to do likewise. In Saidian terms, Hastings knew a great deal about the Orientalized other. He knew all the local languages and dialects, he knew the customs. He obviously viewed this exotic domain with fascination, and perhaps in some limited measure even with respect. Yet he was still a ruthless governor, a colonizer who never relaxed his iron grip on authority. Hastings embodied one form of the ambivalence Bhabha emphasizes, never yielding an inch of authority, while at the same time seeming to become one with the other, and no doubt laughing up his sleeve at pale English visitors who weren’t old India hands.

此外，还有一种历史性的矛盾心理，它以一种截然不同的态度表现出来，这种态度在十九世纪初查尔斯·格兰特执掌东印度公司时开始显现。当时，英国出现了原教旨主义宗教的复兴，主要是卫理公会，福音派的热情蔓延到了帝国的利益之中。查尔斯·格兰特和与他类似的人不再愿意融入当地社会。相反，他们坚持要牢牢地植入一套英国性的标准，尤其是英国圣经的标准——巴巴在其文章开头提到的“英国书籍的到来”。将英国价值观强加于被殖民者，如今成了殖民主义的公开议程，这种意识形态无疑常常出于真诚，为维护国家和商业利益而披上了外衣。历史学家托马斯·巴宾顿·麦考利在一份名为《印度教育备忘录》的著名文件（这份文件很快便臭名昭著）中，将这种态度系统化。该文件坚持认为，在东印度公司统治下，印度人民的教育必须严格按照英国模式进行：传教士不再试图将他们的思想与当地风俗习惯相融合，而是要将一切都严格英国化。这与黑斯廷斯对殖民的态度截然不同，而且同样可以被理解为一种矛盾心理。显然，这里存在着双重标准，但传教士的热情往往伴随着真诚的善意，因此，就个人而言，其结果可能是一种比“融入当地”更富有同情心的政治态度。

Then there is the historical ambivalence that expresses itself in a completely different attitude, the one that surfaced early in the nineteenth century when the East India Company was governed by Charles Grant. There had been a revival of fundamentalist religion in England, mainly Methodism, and evangelical enthusiasm spread itself into the interests of the empire. Charles Grant and others like him no longer had any wish to go native. On the contrary, they insisted that a standard of Englishness, especially the standard of the English Bible—the coming of the English book that Bhabha talks about at the beginning of his essay—be firmly implanted. The imposition of English values on the colonized was now the announced agenda of colonization, the ideology that fronted, no doubt often sincerely, for continued national and business interests. The historian Thomas Babington Macaulay codified this attitude in a famous—soon to be infamous—document called “The Minute on Indian Education,” which insisted that the education of the Indian people under the regime of the East India Company be conducted strictly according to English models: that missionaries no longer try to adapt their ideas to local customs and folkways but that everything be strictly Anglicized. This is a completely different attitude toward colonization from that of Hastings, and it, too, can be understood as ambivalence. A double standard is obviously in play, yet missionary zeal is often accompanied by genuine benevolence, so the result may be, in individuals, a politics that is more sympathetic than the politics of going native.

还有另一个可以称之为“沃伦·黑斯廷斯时刻”的例子，虽然令人痛苦却又引人入胜，那就是约翰·福特那部令人不安的杰作《搜索者》。我希望你们当中有些人看过这部电影。约翰·韦恩饰演的角色是一个漂泊的独行侠——当然，这是西部片中常见的角色——他来到亲戚家，得知家里的一个女儿被印第安人绑架了。在这部电影里，约翰·韦恩是一个公开且恶毒的种族主义者，他对印第安人有着病态的仇恨，但他并非出于无知。从某种意义上说，他已经融入了印第安人的生活。他精通所有美洲原住民的语言和方言，了解他们的习俗。他对自己的仇恨对象进行了深入的研究。在电影中呈现这种复杂的情感组合令人不安，因为我们更容易接受仇恨源于无知的观点。沃伦·黑斯廷斯很像约翰·韦恩扮演的角色，而这只是巴巴在描述殖民者矛盾心理时所思考的众多矛盾之一。他提醒我们，知识和同情之间并没有明确的对应关系，殖民者的思维中蕴含着不止一种态度。一种是立足本土的思维模式，另一种则是强加优越文化标准的思维模式，这两种思维模式都决定了不同的策略，尤其是在教育策略方面。

There is another instance of what you might call the Warren Hastings moment, a painful example though a fascinating one, in the disturbing masterpiece by John Ford called The Searchers. I hope some of you know that film. The John Wayne character is a drifting loner—a stock character in the Western, of course—who shows up at the house of some relatives and hears that a daughter in the family has been abducted by Indians. In this film, John Wayne is an open and vicious racist who obsessively hates the Indians, but he is not an ignorant racist. He has himself, in a certain sense, gone native. He knows all the Native American languages and dialects, he knows their customs. He has made a careful study of the people he hates. This is a volatile mixture to be exposed to in a film because we are much more comfortable with the idea that hatred arises from ignorance. Warren Hastings was a lot like the John Wayne character, and that’s just one of the ambivalences that Bhabha is thinking about when he describes the ambivalence of the colonizer. He reminds us that there’s no clear parallel between knowledge and sympathy and that the mind of the colonizer comes equipped with more than one attitude. There is the local knowledge mindset, and there is the mindset bent on imposing a superior cultural standard, each of which dictates different strategies, particularly strategies of education.

这就是殖民者的矛盾心理。被殖民者的矛盾心理也同样存在，而且，这种矛盾心理也如同殖民者的矛盾心理一样，必须被理解为一种关于同化或收编的复杂态度。巴巴开篇的轶事非常值得关注。主人公并非殖民者，而是一个被彻底收编的人——一位皈依基督教的印度裔福音派基督徒。他误解了那些坐在树下读圣经的人，因为他相信（并且乐于相信）圣经，乃至基督教本身，都是“英国的馈赠”。但这些人之所以抗拒圣经是英国书籍的说法，恰恰是因为他们认为，他们应该信仰的宗教理念必须超越地域限制。他们喜欢自己读到的内容，也想相信它，但他们希望能在其中找到一些与自身习俗相契合之处。他们说，也许有一天我们会受洗，但在此之前，我们得回家收割庄稼。对了，就算我们受洗了，也肯定不能领圣餐，因为那意味着要吃肉。我们不吃肉，因为这就是我们的信仰。

So that’s the ambivalence of the colonizer. Then there is the ambivalence of the colonized, and that, too, like the ambivalence of the colonizer, has to be understood as a complex of attitudes toward assimilation or co-optation. The anecdote with which Bhabha begins is well worth attending to. The protagonist is not a colonizer but someone thoroughly co-opted, a converted evangelical Christian of Indian descent who misunderstands the people he finds sitting under the trees reading the Bible because he believes, and is happy to believe, that the Bible, and for that matter Christianity itself, is “an English gift.” But these people resist the notion of the Bible as an English book precisely because they suppose a religious idea they are meant to believe in must transcend local origin. They like what they read and want to believe it but wish they could find some accommodation to their own folkways in it. Sure, maybe we’ll get baptized one of these days, they say, but in the meantime we have to go home and take care of the harvest. And by the way, if we do get baptized we certainly can’t take the Eucharist because that would require eating meat. We don’t eat meat because that’s who we are.

你可以看出，传教士试图灌输的态度中那些巧妙暗示的附加条件，完全破坏了他的目的。他们并不把这本书视为英文圣经，也不会接受这种定义。他们只会把它视为一种权威——一种普世的权威，而非英国的权威——并且这种权威需要根据他们自身的价值观进行调整。这一前提将深刻地改变他们接受这本书作为神圣文本的方式。正如巴巴所指出的，这是1813年，正是权威体系从沃伦·黑斯廷斯模式转向查尔斯·格兰特模式的时期。人们再也无法考虑将圣经改编以适应当地的信仰和环境了。

You can see that these cunningly insinuated provisos to the attitude that the missionary wants to inculcate completely undermines his purpose. They don’t think of the book as the English Bible and won’t accept it on those terms. They will accept it only as an authority—a universal one, not an English one—that’s adjusted to their own values, and this premise would profoundly alter the way they receive the book as a sacred text. This is 1813, as Bhabha points out, precisely the moment when the regime of authority is moving from the Warren Hastings model to the Charles Grant model. It’s no longer possible to think of adapting the Bible to local beliefs and circumstances.

然而，巴巴对这一刻感兴趣的是，它如何凸显出被殖民人民复杂的态度，即他们的“矛盾心理”。一方面是受人收买的传教士的态度，另一方面是他遇到的那些坐在树下的人们更为复杂有趣的态度。在准备探讨第1881页一段晦涩难懂的文字之前，我想先解释一下：巴巴强调的矛盾心理——我们不妨用他用来指代这种心理的术语“混杂性”来理解——是被殖民者的双重意识，一方面是虽有不同但又顺从权威的服从，即按照自己的方式服从；另一方面则是对既定权威的欣然接受，这正是传教士的态度。以下是巴巴对被殖民者双重意识中这种混杂性的描述：

What interests Bhabha about this moment, though, is the way it places the complex range of attitudes, the “ambivalence,” of the colonized people in relief. There’s the attitude of the suborned missionary, and there’s the more complicated and interesting attitude of the people he encounters sitting under the trees. In preparing to look at a difficult passage on page 1881, I want to gloss it by suggesting to you that the ambivalence Babha emphasizes—which we might as well identify by the term he uses for it, “hybridity”—is the double consciousness of the colonized, hovering, on the one hand, between submission to authority but with a difference, submission on one’s own terms, and, on the other hand, willing acquiescence in authority as given, which is the attitude of the missionary. Here, then, is how Bhabha describes this hybridity in the double consciousness of the colonized:

在我提出的这种“处置”体系中，差异和他者性的位置，或者说对抗的空间，绝非完全处于外部或毫不妥协的对立状态。[换句话说，这不仅仅是“我们”与“他们”的问题。]它是一种压力，一种存在，持续地、尽管不均衡地作用于授权（即权威）的整个边界，也就是说，它存在于我所谓的“作为给予的处置”（我将其理解为顺从——因为不得不顺从，同时暗中保留自尊）和“作为倾向的处置”（因为该体制看起来有吸引力而自发地顺从）之间的表面上。
The place of difference and otherness, or the space of the adversarial, within such a system of “disposal” as I have proposed, is never entirely on the outside or implacably oppositional. [Not just, in other words, a question of us versus them.] It is a pressure, and a presence, that acts constantly, if unevenly, along the entire boundary of authorization [which is also authority], that is, on the surface between what I’ve called disposal-as-bestowal [I take that to mean submission—giving in because one has to while covertly retaining one’s self-respect] and disposal-as-inclination [which is giving in spontaneously because the regime seems attractive].

仅仅因为认输就屈服，这种顺从的形式，使人陷入了巴巴所谓的“狡猾的礼貌”（参见1889年）。在我看来，这种姿态与盖茨所说的“符号化”（signifyin'）密切相关。巴巴列举了几个这种“狡猾的礼貌”的例子，但其实在他开篇的轶事中，那些坐在树下的人物的言辞中，已经蕴含了这种微妙而丰富的反讽。让我举个我自己的例子，来说明“狡猾的礼貌”是如何作为一种“符号化”的形式，以及它如何作为一种被殖民的抵抗姿态，一种对意志的恢复——尽管这种恢复并非反叛，也并非以推翻权威为目的，而是一种在权威框架内勉强维持生存的手段。

Now to give in simply because one sees that one’s beaten, as a form of submission, puts one in the position of what Bhabha calls “sly civility” (cf. 1889). This is a position that seems to me closely related to what Gates calls signifyin’. Bhabha gives several examples of this sly civility, but it’s all present already in the clever and wonderfully rich ironies one finds in the remarks of these figures sitting under the trees in his opening anecdote. Let me just give you an example of my own to illustrate how sly civility works as a form of signifyin’ and as a stance of colonized resistance, a recuperation of the will, which is nevertheless not rebellious, not in any way practiced as an overthrow of authority, but rather as a means of making do within the framework of authority.

两个非裔美国人正在和一个白人交谈。他们兴高采烈地当着他的面称呼他为“比尔”。“嘿，比尔，怎么了？”他们问道。正如我在上一讲中提到的，“比尔”长期以来都是对白人的贬义称呼，很多白人都知道这一点。白人听到别人叫他“比尔”时有两种反应：他可以感到愤慨，质问他们为什么要这样称呼自己，这样一来，讽刺意味就更加浓重了；或者，他可以装傻充愣，就像这个称呼本身所暗示的那样，假装不知道自己正被这种带有讽刺意味的礼貌称呼所蒙蔽。无论哪种方式，对非裔美国人来说都是双赢的局面。这个被他们称为“比尔”的人，比如说，可能是个奴隶主，或者吉姆·克劳时期棉花种植园的监工，又或者是个工厂工头；但他感受到了殖民者的矛盾心理。他喜欢和所有人相处融洽，但由于天性善良，他陷入了困境。他要么抱怨下属对他不公平——当然，在主仆关系中，这种抱怨无关紧要——要么装傻充愣，假装没注意到自己被嘲笑。无论如何，我希望这个场景能展现出“主人”那种狡黠的礼貌。它清楚地表明，尽管权力结构短期内无法被推翻，但仍然存在一种生存之道——至少可以在现有的权力结构中保持幽默感——同时还能给“主人”制造一些麻烦。巴巴（Bhabha）提出了“以施舍代替处置”的概念。下属的这种狡黠礼貌，会让老板觉得下属的顺从是一种勉强的恩惠，既非出于必要，也非出于钦佩。

Two African Americans are having a conversation in the presence of a white person. Cheerfully they refer to this person in his presence as Bill. Hey, Bill, what’s happening, they say. Now as I mentioned in the last lecture, “Bill” has long been a derisive term for white people, as many white people know. The white person has two choices of response in hearing himself referred to as “Bill”: he can either take umbrage and ask why they’re picking on him like that, in which case the barb has been driven home; or he can play the fool, precisely the sort of fool the name is meant to imply, and pretend he doesn’t know that he’s being signified on with sly civility. Either way it’s a win-win situation for the African Americans. This guy they call Bill is a slave owner, let’s say, or the overseer of a cotton plantation during Jim Crow, or a plant foreman; but he feels the ambivalence of the colonizer. He likes to get along with everybody, and because there is an element of good nature in his makeup, he’s stuck. He can either complain that his subordinates are treating him unfairly—which of course is neither here nor there in a master-slave relationship—or he can play the fool and pretend that he doesn’t notice that he’s being made fun of. Either way, this scenario I hope illustrates the sly civility that signifies on the Man. It makes it clear that although the structure of power can’t be overthrown any time soon, there nevertheless is a way of subsisting—at least of keeping one’s sense of humor within the existing structure of power—while giving the Man a hard time. Bhabha speaks of “disposal-as-bestowal.” The sly civility of the subaltern is an attitude that makes the boss feel as though the subaltern’s submission has been bestowed as a grudging favor, neither enforced by necessity nor volunteered in admiration.

这就是巴巴在其关于被殖民者混合性的概念中所涵盖的各种态度。这种态度最丰富多彩、最令人满意的形式体现在一种狡黠的礼貌行为中，或者说是对“统治者”的某种暗示。对于殖民者——他本身就是一个矛盾的人物——人们的选择并非非此即彼，而是变色龙式的，以多种方式呈现，并且受到从真诚到愤世嫉俗的各种情感的微妙影响。在巴巴对后殖民二元论的解构中，类似的社会场景也浮现出来。

This, then, is the range of attitudes that Bhabha encompasses in his notion of the hybridity of the colonized. It takes its most colorful and satisfying form in the performance of sly civility, or signifyin’ on the Man. The options in relation to the colonizer—himself an ambivalent figure—are not binary but chameleonic, performed in many ways and nuanced, too, by a spectrum of feeling that ranges from sincerity to cynicism. Something like this social scenario emerges in Bhabha’s deconstruction of postcolonial binarism.

 

 

第23章

CHAPTER 23

酷儿理论与性别表演性
Queer Theory and Gender Performativity

阅读材料：

Readings:

福柯，米歇尔。“性史。”载于《批判传统》，第 1627-1636 页。

Foucault, Michel. “The History of Sexuality.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1627–1636.

巴特勒，朱迪思。“模仿与性别不服从。”载《批判传统》，第 1707-1718 页。

Butler, Judith. “Imitation and Gender Insubordination.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1707–1718.

虽然本次讲座的阅读材料有很多新内容，但我们会在最后停下来回顾和总结一下最近的学习内容，然后在下次讲座开始时继续进行回顾。不过，首先让我谈谈今天材料中的新内容、挑战性内容，以及可能存在争议的内容。

Although there’s much that’s new in the reading for this lecture, we’ll pause at the end over a review and summing up of what we’ve done recently, and then continue with that retrospect at the beginning of the next lecture. Let me start, though, with what’s new, challenging, and perhaps also subject to criticism in today’s materials.

在本次讲座中，我将探讨朱迪斯·巴特勒文章中最难以捉摸的概念。她称之为“精神过剩”，指的是来自无意识的能量或过剩，它在某种程度上甚至动摇了性别中那些可以被展现和正在展现的方方面面。我们展现身份，我们展现主体性，我们以各种方式展现性别，这些方式我们稍后会讨论。但除了我们能够展现的之外，在精神过剩的背景下，还存在着一种与它相关的“性”，它存在于未经干预的无意识领域，并从中涌现。因此，通过精神过剩展现的性暗示着“真实性”的所在，而巴特勒赖以成名的冷峻的社会身份辩证法却丝毫没有涉足或侵犯这一所在；但至少对我而言，这种对真实性底层结构的暗示，对我们讨论过的许多身份理论（尤其是性别理论）中存在的强结构主义倾向敲响了警钟。

During the course of this lecture, I’ll be talking about the slipperiest concept in Judith Butler’s essay. It’s what she calls “psychic excess,” the charge or excess from the unconscious that in some measure unsettles even the many aspects of gender that can be and are performed. We perform identity, we perform our subjectivity, we perform gender in all the other ways we’ll consider, but beyond what we can perform, there is, in relation to psychic excess, “sexuality” in the untampered-with realm of the unconscious from which it emerges. Sexuality, manifest through psychic excess, suggests therefore a locus of the “authentic,” which the grim socio-identitarian dialectic for which Butler is famous makes no pretense to have access to or invade; but to me, at least, this intimation of an authentic substratum raises a flag or two about the strong structuralism of many accounts of identity that we’ve discussed, perhaps especially gender theory.

那么，让我们从一个看似无害的问题开始。我们当然有权知道这个问题的答案：什么是性？当然，你可能会对“性”这个词本身感到疑惑——尤其如果你对术语比较敏感的话——毕竟，在我们这个饱受争议的语言中，它出现的时间并不长。在过去，人们不会谈论“性”，无论过去是好是坏。他们谈论的是“性行为” ，这个词似乎足以解释他们所了解的正常和异常行为。但“性”这个词更具社会敏感性，因此也去情色化了，如今它涵盖了这一领域。随着“性”这个词在描述我们生活中一个始终受到左右两派思想警察审视的方面时获得了认可，它开始占据主导地位；然而，与此同时，它也开始给那些最杰出、最前卫的性别研究者们带来难题。这表明，我们的性格中存在着真实、本真的一面，至少比我们能够并且确实展现出来的那些方面更贴近我们自身。

So let’s begin with what ought to be an innocent question. Surely we’re entitled to an answer to this question, which is: what is sexuality? Now, of course, you may be given pause—especially if you have an ear fine-tuned to jargon—by the very word “sexuality,” which is relatively recent in our beleaguered language. People didn’t talk about “sexuality” in the good or bad old days. They talked about sex, which seemed adequate to account for both the normative and aberrant behaviors of which they were aware. But “sexuality” is the more socially sensitive, hence de-eroticized, term that now traverses this field of possibilities. And with this cachet of acceptability concerning an aspect of our lives that’s always coming to terms with thought police both to the right and left of us, the word “sexuality” takes hold; yet in doing so it starts to pose a problem for the most brilliant and advanced thinkers about gender. It suggests that there is an aspect of our makeup that’s genuine, authentic, something at the least more our own than the aspects of ourselves that we can and do perform.

对福柯而言，这种被称为“性”的东西——它本身具有一种不可侵犯的真实性，这在他的著作中也令人惊讶——类似于渴望和体验到的身体愉悦。然而，福柯的社会批判坚持认为，这种愉悦总是由围绕它的一系列因素所调控的，这些因素非常复杂，或许在我们即将讨论的这段文字（1804）中阐述得最为透彻。他正在讨论他所谓的“联盟的部署”和他所谓的“性欲的部署”之间的差异和交集。我想引用这段文字，然后简要地评论一下：“简而言之，”他开篇说道，“联盟的部署与社会机体的稳态相协调。”这里所说的联盟的部署——为了明确其定义——是指在特定文化中识别核心生殖单元的方式；通常情况下，这个核心生殖单元是“家庭”，尽管家庭的性质和结构会发生变化。人们对家庭的看法，以及家庭中应该发生和应该避免的活动——例如，大多数文化中都不允许乱伦以及可能导致乱伦的情况——都受到各种话语体系的束缚，这些话语体系传递着各种形式的“知识”，使得某种特定的联盟模式看起来自然而然，尽管这种模式实际上是由法律和限制构建并牢牢维系的。另一方面，我们所理解的“性行为的运用”是指人们谈论性行为的方式，以及通过这种方式鼓励或阻止性行为：它未必是由任何国家机器或实际的法律体系所决定，但却仍然受到各种观点的普遍性和影响力的影响——正如我所说，它被人们谈论。继续这段话：

For Foucault, this thing called sexuality—which has in itself an inviolable authenticity that comes as a surprise in his work, too—is something like desired and experienced bodily pleasure. Foucault’s social critique insists, however, that this pleasure is always orchestrated by a set of factors that surrounds it, a very complicated set of factors that is articulated perhaps best in the passage to which we turn (1804). He’s talking about the difference and the intersection between what he calls the “deployment of alliance” and what he calls the “deployment of sexuality.” I want to quote this passage and then comment on it briefly: “In a word,” he begins by saying, “the deployment of alliance is attuned to a homeostasis of the social body.” The deployment of alliance here—just to get that defined—is the way that in a given culture the nuclear reproductive unit is identified; typically this is the “family,” though the family changes in its nature and structure. The way the family is viewed, the sorts of activities that are supposed to take place and be avoided in the family—incest and the conditions that could threaten incest, for example, should not take place in most cultures—are surrounded by veins of discourse conveying all the forms of “knowledge” that make a given deployment of alliance seem natural even though it is constructed and kept securely in place by laws and restrictions.
