On the other hand, “the deployment of sexuality” we understand to be the way sexuality is talked about and by that means encouraged or discouraged: not dictated by any state apparatus or actual legal system, necessarily, but dictated nonetheless—talked about, as I say—simply by the prevalence and force of various sorts of opinion. To continue the passage:

总之，联盟的部署与社会机体的稳态（或称规范化；这正是他所说的“稳态”）相契合，其功能在于维持这种稳态；由此，联盟与法律有着特殊的联系（也就是说，法律反映了当前社会对家庭的认知——例如，家庭并非指已婚的同性伴侣及其子女）；也由此，联盟的重要阶段在于“再生产”。性行为的部署并非为了自我再生产，而是为了以日益精细的方式增殖、创新、吞并、创造和渗透各个群体，并以日益全面的方式控制人口。
In a word, the deployment of alliance is attuned to a homeostasis [or a regularization; that’s what he means by “homeostasis”] of the social body, which it has the function of maintaining; whence its privileged link with the law [that is, the law reflects current social assumptions about the family—that the family is not a married gay couple with children, for example]; whence too the fact that the important phase for it is “reproduction.” The deployment of sexuality has its reason for being, not in reproducing itself, but in proliferating, innovating, annexing, creating, and penetrating bodies in an increasingly detailed way, and in controlling populations in an increasingly comprehensive way.

值得注意的是，性行为的运用（这本身并非坏事——这些运用大多并非旨在控制结果）如果能容纳节育或同性恋，无疑会成为限制生育的一种手段。仅就这一点而言，性行为的运用就会与联盟的运用产生或隐晦或明显的冲突（“马尔萨斯式伴侣”的情况除外，我稍后会再谈到）。福柯的术语表明，在大多数（但并非所有）文化或社会生物系统中，联盟的运用（安排、制度化）是为了促进和确保生育，而性行为，无疑会受到自身舆论潮流的影响（无论好坏），其运用是为了分配快乐，并受相关社群的认可或反对。因此，在任何文化中，联盟和性行为各自的运用之间都可能存在某种程度的冲突。

Notice that a deployment of sexuality, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing—these deployments aren’t for the most part meant to police outcomes—that accommodated birth control or homosexuality would certainly be a means of curtailing reproduction. Just in that degree, the deployment of sexuality would then come to be, subtly or not so subtly, at odds with the deployment of alliance (except in the case of “the Malthusian couple,” to which I shall return eventually). It is just given in Foucault’s terminology that alliance in most though not all cultures or sociobiological systems is deployed (arranged, institutionalized) to further and ensure reproduction, whereas sexuality, shaped undoubtedly by its own circulating currents of opinion for better or worse, is deployed for the distribution of pleasure, subject to the approval or disapproval of interested communities. There is likely, then, to be some measure of conflict between the respective deployments of alliance and sexuality in any culture.

然而，无论如何，在福柯和巴特勒的理论体系中，性欲的概念始终令我们难以捉摸，因为作为不可侵犯的真我，性欲无法通过与任何其他概念的二元关系来理解。在巴特勒的理论中，性欲渗透于表演之中，因此它在任何意义上都不是表演的对立面，也不是表演的“他者”；而在福柯的理论中，性欲与联盟的重叠过于广泛，以至于不能被视为联盟的“他者”。它以一种其他事物都无法企及的方式存在着。我们将继续思考这个问题。

In any case, however, in Foucault’s scheme as much as in Butler’s, the concept of sexuality continues to elude us because, as the inviolably authentic, sexuality can’t be known in a binary relation to another concept. It permeates performance in Butler, hence is not in any sense the opposite of, or “other” in respect to, performance; and in Foucault it overlaps with alliance too extensively to be seen as the “other” of alliance. It is somehow just there in a way that nothing else is. We’ll keep wondering about this.

回到我们上次讨论萨义德时提到的福柯：福柯的核心思想，也是他在三卷性史著作中不断阐述的思想，是“权力”的概念。这种权力并非通过法律、警察或国家机器公开强制执行的权力，而是以一种更为隐蔽的方式，通过“知识”的传播或扩散来强制执行。这种知识本质上是话语性的，它以某种方式将自身的规范强加于我们所有人，无论好坏。话语既可以揭示或构成抵抗的阵地，也可以使我们趋于顺从；就我们当前的主题而言，它既可以促进性，也可以抑制性。福柯将这种权力形式称为“权力-知识”（有时会加上连字符）。现在，我将再次回到“权力-知识”这个概念，因为它贯穿并引导我们理解福柯的整部著作。让我再次提醒各位，即便某些话语具有进步性，意味着它们比压制性话语更具自省意识、更审慎、更理性（顺便一提，你不必认同这一点也能接受本文的论证结构），福柯也始终竭力避免将某种特定的知识形式等同于真理——尽管他常常愤慨地将某种知识形式称为“真理体制”。权力知识塑造了我们的存在方式，或者至少塑造了我们自认为的存在方式——用巴特勒的话来说，就是我们“表演”自身的方式——但它始终无法摆脱意见的范畴。

To return to what we said about Foucault in discussing Said last time: Foucault’s central idea, the idea he continues to develop throughout his three volumes on the history of sexuality, is the idea of “power” as something other than the power that is openly enforced through legal, police, or state apparatus measures. This kind of power is enforced in its own way, but more insidiously, as the circulation or distribution of “knowledge,” which is discursive in nature and imposes its norms on all of us, for better or for worse. Discourse can reveal or constitute sites of resistance as well as reduce us to conformity, and with respect to our present theme it can either promote or inhibit sexuality. Foucault calls this form of power, sometimes hyphenating it, “power-knowledge.” I return to power-knowledge now as the concept that governs—and guides you through—the whole text of Foucault. Let me remind you again that even though certain discourses are progressive, with the implication that they are more self-conscious, considered, and reasonable than repressive discourses (you don’t have to agree with this, by the way, to accept the structure of the argument), Foucault is at pains never to align a particular form of knowledge with truth—though he often bitterly calls this or that form a “regime of truth.” Power-knowledge conditions the way we are or at least the way we think we are—the way we “perform” ourselves, in Butler’s parlance—but it never escapes the domain of opinion.

因此，就我们提出的问题——“性是什么？”——而言，福柯的回答相当含糊其辞。他谈论性，撰写了一部三卷本的性史，但他并没有谈论性本身，无论“本身”在此语境下意味着什么。他谈论的是性的运用，权力知识如何建构性，如何使性为我们所用，如何使性成为一种例行性的力比多表达，却始终不让我们触及我们一直在追寻的本质：性的本质。它依然迷失在权力的洪流之中。

Hence in relation to our question—What is sexuality?—Foucault is being quite coy. He’s talking about sexuality, he’s writing a three-volume history of it, but he’s not talking about it in itself, whatever “in itself” might mean in this case. He’s talking about the deployment of sexuality, the way power-knowledge constructs it, makes it available to us, makes it a routine performance of libidinal expression, yet without allowing us to stumble upon the essence we continue to seek: the nature of sexuality. It continues to be lost among the vectors of power.

顺便一提，同性婚姻问题巧妙地处于联盟关系和性取向的交汇点。虽然许多同性恋维权人士支持同性婚姻，将其视为一项至关重要的政治事业，但也有人认为同性恋生活的制度化是资产阶级对他们身份的重新定义和正常化。他们认为这是将联盟关系强加于性取向之上，反映了我之前所描述的这两种关系之间的张力。如果性取向真的只是在寻找表达自身的方式，在看似支持性的关系中寻求支持，在看似带有约束性的关系中抵制，那么它似乎对联盟关系并不特别感兴趣。简而言之，同性恋反对同性婚姻就是反对婚姻本身，是倡导过去所谓的自由恋爱——或者更准确地说（也许更准确），自由性取向。或许，我们可以从中观察到，由于对性取向的本质持续感到困惑，我们陷入了一种迷思的冲突之中。无论是像雪莱这样的诗人笔下的自由恋爱，还是20世纪60年代的某种“生活方式”，在我们看来都像是水瓶座式的天真，对此我们唯一能做的回应就是那首流行歌曲《爱情与它有何干系？》。然而，另一方面，自由的性行为却总是让我们感到困惑。

The issue of gay marriage is situated very interestingly, by the way, between the deployment of alliance and the deployment of sexuality. While a great many gay activists support gay marriage as a crucial political cause, there are others who see this institutionalization of gay life as a bourgeois redefinition and normalization of who they are. They see it as the imposition of alliance on sexuality that reflects what I earlier described as the tension between these deployments. If sexuality is really just looking around for ways to get itself expressed, taking advantage of deployment where it seems supportive and trying to resist deployment where it seems more like policing, then it would appear not to be particularly interested in alliance. Simply put, gay opposition to gay marriage is opposition to marriage as such, an advocacy of what used to be called free love—or better (perhaps), free sexuality. Perhaps here, then, we can observe, frustrated by continuing to wonder what sexuality actually is, a conflict of mystifications. Free love, whether in a poet like Shelley or as a 1960s “lifestyle,” seems to us an Aquarian naivety to which the only possible response is the pop song “What’s Love Got to Do with It?” Yet free sexuality, on the other hand, ever and anon, leaves us merely confused.

在阅读巴特勒的著作时，我们必须承认，提出“什么是性？”这个问题本身就是一个错误的开端。我们需要审视巴特勒的论证，看看我们之前对性可能包含的哪些方面被排除在外。我们原本以为这个问题很单纯，但很快就会发现，在巴特勒的理论中，你根本无法成为某种特定的性，当然也无法声称自己是某种特定的性。正如我们将看到的，你可以通过重复、模仿和戏仿（例如反串）来表演某种身份。你可以通过这些方式表演身份，但你无法完全表演性，正是因为巴特勒的思想中始终坦率地探讨着一种精神上的过剩因素。巴特勒的著作，尽管其解构之有力，却并非仅仅关乎“身份的建构”，也并非仅仅关乎表演的领域。它承认，在表演之外，存在着某种难以把握和表达的东西。承认这种超越表演的东西，其主要目的在于解释我们为何要进行表演。如果我们的行为并非为了达成尚未实现的目标，那我们又何必费心呢？然而，巴特勒在探讨无意识问题时，始终清晰地表明，除了行为本身，或者说行为本身无法完全涵盖某些东西。

In reading Butler, we need to admit that to ask the question “what is sexuality?” is, well, something of a false start. We need to see how much of what we thought sexuality might be is excluded from Butler’s argument. We thought our question was an innocent one, but we quickly see that in Butler you simply can’t be a certain sexuality and certainly can’t lay claim to being one. You can perform an identity, as we’ll see, by repeating, by imitating, and by parodying this identity in drag. You can perform an identity in these ways, but you can’t wholly perform sexuality precisely because of the element of psychic excess to which her thinking continues very candidly to return. Butler’s work, for all the powerful sweep of its demystifications, is not just about “the construction of identity,” not just about the domain of performance. It acknowledges that there is something beyond performance that is very difficult to grasp and articulate. The main reason for acknowledging this something beyond is to explain why it is that we perform at all. Why would we bother if our performance were not an effort to achieve a goal we haven’t reached? It’s nevertheless always clear in Butler, as she returns to the question of the unconscious in particular, that there is something in excess of, or not fully to be encompassed by, ideas of performance.

假设我们一开始就走错了方向。我们问了一个无法回答的问题，但与此同时，我们也学到了一些东西。我们了解到，无论性是什么，它都比我们所扮演的身份更加灵活，在某种意义上也更加真实：性比意识更接近力比多驱力。因此，无论性在无意识中扮演什么角色，它始终游离于任何社会编码之外：例如，福柯在谈到“部署的联盟”或“部署的性”时所指的那种编码，以及巴特勒反复提及的“性别化”的那种编码。

So let’s say we’ve made a false start. We’ve asked a question we can’t answer, but at the same time we have learned certain things. We’ve learned that sexuality, whatever it may be, is more flexible and also in some sense more authentic than the identities we perform: sexuality is closer to libidinal drives than consciousness can be. Whatever role sexuality may play in the unconscious, then, it always stands outside any kind of social coding: the sort of coding, for example, that Foucault would indicate in speaking of deployed alliance or deployed sexuality and the sort of coding that Butler refers to repeatedly as “gendering.”

然而，对他们二人而言——这也是我们所学到的另一点——即便从运用或与性别和表演相关的表达方式来看待性，其本质上也是话语性的。它源于语言或符号结构，福柯将其理解为流通的知识，而巴特勒则再次将其理解为表演。福柯将性视为权力知识的产物，权力即知识。巴特勒则将其视为表演的产物——就其可见性而言，也就是说，就其被付诸行动而言。

Still, for both of them—and this is the other thing we’ve learned—even sexuality as viewed through deployment, or through the way it can get expressed in relation to gender and performance, is fundamentally discursive. It arises out of linguistic or semiotic formations, formations that Foucault understands as circulated knowledge and that Butler understands, again, as performance. Foucault sees sexuality as the effect of power-knowledge, power as knowledge. Butler sees it as the effect—insofar as it’s visible, that is, insofar as it is acted out—of performance.

为了探讨人们可能认为的真实自我与表演的自我（即人们为成为自我而进行的姿态性探索）之间的关系，让我们来看巴特勒1711年文章中最具争议的一句话：“自从十六岁起，我就一直是女同性恋。” 请记住，在文章开头，她就明确表示，她写作此文的目的在于对性别研究进行政治化的介入，这种介入以对本体论、对“存在”的哲学反思的形式展开。换句话说，她问道，“成为某种东西”究竟是什么？她在这句话中——这句话刻意显得有些别扭——“我一直都是女同性恋”，意在向我们指出，“成为某种东西”与“成为”某种东西是截然不同的。

In order to confront the relationship between what one might suppose to be authentic selfhood and that which is performed, that which is one’s gestural quest to become a self, let’s take one of the most provocative sentences in Butler’s essay (1711): “Since I was sixteen, being a lesbian is what I’ve been.” Now remember that at the very beginning of the essay, she says her whole purpose is to register a politicized intervention in gender studies that takes the form of a philosophical reflection on ontology, on “being.” What is it, in other words, she says, to be something? What she’s doing in this sentence, which is a deliberately awkward-seeming sentence, “[B]eing a lesbian is what I’ve been,” is pointing out to us that to be something is very different from to be “being” something.

例如，我可以说我很忙，并期望你认为我真的非常忙。但你可能还是会说，怀疑我其实并不忙，“哦，他只是在装忙。”换句话说，我是在表演忙碌。我到处装忙，让你觉得这个游手好闲、爱管闲事的人其实在做事。这就是表演忙碌。但巴特勒提出的观点很有意思：本体论领域应该关注事物的简单存在，在哲学中，它总是与能动性、与行动的表演相对立。但巴特勒谈到她的性取向时——这也是她为什么对这个问题的本体论层面感兴趣的原因——是，表演性的因素实际上已经渗透到本体论中。她说，甚至存在本身，在某种程度上也是我们表演出来的。因此，句子中出现了两个“being”一词：“自从我十六岁以来，我就一直是女同性恋。”

For example, I can say I’m busy and expect you to suppose that I really and truly am busy. But you might say anyway, suspecting that I’m not really busy, “Oh, he’s being busy.” In other words, I’m performing busy-ness. I’m going around being busy, imposing on you the notion that this layabout, this potherer, is actually accomplishing something. That’s the performance of being busy. But here’s the interesting point that Butler is making: the ontological realm is supposed to concern the simple being or existence of things, and in philosophy it’s always contrasted with agency, with the performance of actions. But what Butler is saying about her sexuality—and that’s why she says that she takes an interest in the ontological aspect of the question—is that an element of the performative actually creeps into the ontological. Even being, she says, is something that in some measure we perform. Hence the doubling up of the word “being” in the sentence, “Since I was sixteen, being a lesbian is what I’ve been.”

从某种意义上说，是的，她就是个女同性恋。但从另一个意义上说，她一直以来都是个女同性恋，公开自己的身份，扮演着一个只要表演得连贯一致——正如她在讨论异性恋表演时所说的“重复”——就能被理解的角色，就像所有角色一样。所以她才会那样写这句话。如果你在书页边缘做了个大标记，以为找到了她真正表明自己是某种身份，而不仅仅是被建构成某种身份的地方，我想你会发现她已经巧妙地躲过了你的追查。她刻意地游走于本体论意义上的真实性和她自己对本体论的创新理解之间，后者认为本体论属于表演的范畴，或者至少无法将其与表演割裂开来。她其实并不想明确地站在任何一方，因为对她而言——这也是我最欣赏她作品的地方，尽管它或许也是最令人沮丧的地方——她坦率地窥见了社会批判逻辑之外的真相，而这真相仍然充满神秘。她对此有很多话要说，但她并不认为自己已经穷尽了所有“主题”。

In one sense, yes, she just is a lesbian. But in another sense, she has been being one, outing herself as one, taking up a role that can be understood, as all roles can, readily enough as long as they are performed with coherence—“repeated,” as she puts it in discussing the performance of heterosexuality. So that’s why she puts the sentence that way, and if you made a big mark in the margin and thought you had found the place where she says she really is something, not just constructed as something, I think you’ll see that she has eluded your capture. She deliberately remains on the fence between the sense of the ontological as authentic and her own innovative sense of the ontological as belonging within the realm of, or at least impossible to factor apart from, performance. She really doesn’t want to come down squarely on either side of the fence because for her—and this is what I like best about her work, even though it’s perhaps the most frustrating thing about it—what she candidly glimpses beyond the logic of her social critique remains mysterious. She has a great deal to say about it, but she’s not pretending that she has exhausted the “subject.”

暂且抛开这些神秘因素，至少目前来看，福柯和巴特勒拥有共同的政治诉求似乎显而易见。福柯是一位同性恋作家，在撰写《性史》后期时，他正因艾滋病去世；巴特勒是一位女同性恋作家。他们都十分关注自身边缘化性别角色的政治意义，同时在理论上也对此有着深刻的理解。正如我们经常看到的那样，他们作品中出现的任何冲突，都是理论与实践之间的冲突。他们共同的政治诉求旨在通过否定特权性别角色的真实性（或者用巴特勒的话来说，否定其“原创性”）来动摇异性恋规范。巴特勒问道：谁说异性恋是先于异性恋出现的？福柯也问道：谁说某种文化的性安排是自然而然的？这些正是巴特勒和福柯共同提出的问题，这些政治化的问题。

To set this element of mystery aside, then, at least for now, it seems plain that Foucault and Butler have a common political agenda. Foucault is a gay writer who was dying of AIDS in the later stages of writing The History of Sexuality; Butler is a lesbian writer. Both of them care greatly about the political implications of their marginalized gender roles, while at the same time they are theoretically very sophisticated about them. As so often, any conflict that arises in their work is the conflict we have often noticed between theory and practice. Their common political agenda is aimed at destabilizing the heteronormative by denying the authenticity, or in Butler’s parlance “originality,” of privileged gender roles. Who says heterosexuality came first? Butler asks. Who says a given culture’s sexual arrangements are natural? Foucault asks. These are the sorts of questions, the politicized questions, that Butler and Foucault raise in common.

在我看来，福柯和巴特勒的观点非常接近。但让我们先停下来，看看他们似乎存在分歧的地方。你可能已经注意到，巴特勒的文本在脚注中提到了福柯的作品。巴特勒指出，参议员杰西·赫尔姆斯在抨击罗伯特·梅普尔索普的摄影作品时，虽然谴责了男性同性恋，却完全忽略了女性同性恋，因为他的长篇大论对女性同性恋只字未提。巴特勒认为，被宣布不存在或被默默禁止，比被宣布为异类还要糟糕。她用以下论述来论证自己的观点（1712）： “被明确禁止，就占据了一个话语空间，从中可以提出类似反向话语的东西；而被默许禁止，甚至连被禁止的对象都算不上。”

So it seems to me that Foucault and Butler are very closely in agreement. But let us pause briefly at the moment when they seem not to agree. You’ve probably noticed that one text, Butler’s, refers to the other author’s work in a footnote. Butler notes that the senator Jesse Helms, in having deplored male homosexuality when attacking the photography of Robert Mapplethorpe, simply erases female homosexuality because his diatribe pays no attention to it. It’s even worse, she says, to be declared nonexistent or silently outlawed than to be declared deviant. She justifies this position by saying (1712): “To be prohibited explicitly is to occupy a discursive site from which something like a reverse-discourse can be articulated; to be implicitly proscribed is not even to qualify as an object of prohibition.”

这里她引用了福柯的脚注（1712n15）：“福柯在其权力分析中，大多未能考虑到这种特殊的抹除伎俩。” 巴特勒由此论证，用福柯的术语来说，身份的产生必须以话语为基础。赫尔姆斯仅仅通过省略来拒绝“女同性恋”这一范畴——当然，顺便一提，我们知道这仅仅是或多或少出于疏忽的省略——换句话说，赫尔姆斯对这一范畴的拒绝，就是对话语的抹除。没有话语，就没有身份。巴特勒的脚注暗示了福柯的立场蕴含着这样的含义，这似乎与我们之前对福柯的论述相符。话语创造权力知识。权力知识创造身份。因此，没有讨论，就没有身份认同；而由于赫尔姆斯拒绝就女同性恋进行讨论，从而抹杀了女同性恋这一群体，由此必然得出女同性恋这一类别不存在的结论。脚注继续：

Here’s where she gives us the footnote on Foucault (1712n15): “It is this particular ruse of erasure which Foucault for the most part fails to take account of in his analysis of power.” Butler thus argues that in Foucauldian terms, there’s got to be discourse for there to be identity. Helms’s refusal of the category of “lesbian” simply by omission—and of course we know, by the way, that this is a refusal only by more or less careless omission—Helms’s refusal of this category is, in other words, an erasure of discourse. No discourse, no identity. That is what Butler’s footnote suggests that Foucault’s position entails, and that would seem to make sense in relation to what we’ve said so far about Foucault. Discourse creates power-knowledge. Power-knowledge creates identity. Therefore, where there’s no discourse, there can be no identity, and because Helms has erased the lesbian by refusing discourse about it, it must follow that there is no such category as lesbian. To continue the footnote:

[福柯]几乎总是假定[我们必须尊重“几乎”这个词]权力是通过话语作为其工具而产生的，压迫与臣服和主体化联系在一起，也就是说，它被确立为主体身份的形成原则。
[Foucault] almost always presumes [and we must honor that word “almost”] that power takes place through discourse as its instrument, and that oppression is linked with subjection and subjectivization, that is, that it is installed as the formative principle of the identity of subjects.

然而，为了捍卫福柯的观点，我们应该转向一段引人入胜的文字，这段文字在很多方面都值得关注，尤其是在它预先驳斥了巴特勒在此提出的观点方面。这段文字篇幅较长，但值得一读（1632）：

In defense of Foucault, however, we should turn to a passage that’s fascinating on a number of grounds but especially as a denial in advance of what Butler says here. It’s rather long but worth hearing (1632):

例如，想想曾经被视为“最大的”违背自然之罪——鸡奸的历史。关于鸡奸——这个极其混乱的范畴——的文本极其谨慎，而且人们几乎普遍对此讳莫如深，这使得双重操作成为可能。
Consider for example the history of what was once “the” great sin against nature. The extreme discretion of the texts dealing with sodomy—that utterly confused category—and the nearly universal reticence in talking about it made possible a twofold operation.

福柯在这段文字的开头就指出，在某个时期，同性恋身份（被理解为鸡奸）是一个已知的范畴，但对此保持沉默（巴特勒代表女同性恋者所抱怨的正是这一点）却导致了两件事。他接着会说，鸡奸在当时是受到法律严惩的；但与此同时，他又说，几乎没有人谈论鸡奸。正如你所知，在但丁的作品中，你不会看到对鸡奸的沉默，但在那个时期，大多数人对此避而不谈。因此，法律迫害它，却无人谈论它。这似乎违背了福柯自己关于话语构成身份的前提，同时也明显与巴特勒关于福柯认为话语总是构成身份的论断相矛盾。

We find Foucault saying as this passage opens that at a certain period, the homosexual identity, understood as sodomy, was a known category, but that silence about it (the object of Butler’s complaint on behalf of the lesbian) made two things possible. He’ll go on to say that sodomy was punishable in the extreme by law; but in the meantime he’s saying there was no discourse about it, or almost none. You don’t get silence about sodomy in Dante, as I’m sure you know, but for the most part in this period nobody talks about it. So the law persecutes it, yet nobody talks about it. This would seem to violate Foucault’s own premise that discourse constitutes identity, but it also plainly does contradict Butler’s claim that in Foucault discourse always constitutes identity.

我们继续：

Let’s continue:

[T]人们几乎普遍对谈论此事保持沉默，这使得双重运作成为可能：一方面，刑罚极其严厉（火刑一直持续到十八世纪，直到十八世纪中叶才出现实质性的抗议）[这里的论述也存在缺陷，因为它没有构成抵抗的场所，没有人抱怨这些严厉的刑罚，就像另一方面也没有人经常谈论它们一样]，另一方面，人们的容忍度必然很普遍（我们可以从司法判决的罕见性间接推断出来，也可以从一些关于军队或法庭中人们所认为存在的群体的陈述中更直接地窥见一斑）。
[T]he nearly universal reticence in talking about it made possible a twofold operation: on the one hand, there was an extreme severity (punishment by fire was meted out well into the eighteenth century, without there being any substantial protest expressed before the middle of the century) [Discourse is here failing also in that it’s not constituting a site of resistance, and nobody’s complaining about these severe punishments just as on the other hand nobody’s talking very much about them], and on the other hand, a tolerance that must have been widespread (which one can deduce indirectly from the infrequency of judicial sentences, and which one glimpses more directly through certain statements concerning societies of men that were thought to exist in the army or in the courts).

换句话说，存在一种身份认同，而这种身份认同并非——至少在很大程度上——由话语构成。随着阅读的深入，他会继续指出，某种程度上，同性恋者的困境在同性恋开始被公开讨论后反而加剧了，但他不会否认，在同性恋不被讨论之前，它就不是一个独立的类别。诚然，一旦同性恋成为一个话题，对同性恋的惩罚确实有所减轻，但对同性恋的监视——无论是通过心理治疗、神职人员，还是其他任何可能对此发表意见的人——都变得比之前更加普遍和确定。很难不将福柯的这种观点解读为：沉默虽然对少数人来说是危险的，但对大多数人来说却是一件好事。然而，话语或许能让少数人摆脱极度恐惧，却也对所有幸存者强加了一种霸权权威，并将他们塑造成权力知识所认定的存在状态，而非他们基于自身性取向而自发存在的状态。我们意识到，在这样的时刻，我们便能理解为何福柯认为权力知识即便在其最不具强制性的层面也令人沮丧。

In other words, there was an identity and that identity was not—at least not very much— constituted by discourse. As you read further along, he’ll go on to say that in a way the plight of the homosexual got worse when homosexuality started being talked about, but he will not say that homosexuality was not a category when it was not discussed. Yes, penalties for being homosexual were less severe once it became a topic, but the surveillance of homosexuality—the way it could be attended to by therapy, by the clergy, and by everyone else who might have something to say about it—became far more pervasive and determinate than it was when there was no discourse about it. It’s hard not to interpret Foucault as saying here that silence was, while perilous to the few, a good thing for the many; whereas discourse, which perhaps relieves the few of extreme fear, nevertheless imposes a kind of hegemonic authority on all that remain and constitutes them as something that power-knowledge believes them to be, rather than something that in any sense, according to their sexuality, they spontaneously are. It occurs to us that in a moment of this kind, we can see why Foucault finds power-knowledge even at its least coercive depressing.

沉默抹去了对某一范畴的认知，却抹去了它的存在。因此，在我看来，巴特勒与福柯的分歧其实早已被福柯预先解答，而且即便在这一点上，仔细想想，他们的观点其实是一致的。女同性恋者或许会因为被杰西·赫尔姆斯忽略而感到委屈，但她也因此逃脱了他的怒火。福柯的立场比巴特勒认为的要灵活得多，但这仅仅意味着它与巴特勒的立场相似。正如我所说，他们的观点仍然非常接近。

Silence then erases the knowledge of a category but not its existence. It seems to me, then, that Butler’s disagreement with Foucault is answered in advance by Foucault and that even there, when you think about it, they’re really in agreement with each other. The lesbian may feel slighted in being passed over by Jesse Helms, but she has also escaped his wrath. Foucault’s position is more flexible than Butler takes it to be, but that just means that it’s similar to her own. They remain, as I’ve said, very close to each other’s viewpoint.

然而，在方法上，他们略有不同。福柯更倾向于历史研究。历史学家常常批评他未能给出令人信服的历史解释，因为他从未阐明历史是如何从一个时刻过渡到下一个时刻的。他谈论的是不同的历史时刻，但他将这些时刻视为知识的载体或结构——他有时称之为“认知时刻”。这些时刻随后神秘地转化为新的、不同的时刻。历史学家所要求的因果关系在福柯的论证中往往被忽略。然而，他仍然关注态度随时间推移而发生的变化，而《性史》中的论述也主要集中于这些变化本身。

In method, however, they are somewhat different. Foucault is a more historical writer. Historians often criticize him for not giving acceptable historical explanations because he never shows how you get from one moment in history to the next. He talks about differing moments in history, but he sees them in terms of bodies or structures of knowledge—“epistemic moments,” as he sometimes says. These moments then are mysteriously transformed into new and different moments. The kind of causality the historian requires tends in Foucault’s arguments to be left out. He remains concerned, however, with the way in which attitudes change over time, and it’s the changes in themselves that his argument in The History of Sexuality tends to concentrate on.

为此，他按时间顺序指出了态度结构的演变。例如，从十九世纪初到今天，有四种类型的人受到密切关注，权力与知识围绕着他们展开。他将它们描述为歇斯底里的女性、手淫的儿童、马尔萨斯夫妇以及变态的成年人——即各种类型的同性恋者（参见1634）。福柯所说的“马尔萨斯夫妇”指的是那些根据十九世纪早期政治经济学家托马斯·马尔萨斯的理论而被要求不要过度生育的夫妇，因为经济无法承受过多的生育。这是一种利用联盟来操纵和控制生育的方式，从而创造了一种联盟的运用与性行为的运用出人意料地相互关联的局面，因为显然节育和同性恋行为也都在控制生育。正如你所看到的，这两种部署方式之间并不总是存在冲突——而且无论如何，应该补充的是，性行为的部署——比如当人们“根本不在乎”的时候——很可能会采取增加生育的形式。

To this end, he pinpoints successive structures of attitude temporally. At the start of the nineteenth century and continuing to the present, for example, there are four intensely scrutinized human types around which power-knowledge busies itself. He describes them as the hysterical woman, the masturbating child, the Malthusian couple, and the perverse adult—meaning the homosexual of whatever kind (cf. 1634). By “the Malthusian couple” Foucault means the couple that is enjoined, according to the precepts of the early nineteenth-century political economist Thomas Malthus, not to reproduce too much because the economy won’t stand for it. This is a way of deploying alliance to manipulate and control reproduction, creating a moment in which the deployment of alliance and the deployment of sexuality are surprisingly in league with each other, as obviously birth control and homosexual practices also control reproduction. As you see, it’s not always a question of conflict between these two forms of deployment—and it should be added, in any case, that the deployment of sexuality for its part—as when people “just don’t care”—may very well take forms that increase reproduction.

因此，从十九世纪到近代，这四种问题类型一直是心理治疗、神职人员、家庭或父母建议以及其他各种权力知识传播途径关注的焦点。一旦人们开始怀疑歇斯底里的女性的全部存在就是她的性欲，并从她的子宫（癔症）向外散发，这种状态就很难与家庭天使的形象相符，她就被认定为歇斯底里。手淫的儿童违背了受洗儿童洗净罪孽的宗教教义，也挑战了始于十九世纪之交的关于天真无邪的自然儿童的浪漫崇拜。由于这些以及其他原因，这样的孩子引起了人们的极大恐慌，并受到严密的监视和约束。权力知识宣称手淫会导致阳痿、发育迟缓和早逝——所有这些观点在二十世纪很长一段时间内都主导着儿科文献。

These four problematic types, then, are the focus of attention from the nineteenth century to recent times for psychological therapy, the clergy, family or parental advice, and all the other ways that power-knowledge circulates. The hysterical woman is identified as hysterical once it begins to be suspected that her whole being is her sexuality, emanating outward from her womb (hysteron), a state of things that’s scarcely suitable for the angel of the house. The masturbating child violates the religious doctrine that baptized children are washed clean of sin and challenges, too, the romantic cult of the innocent child of nature that begins at the turn of the nineteenth century. For this and other reasons, this child is a cause of deep alarm and is subject to extreme surveillance and restraint. Power-knowledge declared that masturbation led to impotence, stunted growth, and early death—all opinions that dominated pediatric literature until well into the twentieth century.

马尔萨斯夫妇的理论主要源于十九世纪初的“政治经济学”，但在我们推动全球节育的进步运动中却占据了主导地位。“我们必须控制人口”这种观点或许反映了我们不得不接受的严峻现实，但这种观点最早出自马尔萨斯之口。马尔萨斯希望为了家庭自身的经济利益，像今天中国那样对生育进行管控。福柯就此向他的读者提出了质疑，因为我们这些自由主义者总是急于认为任何形式的霸权都不会得到我们的认可，但这种以权力-知识为中心的理念——尽管不像在中国那样受到严格支持——却是世俗自由主义根深蒂固的一部分。对于身处名义上天主教国家的福柯来说，这一点或许比我们更容易理解。

The Malthusian couple was primarily an offshoot of “political economy” in the early nineteenth century but has prevailed in our progressive campaign promoting birth control around the world. “We must control population” is a sentiment that may well reflect grim necessities to which we find ourselves assenting, but it’s said first in Malthus, who wanted, in the economic interests of families themselves, to police reproduction the way it is policed in China today. Foucault challenges his sympathetic reader on this score, because we liberals eagerly suppose that no form of hegemony would meet with our approval, but this particular focus of power-knowledge, less rigorously endorsed than it is in China, is an ingrained part of secular liberalism. This may have been clearer to Foucault in a nominally Catholic country than it is to us.

最后，正如我之前引用的段落所暗示的那样，关于“性变态的成年人”这一概念最早在十九世纪被公开讨论，当然，时至今日，它仍然被广泛讨论，讨论者往往类似于伍尔夫笔下的女性问题专家和萨义德笔下的东方学家。但如今，“性变态的成年人”也通过蓬勃发展的文学和新闻报道，拥有了属于自己的话语权和论述空间。尽管“性变态的成年人”已然成为主流话语的一部分，但仍然会遭遇争议，并且至少会受到法律和神学禁令的残余影响，因为围绕这一主题，相互冲突的“真理体系”毫不掩饰地并存。

And finally, the perverse adult is first openly discussed in the nineteenth century, as the earlier passage that I quoted suggested, and is still of course widely discussed today, quite often by the equivalent of Woolf’s male experts on women and Said’s Orientalists. But the perverse adult now also has a voice and discourses in his or her own right through a flourishing literature and journalism. The perverse adult is very much in the mainstream of discourse, yet still encounters controversy and at least the remnants of legal and theological prohibition because conflicting “regimes of truth” on this topic quite unashamedly and vocally coexist.

因此，这类观察构成了福柯的历史研究项目，即他关于性“历史”的研究。另一方面，正如你从巴特勒的风格中可以感受到的（我相信你从中能像在巴巴那里一样，认出很多德里达的影子），她关注的是将这些相同的问题更多地导向欧陆哲学传统。我已经提到过，她将你读过的那篇文章理解为对“本体论”（存在哲学）这一哲学分支的贡献。她的基本思路，即源于黑格尔的辩证思维反转，我希望你现在已经熟悉，甚至可能有所预见。

Observations of this sort, then, are what constitute for Foucault a historical project, that of his “history” of sexuality. For Butler, on the other hand, as you can tell from her style, in which I’m sure you recognize a lot of Derrida as you did in Bhabha, it’s a question of taking these same issues and orienting them more toward the Continental tradition of philosophy. I’ve already remarked that she understands the essay you’ve read as a contribution to that branch of philosophy called “ontology,” the philosophy of being. Her basic move, the dialectical inversion of thought that derives from Hegel, is something that I hope by this time you’ve become familiar with and perhaps even anticipate.

对我们而言，或许这类论证的开端是列维-斯特劳斯提出的各种区分。简单回顾一下：直觉上，生的先于熟的，正如简单的时间顺序所表明的那样。然而，如果我们把生熟之间的关系理解为一种话语建构，我们就必须认识到，如果你谈论吃生胡萝卜，那么你肯定已经吃过或至少听说过熟胡萝卜。嗯，这就是巴特勒的论证。异性恋先于同性恋？异性恋是原始的性取向，而同性恋只是对它的模仿？显然不是。如果没有同性恋，谁会想到异性恋的概念，更遑论将其赋予“异性恋规范”的权力？如果你是地球上唯一拥有语言能力的人，你环顾四周，就像夏娃或另一个亚当那样，可能会说你是一个有性欲的存在，但你不会说你是异性恋或同性恋。这些概念彼此依存，它们是已知的、相互影响的实践，彼此否定。它们并不回避“谁先出现”的问题。在性方面，巴特勒的强烈假设是，两者都不是先出现的。它们始终同时存在于我们所认同的那种精神过剩之中。但在社会层面，认为异性恋是自然的，而同性恋是不自然的、次要的、衍生的、模仿异性恋的，这种观点本身就站不住脚，因为在概念上，二者密不可分。

For us, perhaps, the inaugural moves of this kind were the various distinctions made by Lévi-Strauss. Just to review: intuitively, the raw precedes the cooked, as indeed it does in simple chronology. Yet if we understand the relationship between the raw and the cooked to be a discursive formation, we have to recognize that if you talk about eating a raw carrot, you must have eaten or at least heard of a cooked carrot already. Well, this is the Butler move. The heterosexual precedes the homosexual? The heterosexual is the original sexuality and the homosexual is just an imitation of it? Obviously not. If there were no homosexual, who would ever think of the concept of the heterosexual, much less empower the concept as the “heteronormative”? If you’re the only person on earth but endowed with language, you may say, looking around, as the case may be for Eve or for another Adam, that you are a sexual being, but you would not say that you’re either heterosexual or homosexual. The concepts depend on each other as known, differing practices that define each other negatively. They don’t beg the question which came first. In sexuality, the very strong supposition for Butler is that neither came first. They’re always already there together in that psychic excess with which we identify sexuality. But in social terms, the idea that what’s natural is the heterosexual and what’s unnatural, secondary, derivative, and imitative of the heterosexual is the homosexual is belied simply by the fact that you can’t have one conceptually without the other.

性别与变装亦是如此。变装戏仿、模仿、模仿性别，但其表演揭示的是，性别本身始终是一种表演。如果性别不是一种表演——一种反复出现、连贯一致，且包含着服装、姿态、步态和声音等所有标志性特征的表演——那么变装就无法模仿它。坚持认为我们需要表演自己的身份或许显得有损尊严，但至少作为表演者，我们都是技艺精湛的艺术家。此刻，我站在你们面前，展现着我的专业素养。我表演着白人身份、男性气质，以及所有这些特质，甚至更多。或许很难将我的表演完全聚焦于男性气质的表演，而非我表演的其他所有特质，但我的确也在表演男性气质，而想要模仿我的变装者也会专注于此。巴特勒认为，我对所有这些都感到不安，包括男性气质以及我所扮演的一切角色，因为如果我不继续扮演它们，我就会失去对它们的掌控。换句话说，我不断重复着我自认为的自我形象，而这同时也是我希望成为的自我形象。我大概并不自在，我也无法自然而然地融入我自认为的自我形象。我需要不断地扮演它。我持续不断的自我构建同时产生了两种效果。它如其所愿地稳定了我的身份认同，但同时，它也暴露了我对自身身份认同的焦虑，因为我必须不断重复它才能维持下去。从某种意义上说，我成了自己的拖累。

It’s the same thing with gender and drag. Drag parodies, mimics, and imitates gender, but what its performance reveals is that gender is always in and of itself, precisely, performance. If it weren’t performance, repeated and coherent as performance is, replete with all the signatures of clothing, posture, gait, and voice, it couldn’t be imitated by drag. It may seem demeaning to insist that we perform our identities, but at least as performers we’re all virtuosos. Here I am standing in front of you performing professionalism. I’m performing whiteness, masculinity, all those things and more. Perhaps it’s hard to focus on my performance in such a way that I’m exclusively performing masculinity as opposed to all the other things I’m performing, but I’m certainly performing masculinity, too, and the drag impersonator wishing to represent me would concentrate on that. I’m insecure about all of these things, Butler argues, about masculinity and everything else I perform, because I would lose possession of them if I did not keep performing them. In other words, I keep repeating what I suppose myself to be, which at the same time is what I hope I am. I’m not comfortable in my skin, presumably, and I don’t just relax into what I suppose myself to be. I perform it. My perpetual self-construction does two things at once. It stabilizes my identity, as it is meant to do, but at the same time it betrays my anxiety about my identity insofar as I must perpetually repeat it to keep it going. I am, in a sense, the drag of myself.

变装让我们注意到自身的表演。它一劳永逸地揭示了我们自以为是地扮演的性别角色背后，那些看似自然的性别范畴，如同我们穿着舒适的旧衣服一般，其本质究竟是什么。变装的一大特点就是摒弃了舒适的旧衣服，它提醒我们，我们称之为身份的这身“装扮”实际上有多么尴尬。

Drag brings our self-performance to our attention. It shows us once and for all what’s behind the seemingly natural categories of gender that we imagine ourselves to inhabit like a set of comfortable old clothes. Drag, one hallmark of which is its avoidance of comfortable old clothes, reminds us how awkward the self-apparel that we call our identity actually is.

你可能早就纳闷，这一切跟文学理论有什么关系。这很正常，但我希望你注意到巴特勒在文章结尾处提供了一个绝妙的文本应用，她说：“假设艾瑞莎在为我唱歌。”“你让我感觉”——不是像个自然的女人，因为根本不存在所谓的“自然”。“你让我感觉像个自然的女人”，这里的“你”大概是指某个异性恋规范的“他者”，向我展示了真正做女人是什么感觉。然而，假设“艾瑞莎在为我唱歌”。在这种情况下，“像”这个词就不再被强调了，因为此时的意思仅仅是“我”（“你”）让她感到身份认同的满足，仿佛她，一个女同性恋者，是自然的。或者假设她是在为一个变装皇后唱歌：只有变装的男人才能激发她内心深处自认为的自然之美。这无疑是一个借助文学理论来解读歌词的练习。

You have probably asked yourself for some time what any of this has to do with literary theory. Fair enough, but I hope you noticed that Butler offers a fabulous textual application at the end of her essay when she says, “Suppose Aretha is singing to me.” “You make me feel”—not a natural woman, because there’s no such thing as natural. “You make me feel like a natural woman,” “you” presumably being some heteronormative other who shows me what it really is to be a woman. Suppose, however, “Aretha is singing to me.” There’s no stress on “like” in this case because now the sense is just that I (“you”) make her feel fulfilled in her identity, as though she, a lesbian, were natural. Or suppose she is singing to a drag queen: only a man in drag can bring out what she feels to be natural in herself. This is surely an exercise in reading a song text that’s helped by literary theory.

写下这句话——“哲学家心情阴郁地在他的东方地毯上踱步”——时，我显然想到了弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《到灯塔去》中的拉姆齐先生。这句话写得很糟糕，我为此道歉。弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫绝不会写出这样的句子。但我们不妨用它来提醒自己，我们一直在做的是文学理论，一套不仅能帮助我们阅读，还能让我们以出人意料且有趣的方式阅读的规则。

In writing the following sentence—“The philosopher in a dark mood paced on his oriental rug”—I’m obviously thinking of Virginia Woolf’s Mr. Ramsay in To the Lighthouse. It’s a terrible sentence for which I apologize. Virginia Woolf never would have written it. But let’s just use it to remind ourselves that what we’ve been doing is literary theory, a set of protocols that not only helps us read but allows us to read with surprising and interesting results.

马克思主义批评家会关注“他的”，因为马克思主义对这句话的关键在于对某种商品的占有。非裔美国批评家则会关注那些以白色为代表的隐喻，坚持认为解读文学作品的一种方式是揭开白色作为明亮、阳光和中心的神秘面纱，而黑色，正如托妮·莫里森在她的文章中所暗示的那样，则代表着缺失或消极。阴郁的情绪是不好的，需要摒弃。对于后殖民主义批评家来说，问题不仅在于被剥夺的占有（例如马丘比丘的文物），还在于未加区分的商品：所谓“东方”，指的并非真正的东方，而是哈萨克、布哈拉或基里姆地毯。换句话说，概念本身缺乏具体性，暗示着话语的想象或意识中存在着被物化或客体的他者。

The Marxist critic would focus on “his” because the Marxist key to this sentence is the possession of a commodity. The African American critic would call attention to metaphors that are color-coded white, insisting that one of the ways literature needs to be read is through a demystification of white as bright, sunlit, and central, and black, as Toni Morrison suggests in her essay, an absence or negativity. A dark mood is bad and needs to be shunned. For the postcolonial critic, the problem is expropriated possession (like the Machu Picchu artifacts) but also undifferentiated commodity: by “Oriental” you don’t mean Oriental. You mean Kazakh or Bukhara or Kilim. In other words, the very lack of specificity in the concept suggests the reified or objectified other in the imagination or consciousness of the discourse.

最后，就性别理论而言，哲学家拉姆齐先生的男性化愤怒——你还记得他因为无法突破r而感到沮丧吗？他想达到s，却被r挡住了——这种男性化的愤怒掩盖了他柔弱的一面，以及那种在书房里摆放东方地毯的人物所特有的、鲜明的审美情趣。或许，他所表现的仅仅是那种柔弱的教授形象。我的地毯在楼上。

Finally, for gender theory, the masculine anger of the philosopher, Mr. Ramsay—you remember he is so frustrated because he can’t get past r; he wants to get to s, but he can’t get past r—the masculinized anger of the philosopher masks the effeteness, the pronounced aesthetic sensibility of somebody who keeps an Oriental rug in his study. Or maybe what’s being performed is just the effete professorial type. My rug’s upstairs.

 

 

第24章

CHAPTER 24

文学研究的制度建构
The Institutional Construction of Literary Study

阅读材料：

Readings:

Fish, Stanley.“如何识别一首诗。”载于《批评传统》，第 1023-1030 页。

Fish, Stanley. “How to Recognize a Poem When You See One.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1023–1030.

Guillory, John.“文化资本。”载于《批判传统》，第 1472-1483 页。

Guillory, John. “Cultural Capital.” In The Critical Tradition, pp. 1472–1483.

我们已经完成了一系列关于身份认同的理论探讨，始终关注——尽管近来常常是从旁观者的角度——文学中身份的建构方式。稍后我会回到文学这个有时看似缺失的环节。在此之前，我想指出一点，我相信即使我没有提及，你们也已经注意到了：那就是，每一种身份认同的探讨都包含两个章节。每个探讨都止步于第二章，而第二章则像是某种解构时刻，它指向理论本身，指向理论能够提供清晰明确的身份概念这一论断——在大多数情况下，这种身份概念是二元的，也就是第一章所探讨的。例如，在巴巴的理论中，我们发现了“混杂性”的概念，它通过双重意识或多元意识来瓦解文化二元对立。在这种意识中，人们同时体验到对国家机器的认同和颠覆它的意愿。由此产生的行为是“狡猾的礼貌”（或“象征意义”，或“变装”——这是性别理论中一个解构的时刻，此时性别不再被视为本质的东西，而是被视为一种表演）。

We’ve now completed a sequence of theoretical approaches to identity, always with a view—though rather often lately a view from afar—to the way identity is constructed in literature. I’ll return to what may have seemed at times the missing link, literature, in a minute. In the meantime, I just wanted to point out something I’m sure you’ve noticed even when I haven’t mentioned it: namely, that each of these approaches to identity has a history in two chapters. Each history arrives at a second chapter that is something like a deconstructive moment, signifying on theory itself, on the claim that theory can offer a clear and distinct concept of identity—in most cases a binary concept of identity, which is the first chapter. Just for example, we find in Bhabha the notion of hybridity as the undermining of cultural binaries through the double consciousness, or multiple consciousness, in which one experiences simultaneously a kind of identification with a state apparatus and a will to subvert it. The resulting behavior is “sly civility” (or “signifyin’,” or “drag”—the deconstructive moment in gender theory that comes when gender is no longer considered something essential but something performed).

顺便说一句，我可以给你举个亲身经历的例子，说明这种“狡猾的礼貌”是如何运作的，因为我身边的人就是它的受害者。在脱口秀和各种公共利益论坛上，他们会邀请一些人参加，并称他们为“教授”。表面上看，这是一个尊称，意味着被这样称呼的人是专家。也许在过去，这确实代表着尊重，也带有社会声望，因为教授过去往往是富裕阶层的后代，也就是所谓的“年薪一美元”人士。但这些大多都已成为历史。人们不喜欢尊重“所谓的专家”，也不明白为什么要尊重他们。如今，“教授”这个称呼仅仅意味着你是一个不了解现实世界的迂腐之人。如果你本身就是一位教授，被这样称呼简直令人沮丧。这就是成为“狡猾的礼貌”受害者的感受。你要么抗议，要么就装傻充愣，附和大家的观点。巴巴说混合性话语包含恐怖主义的成分，这或许有些夸张。他写这篇文章时远在9/11事件之前，因此，他当时使用这个词或许有些轻率，不符合我们今天的口味；但令人沮丧的恐吓确实存在。对于任何自认为至少与拥有实际或想象中的权威的人平起平坐的人来说，狡黠的礼貌是必要的。通过运用双重意识而产生的底层民众的自信和女主人的不安全感，并非角色的真正互换；一切依旧如故（我不会把我的博士学位交给脱口秀主持人），但角色之间的二元关系已被颠覆。

By the way, I can give you a firsthand example of how sly civility works because people in my walk of life are the objects of it. On talk shows and various public interest panels, they invite people to participate whom they call “professors.” Ostensibly that’s an honorific title that means the person so addressed is an expert. Perhaps at one time it really did convey respect, and it also had social cachet because professors used to be the offspring of the rich, “dollar a year men.” But most of that is now ancient history. Folks don’t like to show respect to a “so-called expert” and don’t see why they should. Today all it means to be called “professor” is that you’re a pedant who doesn’t understand the real world. If you’re a professor, it’s just plain depressing to be called one. This is how it feels to be the object of sly civility. You either protest or you play the fool and confirm everybody’s opinion. Bhabha probably exaggerates when he says the discourse of hybridity entails an element of terrorism. He wrote that long before 9/11 and thus perhaps uses the term a little breezily for our present taste; but frustrating intimidation is certainly involved. Sly civility is necessary to anyone who thinks he’s at least the equal of someone who has real or imagined authority. The subaltern self-confidence and memsahib insecurity that are effected by the exercise of double consciousness is not an actual exchange of roles; things remain as before (I don’t hand over my PhD to the talk show host), yet the binary relation of the roles has been subverted.

我们所考察的每段身份理论史都提供了知识即否定、即符号学知识的例证，而这正是本课程的核心主题。我们只能通过否定来认识自己，而无法真正了解自己。我只能通过否定来认识自己。一旦我将自己否定的事物客观化或归类（如果想要形成稳定的身份概念，无论是我自己的还是他人的，我都必须这样做），我便第一次理解了自己——正如托妮·莫里森、爱德华·萨义德或朱迪斯·巴特勒所论证的那样——分别是白人、西方人和异性恋者。简而言之，自我定义是否定性的，这与语言和文学的符号学理论传统相符。

Each history of identity theory we have considered offers instances of knowledge as negation, as semiotic knowledge, which has been a central theme throughout this course. We don’t know what we are except as the obverse of what we are not. I recognize myself only as not that. As soon as I objectify or pigeonhole what I am not (and I need to do that if stable concepts of identity, mine or another’s, are to emerge at all), I come to understand myself for the first time—according to the argument of a Toni Morrison or an Edward Said or a Judith Butler—as white, Western, and heterosexual, respectively. In short, self-definition is negative in keeping with the tradition of semiotic theories of language and literature.

这一切都是为了向你保证，我们仍然在讨论文学理论。在每一种情况下，身份理论首先是结构主义的，然后是解构主义的。我们阅读中转向社会关系并没有伴随我们最初考察的思维结构的改变——我们最初考察的思维结构是语言作为理解的主要决定因素。我们只是将语言——现在被视为社会理解的决定因素——转化成了我们所谓的“社会文本”。正如德里达所说，我们现在的“中心”不再是索绪尔的语言（langue），一个任意存在的虚拟实体，它作为一个共时系统而存在（产生它的历时性输入仅仅模糊了它作为科学对象的稳定轮廓），而是充满了他人语言的语言。这是一个社会——它本身被理解为一个话语建构系统——争夺关注并努力塑造自身的空间。这才是根本性的改变。当然，结构主义和解构主义也不认为语言是我们自主拥有的东西，因为关键在于语言是我们只能在言语中努力使其成为我们自己的东西；但是，在我们最近的阅读之后，我们能够更清楚地理解语言，它是一种社会形态赋予我们的东西，如果我们不能用它表达意义，它反过来又会塑造我们。

All this is meant to reassure you that we still are talking about literary theory. The theory of identity in each case is first structuralist and then deconstructive. The turn to social relations in our reading has not been accompanied by a change in the structure of thought we first examined when we took up language as the primary determinant of understanding. We have simply transformed language—viewed now as the determinant of social understanding—into what we call a “social text.” Our “center” now, as Derrida would put it, is not Saussure’s langue, a virtual entity that exists arbitrarily as a synchronic system (the diachronic input that produces it merely obscuring its stable outlines as a scientific object), but rather language that is full of other people’s language. It is a space in which society, itself understood as a system of discursive formations, jostles for attention and struggles to shape itself. That’s the fundamental change. Of course, structuralism and deconstruction don’t understand language as our own autonomous possession either, because the point is always that language is something we can only struggle to make our own in speech; but after our recent readings, we are in a position to understand language more clearly as something given to us as a social formation that in turn forms us if we fail to signify on it.

这就引出了我们本次讲座的重点，即阐释的前提条件。是什么使我们能够思考某事，或者认为某事为真？为什么你的想法和我的想法不一样？另一方面，我们之间又为何存在共识？正如你所读到的，我们已经来到了“阐释共同体”这个主题。

This brings us to our focus in this lecture, which concerns the preconditions of interpretation. What makes it possible for us to think something, or to think that something is true? How is it that you come to think one thing and I come to think differently? How is it that, on the other hand, there are areas of agreement among us? As your reading indicates, we have arrived at the topic of “interpretive communities.”

为了探讨这个问题，我们先回到《拖车托尼》这部作品。我们一直都说（希望我这么说不算太讽刺），托尼的故事与我们讨论的话题息息相关，而这部作品本身就是一个阐释阐释运作方式的实例。然而，正如斯坦利·菲什所坚持的，这并非仅仅是“你说存在什么，它就一定存在”的问题。（波洛涅斯说：“这很像鲸鱼。”）不妨从俄罗斯形式主义史学的角度来思考这个问题。在一部特定的文本中，所有在文学中被识别为自功能性的“手法”都存在，其中一些在功能上占主导地位，而另一些则处于功能上的隐蔽地位。这些手法的总和，就是随着时间的推移，阐释社群所接受和认可的、对文学作品构成贡献的总和。批评方法也是如此，它们总是能找到自己想要的东西——这无疑是一个危险信号！——但却仍然站得住脚。 （如果你好奇的话，我已经说服自己，我所说的关于托尼的一切都是站得住脚的，即使谈论某些事情，即主要的事情，比谈论其他事情，即次要的事情，更切题，也更符合尺度。）但是某些回应（托尼实际上是关于我六年级的实地考察）不属于公共领域中任何可解释对象的一部分，因此不算作解释。

In order to approach this issue, let’s first go back to Tony the Tow Truck. We’ve said all along, I hope not too facetiously, that Tony is about whatever it is that we happen to be talking about, and this has been meant as an object lesson in the way interpretation works. As Stanley Fish will insist, though, it’s not just a question of “whatever you say is there must be there.” (“Very like a whale,” says Polonius.) Think of it in Russian formalist historiographical terms. In a given text, all the “devices” that can be identified as auto-functions in literature are present, some syn-functionally dominant and some syn-functionally recessive. The sum of devices is the sum of communally accepted and recognized contributions to the building up of what counts as literature for interpretive communities over time. So it is with critical approaches that always find what they look for—surely a danger signal!—yet are still defensible. (I’ve convinced myself, in case you’re curious, that everything I’ve said about Tony is defensible, even if it’s more to the point, more appropriately in scale, to talk about some things, the dominant things, rather than others, the recessive ones.) But certain responses (Tony is really about my field trip in sixth grade) don’t correspond to any part of what counts as an interpretable object in the public domain, hence don’t count as interpretation.

那么，让我们再次思考一下《托尼》，这次我们把它看作是关于我们最近讨论过的身份认同形式的探讨。例如，我们可以说，《托尼》是马克思主义对阶级作为身份认同的社会决定因素的援引。正如我们之前所说，它是恩格斯和卢卡奇经典著作中的现实主义文本：它没有预言任何社会变革，却忠实地反映了社会存在的结构，包括——正如我们将看到的——种族和性别差异的结构。

So let’s think about Tony once again, then, this time as being “about” the forms of identity we’ve discussed recently. We can say, for example, that Tony is a Marxist invocation of class as the social determination of identity. It’s a realist text in the canon of Engels and Lukács, as we’ve said before: no social change is projected, yet it does faithfully reflect the structure of social existence, including—as we’ll see—the structure of ethnic and gender difference.

托尼的故事具有全球性，反映了美国大熔炉中的多元融合。其实，你早就应该看出托尼是一位意大利裔美国人，拥有底层民众特有的复杂人格。一方面，他相信美国梦：“我喜欢我的工作。” 但另一方面，他也意识到自己在这个世界上拥有一个独立而独特的角落：那间黄色的小修车铺，它在某种程度上构成了他的身份认同。相比之下，尼托是一位神经质的盎格鲁-撒克逊新教徒，而斯皮迪则是约翰·吉洛里所说的“专业/管理阶层”的一员。斯皮迪的有趣之处在于，他的种族出身、阶级，甚至性别——他或许是一位工作狂女性——都不像人们想象的那样重要，因为正如吉洛里的资料来源阿尔文·古尔德纳详尽指出的那样，专业/管理阶层是一个新兴群体，他们拥有共同的利益，但不能说他们共享某个阶级或其他既定的身份。在民间传说的三部曲中，Neato排在第一位并非偶然，因为Neato代表着一个较为古老的阶层，这个阶层正在逐渐被专业/管理阶层所取代。所以Neato排在第一位，Speedy排在第二位。

Tony is a global story that reflects hybridity in the American melting pot. It should have been obvious to you all along that Tony is an Italian American with the complex personality of the subaltern. On the one hand, he believes in the American dream: “I like my job.” Yet on the other hand, he recognizes that he has his own niche in the world, independent and set apart: the little yellow garage, which partly affords him his identity. Neato, in contrast, is a neurotic WASP, and Speedy is a member of what John Guillory calls “the professional/managerial class.” What’s interesting about Speedy is that his ethnic origins, his class, and even his gender—he may be a workaholic woman—are not as relevant as one might imagine them to be because the professional/managerial class—as Guillory’s source, Alvin Gouldner, points out at length—is an emergent group with common interests that can’t be said to share a class or other preexisting identity. It’s no accident that Neato comes first in the folkloric triad because Neato represents an older class, a class that is giving way to the professional/managerial class. So Neato comes first and Speedy comes second.

《托尼》也是一则性别寓言。我们说过，除了那些皱眉和微笑的房子之外，里面没有女性角色，但这还不是全部。很明显，照片里戴着小领结、一本正经地说着“哦，我不想弄脏”的尼托，简直就是一堆同性恋刻板印象的集合体。当然，还有那个“推来推去”的邦比——你肯定不想看到他。

Tony is a gender fable as well. We’ve said there are no women in it except for those frowning and smiling houses, but it’s not just that. Obviously Neato, with his little bow tie in the picture and his prissy “Oh, I don’t want to get dirty,” is just a bundle of gay stereotypes. And then, of course, Bumpy “pushes and pushes”—you don’t want to go there.

所以问题来了，这个问题也确实为我们今天的讨论做好了铺垫：我这些年来在《拖车托尼》这本书里到底在做什么？正如你现在看到的，我一直在做的，正是斯坦利·菲什在研究“雅各布斯、罗森鲍姆、莱文、索恩、海耶斯和奥曼”时所做的。我一直在表明，如果你带着某种预设去解读你所读的内容，你就会进行某种诠释行为，这种行为并非刻意为之，而是或多或少自发的，因为你已经被训练成这样做。

So here is the question, and it really does provide us with our transition to today’s materials: what have I been doing all this time with Tony the Tow Truck? As you can see now, I’ve been doing exactly what Stanley Fish does with “Jacobs, Rosenbaum, Levin, Thorne, Hayes, and Ohmann.” I’ve been showing that if you bring a certain supposition to bear on what you’re reading, you’re going to perform a certain kind of hermeneutic act, not with any particular strain but more or less spontaneously, because that’s what you’re conditioned to do.

菲什教授十七世纪宗教诗歌课的学生毫不费力地将他上一节课黑板上列出的语言学阅读清单解读成了一首诗，当然，你也能看出这份清单很容易让人这样解读。菲什承认这份清单纯属偶然，但他随后又用手指划过他任教学院的教职工名单，说道，这些名字同样可以解读成一首诗。我认为他的观点不无道理，因为托尼已经向我们展示了，当解读方式发生变化时，文本会变得多么灵活多变。我们甚至可以看出，他的学生漏掉了一些重要的知识点。他们忘记提及“Levin”一词的古义是闪电，象征着宗教启示中伴随而来的闪光。同样，我们很难理解为什么学生们会被“Hayes”这个词难住，因为我们就像透过一层薄雾，透过玻璃观看事物时，视线模糊不清。这就是我们对十七世纪宗教诗歌中闪现的宗教真理的反应。

Fish’s class in the devotional poetry of the seventeenth century had no trouble construing the list of readings in linguistics put on the board for his previous class as a poem, and you can see, of course, that the list offered temptations to be construed that way. Fish admits that the list is a lucky find, but then he runs his finger down the list of faculty names at the college where he’s lecturing and says you could just as easily read those names as a poem. I think he does make his point, because Tony has shown us how extraordinarily elastic texts are when interpretation pulls them this way and that. We can even see that his class missed a few important points. It forgot to mention that an archaic meaning of the word “Levin” is lightning, the flash that comes with any religious revelation. Again, it’s hard to understand why the class was stumped by the word “Hayes” because we see through a glass darkly, in a haze. That’s just how we respond to glimpses of religious truth in the devotional poetry of the seventeenth century.

好吧，你说，别再玩文字游戏了，我们仍然有权知道我们称之为文本的有意表达究竟是什么意思。例如，你可能想知道，我是否认为托尼这个角色具有意义，而不仅仅是重要性，正如E·D·赫希所区分的那样。事实上，我的确这么认为。我之前只是顺带提了一下，但这只是一种直觉（奇怪的是，我对它的确定性甚至不如我对所有“方法”所带来的顿悟时刻的确定性），而且相信我，这并非源于我对精神分析的任何偏好。然而，我确实认为，一个写给幼儿的故事，如果其高潮句是“他推啊推，我终于要上厕所了”，那么它显然是在讲如厕训练。处于肛门期的幼儿会知道被推来推去的是什么，而可能对其他方面一无所知。在你嗤之以鼻之前，你难道没看过《南方公园》吗？所以，这就是我的解读，也是我最倾向于提出的解读，胜过我之前尝试过的所有解读。但得出这样的结论需要哪些条件呢？我曾声明自己对精神分析有特殊兴趣，但我确实了解一些相关知识；精神分析是我解读体系的一部分，也是我在此案例中借鉴的部分。

Fine, you say, enough parlor games, we’re still entitled to know what that intentional utterance we call a text is really about. You may want to know, for example, whether I think Tony has a meaning, not just significance, to recall the distinction of E. D. Hirsch. As a matter of fact, I do. I mentioned it in passing, but it’s only an intuition (oddly, I’m less certain about it than I am about the aha! moments that all my “approaches” have yielded up), and it doesn’t arise, believe me, out of any predilections I may have for psychoanalysis. I do believe, however, that a story written for toddlers in which the climactic line is “He pushed and he pushed and I’m on my way” is pretty obviously about potty training. A toddler in the anal phase will know what’s being pushed and pushed and perhaps will know very little else. Before you scoff, have you never watched South Park? So that’s “my” interpretation, offered in preference to all the others I’ve played the ventriloquist for. But what conditions such a conclusion? I’ve disclaimed a special interest in psychoanalysis, but I do know something about it; psychoanalysis is part of my interpretive community, the part I draw on in this particular case.

我们都参与了这场游戏，就像菲什的课堂一样，因为我们作为一个群体，是一个诠释共同体，我们认可多种不同的方法，这一点从你们或多或少都乐于接受我的观点就可见一斑。我们对《拖车托尼》这部影片非常了解，一致认为它讲述的是这个、那个，还有另一个，或许周四还会讲到其他一些东西。在此，我想就我们基本一致的意见提出两点补充。首先，我想说，在我听众所在的诠释共同体——一个对诠释充满好奇的群体——内部，一直以来都存在一种怀疑，认为诠释是一场徒劳无功的游戏，因此你们才想来听这类讲座，看看它到底有多糟糕。我们都共同关注着围绕诠释的各种复杂情况。我们是一个对诠释感兴趣的诠释共同体，所以我们乐于参与到各种视角的奇妙世界中。

We’ve all been playing the game, just like Fish’s class, because we are, as a group, an interpretive community that recognizes a plurality of approaches, evidently so by virtue of the fact that you are more or less willingly taking in what I’m saying. We’ve been being very knowing about Tony the Tow Truck, agreeing that it’s about this, that, and the other thing and probably something else on Thursday. At this point, let me offer two caveats about our basic unanimity. First, I would say that within the interpretive community that makes up my audience, a community of people who are curious about interpretation, there has been a suspicion all along that interpretation is a mug’s game, and you therefore wanted to experience lectures of this kind to find out just how bad it was. All of us have in common a concern with the potential complexity of those circumstances that surround interpretation. We are an interpretive community that’s interested in interpretation, so we play along in the fun house of perspectives.

但其次，我认为在这个诠释群体内部，存在两个亚群体，他们虽然理解这种多元化实践的意义，却仍然极力抵制。其中一个群体一直以来或现在都对本课程中探讨过的某个观点抱有非常坚定的信念，因此他们认为，仅仅将最重要的观点——也就是真正的观点——视为一系列观点中的一个，是对它的贬低。你们可能还记得，在我为开设概览课程而道歉时，我提到过一些学生和同事对概览课程本身就感到不满，因为在他们看来，真正重要的只有马克思的思想，或者其他一些思想。这种观点或许会让你认为，与其说托尼只关注这一个方面，不如说多元化诠释是一种肤浅且带有侮辱性的做法，因为重要的是无论托尼关注什么，都应该认真对待这一个方面。

But second, however, I would hazard that within this interpretive community, there are two subcommunities that grasp the significance of this pluralistic exercise but still want very much to hold out against it. One of them is the community that either always has or has now come to have a very strong commitment to one or another point of view that’s been passed in review in this course, and who therefore finds it demeaning to the most important point of view, the true one, that it be treated merely as one in a series. You’ll recall that during my introductory apology for giving a survey, I mentioned students and colleagues who have bridled at the very idea of a survey course when, after all, the only thing that matters is Marx’s thought, or some other thought. This viewpoint would probably lead you to say not so much that Tony is only about this one thing but that plural interpretation is a facile and insulting exercise because the important thing is to take only this one thing seriously no matter what Tony is about.

我们诠释社群中的第二个子社群仍然坚持“高雅文化”。这个社群并非否认条条大路通罗马，而是坚持认为我们应该诠释《利西达斯》或《古舟子咏》 。按照这种观点，我们用拖车托尼来解读作品，是对高雅文化的不尊重。这种观点的一个隐含意义是，对一部严肃的文学作品采用多种解读方法，最终会就最佳方法（不一定是唯一方法）达成某种共识，而其他所有方法与之相比都会显得微不足道。如果你的执着并非在于某种观点，而在于某种高雅文化的理念，你就不会预先断言哪种方法最佳，而是会认为一部伟大的文学作品会为你指明最佳方向，或许还会提供其自身的诠释框架，而这些框架理应受到尊重。约翰·吉洛里在讨论西方文化中主流经典的捍卫时，所批评的正是这种观点，或者说是这种观点的某种更灵活的说法。

The second subcommunity within our interpretive community is the one that is still committed to “high culture.” This community doesn’t necessarily deny that there are more ways to the woods than one but insists that we should have been interpreting “Lycidas” or The Rime of the Ancient Mariner. According to this view, we have shown a lack of respect for high culture in using Tony the Tow Truck. One implication of this view is that multiple approaches to a serious work of literature would yield a measure of consensus about the best approach (not necessarily the only one), in contrast with which all the other approaches would stand revealed as trivial. If your commitment is not so much to one point of view as to some idea of high culture, you’re not going to say in advance which approach is best, but you are going to suppose that a great work of literature will point you in the best direction, yielding perhaps its own terms for interpretation, which should be honored. This is the view, or perhaps a slightly more flexible version of the view, that John Guillory is criticizing when he discusses defenses of a mainstream canon in Western culture.

然而，作为一个诠释共同体，我们都认同可以像我们一样对文本进行即兴解读。如果有人这样做，我们就会意识到，无论我们是否喜欢，我们自己或许也能做到——这从斯坦利·菲什和约翰·吉洛里的角度来看，都证明了我们同属一个学派，因此我们有很多共同之处。正是这些共同之处，使得文本在许多方面都清晰地呈现在我们所有人面前，而不会引起太多困惑或怀疑。

Nevertheless, we all do have in common, as an interpretive community, the recognition that it’s possible to riff on a text as we have done. If somebody does it, we realize that whether we like it or not, we ourselves could probably do it, too—which is proof, from Stanley Fish’s point of view and also from John Guillory’s, that because we’re in a school we have a great deal in common. It’s what we have in common that brings the text into focus, for all of us and without much confusion or incredulity, in so many ways.

不过，我们现在应该更加认真地谈论“阐释社群”和“学派”，更加仔细地审视作者使用这些术语的真正含义。那么，让我们回到菲什的论述，从他的第一句话（1023）开始。由于这是一系列讲座的一部分，他开篇便说道：

It’s high time though that we speak less casually about “interpretive communities” and “schools” and attend more closely to what our authors mean and don’t mean in using such terms. Turning, then, to Fish, let’s begin with his first sentence (1023). Because this is part of a series of lectures, he begins by saying:

上次我概述了一个论点，即意义既不是固定不变的文本的属性，也不是自由独立的读者的属性，而是解释社群的属性。解释社群既决定了读者活动的形态，也决定了这些活动所产生的文本。
Last time I sketched out an argument by which meanings are the property neither of fixed and stable texts nor of free and independent readers but of interpretative communities that are responsible both for the shape of a reader’s activities and for the texts those activities produce.

我不确定他在这篇演讲中是否进一步阐述了他的论点，所以我认为值得仔细思考这句话。

I’m not sure he carries his argument all that much farther forward in this lecture, which is why I think it’s worthwhile to linger over this sentence.

我将尝试通过勾勒菲什有趣的学术生涯轨迹来阐释这一点。他自己也承认，他实际上改变了两次观点，而这些改变也体现在我刚才读到的那句话中。所以，以下是他的三个基本立场，它们彼此相互影响、相互制约。当我还是菲什在加州大学的学生时，他坚定地持有他的第一个观点。就在他出版《罪的惊愕：〈失乐园〉中的读者》一书之前不久，我当时参加的研讨班算是这本书的试读者。为了举例说明他所说的“文本塑造读者” （这是他的第一个观点）的含义，我将引用他引用的一段弥尔顿的文字。撒旦从火湖中浮现，挺直身躯，手持长矛：“他的长矛，与最高的松树相比……/ 简直就是一根魔杖……”！你突然意识到，大小顺序完全颠倒了，你之前脑海中浮现的——最高的松树——与撒旦的长矛相比，简直就是一根魔杖。弥尔顿究竟想表达什么？他是在告诉你，你以为你了解撒旦有多强大，但你最好不要招惹他，因为他比你想象的还要强大得多。作为亚当的后裔，你已经落入了弥尔顿的句法陷阱，而且会一次又一次地落入其他陷阱，就像你对预设的漠视会让你落入撒旦的魔爪，直到你明白阅读并非妄下结论，而是保留判断。

I’ll try to explicate it by sketching in the interesting arc of Fish’s career. He has actually changed his mind twice, by his own admission, and those changes are in turn registered in the sentence I just read. So here are his three basic positions, succeeding and undermining each other in turn. When I was Fish’s student at the University of California, he firmly held his first opinion. This was just before he published Surprised by Sin: The Reader in “Paradise Lost,” a book for which the seminar I was in was a kind of trial audience. To give you an example of what he meant in claiming that the text produces the reader, which was his first opinion, I will cite a passage that he cites from Milton. Satan emerging from the fiery lake pulls himself up to his full height, holding a spear: “His Spear, to equal which the tallest Pine [okay: spear, pine, about the same size?] / Hewn … / To be the Mast of some great Ammiral [so: mast = pine = spear?] / Were but a wand …”! Suddenly you realize that the sequence of sizes is completely reversed and that what you’d already filled your consciousness with—the tallest pine—is just a wand compared with Satan’s spear. So what’s Milton doing? He’s saying you think you know how big Satan is, but you shouldn’t mess with him because he is much bigger than you could ever imagine he is. You have fallen, being a descendant of Adam, into Milton’s syntactical trap, and will fall repeatedly into others, just as the same unwariness of presupposition will make you fall into Satan’s clutches until you learn that reading doesn’t jump to conclusions but reserves judgment.

我之前没有引用的段落，即这段文字的后续部分，表明即便我们承认他无可比拟的强大，我们看到的也仅仅是撒旦最虚弱的一面。这段文字继续写道：“他不过是一根魔杖，/ 用来支撑他蹒跚的步伐。” 他此刻的虚弱程度已臻极致，然而他已远超我们所能掌控。妄下结论，过早地建立起对文本的解读自信，只会让我们跌倒，而且会一次又一次地跌倒。《失乐园》的句法告诉我们，每当我们过早地认为自己领悟了文本的要旨时，我们就证明自己是堕落的读者，尚未成为能够从堕落的故事中获益的“少数合格的读者”。

What I didn’t quote yet, the continuation of the passage, shows that even once we have acknowledged his incommensurable size, we are still seeing Satan only at his weakest. The passage continues, “were but a wand,/ He walkt with to support uneasy steps.” He’s as weak as he’s ever going to be right now, yet he’s already a lot more than you can handle. To jump to conclusions, achieving premature interpretive confidence, is to fall, repeatedly to fall. The syntax of Paradise Lost teaches us that every time we think too soon that we grasp the point of a text, we prove that we are fallen readers, not yet part of the “fit audience though few” that can benefit from the story of the Fall.

因此，菲什最初的观点是，文本造就了读者。不久之后，在撰写《自我消耗的人工制品》一书的过程中，他的观点发生了转变，几乎完全颠覆了最初的看法。他认为，并非文本造就了读者——以《失乐园》为例，并非文本造就了读者对堕落状态的认知。并非文本造就了读者，而是读者造就了文本。读者创造了文本。毕竟，正是读者在进行阅读行为，无论这种阅读多么误入歧途；也正是读者最终揭示了弥尔顿策略的特征。因此，菲什改变了研究领域，但仍然保留了与最初立场相似的论证结构和对文本动态教化作用的深刻洞见。

Fish’s first opinion was, then, that the text produces the reader. Not too long after that, in the course of writing a book called Self-Consuming Artifacts, he began to have a different opinion that more or less reversed the first one. He decided it isn’t the text that brings the reader into being—into the recognition of a fallen state of being in the case of Paradise Lost. It isn’t the text that brings the reader into being. It’s the reader that brings the text into being. The reader produces the text. It’s the reader, after all, who performs the act of reading, however misguidedly, and it’s the reader who finally makes visible the characteristics of Milton’s strategy. So Fish reverses his field while retaining from his first position a similar structure of argument and range of insight concerning the dynamic didacticism of the texts that interest him.

第二个观点看似合理，直到菲什意识到读者并非独立自主的个体，而是会受到各种影响。因此，他对“读者反应”（他的理论贡献与伊瑟尔的理论贡献一样，都属于这一广泛的领域或学派）的思考发生了第三次革命性的变化，其核心在于：并非文本造就了读者，也并非读者造就了文本，而是阐释共同体造就了读者，而读者反过来又造就了文本。

This second position seemed sound until Fish remembered that a reader isn’t just an autonomous mind but reflects influences. Accordingly, the third revolution in his thinking about “reader response” (the broad field or school to which his theoretical contributions belong, like those of Iser) amounts to this: it’s not the text that produces the reader, it’s not the reader who produces the text, it’s the interpretive community that produces the reader who in turn produces the text.

当菲什（Fish）说（1025）“阐释不是解读的艺术，而是建构的艺术。阐释者不解码诗歌，而是创造诗歌”时，他仅仅处于思考的第二阶段，因为我们仍然可以假设阐释者是一个自主的个体，其阅读或建构策略是自我生成的。然而，他很快澄清（1027）：“但这并不意味着我必须接受主观性。”换句话说，这并非仅仅是说我放入文本中的任何内容都是合理的，并非仅仅是说我们每个人都因为拥有不同的主观性而创作出不同的文本，因此任何离经叛道的阐释都是可能的。他并非此意；正如他接下来所解释的，我不能简单地说《拖车托尼》（Tony the Tow Truck）是关于我六年级的实地考察。“但这并不意味着我必须接受主观性，因为文本的创作方式是社会性的、约定俗成的。”

When Fish says (1025), “Interpretation is not the art of construing but the art of constructing. Interpreters do not decode poems; they make them,” he’s only in phase two of his thinking, because we can still suppose that the interpreter is an autonomous being whose strategies of reading, or constructing, are self-generated. Soon he clarifies, though (1027): “This does not, however, commit me to subjectivity.” In other words, it’s not just a question of saying that whatever I put into a text is legitimate, of saying we all make different texts because we all have different subjectivities, hence any old off-the-wall interpretation is possible. That’s not what he’s saying; for the reason he goes on to provide, I can’t just say Tony the Tow Truck is about my sixth-grade field trip. “This does not, however, commit me to subjectivity because the means by which [texts] are made are social and conventional.”

我们对托尼的种种评价，无论多么五花八门，有时甚至离谱，都建立在某种地方共识之上，某种诠释社群对“什么可以表达”的共识之上。换句话说，如果我希望自己的解读能被理解，就不能有任何天马行空的解读。如果我把自己锁在房间里，或许可以对某些事物进行天马行空的解读（或者更确切地说，创作一篇天马行空的文章），但没人会发表。我的解读，如果它能算作一种解读的话，就源于那些创造并共享“解读”和“文本”概念的社群所采用的技巧和假设。

Everything we said about Tony, for all its variety and occasional outrageousness, was enabled by some local consensus, some opinion shared by an interpretive community, about what it is possible to say. In other words, I can’t have an off-the-wall interpretation of anything if I expect to be understood. If I’m locked in my room, I suppose I can have an off-the-wall interpretation of something (or, rather, produce an off-the-wall text), but no one will publish it. My interpretation, if it’s to count as an interpretation at all, derives from the techniques and assumptions of communities that produce, and share, the very concepts of “interpretation” and “text.”

如果只有那些拥有约定俗成的社群才能生产出任何可以被理解为文本或其他事物的东西，那么主体和客体也就不存在了。这是菲什（Fish）与德里达（Derrida）和解构主义并行的，对西方形而上学传统的批判方式。我希望这一点，正如我们阅读的其他部分一样，显而易见，客体的实际存在根本不成问题。菲什生动地指出，社群生产客体，但他是以实用主义者的身份发言，而非一个得不偿失的怀疑论者或一个隐藏的理想主义者。“生产”一个客体，就是生产出使它变得可以被理解——并被其他具有类似认知的人共同认可——的手段。如果我们反驳说，十四行诗无论我们是否阅读（“生产”）它，它都是一首十四行的诗，我们就忘记了，要了解并清晰地阐述一首诗、一行诗、一定数量的诗行，最终是一首十四行诗，需要一定的教育（这与其他社群的教育有所不同）。这又使我们回到最初的想法，即海德格尔和伽达默尔的“先在性”以及我们总是将事物视为某种事物的方式。然而，菲什的观点与此有所不同，他否认了主观性在诠释过程中的作用。伽达默尔强调历史视域而非浪漫化的个体作者或读者，这或许在某种程度上预示了菲什的观点。菲什坚持认为，个体只能看到或生产出其诠释社群所塑造的、使其可见的事物。

If only communities armed with conventions are the agents that produce whatever it is that becomes intelligible as a text or some other thing, it follows that there are neither subjects nor objects. This is Fish’s way, in parallel with Derrida and deconstruction, of attacking the Western metaphysical tradition. I hope it’s clear here, as elsewhere in our reading, that the actual existence of objects isn’t at all in question. Fish says colorfully that communities produce objects, but he speaks as a pragmatist, not a Pyrrhic skeptic or a closet idealist. To “produce” an object is to produce the means whereby it becomes intelligible—and recognized in common with others similarly informed—as that object. If we retort that a sonnet is a poem of fourteen lines whether we read it (“produce it”) or not, we forget that it takes a certain education (differing from the education of other communities) to know, to set forth intelligibly what a poem, a line, a certain quantity of lines, and finally a sonnet might be. This, too, returns us to our first thoughts, in this case concerning “fore-having” in Heidegger and Gadamer and the way we always see something as something. Fish departs from this idea, though, in denying the role of subjectivity in the hermeneutic process. Anticipated to some degree perhaps by Gadamer’s emphasis on historical horizons rather than romantically conceived individual authors or readers, Fish insists that individuals see, or produce, only what their interpretive communities condition them to make visible.

那么，什么是阐释共同体？我说过，我们都属于同一个共同体，它反映了我们在此相聚的现实，而我之前也只谈到了我们内部的两个持不同意见的子共同体。但这些广泛的共同点显然存在一个复杂之处。我们彼此理解，但同时，正如我相信你们所有人都在思考的那样，我们每个人的观点都不尽相同。即使接受这种论证的弱形式，我们很容易认同，我们确实会根据某些习惯来构建事物，而这些习惯正是在我们作为阐释共同体成员的过程中逐渐形成的。但与此同时，你们每个人都表示，你们对雅各布斯、罗森鲍姆等人的解读方式与菲什的班级并不完全相同，你们对弗莱教授的解读方式也与他补充的解读方式并不完全相同。你们的解读方式略有不同，你们的邻座的解读方式也与你们不同。我们拥有一些富有成效的假设，但我们每个人对文本的解读方式却各不相同。

What, then, is an interpretive community? I have said we all belong to the one that reflects our presence here together and spoke before only of two dissenting subcommunities among us. But there’s an obvious complication of these broad commonalities. We understand each other, yet at the same time it’s equally true, as I’m sure all of you are thinking, that no one of us has exactly the same set of opinions as anyone else. Accepting a weak form of the argument, it’s easy enough to agree that we do bring things into being according to certain habits that have evolved through our membership in an interpretive community. But at the same time, each of you says you don’t quite interpret Jacobs, Rosenbaum, and the rest of them in the way Fish’s class did, nor do you interpret it in quite the way Professor Fry did in supplementing their interpretation. You interpret it a little differently, and your neighbor differently from you. We share productive assumptions, yet each of us produces texts differently.

菲什会对此作何回应？我认为他会做出让步，而且我认为这一点需要承认，因为它削弱了他的立场，但并未动摇：诚然，从某种意义上说，我们都身处同一境地——正如约翰·吉洛里所说，从某种意义上说，我们都在同一所学校里——但从另一个意义上说，我们每个人也是我们所归属和从中涌现的所有诠释社群的总和、综合体。我们每个人都各不相同，因为我们所属的诠释社群的总和总是会与其他人各自所属的社群的总和略有不同。社群的概念依然存在，但或许有人会说，它只是被简化了，因为这种原子式的表述方式让人觉得社群的总和与个体的总和一样大。

What would Fish say to that? I think he would say by way of concession, and I do think this needs to be acknowledged because it weakens without undermining his position: granted, in a rough sense we’re all in this together—just as John Guillory says in a rough sense we’re all in a school—but there’s another sense in which each of us is also the sum total, the composite, of all the interpretive communities to which we now belong and from which we have emerged. We’re each different because the sum of the interpretive communities to which we belong is always going to be a little different from the sum of the communities to which other people severally belong. The community concept is still in place, but perhaps, some would say, only reductively so, as the atomism of this way of putting it makes it seem as though the sum of communities is as great as the sum of individuals.

反对社会建构主义的另一种论点可以称为生物建构主义。像爱德华·威尔逊这样的社会生物学家，以及“人工智能”的支持者和认知科学领域的其他一些学者指出，大脑从出生起或几乎从出生起就被预先设定好，能够识别和处理各种事物。实验室研究表明，审美偏好——这种偏好过去常被嘲笑为客观存在，因为我们总是说“品味无可争议”——实际上也源于我们每个人与生俱来的偏好。我们都偏爱所谓的黄金分割，我们都喜欢拱形，这或许是因为我们喜欢能够提供庇护或保护的形状。无论如何，相当确凿的证据表明，我们天生就具备共享认知和参照的能力。达尔文的最后一本书描述了我们如何从婴儿时期就识别彼此的表情以及动物的表情，因此几乎不存在社会制约的问题。

Another argument against social constructivism might be called biological constructivism. Sociobiological thinkers like Edward O. Wilson, together with proponents of “artificial intelligence” and some others in the field of cognitive science, point out that the brain is hardwired from birth or nearly so to do and recognize all sorts of things. It has been shown in the lab that aesthetic preference, which was always held up to derision when said to be objective—“There is no disputing tastes,” we always say—that even aesthetic preference draws on predilections innate to all of us. We all prefer the so-called golden section, we love arches, possibly because we like shapes that offer shelter or protection. In any case, the fairly conclusive evidence is that we are hardwired to share recognitions and references. Darwin’s last book describes how from infancy we recognize each other’s expressions as well as the expressions of animals, so that there can be very little question of social conditioning.

然而，我不确定菲什的论证是否真的容易被这种观点驳倒，因为毕竟，先天本能与社会制约一样具有群体性。此外，基于先天本能的论证并不能证明我们都感知到同一个对象，而仅仅表明（正如菲什所言）我们都建构了同一个对象。因此，在我看来，尽管反对所谓激进建构主义的论证通常以指向先天倾向的形式出现，但实际上却并不成功；而指出如果我们想要保留确定性解释共同体的概念，那么这些共同体的数量必须几乎与拥有这些共同体的人数一样多的论证，则更有说服力。

I’m not sure Fish’s argument is vulnerable to that position, however, because, after all, hardwiring is as communal as social conditioning. And furthermore, arguments from hardwiring harbor no proof that we all perceive the same object, showing only, in keeping with Fish’s view, that we all construct the same object. So it seems to me that although the argument against so-called radical constructivism usually does take the form of pointing to innate predispositions, it actually doesn’t succeed; and the argument pointing out that if we are to retain the concept of determinate interpretive communities, they must be almost as numerous as the people who share them is the more telling of the two.

约翰·吉洛里将学校视为一个阐释共同体，他的论证实际上终结了他预期会愈演愈烈的学术经典之争（参见1477页）。他认为，未来二十五年甚至更长时间内，学术界的热点话题将是文化战争：经典与非经典之争，文化与多元文化之争——他担心围绕这些术语会展开无休止的争论。然而，这种情况并未发生，因为他的论证如此精辟，以至于所有人都幡然醒悟，意识到这场辩论的框架存在问题。吉洛里的著作《文化资本》并没有平息公众对文化战争的讨论——公众的声音永远不会被压制——但它确实彻底终结了围绕他主要研究对象——那些“学校”中“文化”的争论。

John Guillory’s argument, which treats the school as an interpretive community, actually ended the academic canon debate that he expected to intensify and get worse (cf. 1477). He thought the hot-button topic in the academic world for the next twenty-five years or more would be the culture wars: canonical versus noncanonical, cultural versus multicultural—he feared endless quarrels over those terms. Well, it didn’t happen because his own argument was so brilliant that everybody came to their senses and realized that the debate was improperly framed. Guillory’s book, Cultural Capital, did not silence the public version of the culture wars—nothing ever silences the public—but it did decisively silence the debate about “culture” in those “schools” that are his main subject.

正如我所说，吉洛里的主要关注点——这很大程度上源于社会学家皮埃尔·布迪厄，但也如他所阐述的，源于安东尼奥·葛兰西——在于学派如何建立和传播葛兰西所谓的“霸权”。根据这种观点，学派通常不会培养出掌握特定知识体系或理解力的人才。相反，尤其是在人文领域——吉洛里认为人文领域正因其晦涩难懂而陷入困境——它培养出的是被某种“文化资本”所烙印的人。换句话说，它不断重复，或者用布迪厄的话来说，它“再生产”着某种阶级——这里的“阶级”指的是马克思意义上的上层建筑阶级，而非以金钱甚至家庭为特征的阶级，尽管两者之间当然存在重叠之处。无论学生自认为掌握了哪些具体内容，也无论学校多么强调进步主题，它都通过文化（交响乐门票、餐后演讲中引用诗人诗句，以及对多元文化的热情）来滋生优越感，而这种文化恰恰复制了一种特权倾向——吉洛里认为，西方文化中的学校一直以来都在助长这种倾向。学校复制的与其说是知识，不如说是它自身，是它所体现的态度，是它存在和延续的理由，以及它与权力和国家机器的关系。正因如此，吉洛里认为文化战争的双方都同样地落入了学校所复制的单一意识形态的圈套。任何文本，无论其本身多么进步或“边缘化”，只要它首先被加工，然后被当作文化商品来占有，就无法产生任何影响。

Guillory’s chief preoccupation, as I say—one that he takes over largely from the sociologist Pierre Bourdieu but also, as he elaborates, from Antonio Gramsci—is with the way the school establishes and proliferates what Gramsci called “hegemony.” The school, according to this view, doesn’t typically produce minds armed with specific bodies of knowledge or understanding. It produces instead, especially in the humanities—which Guillory thinks are painting themselves into a corner in their obtuseness—people imprinted by a certain quantum of “cultural capital.” It repeats, in other words, or in Bourdieu’s term it “reproduces,” a certain kind of class—“class” here in Marx’s superstructural sense rather than class coded by money or even necessarily by family, though of course there are overlaps. Regardless of the specific content that a student supposes herself to have been mastering, and regardless of its emphasis on progressive themes, the school breeds superiority through the possession of culture (symphony tickets, quotations from the poets in after-dinner speeches, but also multicultural enthusiasms) that replicates an orientation to privilege that Guillory says the school in Western culture has always fostered. What the school reproduces is not knowledge so much as itself, the attitude that it embodies, its reason for being and for continuation, together with its relation to power and the state apparatus. That’s why Guillory says both sides of the culture wars to an equal extent play into the hands of the monolithic ideology reproduced by the school. No text, no matter how progressive or “marginalized” in itself, can effect change as long as it is first processed and later possessed as a cultural commodity.

当你把多元文化主义，也就是所谓的“非经典”，当作灌输吉洛里所谓的“进步教育学”的唯一途径时，你最终只会将你关注的对象从它们所属的文化中剥离出来，正如“西方文明的伟大丰碑”早已脱离了它们的历史和文化语境一样。你把西方文明和各种替代经典都贬低为同样的、没有根基的文化资本商品。就西方文明而言，它成了餐后演讲的素材；就多元文化课程而言，它成了在类似场合以同样方式提及的机会。而无论哪种情况，根据吉洛里的说法，它都与学习任何文化产品所根植的历史和社会语境毫无关系。

When you embrace multiculturalism, the “noncanonical,” as the only means of inculcating what Guillory calls “progressive pedagogy,” you succeed only in deracinating the objects of your attention from the culture to which they belong in precisely the way that “the great monuments of Western civilization” have long since been deracinated from their historical and cultural circumstances. You reduce both Western Civ and alternative canons to the same rootless commodification as cultural capital. In the case of Western Civ, it’s fodder for after-dinner speeches. In the case of multicultural curricula, it’s the opportunity to allude in precisely the same way on parallel occasions, and in either case it has nothing to do with learning anything at all, according to Guillory, about the historical and social circumstances in which any kind of cultural production is grounded.

这种论点的前提是，在“学派”意识形态下，伟大作品或非经典作品的教学方式是将它们视为思想和原则的载体。它们被当作信息来教授。西方经典被提炼成一种信息，即美国价值观优越，仿佛这些价值观自古以来就未曾改变。多元文化经典则被提炼成一种论证自身价值和重要性的对抗性信息，强调作为任何一位发言者本身的美和意义。所有作品最终都不再是文化产物，不再是那些既源于又阐释其创作历史环境的文化产物。

This argument depends on supposing that the way the great works or noncanonical works are taught under “school” ideology is to view them as vessels of ideas and principles. They’re taught as messages. The Western canon distills itself into a message about the superiority of American values as they descend unchanged from antiquity. The multicultural canon distills itself into a contestatory message about the beauty and importance of being whoever happens to be speaking. What all works cease to be is cultural artifacts that both emerge from and articulate the historical circumstances in which they are written.

归根结底，这种论点是对一种新的教学方法的呼吁。事实上，吉洛里本人最深切的追求在于对伟大作品的推崇。他最初是一位早期现代文学学者，并撰写了一部关于斯宾塞和弥尔顿的优秀著作。他后来在文学社会学领域的研究丝毫没有否定或削弱他早期对特定文化经典的关注。事实上，《文化资本》一书中最为精彩的章节或许是他阐述托马斯·格雷的《乡村教堂墓园挽歌》如何在英语课程中占据主导地位的那一章，尽管这首诗是用白话英语写成的。换句话说，他指出，这首如今已成为文化丰碑的诗歌，是如何削弱了人们对古典文学和拉丁语的推崇，并推动了白话英语国家课程的出现。

This argument is ultimately a plea for a new method of teaching. Guillory’s own deepest commitment is, in fact, to the great works. He began as an early modern scholar and wrote a fine first book on Spenser and Milton. His later work in literary sociology in no ways discredits or undermines the fact that earlier in his career he was interested in a particular cultural canon. In fact, probably the most interesting chapter in Cultural Capital is the one in which he shows how Thomas Gray’s “Elegy in a Country Churchyard” came to predominate in English curricula even though it was written in the vernacular, in English. He shows, in other words, how that poem, now itself a cultural monument, undermined the premium placed on the classics, on Latinity, and helped along the emergence of a vernacular national curriculum.
