吉洛里本人喜爱古典著作，包括那些被格雷的《挽歌》所取代的作品。他实际上赞同葛兰西看似反动的观点，即所有阶层的学生都应该有机会讨论一些共同的主题，古典著作自然也不例外。然而，吉洛里指出，西方文明史的权威们是如何被“经典著作可以具有‘传统’或永恒性”的观念所蒙蔽的。历史不断地改变着经典著作。书籍越多，可读之物就越少，那些曾经的经典作品也必然会悄然从课程体系中消失，包括西方文明史的课程体系。每当我们为一门标准课程制定新的教学大纲时，都会目睹这种情况的发生。（如果我决定引入一些新的理论家——而这或许是我应该做的——那么我们阅读的某些理论家又会受到怎样的影响呢？）如今，我们自以为了解“伟大的古典著作”，读过柏拉图、亚里士多德、荷马、维吉尔的作品，或许还有修昔底德和希罗多德的著作。过去，人们的阅读范围并不止于那些伟大的作品。他们会阅读所有能找到的希腊语和拉丁语书籍，然后，如果还有时间，他们还会阅读当时出版的少量英文书籍。而现代语言和文学为了给自己腾出空间，已经大幅缩减了这一经典范畴。

Guillory himself likes the classics, including the ones displaced by Gray’s “Elegy,” and he actually subscribes to Gramsci’s superficially reactionary-seeming idea that all students of all classes should have the opportunity to discuss some common subject matter, not excluding the classics. Guillory shows, though, how the Western Civ mavens are fooled by the notion that a canon could be “traditional” or permanent. History continuously changes canons. The more books accumulate, the fewer you can read, and the more formerly canonical works must silently drop out of any curriculum, including the Western Civ curriculum. We watch this happen every time we draw up a new curriculum for a standard course. (What would happen to certain theorists in our reading if I decided, as arguably I should, to introduce new ones?) Today we suppose we know the “great classics,” having read some Plato, Aristotle, Homer, Virgil, and maybe Thucydides and Herodotus. In former times, people didn’t stop with those greats. They read everything there was to read in Greek and Latin, and then they read, because they still had a bit of time, such few books as had then been published in English. Modern languages and literatures have radically thinned out this canon to make room for themselves.

吉洛里的论点取决于参与这些辩论的所有人未能区分两种“文化”形式。一种文化是完全没有受过教育的人和新兴的专业人士/管理阶层都能共享的，在这种文化中，文学本身并不重要。在这种文化中，耐克只是一双运动鞋。另一种文化，正如我们所说的，是真正意义上的文化，它不仅包含文明的丰碑，也包含那些被当作护身符传承下来的其他经典。吉洛里认为，我们对这两种文化形式之间关系的理解完全脱节，正是导致他所抱怨的教学脱离根基的原因。他本人认为，任何事物都可以被教授，只要将其置于社会和历史背景下进行教授，就可以循序渐进地进行。他指出，“伟大的著作”之所以伟大，部分原因在于它不可能被简化为西方文明倡导者强加给它的那种陈词滥调式的自我观点的确认（1482）：

Guillory’s argument hinges on the failure of anybody involved in these debates to distinguish between the two forms of “culture.” There is the kind of culture that a person without any education at all and the new professional/managerial class can share, the kind of culture in which literature, precisely, doesn’t matter. In this culture, Nike is an athletic shoe. Then there is culture with a capital K, as we say, featuring the monuments of civilization, but also the alternative canons when they are transmitted as comparable talismans. Guillory says the total disconnect in the way we understand the relations between these two forms of culture is what leads to the deracination in teaching that he complains about. He himself thinks anything is fair game to be taught and can be taught progressively as long as it is taught in terms of its social and historical circumstances. He points out that a “great book” is great in part because it can’t possibly be reduced to the bromidic confirmation of one’s own views that the advocates of Western Civ burden it with (1482):

任何有意义的文化作品都不可能简单到足以用这种方式进行可信的寓言化，因为任何文化作品都会在其形式和内容中客观化那些经典辩论通过分裂的课程体系所寓言化的社会冲突。
No cultural work of any interest at all is simple enough to be credibly allegorized in this way, because any cultural work will objectify in its very form and content the same social conflicts that the canon debate allegorizes by means of a divided curriculum.

《奥德赛》充满了谎言、诡计和阶级背叛。《伊利亚特》中，最有趣的角色之一是忒耳西忒斯，他几乎不认同我们通常认为的西方文化价值观。无论如何，吉洛里所说的“如果你足够仔细认真地阅读，就无法以这种方式将任何事物奉为圭臬”正是这个意思。因此，归根结底，他的论点是一个提升阅读体验的方案，它让我们将“学派”这种阐释共同体与鲜活的文化环境相融合，因为在这样的文化中，耐克既是鞋子又是女神。

The Odyssey is full of lying, trickery, class betrayal. In The Iliad, one of the more interesting characters is Thersites, who is scarcely an advocate of the values that we associate with Western culture. In any case, this is what Guillory means by saying that you cannot monumentalize anything in this way if you read it carefully and attentively enough. So ultimately his argument is a program for better reading, one that ventilates the interpretive community we call a school with the living circumstances that produce and express themselves in a culture where Nike is both a shoe and a goddess.

 

 

理论的利弊

Theory Con and Pro

 

 

第25章

CHAPTER 25

理论的终结？新实用主义
The End of Theory? Neo-Pragmatism

阅读：

Reading:

Knapp, Steven 和 Walter Benn Michaels。“反对理论”。载于《反对理论：文学研究与新实用主义》。WJT Mitchell 编。芝加哥：芝加哥大学出版社期刊，1985 年。

Knapp, Steven, and Walter Benn Michaels. “Against Theory.” In Against Theory: Literary Studies and the New Pragmatism. Ed. W. J. T. Mitchell. Chicago: University of Chicago Press Journals, 1985.

本次讲座的主题是一篇由两位年轻学者撰写的文章，这篇文章一经发表便迅速引发了广泛的赞誉和争议。其中一位当时尚未获得终身教职，他们仍在学术界摸索前行。这篇文章发表于《批判性探究》（Critical Inquiry）期刊，无疑取得了成功。《批判性探究》的编辑很快决定将这篇文章与一系列回应文章《反理论》（Against Theory）一起出版成书。如果您对这篇文章引发的争议感兴趣，那么这本书非常值得一读——我希望能够说服您这样做。

This lecture concerns an essay written to immediate widespread acclaim and controversy by two young scholars, one of them then untenured, who were still making their way in the academic world. They certainly succeeded with this essay, which was published in Critical Inquiry. The editors of Critical Inquiry quickly decided to publish in book form, together with “Against Theory,” a series of responses to the essay. It’s well worth reading in full if you take an interest in the controversies that the article generated—as I hope to persuade you to do.

史蒂文·克纳普和沃尔特·本·迈克尔斯是“新实用主义者”，他们深受哲学家理查德·罗蒂20世纪70年代的重要著作《哲学与自然之镜》的影响；罗蒂的哲学传统可以追溯到20世纪30年代和40年代的约翰·杜威，更早之前，不仅包括亨利·詹姆斯的弟弟威廉·詹姆斯的伟大哲学贡献，而且或许更为重要的是，还包括哲学家查尔斯·桑德斯·皮尔斯的符号学理论。皮尔斯的理论奇特而晦涩，在其《致韦尔比夫人的信》中体现得最为明显，在当时除了包括詹姆斯在内的少数几位同事之外，鲜为人知。然而，剑桥大学以I.A.理查兹为首的一个学术圈却接受了这一理论。在《意义的意义》一书中，理查兹和奥格登在附录中收录了皮尔斯致韦尔比夫人的信件节选，并专门对皮尔斯的符号学进行了一些思考，这些思考成为许多后世批评家了解该主题的入门。他们强调了“第三性”，即符号与指称对象之间“解释者”或人类主体的作用，这成为反驳关于符号与指称对象之间关系是否可靠中介的怀疑论的一种有力方式。

Steven Knapp and Walter Benn Michaels are “neo-pragmatists,” influenced most directly by an important book of the 1970s by the philosopher Richard Rorty, Philosophy and the Mirror of Nature; Rorty in turn worked in a tradition that goes back through John Dewey in the 1930s and 1940s, and before then not only to the great philosophical interventions of William James, Henry’s brother, but also and perhaps most importantly to the theory of signs worked out by the philosopher Charles Sanders Peirce. Peirce’s quirky and difficult theory, which is most perspicuous in his Letters to Lady Welby, was not widely known in its day except among a few colleagues, including James. It was taken up, though, by a circle at the University of Cambridge headed by I. A. Richards. In The Meaning of Meaning, which published excerpts from the Letters to Lady Welby in an appendix, Richards and C. K. Ogden devoted some reflections to Peirce’s semiotics that became the introduction to the subject for many later critics. They emphasized “thirdness,” or the role of an “interpretant” or human agent between sign and referent, which came to be an influential way of retorting against skepticism that the relation between sign and reference is reliably mediated.

如今，实用主义或新实用主义在学术文学思想中日益盛行。皮尔斯的符号学之所以被视为索绪尔符号学的替代方案，是因为它植根于物质世界，并反映了社会互动的动态，包括“阐释共同体”的动态。我将尝试通过克纳普和迈克尔斯的文章来介绍其中的一些观点，并最终阐明，我希望能够证明，索绪尔的前提并非像克纳普和迈克尔斯所认为的那样可以轻易被驳倒。（关于索绪尔对皮尔斯本人的重新解读，我推荐翁贝托·埃科的文章《皮尔斯的阐释概念》，该文认为阐释者并非人类主体，而是一种中介符号。¹）

Today, pragmatism, or neo-pragmatism, is increasingly influential in academic literary thinking. Peirce’s semiotics is proposing itself as an alternative to Saussure’s because it is materially grounded and reflects the dynamics of social interchange, including that of “interpretive communities.” I shall try to introduce some of these ideas by way of the Knapp and Michaels essay, concluding by showing, I hope, why Saussurian premises can’t be dismissed as easily as Knapp and Michaels suggest that they can. (For a Saussurian rereading of Peirce himself, I refer you to an article by Umberto Eco called “Peirce’s Notion of the Interpretant,” which sees the interpretant not as a human agent but as an intermediary sign.1)

1982年是美国文学理论热度与挫败感并存的巅峰时期。正如我们之前所说，文学理论在当时是一个热门话题，而如今已不再如此。我们对文学理论的兴趣——或者至少是对索绪尔式文学理论的兴趣——如今至少在某种程度上已成为历史，正如我们之前所指出的。然而，在1982年，你对这些问题持何种立场至关重要，而克纳普和迈克尔斯的《反对理论》正是在这种氛围下出版的。

1982 was the high-water mark of both the fascination and the frustration with literary theory in this country. It was a hot-button topic—as we’ve said before—in ways that it is not really today. Our interest in literary theory—or at least in what I might as well go ahead and call Saussurian literary theory—is now at least in part historical, as we have indicated. In 1982, though, where you stood on these matters just made all the difference, and it was in that atmosphere that Knapp and Michaels’s “Against Theory” was published.

新实用主义者和索绪尔主义者一样“反基础主义”（这个词是罗蒂用的），他们不把客观世界作为知识和交流的基础，但对新实用主义者来说，重要的是要记住，我们确实知道一些事情（无论出于什么原因：正如文章所论证的，知识和信念之间没有区别）；我们不可能不知道一些事情；而且我们必然且恰当地基于我们所知采取行动，从而在社会环境中扮演行动者的角色。对新实用主义者来说，言语和其他所有行动一样，都是一种行动形式。你可以看出，新实用主义者坚持认为行动是人类存在的核心特征，至少在修辞层面上，这使得他们比解构主义者等其他理论家更强烈地抵制虚无主义或激进怀疑论所带来的所谓“破坏性影响”。

A neo-pragmatist is as “anti-foundational” (the word is Rorty’s) as a Saussurian, offering no account of the objective world as a basis for knowledge and communication, but for the neo-pragmatist the important thing to remember is that we just do know things (for whatever reason: as the essay argues, there is no difference between knowledge and belief); we can’t not know things; and we act, both necessarily and properly, on the basis of what we know, hence playing out the role of agents in our social environment. For the neo-pragmatist, speech is a form of agency like all other actions. You can see that by insisting on agency as the central characteristic of being human, at least as a matter of rhetoric the neo-pragmatist guards much more fervently against the supposed crippling effects of nihilism or radical skepticism than does, for example, the deconstructionist.

你在斯坦利·菲什的文章中大致接触过这些观点。菲什认为，我们通过自身能动性所相信并强化的知识，很大程度上是由我们所属的阐释社群所建构的。你会注意到，在克纳普和迈克尔斯的文章第三部分，他们对菲什的观点进行了礼貌的反驳。他们显然总体上同意菲什的观点，但他们指出菲什的例子恰恰说明了，人们很容易在不经意的口误中重蹈覆辙，养成不良的思维习惯。为此，他们找到了菲什文章中的一段话，菲什在其中又回到了“我们持有知识是与信念相关的，而不仅仅是作为信念”这一观点。菲什在后来出版的《反对理论》一书中对此做出了回应，但这实际上只是一次关于短暂而肤浅问题的友好交流。在本次讲座中，我将重点关注克纳普和迈克尔斯提出的三个论点中的前两个；关于知识和信念这个哲学问题，我将不再赘述，罗蒂的著作对此进行了更深入的探讨。

You encountered roughly these views in the essay of Stanley Fish, who argues that what we believe and reinforce as knowledge through our agency is largely produced by the interpretive community to which we belong. You’ll notice now that in the third part of their essay, Knapp and Michaels engage in polite disagreement with Fish. Their broad agreement with him is clear, but they point to him as an object lesson in how easy it is to reproduce bad habits of thought in a casual slip of tongue. To this end, they find a particular passage in Fish where he slips back into the idea that we hold knowledge in relation to belief, not simply as belief. Fish writes one of the responses in the subsequent book called Against Theory, but this is really a friendly exchange about a transitory and superficial matter. In this lecture, I’m going to pay a lot of attention to the first two arguments of the three offered by Knapp and Michaels; I’ll have little more to say about knowledge and belief, a philosophical issue best reviewed in Rorty.

你会注意到他们的语气与菲什非常相似。这是一种直截了当、毫不含糊、直奔主题的语气，读过德里达或拉康之后，你或许会如释重负地感受到，仿佛摆脱了辩证法的纠缠和摇摆。某种程度上，这种语气是必然的。它源于对新实用主义观点的拥抱，因为你实际上是在告诉读者：做你想做的，想你想想的，不要费力寻找理由，直接开始思考和行动。作为一名文学诠释者，你必然会对所读的内容持有某种观点；你无法避免这一点；所以，只要你在诠释你所读的内容，就直接开始吧。如果你不想以未经中介的读者身份进行独立解读（而且由于解读不可能客观，你或许会选择放弃解读），那么你可以转而研究解读的根基：为什么其他人会在历史上所有可辨识的解读社群（或“公共领域”，借用哈贝马斯相关术语的常用变体）中发表过那样的言论。你唯一可能犯的错误就是拼凑一些理论论证来为自己的行为辩护。

You’ll notice that their tone is very similar to that of Fish. It’s a downright, no-nonsense, let’s-get-on-with-it tone that, after reading Derrida or Lacan, you may well encounter with relief as a vacation from dialectical tacking and veering. In a way, the tone comes with the territory. It follows from the embrace of neo-pragmatist views because what you’re telling your reader is, in effect, you just do what you do and think what you think, don’t grope around for rationales, just get on with the business of thinking and doing. As a literary interpreter, you’re bound to have some opinion about what you’re reading; you can’t escape having one; so as long as you’re interpreting what you read, just get on with it. If you don’t want to interpret on your own in the role of an unmediated reader (and since it’s hard to forget that interpretation can’t be objective, you may prefer to give it up), you can study instead the grounds of interpretation: why other people have said what they said in all the interpretive communities (or “public spheres,” to cite the frequently used adaptation of the equivalent term of Habermas) that can be specified historically. The only way you can go wrong is to cobble together some theoretical justification for what you’re doing.

克纳普和迈克尔斯认为，人们之所以会不必要地、错误地陷入理论提出的问题中，是因为他们犯了三个根本性的错误（第三个错误仍然是将知识和信念割裂开来）。第一个错误是假定意义和意图之间存在差异：换句话说，一方面，要理解意义，就必须能够唤起意图；另一方面，如果没有意图，我们就无法确定意义。这是他们的第一个论点：当人们犯下某种形式的错误（即意图与意义分离的错误）时，他们就会陷入理论的泥潭。我们稍后会回到这个论点。第二个论点源于他们坚持认为语言和言语之间没有区别。他们反对索绪尔的观点，即语言（langue）实际上存在于我们大脑中，就像一个数据库，它产生言语（parole），也就是我们逐句说出的话。这些论点都声称，“理论”之所以能够成立，是因为它假定或预设了头脑中某种先前的状态与将该状态付诸行动的时刻之间存在差异，而严格来说，始终只有行动的时刻。

Knapp and Michaels argue that people become needlessly and erroneously entangled with problems raised by theory when they make three fundamental mistakes (the third being, again, the factoring apart of knowledge and belief). The first is to suppose that there is a difference between meaning and intention: in other words, that to arrive at a meaning you have to be able to invoke an intention, on the one hand; or, on the other hand, that in the absence of an intention we cannot decide upon a meaning. That’s their first argument: people become embroiled in theory when they make one version or another (its theoretical opponent) of the mistake that divides intention from meaning. We’ll come back to that argument in a minute. The second argument follows from their insistence that there is no difference between language and speech. They reject the Saussurian idea that language, or langue, is virtually present as a database in our heads that produces speech, parole, that which is uttered from sentence to sentence. Each of these arguments claims that “theory” enables itself by positing or presupposing a difference between some prior state of things in the mind and the moment of putting that state of things into action, whereas properly speaking there is always only the moment of being in action.

在更仔细地审视这些论点之前，我应该先停下来思考一下作者们对理论的理解。有趣的是，克纳普和迈克尔斯在第一段中将某些准科学的文学思考方式排除在了他们对理论的普遍批判之外：

Before I consider these arguments more closely, I should pause over the authors’ sense of what theory is and is not. In their first paragraph, Knapp and Michaels interestingly exempt certain quasi-scientific ways of thinking about literature from their general indictment of theory:

“理论”一词有时被用来指代一些与具体作品解读并无直接关联的文学主题，例如叙事学、文体学和韵律学。然而，尽管这些主题具有普遍性，但在我们看来，它们本质上是经验性的，因此我们反对理论的论点并不适用于它们。
The term [“theory”] is sometimes applied to literary subjects with no direct bearing on the interpretation of individual works, such as narratology, stylistics, and prosody. Despite their generality, however, these subjects seem to us essentially empirical, and our arguments against theory will not apply to them.

这有点出乎意料，因为首先，在这门理应专注于理论的课程中，我们确实讨论过其中一些内容：叙事学；文体学，即研究文体及其句法和统计方法的科学；以及韵律学，诗学的一个分支，它通过数据分析来形成关于诗歌结构方式的一般性观点。所有这些研究活动都让我们联想到俄国形式主义者。我们所学的叙事学很大程度上源于结构主义，甚至也源于弗洛伊德的某些思想，这种渊源使其听起来颇似理论。然而，对于克纳普和迈克尔斯来说，他们将这些文学思考方式排除在理论挑战之外，他们称之为“经验主义”。我们暂且不深入探讨他们区分好的观察和坏的思辨活动之间的区别——这种区别似乎决定了他们为何将“诗学”排除在非理论之外——对于反基础主义者来说，做出这样的区分应该很难（究竟什么才算事实？）——或许有必要顺便提一下，克纳普和迈克尔斯所谓的“理论”用“诠释学”来形容更为恰当。他们“反对诠释学”，反对为解释寻找理由的做法。

This is a little surprising because for one thing, in this course, which is presumably devoted to theory, we’ve talked about some of these things: narratology; stylistics, which is the science of style and how one can approach it syntactically and statistically; and prosody, an aspect of poetics that works though data to form general ideas about how poems are put together. All of these permissible activities must remind us of the Russian formalists. Narratology, as we studied it, is largely derived from structuralism, indeed also from certain ideas of Freud, and that pedigree makes it sound suspiciously like theory. For Knapp and Michaels, though, those ways of thinking about literature that they exempt from their challenge to theory are what they call “empirical.” Without lingering over the distinction between good observational and bad speculative pursuits that seems to govern their exemption of “poetics” for nontheory—a distinction that should be hard for an anti-foundationalist to make (what counts as a fact?)—it may be useful to remark in passing that a better word for what Knapp and Michaels call “theory” is surely “hermeneutics.” They are “against hermeneutics,” the search for rationales for interpretation.

所以：意图和意义必然是同一回事，语言和言语也必然是同一回事。在我们开始思考这些论断时，我想请大家记住斯坦利·卡维尔在《反理论》一书中对本文的回应中提出的这句话：“我能知道一个词的意义，但我能知道一个词的意图吗？”这是一个发人深省的挑战，我们将在后续的讨论中深入探讨它的一些含义。

So: intention and meaning just must be the same thing, and then, too, language and speech just must be the same thing. As we begin to think about these claims, I’d like you to keep in mind the sentence “I can know the meaning of a word, but can I know the intention of a word?” by Stanley Cavell, from his response to this essay in the book, Against Theory. That’s an invigorating challenge, and we’ll be reflecting on some of its implications in the long run.

在很多方面，我都会赞同克纳普和迈克尔斯的观点，事实上几乎完全赞同，但我打算在最后阶段来个急转弯，我希望这个转弯能够拯救理论，并最终使其变得必要。这是我的职责。经过二十六次讲座，我实在无法承认我们一直在讨论的东西应该从我们的词汇中彻底消失。所以我将尝试斩杀这条恶龙，但你们还得耐心等待一段时间，因为正如我所说，这是一条非常聪明、拥有诸多优点的恶龙。

I’m going to be going a long way down the road in agreement with Knapp and Michaels in what I say now, indeed almost all the way, but I intend to take a sharp turn toward the end of the road that, I hope, saves theory and makes it necessary after all. It’s my duty. I can hardly after twenty-six lectures finally confess that the thing we have been talking about should be banished from our vocabulary. So I’ll try to slay the dragon, but you’re going to have to wait a while because, as I say, it’s a very smart dragon with many virtues.

克纳普和迈克尔斯认为，在我们开始钻研理论之前，我们应该理所当然地认为任何言语都带有意图，而且这种想法是正确的。每当我们遇到我们认为是语言的声音或符号时，我们仅仅因为这样就赋予了它意图；他们认为，语言的定义本身就是意图性的。因此，对于那些我们无法推断其作者的声音和符号，我们就否认它们具有语言的地位，因为我们认为它们没有意图。

Knapp and Michaels say that before we start troubling our heads with theory, we just take it for granted that any utterance has an intention, and rightly so. Whenever we encounter sounds or marks that we suppose to be language, we accord it an intention simply in so doing; language is by definition intentional, they say. Sounds and marks of which we can infer no author, therefore, we deny the status of language because we don’t think they are intended.

克纳普和迈克尔斯举了一个如今广为人知的例子来检验这个假设，并让我们意识到，如果我们自以为知道某件事的含义，那将是多么危险。通常情况下，我们会脱口而出：“我知道那是什么意思”，或者至少会说：“它肯定有某种含义，即使我不知道它具体是什么意思。” 这就是我们对待一段语言的通常方式，前提是我们相信它是语言。假设我们走在沙滩上，偶然发现四条线——“线”这个词本身就带有危险性——也就是说，沙滩上有四排痕迹，看起来很像华兹华斯的诗作《沉睡封印了我的灵魂》的第一节：

Knapp and Michaels give us a now-famous example in which this assumption is tested, and make us realize what’s at stake in supposing that we know the meaning of something. Ordinarily, we just spontaneously say, “I know what that means,” or at least, “It must mean something even though I don’t know what it means.” That’s our normal approach to a piece of language when we believe it to be language. Suppose, then, we’re walking on the beach and come across four lines—“lines” is already a dangerous thing to say—that is, then, four rows of marks in the sand, that look an awful lot like the first stanza of Wordsworth’s “A Slumber Did My Spirit Seal”:

沉睡封印了我的灵魂；
A slumber did my spirit seal;
我没有丝毫人类的恐惧。
I had no human fears.
她似乎是一个没有感觉的东西。
She seem’d a thing that could not feel
岁月的痕迹。
The touch of earthly years.

我们并不感到困惑，因为我们猜想是某个华兹华斯爱好者走过来，在沙滩上刻下了这些字迹。它们就在那里，是对一段有意为之的引述。这段引述的含义很难理解（一些现代最杰出的评论家也为此绞尽脑汁），但既然它是刻意为之，就必然有其意义。这时，一波浪潮涌上岸，在第一节诗的正下方，留下了看似第二节诗的痕迹，这自然让我们感到困惑不已：

We are not perplexed because we assume some Wordsworth lover has come along and scratched these lines in the sand. There they are, an intended quotation of an intended utterance. It’s very hard to know what the utterance means (some of the best critics of modern times have broken their heads against it), but because it’s intended, it must mean something. Then a wave washes ashore and leaves what looks like the second stanza on the beach, right underneath the first one, and that naturally throws us for a loop:

她现在没有一丝动静，也没有一丝力气；
No motion has she now, no force;
她既听不见也看不见；
She neither hears nor sees;
随着地球自转轴的转动，
Roll’d round in earth’s diurnal course,
有岩石、石头和树木。
With rocks, and stones, and trees.

或许，正如克纳普和迈克尔斯所推测的那样，大海是一种泛神论的存在，它喜欢写诗，那么这节诗就是大海的杰作。或许，有一些小人乘坐着一艘小小的潜艇正在进行一项实验。这样一来，我们或许还能勉强推断出这节诗的作者，但更有可能的是，我们会说这只是一个惊人的巧合，的确惊人，但仅仅是一个巧合而已。还能是什么呢？

Maybe, as Knapp and Michaels help us to speculate, the sea is a kind of pantheistic being that likes to write poetry, in which case the sea intended the stanza. Maybe there are tiny men in a tiny submarine who are conducting an experiment. At a stretch, we can still infer authors for the stanza, then, but it’s much more likely that we’ll just say it’s an amazing coincidence, truly amazing, but just a coincidence. What else could it be?

这项练习的目的是让我们意识到，无论我们假定哪些痕迹是文字，我们实际上都预设了这些痕迹具有某种意图。如果沙滩上那些看起来像文字的痕迹并非由任何人或任何存在（包括神灵）所书写，那么这些痕迹就不是语言，而只是碰巧像语言而已。即便它们看起来像语言，我们也会突然意识到，认为它们具有意义是多么愚蠢。有一首诗与我们眼前看到的这堆痕迹完全吻合，那首诗是有意义的，但这堆痕迹本身却没有意义。

The point of the exercise is to make us realize that wherever we suppose marks to be writing, we already suppose an intention for the marks. If nobody wrote the marks on the beach that look like words, if no entity or being from God on down wrote them, then the marks are not language but only like language, coincidentally so. And even though they look like language, we suddenly realize that it would be foolish to think they have meaning. There is a poem that exactly resembles this bunch of marks that we see in front of us, and that poem has meaning, but this bunch of marks does not have meaning.

现在我想，我们大多数人可能都会反对“我们无法解读一堆符号”这种说法。我们或许认同意图即意义，但我们想说的是，如果某个东西看起来像是某种意图的体现，那么我们完全可以根据它所呈现的意义进行相应的解读。或许我们可以找到一个更清晰的例子来说明意图与单纯存在之间的区别——前者是语言，后者则不是。

Now I think probably most of us would resist the idea that we can’t interpret the bunch of marks. We can agree that intention just is meaning, but we want to say that if something looks as though it were intended, then nothing prevents us from accordingly interpreting the meaning it looks as though it had. Perhaps a clearer example of the difference between something intended and something merely existent, the former being language and the latter not, could have been found.

例如，几年前，《纽黑文纪事报》刊登了一张照片，照片上是两位女士在附近的米尔福德，正欣喜若狂地凝视着树干上的一道疤痕，那疤痕看起来像耶稣的头像。不仅是这两位女士，还有数百人前来参观。当然，他们相信这道疤痕之所以如此，是因为上帝有意将其作为某种象征。对他们来说，其含义显而易见。他们也知道，烤奶酪三明治也曾出现过类似的情况。但许多信仰较弱的人会说，上帝并没有让这道疤痕长成这样，这只是一个意外。在这种情况下，没有人会说那是耶稣的脸，或者任何种类的脸，只会说它看起来像一张脸。这样就不会有人想要去解读这道疤痕的含义。正因如此，在我看来，这比华兹华斯诗歌中那道偶然出现的疤痕更能说明问题，因为后者仍然会引发人们的解读。诚然，这样做会让我们假定某种神秘的作者身份，但请注意，对于这道疤痕，我们却没有这样的解读空间。例如，我们不能说“自然”使这些痕迹变成了一张脸，因为我们知道只有基督教的上帝通过自然或通过法令（因此风、细胞生长或穿着白大褂的小人都不能被视为代理人）来创造耶稣的形象。

For example, some years ago the New Haven Register published a picture of two ladies in Milford, near here, gazing in rapture at a scar on a tree trunk that looked like the head of Jesus. Not just these ladies but hundreds of people visited the site. Now of course they believed the scar looked that way because God intended it to be a sign. For them, the meaning was clear. The same thing has happened with toasted cheese sandwiches, as they knew. But many of weaker faith would say that God didn’t make the scar look like that, it was just an accident, and in that case no one would say it is the face of Jesus or a face of any kind, only that it looks like a face. There would be no temptation to interpret the scar, and this is why it seems to me a better example than the accidental simulacrum of Wordsworth’s poem, which would still cry out to be read. Granted that in doing so we are positing some mysterious authorship, but notice that we have no such flexibility with the scar. We can’t say that “nature” made the marks a face, for example, because we know that only the Christian God acting through nature or by fiat (hence neither wind nor cell growth nor tiny men in lab coats understood as agents) would make a likeness of Jesus.

简而言之，无论你对《沉睡封印了我的灵魂》这首歌有何感想，就那道形似耶稣的伤疤而言，你都会欣然接受克纳普和迈克尔斯的论证。你会赞同他们的观点，认为这确实取决于对意图的推断。没有意图，就没有意义；但如果可以推断出意图，那么意图本身就是意义。我认为这对于任何言语行为都是一个无可辩驳的论证——至少，出于稍后会阐述的原因，只要我们能将它们称为言语行为，而我们也会尽可能地这样做。或许，要理解意图本身就是意义，你只需要从词源学的角度思考一下。当我说“我的意思是”时，我的意思是“我希望你理解某某某”。并非所有语言都是如此（德语中有Ich meine，意思是“我打算”，但有 das heißt或das bedeutet，意思是“这意味着”，而不是“我的意思是”），但在我们的语言中确实如此，这或许能帮助我们意识到，将词语分开来理解是违背常识的。

In short, however you feel about “A Slumber Did My Spirit Seal,” in the case of the scar that looks like Jesus you would readily accept Knapp and Michaels’s argument. You would say in confirmation of their view that it really does depend on the inference of an intention. No intention, no meaning, but if an intention can be inferred, that intention just is the meaning. I think this an unshakable argument concerning any and all utterances—at least, for reasons that will appear, insofar as we can call them speech acts, which we shall do insofar as we can. Perhaps in order to see that intention just is meaning you need only think about it etymologically. When I say “I mean,” I mean “I intend you to understand that such and such.” It doesn’t quite work that way in all languages (in German you have Ich meine, I intend, but das heißt or das bedeutet—that means, not I mean), but it does work that way in ours, and it may help us realize that it’s against the grain of common sense to factor the words apart.

你对某个含义或意图的理解可能存在偏差，事实上，你很可能确实错了，但这与含义和意图之间是否存在区别这个问题无关。如果一个句子不是由某个主体（无论是人还是其他生物）有意说出的，它就没有意义，因为它就不是克纳普和迈克尔斯所说的“语言”。这实际上引出了本文的第二个论点。再次重申，要将一个话语理解为语言，就必须假定其包含某种意图。反之，如果我们无法推断出意图，我们也应该能够认识到，我们所看到的并非语言，而只是语言的模拟物，就像猴子用打字机打出的字一样，是对语言的一种有效复制。

You may be wrong about a meaning or intention, you probably are wrong, in fact, but that has nothing to do with the question of whether there is a difference between the meaning and the intention in question. If a sentence weren’t a sentence spoken intentionally by an agent, human or otherwise, it wouldn’t have meaning because it wouldn’t be what Knapp and Michaels call “language.” This actually carries us into the second proposition of the essay. For an utterance to be understood as language at all, to repeat myself once again, an intention needs to be supposed. Conversely, we ought to be able to recognize, supposing we fail to infer an intention, that what we are looking at is not language but just a simulacrum of language, an effective copy of language like the words produced by monkeys on typewriters.

克纳普和迈克尔斯会说，把非符号的声音或标记当作语言来谈论是没有意义的。对于C.S.皮尔斯来说，他区分了数百种不同的符号，所有符号都是有意识的——也就是说，它们具有能动性和目的性，具有实际功能。皮尔斯会同意索绪尔关于符号具有差异性的观点，但对他而言，关于符号的关键在于它是姿态性的，它承载着某种目的。而这正是语言中符号的特征，而不仅仅是言语中符号的特征。语言中的符号本身就是有意识的，蕴含着它的目的。因此，克纳普和迈克尔斯认为，语言和言语之间没有区别。

It makes no sense, Knapp and Michaels would say, to speak of sounds or marks that are not signs as language. For C. S. Peirce, who discriminated among hundreds of different kinds of signs, all signs are active—that is to say, they have an agency and a purpose, a practical function. Peirce would agree with Saussure that signs are differential, but for him the important point to make about a sign is that it is gestural, it carries out a purpose. And this is the characteristic of a sign in language, not just in speech. The sign in language is already active, fraught with its purpose. Hence, Knapp and Michaels say, there is no difference between language and speech.

对于任何从索绪尔那里汲取了“语言是虚拟空间中的共时实体，而言语是实际时间中语言的历时性实践”这一理念的人来说，这种说法都很难接受。但让我们先来理解一下克纳普和迈克尔斯的论点是如何成立的。我认为他们最有力的论证体现在一个脚注中，而这个脚注，如同许多脚注一样，或许是整篇文章中最具启发性的部分：“词典是特定言语行为中常用词汇的索引，而非抽象的、先于意图的可能性矩阵。”仔细想想这句话。我们此前一直认为，语言除了是一套语法和句法规则之外，也是一套用于描述言语行为的定义。克纳普和迈克尔斯在他们的脚注中否定了这一前提。他们声称，词典的定义仅仅是所有词语实际运用情况的总和，因此，任何词条所定义的词语本身就是一个言语行为。 《牛津英语词典》对每个词条都给出了多个定义，这些定义都嵌入在句子中，构成言语行为。即使将这些言语行为从句子中剥离出来，我们仍然可以理解它们所体现的行动主体性。从这个角度来看，定义既是言语行为的产物，也是言语行为的载体。词典中的任何词条都是该词条在历史长河中如何运作的记录。词典是所有言语行为的总和。因此，将语言视为独立于行动主体而存在的事物，将言语视为语言转化为行动的过程，是一种错误。语言，即便从它总是先于我们存在的角度来看，仍然是对我们之前发生的言语行为的记录。词典与历史演讲汇编一样，都是对预期言语行为的汇编。“理论”因此不应再去寻找一个先前的言语媒介来为言语行为奠定基础，正如它不应再去寻找一个意图来证明某种意义的合理性一样。

This claim should be very hard to accept for anyone who has absorbed from Saussure the idea that language is a synchronic entity in virtual space and speech is a diachronic performance of language in actual time. But let us make sure we understand how Knapp and Michaels’ claim can be a plausible one. I think they make their best case in a footnote, which, like so many footnotes, may be the most telling moment in the essay: “[A] dictionary is an index of frequent usages in particular speech acts—not a matrix of abstract, pre-intentional possibilities.” Think about that. Language, we have supposed until now, in addition to being a set of grammatical and syntactical rules, is also a set of definitions made available for speech acts. Knapp and Michaels deny this premise in their footnote. They’re claiming that dictionary definitions are just the sum total, as it were, of words in action, hence that any entry defines a word that is already a speech act. The Oxford English Dictionary gives you multiple definitions of a word, all embedded in sentences, speech acts that can be taken out of sentences and still understood in their agency as performed. Definitions, in this view, are made available by speech acts as well as for them. Any word in a dictionary is a fossilized record of the way the word works and has worked in speech acts throughout history. A dictionary is a sum total of speech acts. To distinguish, therefore, between language as something that exists apart from agency and speech as the translation of language into action is a mistake. Language, even in the sense that it’s always there before we are, is nevertheless a record of verbal actions that have taken place before our own. A dictionary is just as much a compendium of intended speech acts as a compendium of historical speeches would be. “Theory,” therefore, should no more seek out a prior verbal medium in which to ground speech than it should seek out an intention to justify a meaning.

我们确实需要在这个思维挑战的道路上走很长一段路，比预期的要长得多。不过，为了维护索绪尔的理论，必须指出，在某种程度上，他预见到了这种观点。（我尚未开始对理论的拯救；这只是顺带提及。）还记得我说过，为了理解结构主义及其后续影响，我们只需要区分语言和言语，langue和parole，但在索绪尔的理论中，实际上存在第三个中间范畴，他称之为langage。它是所有已知言语行为的总和。正如克纳普和迈克尔斯所说，langage是“经验性的”，与他们所说的language 的含义颇为相似。但对索绪尔而言，langue（与langage相对）仍然是一种代码，而非姿态档案。

We do need to go a long way down the road with this challenge to our thinking, longer than expected, to be sure. It should be said in defense of Saussure, though, that in a way he anticipates this position. (I have not yet begun my rescue of theory; this is just a remark in passing.) Remember I told you that in order to understand structuralism and its aftermath, we need only distinguish between language and speech, langue and parole, but that in Saussure there’s actually a third, intermediate, category that he calls langage. That is the sum total of all known speech acts. Langage is “empirical,” as Knapp and Michaels would say, and not unlike what they mean by language. But for Saussure, langue, as opposed to langage, remains a code, not a gestural archive.

新实用主义的语言观之所以对我们有说服力，是因为巴赫金以及我们近期阅读的许多其他著作都让我们确信，语言是社会性的，它的所有运用都是互动性的，源于他人的言语行为，被使用者挪用为自身的一套言语行为，并作为一种言语行为影响他人。如果真是如此，那么语言的存在是为了交流，这似乎是不言而喻的。或许即便经历了这一切，你也从未想过其他可能性。你又何必呢？毕竟，交流就是我们运用语言的方式。如果语言的“用途”确实如此，那么赋予语言以言语所赋予的能动性也就合情合理了。不过，接下来我要讲的就不是理论了，所以请各位做好准备！

The neo-pragmatist view of language is persuasive for us because Bakhtin and many of our other recent readings have convinced us that language is social, that all of its deployments are interactive, derived from the speech acts of others, appropriated for oneself as one’s own set of speech acts, and influential on yet other people as a speech act. If all this is the case, it would just seem to go without saying that language exists for communication. Perhaps even after all we’ve been through it has never occurred to you to think otherwise. Why would you? After all, communication is what we do with language. And if it’s true that that’s what language is “for,” then it makes sense to see it endowed with the agency that speech appropriates. But here is where I’m going to save theory, so sharpen your pencils!

请注意，我说过语言的存在是为了交流，这似乎是不言而喻的。但除此之外，语言还能用于什么呢？说我们喜欢涂鸦，或者在沙滩上留下毫无意义的痕迹，并不能解释得通。我们大多数人并非如此，而这正是赛·托姆布雷（Cy Twombly）的画作如此引人入胜的原因——他喜欢创作看似模糊的文字，实则毫无意义。我们大多数人喜欢留下能够传递信息的痕迹。我们生活在一个几乎不可能有人断言语言并非用于交流的世界里。我们已经将语言打磨得炉火纯青，使其成为一种高效、灵活，有时甚至雄辩的交流媒介。

Notice that I said it would seem to go without saying that language exists for communication. But what else could it exist for? It won’t help much to say that we like to make doodles, or meaningless marks in the sand. Most of us don’t, and that’s what makes the painting of Cy Twombly, who does like to make meaningless marks that look vaguely inscriptive, so interesting. Most of us like to make marks that communicate. We inhabit a life world in which it is almost inconceivable for anyone to assert that language is not meant for communication. We have refined language to a fare-thee-well as an efficient, flexible, sometimes even eloquent medium of communication.

然而，如果我要挽救这套理论，就必须证明这个看似不言自明的前提是错误的。假设我们从一个我称之为思辨人类学的立场来探讨这个问题。大多数关于“自然状态”的讨论——无论是霍布斯、卢梭，还是马克思关于“原始共产主义”的论述——都属于思辨人类学的范畴，是对史前时期的推测，现在轮到我了。让我们试着运用这种朴实无华的语言技巧，并使其为我们所用。他们说，语言的目的是交流。这难道不是说火的目的是烹饪吗？或者，如果你反驳说火是人体外部的，而语言不是：这难道不是说灵活的拇指的目的是抓握吗？但是，无论是外部的还是内部的，即使我们能够做出这样的区分，我也不确定它是否真的重要。岩壁上的洞并非洞穴，并非为居住而生，除非我们赋予它居住的用途。偶然发现用途，才使得火成为烹饪的好帮手，灵活的拇指成为抓握的工具，岩洞成为避难之所。然而，所有这些事物，以各自的方式，原本就存在于那里，并非仅仅为了让我们利用它们来发挥我们发现的用途。用途是我们赋予原本存在的事物的。

Yet if I am going to save theory, I need to show that this apparently self-evident premise is wrong. Suppose we approach the subject from a standpoint that I shall call speculative anthropology. Most discussions of “the state of nature”—in Hobbes or Rousseau or Marx on “primitive communism”—are speculative anthropology, conjectures about prehistory, and I shall now take my turn. Let us try to take the art of the down-to-earth remark and turn it in our favor. The purpose of language, then, so they say, is for communicating. Isn’t that like saying that the purpose of fire is for cooking? Or, if you object that fire is external to the human organism but language isn’t: isn’t that like saying that the purpose of the prehensile thumb is for grasping? But, external or internal, I’m not sure it matters even if we could safely make such a distinction. A hole in a rock face is not a cave, not meant for dwelling, until we adopt it for that purpose. Stumbling on a purpose is what makes fire a good thing to cook with, the prehensile thumb a good thing to grasp with, and a hole in a rock a good thing to take shelter in, but all of them, in their various ways, are just there, and not just there for us to do with them the useful thing we have discovered. A purpose is what we impose on something that is there already.

语言的出现，就像我们人类的拇指一样，是一种进化突变。我们“发现了它的用途”，当然，这种说法并不完全准确。或许更严谨的说法是，我们发现了语言对我们有用的功能——交流。一旦我们能够运用这种奇特的、能够发出不同声音的能力，语言就成为了我们交流的工具。当然，我们成功地运用了语言，或者说，我们用语言建造了一座巴别塔——无论你更倾向于哪种说法——但无论如何，我们拥有了语言，它已经发展成为我们交流的媒介。

Language appeared among us the same way that the prehensile thumb did, as an evolutionary mutation. We “discovered its use,” though granted, that’s an imperfect way to put it. It might be more circumspect to say that we discovered it had a use for us, which was to communicate, and so once we were able to put this strange capacity to make differential sounds to work, henceforth for us and for our purposes language was there to communicate. Of course, we made an enormous success of it, or a tower of Babel of it, whichever you prefer to think, but in any case we have it, and it has developed among us as a medium of communication.

假设在人类出现能够发出各种声音的能力这一基因突变后的第二天，发生了雪崩、地震或海啸，导致拥有这种突变的个体灭绝。此后，或许有人能够通过手势或其他难以想象的符号系统进行交流，甚至可能拥有惊人的口才，乃至文学天赋。或者，智人可能在进化过程中走了一条弯路，以至于交流不再是人类独有的技能。所有有感知能力的生物都会在某种意义上进行交流，使用符号系统，而这些符号系统在很大程度上只是语言的隐喻形式。但我们这个物种或许在进化过程中发生了某种转变，此后，无论我们发展出何种非凡的能力，交流方式都与老鼠或蚂蚁之间的交流方式并无太大区别。

Suppose that the day after the capacity to deploy varied sounds appeared as a mutation, there was an avalanche or earthquake or tsunami that rendered the possessor of the mutation extinct. In aftertimes there might then have been people communicating, perhaps with incredible eloquence, perhaps even with literary genius, by means of hand gestures or other sign systems that surpass conjecture. Or for that matter, Homo sapiens might have taken a detour in its development such that communication was not anything one could identify as specifically human. All sentient beings communicate in a certain sense, using semiotic systems that are for the most part only metaphorically language, but it’s possible that our particular species could have taken a turn in its development after which, no matter what other extraordinary powers we developed, communication remained much as it is among mice or ants.

你看，这一切皆有可能，当我们从人类学的角度思考语言——我们用于交流的一种属性——时，就会发现这一点。语言的存在方式使得我认为，说它的目的是交流几乎无关紧要。它仅仅是一种现象，就像羽毛一样，碰巧对某些事物有用，这与那些毫无用处的基因突变截然不同。

All of this is possible, you see, when we think about language—an attribute that we use for communication—anthropologically. It exists in such a way that it is, I would think, scarcely relevant to say that its purpose is for communication. It is simply a phenomenon, like feathers, that turns out to be useful for something, unlike mutations for which no use is found.

如果我们遵循索绪尔的观点，就会注意到我们对语言符号的重视程度有所不同。索绪尔强调语言是由差异性和任意性的符号构成的。他否认语言中存在所谓的自然符号。索绪尔和俄国形式主义者——你可能还记得，他们的研究始于发现文学语言中那些不具有交流功能的方面——都告诫我们不要相信拟声词——例如“哔哔哔”——实际上是源自声音或事物、感觉的属性的自然符号。索绪尔认为，拟声符号是词源历史的偶然产物。拟声词在语言中出现频率相当高，因为它便于交流，而且用它交流也很有趣，但它并非作为自然符号进入语言的。它只是在特定词语的演变过程中，当声音和指称对象之间的关系看似自然时才出现的。 Bow-wow 和wauwau在语音上都是拟声词，但在它们各自所属的语言中，它们与其他符号的不同关系决定了它们的具体轮廓和用法。

Notice something about the signs of language to which we give credence if we follow Saussure. Saussure lays every stress on the idea that language is made up of differential and arbitrary signs. He denies that there is such a thing in language as a natural sign. Both Saussure and the Russian formalists—who began their research, you will recall, by discovering aspects of literary language that do not communicate—warn us against believing that onomatopoetic devices—for example, “peep, peep, peep”—are actually natural signs derived from sounds or attributes of things or feelings in the world. Saussure argues that onomatopoetic signs are accidents of etymological history. There’s a fairly high incidence of onomatopoeia in language because it facilitates communication and it’s fun to communicate with, but it doesn’t enter language as a natural sign. It only passes through moments, in the evolution of a given word, when the relationship between sound and referent seems to be natural. Bow-wow and wauwau are both onomatopoetic in speech, but in the languages to which they respectively belong their differential relations with other signs is what conditions their exact contours and usage.

索绪尔和俄国形式主义者都非常重视这一点。当你读到他们反复论述这个看似微不足道的观点时，你或许会疑惑他们为何如此。然而，你可以看出，对他们而言，对拟声词进行恰当的符号学理解至关重要，因为它奠定了他们关于语言的核心信念——如今正受到克纳普和迈克尔斯的挑战——即语言并非言语。当我们说话时，我们不仅试图交流，也试图指称。换句话说，我们试图使语言与自然世界相符。我们采用一套符号系统，一套本身并非自然而是任意的编码，并试图使语言的符号看起来自然。这样做，我们强化了语言存在的目的是为了交流的观念。但我认为，语言并非为了交流；言语才是。

This is a matter upon which great stress is laid both in Saussure and in the Russian formalists. When you read the passages in which they belabor this seemingly trivial point, you may have wondered why they do so. You can see, though, that a properly semiotic understanding of onomatopoeia is important to them because it anchors their core belief about language—now being attacked by Knapp and Michaels—which is precisely that language is not speech. When we speak, we not only try to communicate; we try to refer. In other words, we try to make language correspond to the natural world. We take a system of signs, a code that is not in itself natural but arbitrary, and try to make the signs of language seem natural. In doing so, we reinforce the idea that language exists for communication. But I would say that language isn’t for communication; speech is.

但这一点也需要加以限定，这对于理论的复兴至关重要。正如俄国形式主义者所论证的那样，我们说话或写作并非总是仅仅为了交流。我们的言语中会浮现出一些奇特的模式和关系——例如，不必要或不精炼的重复——这些模式和关系似乎无助于交流。事实上，它们似乎反而阻碍了交流。当我真正开始在组合轴上混杂各种元素时——例如，在刘易斯·卡罗尔的诗句“时值薄暮，滑溜溜的托夫斯/在波浪中旋转翻滚”中——我强调的是节奏、模式和声音重复等元素，这些元素与交流本身并无直接关联，反而会阻碍理解。

But this too is a point that needs to be qualified in a way that’s crucial for the recovery of theory. We don’t always speak, or write, solely to communicate, as the Russian formalists demonstrated. There are peculiar patterns and relations that surface in our speech—unnecessary or uneconomical forms of repetition, for example—that don’t seem to further communication. As a matter of fact, they actually seem to impede it. When I really start mixing things up on the axis of combination—for example, in Lewis Carroll’s “ ’Twas brillig, and the slithy toves / did gyre and gimble in the wabe”—I am laying stress on elements of rhythm, pattern, and sound recurrence that cannot be said to have any direct bearing on communication and that thwart understanding.

这些都是语言在言语中显露的经验事实，因此不能被克纳普和迈克尔斯简单地斥为理论。我们反复认识到的是语言在言语中呈现自身的方式。那些浮现出来的无意义的成分，正是语言对其进化起源的肯定，以及它拒绝完全被智人赋予它的目的——交流——所奴役的表现。同样，在弗洛伊德的理论中，弗洛伊德式口误——即人们无法完整地说完一句话而不犯错，而且常常是令人尴尬的错误——正是那些有意识地努力清晰表达却无法控制的东西的涌现。

These are all empirical facts about language as it peeps through speech, hence cannot be dismissed by Knapp and Michaels as mere theory. What we have learned to recognize recurrently is the way language makes itself heard in speech. Those elements of gratuitous nonsense that bubble up to the surface are language’s assertion of its evolutionary origin and its refusal to be enslaved altogether by the purpose that Homo sapiens found for it, communication. Similarly in Freud, the Freudian slip—the fact that one can’t get through a sentence without making some kind of blunder, often an embarrassing blunder—is the bubbling up of that which the conscious effort to speak intelligibly can’t control.

同样地，我们从对言语行为的实证研究中认识到，语言并非如此，它不受意识的控制，尤其是在字典定义无法反映实际使用情况的时刻。我们从言语行为的不规则性中推断语言。这种语言意识——我将在结论部分详细阐述——让我觉得克纳普和迈克尔斯关于语言和言语之间并无本质区别的说法是误导性的。如果语言和言语之间确实存在区别，正如我所主张的那样，并且如果这种区别正如索绪尔及其后继者直至解构主义所教导的那样，那么我们就成功地拯救了文学理论，并且顺便找到了一种描述其实用价值的方法：文学理论是对言语中语言的研究。

By the same token, we recognize language to be something else, something not subject to the control of consciousness, from the empirical study of speech acts in those moments when no dictionary definition could reflect conformance with active usage. We infer language from the erratic behavior of speech. That sense of language, which I’m going to be talking a lot more about in my concluding remarks, is what suggests to me that Knapp and Michaels mislead us in saying that there is really no difference between language and speech. If there is a difference between language and speech, as I am claiming, and if this difference is much as we have been taught to think of it by Saussure and his successors down through deconstruction, we have succeeded in rescuing literary theory, and we have incidentally found a way of describing what it is good for, pragmatically speaking: literary theory is the study of language in speech.

然而，实用主义者可能会回应说，即便这个观点成立，这充其量也只是理论的得不偿失的胜利。毕竟，我们是实用主义者，我们想要提倡人的能动性，强调言语以及阐释过程中那些促成交流和意义生成的方面。如果我所能想到的仅仅是指出1914年俄国形式主义者所关注的表达简洁性上的缺陷，那我岂不是以相当大的代价拯救了理论？即使是他们，也很快就超越了这一点，不是吗？好吧，在下一讲，也是最后一讲中，我将尝试证明他们并没有超越这一点，他们的研究方法扩展到了所有可以被视为文学手法的领域，包括指称本身——而且他们开创的传统仍然有很大的发展空间。

A pragmatist might respond, though, that even if the point is granted, this is at most a Pyrrhic victory for theory. We’re pragmatists, after all, we want to promote human agency and underline those aspects of speech, and of the interpretive process, whereby communication is effected and meaning is arrived at. I would seem to have saved theory at a pretty considerable cost if all I can think to do with it is point out the lapses in economy of expression that preoccupied the Russian formalists in 1914. Even they quickly got beyond that, didn’t they? Well, in the next and last lecture I’ll try to show that they did not, that their approach expanded to cover every device that could ever be considered literary, including reference itself—and that the tradition they started still has much to achieve.

最后一点，这又回到了克纳普和迈克尔斯所否认的意义与意图之间的区别。他们认为，两个对立的文学阵营其实是搬起石头砸自己的脚。一方面，像E·D·赫希这样的人认为，可以通过援引作者的意图来确定意义。另一方面，解构主义阵营的人则认为，由于不存在可推断的意图，文本本身就没有意义。但这并非解构主义的本意。它并非强调文本没有意义，甚至也不是强调我们无法确定文本的意义是什么。解构主义的重点在于，你无法将意义局限在文本之中。文本蕴含着太多的意义；它们会因意义的过剩而爆发。你无法通过推断意图来控制文本产生意义的方式，因为即使能够正确确定意图——即便这有可能——也永远无法解释语言在言语中以及通过言语迸发出的爆发力。因此，我们之所以能够将理论从“语言与言语没有区别”的论断中拯救出来，其立场同样也回应了“意图与言语没有区别”的论断。语言本身并不存在意图。正如卡维尔所说，我可以知道一个词的含义，但我能知道一个词的意图吗？

One last point for now, which takes us back to the distinction between meaning and intention that Knapp and Michaels deny. They argue that two opposed literary camps are hoisted by the same petard. On the one hand, there are people like E. D. Hirsch, who believe that you can invoke an author’s intention in order to pin down a meaning. On the other, there are people in the deconstructive camp who say that because there is no inferable intention, texts themselves have no meaning. But that’s not what deconstruction says. It is not at all the point that texts have no meaning, nor even finally that one can’t be sure what the meaning is. What deconstruction says is that you can’t rope off meaning in a text. Texts have too much meaning; they explode with excess of meaning. You can’t corral the way texts produce meaning by inferring an intention, because even an intention correctly ascertained—were that possible—would never account for the eruption of language in and through speech. So the position we have taken in rescuing theory from the claim that there is no difference between language and speech is a position that likewise responds to the claim that there is no difference between intention and speech. Language isn’t intended at all. As Cavell says, again, I can know the meaning of a word, but can I know the intention of a word?

语言与言语的问题并非如克纳普和迈克尔斯所言，是“为了理解意义，你必须能够推断作者意图”这一观点的反面。他们提出的这两个被简化的区分之间几乎没有对称性。无论解构主义有何主张，无论其优缺点如何，它是否真正将意图与意义的关系问题置于核心地位，这一点尚不明确。正如克纳普和迈克尔斯所说，言语是有意图的；如果没有意图，就不能称之为言语。但语言会削弱言语的意图，以至于意图在追溯语义过剩的过程中无法发挥决定性的诠释作用。正如我之前所说，在总结这些讲座时，我将尝试展示这一观点为理论研究带来的广阔视野。

The language-speech issue is not really the flip side—as Knapp and Michaels want you to think—of the idea that in order to know a meaning, you have to be able to infer an authorial intention. There is relatively little symmetry between their two collapsed distinctions. It’s just not clear that deconstruction, whatever its claims, whatever its perfections and imperfections, has the question of intention in relation to meaning very much at heart one way or another. Speech is intended, as Knapp and Michaels say; it is not speech if it is not intended. But language compromises the intention of speech to the point where intention can play no decisive hermeneutic role in the tracing out of semantic excess. In concluding these lectures, as I’ve said, I’ll try to exhibit the range of coverage that this viewpoint makes available for theory.

 

 

第26章

CHAPTER 26

结论

Conclusion

现在谁不讨厌理论呢？

Who Doesn’t Hate Theory Now?

在上一讲中，我们试图让理论摆脱克纳普和迈克尔斯的“驱逐”，我们通过指出语言和言语之间确实存在区别来做到这一点。在今天的总结性讲座中，我将继续探讨这一观点。与此同时，当我反复强调我们拯救了理论时，你们或许会问，为什么有人会费心去拯救它？上次我们开始思考，尤其是在新实用主义者声称语言和言语具有共同作用力——在他们看来，二者是同一回事——的情况下，我们是否必须得出这样的结论：理论不可能与实际目标有任何关联。这也是我今天想要再次探讨的问题。我们为什么要费心去拯救文学理论？显然，这与探索交流的局限性息息相关。

In the last lecture, we offered theory a reprieve from its banishment by Knapp and Michaels, and we did so by saying that there really is a difference between language and speech. That’s a claim that I want to continue investigating in today’s concluding lecture. In the meantime, when I keep saying we saved theory, you may well be asking why anybody would bother saving it. We began to wonder last time, especially in view of the neo-pragmatists’ claims about the common agency of language and speech—understood on their view to be one and the same thing—whether we have to conclude that theory can’t possibly have anything to do with practical objectives. That, too, is a concern that I want to revisit today. Why do we bother to save literary theory? Well, it has something to do, plainly, with discovering the limits of communication.

正如我们上次所说，语言无疑是“为了”——也就是说，我们创造语言就是为了——沟通。因此，那个老生常谈、甚至可以说是陈词滥调的问题——“我们彼此沟通得如何？”——不幸的是，我们自己也需要扪心自问。我想谈谈法国人在存在主义时期所说的“沟通缺失”（la manque de la communication）。首先，我想强调的是，我们实际上沟通得相当不错。恭喜我们！我认为，人们通常担心我们是否能够相互理解，尤其是在跨文化敏感方面，这种担忧往往过于戏剧化。我个人的感觉是，很多时候我们对彼此的理解都太透彻了，如果我们不必如此敏锐地关注彼此的“立场”，或许会更好。我认为，我们在提升彼此意识的努力中，存在着某种程度的虚伪。人们普遍认为，我们彼此之间态度恶劣是因为我们不够了解对方的“主体立场”。我对此并不认同。语言本身运作良好，不应成为我们持续敌意的罪魁祸首。语言具有一种粗犷而有效的特性，正如我所说，任何否认这一点的人，或多或少都是在无意中转移人们对其他可能源于沟通困难之外的问题的注意力。

Speech, as we said last time, is unquestionably “for”—that is to say, we have made it for—communication. Hence the old and frankly shopworn question, “How well do we communicate with each other?” is unfortunately one that we in our turn need to ask. I want to say a word or two about what the French during the existentialist period called la manque de la communication. First of all, I want to insist that we actually communicate rather well. Congratulations to us! I think that many of the usual ways in which people worry about whether we can understand each other, especially the transculturally sensitive ways, are quite melodramatically exaggerated. My own feeling is that a good deal of the time we understand each other all too well, and that it might be better if we didn’t sensitize ourselves to quite such an acute pitch about where each of us is “coming from.” I take there to be a measure of bad faith in our efforts to raise each other’s consciousness. The supposition is that we treat each other so badly because we don’t understand each other’s “subject positions” well enough. I’m not convinced of that. Speech is doing just fine, and shouldn’t be blamed for our continued ill will. Speech has a rough and ready efficacy, and anybody who denies that, as I say, is more or less unwittingly deflecting attention away from problems that may stem from grounds other than difficulty of communication.

但如果真是如此，那么理论为何又要跳出来反驳说沟通中其实存在缺陷呢？正如我们所见，克纳普和迈克尔斯否认了这个问题，问题在于语言这个令人烦恼的存在，它不断地在沟通过程中出现，阻碍沟通，正如俄国形式主义者所言，而且从他们的角度来看，这反而是件好事。的确，你在日常对话中能听到的语言的轻微嗡嗡声其实并不算坏事；正如我所说，我们仍然能够很好地沟通，那么理论为何要认为它能够以此为论据，驳斥那些认为语言就是言语，与言语并无本质区别的人的观点呢？

But if this is so, why, then, should theory come along and say to the contrary that there’s a glitch in communication after all? The problem—denied by Knapp and Michaels as we have seen—is this nagging entity called language, which keeps poking up through the communication process, getting in its way, impeding communication, as the Russian formalists suggested, and a good thing, too, from their point of view. Indeed, the slight buzz of language that you can hear in everyday speech isn’t so bad, really; we still do communicate pretty well, as I say, so why should theory suppose it can rest its case on this trivial-seeming point of contention with those people who say that language just is speech and not something different from it at all?

理论的部分功能在于衡量言语沟通的畅通程度，衡量言语在多大程度上仍能有效传达信息的准确性和细节水平。如果你仍然认为这件事无关紧要，我不会责怪你；但我希望通过这次讲座，你能意识到它其实非常重要。

Part of the function of theory is to gauge the degree to which speech communicates in an unimpeded way, to gauge the level of accuracy and detail at which it can be expected still to communicate effectively. If you still don’t consider this matter earth-shatteringly important, I don’t blame you; but I do hope to have convinced you by the end of this lecture that it’s surprisingly important after all.

与此同时，我们需要记住理论不是什么。本学期伊始，我们就区分了理论与哲学、理论与方法论，甚至理论与诠释学，之所以这样做，是因为哲学、方法论和诠释学的全部目的，与理论截然不同，在于发现意义。理论更关注意义是如何受阻的。当然，即便你精通理论，理解理论的目的，你仍然可以做其他事情。你可以成为系统构建者，像哲学家一样解释事物的整体性。同样，正如克纳普和迈克尔斯所说，你仍然可以运用文学数据进行实证研究，并将其组织起来，最终形成我们称之为“诗学”的方法论。最后，你可以进入诠释学的循环，探寻意义；事实上，这是你面对文本或话语时首先要做的事情，任何基于这种初步接触而进行的思考，包括理论，都会重新审视阐释工作的条件。你可以做所有这些事情，而且不必觉得理论站在一旁挥舞着拳头或对你指手画脚。理论不必像看门狗一样令人畏惧。至少在我看来（当然并非所有人都同意我的观点），理论实际上让我们能够自由地探索，它只是提醒我们在思考诠释和意义问题时，最好牢记一些限制或保留意见。

In the meantime, we need to remember what theory isn’t. We began the semester by distinguishing between theory and philosophy, theory and methodology, even between theory and hermeneutics, and we did so because the whole purpose of philosophy, methodology, and hermeneutics, in contrast with that of theory, is to discover meaning. Theory is more interested in the way meaning is impeded. Certainly, though, even though you’re good at theory and you understand the purpose of theory, you can still do these other things. You can be a system builder, explaining the totality of things as a philosopher. Likewise, as Knapp and Michaels say, you can still work empirically with literary data, organized to result in what we call “poetics,” a methodology. And finally you can enter the hermeneutic circle and search for meaning; indeed, that is the first thing you do in confronting a text or utterance, and any reflection that succeeds upon this first engagement, including theory, reconsiders the conditions of the interpretive effort. You can do all these things, and you don’t have to feel as though theory were standing on the sidelines shaking its fist or wagging its finger at you. Theory doesn’t have to be feared as a watchdog. At least in my opinion, and not everyone agrees with me, theory really lets us go our own way and simply reminds us that there are limits or reservations that it’s best to keep in mind while thinking through problems of interpretation and meaning.

因此，我将理论定义为（也已被定义为）一种消极的思维运动，它描绘了对沟通抱持怀疑态度的合理方式——而非那些令人焦虑不安、忧心忡忡的方式。理论是一种反作用力，它反对那些通常被认为是真理、被假定为真理，以及——当然，这里就引出了关键点——被宣读为真理的事物：被表达出来、被阐述出来、被宣读为真理。如果真是如此，为什么还要对语言如此大惊小怪？为什么我们如此迅速地将关注点缩小到语言上？我上次关于语言和言语之间关系的论述可能让你觉得不够令人信服，因为它过于狭隘。现在，我想大大拓宽我对“语言”一词的理解。我认为，理论通过三种方式促使人们对言语的有效性，即那些符合某种意图的言语的有效性，产生一定程度的怀疑。

So theory I would define, and have defined, as a negative movement of thought mapping the legitimate ways—as opposed to the anguished, hand-wringing ways—to be suspicious of communication. Theory is an antithetical counterforce to that which is commonly supposed to be true, posited as true, and—here of course one comes to the point—spoken as true: enounced, articulated, spoken as true. If that’s the case, why the fuss about language specifically? Why do we so quickly narrow our focus down to language? What I said last time about the relationship between language and speech may have seemed unconvincing to you because it was so narrow. I want now to broaden considerably the sense of what I mean by “language.” Theory, I believe, encourages a measure of suspicion about the efficacy of speech, of that which is spoken in keeping with an intention, in three ways.

上次我提到过其中之一，这次我要描述三个。第一个，也是我上次提到的，是语言如何干扰语音作为声音的指称功能。也就是说，如果我们把语音视为一种交流媒介，那么即便在我们说话的时候，我们也不得不问自己：为什么语音会受到如此多的声学噪音的干扰，而这些噪音对我们来说大多毫无用处？当然，有时候，声音的模式似乎确实有助于交流。你可能会问，声音难道不是对意义的强化吗？我之前讲过新批评，你们高中时就已经学过新批评了。你们就是通过新批评学习文学阐释的。新批评所寻找的，而且也确实发现的，是声音对意义的强化。诗歌理解手册里就是这么说的，蒲柏在他的《论批评》中也最早提出了这个观点。我们有很多机会去欣赏那些通过声音模式的运用而增强的、精心构思的意义或结构的复杂性。例如，《教皇》中受伤的蛇拖着缓慢的身躯前行，《卡米拉》中迅捷的蛇在平原上穿梭，它们各自笨拙而充满活力的声音都令我们感到愉悦。

Last time I mentioned one of these, but now I shall describe three. The first, which I did mention last time, is the way language obtrudes itself on the referential function of speech as sound. That is, if we think of speech as a medium of communication, we’re forced to ask ourselves, even as we engage in speech, how and why it is that speech is so much burdened, in ways that are of no use whatsoever to us for the most part, by acoustic noise. Sometimes, to be sure, patterns of sound seem to help communication along. You might ask whether sound isn’t a reinforcement of meaning. I told you back when we covered the New Criticism that all of you had already done the New Criticism in high school. That’s the way you learned literary interpretation. What the New Critic looks for, and certainly finds, is the reinforcement of sense by sound. That’s what it says in handbooks about understanding poetry, and Pope said it first in his Essay on Criticism. There are plenty of occasions on which we can revel in the complexity of an intentional meaning or intentional structure that is augmented by the way sound patterns are used. The wounded snake in Pope drags its slow length along, swift Camilla scours the plain, and their respective cumbersome and turbo-charged sounds delight us.

与此同时，正如俄罗斯形式主义者在研究俄罗斯传统中的头韵诗、民间传说和民间诗歌（包括谚语诗）时所发现的那样，我们根本无法把握其中涉及的声音元素的语义目的。我们的自发性言语中有一种奇特的倾向，即声音的重复——这不仅仅是因为我们大多数人说话时都使用抑扬格，并且无意识地使用头韵。雅各布森在《语言学与诗学》中提醒我们，当附近发生暴力事件时，我们会自称是“无辜的旁观者”。我们本可以说“目击者”，而不是“旁观者”，但双扬抑格决定了我们的选择。一个人之所以是无辜的旁观者，并非因为这个表达具有任何特定的含义或语义价值，而是因为它朗朗上口。这种声音的功能，可以称之为言语中声音的过度决定性表现，在经济学家看来或许是非理性的。他们在那里，他们在工作，但这很难称之为沟通。

At the same time, as the Russian formalists discovered when working with alliterative verse, folklore, and folk verse in the Russian tradition, verse embodying proverbs, there is simply no way of grasping a semantic purpose in the sound elements that are involved. There is a strange pull in our spontaneous utterances toward repetitiousness of sound—it’s not just that we all for the most part speak in iambics and alliterate without knowing it. Jakobson reminds us in “Linguistics and Poetics” about that moment when a violent event takes place nearby and we identify ourselves as an “innocent bystander.” We could have said “witness,” not “bystander,” but the double dactyl determined our choice. A person is an innocent bystander not because that expression has any particular meaning or semantic valence but because it’s catchy. Such functions of sound, which could be called overdetermined appearances of sound in speech, are what an economist might call irrational. They’re there, they’re doing a job, but it’s hard to call it communication.

以上便是关于声音的部分，但这并非仅仅是声音的问题。如果仅仅如此，如果文学理论仅仅局限于俄国形式主义者最初两三年的研究成果，我们大概就不会开设这门学科的入门概览课程了。语言还会以其他两种方式阻碍言语的表达。首先，语言本身会产生一种无法控制的语义漂移，这种漂移偏离了言语本身的语义漂移，从而扰乱了言语的表达。语言似乎拥有其自身的意义。索绪尔曾花费数年时间研究拉丁语和其他印欧语系诗歌中蕴含的字谜。他试图基于这些发现构建一套关于诗歌的普遍理论。意义之中蕴含着意义，这种意义不可能是人为植入的，然而，奇怪的是，我们却能从中找到它。不妨试着一边阅读以下内容，一边背诵一首著名的诗歌——就是我们在上一讲中讨论的那首，因为它是克纳普和迈克尔斯在《反对理论》一书中举的例子：

So much, then, for sound, but it’s not only a matter of sound. If it were only that, if literary theory were only about the first two or three years’ worth of research performed by the Russian formalists, we probably wouldn’t be offering an introductory survey course in the subject. Speech is impeded by language in two other ways. It is disturbed to begin with by the way language produces in what’s being said an uncontrollable semantic drift that wanders away from the semantic drift of speech. Language seems to have a meaning of its own. It was Saussure who devoted years of research to finding anagrams embedded in Latin and other Indo-European verse. He wanted to build a general theory of poetry out of these discoveries. There was meaning within meaning that couldn’t possibly have been planted there and yet, strangely enough, one could find it there. Try reciting a well-known poem—the one that we took up in the last lecture because it was the example given in Knapp and Michaels’s “Against Theory”—while reading this:

啊，贫民窟里死人，嗯，我用矛刺穿了海豹。眼睛加了，知道休谟，而且凶猛！沙阿缝（呃！）很薄；滴答声像打结一样难受：砰！呃，翻过背风的耳朵。不再！避开哈希，没有四，嘘！膝盖后腿，北欧式的轻松。角色溺水，受伤，死亡，骨灰瓮：所有尸体，牛去哪儿了？——嘶！-onus条目。
Ah slum per dead, um, I spear’d seal. Eye add, know Hume, ’n fierce! Shah seam (duh!) thin; the tic oud-knot fee ill: thud! Uh shover the lee ears. No mo’! Shun hash e’en ow, no fours, shhh! knee th’rears, Norse ease. Role drown, an’ hurts, die, urn: all corpse, whither oxen?—sst!-onus entries.

这就是你将要背诵的内容：

And this is what you will have recited:

沉睡封印了我的灵魂；
A slumber did my spirit seal;
我没有丝毫人类的恐惧：
I had no human fears:
她似乎是一个没有感觉的东西。
She seem’d a thing that could not feel
岁月的痕迹。
The touch of earthly years.
她现在没有一丝动静，也没有一丝力气；
No motion has she now, no force;
她既听不见也看不见；
She neither hears nor sees;
在地球的昼夜循环中滚动
Roll’d ’round in earth’s diurnal course
有岩石、石头和树木。
With rocks, and stones, and trees.

你可以看出，第一种创作“诗”的方法，本质上就是在进行一种练习，这与乔伊斯在《芬尼根守灵夜》中所做的练习如出一辙。事实上，当我以这种方式创作这首诗时，我一直在想，它完全可以收录在《芬尼根守灵夜》里。你可以想象，我当时对自己相当满意。请注意，我只使用了真正的词语。文本中没有任何非单词。我使用了某种时代错置，用了一两个外来词，但我也使用了标点符号，以使这段文字在某种程度上具有意义，其中一部分内容与死亡有关，并且与华兹华斯诗歌的意义有着惊人的重叠。我本可以让它变成胡言乱语——就像刘易斯·卡罗尔的“'Twas brillig, and the slithy toves / did gyre and gimble in the wabe”那样——这才是语言受不可控的语义漂移影响的更明显的方式。刘易斯·卡罗尔那首著名的无厘头诗歌的妙处在于，我们都以为自己知道它的意思：“风很大，黏糊糊的蟾蜍在波浪中跳跃嬉戏。”我们以为它的意思大概就是这样，但语义漂移——这正是刘易斯·卡罗尔故意引入的，目的是为了掩盖我们想象中存在的字面意思——使我们无法对它的含义得出任何确切的结论。

You can see that to write the “poem” the first way is to perform an exercise that is essentially what Joyce is doing in Finnegans Wake. As a matter of fact, as I composed the poem this way, I kept saying to myself that it could be in Finnegans Wake. I was quite pleased with myself, as you can imagine. Notice that I have used only real words. There’s nothing in the transcript that is not a word. I have indulged in some anachronism and used a foreign word or two, but I have also used punctuation to help this discourse make some degree of sense, a certain amount of it concerning death and overlapping uncannily with the sense of Wordsworth’s poem. I could have just left it at nonsense—like Lewis Carroll’s “ ’Twas brillig, and the slithy toves / did gyre and gimble in the wabe”—which is the more obvious way that speech is affected by uncontrollable semantic drift. The amusing point of Lewis Carroll’s famous nonsense verse is that we all think we know what it means: “ ’Twas blusterous and the slimy toads did leap and frolic in the waves.” We think it means something like that, but semantic drift—which is what Lewis Carroll deliberately introduces to overwhelm the plain sense we imagine to be present—prevents us from drawing any secure conclusions about the meaning.

我希望我那近乎荒谬的华兹华斯诗作《沉睡封印我的灵魂》的转录能向我们展示言语中语义漂移的程度。假设你是一个与我们所有人所属的阐释社群相距甚远的人（正如斯坦利·菲什所说），你甚至不知道什么是诗，更不用说华兹华斯的这首诗能被大多数文学专业的学生一眼认出。有人在你面前朗诵了我刚才引用的那段文字。如果你擅长写作并把它转录下来，你很可能会写出像我写在黑板上的那样的东西。换句话说，你不会自然而然地意识到你听到的正是华兹华斯实际写下的。这种语义漂移存在于任何话语中。

I hope my quasi-nonsensical transcription of Wordsworth’s “A Slumber Did My Spirit Seal” can show us the extent to which there is semantic drift in speech. Let’s say that you are a person far removed from the interpretive community to which all the rest of us belong, as Stanley Fish would put it, and you don’t even know what a poem is, let alone that this poem by Wordsworth can be identified instantly by most students of literature. Somebody recites in your presence what I just quoted to you. If you were good at writing and transcribed the thing, you might very well produce something like what I put on the board. In other words, it wouldn’t just spontaneously occur to you that what Wordsworth actually wrote was what you were hearing. This kind of semantic drift is present in any utterance.

言语很少会像这样被误解，因为我们非常擅长理解语境。这也是所谓的沟通难题并没有人们有时声称的那么严重的原因之一。因此，我们不太可能犯下严重的错误，但当然，偶尔也会犯错。林登·约翰逊的演讲稿撰写人在他的演讲稿中写了“misled”（误导）这个词，约翰逊读完演讲稿后，猛地捶了一下讲台，说道：“我们不会被误导（myzled）！” 我希望不会发生这种情况。我们都知道，这就是拼写检查的弊端。你打开拼写检查，写完论文，却懒得修改，然后就交了上去。结果论文里满是低级错误，因为语言中充满了同音词，而拼写检查总是莫名其妙地给你选错词。坦白说，你现在很尴尬，因为你的老师正在嘲笑你的错误，而不是关注你重要的思考。简而言之，不要使用拼写检查，只需记住拼写检查可以向我们展示语言的语义漂移在口语中渗透的程度。

Utterances are not often mistaken in this way because we’re really very good at understanding context. That’s one of the reasons why the so-called problem of communication isn’t as great as people sometimes claim it is. Hence we’re not likely to go badly wrong, yet certainly there are occasions when we do. A speechwriter for Lyndon Johnson wrote the word “misled” in a speech for him, and when Johnson read the speech he pounded his fist on the podium and said “We will not be myzled.” I should hope not. As we all know, that’s the trouble with spell-check. You put it on, you write your term paper and don’t bother to edit it, you turn the paper in. It’s full of howlers because, of course, the language is full of homonyms, and spell-check always uncannily gives you the wrong word. You’re in the soup, frankly, because your teacher is laughing at your blunders instead of paying attention to your important thoughts. In short, don’t use spell-check, just remember that spell-check can show us how much the semantic drift of language permeates speech.

语言阻碍言语表达还有第三种方式。请记住，我说过语言（langue）是一种虚拟实体，因为我们永远无法以任何成文形式实际接触到它。没错，我们有词典里的词汇，但这只是语言的一部分。到目前为止，请注意，我们在讨论语义漂移时只谈到了词汇；但除了词汇之外，语言（langue）还是一套规则——语法和句法规则，只有通过这些规则，言语才能有意义。因此，语言除了提供声音和词语选择之外，还对我们在言语表达时的选择产生语法和句法上的影响。

There’s yet a third way in which language impedes speech. Remember I have said that language, langue, is a virtual entity because we could never actually encounter it written down in any codified form. Yes, we have the lexicon in a dictionary, but that’s only part of it. So far, notice that we’ve only been talking about the lexicon when we talk about semantic drift; but in addition to the lexicon, language, langue, is a set of rules—the rules of grammar and syntax by means of which, and only by means of which, speech can make sense. Thus in addition to offering sound and word choice, language has a grammatical and syntactical bearing on the choices that we can make while producing speech.

不幸的是，这些规则有时并不那么容易捉摸。例如，当我们用“It is raining”这个看似无害的表达来阐释雅各布森的六组信息结构时，我们就被“It is raining”的元语言功能弄得措手不及。我们不禁自问：“‘它’到底是什么？”这个“它”可能会把我们引向各种奇特的方向：木星普鲁维乌斯、上帝、宇宙、云朵。有些解释看似合理，但没有一个是确定的。我们意识到，“它”在这个句子中只是一个占位符，并没有发挥它应有的作用。而且，相信我，这种怪异现象并非英语独有。正如我之前所说，在其他语言中也能找到类似的例子：il pleut、es regnet等等。在所有这些表达中，“它”都未能发挥其应有的作用。我们开始意识到，即使我们不断努力去理解，如果我们过分依赖一句无害的话语，我们仍然会陷入经济学家所说的非理性之中。

Unfortunately those rules can be slippery. When we talked about the innocuous expression “It is raining” as an illustration of Jakobson’s six sets to the message, just for example, we were brought up short by the metalingual function of “It is raining.” We asked ourselves, “What on earth is ‘it’?” It can lead us in strange directions, this “it”: Jupiter Pluvius, God, the cosmos, the clouds. Some of it is plausible, but none of it is definite. We realize that “it” is a placeholder in the sentence that is not doing its job and, believe me, this oddity is not confined to English. As I said before, you can find in other languages: il pleut, es regnet, and so on. In all of those expressions, “it” is not doing its job. We start to realize that if we lean too hard even on an innocuous utterance, we’re in the presence of what the economists, again, would call irrationality, despite our continuous effort to make sense.

然而，真正决定语篇漂移如何支配任何话语的，是谓词在语言中的运作方式。正如我之前所说，任何断言，任何真理的宣告，同时也是一种隐喻。任何断言的深层结构都宣称A是B；也就是说，从定义上讲，它就是一个断言。但是，当“A是B”是语法学家所说的系词（copula）——主语和谓语之间的连接——时，我们理解A和B之间的关系并非同一性关系，并非A是B的隐喻性宣告，而是一种连接，例如，德曼（de Man）会称之为转喻（metonymic）。问题在于，任何以转喻方式宣告A是B的句子——也就是说，作为语法命题——同时也是一个隐喻。任何隐喻都不可能完全成立，它总是包含着所谓的误用（catachresis）的成分。朱丽叶并非真正的太阳。语法否认同一性，但坚持某种逻辑；隐喻（或者德曼所说的“修辞”）宣称一种身份，却违背逻辑。因此，每一个以“存在”为核心的句子（而它们确实如此）都同时提出了这两个不可调和的主张。

What really conditions the way drift governs any utterance, however, is the way predication works in language. As I said before, any assertion, any declaration of a truth, is at the same time a metaphor. The deep structure of any assertion proclaims that A is B; that is, it is an assertion by definition. But when “A is B” is the connection of subject and predicate that grammarians call a copula, we understand that the relationship between A and B is not a relationship of identity, a metaphorical declaration that A is B, but rather a connection that de Man, for example, would call metonymic. The problem is that any sentence declaring that A is B metonymically—that is to say, as a grammatical proposition—is at the same time a metaphor. No metaphor stands on all fours but always has an element of what’s called catachresis in it. Juliet is not really the sun. Grammar disclaims identity but adheres to a logic; metaphor (or what de Man calls “rhetoric”) asserts an identity but defies logic. Every sentence, then, that turns on the hinge of “to be” (and they all do) makes both of these irreconcilable claims at once.

这就是德曼在《符号学与修辞学》中提出的观点：任何话语中都存在着语法与修辞之间的永恒张力。没有哪条话语是不符合语法的，也没有哪条话语是完全不包含修辞的，但遗憾的是，语法与修辞总是或明或暗地相互冲突，正如谓词与隐喻必然相互冲突一样。换句话说，没有哪个句子中的语法和句法规则不会微妙地干扰我们所谓的修辞规则——即修辞格的运用方式，而这些方式可以提炼成我们对隐喻的理解。

This is the point that de Man is making in “Semiology and Rhetoric”: there is a perpetual tension in any utterance between grammar and rhetoric. There’s no competent utterance that’s not grammatical, there’s no utterance of any kind that’s not rhetorical, but unfortunately grammar and rhetoric are always openly or subtly at odds with each other, just in the way that predication and metaphor have to be at odds with each other. In other words, there isn’t a sentence in which the rules of grammar and syntax are not subtly interfering with what you might call the rules of rhetoric—the ways in which tropes deploy themselves, ways that can be distilled in an understanding of what we call metaphor.

所以，正如我所说，每一句话都受到声音变幻莫测、词语语义漂移和词语回响的影响，也受到语法和修辞不相容性的影响。所有这些扭曲言语的因素，正是索绪尔及其传统所称的“语言”的一部分。换句话说，它们是语言——如果我可以这样说的话——通过言语表达的方式，是我们在任何场合所说的任何话都受到另一种声音影响的方式。我们从社会学的角度将其理解为巴赫金的多语现象。我们从精神分析的角度将其理解为潜意识中存在的他者话语。我们从纯粹的语言学角度将其理解为语言（langue ），但我认为，现在我们也可以将其比喻性地理解为一种先前的言语，它萦绕在我们有意言语的主体性之中。语言是一种无意识的言语。

So every sentence, as I say, is shadowed not just by the vagaries of sound, not just by the semantic drift of words and word-echoes, but also by the incompatibility of grammar and rhetoric. All of these warping influences on speech are part of what Saussure and his tradition call language. They are the ways, in other words, in which language—if I can put it this way—speaks through speech, the ways in which anything that we say on any occasion is shadowed by another voice. We’ve understood this in social terms as Bakhtinian polyglossia. We have understood it in psychoanalytic terms as the discourse of the otherness that inhabits the unconscious. We have understood it in purely linguistic terms as langue, but we can also, I think, metaphorically speaking, understand it now as a prior speech that haunts the agency of our intentional speech. Language is an unintentional speech.

请记住：没有人——任何理论家，任何头脑清醒的人——会试图反驳“言语是有意图的”这一论断，即我们说话是有意图的。克纳普和迈克尔斯的观点正是如此，他们给我们敲响了警钟，提醒我们怀疑意图是多么的不合时宜。认为言语并非出于意图：这究竟意味着什么？言语本身就是一种意图，但我一直试图论证，存在一种言语，即“语言的言语”，它是无意图的，它就那样存在着。它无法被排除在外。或许，当我们关注沟通的成功时，我们可以忽略它，但我们不能把它抛诸脑后，仿佛它不存在一样。它总会再次出现。如果我们足够认真地对待诠释的艺术——换句话说，如果我们真的对人们所说的话施加某种压力：一种超越语用层面的压力，使我们能够注意到任何场合下任何话语都具有的惊人多样性——那么它总会在某个时刻与我们正面交锋。

Keep in mind: nobody—no theorist, nobody in her right mind—would ever try to resist the claim that speech is intentional, that we intend what we say. That’s where Knapp and Michaels are right and give us a bracing reminder about the degree to which skepticism about intention is misplaced. The idea that speech is somehow not intended: what could that mean? Speech just is intention, but I’ve been trying to argue that there is a speech, the “speech of language,” which is unintentional, which is just there. It can’t be factored out. It can be ignored, perhaps, when we focus on the successes of communication, but it can’t be set aside as though it were not there. It will always come back. It will always confront us at some point if we take the arts of interpretation seriously enough—if, in other words, we really do bring some pressure to bear on the things that people say: a pressure that goes beyond the pragmatic and enables us to notice the amazing variability that belongs to any utterance on any occasion.

语言的起源之一，便是通过言语来表达。仿佛它在宣告自身的存在，在我们发现它的用途之前，它原本就是那样。还记得我们上次说过什么吗？你必须先发现火可以用来烹饪。火并非“为了”烹饪而存在。山洞并非用来居住的。灵巧的拇指并非用来抓握的。你必须引导这些自然现象为人类所用。语言存在于我们的言语之中，仿佛在提醒我们，它并非一直为我们服务，提醒我们，有意识的表达史是我们永无止境地驾驭语言的努力。专业作家对此感受最为深刻。他们试图驾驭语言，使其臣服。但这实际上是我们所有人的共同追求，无论我们是在创作伟大的美国小说，还是在修改一篇学期论文。我们都在努力驾驭语言，而我们都知道这并非易事。我只是想解释一下为什么这不容易。

Language speaks through speech partly as its origin. It is as though it were asserting its identity as what it was back before we discovered it was useful for something. Remember what we said about that last time: you have to discover that fire is useful for cooking. Fire is not “for” cooking. A cave is not for dwelling. A prehensile thumb is not for grasping. You have to channel these phenomena for human uses. Language is there in what we say as if to remind us that it wasn’t always at our service, to remind us that the history of conscious expression is our never-ending effort to master language. It’s the professional writer who feels this most acutely. You try to wrestle language into submission. But it’s really the ambition of all of us, whether we’re writing the great American novel or revising a term paper. We’re wrestling language into submission, and we all know it’s not easy. I’m just trying to explain why it’s not easy.

因此，语言既是言语的起源，也是言语的终结。换句话说，语言标志着言语的主动性最终受到质疑，某种程度上被削弱。我认为，将语言——再次以比喻的方式——称为言语的墓志铭是恰当的，也是公平的。在任何特定的言语中，即便其主动性仍在彰显，其自身的终结也已铭刻于此。

Language speaks through us, then, as the origin of speech, but it also speaks as the death of speech. It speaks, in other words, as the moment in which the purposeful agency of speech is finally called into question, in a certain sense undermined. I think it’s appropriate, I think it’s fair, to call language—again metaphorically—the epitaph of speech, the moment at which, in any given speech, the end of its own agency is inscribed even as that agency is asserting itself.

我想通过例子来检验这些论断，并进一步向你们展示语义漂移是如何运作的，以及语法和修辞之间微妙的关系是如何运作的。我们来看几篇墓志铭。如果语言是言语的墓志铭，那么为什么不看看墓志铭中发生了什么呢？

I want to test these assertions by example and also show you a bit more about how semantic drift functions—and also how the perilous relationship between grammar and rhetoric works. Let’s look at a couple of epitaphs. If language is the epitaph of speech, why not see what happens in epitaphs?

我最喜欢的墓志铭，希望你在漫步墓园时看到它时也能会心一笑。墓碑上写着：“我早就告诉过你我病了。” 这句话很有意思，原因有很多。首先，这一点值得深思：从这句抱怨中，我们可以推断出不止一个人在有效地传达信息，而是很多人。艾米莉·狄金森和其他作家的作品中有很多关于死后发声的先例，当然，这里最明显的发声者是死者本人：“这些年来，我一直坐在角落里告诉你我头疼。你却从来没听过。”

My favorite epitaph by far will I hope give you a chuckle, too, when you come across it walking through a cemetery. On the tombstone you find written, “I told you I was sick.” Now this is a very interesting expression for a number of reasons. For one thing, and one should pause over this, one can infer from this complaint a number of speakers who are speaking effectively and communicating a clear message, not just one but many. There’s plenty of precedent for posthumous speech in Emily Dickinson and other writers, and of course here the most obvious speaker is the dead person speaking from the grave: “There I was, sitting in the corner all those years telling you I had a headache. You never listened to me.”

但说话者也可能是其他人，我这么说并非质疑其意图。当我们假定存在某种意图时，我们只是在几个可能的说话者中选出谁，这完全符合“我们面对的是有意识的言语”这一假设，无需质疑。说话者也可能是一位道歉的亲戚，承认自己没听进去，但又带着一丝幽默，于是用死者的口吻抱怨道：“我告诉过你我生病了”，以此作为一种道歉：“是的，我知道你说过，我真该为此自责，但我当时心不在焉。”

But the speaker could be somebody else, and I’m not introducing a measure of skepticism about intention in saying this. When we posit an intention, we just decide which of several candidates to speak may be speaking, adhering quite properly without question to the supposition that we are in the presence of intentional speech. The speaker could be an apologetic relative, someone acknowledging that they hadn’t listened, but with a sense of humor, hence putting in the voice of the dead person the complaint, “I told you I was sick,” as a form of apology: “Yes, I know you did, and I could kick myself for it, but I had other things on my mind.”

然而，说话者也可能是一位在墓前说教的人，这在十八世纪的墓志铭中很常见。他可能是一位哲学家，说道：“疾病是人类的生存状态，正如我一直告诉你们的那样。我出版了很多著作，其全部主旨就是‘我病了’。我是陀思妥耶夫斯基笔下的地下室人。我是一个病人，一个重病患者。好吧，就让我的病情恶化吧。”或者，说话者也可能是一位文化评论家，以寓言式的口吻在墓碑上刻下文化的死亡。文明早已病入膏肓，最终，它就此消亡。用通俗易懂的方式表达，那就是：“我，文明，告诉过你们我病了。我有很多方法可以告诉你们我身体不适：你们却置若罔闻，这就是结果。”

Yet again, the speaker could be someone moralizing over the grave, a frequent habit in eighteenth-century epitaphs. It could be a philosopher saying, “Sickness is the human condition, as I kept telling you. I published many volumes, the whole purport of which was ‘I am sick.’ I’m Dostoevsky’s Underground Man. I am a sick man, a very sick man. Well, let it get worse.” Or yet again, the speaker could be a cultural critic, inscribing on the stone, in an allegorical mood, the death of culture. Civilization has been in a bad way for a long time and here, finally, it lies. The way to communicate this colloquially would then be, “I, civilization, told you I was sick. I had many ways of letting you know that all was not well with me: you didn’t pay any attention, and here is the result.”

我认为，所有这些解读墓志铭的方式都符合诠释学的范畴。它们与我们理解说话者意图的努力是一致的。但假设我们说，“语言”必然像在其他任何话语中一样，在这段话语中显露出来。你会发现，这里的问题不在于声音。甚至也不在于语义的偏移，尽管如果你把这段墓志铭背诵给站在你旁边的一位视障人士听，其中的“aye tolled yew eye was seek”可能会让人停下来思考，就像潜藏的存在主义隐喻“I was sickness”或青少年时期表达强烈自我欣赏的“I was sick”一样。语言以另一种方式显现自身。它让我们突然以一种或许任何说话者都不希望的方式理解这句话。于是，它变成了一个寓言，由语言巧妙地引入，恰恰是关于言语的无力。这正是言语的问题所在，不是吗？ “我一遍又一遍地告诉你，”语言的魔咒下，言语说道，“但你却充耳不闻。”这是因为语言削弱了我的言语。这就是当讲师的弊端。“你没听进去，”语言在我言语中留下的墓志铭如此写道。“哦，好吧，”你说，“他的语言只是在开玩笑。”

I would say that all these ways of reading the epitaph are available to hermeneutics. They are consistent with the effort we make to understand what a speaker means. But suppose we say that “language” must be obtruding itself in this utterance, as in any other. You can see that it isn’t here a question of sound. It isn’t even a question of semantic drift, although “aye tolled yew eye was seek,” if you recite the epitaph to a sight-impaired person standing next to you, might give pause, as might the lurking existential metaphor, “I was sickness,” or the recent teenage expression of intense self-admiration, “I was sick.” Language makes itself felt in yet another way. It makes us suddenly understand the sentence in a way that perhaps no individual speaker would wish for. It then becomes an allegory, cleverly introduced by language, precisely about the inefficacy of speech. That’s just the problem with speech, isn’t it? “Again and again and again I tell you something,” speech says under the spell of language, “and you don’t listen.” It’s because language weakens my speech. That’s the problem with being a lecturer. “You didn’t listen,” says language’s epitaph in my speech. “Oh, well,” you say, “his language is just joking.”

所以，根据语言以言语为代价所引入的寓言，以及对言语的诠释——言语本身就是如此。坐在角落里，愤愤不平地抱怨没人听她或他说话的人，实际上是一位寓言家，他告诉我们，言语总是如此。因此，当我说语言是言语的墓志铭时，我们意识到，躺在这里的正是言语本身。尽管竭力想要说真话，言语却最终还是说谎了，它就此长眠于此。

So it is—according to the allegory introduced by language at the expense of speech, signifyin’ on speech—with speech in general. This person sitting in the corner, complaining bitterly about nobody ever listening to her or to him, is actually an allegorist telling us that that’s the way speech always is. Thus when I say language is the epitaph of speech, we realize that it is speech itself that’s lying here. Having lied in spite of every effort to speak true, here lies speech.

那么，我们再来看一个例子：“约翰·多伊长眠于此”，这或许是最初的墓志铭。这次我们甚至无需在说话者身上停留片刻，直接探讨语言本身带来的问题。首先，约翰·多伊显然并非长眠于“此处”。事实上，仔细想想，约翰·多伊完全有可能长眠于除“此处”以外的任何地方，因为我们知道，在这句话出现的地方，约翰·多伊不可能存在。正如我所说，他可能在其他任何地方。因此，任何墓志铭都是一种自我宣示的衣冠冢，一种刻在尸体不在的地方的铭文——这当然也揭示了语言的任意性。语言并非由依附于现实世界的自然符号构成。就身体而言，纹身是指向外部的言语，是雅各布森所说的情感意动性话语，而非铭文或指称性话语，即便它们表达的是“我的皮肤在这里”。言语存在于事物之上，存在于事物的边缘，例如一块岩石上，但它所说的谎言，顺从于语言，即便如此，也是对其所指对象的错位。

So let’s try another one: “Here lies John Doe,” probably the Ur-epitaph. Let’s not even pause over the speaker this time. Let’s turn immediately to the problems posed by language. In the first place, John Doe obviously does not lie precisely “here.” In fact, if you think about it, it’s altogether possible that John Doe could lie absolutely anywhere except “here,” because where the sentence is we know John Doe cannot be. He could be anyplace else, as I say. Hence any epitaph is therefore a self-declared cenotaph, an inscription on a place where the body isn’t—which of course tells us a lot, too, about the arbitrary nature of language.
